questions.q: How many legs does a spider have?
questions.f: Spiders are arachnids, and all arachnids have eight legs.

questions.q: What do baby cows drink to grow?
questions.f: Baby cows are called calves and drink their mother's milk.

questions.q: Which animal says 'moo'?
questions.f: Cows moo to call their calves and talk to the herd.

questions.q: What covers a fish's body?
questions.f: Overlapping scales protect fish and help them slip through water.

questions.q: True or False: All birds can fly.
questions.f: Penguins and ostriches are birds that cannot fly at all.

questions.q: What do bees make that is sweet to eat?
questions.f: Bees turn flower nectar into honey inside their hive.

questions.q: Which small animal carries a hard shell and crawls slowly?
questions.f: A snail can pull its whole soft body inside its shell to hide.

questions.q: What is a baby dog called?
questions.f: Baby dogs are called puppies and are born unable to see.

questions.q: Which animal is known as the king of the jungle?
questions.f: Male lions have big manes and a roar you can hear for miles.

questions.q: Where do fish live?
questions.f: Fish breathe underwater using gills instead of lungs.

questions.q: True or False: A penguin is a bird that cannot fly.
questions.f: Penguins use their wings as flippers to 'fly' through the water instead.

questions.q: What do rabbits love to eat?
questions.f: Rabbits nibble carrots and grass with teeth that never stop growing.

questions.q: Which animal hops and says 'ribbit'?
questions.f: Frogs are amphibians that start life as tadpoles in water.

questions.q: What is a baby cat called?
questions.f: Kittens purr, which can help calm them and even heal their bones.

questions.q: Which animal carries its baby in a pouch?
questions.f: A baby kangaroo, called a joey, is smaller than a grape at birth.

questions.q: How many humps does a Bactrian camel have?
questions.f: Camel humps store fat, not water, giving them energy in the desert.

questions.q: Which animal is the biggest on land today?
questions.f: African elephants can weigh as much as six cars put together.

questions.q: True or False: Snakes have tiny legs hidden under their scales.
questions.f: Snakes have no legs and slither by gripping the ground with their scales.

questions.q: What color is a polar bear's fur?
questions.f: Polar bear fur looks white but is actually clear, and their skin is black.

questions.q: Which bird can fan out a colourful tail?
questions.f: A male peacock spreads its shimmering tail to show off to females.

questions.q: True or False: A jellyfish has a brain.
questions.f: Jellyfish have no brain, heart, or bones, yet they have swum the seas for ages.

questions.q: What do we call animals like cats, dogs, and cows?
questions.f: Mammals have hair or fur and feed their babies milk.

questions.q: Which bird is famous for copying words people say?
questions.f: Parrots don't understand words but can mimic many sounds they hear.

questions.q: What is a baby sheep called?
questions.f: Lambs can stand and walk within minutes of being born.

questions.q: Which insect is shaped like a twig to hide from enemies?
questions.f: A stick insect stays very still so predators think it is just a branch.

questions.q: True or False: A butterfly starts life as a caterpillar.
questions.f: A caterpillar forms a chrysalis and transforms into a butterfly inside.

questions.q: Which animal builds dams in rivers using sticks?
questions.f: Beavers' front teeth never stop growing, so gnawing wood keeps them short.

questions.q: What do most birds build to lay their eggs in?
questions.f: Birds build nests from twigs, grass, and mud to keep eggs safe and warm.

questions.q: Which sea animal is a mammal, not a fish?
questions.f: Dolphins breathe air through a blowhole and must surface to breathe.

questions.q: How many legs does a normal insect have?
questions.f: All insects have six legs and three body parts: head, thorax, and abdomen.

questions.q: Which animal is the fastest runner on land?
questions.f: A cheetah can sprint about 112 km per hour, faster than cars in town.

questions.q: Which is the tallest animal in the world?
questions.f: A giraffe can grow taller than a two-storey house, about 5.5 metres.

questions.q: Which is the largest animal that has ever lived?
questions.f: A blue whale's heart alone is about the size of a small car.

questions.q: What do we call an animal that only eats plants?
questions.f: Herbivores like cows and deer have flat teeth for grinding leaves.

questions.q: What do we call an animal that only eats meat?
questions.f: Carnivores like tigers have sharp teeth for tearing meat.

questions.q: Which big cat has stripes?
questions.f: Every tiger's stripe pattern is unique, like a human fingerprint.

questions.q: Which animal is called man's best friend?
questions.f: Dogs were the first animals humans tamed, over 15,000 years ago.

questions.q: What is a group of lions called?
questions.f: A pride of lions is usually led by related females who hunt together.

questions.q: Which animal sleeps through the whole winter, called hibernating?
questions.f: Bears live off stored body fat while hibernating and rarely wake up.

questions.q: What is a baby kangaroo called?
questions.f: A joey lives in its mother's pouch for months while it grows.

questions.q: True or False: Bats use sound to find their way in the dark.
questions.f: Bats send out squeaks and listen for echoes, a trick called echolocation.

questions.q: Which reptile can regrow its tail if it breaks off?
questions.f: Many lizards drop their tail to escape, then slowly grow a new one.

questions.q: Which animal is famous for a hard shell it hides inside?
questions.f: A turtle's shell is part of its skeleton, so it can never leave it.

questions.q: What is a group of wolves called?
questions.f: Wolf packs are family groups that hunt and raise pups together.

questions.q: Which large Australian bird cannot fly?
questions.f: The emu is Australia's tallest bird and runs fast instead of flying.

questions.q: Which animal uses a long, sticky tongue to slurp up ants?
questions.f: A giant anteater can eat tens of thousands of ants in a single day.

questions.q: Which of these animals lays eggs but is a mammal?
questions.f: The platypus is one of the very few mammals that lays eggs.

questions.q: What do we call an animal awake at night and asleep by day?
questions.f: Nocturnal animals like owls have big eyes to see in the dark.

questions.q: True or False: A group of fish is called a school.
questions.f: Fish swim in schools to confuse predators and find food together.

questions.q: Which black-and-white animal eats mostly bamboo?
questions.f: A giant panda can eat bamboo for up to 14 hours a day.

questions.q: What is a baby horse called?
questions.f: A foal can stand and walk within a couple of hours of being born.

questions.q: True or False: Spiders are insects.
questions.f: Spiders are arachnids with eight legs; insects have only six.

questions.q: Which giant reptile lives in rivers and has a powerful bite?
questions.f: Crocodiles have the strongest bite of any animal alive today.

questions.q: Which animal is known for stinging and buzzing near flowers?
questions.f: Bees help flowers grow fruit by carrying pollen from bloom to bloom.

questions.q: What do we call an animal with a backbone?
questions.f: Fish, birds, reptiles, and mammals are all vertebrates with backbones.

questions.q: True or False: Owls can turn their heads in a full circle.
questions.f: Owls turn their heads about 270 degrees, but not all the way around.

questions.q: Which sea creature is known for pinching with two big claws?
questions.f: Crabs walk sideways because of the way their leg joints bend.

questions.q: Which African animal has black and white stripes?
questions.f: No two zebras have exactly the same stripe pattern.

questions.q: What is a group of birds flying together called?
questions.f: Birds fly in flocks to stay safe and save energy on long trips.

questions.q: Which animal is the national animal of India?
questions.f: The Bengal tiger became India's national animal in 1973.

questions.q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.f: Two octopus hearts pump blood to the gills and one to the rest of the body.

questions.q: What color is an octopus's blood?
questions.f: Octopus blood is blue because it uses copper, not iron, to carry oxygen.

questions.q: Which amphibian can regrow lost legs and even parts of its heart?
questions.f: The axolotl is a Mexican salamander that stays a 'baby' its whole life.

questions.q: How do geckos walk upside down on ceilings?
questions.f: Gecko toes have millions of tiny hairs that grip using microscopic forces.

questions.q: Which insect can lift about 50 times its own body weight?
questions.f: An ant lifting 50 times its weight is like you lifting a small truck.

questions.q: About how long can a giant tortoise live?
questions.f: Some giant tortoises have lived over 150 years, longer than any human.

questions.q: Which bird lays the largest egg of any living animal?
questions.f: One ostrich egg weighs about as much as two dozen chicken eggs.

questions.q: How many bones does a snake's body roughly contain?
questions.f: A snake's long backbone can have hundreds of vertebrae and ribs.

questions.q: Which animal has a tongue that can be longer than its own body?
questions.f: A chameleon's tongue rockets out to snatch insects in a flash.

questions.q: True or False: A cockroach dies instantly if it loses its head.
questions.f: A headless cockroach can survive a while, breathing through tiny body holes.

questions.q: Which mammal is famous for migrating thousands of kilometres in herds?
questions.f: Over a million wildebeest cross Africa's plains each year for fresh grass.

questions.q: Which animal has fingerprints almost identical to a human's?
questions.f: Koala fingerprints are so human-like they could confuse a crime scene.

questions.q: How many eyes does a honeybee have?
questions.f: A bee has two large eyes plus three tiny eyes on top of its head.

questions.q: Which sea animal can turn nearly transparent to hide?
questions.f: Many jellyfish are see-through, making them almost invisible in water.

questions.q: True or False: A hummingbird can fly backwards.
questions.f: Hummingbirds are the only birds able to hover and fly backwards.

questions.q: How does a camel survive so long without drinking water?
c: It stores fat and saves water
questions.f: A camel can drink over 100 litres of water in just a few minutes.

questions.q: Which insect performs a 'waggle dance' to share directions?
questions.f: A bee dances in a figure-eight to tell hive-mates where flowers are.

questions.q: Which arctic animal has clear, hollow hairs that trap heat?
questions.f: Polar bear hairs are hollow tubes that trap warm air near the skin.

questions.q: True or False: An adult elephant cannot jump.
questions.f: An elephant is too heavy to lift all four feet off the ground at once.

questions.q: Which slow rainforest animal can sleep up to 20 hours a day?
questions.f: Sloths move so slowly that green algae can grow on their fur.

questions.q: True or False: Starfish can grow back an arm they have lost.
questions.f: Some starfish can even grow a whole new body from a single lost arm.

questions.q: How does an electric eel catch its food?
questions.f: An electric eel can produce a jolt of about 600 volts to stun prey.

questions.q: Which whale sings long, complicated songs?
questions.f: Humpback songs can last over 20 minutes and travel far underwater.

questions.q: How many stomach chambers does a cow have?
questions.f: A cow's four-part stomach helps it digest tough grass by chewing it twice.

questions.q: Which butterfly migrates thousands of kilometres each year?
questions.f: Monarch butterflies travel from Canada to Mexico across generations.

questions.q: Which animal has the longest migration of any mammal?
questions.f: Gray whales swim about 20,000 km round trip between feeding and breeding areas.

questions.q: Why do flamingos look pink?
questions.f: Flamingos get their pink colour from tiny shrimp and algae they eat.

questions.q: Which of these animals is NOT a mammal?
questions.f: Snakes are reptiles; whales, bats, and dolphins are all mammals.

questions.q: Which animal has the largest brain of any creature on Earth?
questions.f: A sperm whale's brain weighs about 8 kg, five times a human's.

questions.q: Which of these is the fastest animal overall?
questions.f: A diving peregrine falcon reaches over 300 km per hour, faster than any car.

questions.q: Which of these is an amphibian, not a reptile?
questions.f: Amphibians like salamanders have moist skin and begin life in water.

questions.q: Which animal can freeze solid in winter and thaw out alive?
questions.f: The wood frog's body makes a natural antifreeze so ice won't destroy its cells.

questions.q: Which of these animals does NOT hibernate in winter?
questions.f: Wolves stay active all winter, while the others sleep to save energy.

questions.q: Which is the smallest mammal in the world by weight?
questions.f: The bumblebee bat weighs about as much as two paperclips.

questions.q: True or False: A shark is a fish, not a mammal.
questions.f: Sharks are fish that breathe with gills, but their skeletons are made of cartilage.

questions.q: Which of these is the most venomous animal in the sea?
questions.f: The box jellyfish carries enough venom to be one of the ocean's deadliest animals.

questions.q: Which animal's babies are called 'kits'?
questions.f: Baby rabbits are called kits, born hairless with their eyes shut.

questions.q: Which of these animals has the longest lifespan?
questions.f: Greenland sharks can live over 250 years, aging incredibly slowly in cold water.

questions.q: Which bird travels the farthest each year, pole to pole?
questions.f: The Arctic tern flies about 70,000 km a year chasing endless summer.

questions.q: Which animal camouflages by matching the colour of the seafloor?
questions.f: A flounder can change its skin pattern to match sand or gravel below it.

questions.q: True or False: Insects wear their skeleton on the outside.
questions.f: Insects have a hard outer shell called an exoskeleton and must shed it to grow.

questions.q: Which of these animals does NOT lay eggs?
questions.f: Horses give birth to live foals; snakes, ostriches, and frogs all lay eggs.

questions.q: Which reptile can hold its breath underwater for hours while resting?
questions.f: A resting sea turtle can stay underwater for hours before surfacing for air.

questions.q: Which of these snakes is the longest in the world?
questions.f: A reticulated python can grow longer than a school bus, over 6 metres.

questions.q: Which animal changes colour mainly to communicate, not to hide?
questions.f: Cuttlefish flash colours across their skin to signal other cuttlefish.

questions.q: True or False: Octopuses can taste things with their arms.
questions.f: An octopus's suckers can taste whatever they touch, even in the dark.

questions.q: True or False: Poison dart frogs use bright colours to warn predators.
questions.f: Bright warning colours tell predators 'I taste bad or I'm dangerous'.

questions.q: Which of these animals is a marsupial that carries young in a pouch?
questions.f: Wombats have backward-facing pouches so dirt doesn't get in while they dig.

questions.q: Which creature has the most legs of these choices?
questions.f: Despite its name meaning 'thousand feet', most millipedes have a few hundred.

questions.q: Why does a chameleon change colour?
c: Special cells stretch to shift colour
questions.f: Chameleons move tiny crystals in their skin cells to change the light they reflect.

questions.q: How does a snake 'smell' the air around it?
questions.f: A snake's forked tongue collects scent and passes it to a special mouth organ.

questions.q: Why can't most fish survive out of water for long?
c: Their gills need water to get oxygen
questions.f: Gills collapse in air, so a fish suffocates even though oxygen is all around it.

questions.q: What makes a firefly glow at night?
c: A chemical reaction in its body
questions.f: Fireflies mix chemicals to make cold light, a process called bioluminescence.

questions.q: Why do deep-sea anglerfish have a glowing lure on their heads?
c: To attract prey in the dark
questions.f: Glowing bacteria light the lure, drawing curious prey straight to the fish's jaws.

questions.q: True or False: Tardigrades can survive the vacuum of outer space.
questions.f: These tiny 'water bears' survived space by drying out and pausing their life.

questions.q: Why do Arctic hares turn white in winter?
questions.f: A white coat hides the hare against snow so predators can't spot it.

questions.q: Why do migrating birds fly in a V-shape?
c: To save energy in each other's air currents
questions.f: Each bird rides the swirling air off the one ahead, so the flock flies farther.

questions.q: What is the main reason sloths move so slowly?
c: Their leafy diet gives little energy
questions.f: Leaves are so low in energy that sloths move slowly and digest for weeks.

questions.q: True or False: Cold-blooded animals make their own body heat.
questions.f: Cold-blooded animals like reptiles warm up by basking in the sun instead.

questions.q: True or False: Some frogs breathe partly through their skin.
questions.f: Frog skin lets oxygen pass straight into the blood, especially underwater.

questions.q: How do honeybees keep their hive warm in cold weather?
questions.f: Thousands of bees vibrate their muscles to heat the whole hive from within.

questions.q: Why is the axolotl special among animals with backbones?
c: It regrows limbs, organs, and nerves
questions.f: Scientists study axolotls hoping to learn how to help humans heal wounds.

questions.q: How does a rattlesnake sense a warm animal in the dark?
questions.f: Special pits between eye and nostril 'see' the body heat of nearby prey.

questions.q: Why do camels have two rows of long eyelashes?
questions.f: Long lashes plus closable nostrils keep blowing sand out of a camel's face.

questions.q: Which animal has the strongest bite force ever measured?
questions.f: A saltwater crocodile's bite is many times stronger than a lion's.

questions.q: How does a mantis shrimp strike its prey so powerfully?
c: It punches with a spring-loaded claw
questions.f: The mantis shrimp's punch is so fast it boils the water into tiny bubbles.

questions.q: Mixing red and yellow paint makes which color?
questions.f: Orange got its name from the fruit, not the other way around!

questions.q: Mixing blue and yellow paint makes which color?
questions.f: Leaves look green because they bounce green light back to your eyes.

questions.q: Mixing red and blue paint makes which color?
questions.f: Long ago purple dye was so rare only kings and queens could wear it.

questions.q: Mixing black and white paint makes which color?
questions.f: Adding more or less black gives you dozens of different greys.

questions.q: On a clear day, what color is the sky?
questions.f: The sky is blue because tiny bits of air scatter blue sunlight around.

questions.q: Adding white paint to red makes which color?
questions.f: A lighter version of a color is called a 'tint'.

questions.q: A colored wax stick you draw with is a?
questions.f: The biggest crayon ever made was longer than a car!

questions.q: What do painters usually spread paint with?
questions.f: Some brushes are made from just a few animal or plastic hairs.

questions.q: A drawing you make of your own face is a?
questions.f: Van Gogh painted over 30 self-portraits of himself.

questions.q: Soft, earthy material shaped into pots is?
questions.f: Wet clay is squishy, but baking it in a hot oven makes it rock hard.

questions.q: Folding paper into cranes and shapes is called?
questions.f: 'Origami' comes from Japanese words meaning 'folding paper'.

questions.q: A statue you can walk all the way around is a?
questions.f: Sculptures are '3D' art, so you can see them from every side.

questions.q: How many colors are in a rainbow?
questions.f: Remember them with 'ROY G BIV' — red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet.

questions.q: What do you rub on paper to remove pencil marks?
questions.f: The first erasers were made from bread before rubber was used!

questions.q: What tall stand holds an artist's canvas upright?
questions.f: An easel tips back a little so paint doesn't drip down the picture.

questions.q: What color are the sunflowers in Van Gogh's famous painting?
questions.f: Van Gogh loved the color yellow and painted many, many sunflowers.

questions.q: Coal and the night sky are usually what color?
questions.f: Black soaks up almost all the light that hits it.

questions.q: Fresh, clean snow is usually what color?
questions.f: Snow looks white because it bounces back all the colors of light.

questions.q: A painting of hills, trees and fields is called a?
questions.f: A 'seascape' is the same idea but shows the ocean instead.

questions.q: Which of these is a 'warm' color?
questions.f: Warm colors like red and orange remind us of fire and sunshine.

questions.q: Sticky stuff used to join craft paper together is?
questions.f: Some glue is made from boiled-down plants and animal bits!

questions.q: What strong cloth do artists often paint on?
questions.f: The same tough cloth is used to make sturdy shoes and tents.

questions.q: Which of these is used to color in pictures?
questions.f: Colored pencils have soft, waxy 'lead' instead of grey graphite.

questions.q: A flat shape with exactly three sides is a?
questions.f: Artists use triangles to guide your eye around a picture.

questions.q: Mixing lots of different paint colors together usually makes?
questions.f: Each color soaks up some light, so the mix ends up dull and muddy.

questions.q: Art made by gluing paper or fabric scraps together is a?
questions.f: 'Collage' comes from a French word meaning 'to glue'.

questions.q: The flat board where a painter mixes colors is a?
questions.f: A 'color palette' can also mean the set of colors an artist chooses.

questions.q: Red, yellow and blue are the three primary colors of paint.
questions.f: From these three you can mix almost every other color!

questions.q: Purple is one of the primary colors.
questions.f: Purple is a 'secondary' color, made by mixing red and blue.

questions.q: A rainbow always shows its colors in the same order.
questions.f: Red is always on the outside and violet on the inside.

questions.q: Who painted the famous Mona Lisa?
questions.f: Leonardo carried the Mona Lisa around with him for years and never sold it.

questions.q: The Mona Lisa is most famous for her mysterious?
questions.f: Her smile seems to change depending on where you look on her face.

questions.q: Which artist painted many pictures of sunflowers?
questions.f: Van Gogh made a whole series of sunflower paintings to decorate a friend's room.

questions.q: In which country did origami become a famous art?
questions.f: Skilled folders can make a paper crane without any cutting or glue.

questions.q: Rangoli patterns are made on the floor during festivals in?
questions.f: Rangoli is believed to welcome guests and bring good luck.

questions.q: The art of beautiful, fancy handwriting is called?
questions.f: Calligraphers use special pens with flat tips to make thick and thin lines.

questions.q: Mehndi skin designs are drawn using paste from which plant?
questions.f: Henna paste is green but it stains skin a reddish-brown color.

questions.q: The Sistine Chapel ceiling was painted by?
questions.f: He painted it lying on his back on high scaffolding for years.

questions.q: A picture made from tiny colored tiles or glass is a?
questions.f: Ancient Romans covered whole floors in tiny mosaic tiles.

questions.q: Shaping wet clay into bowls on a spinning wheel is called?
questions.f: The spinning 'potter's wheel' is one of the oldest machines in the world.

questions.q: How many primary colors are there for mixing paint?
questions.f: Red, yellow and blue are the three you can't make by mixing others.

questions.q: A painting made on fresh, wet wall plaster is called a?
questions.f: The paint soaks into the wet plaster, so a fresco can last for centuries.

questions.q: The famous statue of David was carved from what stone?
questions.f: Michelangelo's David is over 5 metres tall — taller than three kids stacked up!

questions.q: Which tool do sculptors use to chip away at stone?
questions.f: They tap the chisel with a hammer to break off small stone chips.

questions.q: Paint that mixes with water and looks see-through is?
questions.f: Watercolor is tricky because you usually can't paint over your mistakes.

questions.q: Van Gogh's famous swirly night-sky painting is called?
questions.f: He painted the swirling stars from the view outside his window.

questions.q: Rangoli patterns are often made using colored?
questions.f: Some artists also use flower petals, rice or colored sand.

questions.q: Colors like grey, black and white are called?
questions.f: Neutral colors go well with almost any other color.

questions.q: A soft, chalky stick used for smudgy colored drawings is a?
questions.f: You can blend pastels with your finger to make soft, dreamy pictures.

questions.q: The Japanese art of arranging flowers is called?
questions.f: Ikebana focuses on shape and empty space, not just pretty blooms.

questions.q: Which country is the artist Pablo Picasso from?
questions.f: Picasso could draw beautifully as a young child and made art his whole life.

questions.q: A quick, rough drawing made to plan artwork is a?
questions.f: Artists often fill whole 'sketchbooks' with ideas before painting.

questions.q: The frame-by-frame art that makes cartoons move is?
questions.f: Old cartoons needed thousands of hand-drawn pictures for a few minutes!

questions.q: Which famous Indian building is made of white marble?
questions.f: The marble seems to change color in morning, noon and evening light.

questions.q: A sculpture showing just a person's head and shoulders is a?
questions.f: Ancient Romans made stone busts of their leaders and heroes.

questions.q: Colors opposite each other on the color wheel are called?
questions.f: Complementary colors, like blue and orange, make each other look brighter.

questions.q: Green, orange and purple are called secondary colors.
questions.f: Each one is made by mixing two primary colors together.

questions.q: Leonardo da Vinci also designed machines and studied nature.
questions.f: His notebooks are full of flying machines, bridges and body drawings.

questions.q: Vincent van Gogh became famous mostly after he died.
questions.f: He struggled to sell his art while alive, but now it's worth millions.

questions.q: Black is a color of the rainbow.
questions.f: Black is actually the absence of light, so it's not in a rainbow.

questions.q: How many colors does a standard color wheel usually show?
questions.f: It has primary, secondary and in-between colors arranged in a circle.

questions.q: The Mona Lisa was painted around which time?
questions.f: That makes the painting over 500 years old!

questions.q: About how long did Michelangelo take to paint the Sistine ceiling?
questions.f: He painted over 300 figures on the huge curved ceiling.

questions.q: How many paintings did Van Gogh sell while he was alive?
questions.f: Most people think he sold only one painting before he died.

questions.q: Which ancient people were famous for detailed floor mosaics?
questions.f: Some Roman mosaics used over a million tiny tiles!

questions.q: Animals that blend into their surroundings to hide use?
questions.f: An octopus can change its skin color and pattern in under a second.

questions.q: The three primary colors of LIGHT (red, green, blue) are known as?
questions.f: Your phone and TV screens make every color using tiny red, green and blue lights.

questions.q: Color printers mix cyan, magenta, yellow and black, known as?
questions.f: The 'K' stands for black, the 'key' color that adds shadows.

questions.q: Hokusai's famous 'Great Wave' print shows which mountain?
questions.f: Tiny Mount Fuji sits behind a giant curling wave in the picture.

questions.q: Long ago, precious blue paint was crushed from which stone?
questions.f: This deep blue stone was once ground up and worth more than gold.

questions.q: Early cave artists often drew using burnt wood, called?
questions.f: Some cave paintings are over 30,000 years old and still visible today.

questions.q: A leaf looks green because it reflects green light and absorbs?
questions.f: The green stuff inside leaves, called chlorophyll, soaks up other colors for food.

questions.q: Which famous painting was stolen from the Louvre in 1911?
questions.f: The theft made the Mona Lisa even more famous when it was found two years later.

questions.q: Making parts of a drawing darker to show its shape is called?
questions.f: Good shading can make a flat circle look like a round ball.

questions.q: Tibetan monks make detailed patterns from colored sand called a?
questions.f: They spend days making it, then sweep it away to show nothing lasts forever.

questions.q: On the Sistine ceiling, God reaches out to touch which figure?
questions.f: Their almost-touching fingers are one of the most famous images in art.

questions.q: Terracotta pots and the famous Terracotta Army are made of?
questions.f: China's Terracotta Army has over 8,000 clay soldiers, each with a different face.

questions.q: How many sides does a hexagon, a shape often used in tiling, have?
questions.f: Bees build their honeycomb out of perfect little hexagons.

questions.q: Which artist painted 'Girl with a Pearl Earring'?
questions.f: It's sometimes called the 'Mona Lisa of the North'.

questions.q: A picture made using only shades of a single color is?
questions.f: 'Mono' means one, so monochrome means 'one color'.

questions.q: Which fast-drying paint is very popular in schools and studios?
questions.f: Acrylic paint dries in minutes, while oil paint can take weeks.

questions.q: In pointillism, tiny dots of color blend together in?
questions.f: Step back from the painting and thousands of dots turn into one clear picture.

questions.q: Which Indian festival is famous for throwing colored powder?
questions.f: Holi is often called the 'festival of colors' and welcomes spring.

questions.q: Art sprayed or painted on public walls, like by Banksy, is?
questions.f: Banksy is so mysterious that no one knows for sure who the artist really is.

questions.q: The color red can make people feel excited or hungry.
questions.f: That's one reason so many food restaurants use red in their signs.

questions.q: A chameleon can change the color of its skin.
questions.f: It shifts color to hide, to warm up, and even to show its mood.

questions.q: The sky looks blue because sunlight scatters in the air.
questions.f: Blue light bounces around the most, so it reaches your eyes from all over.

questions.q: Warm colors like red and orange remind many people of fire.
questions.f: Cool colors like blue and green remind us of water and grass instead.

questions.q: Which of these artists is famous for Cubism and blocky shapes?
questions.f: In Cubist art, a face might show the front and side at the same time.

questions.q: Which of these was created FIRST in history?
questions.f: Egyptians decorated tombs thousands of years before the other three existed.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a way to make a sculpture?
questions.f: Sketching is drawing on a flat surface, not making a 3D shape.

questions.q: Which pair of colors are complementary (opposite on the wheel)?
questions.f: Sports teams and posters often pair opposites to really grab your eye.

questions.q: Mixing red light and blue light makes which color?
questions.f: Mixing colored light works differently than mixing colored paint.

questions.q: Which famous artwork is a SCULPTURE, not a painting?
questions.f: 'The Thinker' is a bronze statue of a man deep in thought.

questions.q: Which artist is famous for melting clocks in dreamlike scenes?
questions.f: Dali's art belongs to a strange, dreamy style called Surrealism.

questions.q: Making prints by carving a picture into wood is called?
questions.f: You carve the design, add ink, then press paper on top to print it.

questions.q: Which country is famous for delicate blue-and-white porcelain?
questions.f: This fine pottery was so prized that we still call dishes 'china'.

questions.q: Which art uses a needle and thread to make pictures on cloth?
questions.f: Some huge embroidered cloths tell entire stories with stitches.

questions.q: Which artist is famous for giant close-up flower paintings?
questions.f: She painted flowers so big they filled the whole canvas.

questions.q: Which of these took far longer to create?
questions.f: Michelangelo spent about four years on the ceiling alone.

questions.q: A mural is a large painting made where?
questions.f: Some city murals are taller than a whole building.

questions.q: Which South Indian art uses white rice-flour patterns at doorways?
questions.f: People draw fresh kolam patterns on the ground each morning.

questions.q: In printmaking, which tool rolls ink onto a surface?
questions.f: A brayer is a little roller that spreads a thin, even layer of ink.

questions.q: Which Paris museum displays the Mona Lisa?
questions.f: The Louvre is so big it would take days to see every artwork inside.

questions.q: Which style of Aboriginal Australian art uses patterns of dots?
questions.f: The dot patterns often tell stories about land, animals and ancestors.

questions.q: Which is usually the tallest kind of artwork?
questions.f: The Statue of Unity in India is taller than a 50-storey building.

questions.q: Adding a color's complement (opposite) can make it look duller.
questions.f: Mixing opposite colors together often makes a muddy grey-brown.

questions.q: Michelangelo was a sculptor as well as a painter.
questions.f: He actually saw himself as a sculptor first, and painting second.

questions.q: Abstract art always shows real objects very clearly.
questions.f: Abstract art uses shapes and colors instead of showing real things.

questions.q: The color wheel can be split into warm colors and cool colors.
questions.f: Reds and oranges feel warm, while blues and greens feel cool.

questions.q: Why does the daytime sky look blue?
c: Blue light scatters most in the air
questions.f: Air scatters blue light in every direction, filling the whole sky with blue.

questions.q: Why does a red apple look red to your eyes?
c: It reflects red light and absorbs the rest
It is covered in red paint
questions.f: Objects don't 'have' color — they just bounce certain colors of light to you.

questions.q: The most expensive painting ever sold is a Leonardo work called?
questions.f: It sold for about 450 million dollars in 2017.

questions.q: Why do colors look duller the more paints you mix together?
questions.f: Each color soaks up some light, so a big mix reflects very little and looks muddy.

questions.q: The artist's technique of strong light and deep shadow is called?
questions.f: The word is Italian for 'light-dark' and makes paintings look dramatic.

questions.q: Why do sunsets often look red and orange?
c: The blue light has scattered away
questions.f: At sunset light travels through more air, so the blue is scattered out first.

questions.q: What does 'perspective' help an artist show on flat paper?
questions.f: Lines that meet at a faraway point make a road look like it stretches for miles.

questions.q: Which is the oldest known form of human art?
questions.f: Some cave paintings of animals are more than 30,000 years old.

questions.q: In art, what is 'negative space'?
questions.f: Clever artists shape the empty space to hide a second picture inside.

questions.q: The 'Great Wave' and other Japanese prints were made using carved?
questions.f: A different carved block was used for each color in the print.

questions.q: Which blue pigment was once more precious than gold?
questions.f: Made from lapis lazuli stone, it was saved for the most important paintings.

questions.q: Why do stained-glass windows glow with color in sunlight?
c: Colored glass lets only some colors through
questions.f: Each piece of colored glass filters the sunlight passing through it.

questions.q: Art made to trick your eye into seeing something real is called?
questions.f: The French name means 'deceive the eye' — some look like real 3D objects!

questions.q: Which artist is famous for dripping and splashing paint onto huge canvases?
questions.f: He laid the canvas on the floor and flung paint from all sides.

questions.q: Why do many animals use camouflage colors and patterns?
questions.f: A hidden animal can sneak up on its food or escape becoming food itself.

questions.q: What is a 'fresco'?
c: A painting on fresh wet plaster
questions.f: The color sinks into the drying plaster and becomes part of the wall.

questions.q: A painting of objects like fruit, flowers or bowls is called a?
questions.f: 'Still life' art shows things that stay still, unlike people or animals.

questions.q: White light is made of all the rainbow colors mixed together.
questions.f: A glass prism can split white light back into a rainbow.

questions.q: Impressionist painters used small strokes to capture light.
questions.f: Monet painted the same haystacks again and again as the light changed.

questions.q: Placing complementary colors side by side makes each look brighter.
questions.f: Artists use this trick to make one part of a painting really jump out.

questions.q: How many lungs does a person have?
questions.f: Your two lungs sit in your chest and fill up like balloons every time you breathe in.

questions.q: What is the gooey stuff that comes out of your nose called?
questions.f: Snot is sticky on purpose so it can trap dust and germs before they reach your lungs.

questions.q: What salty liquid appears on your skin when you get hot?
questions.f: Sweat cools you down by carrying heat away as it dries on your skin.

questions.q: Which body part do you use to smell a flower?
questions.f: Your nose can tell apart thousands of different smells.

questions.q: Which curved bones form a cage around your heart and lungs?
questions.f: You have twelve pairs of ribs curving around your chest like a bony cage.

questions.q: What grows on the top of your head?
questions.f: Each hair grows for a few years, then rests and falls out to make room for a new one.

questions.q: Which joint lets you bend your arm in the middle?
questions.f: Bumping your elbow can give a funny tingly zap people call hitting your funny bone.

questions.q: What colour is human blood inside your body?
questions.f: Blood can look blue through your skin, but it is always red inside you.

questions.q: How many senses does a human have?
questions.f: The five senses are sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.

questions.q: Which organ pumps blood all around your body?
questions.f: Your heart squeezes tight to push blood around your whole body without ever taking a break.

questions.q: True or False: Your skin is the largest organ of your body.
questions.f: Your skin is your biggest organ, growing all over you like a stretchy waterproof coat.

questions.q: What do you mainly use your eyes for?
questions.f: You blink about fifteen times a minute to keep your eyes clean and wet.

questions.q: What are the swirly patterns on your fingertips called?
questions.f: No two people in the whole world have exactly the same fingerprints.

questions.q: Which bone protects your brain like a helmet?
questions.f: Your skull is made of bony plates that lock together to keep your brain safe.

questions.q: What covers the outside of your whole body?
questions.f: You shed tiny skin flakes all day, and a lot of house dust is really old skin!

questions.q: True or False: You taste food only with your teeth.
questions.f: You taste food with thousands of tiny taste buds on your tongue, not your teeth.

questions.q: What do your teeth help you do to your food?
questions.f: Your teeth chew food into small mushy bits so your tummy can break it down more easily.

questions.q: Which part of your body do you use to hear music?
questions.f: Your ears do two jobs at once: they help you hear and help you balance.

questions.q: What comes out of your eyes when you cry?
questions.f: Tears keep your eyes clean and washed, and you make them even when you are not sad.

questions.q: What happens to your chest when you breathe in air?
questions.f: Your lungs fill with air like balloons, so your whole chest puffs up bigger.

questions.q: True or False: Your heart is roughly the size of your own fist.
questions.f: Make a fist and that is about how big your busy little heart is.

questions.q: What is the wet, sticky liquid inside your mouth called?
questions.f: You make enough spit each day to fill about six drinking glasses.

questions.q: Which body part bends so you can sit down?
questions.f: Your knee is the biggest joint in your whole body.

questions.q: What do you suddenly make when dust tickles your nose?
questions.f: A sneeze can blast air out of your nose faster than a car drives on a motorway.

questions.q: How many toes does a person usually have in total?
questions.f: Your toes help you balance and push off the ground when you walk and run.

questions.q: What is the soft pink muscle that helps you taste and talk?
questions.f: Your tongue is really a bundle of muscles working together.

questions.q: True or False: The hair on your head keeps growing longer over time.
questions.f: Head hair grows about a centimetre each month, which adds up over a whole year.

questions.q: Which part of your hand helps you grip, one on each hand?
questions.f: Your thumb can touch every finger, which helps you hold pencils and open jars.

questions.q: What do we call the little hairs sitting above your eyes?
questions.f: Eyebrows help stop sweat and rain from dripping straight into your eyes.

questions.q: What do your eyes do when you blink?
questions.f: Blinking spreads a thin layer of tears to keep your eyes wet and comfy.

questions.q: How many bones does a grown-up human have?
questions.f: Over half of all your bones are found in your hands and feet.

questions.q: What is the yellowish gunk that forms inside your ears?
questions.f: Earwax is helpful because it traps dirt and keeps tiny bugs out of your ears.

questions.q: True or False: A baby is born with more bones than a grown-up.
questions.f: Babies have about 300 bones, and many join together as they grow up.

questions.q: What is the tube called that carries air down to your lungs?
questions.f: Your windpipe has bendy rings that keep it open like a vacuum hose.

questions.q: What are your hair and fingernails both mostly made of?
questions.f: Keratin is the same tough stuff that makes up a rhino's horn.

questions.q: How many teeth are in a full set of adult teeth?
questions.f: The last four adult teeth, called wisdom teeth, often appear when you are almost grown.

questions.q: Which sense lets you feel if something is hot, cold or fluffy?
questions.f: Your skin is packed with tiny sensors that feel the world all around you.

questions.q: What do your kidneys make from the waste in your blood?
questions.f: Your two kidneys clean your whole blood supply many times every single day.

questions.q: What is the food pipe called that runs from your mouth to your stomach?
questions.f: Muscles squeeze the food down your gullet, so you could even swallow upside down.

questions.q: True or False: It is almost impossible to tickle yourself.
questions.f: Your brain knows the tickle is coming and cancels the surprise, so it does not work.

questions.q: How many baby teeth does a young child usually grow?
questions.f: Baby teeth are also called milk teeth, and they fall out to make room for adult ones.

questions.q: Which dome-shaped muscle under your lungs helps you breathe?
questions.f: When your diaphragm pulls down, air rushes in to fill your lungs.

questions.q: What is the hard white coating on the outside of a tooth?
questions.f: Enamel is the toughest material your body makes, which is why teeth can crunch hard food.

questions.q: How many chambers, or rooms, does your heart have?
questions.f: Your heart is really two pumps side by side, each with two rooms.

questions.q: True or False: Your nose and ears keep changing shape as you get older.
questions.f: They are made of soft cartilage, which slowly droops and grows over the years.

questions.q: What are the tiny bumps on your tongue that sense flavour called?
questions.f: You have thousands of taste buds, and they can pick out sweet, sour, salty and bitter.

questions.q: What is the bendy row of bones running down your back called?
questions.f: Your spine is made of many small bones stacked like beads, so your back can bend and twist.

questions.q: Which organ do you use to think, remember and dream?
questions.f: Your brain feels a bit like squishy jelly if you could hold it.

questions.q: What is the red liquid that carries oxygen around your body?
questions.f: An adult has about five litres of blood, enough to fill a big drink bottle a few times.

questions.q: Which coloured part of your eye can be brown, blue or green?
questions.f: The iris is a ring of muscle that opens and closes to control how much light gets in.

questions.q: True or False: Bones are alive and can slowly heal after they break.
questions.f: Bones are living tissue, so a cracked bone can knit itself back together over weeks.

questions.q: What is the medical name for your voice box in your throat?
questions.f: Air passing over stretchy folds in your larynx makes the sounds of your voice.

questions.q: Which vitamin does your skin make when sunlight touches it?
questions.f: Vitamin D helps keep your bones strong, and a little sunshine helps your body make it.

questions.q: What are the 20 first teeth that later fall out called?
questions.f: Milk teeth get wobbly and drop out as the bigger adult teeth push up underneath.

questions.q: Which pair of organs clean your blood and make urine?
questions.f: Each kidney is about the size of your fist and works like a busy filter.

questions.q: Which lung is a little smaller to leave room for your heart?
questions.f: Your heart tucks into the left side of your chest, so the left lung is the smaller one.

questions.q: What do we call the place where two bones meet and can move?
questions.f: Your knees, elbows and knuckles are all joints that let your body bend.

questions.q: What is the soft jelly inside your bones that makes blood cells?
questions.f: Deep inside your bones, marrow makes millions of fresh blood cells every second.

questions.q: Which body part sends fast messages, working like tiny wires?
questions.f: Nerves carry signals between your brain and the rest of your body at amazing speed.

questions.q: About how many muscles does the human body have?
questions.f: Your muscles make up almost half of your whole body weight.

questions.q: What is the longest bone in the human body?
questions.f: The thigh bone, or femur, is so strong it can hold more weight than concrete.

questions.q: About how many times does a resting heart beat each day?
questions.f: Over a lifetime your heart beats more than two billion times.

questions.q: What is the smallest bone in your body, hidden inside the ear?
questions.f: The stirrup bone is roughly the size of a single grain of rice.

questions.q: Which part of your eye opens wider in the dark to let in light?
questions.f: Your pupil is really a hole, and it grows bigger so you can see in dim light.

questions.q: True or False: Your fingernails grow faster than your toenails.
questions.f: Fingernails grow about twice as fast, partly because your hands move around so much.

questions.q: Which thin skin inside your ear vibrates when sound hits it?
questions.f: Your eardrum shivers like a tiny drum skin whenever sound waves bump into it.

questions.q: How many bones are packed into each of your feet?
questions.f: Your two feet together hold about a quarter of all the bones in your body.

questions.q: Which gas do red blood cells carry from your lungs to your body?
questions.f: Red blood cells act like delivery trucks, dropping off oxygen everywhere it is needed.

questions.q: What causes hiccups inside your body?
questions.f: Hiccups come from the diaphragm under your lungs twitching suddenly and snapping shut.

questions.q: Where inside your body are new blood cells made?
questions.f: Soft marrow deep in your bones churns out fresh blood cells all the time.

questions.q: True or False: The stirrup bone in your ear is the largest bone in your body.
questions.f: It is actually the smallest bone, tinier than a grain of rice; the thigh bone is the biggest.

questions.q: How much blood does a grown-up body hold, roughly?
questions.f: That is enough blood to fill a big drink bottle about a dozen times over.

questions.q: Which part of your brain sits at the back and keeps you balanced?
questions.f: The cerebellum fine-tunes every step you take so you do not topple over.

questions.q: What are the millions of tiny air sacs in your lungs called?
questions.f: These little balloon-like sacs give your lungs a huge area to soak up oxygen.

questions.q: How fast do nerve signals zoom toward your brain?
questions.f: Signals can race along your nerves at over a hundred metres every second.

questions.q: True or False: More than half your bones are in your hands and feet.
questions.f: Your hands and feet together hold about 106 of your 206 bones.

questions.q: Which blood vessels carry blood away from your heart?
questions.f: Arteries carry blood away from the heart, while veins bring it back again.

questions.q: How long is your small intestine when it is stretched out?
questions.f: Even though it is called small, it is far longer than the large intestine; it is just thinner.

questions.q: What liquid in your stomach helps break down the food you eat?
questions.f: Stomach acid is so strong it could dissolve metal, but a slimy lining keeps you safe.

questions.q: Which sense is closely linked to taste and makes food flavourful?
questions.f: Block your nose and food tastes boring, because much of flavour actually comes from smell.

questions.q: True or False: You blink around fifteen times every minute.
questions.f: That adds up to thousands of blinks a day, each one giving your eyes a quick wash.

questions.q: What is the natural pigment that gives skin and hair their colour?
questions.f: Melanin also acts like a built-in sunscreen against harmful rays.

questions.q: How many pairs of ribs does a typical person have?
questions.f: Your ribs curve round to protect your heart and lungs like a bony cage.

questions.q: Which large organ cleans your blood and does over 500 jobs?
questions.f: The liver is your body's busy chemical factory, even helping turn food into energy.

questions.q: What are the tubes called that carry blood back to your heart?
questions.f: Veins often look blue through your skin, but the blood inside is still red.

questions.q: What are the billions of message-carrying cells in your brain called?
questions.f: Your brain has tens of billions of neurons wiring your thoughts together.

questions.q: About how many times do you breathe in and out each day?
questions.f: You breathe without thinking about it, even while you are fast asleep.

questions.q: What is the soft, bendy tissue in your ears and nose tip called?
questions.f: Cartilage is rubbery and smooth, and it also cushions the ends of your bones.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the five main senses?
questions.f: Balance is handled deep inside your ears, but it is not counted as one of the five main senses.

questions.q: Which of these body parts contains the most bones?
questions.f: Each hand has 27 bones, which is why you can do tiny, careful jobs like tying a knot.

questions.q: Do you have more muscles or more bones in your body?
questions.f: You have around 600 muscles but only 206 bones, so muscles win easily.

questions.q: Which of these body parts is made of bendy cartilage, NOT hard bone?
questions.f: The bendy tip of your nose is made of the same rubbery stuff as your ears.

questions.q: True or False: Sharks have skeletons made of cartilage, not bone.
questions.f: A shark's whole skeleton is bendy cartilage, the same soft stuff that shapes your ears.

questions.q: Which of these travels around your body the fastest?
questions.f: Nerve signals zoom faster than a racing car, while food takes hours to digest.

questions.q: Which of these body parts keeps slowly growing your entire life?
questions.f: The soft cartilage in your ears and nose makes them droop and grow as you age.

questions.q: Which of these carries oxygen-rich blood away from the heart?
questions.f: The body's biggest artery, the aorta, is about as wide as a garden hose.

questions.q: True or False: You have more muscles in your body than bones.
questions.f: Around 600 muscles beat 206 bones, and it takes many muscles just to smile.

questions.q: Which of these organs does NOT help you breathe?
questions.f: The stomach handles food, while the lungs, windpipe and diaphragm all work together for breathing.

questions.q: What happens FIRST when you eat a meal?
questions.f: Digestion starts the moment you chew, as spit begins breaking food down in your mouth.

questions.q: Which is longer when stretched out, your small or large intestine?
questions.f: The small intestine is about 6 metres long, far longer than the large one; it is just narrower.

questions.q: True or False: Lined up end to end, your blood vessels would stretch about 100,000 kilometres.
questions.f: That is long enough to wrap around the whole Earth roughly two and a half times.

questions.q: Which of these usually heals the fastest?
questions.f: The mouth heals quickly because saliva keeps it clean and blood flows to it richly.

questions.q: Which of these grows about twice as fast as the others?
questions.f: Your fingernails race ahead, especially on the hand you use most.

questions.q: Which body system removes waste from your blood as urine?
questions.f: Your kidneys, the stars of the urinary system, filter your blood around the clock.

questions.q: Which of these can you NOT do at the same time as swallowing?
questions.f: A little flap closes your windpipe as you swallow, so food goes down the right tube.

questions.q: Which sense takes up the largest share of your brain's attention?
questions.f: A huge chunk of your brain works just to turn light into the pictures you see.

questions.q: Which of these body parts has the thickest skin?
questions.f: The thick skin on your soles cushions your body's weight every time you walk or jump.

questions.q: True or False: Your funny bone is actually a nerve, not a bone.
questions.f: Banging your elbow zaps the ulnar nerve, giving that weird tingly funny-bone feeling.

questions.q: For its size, which is the strongest muscle in the human body?
questions.f: The jaw's chewing muscle can clench your back teeth with a surprisingly huge force.

questions.q: Why does your skin turn darker after time in the sun?
c: It makes more melanin to protect you
questions.f: Melanin is a natural pigment that acts like built-in sunscreen against harmful rays.

questions.q: True or False: The spot called the funny bone is really the ulnar nerve.
questions.f: There is no funny bone at all; the tingle comes from squashing a nerve near your elbow.

questions.q: Why do you get goosebumps when you feel cold?
c: Tiny muscles pull your hairs upright
questions.f: Goosebumps are left over from furry ancestors, whose raised hair trapped warm air.

questions.q: Why does a doctor hear a lub-dub when listening to your heart?
questions.f: The lub-dub is little doors called valves slamming shut to stop blood flowing backwards.

questions.q: What causes brain freeze when you eat ice cream too fast?
c: Cold on the roof of your mouth
questions.f: Cold on the roof of your mouth confuses nearby nerves, so your brain thinks your forehead hurts.

questions.q: True or False: Your body makes millions of new blood cells every second.
questions.f: Bone marrow works nonstop, replacing worn-out blood cells almost as fast as they wear out.

questions.q: Why can you still feel your way around a pitch-black room?
questions.f: Your skin is packed with millions of touch sensors that feel shape, pressure and warmth.

questions.q: Why do you shiver when you get very cold?
c: Muscles shake fast to make heat
questions.f: Shivering is your muscles quivering quickly to warm your body back up.

questions.q: Which part of the brain controls automatic jobs like your heartbeat?
questions.f: The brain stem quietly runs your breathing and heartbeat so you never have to think about them.

questions.q: True or False: Red blood cells have no centre, leaving more room for oxygen.
questions.f: Losing their nucleus lets red blood cells carry even more oxygen around your body.

questions.q: Why do your muscles ache after lots of hard exercise?
questions.f: Working muscles make lactic acid, which can leave them feeling tired and sore for a while.

questions.q: Why do people yawn, according to one leading idea?
c: To cool the brain and take in air
questions.f: Scientists think a big yawn helps cool your brain and pull in a fresh gulp of air.

questions.q: What makes a sneeze burst out of your nose so fast?
c: Air rushing to clear your nose
questions.f: A sneeze is a powerful puff of air blasting out dust and germs from your nose.

questions.q: True or False: Smells can suddenly bring back strong old memories.
questions.f: The smell part of your brain sits right next to the memory part, so scents can whisk you back in time.

questions.q: Why do your ears sometimes pop on an aeroplane?
c: Air pressure changes on your eardrum
questions.f: As the plane climbs, changing air pressure tugs your eardrum until it pops back level.

questions.q: What is the body process that releases energy from food inside your cells?
questions.f: Cell respiration uses oxygen to unlock energy from food, powering everything you do.

questions.q: Why does a scab form over a cut as it heals?
c: Blood clots to seal the cut
questions.f: Tiny cells called platelets make the blood clot, plugging the cut like a natural plaster.

questions.q: Why do your pupils shrink in bright light?
c: To protect the eye and see clearly
questions.f: Shrinking the pupil lets in less light, keeping your view sharp and your eye comfy.

questions.q: Why is bone marrow so important for keeping you alive?
questions.f: Without marrow making fresh blood cells, your body could not carry oxygen or fight germs.

questions.q: How many wings does a bird have?
questions.f: Birds have two wings, which they flap to lift themselves into the air.

questions.q: What are birds' bodies covered in?
questions.f: Feathers keep birds warm, dry, and light enough to fly.

questions.q: Where do most birds lay their eggs?
questions.f: Birds build cosy nests to keep their eggs safe and warm.

questions.q: What do baby birds hatch from?
questions.f: Every bird begins life curled up inside an egg.

questions.q: What body part do birds flap to fly?
questions.f: Birds push against the air with their wings to stay up.

questions.q: Which bird is famous for hooting at night?
questions.f: Owls are night hunters and call 'hoot-hoot' in the dark.

questions.q: Which bird can be taught to say words?
questions.f: Parrots can copy human speech and other sounds they hear.

questions.q: What do we call a baby chicken?
questions.f: A baby chicken is called a chick, and it says 'cheep'.

questions.q: Which big bird cannot fly but runs fast?
questions.f: The ostrich is too heavy to fly, so it runs on powerful legs.

questions.q: What do birds use to peck their food?
questions.f: Birds have no teeth; they grab and crack food with a beak.

questions.q: Which pink bird often stands on one leg?
questions.f: Flamingos rest on one leg to keep the other warm and save energy.

questions.q: True or False: A peacock can fan out a huge tail of colourful feathers.
questions.f: A male peacock spreads a shimmering fan of feathers to impress peahens.

questions.q: Which bird goes 'quack'?
questions.f: Ducks quack, and their oily feathers keep them dry on water.

questions.q: Which white bird glides gracefully on lakes?
questions.f: Swans are large white water birds with very long, curved necks.

questions.q: How many legs does an insect have?
questions.f: Every insect has six legs, arranged in three matching pairs.

questions.q: How many legs does a spider have?
questions.f: A spider has eight legs, two more than any insect.

questions.q: True or False: Bees make honey from flower nectar.
questions.f: Bees gather sweet nectar and turn it into honey inside the hive.

questions.q: Which wriggly creature turns into a butterfly?
questions.f: A hungry caterpillar changes completely to become a butterfly.

questions.q: What does a spider spin to catch prey?
questions.f: Spiders spin sticky silk webs to trap insects for food.

questions.q: True or False: A ladybird is a type of beetle.
questions.f: Ladybirds are small beetles, and their bright spots warn birds away.

questions.q: Which insects live together in a hive?
questions.f: Thousands of bees share one hive and work together as a team.

questions.q: Which tiny insects often march in long lines?
questions.f: Ants follow scent trails, so they line up nose to tail.

questions.q: What do butterflies drink from flowers?
questions.f: Butterflies sip sugary nectar through a long, straw-like tongue.

questions.q: Which insect can flash light in the dark?
questions.f: Fireflies glow in their bellies to send signals to each other.

questions.q: Which insect zips over ponds with a long thin body?
questions.f: Dragonflies are speedy hunters that patrol above the water.

questions.q: Which insect jumps far using strong back legs?
questions.f: A grasshopper can leap many times the length of its own body.

questions.q: Which insect buzzes near your ear at night?
questions.f: Mosquitoes buzz with fast-beating wings while looking for a meal.

questions.q: True or False: Spiders have eight legs.
questions.f: Spiders always have eight legs, which is how we tell them from insects.

questions.q: Which insect chirps loudly on warm nights?
questions.f: Male crickets chirp by rubbing their wings together.

questions.q: Which is the largest living bird?
questions.f: The ostrich can stand taller than a person and weigh over 100 kg.

questions.q: Which bird can hover and even fly backwards?
questions.f: Hummingbirds beat their wings so fast they can hover like helicopters.

questions.q: What is a bird's long yearly journey to warmer places called?
questions.f: Migration lets birds follow food and warmth across the seasons.

questions.q: Where do most penguins live?
questions.f: Most penguins live in the icy south; none live at the North Pole.

questions.q: What do penguins mainly eat?
questions.f: Penguins dive to catch fish, squid, and tiny shrimp called krill.

questions.q: Which bird of prey is famous for very sharp eyesight?
questions.f: An eagle can spot a rabbit from far up in the sky.

questions.q: Which large flightless bird lives in Australia?
questions.f: The emu is Australia's biggest bird and cannot fly.

questions.q: Which bird can turn its head almost all the way around?
questions.f: Owls can twist their necks about 270 degrees to look behind them.

questions.q: Which bird pecks holes in tree trunks?
questions.f: Woodpeckers drum on trees to find insects hiding under the bark.

questions.q: What do we call a group of geese flying together?
questions.f: Geese fly in a V-shaped flock to save energy on long trips.

questions.q: Which colourful bird has a huge beak in rainforests?
questions.f: A toucan's giant beak is light and helps it reach faraway fruit.

questions.q: Which bird lays its eggs in other birds' nests?
questions.f: The cuckoo tricks other birds into raising its chicks for it.

questions.q: True or False: Penguins can fly through the air.
questions.f: Penguins cannot fly, but they use their wings to 'fly' underwater.

questions.q: Which body feature makes birds light enough to fly?
questions.f: Many bird bones are hollow, saving weight for easier flight.

questions.q: Which bird is often kept on farms to lay eggs?
questions.f: A hen can lay an egg almost every single day.

questions.q: How many main body parts does an insect have?
questions.f: Insects have a head, a middle (thorax), and a back part (abdomen).

questions.q: What do we call a butterfly's resting stage inside a case?
questions.f: Inside its chrysalis, a caterpillar rebuilds itself into a butterfly.

questions.q: Which insect group has the most species on Earth?
questions.f: There are over 350,000 kinds of beetle, more than any other animal.

questions.q: What yellow dust do bees carry from flower to flower?
questions.f: By moving pollen, bees help flowers make seeds and fruit.

questions.q: Which insect can carry things many times its own weight?
questions.f: An ant can lift objects around 50 times heavier than itself.

questions.q: In a beehive, who lays all the eggs?
questions.f: One queen bee can lay up to 2,000 eggs in a single day.

questions.q: True or False: Dragonflies catch other insects in mid-air.
questions.f: Dragonflies are expert flyers that snatch prey while zooming along.

questions.q: What do most caterpillars eat?
questions.f: Caterpillars munch leaves nonstop to grow fast before changing.

questions.q: Which insect spins silk people use to make cloth?
questions.f: Silkworms wrap themselves in one long silk thread to make a cocoon.

questions.q: True or False: A honeybee can sting many times without being harmed.
questions.f: A honeybee's stinger is barbed, so it can sting only once.

questions.q: How many wings does a honeybee have?
questions.f: A bee has four wings that hook together to beat as one pair.

questions.q: True or False: A spider is a kind of insect.
questions.f: Spiders are arachnids; they have eight legs and no wings or antennae.

questions.q: Which beetle rolls balls of animal dung?
questions.f: Dung beetles roll poop into balls to eat and to feed their young.

questions.q: What do we call a large family of ants living together?
questions.f: An ant colony can hold millions of ants all working as one.

questions.q: Which insect's baby is called a maggot?
questions.f: A maggot is the young larva of a fly before it grows wings.

questions.q: How fast can a peregrine falcon dive?
questions.f: Diving over 300 km/h, the peregrine is the fastest animal on Earth.

questions.q: About how many times per second can a hummingbird beat its wings?
questions.f: Their wings blur at around 50 beats a second, making a humming sound.

questions.q: Which is the largest species of penguin?
questions.f: Emperor penguins can stand over one metre tall on the Antarctic ice.

questions.q: Which bird has the largest wingspan of any living bird?
questions.f: An albatross's wings can stretch about 3.5 metres, wider than a car.

questions.q: An ostrich egg weighs about the same as how many chicken eggs?
questions.f: An ostrich egg is the biggest egg laid by any living bird today.

questions.q: The Arctic tern is famous for what amazing feat?
questions.f: Arctic terns fly pole to pole each year, about 70,000 km round trip.

questions.q: How fast can an ostrich run on land?
questions.f: Long, springy legs let an ostrich sprint faster than a racehorse.

questions.q: True or False: Emperor penguins can dive deeper than 500 metres.
questions.f: Emperor penguins dive over 500 m and hold their breath for many minutes.

questions.q: How do penguins keep their feathers waterproof?
questions.f: Penguins comb oil from a special gland through their feathers to stay dry.

questions.q: How do migrating birds often find their way?
questions.f: Birds read the Sun, stars, and even Earth's magnetic field to navigate.

questions.q: Which bird's heart can beat over 1000 times a minute?
questions.f: A hummingbird's tiny heart races to power its super-fast wings.

questions.q: What do we call the hard tip a chick uses to break its shell?
questions.f: Chicks are born with an egg tooth that drops off soon after hatching.

questions.q: Which bird of prey snatches fish by diving feet-first into water?
questions.f: Ospreys have spiky feet that grip slippery fish tightly.

questions.q: How many eyes do most spiders have?
questions.f: Most spiders have eight eyes, yet many still see quite poorly.

questions.q: How many stages are in a butterfly's life cycle?
questions.f: Egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, then adult: four amazing steps.

questions.q: How does a honeybee tell others where to find flowers?
questions.f: A dancing bee wiggles to show the direction and distance to food.

questions.q: How many spots does a common seven-spot ladybird have?
questions.f: Its name gives it away: this ladybird wears exactly seven black spots.

questions.q: How do ants leave a path for others to follow?
questions.f: Ants lay down smelly chemicals called pheromones to mark the way.

questions.q: True or False: For its weight, spider silk is stronger than steel.
questions.f: Spider silk is amazingly tough, yet lighter than a strand of hair.

questions.q: Where does a butterfly taste its food?
questions.f: Butterflies have taste sensors on their feet to check if a plant is good.

questions.q: How does a grasshopper make its chirping sound?
questions.f: It scrapes a rough leg against a wing, like a tiny fiddle.

questions.q: About how many flowers must bees visit for one jar of honey?
questions.f: Making honey is huge work: millions of flower visits for one jar.

questions.q: True or False: Insects breathe through tiny holes in their sides, not a nose.
questions.f: Air enters small holes called spiracles that run along an insect's body.

questions.q: What are a caterpillar's tiny gripping back legs called?
questions.f: Stumpy prolegs help a caterpillar cling tight as it climbs plants.

questions.q: True or False: Dragonflies were flying before the dinosaurs appeared.
questions.f: Giant dragonfly ancestors buzzed around about 300 million years ago.

questions.q: How many wings does a dragonfly have?
questions.f: Dragonflies move each of their four wings on its own for sharp turns.

questions.q: About how many times a second does a honeybee beat its wings?
questions.f: Around 200 beats a second create the bee's familiar buzzing sound.

questions.q: Which of these birds CANNOT fly?
questions.f: The ostrich's wings are too small for its heavy body to lift off.

questions.q: Which bird lays the smallest eggs?
questions.f: A hummingbird's egg is about the size of a small jelly bean.

questions.q: Which of these can dive the fastest?
questions.f: No bird beats the peregrine falcon in a high-speed hunting dive.

questions.q: Which is the heaviest bird that can still fly?
questions.f: The kori bustard can weigh around 18 kg and only just get airborne.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a bird of prey?
questions.f: Flamingos filter tiny food from water; the others hunt with talons.

questions.q: Which bird travels the farthest each year?
questions.f: The Arctic tern's yearly journey is the longest migration of all animals.

questions.q: What does a penguin mainly use its wings for?
questions.f: A penguin's stiff flippers push it through water like a torpedo.

questions.q: How many birds can see ultraviolet light that humans cannot?
questions.f: Many birds see UV light, helping them spot food and choose mates.

questions.q: True or False: Owls can roll their eyeballs around like we do.
questions.f: An owl's eyes are fixed, so it turns its whole head to look around.

questions.q: Why can't an ostrich fly, even though it has wings?
c: It is heavy with small wings
questions.f: Big bodies and short wings ground the ostrich, so it runs instead.

questions.q: Which bird builds the largest nest?
questions.f: Bald eagles pile sticks into nests that can weigh as much as a car.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT an insect?
questions.f: A spider has eight legs and two body parts, so it is not an insect.

questions.q: Which insect goes through complete metamorphosis?
questions.f: Butterflies fully rebuild in a chrysalis; grasshoppers just grow bigger.

questions.q: True or False: An ant can lift many times its own body weight.
questions.f: Ants have super-strong muscles for their tiny size.

questions.q: Which of these insects does NOT sting?
questions.f: Butterflies have no sting; they sip nectar and harm nobody.

questions.q: Which insect can see almost all around it with huge eyes?
questions.f: A dragonfly's eyes have thousands of lenses covering most of its head.

questions.q: Which pair are arachnids, not insects?
questions.f: Arachnids have eight legs; spiders and scorpions are both in this group.

questions.q: Which bee does no work and only mates with the queen?
questions.f: Drones are male bees whose one job is to father new bees.

questions.q: True or False: Every spider spins a web to catch food.
questions.f: Some spiders, like jumping spiders, pounce on prey instead of trapping it.

questions.q: Which insect lives only about one day as an adult?
questions.f: Adult mayflies barely eat; they mate, lay eggs, and die within a day.

questions.q: Which useful material do bees make besides honey?
questions.f: Bees make wax to build the neat six-sided cells of the honeycomb.

questions.q: Which insects 'farm' aphids for their sweet honeydew?
questions.f: Ants protect aphids and, in return, drink the sugary honeydew they make.

questions.q: Why are a bird's bones hollow?
c: To make the body light for flight
questions.f: Hollow bones cut weight, so wings need less power to lift the bird.

questions.q: The peregrine falcon is the fastest animal on Earth during what?
questions.f: In its dive, or 'stoop', the falcon folds its wings and plunges like a dart.

questions.q: How do emperor penguins survive Antarctica's freezing winter?
questions.f: Penguins crowd into huge huddles, taking turns to warm up in the middle.

questions.q: Why do many birds migrate thousands of kilometres each year?
questions.f: As cold weather hides food, birds fly to places where meals are plenty.

questions.q: How does a hummingbird survive a cold night without eating?
c: It slows its body into torpor
questions.f: In torpor a hummingbird cools down and slows right down to save energy.

questions.q: What makes a peacock's tail shimmer with colour?
questions.f: Microscopic ridges scatter light, so the colours shift as the bird moves.

questions.q: Why do flamingos turn pink?
c: From colours in the food they eat
questions.f: Pink pigments in shrimp and algae slowly tint a flamingo's feathers.

questions.q: How do owls fly so silently when hunting?
questions.f: Comb-like feather edges break up the air, hushing an owl's wingbeats.

questions.q: True or False: The ostrich has the largest eye of any land animal.
questions.f: Each ostrich eye is about 5 cm across, bigger than its own brain.

questions.q: Which bird has been seen flying over the towering Himalayas?
questions.f: Bar-headed geese cross the world's highest mountains on migration.

questions.q: Inside its chrysalis, what happens to a caterpillar's body?
c: It turns to mush and rebuilds
questions.f: The caterpillar dissolves into a soup, then reforms as a butterfly.

questions.q: Why do honeybees perform a 'waggle dance'?
questions.f: The dance's angle and length tell hive-mates exactly where flowers grow.

questions.q: How do fireflies make their glowing light?
questions.f: Chemicals mix in the firefly's body to make cool light with almost no heat.

questions.q: Why is spider silk so incredibly strong for its weight?
c: Its protein fibres line up tightly
It is secretly made of metal
questions.f: Neatly stacked protein chains make silk tougher than the same weight of steel.

questions.q: How do ants find the shortest path to food?
c: By following the strongest scent trail
questions.f: The quickest route gets walked most, so its scent grows strongest fastest.

questions.q: Why do ladybirds wear bright red-and-black colours?
c: To warn predators they taste bad
questions.f: Bold warning colours tell birds this beetle is a nasty, bitter snack.

questions.q: Why can't insects grow as big as a dog today?
c: Their air tubes limit their size
There is no food for them
questions.f: Insects breathe through tubes, and those tubes cannot supply a giant body.

questions.q: How can a fly walk upside down on a ceiling?
c: Sticky pads and tiny claws on its feet
questions.f: Hairy foot pads make just enough stickiness to grip smooth surfaces.

questions.q: True or False: Some cicadas stay underground for 17 years before coming out.
questions.f: Periodical cicadas wait 13 or 17 years, then all emerge together at once.

questions.q: Why do moths fly towards a bright light at night?
c: They navigate by moonlight and get confused
questions.f: Moths steer by the distant Moon, so a nearby lamp scrambles their path.

questions.q: Diwali is celebrated with rows of tiny oil lamps called what?
questions.f: Diyas are little clay lamps filled with oil and a cotton wick — homes glow with hundreds of them!

questions.q: The colorful powder people toss during Holi is called what?
questions.f: Gulal comes in bright pinks, yellows, greens and blues — everyone ends up rainbow-colored!

questions.q: What do many families set up and decorate inside their home for Christmas?
questions.f: The evergreen tree is trimmed with lights, baubles and a shining star or angel on top!

questions.q: At Mexican birthday parties, kids swing a stick at which hanging treat-holder?
questions.f: Piñatas are stuffed with sweets and toys that rain down when they finally burst open!

questions.q: Which song do people around the world sing at birthday parties?
questions.f: It is one of the most sung songs on Earth, translated into dozens of languages!

questions.q: Which color is considered lucky and worn everywhere during Chinese New Year?
questions.f: Red is thought to bring joy and good fortune — and to scare bad luck away!

questions.q: At Halloween, glowing lanterns are carved from which vegetable?
questions.f: You scoop out the insides, cut a spooky face, and pop a candle inside to make it glow!

questions.q: Which big roasted bird is the star of an American Thanksgiving dinner?
questions.f: Families gather around the table to share turkey with stuffing, gravy and pumpkin pie!

questions.q: What do you call your father's brother?
questions.f: An uncle can be your parent's brother — or the husband of your aunt!

questions.q: What do you call your father's sister?
questions.f: In Hindi she might be called Bua, and in Spanish, Tía!

questions.q: What do people say to wish each other a happy Eid?
questions.f: "Eid Mubarak" means "Blessed Eid" — families hug and share sweets to celebrate!

questions.q: Hanukkah candles are placed in a special holder called what?
questions.f: One extra candle, the shamash, is used to light all the others!

questions.q: During Chinese New Year, children receive money tucked inside what?
questions.f: These lucky red envelopes are called hongbao — the red is believed to bring good fortune!

questions.q: At Easter, chocolate treats are often shaped like what?
questions.f: Eggs stand for new life and springtime — some are hidden for kids to hunt!
