questions.q: In the Christmas story, Santa's sleigh is pulled through the sky by what?
questions.f: Eight reindeer pull the sleigh — and red-nosed Rudolph leads the way in the fog!

questions.q: On Day of the Dead, faces are painted to look like colourful what?
questions.f: The cheerful painted skulls, called calaveras, remember loved ones with smiles, not sadness!

questions.q: What do you call three babies born to the same mother at the same time?
questions.f: Two are twins, three are triplets, four are quadruplets — and it keeps counting up!

questions.q: At Raksha Bandhan, a sister ties a decorated thread onto her brother's what?
questions.f: The thread is called a rakhi, a sign of love and protection between siblings!

questions.q: At Christmas, what do people wrap in colourful paper and place under the tree?
questions.f: Many people open their presents on Christmas morning — often still in pyjamas!

questions.q: Which round Indian sweet is shared with family during Diwali?
questions.f: Diwali tables overflow with sweets like ladoo, barfi and jalebi to share with everyone!

questions.q: On Halloween night, children go trick-or-treating dressed up in what?
questions.f: Kids dress as ghosts, superheroes, witches and monsters to collect candy from doors!

questions.q: At Christmas, people mail each other decorated greeting what?
questions.f: Christmas cards often show snowy scenes, robins or a jolly Santa Claus!

questions.q: Your brothers and sisters together are called your what?
questions.f: You share the same parents with your siblings — even if you look totally different!

questions.q: What do we call a carved, glowing Halloween pumpkin?
questions.f: The name comes from an old Irish tale about a wanderer called Stingy Jack!

questions.q: At birthday parties, kids often wear a pointy paper what?
questions.f: Cone-shaped party hats and noisy party blowers make birthdays extra fun!

questions.q: Eid al-Fitr comes right after a month of daytime fasting called what?
questions.f: After a month of fasting from dawn to sunset, Eid is a joyful day of feasting!

questions.q: Christmas songs sung by groups going door to door are called what?
questions.f: Carol singers sometimes carry candles or lanterns as they sing in the cold night!

questions.q: On Halloween, children go door to door saying "trick or treat."
questions.f: If you don't get a treat, the playful "trick" is a joke — but treats almost always win!

questions.q: Your grandfather is your parent's father.
questions.f: Grandfathers have loving nicknames everywhere — Dada or Nana in Hindi, Abuelo in Spanish!

questions.q: In Japan, people take off their shoes before stepping into a home.
questions.f: Shoes stay by the door to keep the floors clean — cosy indoor slippers wait inside!

questions.q: Which festival is known around the world as the Festival of Colors?
questions.f: Holi welcomes spring with clouds of colored powder and splashes of water — pure joy!

questions.q: Diwali celebrates the return of which prince to the city of Ayodhya?
questions.f: People lit rows of lamps to guide Rama home after 14 years — that's why we light diyas!

questions.q: Which festival celebrates the birth of Jesus?
questions.f: Christians remember Jesus's birth in a stable, watched over by shepherds and wise men!

questions.q: The 12-animal cycle used at Chinese New Year is known as the what?
questions.f: Each year has an animal — Rat, Ox, Tiger and more — and yours depends on your birth year!

questions.q: Which spinning-top toy do children play with at Hanukkah?
questions.f: A dreidel has a Hebrew letter on each side, and players win or lose chocolate coins!

questions.q: The Day of the Dead festival comes from which country?
questions.f: In Mexico, families build colorful altars to welcome back the spirits of loved ones!

questions.q: Which country celebrates Thanksgiving with turkey on the fourth Thursday of November?
questions.f: Canada has Thanksgiving too, but they celebrate it in October instead!

questions.q: On which date is Halloween celebrated each year?
questions.f: Halloween falls the night before All Saints' Day, when spooky spirits were said to roam!

questions.q: Eid al-Fitr marks the end of which holy month of fasting?
questions.f: After Ramadan, families dress in new clothes, give to charity, and share big feasts!

questions.q: Which crispy potato pancake is a favourite food at Hanukkah?
questions.f: Latkes are fried in oil — a reminder of the Hanukkah miracle of the lamp oil!

questions.q: Which bright orange flower is used to decorate Day of the Dead altars?
questions.f: Marigolds, called cempasúchil, are believed to guide spirits home with their strong scent!

questions.q: Chinese New Year follows which kind of calendar?
questions.f: Because it follows the moon, the date shifts each year between late January and February!

questions.q: Which festival is famous for colourful dragon and lion dances in the streets?
questions.f: Dancers hide inside the long dragon, weaving it through the crowd to drums and cymbals!

questions.q: In Japan, guests are often given what to wear on their feet indoors?
questions.f: There are even special separate slippers just for using the bathroom!

questions.q: The Christmas gift-bringer Santa Claus is also known by which name?
questions.f: In many places he's Father Christmas, in France Père Noël, and in Italy Babbo Natale!

questions.q: Which festival is called the Jewish Festival of Lights?
questions.f: Each night for eight nights, one more menorah candle is lit until all eight glow!

questions.q: The night before Holi, people light a big bonfire in a ritual called what?
questions.f: The bonfire celebrates good defeating evil — then the colors come out the next morning!

questions.q: Onam is a joyful harvest festival from which Indian state?
questions.f: Onam features snake-boat races, flower carpets and a huge feast served on banana leaves!

questions.q: Which colourful floor art is made with powders during Diwali?
questions.f: Rangoli patterns near the doorway welcome guests and the goddess Lakshmi!

questions.q: Which Thai festival is famous for giant, friendly water fights?
questions.f: Songkran is the Thai New Year — splashing water is a wish to wash away the old year!

questions.q: Nowruz is the New Year for which culture?
questions.f: Nowruz means "new day" and begins on the first day of spring, celebrated for thousands of years!

questions.q: Which spring festival is celebrated with egg hunts and chocolate bunnies?
questions.f: Eggs and bunnies stand for new life bursting out in springtime!

questions.q: Your cousin is the child of your what?
questions.f: First cousins share the same grandparents as you — that's what makes them cousins!

questions.q: Which festival ends a fasting month with feasts, new clothes and gifts?
questions.f: Eid al-Fitr's name means "festival of breaking the fast" after the month of Ramadan!

questions.q: Raksha Bandhan celebrates the special bond between which family members?
questions.f: Sisters tie a rakhi thread and brothers promise to protect them — and give a gift back!

questions.q: Which harvest festival is celebrated in the US with pumpkin pie and gratitude?
questions.f: Families take turns saying what they are thankful for before digging into the feast!

questions.q: The menorah is lit over eight nights during Hanukkah.
questions.f: One candle is added each night, so by the final night all eight are shining brightly!

questions.q: On St Patrick's Day, people wear the colour green.
questions.f: Green stands for Ireland's rolling hills — some cities even dye their rivers green!

questions.q: Holi is celebrated in spring.
questions.f: Holi welcomes the warm spring season and celebrates colour, love and new beginnings!

questions.q: During Ramadan, Muslims fast from food and drink during daylight hours.
questions.f: They eat a meal before dawn and break the fast after sunset, often with dates!

questions.q: How many days does the Diwali celebration traditionally last?
questions.f: Each of the five days has its own meaning, from cleaning the house to honouring family!

questions.q: For how many nights is Hanukkah celebrated?
questions.f: Eight nights remember how a tiny bit of oil kept the temple lamp burning for eight days!

questions.q: How many candles does a Hanukkah menorah hold in total?
questions.f: Eight candles for the eight nights, plus one helper candle called the shamash!

questions.q: Chinese New Year firecrackers are said to scare away a monster named what?
questions.f: Legend says the beast Nian feared loud noises and the colour red — so both keep it away!

questions.q: Which goddess of wealth is honoured during Diwali?
questions.f: People keep doors and windows open and lamps lit to welcome Lakshmi into their homes!

questions.q: Day of the Dead is celebrated on the first two days of which month?
questions.f: November 1st honours children who have passed, and the 2nd honours the adults!

questions.q: The chocolate coins given to children at Hanukkah are called what?
questions.f: Gelt means "money" in Yiddish — the foil-wrapped coins are also used to play dreidel!

questions.q: Which round pastry is shared at the Chinese Mid-Autumn Festival?
questions.f: Mooncakes are round like the full moon, often stuffed with sweet lotus paste and egg yolk!

questions.q: American Thanksgiving falls on the fourth what of November?
questions.f: The day after, called Black Friday, is one of the busiest shopping days of the year!

questions.q: Halloween grew out of an ancient Celtic festival called what?
questions.f: At Samhain people believed the spirits could roam, so they wore disguises to blend in!

questions.q: How many animals are in the Chinese zodiac?
questions.f: The 12 animals are said to have raced across a river — the Rat cleverly finished first!

questions.q: Eid al-Adha is known as the festival of what?
questions.f: It remembers Prophet Ibrahim's faith, and families share meat with neighbours and the poor!

questions.q: Before Eid begins, families look to the sky to spot the new what?
questions.f: Spotting the thin crescent moon signals that the festival can finally begin!

questions.q: Which sweet treats are shaped and decorated to look like skulls at Day of the Dead?
questions.f: Sugar skulls, or calaveras, are painted in bright colours and often show a smiling face!

questions.q: In Korea, a baby's first birthday is a big celebration called what?
questions.f: Reaching the first birthday was so special that families throw a huge feast to mark it!

questions.q: The lively garba and dandiya dances of Navratri come from which Indian state?
questions.f: Dancers whirl in circles for nine nights, clacking colourful sticks in the dandiya dance!

questions.q: At Christmas, children hang up what by the fireplace for Santa to fill?
questions.f: The story says a bag of gold once landed in a stocking drying by the fire!

questions.q: Pongal is a joyful harvest festival celebrated mainly in which Indian state?
questions.f: A sweet rice dish, also called pongal, is cooked until it bubbles over — a sign of plenty!

questions.q: According to Christmas tradition, how many wise men visited the baby Jesus?
questions.f: Tradition says three, because they brought three gifts: gold, frankincense and myrrh!

questions.q: Dussehra celebrates good beating evil when Rama defeats which demon king?
questions.f: Giant statues of ten-headed Ravana are filled with fireworks and set alight!

questions.q: In China, why are long noodles served at birthdays?
questions.f: You're supposed to slurp a longevity noodle without biting it — the longer, the better!

questions.q: The beautiful flower carpet made on the ground during Onam is called what?
questions.f: Families add a new ring of flower petals each day, so the pookalam grows bigger and bigger!

questions.q: The huge Onam feast served on a banana leaf is called what?
questions.f: An Onam Sadhya can have more than 20 different dishes, all eaten with your hands!

questions.q: What do you call your sibling's son?
questions.f: Your sibling's son is your nephew, and their daughter is your niece!

questions.q: The Chinese zodiac includes both a Dragon and a Rat.
questions.f: The Dragon is the only mythical animal in the zodiac and is seen as the luckiest of all!

questions.q: A baby born on February 29 has a birthday only about once every four years.
questions.f: February 29 only appears in a leap year, so "leaplings" often celebrate on the 28th or March 1st instead!

questions.q: Sugar skulls are a treat made for Mexico's Day of the Dead.
questions.f: They're often decorated with the name of a loved one written across the forehead!

questions.q: Diwali always lasts exactly one day.
questions.f: Diwali actually spans five days, each with its own special customs and meaning!

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a festival of lights?
questions.f: Holi is the festival of colours! Diwali, Hanukkah and Loy Krathong all shine with lamps or candles.

questions.q: Which festival marks the first day of spring as the Persian New Year?
questions.f: Families set out a special table called the Haft-Seen with seven symbolic items starting with 'S'!

questions.q: Which of these festivals happens earliest in the calendar year?
questions.f: Chinese New Year lands in Jan–Feb, Holi in March, Diwali in Oct–Nov, and Christmas in December!

questions.q: Which of these festivals did NOT begin in India?
questions.f: Hanukkah is a Jewish festival from the Middle East — the other three are all Indian celebrations!

questions.q: Which of these foods is NOT traditionally eaten at Hanukkah?
questions.f: Mooncakes belong to China's Mid-Autumn Festival! The rest are fried-in-oil Hanukkah favourites.

questions.q: Which pair are BOTH harvest festivals?
questions.f: Both Onam and Thanksgiving give thanks for a good harvest with a huge shared feast!

questions.q: For which festival do people say "Shubh Deepavali"?
questions.f: "Shubh Deepavali" means "Happy Diwali" — Deepavali means "a row of lights"!

questions.q: Which spring festival remembers the ancient journey of the Jewish people out of Egypt?
questions.f: At the Passover meal, families eat flat bread called matzah and retell the escape story!

questions.q: Which festival is celebrated on the exact same date, December 25, every year?
questions.f: Eid, Diwali and Chinese New Year follow the moon, so their dates shift a little every year!

questions.q: In Korea, what is the tradition where a one-year-old picks an object to hint at their future?
questions.f: If the baby grabs a pencil they might become a scholar, or coins for a rich life!

questions.q: In which country do people hurl tomatoes at each other during the festival La Tomatina?
questions.f: In the town of Buñol, thousands squash tens of thousands of tomatoes into a giant red mess!

questions.q: Which of these festivals does NOT usually involve fireworks or firecrackers?
questions.f: Thanksgiving is quiet and cosy, while the others light up the sky with bangs and sparkles!

questions.q: Which of these is a SWEET festival treat, not a savoury one?
questions.f: Gulab jamun are soft fried balls soaked in sugary syrup — a favourite at Indian festivals!

questions.q: Which festival honours ancestors with home altars, candles and marigold flowers?
questions.f: The altar, called an ofrenda, holds photos and favourite foods to welcome the spirits back!

questions.q: Which comes first on the calendar, Halloween or Day of the Dead?
questions.f: Halloween is October 31, and Day of the Dead follows right after on November 1 and 2!

questions.q: Which huge Brazilian festival is famous for street parades and samba dancing?
questions.f: Rio's Carnival features dazzling costumes and floats, with millions dancing in the streets!

questions.q: Which Indian festival features garba and dandiya dances over nine nights?
questions.f: Navratri means "nine nights," each often celebrated by wearing a different colour!

questions.q: Which country's national day features shamrocks, the colour green and lively parades?
questions.f: St Patrick's Day celebrates Ireland — the three-leaf shamrock is its lucky symbol!

questions.q: Chinese New Year sparks the world's largest yearly human migration as people travel home.
questions.f: Billions of trips are made across China so families can be together — it's called Chunyun!

questions.q: Thanksgiving is celebrated in different months in the United States and Canada.
questions.f: Canadians feast in October, while Americans wait until the fourth Thursday of November!

questions.q: Nowruz marks the start of spring in the Persian calendar.
questions.f: Nowruz, whose name means "new day," has been celebrated for over 3,000 years across Iran and beyond!

questions.q: Vesak is a festival that celebrates the life of the Buddha.
questions.f: Buddhists light lanterns and give to those in need to mark the Buddha's birth and teachings!

questions.q: Why do people light diyas and lamps during Diwali?
c: To celebrate light winning over darkness
questions.f: The lamps stand for hope, knowledge and goodness shining brighter than darkness and evil!

questions.q: Why is the colour red so important during Chinese New Year?
c: It is believed to scare away bad luck
It is the cheapest dye to make
It glows brightly in the dark
questions.f: The story says loud noises and red frightened the monster Nian — so red means good fortune!

questions.q: The Hanukkah miracle tells of oil that should have lasted one day but burned for how many?
questions.f: That surprising eight-day glow is why Hanukkah lasts eight nights and features fried foods!

questions.q: Why do festivals like Eid, Diwali and Chinese New Year fall on different dates each year?
c: The dates are chosen at random
questions.f: These festivals use lunar calendars based on the moon's phases, which don't match our solar year!

questions.q: Day of the Dead is joyful, not sad, because families believe what?
c: The spirits of loved ones return to visit
The festival brings the first snow
It marks the end of summer
It is the start of the school year
questions.f: Instead of mourning, families throw a warm party of food, music and memories to welcome them home!

questions.q: Why do Muslims fast from dawn to sunset during Ramadan?
c: To practise self-control and feel gratitude
Because food is banned all year
questions.f: Fasting helps people feel closer to their faith and understand those who don't have enough to eat!

questions.q: In the Chinese zodiac, how many years until your birth animal comes around again?
questions.f: With 12 animals taking one year each, your zodiac animal returns every 12th birthday!

questions.q: Why is money given in red envelopes at Chinese New Year, rather than wrapped gifts?
c: Red money is thought to pass on good luck
Paper is easier to carry than boxes
It hides how much is inside
questions.f: Elders give hongbao to children as a wish for a safe, lucky and happy new year!

questions.q: Rangoli patterns are drawn near the doorway at Diwali mainly to do what?
c: Welcome guests and the goddess Lakshmi
questions.f: Made from coloured powder, rice or petals, rangoli is a bright sign of welcome and good luck!

questions.q: Why does the festival of Eid move about 11 days earlier each year?
c: The Islamic calendar is shorter than the solar year
Leap years remove a whole day
The moon disappears for a month
questions.f: The lunar year is around 11 days shorter, so Eid slowly drifts through all the seasons over time!

questions.q: Which festival is celebrated by the MOST people across the whole world?
questions.f: Around two billion people mark Christmas, making it one of the most celebrated days on Earth!

questions.q: Long ago, why did people wear costumes and masks on Halloween?
c: To disguise themselves from wandering spirits
To stay warm in the cold
questions.f: People believed that dressing up would trick roaming spirits into leaving them alone!

questions.q: By tradition, why do people try to blow out all their birthday candles in one breath?
c: To make a secret wish come true
To cool down the cake faster
questions.f: The custom says a wish blown out in a single breath — kept secret — is sure to come true!

questions.q: Chinese New Year celebrations last until the 15th day, ending with which event?
questions.f: On the final night, glowing lanterns are released and sweet rice balls are eaten!

questions.q: Before pumpkins were used, jack-o'-lanterns were carved from which vegetable?
questions.f: In Ireland people carved scary faces into turnips — pumpkins were only found later in America!

questions.q: Round mooncakes are shared at the Mid-Autumn Festival to celebrate what?
c: The longest day of the year
questions.f: Families gather outside to admire the bright, round autumn moon while eating matching round cakes!

questions.q: Why is a 'coming of age' birthday, like 15 or 16, extra special in many cultures?
c: It marks growing from a child toward adulthood
It is the day you retire from work
It is your very last birthday
It means you can fly a plane
questions.f: Latin America celebrates a girl's 15th with a Quinceañera, and the US often marks a Sweet Sixteen!

questions.q: Diwali falls on one of the darkest new-moon nights, which is why the lamps shine so brightly.
questions.f: With no moonlight, the thousands of little diyas make the whole night glow with warmth!

questions.q: The letters on a Hanukkah dreidel stand for "a great miracle happened there."
questions.f: In Israel, one letter is changed so the dreidel instead says "a great miracle happened HERE"!

questions.q: During Ramadan, Muslims eat a pre-dawn meal called suhoor before the day's fast begins.
questions.f: After sunset, the fast is broken with a meal called iftar, often started by eating a date!

questions.q: Which food is made from milk?
questions.f: It can take about 10 pounds of milk to make just one pound of cheese!

questions.q: Bread is mostly made from ground-up grains called what?
questions.f: Flour is just grain seeds crushed into a fine powder, then mixed with water to make dough.

questions.q: Which sweet, sticky food do bees make?
questions.f: Bees store honey in wax honeycombs to eat during the winter when no flowers bloom.

questions.q: Which drink do we get from cows?
questions.f: A dairy cow can make around six to eight gallons of milk every single day!

questions.q: French fries are made from which vegetable?
questions.f: Potatoes were the first vegetable ever grown in space, back in 1995!

questions.q: Which long yellow fruit do you peel before eating?
questions.f: A bunch of bananas is called a 'hand,' and each single banana is a 'finger'!

questions.q: Ketchup is made mainly from which food?
questions.f: Long ago, ketchup was sold as a medicine before it became a sauce for fries!

questions.q: Which breakfast food comes from a chicken?
questions.f: A fresh egg sinks in water, but an old egg floats!

questions.q: Which cold, sweet treat is scooped onto a cone?
questions.f: Ice cream cones became a huge hit at the 1904 World's Fair in St. Louis!

questions.q: Raisins are the dried version of which fruit?
questions.f: Drop a raisin into fizzy soda and it will bounce up and down like a tiny elevator!

questions.q: Which vegetable makes your eyes water when you cut it?
questions.f: A cut onion puffs out a gas that stings your eyes, so you make tears to wash it away.

questions.q: Popcorn is made by heating up which food?
questions.f: An ear of corn almost always has an even number of rows of kernels!

questions.q: Which round red fruit grows on trees in orchards?
questions.f: Apples float in water because they are about one-quarter air!

questions.q: Orange juice is squeezed from which fruit?
questions.f: One orange can hold more than 50 seeds, though many types are grown to have none at all.

questions.q: Which crunchy orange vegetable do rabbits love?
questions.f: Carrots get sweeter after a frost, because the plant makes extra sugar to fight the cold!

questions.q: Peanut butter is made by grinding up what?
questions.f: It takes about 540 peanuts to make one 12-ounce jar of peanut butter!

questions.q: Which dark drink is made from roasted beans?
questions.f: Coffee beans are really the seeds inside a small red fruit called a coffee cherry!

questions.q: Butter is made by churning which part of milk?
questions.f: Shake a jar of cream long enough and you will make real butter at home!

questions.q: Which leafy green is the main part of most salads?
questions.f: Lettuce is about 95 percent water, which is why it feels so cool and crunchy!

questions.q: Which grain is boiled and eaten with meals across Asia?
questions.f: More than half of all the people in the world eat rice as their main food!

questions.q: Spaghetti is a type of what?
questions.f: There are more than 300 different shapes of pasta with all sorts of fun names!

questions.q: Which fruit has a hard brown shell with water inside?
questions.f: The water inside a young coconut is so clean it has been used as a natural drink for astronauts.

questions.q: Jam is usually made by cooking fruit with what?
questions.f: Sugar helps jam stay good for a long time by stopping mold from growing.

questions.q: Which big orange fruit is carved with faces in autumn?
questions.f: Pumpkins are secretly fruits, because to scientists anything with seeds inside is a fruit!

questions.q: Which yellow spread melts when you put it on warm toast?
questions.f: It takes about a gallon of milk's worth of cream to make one pound of butter.

questions.q: Honey is made by bees.
questions.f: One honeybee makes only about one-twelfth of a teaspoon of honey in its whole life!

questions.q: Tomatoes grow underground like potatoes.
questions.f: Tomatoes grow on vines up in the sunshine; potatoes are the ones hiding underground.

questions.q: Bananas grow on giant tree trunks made of wood.
questions.f: A banana plant is actually the world's largest herb, with a soft stem, not a woody tree!

questions.q: Cutting an onion can make your eyes water.
questions.f: Chilling an onion before you chop it makes fewer stinging fumes and fewer tears!

questions.q: Cheese is made from milk.
questions.f: Cheesemakers add tiny helpers called bacteria to milk to turn it thick and tasty.

questions.q: Pizza was invented in which country?
questions.f: The Margherita pizza was named for Queen Margherita of Italy in 1889!

questions.q: Sushi comes from which country?
questions.f: Sushi began long ago as a clever way to keep fish fresh by packing it in rice!

questions.q: Tacos come from which country?
questions.f: In Mexico, some tacos are filled with crunchy toasted grasshoppers called chapulines!

questions.q: Curry and naan bread are famous foods of which country?
questions.f: India grows and uses more spices than any other country on Earth!

questions.q: Chocolate is made from the beans of which plant?
questions.f: Cacao beans were once so valuable that some peoples used them as money!

questions.q: Maple syrup comes from the sap of which tree?
questions.f: It takes about 40 gallons of maple sap to make just one gallon of syrup!

questions.q: Bees make honey from what that they collect from flowers?
questions.f: Bees visit about two million flowers to make a single pound of honey!

questions.q: Prunes are the dried version of which fruit?
questions.f: In the year 2000, prunes were officially allowed to be called 'dried plums' to sound tastier!

questions.q: Guacamole is a dip made mainly from which fruit?
questions.f: An avocado is actually a berry with one giant seed in the middle!

questions.q: Which bright yellow spice gives Indian curry its color?
questions.f: Turmeric stains everything yellow and has been used as a natural dye for cloth!

questions.q: Which food is made by letting milk turn thick and tangy?
questions.f: In India, this creamy food is called dahi and is eaten with almost every meal!

questions.q: Which Italian dish is baked in flat layers of pasta and cheese?
questions.f: The word lasagna first meant the pot the dish was cooked in, not the food itself!

questions.q: Which flatbread is baked on the wall of a hot clay oven?
questions.f: The clay oven that bakes naan is called a tandoor and can get hotter than 900 degrees!

questions.q: Soy sauce is made from which bean?
questions.f: Making soy sauce the old way can take many months of the beans slowly fermenting!

questions.q: Which fruit is called the 'king of fruits' for its powerful smell?
questions.f: Durian smells so strong that it is banned on many buses and trains in Asia!

questions.q: Oatmeal is made from which grain?
questions.f: Oats are so filling because they are packed with a special sponge-like fiber.

questions.q: Pickles are made from which vegetable soaked in vinegar?
questions.f: Cucumbers are about 95 percent water, one of the wateriest foods you can crunch!

questions.q: Hummus is a creamy dip made mainly from which food?
questions.f: Chickpeas have a second name: garbanzo beans!

questions.q: Vanilla flavor comes from the pod of which kind of plant?
questions.f: Vanilla is one of the few orchids that grows a food we can eat!

questions.q: Which red spice is made from dried, ground chili peppers?
questions.f: Paprika can taste sweet or spicy depending on which peppers are ground up!

questions.q: Which smooth, frozen Italian treat is softer than ice cream?
questions.f: Gelato has less air whipped into it than ice cream, so it tastes rich and dense!

questions.q: Which thin, round Mexican bread wraps up a taco or burrito?
questions.f: Tortillas can be made from ground corn or from wheat flour.

questions.q: Which twisted baked snack is often sprinkled with salt?
questions.f: The twisted pretzel shape is said to look like arms folded in prayer long ago!

questions.q: Which staple food is made from wheat flour and baked as a loaf?
questions.f: Sliced bread was invented in 1928, which is why we say 'the best thing since sliced bread'!

questions.q: Marzipan candy is made mostly from which ground nut?
questions.f: Ground almonds and sugar can be shaped and painted to look just like tiny fruits!

questions.q: A watermelon is mostly made of water.
questions.f: A watermelon is about 92 percent water, basically a giant juicy balloon!

questions.q: White chocolate contains no cocoa solids at all.
questions.f: White chocolate is made from cocoa butter, milk, and sugar, but none of the brown cocoa!

questions.q: A tomato is really a fruit, not a vegetable.
questions.f: To scientists, a tomato is a fruit because it grows from a flower and holds seeds!

questions.q: French fries were first invented in France.
questions.f: Many food historians say fries were actually first made in Belgium, not France!

questions.q: Chili peppers get their heat from a chemical called capsaicin.
questions.f: Capsaicin tricks your mouth into feeling burning heat, even though nothing is actually hot!

questions.q: About how many flowers must bees visit to make one pound of honey?
questions.f: To gather that nectar, bees fly a distance equal to more than twice around the whole Earth!

questions.q: About how many gallons of sap make one gallon of maple syrup?
questions.f: Trees are tapped in early spring when the sap starts flowing again after winter.

questions.q: Which vitamin do oranges and lemons give us lots of?
questions.f: Long ago, sailors ate citrus fruit so they would not get sick from a lack of Vitamin C!

questions.q: About how much of a watermelon is water?
questions.f: That is why a big slice of cold watermelon is so refreshing on a hot day!

questions.q: Which mineral in milk helps build strong bones and teeth?
questions.f: Your body keeps most of its calcium locked away inside your bones like a storage bank!

questions.q: Which scale measures how spicy a chili pepper is?
questions.f: A sweet bell pepper scores zero, while the hottest peppers score over two million!

questions.q: About how many pounds of milk make one pound of cheese?
questions.f: Cheese is like packed-up milk, which is why a little block holds so much goodness!

questions.q: Which country grows the most coffee in the world?
questions.f: Brazil has grown more coffee than any other country for over 150 years!

questions.q: When you eat broccoli, which part of the plant are you eating?
questions.f: If you leave broccoli too long, those tiny green buds burst open into little yellow flowers!

questions.q: Carrots were mostly which color before farmers made them orange?
questions.f: Long ago most carrots were purple or yellow, and orange ones were bred later in the Netherlands!

questions.q: Which gas do tiny yeast make that puffs up bread dough?
questions.f: The gas gets trapped as bubbles, leaving all the little holes you see inside a slice of bread!

questions.q: Saffron, the priciest spice, comes from the threads of which flower?
questions.f: It takes around 75,000 crocus flowers to make just one pound of saffron by hand!

questions.q: Rice is often grown in flooded fields called what?
questions.f: Flooding the fields keeps weeds from growing while the rice plants love the standing water.

questions.q: Which acid makes lemons and limes taste so sour?
questions.f: Citric acid is so sour it can even be used to clean and shine metal!

questions.q: Which country eats the most chocolate per person?
questions.f: People in Switzerland eat around 20 pounds of chocolate each every year!

questions.q: Bananas are very slightly radioactive because they contain which element?
questions.f: Don't worry, you would need to eat millions of bananas at once for it to matter!

questions.q: Apples float in water because they are about one-quarter what?
questions.f: That trapped air is why apple bobbing is such a splashy game at parties!

questions.q: Which country grows the most rice in the world?
questions.f: China and India together grow over half of all the rice on the planet!

questions.q: Crunchy celery is about 95 percent what?
questions.f: Celery has so few calories that your body uses lots of energy just to chew and digest it!

questions.q: Most bread around the world is made from which grain?
questions.f: Wheat has a stretchy protein called gluten that lets dough puff up and hold its shape.

questions.q: The spice nutmeg is really the ground-up seed of what?
questions.f: The same nutmeg fruit gives two spices: nutmeg from the seed and mace from its lacy red coat!

questions.q: Which natural sugar gives fruit its sweet taste?
questions.f: Fructose is the sweetest of all the natural sugars found in food!

questions.q: Which vitamin do carrots give that helps you see in dim light?
questions.f: Carrots turn their orange color into Vitamin A inside your body to help your eyes!

questions.q: How many basic tastes can your tongue sense?
questions.f: The five are sweet, sour, salty, bitter, and umami, the savory taste!

questions.q: Sealed honey can last for thousands of years without spoiling.
questions.f: Explorers found honey in ancient Egyptian tombs that was still perfectly good to eat!

questions.q: Peanuts are true nuts, just like walnuts and almonds.
questions.f: Peanuts are actually legumes, more like peas and beans, and they grow underground!

questions.q: A cow has four stomach compartments to digest tough grass.
questions.f: A cow brings food back up to chew again, a chewy habit called 'chewing the cud'!

questions.q: Long ago, most carrots were purple, not orange.
questions.f: Orange carrots became popular only a few hundred years ago after farmers bred them that way!

questions.q: Which of these is NOT made from milk?
questions.f: Tofu is made from soybeans, so it is a great milk-free food for people who don't eat dairy!

questions.q: Which of these is really a fruit, even though we cook it like a vegetable?
questions.f: A bell pepper grows from a flower and holds seeds, which makes it a fruit to scientists!

questions.q: Which of these is a legume, like beans and peas, not a tree nut?
questions.f: Legumes grow in pods and are packed with protein to help you grow strong!

questions.q: Which warm spice is made from the bark of a tree?
questions.f: Cinnamon sticks are pieces of dried bark that curl up as they dry!

questions.q: Which of these is a whole grain that keeps its healthy outer layer?
questions.f: Whole grains keep the bran and germ of the seed, which hold most of the fiber and vitamins!

questions.q: Which of these fruits is NOT a citrus fruit?
questions.f: Citrus fruits like lemons and limes are related, but a juicy mango belongs to a different family!

questions.q: Which of these cheeses first came from Italy?
questions.f: Real Parmesan cheese is aged for one to three years before it is ready to eat!

questions.q: Which cooking method uses very hot oil?
questions.f: Frying makes food crispy because the hot oil quickly dries and browns the outside!

questions.q: Which Korean side dish is made by fermenting cabbage with spices?
questions.f: Some Korean families bury pots of kimchi underground to keep it cool while it ferments!

questions.q: Which nutrient in eggs and beans helps build your muscles?
questions.f: Your body breaks protein down into tiny building blocks to make new muscles, skin, and hair!

questions.q: Which of these is a leafy herb, not a ground-up spice?
questions.f: Herbs usually come from the green leaves of a plant, while spices come from seeds, bark, or roots!

questions.q: Which of these foods grows underground?
questions.f: The knobby ginger we eat is really an underground stem called a rhizome!

questions.q: Which chili pepper is the hottest?
questions.f: A habanero can be around 100 times spicier than a mild jalapeño!

questions.q: Which ingredient makes cakes and muffins puff up and rise?
questions.f: Baking powder makes tiny gas bubbles the moment it gets wet and warm, lifting the batter!

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the five basic tastes?
questions.f: 'Spicy' is not a taste at all; it is really a burning feeling your mouth senses as heat!

questions.q: The sandwich is said to be named after a place in which country?
questions.f: The story says the Earl of Sandwich asked for meat in bread so he could eat without stopping his card game!

questions.q: Which of these is really a berry to scientists?
questions.f: A watermelon is a giant berry, but a strawberry isn't a true berry at all!

questions.q: Which of these foods is a fungus, not a plant?
questions.f: Mushrooms are more closely related to animals than to plants in the tree of life!

questions.q: Which nutrient in bread, rice, and pasta gives you quick energy?
questions.f: Your body breaks carbohydrates down into sugar to fuel your muscles and your brain!

questions.q: A banana is a berry to scientists, but a strawberry is not.
questions.f: True berries grow from one flower with seeds inside, which fits the banana but not the strawberry!

questions.q: Cashews are safe to eat raw straight off the tree.
questions.f: Raw cashews have a stinging chemical in their shell, so they must be roasted before we eat them!

questions.q: Bell peppers have no capsaicin, so they are never spicy.
questions.f: With no capsaicin, sweet bell peppers score a big fat zero on the spicy scale!

questions.q: Why does bread dough rise before it is baked?
questions.f: Living yeast eats the sugar in dough and burps out carbon dioxide gas that puffs it up!

questions.q: Why does a sliced apple turn brown after a while?
c: It reacts with oxygen in the air
It loses its color to water
questions.f: Squeezing lemon juice on apple slices slows the browning because the acid blocks the reaction!

questions.q: Which spice is the most expensive in the world by weight?
questions.f: Saffron costs so much because each flower gives only three tiny threads, picked by hand!

questions.q: Why does chopping an onion make you cry?
questions.f: The onion's gas mixes with tears to make a mild acid, so your eyes water to wash it away!

questions.q: What is the main step that turns liquid milk into solid cheese?
questions.f: Cheesemakers add special helpers that make milk clump into solid curds and watery whey!

questions.q: Why does bread turn hard and stale after a few days?
questions.f: Surprisingly, the fridge makes bread go stale faster, so a bread box keeps it fresher!

questions.q: What chemical makes chili peppers feel burning hot?
questions.f: Milk helps cool the burn better than water because it washes the oily capsaicin away!

questions.q: Which reaction browns toast and gives seared food its rich flavor?
questions.f: The Maillard reaction happens when heat makes sugars and proteins join, creating tasty brown crusts!

questions.q: Why does a corn kernel pop into popcorn?
questions.f: Each kernel is a tiny pressure cooker: the steam builds up until the kernel bursts and puffs inside out!

questions.q: Which grain is grown in the largest amount by weight in the world?
questions.f: Maize, also called corn, isn't just food; it becomes fuel, plastics, and feed for animals too!

questions.q: Why does salt help keep food from spoiling?
c: It draws water out of microbes
questions.f: Without water, the tiny microbes that rot food can't grow, so salted meat and fish last for months!

questions.q: What gives carrots and sweet potatoes their bright orange color?
questions.f: Eating tons of orange foods can even tint your skin a little orange, though it is harmless!

questions.q: Why does milk go sour if left out too long?
questions.f: The same souring by bacteria is used on purpose to make yogurt and cheese taste tangy!

questions.q: Umami, the fifth basic taste, tastes mostly like what?
questions.f: Umami is the rich, meaty flavor found in cheese, mushrooms, tomatoes, and soy sauce!

questions.q: Yeast, which makes bread rise, is really a tiny type of what?
questions.f: Yeast is a living microscopic fungus, and a single spoonful can hold billions of them!

questions.q: Where is the spiciest part of a chili pepper?
questions.f: Most of the fiery capsaicin sits in the pale spongy ribs, not in the seeds as many people think!

questions.q: The Maillard reaction is why toast turns brown and smells delicious.
questions.f: The very same reaction browns cookies, seared steak, and roasted coffee beans!

questions.q: Spiciness is a real taste picked up by your taste buds.
questions.f: Spiciness is not a taste; it is a heat-and-pain signal sensed by nerves, not taste buds!

questions.q: Which animal did knights ride into battle?
questions.f: War horses were specially trained and even wore their own armor.

questions.q: What is the water-filled ditch around a castle called?
questions.f: Moats also stopped enemies from digging tunnels under the walls.

questions.q: How many horns did Triceratops have on its face?
questions.f: Triceratops had one of the biggest skulls of any land animal ever.

questions.q: What did a castle raise and lower to cross its moat?
questions.f: Heavy chains lifted the drawbridge like a giant seesaw.

questions.q: Where did Stone Age people paint pictures of animals?
questions.f: Some cave paintings are over 30,000 years old and still colourful.

questions.q: What did ancient Egyptians wrap mummies in?
questions.f: One mummy could be wrapped in bandages hundreds of metres long.

questions.q: What giant stone tombs did the Egyptians build for their kings?
questions.f: The Great Pyramid was built about 4,500 years ago.

questions.q: Woolly mammoths had two long, curved... what?
questions.f: A mammoth tusk could grow longer than a grown-up is tall.

questions.q: Dinosaurs are still alive on Earth today.
questions.f: The last dinosaurs died out about 66 million years ago, long before people.

questions.q: What metal suit did a knight wear to protect his body?
questions.f: A full suit of armour could weigh as much as a large dog.

questions.q: What do we call a scientist who digs up dinosaur bones?
questions.f: Paleontologists brush bones free using tools as small as toothbrushes.

questions.q: Ancient Egyptians wrote using tiny pictures called...?
questions.f: There were more than 700 different hieroglyph pictures to learn.

questions.q: What round invention helps carts and cars roll along?
questions.f: The wheel was invented over 5,000 years ago, first for making pottery.

questions.q: Which fierce dinosaur is nicknamed 'T. rex'?
questions.f: T. rex had teeth as long as bananas for crunching bone.

questions.q: A castle's tall stone walls helped keep enemies out.
questions.f: Some castle walls were thicker than a car is long.

questions.q: What did a knight hold to block blows in a fight?
questions.f: Knights painted colourful patterns on shields to show which family they came from.

questions.q: What do we call a king who ruled ancient Egypt?
questions.f: Pharaohs were believed to be part god by their people.

questions.q: What is a hard, rocky print of an ancient animal called?
questions.f: Fossils form when bones slowly turn to stone over millions of years.

questions.q: The Great Pyramid of Egypt is made of stone blocks.
questions.f: It holds about 2.3 million stone blocks, some heavier than a car.

questions.q: What tall circle of standing stones sits in England?
questions.f: People dragged some Stonehenge stones from over 200 kilometres away.

questions.q: What did explorers sail across the sea in long ago?
questions.f: Old sailing ships used the wind in their sails to travel the world.

questions.q: What sweet food, made by bees, did ancient Egyptians love?
questions.f: Honey found in Egyptian tombs was still edible thousands of years later.

questions.q: Which dinosaur had bony plates along its back?
questions.f: Stegosaurus had a brain only about the size of a walnut.

questions.q: Stone Age people made their tools out of stone.
questions.f: They chipped sharp edges onto flint to make knives and axes.

questions.q: What did the ancient Romans build to travel far, long and straight?
questions.f: Some Roman roads were so well built you can still walk on them today.

questions.q: What did cave people make to keep warm and cook food?
questions.f: Learning to control fire helped early humans survive cold nights.

questions.q: What long, sharp weapon did many knights fight with?
questions.f: A knight's sword was often given a name, like a treasured friend.

questions.q: Egyptians made paper-like sheets from a reed plant called...?
questions.f: The word 'paper' comes from this Egyptian reed, papyrus.

questions.q: What did dinosaurs hatch out of?
questions.f: Some dinosaur eggs were round, others long like a giant potato.

questions.q: Knights lived in castles long ago.
questions.f: Castles had thick walls, towers, and sometimes secret escape tunnels.

questions.q: Which river was ancient Egypt built along?
questions.f: The Nile is one of the longest rivers in the whole world.

questions.q: What is a preserved Egyptian body wrapped in bandages called?
questions.f: Egyptians dried bodies with salt so they would last thousands of years.

questions.q: What was the ruler of the ancient Roman Empire called?
questions.f: The very first Roman emperor was named Augustus.

questions.q: Which sports contest did the ancient Greeks start, held every four years?
questions.f: The first Olympics were held in Greece nearly 2,800 years ago.

questions.q: Which dinosaur had a very long neck to reach tall trees?
questions.f: Its neck let it munch leaves that other animals could not reach.

questions.q: Which ancient Indus Valley city is famous today?
questions.f: Mohenjo-daro had brick houses and covered drains 4,500 years ago.

questions.q: The Great Wall of China is thousands of kilometres long.
questions.f: Joined together, its walls stretch more than 20,000 kilometres.

questions.q: Which explorer sailed west in 1492 and reached the Americas?
questions.f: Columbus actually thought he had landed in India, not a new land.

questions.q: What salt did Egyptians use to dry out mummies?
questions.f: Natron soaked up all the moisture so the body would not rot.

questions.q: Which metal gave its name to the age after the Stone Age?
questions.f: Bronze is made by mixing copper and tin together.

questions.q: On which mountain did Greek myths say the gods lived?
questions.f: Mount Olympus is the tallest mountain in all of Greece.

questions.q: What did the ancient Romans build to carry water into cities?
questions.f: Some Roman aqueducts still carry water in Europe today.

questions.q: The wheel was invented long before the first car.
questions.f: The wheel is about 5,000 years old; cars are barely 150 years old.

questions.q: Which boy pharaoh's golden tomb was found full of treasure?
questions.f: 'King Tut' became pharaoh when he was only about nine years old.

questions.q: What did Stone Age hunters throw to catch animals from far away?
questions.f: Later they added a special stick, an atlatl, to throw spears even faster.

questions.q: What did the printing press help make many copies of?
questions.f: Before printing, every book had to be copied out slowly by hand.

questions.q: Which flying reptile lived alongside the dinosaurs?
questions.f: Pterosaurs were the first backboned animals ever to fly.

questions.q: What huge Egyptian statue has a lion's body and a human head?
questions.f: The Great Sphinx was carved from a single giant block of stone.

questions.q: The ancient Greeks invented democracy, where people vote.
questions.f: In Athens, citizens gathered on a hillside to vote on new laws.

questions.q: What is a boy training to become a knight called?
questions.f: A squire cleaned the armour and learned to ride before becoming a knight.

questions.q: Which explorer's ships first sailed all the way around the world?
questions.f: Magellan died on the trip, but his crew finished the round-the-world voyage.

questions.q: What clothing did ancient Romans wrap around themselves?
questions.f: Only Roman citizens were allowed to wear the white toga.

questions.q: What swinging log did attackers use to smash castle gates?
questions.f: The heavy end was often carved to look like a ram's head.

questions.q: Dinosaurs lived on Earth millions of years before humans.
questions.f: Humans and T. rex are separated by about 66 million years.

questions.q: What tall stone supports did the Greeks use to hold up temples?
questions.f: The Parthenon temple in Athens still stands on its columns today.

questions.q: What did the ancient Maya make a special drink from?
questions.f: Their chocolate drink was bitter and frothy, not sweet like today's.

questions.q: The printing press made books much faster than copying by hand.
questions.f: One press could print in a day what took a person months to copy.

questions.q: Which ancient people built the pyramids of Giza?
questions.f: Thousands of skilled workers, not slaves, built the Giza pyramids.

questions.q: What did knights hold contests of, charging on horseback with poles?
questions.f: A joust used long wooden lances that were meant to shatter safely.

questions.q: What did early farmers grow after they stopped only hunting?
questions.f: Growing wheat and barley let people settle in one place and build towns.

questions.q: How many 'Wonders of the Ancient World' were there?
questions.f: Only one of the seven, the Great Pyramid, still stands today.

questions.q: About how many stone blocks make up the Great Pyramid?
questions.f: Each block can weigh more than a large car.

questions.q: Which is the ONLY ancient Wonder still standing today?
questions.f: It has stood for around 4,500 years.

questions.q: Roughly how long ago did the last dinosaurs die out?
questions.f: A giant asteroid strike is the leading reason scientists give.

questions.q: A Tyrannosaurus rex tooth was about as long as a...?
questions.f: T. rex could crush bone with a bite stronger than any animal alive today.

questions.q: In Roman numerals, which number does the letter 'X' mean?
questions.f: In Roman numerals, 'C' means one hundred and 'M' means one thousand.

questions.q: What did the Rosetta Stone finally help scholars read?
questions.f: It repeated the same message in three scripts, cracking the code.

questions.q: Which explorer sailed around Africa to reach India by sea?
questions.f: His voyage opened a busy new sea route for trade with India.

questions.q: The Roman Colosseum could hold tens of thousands of spectators.
questions.f: About 50,000 people packed in to watch the shows.

questions.q: What was a knight's armour of linked metal rings called?
questions.f: A chainmail shirt could contain over 30,000 tiny iron rings.

questions.q: Which armoured dinosaur had a heavy bony club on its tail?
questions.f: One swing of that tail club could break a predator's bones.

questions.q: Which ancient Greek is remembered as the 'father of medicine'?
questions.f: Many doctors still promise to follow rules named after him.

questions.q: What powered the first big machines of the Industrial age?
questions.f: Boiling water made steam that pushed engines and trains along.

questions.q: What flying machine did the Wright brothers famously build?
questions.f: Their first flight in 1903 lasted only about 12 seconds.

questions.q: Which number system with a symbol for zero came from ancient India?
questions.f: The idea of zero as a number spread from India across the world.

questions.q: What sharp stone did early people strike to make sparks for fire?
questions.f: Hitting flint against iron sends out hot sparks to light tinder.

questions.q: Which Greek goddess was the Parthenon temple built to honour?
questions.f: The city of Athens was named after the goddess Athena.

questions.q: Some dinosaurs ate only plants, not meat.
questions.f: Long-necked giants like Brachiosaurus munched leaves all day long.

questions.q: Which famous queen ruled ancient Egypt near its end?
questions.f: Cleopatra could speak many languages and was a clever ruler.

questions.q: What large public pool did the city of Mohenjo-daro have?
questions.f: It was built watertight with bricks and tar over 4,000 years ago.

questions.q: What is the study of digging up ancient objects called?
questions.f: Archaeologists brush away dirt carefully so they don't break clues.

questions.q: Which Italian explorer travelled to China and met the great Kublai Khan?
questions.f: His stories of China amazed people back home in Europe.

questions.q: The Indus Valley cities had covered drains for dirty water.
questions.f: Their planning of streets and drains was ahead of its time.

questions.q: For how long was the Great Pyramid the tallest building on Earth?
questions.f: Nothing taller was built until a European cathedral in the 1300s.

questions.q: What did the ancient Chinese invent that we still write on today?
questions.f: They first made paper from mashed-up plant fibres and rags.

questions.q: How many legs did T. rex walk on?
questions.f: T. rex balanced on two powerful back legs, using its tail for balance.

questions.q: What did ancient Romans use as money?
questions.f: Roman coins often showed the face of the current emperor.

questions.q: Which of these did NOT exist in the Stone Age?
questions.f: Metal tools only came later, in the Bronze and Iron Ages.

questions.q: Which way of travelling came FIRST in history?
questions.f: For most of history, walking was the only way to get around.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT an ancient Egyptian thing?
questions.f: Television was invented only about 100 years ago.

questions.q: Which of these dinosaurs was a meat-eater?
questions.f: Velociraptor was actually about the size of a large turkey.

questions.q: Which explorer sailed the Pacific and reached Australia and New Zealand?
questions.f: Cook made detailed maps that sailors used for many years.

questions.q: Which ancient Wonder was a famous set of terraced gardens?
questions.f: No one is fully sure where these gardens really were.

questions.q: Which age came BEFORE the Bronze Age?
questions.f: People named these ages after the main material used for tools.

questions.q: Which of these was NOT a job in a medieval castle?
questions.f: Astronauts came about 900 years after the age of castles.

questions.q: Which invention let people travel much faster than a horse?
questions.f: Early steam trains could puff along faster than any galloping horse.

questions.q: Which of these giant ancient buildings was used for chariot races?
questions.f: Rome's Circus Maximus could seat around 150,000 fans.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT usually found inside a pyramid?
questions.f: Pyramids had hidden passages to fool robbers, but no pools.

questions.q: Which came LAST in history?
questions.f: The telephone was invented in 1876, the most recent of these.

questions.q: Which of these materials replaced chainmail as knights' armour?
questions.f: Shiny steel plates could turn aside arrows and blades.

questions.q: Ancient Egypt began before ancient Rome existed.
questions.f: Egypt's pyramids were already ancient when Rome was just a village.

questions.q: Which giant Ice Age animal is a relative of today's elephants?
questions.f: Frozen mammoths have been found almost perfectly preserved in ice.

questions.q: The Indus Valley civilisation is older than ancient Rome.
questions.f: Its cities thrived over 4,000 years ago, long before Rome grew big.

questions.q: Many small dinosaurs are now known to have had...?
questions.f: Feathers may have kept them warm long before any bird could fly.

questions.q: What is the correct order: page, then squire, then...?
questions.f: A boy trained for years as page and squire before earning knighthood.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a real ancient civilisation?
questions.f: Wakanda is a made-up land from comic-book stories, not real history.

questions.q: Which of these did NOT help ancient sailors find their way?
questions.f: Sailors read the night sky like a giant map before machines existed.

questions.q: Which ancient people are most famous for early democracy?
questions.f: 'Democracy' comes from Greek words meaning 'rule by the people'.

questions.q: Which is the biggest of these ancient structures?
questions.f: The Great Pyramid covers an area bigger than nine football pitches.

questions.q: Why did the Nile's yearly flood help Egyptian farmers?
c: It left rich mud for growing crops
It washed away all the sand
questions.f: Egyptians called their land 'the gift of the Nile' for this reason.

questions.q: What do most scientists think wiped out the dinosaurs?
questions.f: The asteroid left a crater over 150 kilometres wide near Mexico.

questions.q: Which single number idea from India made maths far easier?
questions.f: Without a zero, it is very hard to write large numbers neatly.

questions.q: Why do scientists think Stonehenge was built?
c: To track the Sun and seasons
questions.f: On midsummer morning, the Sun rises perfectly above one key stone.

questions.q: What breakthrough tool let ships know their direction far from land?
questions.f: A magnetic compass needle always swings to point roughly north.

questions.q: Why does tree sap called amber preserve ancient insects so well?
c: It hardens and seals them airtight
questions.f: Insects trapped in amber can look almost alive after millions of years.

questions.q: What was the single giant landmass when early dinosaurs appeared?
questions.f: Pangaea slowly split apart into today's separate continents.

questions.q: Why did the printing press change the world so greatly?
c: Books became cheap and spread ideas fast
questions.f: Suddenly ordinary people could own books and learn to read.

questions.q: What was the largest land animal that ever lived?
questions.f: Argentinosaurus may have weighed as much as 100 tonnes.

questions.q: What powder, invented in China, later changed warfare forever?
questions.f: Chinese inventors first used gunpowder for colourful fireworks.

questions.q: Which invention by Thomas Edison lit up homes cleanly?
questions.f: Edison tested thousands of materials before finding one that glowed for hours.

questions.q: Who is credited with inventing the telephone in 1876?
questions.f: His first words down the wire were a call to his assistant, Watson.

questions.q: Why is the Rosetta Stone so important to historians?
c: It shows the same text in three scripts
It is made of pure gold
It is the oldest rock on Earth
questions.f: Matching the scripts let scholars finally read Egyptian hieroglyphs.

questions.q: During the Ice Age, so much water froze that the seas were lower.
questions.f: Lower seas made land bridges that people and animals could walk across.

questions.q: What is the period of knights and castles in Europe often called?
questions.f: It is also called the medieval period and lasted about 1,000 years.

questions.q: Roads were so central to the Roman Empire that people said all roads lead to...?
questions.f: Rome's road network stretched over 400,000 kilometres in total.

questions.q: What secret writing of the Indus Valley can experts still NOT read?
questions.f: With no 'Rosetta Stone' for it, the Indus script stays a mystery.

questions.q: How do fossils usually form over millions of years?
c: Minerals slowly replace the bone with stone
The bone is painted by rain
questions.f: That is why we often say bones 'turn to stone' as fossils.

questions.q: Ancient people could send a message no faster than a horse could carry it.
questions.f: Before phones and radio, news travelled at the speed of the fastest rider.

questions.q: How do scientists often work out the age of a fossil?
c: By studying the rock layers around it
questions.f: Deeper rock layers are usually older, like pages near the bottom of a book.

questions.q: How many wheels does a bicycle have?
questions.f: "Bi" means two, so a bi-cycle rolls on two wheels.

questions.q: What do you push with your feet to make a bicycle go?
questions.f: Pushing the pedals spins a chain that turns the back wheel.

questions.q: Which machine flies high in the sky carrying lots of people?
questions.f: Big jets cruise higher than the tallest mountains on Earth.

questions.q: True or false: A rocket blasts off to travel into space.
questions.f: Rockets must reach about 28,000 km/h to circle the Earth.

questions.q: What spins fast on top of a helicopter?
questions.f: A helicopter's spinning blades are called rotors.

questions.q: What kind of machine floats on water and carries people?
questions.f: Even huge steel ships float because they push aside heavy water.

questions.q: What runs along metal rails instead of a road?
questions.f: Steel wheels on steel rails slide smoothly with very little friction.

questions.q: True or false: A submarine can travel deep underwater.
questions.f: Some submarines stay underwater for months without coming up.

questions.q: What do you squeeze to make a bicycle stop?
questions.f: Brakes rub the wheel and turn motion into heat to slow you.

questions.q: A playground slide works like which simple machine?
questions.f: A ramp, or inclined plane, lets you move up or down gently.

questions.q: Which tool twists screws into wood?
questions.f: A screw is really a ramp wrapped around a pole!

questions.q: What do you pull to raise a flag up a tall pole?
questions.f: A pulley changes the direction of your pull so lifting feels easier.

questions.q: What giant spinning wheel do you ride at a fair?
questions.f: The first Ferris wheel in 1893 could carry over 2,000 people!

questions.q: Which kitchen machine keeps your food cold?
questions.f: Before fridges, families kept food cold with delivered blocks of ice.

questions.q: Which machine washes your dirty clothes with water?
questions.f: Long ago, washing clothes by hand could take a whole day.

questions.q: True or false: A car needs fuel or electricity to move.
questions.f: Petrol cars burn fuel; electric cars store power in big batteries.

questions.q: What do you buckle up in a car to stay safe?
questions.f: Volvo gave away its seatbelt design free so every car could use it.

questions.q: What shines light on the road at the front of a car?
questions.f: Early car headlights burned gas flames, like little lanterns.

questions.q: Which machine has a siren and a long ladder to fight fires?
questions.f: The tallest fire-truck ladders reach higher than a ten-story building.

questions.q: What do you turn to steer a car?
questions.f: The very first cars were steered with a stick, like a boat's tiller.

questions.q: What round part rolls to help bikes and cars move along?
questions.f: People invented the wheel more than 5,000 years ago.

questions.q: True or false: A kite has an engine to fly.
questions.f: A kite has no engine — it rides on the moving wind instead.

questions.q: Which machine sucks up dust and dirt from the floor?
questions.f: A vacuum uses a spinning fan to suck air and dust into a bag.

questions.q: Which machine washes a pile of dirty dishes for you?
questions.f: A dishwasher sprays hot water to blast food off the plates.

questions.q: What floats up into the sky using hot air inside it?
questions.f: Hot air is lighter than cool air, so the balloon rises.

questions.q: What do you climb to reach a high shelf or roof?
questions.f: A ladder's rungs are like tiny steps you can carry anywhere.

questions.q: Which long yellow vehicle carries children to school?
questions.f: School buses are painted bright yellow so they're easy to spot.

questions.q: What has two wheels and a loud engine, like a fast bicycle?
questions.f: A motorcycle rider leans into corners to help it turn.

questions.q: Which machine lifts people up floors in a tall building?
questions.f: Elevators use strong cables and pulleys to lift the room-sized box.

questions.q: What machine takes a photograph to save a picture?
questions.f: A camera captures light through a lens to freeze a moment.

questions.q: Which two brothers built and flew the first powered airplane?
questions.f: Their first flight in 1903 lasted only about 12 seconds.

questions.q: A see-saw is an example of which simple machine?
questions.f: A see-saw balances on a middle point called the fulcrum.

questions.q: True or false: Maglev trains float above the track using magnets.
questions.f: With nothing touching the rails, the ride is smooth and very quiet.

questions.q: What is a ramp, or inclined plane, good for?
questions.f: A ramp trades a longer path for an easier climb.

questions.q: What pushes most boats and ships through the water?
questions.f: A spinning propeller screws through water like a fan through air.

questions.q: Which vehicle is built to travel deep under the sea?
questions.f: Submarines dive by filling tanks with water to grow heavier.

questions.q: A screw is which simple machine in disguise?
c: A ramp wrapped around a pole
questions.f: That spiral ridge, called the thread, grips tightly as it turns.

questions.q: Who flies an airplane?
questions.f: Pilots practise for hours in copycat cockpits called simulators.

questions.q: What did Alexander Graham Bell famously invent?
questions.f: His first phone call in 1876 went to his helper in the next room.

questions.q: What is the main job of a car's engine?
c: To make power to move it
questions.f: Most engines make power by burning fuel in tiny controlled bursts.

questions.q: An axe blade or a knife is which simple machine?
questions.f: A wedge is really two ramps back-to-back that split things apart.

questions.q: What are gears?
c: Wheels with teeth that turn each other
questions.f: Gear teeth lock together so one wheel can spin another.

questions.q: What do a bicycle's gears help you do?
questions.f: Low gears make pedalling easy; high gears make you go fast.

questions.q: What is a robot?
c: A machine that can do tasks by itself
questions.f: The word 'robot' comes from a Czech word meaning hard work.

questions.q: What pushes a sailboat along the water?
questions.f: Sailors angle the sail to catch wind from many directions.

questions.q: What moving staircase carries you up without walking?
questions.f: An escalator's steps flatten out and fold away at the top.

questions.q: What is the round rubber part of a car wheel called?
questions.f: Tyres are filled with air to cushion every bump in the road.

questions.q: True or false: An airplane's wings help lift it into the air.
questions.f: Air rushing over the curved wing makes an upward push called lift.

questions.q: What is the flat steering part at the back of a boat called?
questions.f: Turning the rudder pushes water sideways and swings the boat around.

questions.q: What heavy metal object stops a boat from drifting away?
questions.f: The anchor digs into the seabed and grips the mud or sand.

questions.q: What machine keeps the time on your wrist?
questions.f: Old watches keep time with a tiny coiled spring and gears.

questions.q: True or false: A helicopter can hover, staying still in the air.
questions.f: Hovering lets helicopters rescue people from cliffs and rooftops.

questions.q: What do we call a robot vehicle that explores other planets?
questions.f: Rovers have driven for years across the dusty surface of Mars.

questions.q: What long-armed machine lifts heavy loads at a building site?
questions.f: Tall tower cranes are built taller as the building grows.

questions.q: What machine prints words and pictures onto paper?
questions.f: Some printers spray millions of tiny ink droplets every second.

questions.q: Which invention gives light by heating a thin wire?
questions.f: Edison tested thousands of materials to find one that glowed well.

questions.q: What machine mixes food by spinning blades very fast?
questions.f: Whirling blades chop and swirl food into a smooth mixture.

questions.q: True or false: The first cars were steered with a stick, not a wheel.
questions.f: That steering stick was called a tiller, just like on a small boat.

questions.q: What is a train's front vehicle that pulls the carriages called?
questions.f: Locomotives once ran on steam, then diesel, and now often electricity.

questions.q: Which machine copies pages by shining bright light on them?
questions.f: A photocopier uses static electricity to stick ink powder to paper.

questions.q: How long did the Wright brothers' first flight last?
questions.f: In those 12 seconds the plane flew about the length of a jumbo jet.

questions.q: How many wheels does a large truck with a trailer usually have?
questions.f: That's why big trucks are nicknamed 'eighteen-wheelers'.

questions.q: How many types of simple machine are there?
questions.f: Lever, wheel, pulley, ramp, wedge, and screw — six in all.

questions.q: True or false: The very first bicycles had no pedals at all.
questions.f: Riders pushed along with their feet, like on a scooter.

questions.q: What does a maglev train use instead of wheels?
questions.f: Test maglev trains have raced at over 600 km/h in Japan.

questions.q: About how fast must a rocket travel to orbit the Earth?
questions.f: That's around eight kilometres every single second!

questions.q: Which country built the world's first high-speed 'bullet train'?
questions.f: Japan's Shinkansen started whisking passengers along in 1964.

questions.q: What does a car engine burn to make power?
c: A mix of fuel and air
questions.f: Tiny sparks light the mixture, and the pushes turn the wheels.

questions.q: What helps a moving bicycle stay balanced and upright?
questions.f: Steer slightly toward a lean and the bike straightens itself up.

questions.q: Who invented the World Wide Web in 1989?
questions.f: He gave his web-sharing idea to the whole world for free.

questions.q: Who built the first practical petrol-powered car in the 1880s?
questions.f: His three-wheeled 'Motorwagen' is seen as the first modern car.

questions.q: What shape gives an airplane wing its lifting power?
questions.f: Air speeds over the curved top, lowering the pressure and lifting the wing.

questions.q: Which simple machine is hidden inside a doorknob?
questions.f: Turning the wide knob easily twists the thin rod inside.

questions.q: True or false: A submarine dives by filling tanks with water.
questions.f: These are called ballast tanks; blowing them empty makes it rise.

questions.q: How does a zipper hold its two sides tightly together?
questions.f: A little slider hooks the teeth together as it moves along.

questions.q: How does Velcro stick two pieces together?
questions.f: It was inspired by prickly plant burrs that cling to fur.

questions.q: What does a helicopter's small tail rotor stop it from doing?
questions.f: Without it, the body would spin the opposite way to the top blades.

questions.q: What powers a steam engine?
questions.f: Steam engines helped power the factories of the Industrial Revolution.

questions.q: True or false: Flying faster than the speed of sound is called supersonic.
questions.f: When a plane breaks the sound barrier it can make a loud 'boom'.

questions.q: What do differently sized gears change as they turn together?
questions.f: A small gear driving a big gear turns it slower but with more force.

questions.q: Which invention by Gutenberg spread books around the world?
questions.f: Before it, every single book had to be copied slowly by hand.

questions.q: How many wheels does a standard skateboard have?
questions.f: Each wheel spins on tiny metal rings called bearings.

questions.q: Which retired plane could fly faster than the speed of sound?
questions.f: Concorde crossed the whole Atlantic Ocean in under four hours.

questions.q: True or false: A bicycle is one of the most efficient machines ever.
questions.f: It turns almost all your leg power straight into smooth motion.

questions.q: What is the moving belt that carries luggage at airports?
questions.f: Conveyor belts also move parcels, food, and car parts in factories.

questions.q: What robotic machine is often used to build cars in factories?
questions.f: These strong arms weld and paint car bodies without ever tiring.

questions.q: What machine part stores energy by coiling tightly up?
questions.f: A wound spring slowly releases energy to run clocks and wind-up toys.

questions.q: Who improved the steam engine, giving us the power unit 'watt'?
questions.f: We measure power in watts, named in his honour.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a simple machine?
questions.f: The six simple machines are all far older and far simpler.

questions.q: Which of these usually travels the fastest?
questions.f: Passenger jets cruise at around 900 km/h, high above the weather.

questions.q: Which of these was invented first, thousands of years ago?
questions.f: People were rolling wheels more than 5,000 years ago.

questions.q: Which vehicle can run its engine where there is no air?
questions.f: Rockets carry their own oxygen, so they work in empty space.

questions.q: True or false: A big gear turning a small gear makes the small one spin faster.
questions.f: Fewer teeth mean the little gear must whirl around more times.

questions.q: Which simple machine best helps roll a heavy barrel onto a truck?
questions.f: The gentle slope trades a longer push for a much easier lift.

questions.q: Which of these flies with NO engine at all?
questions.f: Gliders ride on rising warm air to stay up for hours.

questions.q: Which of these normally travels on rails?
questions.f: Trams share city streets but run on smooth metal tracks.

questions.q: Which of these is the largest vehicle?
questions.f: The biggest container ships are longer than four football pitches.

questions.q: True or false: A pulley with more wheels lets you lift with less effort.
questions.f: You pull more rope, but each pull feels much lighter.

questions.q: Which of these was invented most recently?
questions.f: Smartphones put a phone, camera, and computer in one pocket.

questions.q: Which of these needs a long runway to take off?
questions.f: Jumbo jets speed up to about 290 km/h before lifting off.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT powered by an engine?
questions.f: A sailboat borrows its power from the free, blowing wind.

questions.q: Which machine would you use to see something too tiny for your eyes?
questions.f: Powerful microscopes can reveal cells, germs, and even atoms.

questions.q: True or false: Helicopters can fly backwards and sideways.
questions.f: Tilting the spinning rotor lets them slide in any direction.

questions.q: Which part of a bicycle passes your pedalling to the back wheel?
questions.f: The chain loops over toothed gears called sprockets.

questions.q: Which of these needs the most force to get moving?
questions.f: A heavy train can need over a kilometre of track just to stop.

questions.q: Which of these came first in history?
questions.f: Steam locomotives were pulling passengers back in the 1820s.

questions.q: True or false: A car's brakes turn its motion into heat to stop it.
questions.f: That's why brakes can get hot enough to smell after a big stop.

questions.q: Which vehicle is pushed along by a powerful jet engine?
questions.f: Jet engines shoot hot air backwards to thrust the plane forward.

questions.q: What is a robot usually best at, compared with a person?
c: Repeating the exact same task many times
questions.f: Factory robots can repeat a move perfectly thousands of times a day.

questions.q: A wheelbarrow makes lifting easier by acting as which simple machine?
questions.f: The wheel is the pivot, so your load feels lighter to lift.

questions.q: Why do steel train wheels on steel rails save so much energy?
questions.f: Low friction means a small engine can pull a very heavy train.

questions.q: What force pulls a bicycle and rider down a hill?
questions.f: Gravity speeds you up going down, and works against you going up.

questions.q: Why can a heavy steel ship float instead of sinking?
c: It pushes aside water weighing more than the ship
It is full of only air
questions.f: This upward push is called buoyancy, discovered by Archimedes.

questions.q: True or false: A rocket flies by pushing gas backwards, so it is pushed forward.
questions.f: For every push there is an equal push back — Newton's third law.

questions.q: What is the record test speed of the fastest maglev train?
questions.f: Japan's maglev hit 603 km/h in 2015 — faster than a race car.

questions.q: Why do airplane wings lift the plane upward?
c: Faster air on top lowers the pressure
The wings flap like a bird
questions.f: The wing's curved shape speeds up the air flowing over its top.

questions.q: How does a long lever let a small push move a huge load?
c: It trades extra distance for extra force
questions.f: Push the long end far, and the short end lifts a lot with less effort.

questions.q: What is the fastest human-made machine ever built?
questions.f: It races around the Sun at about 700,000 km/h.

questions.q: True or false: Gears can swap speed for turning power, but not make free energy.
questions.f: Machines can trade one thing for another, but never get something for nothing.

questions.q: Why does a helicopter need a spinning tail rotor?
c: To stop its body spinning the other way
questions.f: The main rotor tries to twist the body, so the tail rotor pushes back.

questions.q: What made the Concorde airliner so special?
c: It flew faster than the speed of sound
questions.f: Concorde cruised at about 2,180 km/h, twice the speed of sound.

questions.q: Who sketched a flying 'aerial screw' machine over 500 years ago?
questions.f: His helicopter-like drawing was made long before real ones flew.

questions.q: True or false: Friction helps bike brakes grip but also makes machines heat up.
questions.f: Engineers add oil to slippery parts to fight unwanted friction.

questions.q: Why do gears with different numbers of teeth change the speed?
c: The gear ratio sets how many times each turns
