questions.f: Two turns of a small gear may give just one turn of a big one.

questions.q: How does a submarine rise back up to the surface?
c: It pushes water out of its ballast tanks
questions.f: Blowing the tanks empty with air makes the submarine lighter than water.

questions.q: What did the handy zipper replace on many boots and clothes?
questions.f: One quick pull now does the work of fastening many buttons.

questions.q: Which is the largest passenger airplane, with two full decks?
questions.f: An A380 can carry more than 800 passengers across its two floors.

questions.q: True or false: A rocket works in space because it carries its own oxygen.
questions.f: There is no air in space, so a rocket must bring what it needs to burn.

questions.q: Why is a maglev train smoother and quieter than a normal train?
questions.f: Floating on magnets means there is almost nothing to rattle or squeak.

questions.q: What do engineers call the twisting or turning force in a machine?
questions.f: A tight jar lid needs plenty of torque from your hand to open.

questions.q: How many strings does a standard violin have?
questions.f: A violin has 4 strings and no frets, so players find every note by feel!

questions.q: What do you usually hit to play a drum?
questions.f: Drums make sound when a stretched skin vibrates after you hit it.

questions.q: How many keys does a full-size piano have?
questions.f: A piano has 88 keys — 52 white ones and 36 black ones.

questions.q: How do you make a trumpet sound?
questions.f: Trumpet players buzz their lips into the mouthpiece to make sound.

questions.q: Which instrument do you blow air across to play?
questions.f: You blow across the flute's hole, like blowing across a bottle top.

questions.q: Which of these is a percussion instrument?
questions.f: Percussion instruments make sound when you hit, shake, or scrape them.

questions.q: A guitar makes sound when its strings vibrate.
questions.f: Plucking a string makes it wobble fast, and that wobble is the sound.

questions.q: How many strings does a ukulele usually have?
questions.f: The tiny ukulele has just 4 strings and comes from Hawaii.

questions.q: Which body part do singers use to make their voice?
questions.f: Air rushing past your vocal cords makes them vibrate and sing.

questions.q: What does a microphone do?
questions.f: A microphone turns your voice into electricity so speakers can boom it out.

questions.q: Which instrument has black and white keys?
questions.f: You press piano keys and little hammers inside tap the strings.

questions.q: Which of these instruments do you shake to play?
questions.f: Maracas rattle because tiny beads bounce inside them.

questions.q: You blow into a flute to make music.
questions.f: Air blown across the flute's hole vibrates and makes the note.

questions.q: What do you call a group of people singing together?
questions.f: In a choir, different voices blend to make rich, layered sound.

questions.q: Which of these is a wind instrument?
questions.f: Wind instruments make sound from air moving through a tube.

questions.q: What do you tap your foot to when you hear music?
questions.f: The beat is the steady pulse that keeps everyone in time.

questions.q: Which instrument is the biggest in the string family?
questions.f: The double bass is so tall players often stand up to play it.

questions.q: What do you use to play a violin?
questions.f: The bow is strung with horsehair that grips the strings to make them sing.

questions.q: Drums belong to the percussion family.
questions.f: Anything you strike or shake for sound is percussion.

questions.q: Which instrument do you squeeze while pressing keys to play?
questions.f: You pump the accordion's bellows like a lung to push air over the reeds.

questions.q: What is a song's words called?
questions.f: Lyrics are the words we sing along to in a song.

questions.q: Which instrument is shaped like a large golden horn you blow?
questions.f: Brass instruments like the trumpet are made of shiny metal.

questions.q: How do maracas make their sound?
questions.f: Shaking maracas makes the beads bounce and rattle against the shell.

questions.q: Clapping your hands can make a rhythm.
questions.f: Your hands are a percussion instrument you always carry with you!

questions.q: Which of these do you dance to?
questions.f: Dancing is moving your body in time with music's beat.

questions.q: Which instrument has a keyboard AND uses air pumped through pipes?
questions.f: A pipe organ pushes air through huge pipes to make giant sounds.

questions.q: What is the leader of an orchestra called?
questions.f: The conductor waves a baton to keep all the musicians together.

questions.q: Which instrument do you strum?
questions.f: Strumming means brushing your hand across several strings at once.

questions.q: A whistle makes sound when air moves through it.
questions.f: Air swirling inside a whistle vibrates and makes that sharp tweet.

questions.q: Which family does the trumpet belong to?
questions.f: Brass instruments are metal, and you buzz your lips to play them.

questions.q: Which instrument has the most strings: harp, violin, or guitar?
questions.f: A concert harp can have 47 strings — far more than a 6-string guitar.

questions.q: What makes sound travel to your ears?
questions.f: Sound is vibrations that ripple through the air like invisible waves.

questions.q: Which drum from India is played with the fingers and palms?
questions.f: The tabla is a pair of hand drums used in Indian classical music.

questions.q: Which instrument comes from Australia's Aboriginal people?
questions.f: The didgeridoo is a long wooden tube that makes a deep droning sound.

questions.q: Which instrument from Scotland uses a bag of air?
questions.f: A piper squeezes the bag to keep air flowing so the sound never stops.

questions.q: Which Indian string instrument did Ravi Shankar make famous?
questions.f: The sitar has extra strings that hum along and give it a shimmering sound.

questions.q: A shorter, tighter string makes a sound that is…
questions.f: Short tight strings vibrate faster, and faster vibrations sound higher.

questions.q: An orchestra has four main instrument families.
questions.f: They are strings, woodwind, brass, and percussion.

questions.q: Which of these is a brass instrument?
questions.f: The trombone changes notes by sliding a long metal tube in and out.

questions.q: What do we call how fast or slow music goes?
questions.f: Tempo is Italian for 'time' — a fast tempo makes music feel exciting.

questions.q: Which of these instruments is a woodwind?
questions.f: Woodwinds like the clarinet use a thin reed that vibrates when you blow.

questions.q: How does a cello sound compared to a violin?
questions.f: The cello is bigger, and bigger instruments make deeper, lower sounds.

questions.q: What is a very loud sound in music called?
questions.f: 'Forte' means loud in Italian, and 'piano' means soft.

questions.q: Which instrument has bars you hit with mallets?
questions.f: Each xylophone bar is a different length, so each makes a different note.

questions.q: The word 'piano' is short for 'pianoforte'.
questions.f: It means 'soft-loud' because the piano can play both quiet and loud.

questions.q: Which instrument uses a reed to make its sound?
questions.f: The oboe uses two reeds that buzz together when you blow through them.

questions.q: Which famous composer kept writing music after going deaf?
questions.f: Beethoven lost his hearing but 'felt' the music through vibrations.

questions.q: What do we call a steady pattern of long and short sounds?
questions.f: Rhythm is how the beats and notes are spaced out in time.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a string instrument?
questions.f: The flute is a woodwind — it has no strings, just air.

questions.q: Which instrument do you play with a bow and hold under your chin?
questions.f: You tuck the violin under your chin and draw the bow across its strings.

questions.q: Bigger instruments usually make lower sounds.
questions.f: A big double bass rumbles low while a tiny violin sings high.

questions.q: Which dance from Argentina is danced by two people close together?
questions.f: The tango began in the streets of Buenos Aires long ago.

questions.q: Which energetic folk dance comes from Punjab, India?
questions.f: Bhangra was danced by farmers celebrating the harvest festival.

questions.q: What do dancers who spin on their heads perform?
questions.f: Breakdancing started on the streets of New York in the 1970s.

questions.q: Which instrument has pedals, strings, and is played standing up?
questions.f: A harpist plucks the strings with their fingers and changes notes with foot pedals.

questions.q: What is a group of musicians playing together called?
questions.f: A band can have singers, guitars, drums, and more all together.

questions.q: A xylophone is a percussion instrument.
questions.f: You hit its bars with mallets, so it belongs to percussion.

questions.q: Which instrument makes sound by hitting cymbals together?
questions.f: Two metal cymbals crash to make a big shimmering clash.

questions.q: What is it called when you sing without any instruments?
questions.f: 'A cappella' means singing using only voices, no instruments at all.

questions.q: Which instrument family includes the tuba and the trumpet?
questions.f: The tuba is the biggest brass instrument and makes the lowest sounds.

questions.q: How many keys on a piano are black?
questions.f: The 36 black keys are grouped in twos and threes to help you find notes.

questions.q: Sound travels faster through which of these?
questions.f: Sound zips about four times faster in water than in air.

questions.q: How many notes are in a musical octave?
questions.f: An octave runs from one note to the same note higher, like do to do.

questions.q: Which instrument has the highest voice in a string quartet?
questions.f: A string quartet has two violins, a viola, and a cello.

questions.q: What is measured in 'beats per minute'?
questions.f: A fast song might be 140 beats per minute; a slow one about 60.

questions.q: Why can't sound travel through outer space?
c: There is no air to vibrate
questions.f: Sound needs a material to travel through, and space is empty.

questions.q: How many strings does a standard classical guitar have?
questions.f: Each of the 6 strings is a different thickness to make different notes.

questions.q: A higher pitch means the air is vibrating faster.
questions.f: Fast vibrations sound high; slow vibrations sound low.

questions.q: What is the name for a very high female singing voice?
questions.f: Soprano is the highest voice; bass is the lowest.

questions.q: What is the lowest male singing voice called?
questions.f: A bass singer can rumble notes so low they seem to shake the floor.

questions.q: What is the small stick a conductor waves to lead the orchestra?
questions.f: The baton helps every musician see the beat even from the back row.

questions.q: What are the three foot pedals on a grand piano for?
c: Changing how notes ring and sustain
questions.f: The right pedal lets notes ring on even after you lift your fingers.

questions.q: What does the word 'quartet' tell you about the group's size?
questions.f: 'Quartet' comes from the word for four, so it always means four musicians.

questions.q: What is the curved sign that means 'stay silent' in music called?
questions.f: Rests are just as important as notes — silence is part of the music.

questions.q: The largest instrument in an orchestra's string section is the double bass.
questions.f: The double bass is taller than most adults and plays the deepest notes.

questions.q: What do we call notes played one after another going up or down?
questions.f: Practising scales helps musicians' fingers learn where every note lives.

questions.q: Which of these is a ballet move done on the tips of the toes?
questions.f: Ballet dancers wear special stiff shoes to balance en pointe.

questions.q: What are the five lines that music is written on called?
questions.f: Notes sit on the lines and in the spaces of the staff.

questions.q: How many valves does a standard trumpet have?
questions.f: With just three valves a trumpet can still play dozens of notes.

questions.q: How does an echo happen?
questions.f: Sound waves bounce off a wall or cliff and come back to your ears.

questions.q: Middle C is a note near the center of a piano keyboard.
questions.f: Middle C sits right in the middle and helps players find their place.

questions.q: What is a song sung to help a baby sleep called?
questions.f: Lullabies have slow, gentle rhythms that feel calm and soothing.

questions.q: Which dance from Spain uses stamping feet and clapping?
questions.f: Flamenco dancers wear shoes with nails in the soles for loud stamps.

questions.q: Which part of your body helps you keep balance while dancing?
questions.f: Tiny fluid-filled tubes in your ears sense which way is up.

questions.q: What is the metal part of a woodwind reed usually made from?
questions.f: Clarinet and oboe reeds are cut from a tall grass-like cane plant.

questions.q: How many sections does a typical drum kit's cymbals and drums make?
questions.f: A drum kit lets one player use hands and feet to play many parts at once.

questions.q: The Hawaiian hula dance uses hand movements to tell a story.
questions.f: In hula, gentle hand gestures can mean waves, rain, or trees.

questions.q: What do you call two notes played at the same time that sound nice together?
questions.f: Harmony is when different notes blend to make a fuller sound.

questions.q: Which instrument is NOT part of the woodwind family?
questions.f: The trumpet is brass — you buzz your lips instead of blowing across a reed or hole.

questions.q: Order these from lowest to highest: cello, double bass, violin. Which is lowest?
questions.f: The bigger the string instrument, the lower it sounds — bass is biggest.

questions.q: What do we call a group of exactly eight musicians?
questions.f: 'Oct' means eight, like the eight arms of an octopus.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a brass instrument?
questions.f: Surprise — the saxophone is a woodwind because it uses a reed, not lips.

questions.q: Why does a guitarist press a string against the frets?
questions.f: Pressing a fret shortens the string, so it vibrates faster and sounds higher.

questions.q: Which giant instrument is built into churches, called the king of instruments?
questions.f: A big pipe organ can have thousands of pipes and fill a whole cathedral.

questions.q: A trombone changes its notes using a sliding tube instead of valves.
questions.f: Moving the slide makes the air tube longer or shorter to change the pitch.

questions.q: Which of these makes sound when struck, not blown or bowed?
questions.f: You hit a xylophone's bars, so it belongs to the percussion family.

questions.q: Rank by pitch: which of these sounds the HIGHEST?
questions.f: The piccolo is a tiny flute that plays the highest notes in the orchestra.

questions.q: Which country did the composer Beethoven come from?
questions.f: Beethoven was born in Bonn, Germany, over 250 years ago.

questions.q: Which instrument uses a longer air column to make lower notes?
questions.f: The tuba's tubing is over 5 metres long if you unrolled it!

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a way to play a violin?
questions.f: You can bow, pluck (pizzicato), or tap a violin — but never blow it.

questions.q: Which section of an orchestra usually has the most players?
questions.f: An orchestra can have over 30 string players but only a few tubas.

questions.q: The saxophone is made of brass but counts as a woodwind instrument.
questions.f: It's the reed, not the metal, that puts the sax in the woodwind family.

questions.q: Which pair of instruments both use a bow?
questions.f: Both the violin and cello are bowed string instruments.

questions.q: Which of these dances is traditionally performed on ice?
questions.f: Ice dancers glide and spin to music on frozen rinks.

questions.q: Which string instrument is plucked and has frets, unlike a violin?
questions.f: A guitar's frets are the metal bars that help you find each note.

questions.q: Which musical term means gradually getting louder?
questions.f: A crescendo builds the sound bigger and bigger, like a rising wave.

questions.q: A conductor makes no sound but keeps the whole orchestra together.
questions.f: The conductor's waving hands show the tempo and when each part comes in.

questions.q: Which instrument's name means 'soft-loud' in Italian?
questions.f: It was named because, unlike older keyboards, it could play soft AND loud.

questions.q: Which of these would make the LOWEST sound?
questions.f: Long, thick, loose strings vibrate slowly, giving deep low notes.

questions.q: Which dance style features fast footwork tapping out rhythms with metal-tipped shoes?
questions.f: Tap shoes have metal plates that click loudly on the floor like a drum.

questions.q: Why does a thicker guitar string sound lower than a thin one?
questions.f: Heavier strings are harder to wobble, so they vibrate slower and sound deeper.

questions.q: What is the scientific word for how high or low a sound is?
questions.f: Pitch depends on frequency — how many times a second something vibrates.

questions.q: Frequency is measured in units called what?
questions.f: A sound at 440 hertz vibrates 440 times every single second.

questions.q: Why does an opera singer's high note sometimes shatter a glass?
c: The note matches the glass's natural vibration
The glass is thin from age
questions.f: When sound matches a glass's resonant frequency, it shakes until it breaks.

questions.q: What is the highest-pitched instrument in a standard orchestra?
questions.f: The piccolo is a mini flute that can pierce right over the whole orchestra.

questions.q: Sound cannot travel through the vacuum of space.
questions.f: With no air or material to vibrate, sound waves have nothing to move through.

questions.q: Which composer wrote his famous Ninth Symphony while completely deaf?
questions.f: Beethoven never heard his Ninth Symphony, yet it became one of the world's most loved pieces.

questions.q: Why does a longer organ pipe make a lower note?
c: Longer air columns vibrate more slowly
It is made of thicker metal
questions.f: The longest organ pipes are taller than a house and rumble the deepest notes.

questions.q: What is it called when a sound wave bounces back to you?
questions.f: Bats and dolphins use bouncing sound, called echolocation, to 'see' with their ears.

questions.q: Which of these instruments makes sound WITHOUT strings, reeds, or blowing?
questions.f: You play a theremin by waving your hands near antennas — never touching it!

questions.q: Why do you tune a violin string tighter to raise its pitch?
questions.f: Turning the peg tightens the string so it vibrates faster and sounds higher.

questions.q: What word describes why a flute and violin sound different?
questions.f: Timbre (say 'TAM-ber') is why every instrument has its own unique voice.

questions.q: A drum makes sound because its stretched skin vibrates up and down.
questions.f: Hitting the drumhead pushes it in and out, sending sound waves through the air.

questions.q: Which instrument family makes sound from a vibrating column of air?
questions.f: In flutes, trumpets and organs, it's the air inside that actually vibrates.

questions.q: What is the lowest and largest brass instrument in the orchestra?
questions.f: The tuba's deep notes are the foundation the whole brass section sits on.

questions.q: Why do orchestras tune all instruments to the same note before playing?
c: So the notes match and don't clash
questions.f: Musicians tune to an 'A' note, usually given by the oboe, so they sound in harmony.

questions.q: What does the sitar have that a guitar does not, giving its shimmering sound?
c: Extra 'sympathetic' strings that vibrate on their own
questions.f: The sitar's spare strings hum along by themselves when other strings play.

questions.q: What is a piece where instruments copy each other, like a round?
questions.f: 'Row, Row, Row Your Boat' sung in a round is a simple canon.

questions.q: The didgeridoo is played using a trick called circular breathing.
questions.f: Players breathe in through the nose while pushing out air stored in their cheeks, so the drone never stops.

questions.q: What is the superstar solo moment where one player shows off alone called?
questions.f: In a cadenza the orchestra pauses so a soloist can dazzle the audience.

questions.q: Which Greek god is the king of all the gods?
questions.f: Zeus threw thunderbolts that were forged by giant one-eyed Cyclopes.

questions.q: Thor, the Norse god of thunder, carries a magic what?
questions.f: Thor's hammer, Mjolnir, always flies back to his hand after he throws it.

questions.q: A unicorn is famous for having one what on its forehead?
questions.f: The unicorn is the official national animal of Scotland.

questions.q: Which legendary bird is reborn from its own ashes?
questions.f: Legends say only one phoenix lives in the whole world at a time.

questions.q: Medusa had wriggling snakes instead of what?
questions.f: In the myths, looking straight at Medusa would turn you to stone.

questions.q: Ganesha, a beloved Hindu god, has the head of which animal?
questions.f: Ganesha's favorite treat is a sweet dumpling called a modak.

questions.q: A mermaid is half human and half fish.
questions.f: Long ago, sailors sometimes mistook manatees for mermaids.

questions.q: Hercules is a famous Greek hero known for being incredibly what?
questions.f: Hercules is the Roman name; the Greeks called this hero Heracles.

questions.q: In stories, dragons often breathe out what?
questions.f: The flag of Wales has a big red dragon right in the middle of it.

questions.q: Pegasus is a magical horse with what special feature?
questions.f: There is a horse-shaped group of stars in the night sky named Pegasus.

questions.q: Hanuman, a brave hero of Indian epics, is what kind of animal?
questions.f: In the Ramayana, Hanuman leaps all the way across the ocean in one giant jump.

questions.q: A cyclops is a giant with just one big eye.
questions.f: A cyclops's single eye sits right in the middle of its forehead.

questions.q: Anubis, an Egyptian god, has the head of which animal?
questions.f: Anubis was believed to gently guide people in Egyptian afterlife stories.

questions.q: A centaur is half human and half what?
questions.f: The wise centaur Chiron was a teacher to many Greek heroes.

questions.q: Which Greek god of the sea carries a three-pronged spear?
questions.f: Poseidon's three-pronged spear is called a trident.

questions.q: Which magical being grants wishes in old Arabic tales?
questions.f: In Arabic stories these wish-granters are called jinn.

questions.q: The Minotaur has the body of a man and the head of a what?
questions.f: The Minotaur lived in a twisting maze called the Labyrinth.

questions.q: Which flying, treasure-guarding creature appears in fairy tales?
questions.f: In the old tale of Beowulf, a dragon guards a huge pile of gold.

questions.q: Ra, an important Egyptian god, is the god of the what?
questions.f: Egyptians believed Ra sailed across the sky in a boat each day.

questions.q: A griffin has the body of a lion and the head of which bird?
questions.f: Old legends said griffins guarded mountains full of gold.

questions.q: Loki, a Norse god, is well known as a trickster.
questions.f: Loki could shape-shift into a fish, a fly, or even a horse.

questions.q: Which one-eyed giants forged Zeus's thunderbolts?
questions.f: Each Cyclops has a single eye in the middle of its forehead.

questions.q: In Greek myth, who flew too close to the sun with wax wings?
questions.f: The sun melted the wax and the feathered wings fell apart.

questions.q: The Sphinx has a lion's body and the head of a what?
questions.f: The Greek Sphinx loved to stump travelers with tricky riddles.

questions.q: A phoenix bursts into flames and then rises again.
questions.f: A brand-new phoenix is born from the ashes of the old one.

questions.q: Which Greek messenger god wears winged sandals?
questions.f: The Romans called this speedy messenger god Mercury.

questions.q: In Norse myth, who is the wise, one-eyed chief of the gods?
questions.f: Odin had two ravens who flew the world and brought him news.

questions.q: A mermaid is usually said to live where?
questions.f: Explorer Christopher Columbus once wrote that he saw 'mermaids' — really manatees!

questions.q: Which Greek hero defeated the snake-haired Medusa?
questions.f: Perseus used his shiny shield like a mirror so he never looked at her directly.

questions.q: In Chinese stories, dragons are lucky and bring good fortune.
questions.f: Chinese emperors wore special robes decorated with dragons.

questions.q: On which mountain did the Greek gods live?
questions.f: Mount Olympus is a real mountain — the tallest in all of Greece!

questions.q: What is the Roman name for the Greek king of the gods, Zeus?
questions.f: Jupiter is also the name of the biggest planet in our Solar System.

questions.q: Which Roman god of war shares his name with a planet?
questions.f: Mars was the Roman version of the Greek war god Ares.

questions.q: In the Ramayana, who is the ten-headed villain that Rama battles?
questions.f: The festival of Dussehra celebrates Rama's victory over Ravana.

questions.q: Which strong Norse god protects both gods and humans?
questions.f: The day Thursday is named after Thor — 'Thor's day.'

questions.q: Excalibur is the famous sword of which legendary king?
questions.f: Young Arthur first proved he was king by pulling a sword from a stone.

questions.q: The Greek god Hades rules over which realm?
questions.f: A three-headed dog named Cerberus guards the gates of Hades's realm.

questions.q: Which Egyptian goddess is a great magician and mother of Horus?
questions.f: Isis was worshipped in Egypt for thousands of years.

questions.q: The Greek gods were said to eat a special food called ambrosia.
questions.f: They also drank a sweet drink called nectar to stay young forever.

questions.q: Which Greek hero was unbeatable except for one weak heel?
questions.f: Today we still call a person's one weak spot an 'Achilles heel.'

questions.q: In Norse myth, what is the name of the giant world-tree?
questions.f: Its huge branches were said to hold up the whole world.

questions.q: Which Egyptian god has the head of a falcon?
questions.f: The 'Eye of Horus' was a popular good-luck symbol in ancient Egypt.

questions.q: A famous lake monster is said to live in which Scottish loch?
questions.f: People nicknamed the mystery monster 'Nessie.'

questions.q: Cerberus, the guard dog of the Greek underworld, has three heads.
questions.f: In one story, beautiful music made Cerberus fall fast asleep.

questions.q: Which winged horse did the hero Bellerophon tame in Greek myth?
questions.f: Legends say Pegasus sprang from the neck of Medusa.

questions.q: What is the Roman name for the sea god Poseidon?
questions.f: The eighth planet, Neptune, is named after this sea god.

questions.q: In Hindu myths, which god is often shown with blue skin and a flute?
questions.f: Krishna's flute music was said to charm both people and animals.

questions.q: Who is the clever Greek hero of the ten-year journey in the Odyssey?
questions.f: His long trip home from the Trojan War took a full ten years.

questions.q: Which Egyptian sun god was believed to sail across the sky each day?
questions.f: Egyptians imagined a giant serpent tried to attack Ra's boat every night.

questions.q: In ancient Egypt, cats were seen as special and sacred.
questions.f: The cat-headed goddess Bastet was believed to protect people's homes.

questions.q: Which Greek goddess of wisdom is the city of Athens named after?
questions.f: The owl was Athena's special bird, a symbol of being wise.

questions.q: In Norse legends, where do brave warriors feast after their lives end?
questions.f: Valhalla is the great hall belonging to the god Odin.

questions.q: Which legendary English outlaw robbed the rich to help the poor?
questions.f: Robin Hood lived in Sherwood Forest with his band of Merry Men.

questions.q: Which giant many-armed sea monster from legend attacked ships?
questions.f: Real giant squid, longer than a school bus, may have inspired the Kraken.

questions.q: Which Greek goddess of love was born from sea foam?
questions.f: The Romans called this goddess of love Venus.

questions.q: The Egyptian god Anubis was believed to help guide people in the afterlife.
questions.f: Anubis was shown with the head of a jackal, a desert animal.

questions.q: Which fire-breathing Greek monster was part lion, goat, and snake?
questions.f: Today we call anything wildly mixed-together a 'chimera.'

questions.q: In the Mahabharata, which archer prince is guided by Lord Krishna?
questions.f: Krishna served as Arjuna's chariot driver and gave him wise advice.

questions.q: Which Greek god of music and light plays a golden lyre?
questions.f: In some myths Apollo drove the blazing sun across the sky.

questions.q: What glowing weapon does Zeus hurl down from the sky?
questions.f: The Cyclopes forged Zeus's thunderbolts deep in a fiery workshop.

questions.q: How many great labors did the Greek hero Hercules complete?
questions.f: One labor was cleaning enormous stables in just a single day.

questions.q: What did Odin trade for a drink from the well of wisdom?
questions.f: Odin's two ravens were named Huginn and Muninn — 'Thought' and 'Memory.'

questions.q: How many heads did the Hydra grow back for each one cut off?
questions.f: Hercules finally beat it by burning each neck so no head could regrow.

questions.q: Which hero escaped the Labyrinth using a ball of thread?
questions.f: Princess Ariadne gave Theseus the thread so he could find his way back.

questions.q: Whose children in Norse myth include a giant wolf and a huge serpent?
questions.f: The wolf Fenrir was so strong the gods needed a magic ribbon to hold him.

questions.q: The Egyptian god Thoth, keeper of wisdom, has the head of which bird?
questions.f: Thoth was believed to have invented writing itself.

questions.q: Which Greek hero sailed on the ship Argo to find the Golden Fleece?
questions.f: Jason's brave crew were called the Argonauts.

questions.q: In Greek myth, King Midas turned everything he touched into gold.
questions.f: It became a big problem when even his dinner turned to solid gold!

questions.q: Which Greek Titan holds up the sky on his shoulders?
questions.f: We name books of maps 'atlases' after Atlas.

questions.q: What is the name of Thor's magical hammer?
questions.f: Legends said only someone truly worthy could even lift Mjolnir.

questions.q: In the Ramayana, which monkey hero helped build a bridge to Lanka?
questions.f: A whole army of monkeys carried stones to help build the bridge.

questions.q: Which Greek musician charmed animals and rocks with his lyre?
questions.f: His beautiful music once put the guard dog Cerberus to sleep.

questions.q: The Norse rainbow bridge to the gods' home is called Bifrost.
questions.f: A watchful god named Heimdall guarded the Bifrost bridge.

questions.q: What is the name of Odin's amazing eight-legged horse?
questions.f: Sleipnir was said to be the fastest horse in all the nine worlds.

questions.q: Which Egyptian god of the desert and storms was the rival of Osiris?
questions.f: Set was linked to sandstorms and the wild, dry desert.

questions.q: In Greek myth, the goddess Demeter brings which season when she is sad?
questions.f: Her daughter Persephone spends part of each year in the underworld.

questions.q: Which mighty hero of the Mahabharata is famous for enormous strength?
questions.f: Bhima was said to have the strength of many elephants combined.

questions.q: The Greek hero Achilles was said to be unbeatable except at his heel.
questions.f: An 'Achilles heel' now means a strong person's single weak point.

questions.q: Which singing creatures in Greek myth lured sailors toward the rocks?
questions.f: Odysseus had his crew plug their ears with wax to pass the Sirens safely.

questions.q: Which fruit did Persephone eat that tied her to the underworld?
questions.f: She ate a few seeds, so she must return underground for part of every year.

questions.q: In Greek myth, how many Fate sisters spun the thread of each life?
questions.f: One sister spun the thread, one measured it, and one cut it.

questions.q: In Hindu myth, the god Vishnu appears on Earth in forms called avatars.
questions.f: Both Rama and Krishna are said to be avatars of Vishnu.

questions.q: Which Greek monster with a woman's face asked travelers a riddle?
questions.f: The hero Oedipus was the one who finally solved the Sphinx's riddle.

questions.q: What maze did the craftsman Daedalus build to trap the Minotaur?
questions.f: The Labyrinth was so twisty that no one could find the way out.

questions.q: Which gentle Norse god of light was loved by almost everyone?
questions.f: Baldur's mother asked everything in the world to promise to keep him safe.

questions.q: What magical cap made its wearer invisible in Greek myth?
questions.f: The hero Perseus used it to sneak past his enemies unseen.

questions.q: In Egyptian myth, a person's heart was weighed against what?
questions.f: A heart lighter than the feather of truth was believed to pass the test.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the Greek Olympian gods?
questions.f: Anubis is an Egyptian god, not a Greek one.

questions.q: Which Greek hero is famous for solving the Sphinx's riddle?
questions.f: The answer to the Sphinx's famous riddle was 'a human.'

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a Norse god?
questions.f: Ganesha is a much-loved Hindu god, celebrated across India.

questions.q: Which of these Greek beings is a monster, not a god?
questions.f: The Minotaur was a bull-headed monster who lived inside a maze.

questions.q: Which Roman goddess matches the Greek goddess of love, Aphrodite?
questions.f: The planet Venus shines brighter in our sky than any star.

questions.q: Which creature is a mix of an eagle and a lion?
questions.f: Griffins were said to guard mountains piled high with gold.

questions.q: Which of these is an Egyptian goddess, NOT a Greek one?
questions.f: Bastet was a cat goddess believed to protect people's homes.

questions.q: Which weapon belongs to Poseidon, not to Zeus?
questions.f: A trident is a three-pronged spear, perfect for the god of the sea.

questions.q: For a task needing super strength, which Greek hero would you call?
questions.f: Hercules completed twelve near-impossible labors.

questions.q: Roman gods were often the same as Greek ones, just with new names.
questions.f: The Greek god Zeus became the Roman god Jupiter.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a mythical creature but a real animal?
questions.f: The narwhal's long spiral tusk may have helped start unicorn legends!

questions.q: Which Egyptian god did farmers thank for the yearly Nile flood?
questions.f: The flood left behind rich black mud that helped crops grow.

questions.q: Which of these is a hero of the Ramayana, NOT a Greek myth?
questions.f: Rama's story is loved and retold across India and Southeast Asia.

questions.q: Which Greek creature is most horse-like?
questions.f: A centaur has a human's upper body joined to a horse's body.

questions.q: Rank by heads: which Greek monster grew the MOST?
questions.f: The Hydra could sprout two new heads for every one that was cut off.

questions.q: A phoenix and a griffin are both make-believe creatures.
questions.f: The phoenix is reborn in fire, while the griffin is part eagle, part lion.

questions.q: Three of these are Greek monsters — which one is a god?
questions.f: Dionysus is the cheerful Greek god of grapes and celebrations.

questions.q: Which would leave the biggest footprint: a giant, a fairy, or a pixie?
questions.f: In 'Jack and the Beanstalk,' a giant lives in a castle above the clouds.

questions.q: Medusa was one of three snake-haired sisters called the Gorgons.
questions.f: Of the three Gorgon sisters, only Medusa was not immortal.

questions.q: Which of these did the ancient Greeks believe caused thunder?
questions.f: The Norse people blamed thunder on Thor's swinging hammer instead.

questions.q: Which two animals combine to make a griffin?
questions.f: The eagle rules the sky and the lion rules the land — a mighty mix!

questions.q: Which of these creatures has living snakes for hair?
questions.f: Medusa was the most famous gorgon of all.

questions.q: Why did the Greek youth Narcissus waste away by a pool?
c: He fell in love with his own reflection
questions.f: The word 'narcissist,' meaning someone very vain, comes from his name.

questions.q: Which Greek god of the wild had the legs and horns of a goat?
questions.f: Pan loved making music on a set of reed pipes.

questions.q: In Norse belief, what was Ragnarok?
c: A great final battle of the gods
questions.f: Norse myths said the world would be born fresh and green again afterward.

questions.q: Many cultures worldwide tell dragon stories, from China to Europe.
questions.f: Chinese dragons usually bring luck, while European dragons often guard treasure.

questions.q: Why does Egyptian myth say the sun vanishes each night?
c: Ra sails his boat through the underworld
questions.f: Egyptians believed Ra faced a giant serpent named Apophis every night.

questions.q: Which is the home of the Norse gods, joined to Earth by a rainbow?
questions.f: The shimmering rainbow bridge to Asgard was called Bifrost.

questions.q: What clever trick finally let the Greeks win the Trojan War?
questions.f: Soldiers hid inside the hollow wooden horse to sneak into Troy.

questions.q: In Greek myth, why do we have echoes, according to the nymph Echo?
c: She could only repeat others' words
She lived deep in a cave
questions.f: A curse left Echo able to repeat only the last words she heard.

questions.q: A giant 'world tree' linking the heavens and Earth appears in Norse myth.
questions.f: The Norse world tree was a giant ash called Yggdrasil.

questions.q: Which Greek Titan was punished for giving fire to humans?
questions.f: Prometheus's gift of fire helped humans cook food and stay warm.

questions.q: The phoenix is the only bird in legend that can do what?
c: Be reborn from its own ashes
questions.f: Phoenix legends appear in Greek, Egyptian, and Chinese stories alike.

questions.q: Why is Hanuman honored as a symbol of devotion in Indian tradition?
c: He served Lord Rama with total loyalty
questions.f: Stories say Hanuman once carried a whole mountain of healing herbs.

questions.q: What lesson did King Midas learn from his golden touch?
c: That some things matter more than gold
questions.f: He couldn't eat or hug anyone once everything he touched turned to gold.

questions.q: Greek and Roman myths share the same gods under different names.
questions.f: The Greek goddess Aphrodite is the very same goddess as Roman Venus.

questions.q: In Egyptian myth, which green-skinned god rules the peaceful afterlife?
questions.f: Osiris's green skin stood for new plants and fresh growth.

questions.q: Which mythical creature is a symbol of purity in many legends?
questions.f: Old stories claimed a unicorn's horn could make dirty water clean.

questions.q: Some Greek myths were made to explain nature, like the changing seasons.
questions.f: Winter was said to arrive when Demeter missed her daughter Persephone.

questions.q: In the Ramayana, why do people celebrate the festival of Diwali?
c: To welcome Rama home from exile
questions.f: People light rows of little lamps to guide Rama's way home.

questions.q: Which brave Norse god gave up his hand to the great wolf Fenrir?
questions.f: Tyr was remembered as one of the bravest of all the Norse gods.

questions.q: Why might so many cultures around the world have flood myths?
c: Big floods really happened and people told stories about them
questions.f: Flood stories appear in Babylonian, Indian, and many other traditions.

questions.q: How many sides does a triangle have?
questions.f: 'Tri' means three — the same start as tricycle, tripod, and triceratops!

questions.q: How many corners does a square have?
questions.f: A square has 4 corners and 4 sides, all exactly the same length.

questions.q: Which shape is perfectly round with no corners at all?
questions.f: Every point on a circle is exactly the same distance from its middle.

questions.q: How many sides does a pentagon have?
questions.f: 'Penta' means five — a starfish body and a pentagon both have five points!

questions.q: How many sides does a hexagon have?
questions.f: Honeybees build hexagons because they fit together with zero wasted space.

questions.q: What number comes right after 19?
questions.f: After 19 the ones digit rolls back to 0 and the tens digit ticks up to 2.

questions.q: How many wheels does a bicycle have?
questions.f: 'Bi' means two — that's why a bicycle has two wheels and binoculars have two eyepieces.

questions.q: Numbers like 2, 4, 6, and 8 are called what?
questions.f: Even numbers can always split into two equal teams with nobody left over.

questions.q: Numbers like 1, 3, 5, and 7 are called what?
questions.f: Share an odd number of sweets between two friends and one is always left over.

questions.q: Which number means nothing, or none at all?
questions.f: The idea of zero as a number came from ancient India, and it changed maths forever!

questions.q: How many days are in one week?
questions.f: Long ago people named the seven days after the Sun, Moon, and five bright planets.

questions.q: What is 5 + 5?
questions.f: Ten is the first number that needs two digits to write it down.

questions.q: What is 6 + 5?
questions.f: 11 and 12 are the only 'teen' numbers that don't actually say 'teen'!

questions.q: Counting by tens: 10, 20, 30 … what comes next?
questions.f: Counting by tens is easy because every number ends in a 0.

questions.q: How many sides does a stop sign (an octagon) have?
questions.f: Stop signs are octagons so drivers know them by shape even in fog or snow.

questions.q: What is 9 minus 8?
questions.f: One is the first counting number — everything else is built by adding more ones.

questions.q: Which is the biggest number: 15, 51, 5, or 1?
questions.f: Swap the digits of 15 and you get 51 — in numbers, the order of digits really matters.

questions.q: A circle has four corners.
questions.f: A circle has no corners at all — its edge is one smooth curve the whole way round.

questions.q: Zero means nothing, or none.
questions.f: Zero is powerful — it holds the 'empty' spot, so 205 isn't mixed up with 25.

questions.q: The number 4 is an even number.
questions.f: Four splits neatly into two twos, so it's even — like 2, 6, 8, and 10.

questions.q: Which of these shapes has exactly three corners?
questions.f: 'Triangle' means 'three angles' — count its three pointy corners!

questions.q: Which shape looks like a stretched circle, the shape of an egg?
questions.f: Running tracks are oval so runners can go round and round without sharp corners.

questions.q: What is half of 100?
questions.f: Half means splitting into two equal parts — 50 and 50 make 100.

questions.q: What number comes right after 99?
questions.f: 100 is the smallest number that needs three digits to write it.

questions.q: Counting down: 3, 2, 1 … what comes next?
questions.f: After 1 comes 0 — the perfect countdown for a rocket launch: 3, 2, 1, blast off!

questions.q: What is 7 + 6?
questions.f: Some people think 13 is unlucky, but it's just an ordinary number like any other!

questions.q: What is 8 + 8?
questions.f: Doubling is a handy trick: double 8 is 16, and double 16 is 32.

questions.q: A triangle has three sides.
questions.f: Every triangle has three sides and three corners — no more, no less.

questions.q: When counting up, ten comes before nine.
questions.f: Counting up we say nine first, then ten: …7, 8, 9, 10.

questions.q: Which is the biggest number: 9, 5, 2, or 7?
questions.f: Nine is the biggest number you can write with a single digit.

questions.q: What do we call a group of 12?
questions.f: Bakers sometimes add one extra, so 13 is called a 'baker's dozen'!

questions.q: How many months are in a year?
questions.f: September means 'seventh month' — it really was seventh in the old Roman calendar!

questions.q: What is the Roman numeral for 10?
questions.f: An old story says X is two V-fives joined tip to tip: 5 + 5 = 10!

questions.q: What is the Roman numeral for 5?
questions.f: Some think V looks like an open hand — five fingers spread wide!

questions.q: What is the Roman numeral for 1?
questions.f: The Roman I is just a single stroke — like holding up one finger.

questions.q: How many hours are in one day?
questions.f: Earth spins all the way around once every 24 hours — that spin makes day and night.

questions.q: How many minutes are in one hour?
questions.f: We got 60-minute hours from the ancient Babylonians, who loved counting in sixties.

questions.q: What do we call a period of 100 years?
questions.f: 'Century' comes from 'centum', Latin for hundred — same root as centipede.

questions.q: What do we call a period of 10 years?
questions.f: 'Deca' means ten, so a decade is ten years and a decathlon has ten events.

questions.q: How many days does February have in a leap year?
questions.f: A leap year has an extra day every 4 years to keep our calendar lined up with the Sun.

questions.q: About how many days are in one year?
questions.f: Earth takes about 365 days to travel once all the way around the Sun.

questions.q: When you cut something into two equal parts, each part is called…?
questions.f: Two halves always join back together to make one whole.

questions.q: One slice of a pizza cut into four equal pieces is what fraction?
questions.f: Four quarters make a whole — that's also why 25 cents is called a 'quarter'.

questions.q: How many is one thousand written in digits?
questions.f: One thousand is ten hundreds stacked together.

questions.q: Which is bigger, a million or a thousand?
questions.f: A million is a thousand thousands — you'd need to count a long time to reach it!

questions.q: What do we call a shape with eight sides?
questions.f: 'Octo' means eight — the same start as octopus, which has eight arms!

questions.q: What do we call a shape with five sides?
questions.f: The famous Pentagon building in the USA is shaped like a five-sided pentagon.

questions.q: What do we call a shape with six sides?
questions.f: Snowflakes almost always grow with six sides, just like a hexagon.

questions.q: On a clock, what does the long hand point to?
questions.f: The short hand shows the hour, and the long hand shows the minutes.

questions.q: What do we call a group of 20?
questions.f: A 'score' means twenty — a famous old speech began 'Four score and seven years ago'.

questions.q: There are seven days in a week.
questions.f: Nearly every country uses a seven-day week, an idea thousands of years old.

questions.q: A dozen means twelve.
questions.f: Eggs are often sold by the dozen — that's twelve eggs in a box.

questions.q: The Roman numeral V stands for the number ten.
questions.f: V stands for five. Ten is written X in Roman numerals.

questions.q: There are 100 minutes in one hour.
questions.f: An hour has 60 minutes, not 100 — clocks count in sixties, not tens.

questions.q: Half of something means one of two equal parts.
questions.f: If you and a friend share a chocolate bar fairly, you each get one half.

questions.q: Short hand on 3, long hand on 12 — what time is it?
questions.f: When the long hand points straight up to 12, it's exactly o'clock with no extra minutes.

questions.q: Which symbol did the ancient Romans use for the number zero?
c: They had no symbol for zero
questions.f: Romans had no zero at all — the powerful zero came to Europe later, from India and Arabia.

questions.q: Counting by fives: 5, 10, 15, 20 … what comes next?
questions.f: Numbers you say when counting by five always end in a 5 or a 0.

questions.q: What do we call two of something, like two matching shoes?
questions.f: 'Pair' comes from a Latin word meaning 'equal', like two things that match.

questions.q: A shape with four equal sides and four square corners is a…?
questions.f: Tilt a square onto one corner and people call it a diamond, but it's still a square!

questions.q: What is the Roman numeral for 100?
questions.f: C stands for 'centum', the Latin word for one hundred.

questions.q: What is the Roman numeral for 50?
questions.f: To read Roman numbers you add the pieces up: L + X + I equals 61!

questions.q: What is the Roman numeral for 1,000?
questions.f: M comes from 'mille', Latin for a thousand — the same root as millimetre and millipede.

questions.q: What is the Roman numeral for 500?
questions.f: Roman numerals only use seven letters: I, V, X, L, C, D and M.

questions.q: How many degrees are in a full circle, all the way around?
questions.f: The Babylonians chose 360 because it splits neatly into halves, thirds, quarters and more.

questions.q: How many degrees are in a right angle, the corner of a square?
questions.f: A right angle is a perfect square corner, and four of them fit around a point: 4 × 90 = 360.

questions.q: How many degrees are there along a perfectly straight line?
questions.f: A straight line is like two right angles side by side: 90 + 90 = 180.

questions.q: How many seconds are in one hour?
questions.f: 60 seconds in a minute times 60 minutes in an hour makes 3,600 seconds.

questions.q: What do we call a shape with ten sides?
questions.f: 'Deca' means ten, the same start as decade (ten years) and decimal (counting in tens).

questions.q: What do we call a shape with nine sides?
questions.f: 'Nona' comes from the Latin word for nine.

questions.q: Add up all the dots on a normal dice (1+2+3+4+5+6). What do you get?
questions.f: On a fair dice, the numbers on opposite faces always add up to 7.

questions.q: In India, ten million (1,00,00,000) has a special name. What is it?
questions.f: In India big numbers use lakhs and crores: 100 lakhs make one crore.

questions.q: What do we call the number written on top of a fraction?
questions.f: In 3/4, the top number 3 (the numerator) tells you how many pieces you have.

questions.q: What do we call the number written on the bottom of a fraction?
questions.f: In 3/4, the bottom number 4 (the denominator) tells you how many equal pieces the whole was cut into.

questions.q: The fraction 3/4 is the same as what percentage?
questions.f: 'Per cent' means 'out of 100', so three-quarters is 75 out of 100.

questions.q: The fraction 1/2 is the same as what percentage?
questions.f: One half is 50 out of 100 — exactly halfway to a full 100%.

questions.q: One million is a 1 followed by how many zeros?
questions.f: A million looks like this: 1,000,000 — count the six zeros!

questions.q: One billion is a 1 followed by how many zeros?
questions.f: A billion is a thousand millions — 1,000,000,000.

questions.q: A 'googol' is a 1 followed by how many zeros?
questions.f: A googol is so huge it's bigger than the number of atoms in your whole body — and it inspired the name Google!

questions.q: What is 7 × 7?
questions.f: 7 × 7 = 49, one less than 50 — a handy fact to remember.

questions.q: In the doubling pattern 2, 4, 8, 16 … what comes next?
questions.f: Each number is double the one before — keep doubling and it grows shockingly fast!

questions.q: Counting by threes: 3, 6, 9, 12 … what comes next?
questions.f: The three times table is hiding in music and clocks all over the place.

questions.q: What do we call a shape with twelve sides?
questions.f: A dodecagon has 12 sides — some countries have even made 12-sided coins!

questions.q: How many seconds are in one whole day?
questions.f: That's 60 × 60 × 24 = 86,400 seconds ticking past every single day.

questions.q: A right angle measures 90 degrees.
questions.f: The little square drawn in a corner is the symbol for a 90-degree right angle.

questions.q: There are 1,000 years in a millennium.
questions.f: 'Mille' means thousand, so a millennium is a thousand years — ten centuries.

questions.q: A million is bigger than a billion.
questions.f: A billion is a thousand times bigger than a million!

questions.q: The number on the bottom of a fraction is called the denominator.
questions.f: The denominator tells you how many equal parts the whole has been split into.

questions.q: Which of these shapes has the most sides?
questions.f: Octagon 8, pentagon 5, square 4, triangle 3 — the octagon wins by a lot.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a prime number?
questions.f: 27 = 3 × 9, so it has extra factors. A prime number can only be divided by 1 and itself.

questions.q: Which of these is the largest number?
questions.f: Even though 999 has big digits, 1,001 is over a thousand — count the digits first!

questions.q: Which of these fractions is the biggest?
questions.f: Three quarters is the most — imagine three of a pizza's four slices on your plate.

questions.q: Which of these fractions is the smallest?
questions.f: The more pieces you cut a cake into, the smaller each slice — so 1/8 is tiniest here.

questions.q: Which of these Roman numerals equals 40?
questions.f: When a smaller numeral sits before a bigger one, you subtract: XL is 50 − 10 = 40.

questions.q: Which of these does NOT add up to 10?
questions.f: 6 + 5 makes 11, not 10 — the odd one out.

questions.q: Rank these times: which lasts the LONGEST?
questions.f: A day holds 24 hours, each hour holds 60 minutes, and each minute holds 60 seconds.

questions.q: Which of these is the SHORTEST amount of time?
questions.f: You can blink a couple of times in a single second.

questions.q: If today is Monday, what day will it be in 2 days?
questions.f: Monday plus one is Tuesday, plus one more is Wednesday.

questions.q: Which unit is best for weighing a small apple?
questions.f: Grams measure weight, litres measure liquid, and metres measure length.

questions.q: Which unit would you use to measure how much water fills a bottle?
questions.f: Litres measure liquid — a large water bottle often holds one or two litres.

questions.q: Which unit is used to measure length or distance?
questions.f: A big step for an adult is roughly one metre long.

questions.q: How much does one kilogram equal?
questions.f: 'Kilo' means a thousand, so a kilogram is 1,000 grams and a kilometre is 1,000 metres.

questions.q: In India, what is one hundred thousand (1,00,000) called?
questions.f: A lakh is written 1,00,000, and 100 lakhs make one crore.

questions.q: A box holds 24 eggs. If you use 6, how many are left?
questions.f: 24 − 6 = 18. That's still one and a half dozen eggs remaining!

questions.q: Which of these patterns is counting DOWN by 2 each time?
questions.f: Counting down by 2 through even numbers: 10, 8, 6, 4, 2, 0.

questions.q: Three of these are shapes. Which one is NOT?
questions.f: A rhombus is a slanted square and a trapezoid has one pair of parallel sides — but a zebra is an animal!

questions.q: A clock shows 3:15. Where is the long (minute) hand pointing?
questions.f: Each clock number is 5 minutes apart, so the 3 marks 15 minutes past.

questions.q: A billion is the same as a thousand millions.
questions.f: A billion = 1,000 × 1,000,000. You'd count for over 30 years to reach a billion out loud!

questions.q: The fraction 1/2 is bigger than 3/4.
questions.f: Three quarters is bigger — 3/4 is 75% while 1/2 is only 50%.

questions.q: A right angle is bigger than a straight angle.
questions.f: A right angle is 90 degrees and a straight angle is 180 — the straight one is twice as big.

questions.q: What do we call a number that can only be divided evenly by 1 and itself?
questions.f: 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11 are primes — and there are infinitely many, going on forever!

questions.q: What do we call numbers that go on forever with no end?
questions.f: There's no biggest number — add 1 to any number and you get an even bigger one!

questions.q: What is a 1 followed by a googol of zeros called?
questions.f: A googolplex is so gigantic you couldn't write out all its zeros even using the whole universe as paper.

questions.q: Why do honeybees build their honeycomb using hexagon shapes?
c: They fit together with no wasted space
Bees have six legs to copy
questions.f: Hexagons tile perfectly with no gaps, using the least wax to hold the most honey — clever bees!

questions.q: What happens when you multiply any number by zero?
questions.f: Zero groups of anything is nothing at all, so the answer is always 0.

questions.q: Which sequence shows the famous Fibonacci numbers?
questions.f: Fibonacci numbers show up in sunflowers, pinecones and even snail shells!

questions.q: In the Fibonacci pattern, how do you get each new number?
c: Add the two numbers before it
questions.f: 1 + 1 = 2, then 1 + 2 = 3, then 2 + 3 = 5 — each number is the two before it added together.

questions.q: The number 'pi', used for circles, is about equal to what?
questions.f: Pi's digits never stop and never repeat — computers have worked out trillions of them!

questions.q: Pi compares the distance around a circle to which of its measurements?
questions.f: Every circle is about 3.14 times wider around its edge than straight across the middle.

questions.q: Which is the only even number that is also a prime number?
questions.f: Every other even number can be split by 2, so 2 is the one and only even prime.

questions.q: What do we call a number that reads the same forwards and backwards, like 121?
questions.f: 121 and 4554 are palindromes — words like 'level' and 'racecar' are palindromes too!

questions.q: Why can't you divide a number by zero?
questions.f: Sharing sweets among zero friends makes no sense, so mathematicians say it's 'undefined'.

questions.q: What is 10 × 10 × 10?
questions.f: Multiplying by ten three times adds three zeros: 10 × 10 × 10 = 1,000.

questions.q: Which of these is the largest number?
questions.f: Each step up is a thousand-or-more times bigger, and a billion towers over them all.

questions.q: What do we call the answer to a multiplication problem?
questions.f: Add and you get a sum; multiply and you get a product; divide and you get a quotient.

questions.q: What do we call the answer to a subtraction problem?
questions.f: Subtracting tells you the 'difference' — how far apart two numbers are.

questions.q: What do we call a shape whose sides are all equal and all angles are equal?
questions.f: A square is a regular shape; a stretched rectangle is not, because its sides aren't all equal.

questions.q: Zero is an even number.
questions.f: Zero sits between two odd numbers, −1 and 1, and splits evenly by 2, so it counts as even.

questions.q: Pi is exactly equal to 3.
questions.f: Pi is about 3.14159… and its digits go on forever without ever stopping.

questions.q: There is a single biggest number that no number can ever beat.
questions.f: Numbers never run out — whatever number you name, adding 1 makes a bigger one.

questions.q: What do fish use to breathe underwater?
questions.f: Gills pull oxygen straight out of the water, so fish never surface for air.

questions.q: True or False: A whale is a kind of fish.
questions.f: Whales are mammals, so they breathe air through a blowhole.

questions.q: What kind of water fills the ocean?
questions.f: The sea is so salty that you float in it more easily than in a pool.

questions.q: What is a big group of fish swimming together called?
questions.f: Swimming in a school makes it hard for a predator to pick just one fish.

questions.q: True or False: Crabs usually walk sideways.
questions.f: A crab's leg joints bend sideways, so scuttling left and right is easiest.

questions.q: Which sea animal has eight arms?
questions.f: Each octopus arm can taste and touch whatever it grabs.

questions.q: What do dolphins come to the surface to get?
questions.f: Dolphins are mammals and breathe air through a blowhole on top of the head.

questions.q: What is the sandy place where the ocean meets land called?
questions.f: Beach sand is made of tiny bits of rock and crushed seashells.

questions.q: True or False: Sharks are a kind of fish.
questions.f: Sharks are fish, but their skeleton is bendy cartilage instead of bone.

questions.q: What do surfers ride on top of at the sea?
questions.f: Most waves are made by wind pushing across the ocean's surface.

questions.q: Which is the biggest animal living in the ocean?
questions.f: The blue whale is the largest animal that has ever lived on Earth.

questions.q: What do we call a person who swims deep underwater with an air tank?
questions.f: Divers breathe from tanks of air in a kit called scuba.

questions.q: What hard thing does a sea turtle carry on its back?
questions.f: A turtle's shell is part of its body, so it can never crawl out of it.

questions.q: Which of these animals lives in the ocean?
questions.f: Seahorses grip seaweed with their curly tails so currents don't sweep them away.

questions.q: What does a shark grow rows and rows of?
questions.f: When a tooth falls out a new one moves up, so a shark never runs out.

questions.q: What do we call frozen ocean water floating near the poles?
questions.f: Sea ice forms a floating cap on the ocean where it is bitterly cold.

questions.q: True or False: The ocean covers more of Earth than land does.
questions.f: Ocean covers about 71% of the planet, which is why Earth looks blue from space.

questions.q: Which sea creature has a round body and stinging tentacles?
questions.f: A jellyfish uses its stinging tentacles to catch tiny food from the water.

questions.q: What is a baby whale called?
questions.f: A baby whale is a calf, and it drinks its mother's milk underwater.

questions.q: Which sea animal has a long, snake-like body?
questions.f: Eels look like snakes but are really long, slippery fish.

questions.q: What sticky green plant-like living thing grows in the sea?
questions.f: Seaweed is a kind of algae with no roots or flowers like land plants.

questions.q: Which sea animal uses a blowhole on its head to breathe?
questions.f: A whale's spout is the misty breath it blows out when it surfaces.

questions.q: Which sea creature squirts a cloud of ink to escape?
questions.f: The dark ink hides the squid while it jets away to safety.

questions.q: What are the tiny drifting living things that float in the sea called?
questions.f: Plankton drift with the current and feed many bigger ocean animals.

questions.q: Which shellfish has two big claws and turns red when cooked?
questions.f: A lobster can shoot backwards very fast by flipping its powerful tail.

questions.q: Which part of a shark is made of bendy cartilage instead of bone?
questions.f: A cartilage skeleton makes a shark lighter and more flexible than bony fish.

questions.q: Which sea animal can regrow a lost arm?
questions.f: A few kinds of starfish can even regrow a whole body from a single arm!

questions.q: What covers a fish's body to help protect it?
questions.f: Scales overlap like tiny shields and are coated in slippery slime.

questions.q: Which fish hides safely among a sea anemone's stinging tentacles?
questions.f: A slimy coating keeps the anemone's stingers from hurting the clownfish.

questions.q: What do we call the regular rise and fall of the sea's water level?
questions.f: Tides happen mostly because the Moon's gravity gently pulls the ocean.

questions.q: What is the hard reef built by tiny animals called polyps?
questions.f: A coral reef can take hundreds of years for the tiny animals to build.

questions.q: Which fish puffs up like a spiky balloon when it is scared?
questions.f: It gulps water to look far too big and spiky to swallow.

questions.q: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.f: The Pacific is so wide it covers more area than all the land put together.

questions.q: What do we call a group of dolphins swimming together?
questions.f: Dolphins in a pod work as a team to herd fish for dinner.

questions.q: Which sea animal has a long tusk like a unicorn's horn?
questions.f: A narwhal's 'horn' is really a giant tooth that pokes out through its lip.

questions.q: Which shark is the largest fish in the whole sea?
questions.f: The gentle whale shark is huge yet feeds on tiny drifting plankton.

questions.q: What do sea otters use as a tool to crack open shellfish?
questions.f: An otter floats on its back and smashes a shell against a rock on its tummy.

questions.q: Which sea animal flashes colours across its skin to blend in?
questions.f: A cuttlefish can change colour in a heartbeat to hide or to show off.

questions.q: Which tiny shrimp-like animals do many whales love to eat?
questions.f: A blue whale can gulp down tonnes of tiny krill in a single day.

questions.q: Which crab borrows an empty shell to live inside?
questions.f: As it grows, a hermit crab moves house into a bigger empty shell.

questions.q: What unusual colour is an octopus's blood?
questions.f: Copper in the blood makes it blue instead of red like ours.

questions.q: What is the top layer of the ocean that sunlight reaches called?
questions.f: Almost all sea plants and most animals live in this bright top layer.

questions.q: Which reptile crawls onto beaches to lay its eggs in the sand?
questions.f: The buried eggs hatch and the tiny babies race to reach the sea.

questions.q: What kind of living thing is seaweed really?
questions.f: Seaweed is algae, so it has no true roots, stems, or flowers.

questions.q: What do we call ocean water flowing steadily like a river through the sea?
questions.f: Currents can carry animals and even seeds thousands of kilometres.

questions.q: Which deep-sea animal has eyes as big as dinner plates?
questions.f: Those huge eyes help the giant squid spot faint light in the dark deep.

questions.q: Which giant flat sea animal 'flies' by flapping wing-like fins?
questions.f: A manta ray can be wider than a car from wingtip to wingtip.

questions.q: What do barnacles glue themselves onto?
questions.f: A barnacle cements its own head down and stays stuck there for life.

questions.q: Which fish is famous as one of the fastest swimmers in the sea?
questions.f: A sailfish can zoom through the water faster than a car drives in town.

questions.q: Which shelled sea animal is a cousin of the octopus?
questions.f: A nautilus lives inside a beautiful spiral shell it grows itself.

questions.q: What is the white foam at the top of a breaking wave called?
questions.f: Crashing waves whip air into the water to create bubbly sea foam.

questions.q: What are animals like crabs, lobsters, and shrimp called?
questions.f: Crustaceans wear a hard shell on the outside instead of an inside skeleton.

questions.q: Which clever sea mammal is often seen barking and balancing at the coast?
questions.f: Sea lions are strong swimmers that can also gallop on their flippers on land.

questions.q: True or False: A male seahorse carries the babies, not the female.
questions.f: Dad seahorse keeps the eggs safe in a pouch until the babies hatch.

questions.q: True or False: Coral is a plant.
questions.f: Coral is really made of thousands of tiny animals called polyps.

questions.q: True or False: The Moon helps cause the ocean's tides.
questions.f: The Moon's gravity tugs the sea into a bulge that we feel as high tide.

questions.q: True or False: A starfish has no brain.
questions.f: A starfish senses the world using its arms instead of a brain.

questions.q: True or False: Octopuses can live in fresh water lakes.
questions.f: Octopuses live only in the salty sea, never in lakes or rivers.

questions.q: How many main oceans does the Earth have?
questions.f: They are the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Arctic, and Southern Oceans.

questions.q: About how much of Earth's surface is covered by ocean?
questions.f: With most of the planet under water, Earth looks blue from space.

questions.q: What do we call the deep ocean layer where no sunlight ever reaches?
questions.f: The midnight zone is pitch black and freezing cold all the time.

questions.q: About what fraction of a jellyfish's body is water?
questions.f: A jellyfish is almost entirely water, so it nearly vanishes if it dries out.

questions.q: How does a dolphin find food in dark or murky water?
questions.f: It makes clicking sounds and listens for the echoes bouncing back.

questions.q: What are the tiny drifting plants that make oxygen called?
questions.f: Phytoplankton make roughly half of all the oxygen we breathe.

questions.q: Which is the largest coral reef system in the world?
questions.f: It stretches so far along Australia that it can be seen from space.

questions.q: How many teeth might a shark grow over its whole life?
questions.f: Sharks replace lost teeth again and again, so they use thousands in a lifetime.

questions.q: What makes most ordinary ocean waves?
questions.f: Wind dragging across the surface pushes the water up into waves.

questions.q: What usually causes a giant tsunami wave?
questions.f: The seabed suddenly jolts and shoves a huge wall of water across the ocean.

questions.q: How long can a resting sea turtle stay underwater without a breath?
questions.f: When a turtle rests its body slows right down so it needs very little air.

questions.q: What do we call animals that make their own light in the deep sea?
questions.f: Special chemicals in their bodies react to make a glow with almost no heat.

questions.q: How many legs does a crab have in total, counting its claws?
questions.f: Crabs are 'decapods', a word that means ten-footed.

questions.q: Which sense helps a shark find a tiny bit of blood from far away?
questions.f: A shark's nose is so sensitive it can detect just a few drops in the water.

questions.q: What mainly makes seawater taste salty?
questions.f: Rivers slowly wash salt out of rocks and carry it down to the sea.

questions.q: What do we call baby fish that have just hatched?
questions.f: Tiny newly hatched fish are called fry, and huge numbers of them hatch at once.

questions.q: Which cold ocean surrounds the North Pole?
questions.f: The Arctic is the smallest and coldest ocean, often capped with floating ice.

questions.q: How do many fish stay at the right depth without sinking?
questions.f: This air-filled bag inside works like a built-in float.

questions.q: What do we call the extra-strong tides at full and new moon?
questions.f: The Sun and Moon line up and pull the sea together for a bigger tide.

questions.q: What is the name of the deepest known point in the ocean?
questions.f: Challenger Deep lies nearly 11 kilometres down in the Mariana Trench.

questions.q: Which flat sea animal can give an electric shock to stun its prey?
questions.f: An electric ray builds up a charge and zaps prey with a jolt.

questions.q: What do we call the thick layer of fat that keeps whales warm?
questions.f: Blubber traps body heat so whales stay warm even in icy seas.

questions.q: What are the tiny animals that build a coral reef called?
questions.f: Each soft polyp builds a tiny stony cup, and millions together form the reef.

questions.q: True or False: The Mariana Trench is deeper than Mount Everest is tall.
questions.f: You could sink all of Everest into it and still have about 2 km of water on top.

questions.q: True or False: It is safe to drink seawater when you are thirsty.
questions.f: Seawater is so salty that drinking it makes you even thirstier and unwell.

questions.q: True or False: Plankton includes both tiny plants and tiny animals.
questions.f: Plant plankton are phytoplankton and animal plankton are zooplankton.

questions.q: True or False: An octopus can squeeze through a gap the size of its eye.
questions.f: With no bones, the only hard part is its beak, so it fits through tiny gaps.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a mammal?
questions.f: A shark is a fish; the others breathe air and feed their babies milk.

questions.q: Which ocean zone is the very deepest of these?
questions.f: Hadal zones are the deep ocean trenches, the most extreme place in the sea.

questions.q: Which of these fish lives DEEPEST in the dark ocean?
questions.f: The anglerfish dangles a glowing lure to draw prey close in the black deep.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a real ocean?
questions.f: The Sahara is the world's biggest hot desert, not an ocean.

questions.q: Which of these animals does NOT have a backbone?
questions.f: A crab is an invertebrate, wearing a hard shell instead of an inner skeleton.

questions.q: Which is the SMALLEST kind of shark?
questions.f: The dwarf lanternshark fits in your hand and even glows in the dark.

questions.q: Which travels faster across the sea: a tsunami or a normal wave?
questions.f: In deep water a tsunami can race along as fast as a jet plane.

questions.q: Which sea creature can grow young again and may never die of old age?
questions.f: This tiny jellyfish can reset its body back to a baby stage and start over.

questions.q: Which does a healthy coral reef need most?
questions.f: If the water gets too hot the coral turns ghostly white, called bleaching.

questions.q: Which animal has blue blood that people use to help test medicines?
questions.f: A horseshoe crab's pale blue blood helps check that medicines are safe.

questions.q: Which is the correct order of ocean layers from top to bottom?
questions.f: Light fades away the deeper down you go into the ocean.

questions.q: Which whale is famous for one of the longest journeys of any animal?
questions.f: Humpbacks travel thousands of kilometres between feeding and breeding seas.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT built by living creatures?
questions.f: Coral, oysters, and barnacles are all made by animals; a dune is piled by wind.

questions.q: Which tide has the SMALLEST rise and fall?
questions.f: Neap tides happen when the Sun and Moon pull at right angles to each other.

questions.q: Which of these bodies of water is famously the saltiest?
questions.f: It is so salty that swimmers bob on top and almost nothing can live in it.

questions.q: A blue whale's tongue can weigh about as much as which animal?
questions.f: And its heart is roughly the size of a small car!

questions.q: Which animal strains its tiny food from the water instead of biting?
questions.f: Baleen hangs like a giant comb that traps krill as water flows out.

questions.q: Which grows more slowly, coral or a tree?
questions.f: Many corals grow only a few centimetres in a whole year.

questions.q: Which fish can survive the crushing pressure at the bottom of the sea?
questions.f: Deep-sea snailfish thrive where the pressure would crush a submarine.

questions.q: True or False: The Pacific is both the largest and the deepest ocean.
questions.f: It is the biggest ocean and it holds the deep Mariana Trench.

questions.q: True or False: Some sharks can glow in the dark deep sea.
questions.f: Certain deep-water sharks are bioluminescent and give off a soft glow.

questions.q: True or False: Coral reefs cover most of the ocean floor.
questions.f: Reefs cover less than 1% of the ocean, yet they shelter a quarter of sea life.

questions.q: Why do you float more easily in the sea than in a swimming pool?
questions.f: Denser salty water pushes up on you harder, helping you float.

questions.q: Why is the deep ocean completely dark?
questions.f: Below about one kilometre, no sunlight can get through the water.

questions.q: What mainly causes the ocean's tides?
questions.f: The Moon's pull stretches the sea into bulges that we feel as high tides.

questions.q: Why do coral reefs turn white and 'bleach'?
questions.f: Heat stresses the coral so it pushes out the colourful algae living inside it.

questions.q: How does an anglerfish attract prey in the pitch-black deep?
questions.f: Tiny glowing bacteria light up the lure that dangles over its mouth.

questions.q: What is the ocean's 'twilight zone'?
c: The very top of the waves
questions.f: So little light reaches here that plants cannot grow.

questions.q: Why can't most deep-sea fish survive if brought up to the surface?
questions.f: Their bodies are built for the crushing deep, so rising up damages them.

questions.q: Which makes more of Earth's oxygen: forests or ocean plankton?
questions.f: Tiny phytoplankton in the sea produce about half of all our oxygen.

questions.q: What is a 'red tide'?
c: A huge bloom of tiny algae
questions.f: Millions of tiny algae can turn the water red and be harmful to sea life.

questions.q: Why must whales keep returning to the surface?
questions.f: Whales are mammals with lungs, so they must breathe air like we do.

questions.q: What is the huge 'Great Pacific Garbage Patch' mostly made of?
questions.f: Swirling currents gather bits of plastic into an enormous drifting zone.

questions.q: Why is the Mariana Trench so hard for people to explore?
questions.f: Fewer people have reached its bottom than have walked on the Moon.

questions.q: What is 'upwelling' in the ocean?
questions.f: Rising deep water brings up nutrients that feed enormous crowds of fish.

questions.q: Which of these can be the longest animal ever measured?
questions.f: A stringy siphonophore found near Australia stretched longer than a blue whale.

questions.q: Why do flying fish leap and glide above the waves?
questions.f: They spread wing-like fins and glide to flee hungry hunters below.

questions.q: What is echolocation, used by dolphins and whales?
questions.f: They send out clicks and read the echoes that bounce back off objects.

questions.q: Why does the open sea look blue to our eyes?
questions.f: Water soaks up red light and scatters blue light back up to us.

questions.q: True or False: The Southern Ocean around Antarctica is counted as a real ocean.
questions.f: Many maps now show it as the fifth ocean, circling all of Antarctica.

questions.q: True or False: Sound travels faster through water than through air.
questions.f: Sound moves about four times faster in water, so whale songs carry a long way.

questions.q: True or False: The ocean holds about 97% of all the water on Earth.
questions.f: Only a tiny slice of Earth's water is the fresh water we can drink.

questions.q: What do plants use sunlight to make?
questions.f: Plants are like tiny cooks, turning sunlight into their own food.

questions.q: Which part of a plant usually grows below the ground?
questions.f: Roots drink water from the soil and hold the plant steady.

questions.q: What is the flat green part that catches sunlight?
questions.f: A leaf works like a little solar panel soaking up sunshine.

questions.q: What gas do trees give off that people need?
questions.f: One big tree can make enough oxygen for two people each day.

questions.q: Which insect visits flowers and helps make honey?
questions.f: A single bee may visit thousands of flowers in one busy day.

questions.q: What sweet juice do bees sip from flowers?
questions.f: Bees turn flower nectar into the sticky honey we love to eat.

questions.q: What do we call the tall, woody part of a tree?
questions.f: The trunk is really the tree's giant, strong stem.

questions.q: Which tall plant grows from a small striped seed?
questions.f: A sunflower can shoot up taller than a grown-up in one summer.

questions.q: What is the colorful part of a plant that attracts bees?
questions.f: Bright petals act like a sign saying 'sweet nectar this way!'

questions.q: Which fruit grows on a vine and can be green or purple?
