questions.f: Grapes grow in bunches and can be dried into raisins.

questions.q: What do plants drink up through their roots?
questions.f: Roots pull water from the soil and send it up the whole plant.

questions.q: Which spiky plant is famous for living in the desert?
questions.f: A cactus stores water inside its thick stem for dry desert days.

questions.q: What do we call a place packed full of trees?
questions.f: Forests are home to more plants and animals than almost anywhere.

questions.q: Which orange vegetable grows underground?
questions.f: The orange carrot we crunch is really the plant's root.

questions.q: In which season do most flowers bloom and trees grow leaves?
questions.f: Warm spring weather wakes up plants after their winter rest.

questions.q: What is the tough outer shell that protects a seed?
questions.f: The seed coat guards the tiny baby plant sleeping inside.

questions.q: Which part holds a plant up and carries water?
questions.f: The stem is like a straw and a pole rolled into one.

questions.q: Which of these does a plant NOT need to grow?
questions.f: Plants only need light, water, air, and soil, no toys required!

questions.q: What is the yellow dust inside flowers called?
questions.f: Pollen helps flowers make seeds, but it can make us sneeze.

questions.q: Which fruit grows on a tree and can be red or green?
questions.f: Some apple trees keep growing fruit for over 100 years.

questions.q: What do we call baby plants that have just sprouted?
questions.f: A seedling pushes its first tiny leaves up toward the light.

questions.q: What color is a healthy, growing leaf?
questions.f: Leaves are green because of a coloring called chlorophyll.

questions.q: Which living thing usually grows biggest and lives longest?
questions.f: Some trees have been alive for thousands of years.

questions.q: On which kind of tree do coconuts grow?
questions.f: Coconuts can float across the sea and grow on a new beach.

questions.q: What sweet food do bees make and store in their hive?
questions.f: Bees flap their wings to dry nectar into thick, golden honey.

questions.q: What tiny thing do you plant to grow a new plant?
questions.f: Inside every seed is a tiny baby plant waiting to sprout.

questions.q: Plants can make their own food.
questions.f: Plants cook food from sunlight, so they never go grocery shopping.

questions.q: All trees stay green all year long.
questions.f: Many trees drop their leaves in autumn and grow new ones in spring.

questions.q: A cactus can store water inside its stem.
questions.f: A fat cactus stem is like a water bottle for dry days.

questions.q: Every kind of plant grows flowers.
questions.f: Ferns and mosses never flower, yet they still grow just fine.

questions.q: Which gas do plants take in to help make food?
questions.f: Plants breathe in carbon dioxide, the gas we breathe out.

questions.q: Which green coloring helps leaves catch sunlight?
questions.f: Chlorophyll grabs sunlight and also paints leaves green.

questions.q: What is the tallest kind of tree on Earth?
questions.f: Coast redwoods can grow taller than a 30-story building.

questions.q: Which fast-growing plant do pandas munch on all day?
questions.f: A panda can chew on bamboo for up to 12 hours a day.

questions.q: Which plant snaps its leaves shut to trap flies?
questions.f: The Venus flytrap can snap closed in less than one second.

questions.q: What is the process plants use to make food from sunlight?
questions.f: Photosynthesis mixes sunlight, water, and air into plant food.

questions.q: Which mighty tree grows from a little acorn?
questions.f: One oak tree can drop thousands of acorns in a single year.

questions.q: What do we call plants that catch and eat insects?
questions.f: These plants eat bugs to get food the poor soil cannot give them.

questions.q: Which spinning 'helicopter' seed comes from a maple tree?
questions.f: Maple seeds twirl like helicopter blades to drift far from the tree.

questions.q: What are the circles inside a tree trunk that show its age?
questions.f: Each ring is usually one year, so you can count a tree's birthdays.

questions.q: Which giant desert cactus can live for over 100 years?
questions.f: A tall saguaro cactus can grow arms that reach for the sky.

questions.q: Which giant flower smells like rotting meat?
questions.f: Rafflesia's stink attracts flies, which spread its pollen around.

questions.q: Which juicy plant part holds the seeds?
questions.f: A fruit is really the plant's clever way of packaging its seeds.

questions.q: How does a coconut travel to grow on a new island?
questions.f: Coconuts can float on ocean waves for weeks before landing.

questions.q: Which plant lures bugs into a deep, slippery cup?
questions.f: Insects slide into the pitcher plant's cup and cannot climb out.

questions.q: What do we call trees that keep their leaves all year?
questions.f: Pine and spruce trees stay green even in the snowy winter.

questions.q: Which nut actually grows underground, not on a tree?
questions.f: Peanuts grow in shells buried in the soil, like little treasures.

questions.q: What helps dandelion seeds float away on the breeze?
questions.f: Each dandelion seed rides its own fluffy parachute in the wind.

questions.q: Wood from which tree is used to make most pencils?
questions.f: Soft cedar wood is easy to sharpen without breaking the pencil.

questions.q: Which of these fruits is really a type of berry?
questions.f: Surprise! Bananas count as berries, but strawberries do not.

questions.q: Which flower is famous for its sweet smell and sharp thorns?
questions.f: A rose grows thorns to stop hungry animals from eating it.

questions.q: Besides drinking water, what else do roots do?
questions.f: Roots grip the soil so wind and rain can't knock the plant over.

questions.q: Which forest is home to the most kinds of plants?
questions.f: The rainforest is bursting with more plant types than anywhere else.

questions.q: Which bug-eating plant is sticky and shaped like a tiny star?
questions.f: A sundew's shiny drops look like dew but trap insects with glue.

questions.q: Which tree gives us the syrup we pour on pancakes?
questions.f: Maple syrup is boiled down from sweet sap inside the tree.

questions.q: Which brightly colored parts of a flower attract pollinators?
questions.f: Colorful petals are like billboards inviting bees to visit.

questions.q: Mushrooms are actually plants.
questions.f: Mushrooms are fungi, not plants, and they can't make their own food.

questions.q: Bamboo is one of the fastest-growing plants on Earth.
questions.f: Some bamboo can shoot up almost a meter in just one day.

questions.q: Trees breathe in carbon dioxide to help make food.
questions.f: Trees soak up the very gas we breathe out to build their food.

questions.q: How much time does one ring in a tree trunk usually stand for?
questions.f: Counting the rings is like counting how many years the tree has lived.

questions.q: About how tall is the tallest tree ever measured?
questions.f: That coast redwood is taller than a football field is long.

questions.q: How fast can a Venus flytrap snap its trap shut?
questions.f: Tiny trigger hairs make the trap slam faster than you can blink.

questions.q: Which tree can live almost 5,000 years, one of the oldest alive?
questions.f: Some bristlecone pines were already old when the pyramids were built.

questions.q: Where does a plant make most of its food?
questions.f: Leaves are like busy kitchens cooking food out of sunlight.

questions.q: Water travels up a plant through tiny tubes called what?
questions.f: Xylem tubes work like drinking straws pulling water to the top.

questions.q: A sunflower's big head is actually made of what?
questions.f: Each 'seed' spot was once its own little flower on the head.

questions.q: Which flower part catches pollen to start making seeds?
questions.f: The sticky stigma grabs pollen grains that land on the flower.

questions.q: What are maple 'helicopter' seeds designed to do as they fall?
questions.f: Spinning slows them down so the wind can carry them farther.

questions.q: How much can fast bamboo grow in a single day?
questions.f: You could almost watch record bamboo grow before your eyes.

questions.q: Which country grows the most bananas in the world?
questions.f: India's warm, wet weather is perfect for huge banana harvests.

questions.q: What sweet substance do plants make and store as food?
questions.f: Photosynthesis turns sunlight into sugar the plant can use for energy.

questions.q: A honeybee's waggle dance tells other bees what?
questions.f: The dance points the way and distance to the best flowers.

questions.q: Which palm grows the world's largest and heaviest seed?
questions.f: A coco de mer seed can weigh as much as a big dog.

questions.q: How do prickly burr seeds usually travel to new places?
questions.f: Burrs hitch a ride on fur, then drop off far from home.

questions.q: Leaves look green because plants use the LEAST of which light?
questions.f: Plants soak up red and blue light but bounce green light back to us.

questions.q: A pumpkin, cucumber, and tomato are all really which of these?
questions.f: They all grow from flowers and hold seeds, so they count as fruits.

questions.q: About how many plant types live in the Amazon rainforest?
questions.f: Scientists still discover brand-new Amazon plants every year.

questions.q: Where does a busy bee carry pollen back to its hive?
questions.f: Bees pack pollen into fuzzy 'baskets' on their back legs.

questions.q: What do we call plants that come back and live for many years?
questions.f: Perennials rest in winter and grow again each spring.

questions.q: Which African tree stores water in its huge, swollen trunk?
questions.f: A baobab's fat trunk can hold thousands of liters of water.

questions.q: Where do pine trees keep and spread their seeds?
questions.f: Pine cones open in dry weather to let their seeds fly away.

questions.q: Which fruit is famous for wearing its seeds on the outside?
questions.f: A strawberry can have around 200 tiny seeds dotting its skin.

questions.q: About how many flowers do bees visit to make one jar of honey?
questions.f: Bees travel a huge distance, sipping millions of flowers for one jar.

questions.q: A strawberry keeps its seeds on the outside of the fruit.
questions.f: Those little specks all over a strawberry are its seeds.

questions.q: The Amazon rainforest makes a big share of Earth's oxygen.
questions.f: Its billions of trees are sometimes called the 'lungs of the planet'.

questions.q: Bamboo is actually a giant type of grass.
questions.f: Even the tallest bamboo belongs to the same family as lawn grass.

questions.q: Trees stop growing once they reach full height.
questions.f: Trees keep getting wider every year, adding a new ring each time.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT part of a flower?
questions.f: Bark is the woody skin of a tree trunk, not part of a flower.

questions.q: Which seed travels farthest on the wind?
questions.f: Light, fluffy dandelion seeds can float for kilometers on a breeze.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a real way seeds travel?
questions.f: Photosynthesis makes food, but it never carries seeds anywhere.

questions.q: Which carnivorous plant has the fastest trap of all?
questions.f: An underwater bladderwort sucks in prey in a fraction of a second.

questions.q: Which of these does a plant NOT need for photosynthesis?
questions.f: Some plants grow floating in water with no soil at all.

questions.q: When a seed sprouts, which part usually pushes out first?
questions.f: The root grows down first to find water before leaves appear.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a fruit if you ask a scientist?
questions.f: A potato is a swollen stem, while the others grow from flowers.

questions.q: Which pollinator visits flowers mostly at night?
questions.f: Many night flowers are pale and sweet-smelling to attract moths.

questions.q: Which of these trees drops all its leaves in winter?
questions.f: Birches are 'deciduous', while pines and firs stay green all year.

questions.q: What are the tiny holes in leaves that let gases in and out?
questions.f: Stomata open and close like little mouths on the leaf's surface.

questions.q: A cactus's sharp spines are really modified what?
questions.f: Thin spines lose less water than flat leaves and scare off animals.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a job that roots do?
questions.f: Roots live in the dark, so leaves do all the sunlight-catching.

questions.q: Which plant makes new plants from spores instead of seeds?
questions.f: Ferns are ancient plants that spread dusty spores instead of seeds.

questions.q: Why do many leaves turn red and orange in autumn?
questions.f: As green chlorophyll fades, hidden yellow and orange colors show up.

questions.q: Which flower part swells into the fruit after pollination?
questions.f: Once pollinated, the flower's ovary grows into a seed-filled fruit.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT really a tree, even though it's tall?
questions.f: A banana 'tree' has no wood; it's actually a giant herb.

questions.q: Which seeds often spread after animals eat the fruit?
questions.f: Animals eat berries, then drop the seeds far away in their poop.

questions.q: A peanut grows underground instead of on a tree.
questions.f: After its flower fades, the peanut plant pushes seeds into the soil.

questions.q: Some plants can grow with no soil at all.
questions.f: Water plants and some crops grow with just water and nutrients.

questions.q: All carnivorous plants live only in hot deserts.
questions.f: Many bug-eaters actually live in wet, soggy bogs, not deserts.

questions.q: A banana plant is not really a tree.
questions.f: Its 'trunk' is made of soft leaf stalks, not hard wood.

questions.q: Why do plants look green to our eyes?
questions.f: Plants absorb red and blue light but bounce green light back to us.

questions.q: What is the underground fungus network that links trees called?
questions.f: Through it, trees can share food and even send warning signals.

questions.q: Why does a picked flower slowly droop and wilt?
questions.f: Without water filling its cells, the stem goes soft and floppy.

questions.q: What is the name of the tallest living tree on Earth?
questions.f: Hyperion is a coast redwood taller than the Statue of Liberty.

questions.q: About how old is Methuselah, one of the oldest living trees?
questions.f: This bristlecone pine sprouted long before ancient Rome existed.

questions.q: Why does a Venus flytrap bother catching insects?
questions.f: Boggy soil is poor, so bugs give the plant nitrogen it needs.

questions.q: What do we call moving pollen from one flower to another?
questions.f: Without pollination, most plants could never make seeds or fruit.

questions.q: Why do many desert cacti open their leaf pores only at night?
questions.f: Opening at night in the cool air means far less water escapes.

questions.q: What is Pando, thought to be the world's largest living thing?
questions.f: Pando's thousands of aspen trunks all share one huge root system.

questions.q: Why do leaves have tiny pores called stomata?
questions.f: Stomata let in carbon dioxide and let out oxygen and water vapor.

questions.q: What chemical makes a chili pepper taste fiery hot?
questions.f: Capsaicin tricks your mouth into feeling heat that isn't burning you.

questions.q: About how heavy can the world's largest seed grow?
questions.f: The coco de mer seed is heavier than many young children.

questions.q: Why do flowers have bright colors and sweet scents?
questions.f: Colors and smells guide bees and birds that carry pollen for them.

questions.q: What do we call a plant that grows on another plant for support?
questions.f: Rainforest orchids perch high on branches to reach the sunlight.

questions.q: Why does a tree form one new ring each year?
questions.f: Wood grows fast and pale in spring, then slow and dark by autumn.

questions.q: What gives autumn leaves their red and orange colors?
questions.f: These colors hid under the green all summer and appear as it fades.

questions.q: Trees can share food and signals through underground fungi.
questions.f: Scientists nicknamed this hidden network the 'Wood Wide Web'.

questions.q: A Venus flytrap counts touches before it snaps shut.
questions.f: Two quick touches on its hairs tell it a real bug has arrived.

questions.q: The world's largest living thing is a kind of animal.
questions.f: It's Pando, a giant grove of aspen trees sharing one root system.

questions.q: Some cacti open their leaf pores at night to save water.
questions.f: This clever nighttime trick helps them survive scorching deserts.

questions.q: What does water turn into when it freezes?
questions.f: Water freezes into solid ice at 0 degrees Celsius.

questions.q: What puffs out of a kettle when water boils?
questions.f: Real steam is invisible; the white cloud is tiny water droplets!

questions.q: Ice is just frozen water.
questions.f: Ice, snow, and steam are all the same stuff: water in different forms!

questions.q: Which state of matter is a rock?
questions.f: Solids keep their shape; liquids take the shape of their container.

questions.q: Which of these melts on a hot sunny day?
questions.f: Melting is a solid turning into a liquid as heat makes its particles wiggle apart.

questions.q: Hot air rises.
questions.f: That is how hot air balloons fly: a flame heats the air inside!

questions.q: Which of these floats in a bathtub?
questions.f: The duck is full of air, making it lighter than the water it sits on.

questions.q: Which of these is a liquid?
questions.f: Liquids have no shape of their own and take the shape of the cup.

questions.q: Which of these is a gas?
questions.f: You cannot see air, but it is real matter and even has weight!

questions.q: What do you see when you look into a still puddle?
questions.f: Smooth water bounces light back at you, just like a mirror.

questions.q: Where at home do magnets stick easily?
questions.f: Fridge doors have steel inside, and magnets love to grab steel.

questions.q: What do you need to make a shadow?
questions.f: Your shadow is longest in the morning and evening when the Sun is low.

questions.q: What makes snow melt?
questions.f: Melted snow turns back into water, which can freeze into snow again someday!

questions.q: What color is the sky on a clear, sunny day?
questions.f: Sunlight is scattered by the air, and blue scatters the most.

questions.q: Which of these gives Earth light and heat?
questions.f: The Sun is a giant ball of glowing gas about 150 million kilometres away.

questions.q: What pulls a dropped ball down to the ground?
questions.f: Gravity pulls everything toward the centre of the Earth.

questions.q: Which of these sinks in water?
questions.f: Objects denser than water sink; lighter ones float on top.

questions.q: A magnet can pull a metal paper clip toward it.
questions.f: Magnets pull on iron and steel, but not on plastic or paper.

questions.q: What travels through the air to reach your ears so you can hear?
questions.f: Sound is a vibration that ripples through the air as invisible waves.

questions.q: Rub a balloon on your hair and your hair will do what?
questions.f: Rubbing builds up static electricity, which makes hairs push apart and rise.

questions.q: What happens when you pour water into a differently shaped cup?
questions.f: Liquids flow and fit their container, while solids keep their own shape.

questions.q: Which of these lets light shine through it?
questions.f: Materials you can see through are called transparent.

questions.q: What happens to a puddle on a warm, sunny day?
questions.f: The water evaporates into invisible vapour and floats up into the air.

questions.q: Which of these is a solid?
questions.f: An ice cube keeps its shape until heat melts it back into liquid water.

questions.q: Boiling water is very what?
questions.f: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius, far too hot to touch!

questions.q: What do green plants use from the Sun to grow?
questions.f: Plants soak up sunlight to make their own food in a process called photosynthesis.

questions.q: Which way does a ball roll when you push it?
questions.f: A push or a pull is called a force, and it makes things move.

questions.q: You can see your face in a calm, still lake like a mirror.
questions.f: Smooth water reflects light evenly, so it acts like a natural mirror.

questions.q: What is snow made of?
questions.f: Every snowflake is frozen water with six sides, and no two are exactly alike!

questions.q: Which is easier to squash and change shape?
questions.f: Soft solids can bend and squash, while hard solids hold firm.

questions.q: How many colours are in a rainbow?
questions.f: Remember them as ROYGBIV: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet!

questions.q: At what temperature does water freeze?
questions.f: Ponds start to freeze only when the temperature drops to zero degrees Celsius.

questions.q: At what temperature does water boil?
questions.f: At 100 degrees Celsius water bubbles wildly as it turns into gas.

questions.q: Which gas makes party balloons float up?
questions.f: Helium is lighter than air, so a helium balloon rises instead of falling.

questions.q: When the two north poles of magnets meet, what happens?
questions.f: Opposites attract: a north pole and a south pole snap together instead!

questions.q: Which tool has a needle that always points north?
questions.f: A compass needle is a tiny magnet pulled by Earth, which is a giant magnet!

questions.q: What happens when you mix baking soda and vinegar?
questions.f: The fizz is carbon dioxide gas, the same gas that makes soda bubbly!

questions.q: Which of these will a magnet pick up?
questions.f: Magnets grab metals like iron and steel, never plastic, rubber, or wood.

questions.q: Oil floats on top of water.
questions.f: Oil is less dense than water, so it always rises to the top.

questions.q: Sugar dissolves fastest in which kind of water?
questions.f: Heat makes water particles zoom around and pull the sugar apart faster.

questions.q: Where does the water go when a puddle dries up in the Sun?
questions.f: The water turns into invisible vapour and floats up to help make clouds.

questions.q: Which gas do people need to breathe in to stay alive?
questions.f: Every breath you take pulls oxygen into your lungs and blood.

questions.q: What do we call it when a solid turns into a liquid?
questions.f: Chocolate melting in your warm hand is a solid becoming a liquid.

questions.q: What do we call it when a liquid turns into a gas?
questions.f: Wet clothes dry because the water evaporates into the air.

questions.q: Which metal is strongly attracted to a magnet?
questions.f: Iron, nickel, and cobalt are the main magnetic metals; gold and copper are not.

questions.q: A rainbow can appear in the spray from a garden hose.
questions.f: Any water drops in sunshine can split light into colours, even a waterfall's mist!

questions.q: Which of these makes a sound by vibrating?
questions.f: All sounds come from something vibrating and shaking the air.

questions.q: What do batteries store to power your toys?
questions.f: A battery stores chemical energy and turns it into electricity when used.

questions.q: Ice, liquid water, and steam are all the same substance.
questions.f: They are all water; only the temperature and state are different.

questions.q: Which of these is transparent, meaning you can see through it?
questions.f: Transparent materials let light pass straight through them.

questions.q: What do we call a push or a pull on an object?
questions.f: Forces can start, stop, speed up, or turn moving things.

questions.q: A ball rolling across grass slows down because of what?
questions.f: Friction is a rubbing force between surfaces that slows things down.

questions.q: The Moon makes its own light.
questions.f: The Moon has no light of its own; it only reflects sunlight back to us.

questions.q: How many poles does every magnet have?
questions.f: Every magnet has a north pole and a south pole, no matter how you cut it!

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a solid?
questions.f: Water is a liquid; it flows and has no shape of its own.

questions.q: Where does salt come from that we sprinkle on food?
questions.f: Sea salt is left behind when seawater dries up in the Sun.

questions.q: What do we call heat that moves from the Sun to your skin?
questions.f: The Sun sends out energy as light and warmth across space.

questions.q: Which of these will float on water?
questions.f: Wood is less dense than water, so it bobs on the surface.

questions.q: What appears in the sky when sunlight passes through raindrops?
questions.f: Each raindrop acts like a tiny prism, bending light into seven colours.

questions.q: Rubbing your feet on a carpet can build up what on your body?
questions.f: The tiny shock you feel touching a doorknob is that static jumping across!

questions.q: Which two elements make up a water molecule?
questions.f: That is why scientists call water H2O: two hydrogens joined to one oxygen.

questions.q: Which gas makes up most of the air we breathe?
questions.f: Air is about 78 percent nitrogen; oxygen is only about a fifth of each breath!

questions.q: What is frozen carbon dioxide called?
questions.f: Dry ice is minus 78 degrees C and turns straight into fog-like gas without melting!

questions.q: Why does popcorn pop?
c: Steam builds up inside the kernel
questions.f: Water inside the kernel turns to steam until the hard shell bursts open!

questions.q: Sprinkling salt on ice makes it melt faster.
questions.f: Salt lowers water's freezing point, which is why trucks salt icy winter roads.

questions.q: What gas makes the bubbles in fizzy drinks?
questions.f: The gas is squeezed in at the factory and rushes out as bubbles when you open it!

questions.q: What forms when iron is left in water and air for a long time?
questions.f: Mars looks red because its dust is full of rusty iron!

questions.q: Water expands and takes up more space when it freezes.
questions.f: Freezing water expands so hard it can crack rocks and burst metal pipes!

questions.q: What does a glass prism do to white light?
questions.f: White light is secretly every rainbow colour mixed together; a prism un-mixes them!

questions.q: How hot can a lightning bolt get?
questions.f: Lightning reaches about 30,000 degrees C, five times hotter than the Sun's surface!

questions.q: Which metal is a liquid at room temperature?
questions.f: Mercury is the only metal that flows like a liquid without being heated.

questions.q: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.f: Au comes from 'aurum', the old Latin word for gold.

questions.q: What is the chemical symbol for oxygen?
questions.f: Every element has a short symbol; oxygen's is simply the letter O.

questions.q: Materials that let electricity flow through them are called what?
questions.f: Metals like copper are great conductors, which is why wires are made of them.

questions.q: Materials that block electricity, like rubber, are called what?
questions.f: Rubber and plastic wrap the outside of wires to keep the electricity safely inside.

questions.q: About how much of the air around us is oxygen?
questions.f: Oxygen is roughly 21 percent of air; most of the rest is nitrogen.

questions.q: Which travels faster, light or sound?
questions.f: Light is so fast it could circle the whole Earth about seven times in one second!

questions.q: Sound cannot travel through the empty space between planets.
questions.f: Space has no air to carry sound waves, so astronauts talk using radios!

questions.q: When you shine red, green, and blue light together, what colour appears?
questions.f: Red, green, and blue are the primary colours of light and combine to make white.

questions.q: What do we call energy that is stored in food and batteries?
questions.f: Your body turns the chemical energy in food into the energy to run and jump!

questions.q: The energy of a moving object is called what?
questions.f: A rolling ball and a running dog both have kinetic energy from moving.

questions.q: What is the tiny building block that all matter is made of?
questions.f: Atoms are so small that millions could fit across the width of a single hair!

questions.q: What do we call two or more atoms joined together?
questions.f: A water molecule is just three atoms: two hydrogen and one oxygen, stuck together.

questions.q: Metals are usually good at carrying heat.
questions.f: That is why a metal spoon in hot soup soon feels warm all the way up the handle.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of static electricity?
questions.f: Static builds up when charges collect on something, then jumps as a tiny spark!

questions.q: Common table salt is made from which two elements?
questions.f: On their own, sodium and chlorine are dangerous, but joined they make safe salt!

questions.q: What do we call the pull that makes a compass point north?
questions.f: Earth has a magnetic field, as if a giant bar magnet ran through its centre.

questions.q: What happens to most liquids when they get very cold?
questions.f: Cooling slows a liquid's particles until they lock together into a solid.

questions.q: Which of these will a magnet NOT attract?
questions.f: Magnets pull only a few metals; aluminium simply ignores them!

questions.q: Which of these temperatures is the coldest?
questions.f: Your home freezer runs near minus 18 degrees C to keep ice cream solid.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a state of matter?
questions.f: Matter takes up space; a shadow is just a spot where light is blocked.

questions.q: Sound travels faster through water than through air.
questions.f: Sound moves about four times faster in water; whales chat across huge distances!

questions.q: Which of these sinks in water?
questions.f: Yet giant steel ships float because their air-filled shape is less dense than water!

questions.q: Which change turns water vapour into liquid drops?
questions.f: That is why a cold drink 'sweats': vapour in the air turns to drops on the glass.

questions.q: Helium is heavier than air.
questions.f: Helium is the second-lightest element in the universe, so helium balloons rise!

questions.q: Which of these kitchen liquids is an acid?
questions.f: Lemons are so acidic you can even use one to power a tiny light bulb!

questions.q: What is the correct order as water heats up from cold?
questions.f: Adding heat moves water from solid to liquid to gas, in that order.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a metal?
questions.f: Carbon is a non-metal; you find it in pencil lead and even in diamonds!

questions.q: With no air, which falls faster, a hammer or a feather?
c: They fall at the same speed
questions.f: An astronaut proved this on the airless Moon: hammer and feather landed together!

questions.q: Which colour of light carries the most energy?
questions.f: Violet and blue light have the shortest waves and the most energy.

questions.q: In a jar of honey, water, and oil, which sinks to the very bottom?
questions.f: The densest liquid, honey, sits at the bottom and the lightest, oil, floats on top.

questions.q: Which of these does NOT need a magnet to work?
questions.f: Motors, compasses, and fridge magnets all rely on magnetism; a rubber band does not.

questions.q: Which is louder, a whisper or a jet engine?
questions.f: Loudness is measured in decibels, and a jet engine is far louder than a whisper.

questions.q: A balloon rubbed on your hair can stick to a wall.
questions.f: Static electricity on the balloon pulls it against the wall like invisible glue.

questions.q: Which material is the best at keeping heat in?
questions.f: Wool traps tiny pockets of air, which slow heat from escaping; that keeps you warm.

questions.q: Which of these is the hardest natural material on Earth?
questions.f: Diamonds are so hard that only another diamond can scratch them!

questions.q: Put these in order from smallest to largest.
questions.f: Atoms join to make molecules, and trillions of molecules make one grain of sand.

questions.q: Why do heavy steel ships float instead of sinking?
c: Their shape holds lots of air
They are made of hollow gold
questions.f: A ship's wide, hollow shape spreads its weight so it is less dense than water.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a source of energy?
questions.f: The Sun, wind, and coal all give energy; a shadow is just blocked light.

questions.q: Warm water can hold less dissolved gas than cold water.
questions.f: That is why a warm fizzy drink goes flat faster; the gas escapes more easily.

questions.q: Why do you see lightning before you hear thunder?
questions.f: Light reaches you almost instantly, but sound takes a few seconds per kilometre.

questions.q: Why does ice float on water?
c: Ice is less dense than water
questions.f: Floating ice keeps ponds warmer underneath, so fish can survive the winter!

questions.q: What is the coldest temperature possible, called absolute zero?
questions.f: At absolute zero atoms almost stop moving, and nothing can ever get colder!

questions.q: Why does water boil at a lower temperature on a tall mountain?
questions.f: On Mount Everest water boils at about 71 degrees C, so tea comes out lukewarm!

questions.q: Metal and wood at the same temperature; why does metal feel colder?
c: Metal pulls heat from your hand faster
questions.f: Metal conducts heat away from your skin far faster than wood does.

questions.q: What actually causes the sound of thunder?
c: Lightning heats air so fast it bursts outward
questions.f: Lightning superheats the air in a split second, and it explodes outward as a boom!

questions.q: Sound can travel through the empty vacuum of space.
questions.f: Space has no air to carry the waves, so it is completely silent out there.

questions.q: Why does the sky look blue during the day?
c: Blue light scatters most in the air
The Sun gives off blue fire
questions.f: At sunset light crosses more air, so reds and oranges take over the sky instead!

questions.q: Why does sweating help cool you down?
c: Sweat is made of ice water
questions.f: As sweat evaporates it takes body heat with it, leaving your skin cooler.

questions.q: What are stars, including our Sun, mostly made of?
questions.f: Hydrogen is the most common element in the whole universe.

questions.q: Why can't a magnet pick up a copper coin?
c: Copper is not a magnetic metal
questions.f: Only iron, nickel, and cobalt are magnetic; most other metals are not.

questions.q: What force keeps the planets orbiting around the Sun?
questions.f: The Sun's enormous gravity holds every planet in its looping path.

questions.q: What happens to the tiny atoms in something as it gets hotter?
questions.f: Heat is really the energy of atoms jiggling; the hotter it is, the faster they move.

questions.q: Why does a straw look bent in a glass of water?
c: Light bends as it enters the water
Your eyes are tricked by colour
questions.f: Light changes speed and bends when it passes into water; this is called refraction.

questions.q: Which is the lightest element on the periodic table?
questions.f: A single hydrogen atom has just one proton, the simplest atom of all.

questions.q: When all the colours of light are mixed together, they make white light.
questions.f: Sunlight looks white but secretly contains every colour of the rainbow!

questions.q: Why does breathing helium make your voice squeaky?
questions.f: Sound zips faster through light helium, which raises the pitch of your voice.

questions.q: Why does a hot air balloon rise into the sky?
c: Hot air is lighter than cool air
questions.f: Heating the air inside makes it less dense, so the whole balloon floats upward.

questions.q: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth.
questions.f: Even at light's incredible speed, the Sun is so far that its light is 8 minutes old!

questions.q: Gravity on the Moon is weaker than gravity on Earth.
questions.f: The Moon's gravity is about one-sixth of Earth's, so you could jump six times higher!

questions.q: Which planet do we live on?
questions.f: Earth is the only planet we know of that has life on it.

questions.q: What gives Earth its light and heat during the day?
questions.f: The Sun is so bright that its light reaches us even from 150 million kilometres away.

questions.q: What glows in the night sky and changes shape each month?
questions.f: The Moon does not really change shape — we just see different amounts of its sunlit side.

questions.q: True or False: The Sun is a star.
questions.f: The Sun only looks bigger than other stars because it is the closest one to us.

questions.q: What do stars seem to do in the night sky?
questions.f: Stars twinkle because their light wiggles as it passes through Earth's moving air.

questions.q: Which planet is called the Red Planet?
questions.f: Mars looks red because its soil is full of rusty iron, like an old nail.

questions.q: How many moons does Earth have?
questions.f: Our one Moon is the fifth-largest moon in the whole solar system.

questions.q: What do astronauts wear to breathe outside their spaceship?
questions.f: A spacesuit is like a tiny wearable spaceship that carries its own air to breathe.

questions.q: Where do astronauts live while working in orbit?
questions.f: The International Space Station circles the whole Earth about every 90 minutes.

questions.q: True or False: The Moon makes its own light.
questions.f: The Moon works like a giant mirror, reflecting light that comes from the Sun.

questions.q: What shape is planet Earth?
questions.f: Earth bulges a little at its middle, so it is not a perfectly round ball.

questions.q: In which direction does the Sun rise each morning?
questions.f: The Sun is not moving across the sky — Earth is spinning you toward it.

questions.q: Which tool makes faraway stars and planets look closer?
questions.f: Galileo used a small telescope to spot Jupiter's four biggest moons over 400 years ago.

questions.q: What roars up with fire and smoke to reach space?
questions.f: To reach space, a rocket must fly faster than a speeding bullet.

questions.q: What force pulls a jumping child back down to the ground?
questions.f: Without gravity you would float away like an astronaut in space.

questions.q: True or False: Astronauts float around inside the space station.
questions.f: They are really falling around Earth all the time, which makes everything float.

questions.q: What do we call everything that exists in space?
questions.f: The universe is so huge that nobody has ever found its edge.

questions.q: What covers most of planet Earth's surface?
questions.f: About seven out of every ten parts of Earth's surface is ocean water.

questions.q: What colour does a clear daytime sky look?
questions.f: The sky looks blue because air scatters the Sun's blue light all around.

questions.q: True or False: You can breathe in outer space without a helmet.
questions.f: Space has no air at all, so astronauts must always carry oxygen with them.

questions.q: Which season is usually the coldest of the year?
questions.f: Winter is cold because your part of Earth is tilted away from the Sun.

questions.q: Which planet is famous for its bright rings?
questions.f: Saturn's rings are made of billions of chunks of ice, from tiny grains to house-sized blocks.

questions.q: What do we call the Sun and its family of planets together?
questions.f: Our Solar System has eight planets, plus moons, comets and asteroids.

questions.q: What does Earth do to make day turn into night?
questions.f: Earth spins once every 24 hours, giving us one day and one night.

questions.q: Is the surface of the Sun hot or cold?
questions.f: The Sun's surface is about 5,500 degrees Celsius — hot enough to melt any metal.

questions.q: What is the Sun made of — a giant ball of what?
questions.f: The Sun is a huge spinning ball of gas, mostly hydrogen.

questions.q: True or False: There is no air to breathe on the Moon.
questions.f: With no air, the Moon has no wind and no sound at all.

questions.q: How many planets travel around our Sun?
questions.f: There used to be nine until Pluto was renamed a dwarf planet in 2006.

questions.q: What do we call the bright dots we see scattered across the night sky?
questions.f: Every star you see is a giant ball of glowing gas, like our own Sun.

questions.q: What is the job of a person who travels into space?
questions.f: Astronauts train for years before they ever fly into space.

questions.q: Which planet is the largest in our solar system?
questions.f: Jupiter is so big that more than 1,300 Earths could fit inside it.

questions.q: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
questions.f: Even though Mercury is closest to the Sun, Venus is actually the hottest planet.

questions.q: What is the name of the galaxy we live in?
questions.f: The Milky Way holds more than 100 billion stars.

questions.q: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.f: He stepped onto the Moon in 1969 and called it one small step for man.

questions.q: What do we call a ball of ice and dust with a long glowing tail?
questions.f: Halley's Comet swings past Earth about every 76 years, next in 2061.

questions.q: What do we call a group of stars that forms a picture in the sky?
questions.f: The famous Big Dipper stars are part of a constellation called the Great Bear.

questions.q: Which planet is the hottest in our solar system?
questions.f: Thick clouds trap heat on Venus, making it hot enough to melt lead.

questions.q: Which planet is farthest from the Sun?
questions.f: Neptune is so far away that sunlight takes over four hours to reach it.

questions.q: True or False: A year is the time Earth takes to circle the Sun once.
questions.f: Earth travels almost a billion kilometres on its yearly loop around the Sun.

questions.q: Who was the first person ever to travel into space?
questions.f: Yuri Gagarin from Russia orbited Earth once in 1961 in just 108 minutes.

questions.q: What do we call a rocky object orbiting the Sun that is smaller than a planet?
questions.f: Most asteroids circle the Sun in a wide ring between Mars and Jupiter.

questions.q: Rakesh Sharma in 1984 was the first person in space from which country?
questions.f: From orbit he was asked how India looked, and he replied it looked wonderful.

questions.q: True or False: The Moon is closer to Earth than the Sun is.
questions.f: The Sun is about 400 times farther from us than the Moon.

questions.q: What do we call a meteor streaking as a bright line across the night sky?
questions.f: A shooting star is not a star at all — it is a tiny rock burning up in the air.

questions.q: What was the first human-made satellite launched into space?
questions.f: Sputnik was launched in 1957 and beeped radio signals back to Earth.

questions.q: Which planet spins tipped over on its side like a rolling ball?
questions.f: Uranus is tilted so far that its poles take turns pointing almost at the Sun.

questions.q: What are Saturn's famous rings mostly made of?
questions.f: If you could gather Saturn's rings into a ball, it would be quite small.

questions.q: What do we call the Moon when we can see its whole bright circle?
questions.f: A full moon happens about once a month, which is where the word month comes from.

questions.q: What do we call the Moon phase when we cannot see it at all?
questions.f: During a new moon, the Moon's dark side faces us and its bright side faces the Sun.

questions.q: True or False: Stars shine forever and never change or die.
questions.f: Stars are born, shine for billions of years, and eventually run out of fuel.

questions.q: How long does the International Space Station take to circle Earth once?
questions.f: Astronauts on the station see about 16 sunrises and sunsets every single day.

questions.q: What do we call the curved path a planet takes around the Sun?
questions.f: Planets stay in their orbits because the Sun's gravity keeps pulling them around.

questions.q: Which planet has two tiny moons named Phobos and Deimos?
questions.f: Phobos, the bigger moon, is slowly falling closer to Mars each year.

questions.q: What do we call any natural object that orbits around a planet?
questions.f: Jupiter has dozens of moons, while Mercury and Venus have none at all.

questions.q: True or False: The Sun is far bigger than the planet Earth.
questions.f: About one million Earths could fit inside the Sun.

questions.q: In Russia, people who travel to space are called what?
questions.f: Astronaut and cosmonaut mean almost the same thing — a space traveller.

questions.q: Which planet is closest to Earth in size?
questions.f: Venus is sometimes called Earth's twin because they are nearly the same size.

questions.q: Which small icy world was once called the ninth planet?
questions.f: Pluto is so far away that one year there lasts about 248 Earth years.

questions.q: What do we call a huge group of billions of stars held together by gravity?
questions.f: There are more galaxies in the universe than grains of sand on all Earth's beaches.

questions.q: About how long does sunlight take to travel from the Sun to Earth?
questions.f: So the sunlight warming you now actually left the Sun about eight minutes ago.

questions.q: How long is one year on Mercury, the fastest-orbiting planet?
questions.f: Mercury races around the Sun so fast that its year is shorter than three months.

questions.q: About how hot is the deep centre, or core, of the Sun?
questions.f: The Sun's core is where hydrogen is squeezed together to make its energy.

questions.q: Which gas makes up most of the air in Earth's atmosphere?
questions.f: Nitrogen is about 78 percent of our air, while oxygen is only about 21 percent.

questions.q: About how high above Earth does the International Space Station orbit?
questions.f: At 400 kilometres up, the station zooms along at about 28,000 kilometres per hour.

questions.q: What is the name of the tallest volcano in the solar system, found on Mars?
questions.f: Olympus Mons is about three times taller than Mount Everest.

questions.q: Which planet has the shortest day, spinning around in only about 10 hours?
questions.f: Jupiter spins so fast that it bulges out at its middle like a squished ball.

questions.q: True or False: On Venus, one day lasts longer than one whole year.
questions.f: Venus spins so slowly that it turns around once every 243 Earth days.

questions.q: Other than the Sun, what is the closest star to our solar system?
questions.f: Even the nearest star is so far that its light takes over four years to reach us.

questions.q: About how long does the Moon take to go through all of its phases?
questions.f: The full cycle of Moon phases takes about 29.5 days, roughly one month.

questions.q: How fast must a spacecraft travel to stay in orbit around Earth?
questions.f: That is more than 20 times faster than a passenger jet plane.

questions.q: True or False: You would weigh exactly the same on the Moon as on Earth.
questions.f: On the Moon you would weigh about six times less, so you could jump much higher.

questions.q: The Moon's gravity is about how strong compared with Earth's gravity?
questions.f: That weak gravity is why the Apollo astronauts bounced when they walked.

questions.q: About how long does Neptune take to orbit the Sun one time?
questions.f: Neptune has only completed one full orbit since it was discovered in 1846.

questions.q: What do we call it when the Moon blocks out the Sun during the day?
questions.f: During a total solar eclipse, day turns to twilight and stars can appear.

questions.q: What do we call it when Earth's shadow falls across the Moon?
questions.f: During a lunar eclipse the Moon often glows red, earning it the name blood moon.

questions.q: How many official constellations do astronomers around the world recognise?
questions.f: The constellations were finally agreed upon and mapped out in the 1920s.

questions.q: True or False: There is no sound in outer space.
questions.f: Sound needs air or water to travel, and space is an empty vacuum.

questions.q: What is the largest moon in the whole solar system, orbiting Jupiter?
questions.f: Ganymede is even bigger than the planet Mercury.

questions.q: Mars looks red because its dusty soil is full of what?
questions.f: The iron in Mars's soil rusted long ago, giving the whole planet a reddish colour.

questions.q: Which gas makes up most of the Sun?
questions.f: The Sun turns hydrogen into helium deep in its core to make all its energy.

questions.q: True or False: Comets are made mostly of hot, glowing rock.
questions.f: Comets are really dirty snowballs of ice and dust, sometimes called cosmic snowballs.

questions.q: Where is the main asteroid belt located in our solar system?
questions.f: Millions of asteroids circle there, but they are so spread out that ships fly through safely.

questions.q: Which star sits almost directly above Earth's North Pole?
questions.f: Because it barely moves, sailors used Polaris, the North Star, to find their way.

questions.q: Which planet is so light it could float in a giant tub of water?
questions.f: Saturn is a giant ball of gas, making it the least dense planet of all.

questions.q: What is the name of India's series of missions sent to explore the Moon?
questions.f: In 2023, Chandrayaan-3 landed near the Moon's little-explored south pole.

questions.q: What was the name of India's spacecraft that reached Mars orbit in 2014?
questions.f: India was the first country to reach Mars orbit on its very first try.

questions.q: How long can the footprints left by astronauts last on the Moon?
questions.f: With no wind or rain on the Moon, those footprints will stay for a very long time.

questions.q: What do we call the huge distance that light travels in one whole year?
questions.f: A light-year is about 9.5 trillion kilometres — a way to measure giant space distances.

questions.q: Which planet is the smallest in our solar system?
questions.f: Mercury is only a little bigger than our Moon.

questions.q: Of these planets, which one is farthest from the Sun?
questions.f: The order outward is Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, then Neptune the farthest.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a planet?
questions.f: A comet is a small icy body that orbits the Sun, not a planet.

questions.q: Which planet is the hottest, even though Mercury sits closer to the Sun?
questions.f: Venus's thick clouds trap heat like a blanket, keeping it hotter than Mercury.

questions.q: Going outward from the Sun, which planet comes right after Earth?
questions.f: The rocky inner planets in order are Mercury, Venus, Earth, then Mars.

questions.q: True or False: Saturn has more known moons than Jupiter does.
questions.f: Astronomers have now counted over 140 moons around Saturn, more than any other planet.

questions.q: Which is the largest object in our whole solar system?
questions.f: The Sun holds more than 99 percent of all the material in the solar system.

questions.q: Why is Pluto now called a dwarf planet instead of a full planet?
c: It has not cleared its orbit of other objects
questions.f: A real planet must sweep its path clear, but Pluto shares its space with many icy bodies.

questions.q: Which planet looks blue-green because of methane gas high in its air?
questions.f: The methane in Uranus's atmosphere soaks up red light and reflects back blue-green.

questions.q: True or False: Pluto is bigger than Earth's Moon.
questions.f: Pluto is actually smaller than our Moon, which is one reason it was reclassified.

questions.q: What is the main reason Earth has different seasons through the year?
questions.f: Earth is tilted about 23 degrees, so each half leans toward the Sun for part of the year.

questions.q: What do we call a space rock that survives and lands on the ground?
questions.f: In space it is a meteoroid, a streak in the sky is a meteor, and on the ground it is a meteorite.

questions.q: True or False: The Sun holds over 99 percent of the solar system's mass.
questions.f: Everything else — all the planets and moons — is just the leftover crumbs.

questions.q: When it is summer in India, what season is it down in Australia?
questions.f: The two halves of Earth have opposite seasons because of the planet's tilt.

questions.q: Which planet is the second one out from the Sun?
questions.f: Venus is also the brightest planet in our sky, often called the morning or evening star.

questions.q: What do we call an object with gravity so strong that not even light can escape?
questions.f: There is a giant black hole at the very centre of our Milky Way galaxy.

questions.q: True or False: A shooting star is usually a small rock, not a real star.
questions.f: Most shooting stars are pieces of dust or rock no bigger than a grain of sand.

questions.q: Which large galaxy is the closest neighbour to our own Milky Way?
questions.f: Andromeda is racing toward us and will meet the Milky Way in billions of years.

questions.q: During a solar eclipse, which object lines up between the Sun and Earth?
questions.f: The Moon's shadow sweeps across Earth, and only a narrow strip sees a total eclipse.

questions.q: Which planet is the fourth one out from the Sun?
questions.f: After Mars come the four giant planets: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a rocky planet?
questions.f: Jupiter is a gas giant with no solid surface to stand on.

questions.q: Kalpana Chawla, born in India, became famous around the world as what?
questions.f: She was the first woman of Indian origin to fly to space, aboard a Space Shuttle.

questions.q: How does the Sun produce its enormous light and heat?
questions.f: In fusion, hydrogen atoms squeeze together into helium, releasing huge amounts of energy.

questions.q: In billions of years, our Sun will swell up into which kind of star?
questions.f: As a red giant, the Sun may grow big enough to swallow the innermost planets.

questions.q: What is the real reason we have day and night?
questions.f: As Earth spins, your side turns to face the Sun for day and away for night.

questions.q: Why do astronauts float around inside the orbiting space station?
c: They are constantly falling around Earth
There is no gravity up there
questions.f: Gravity is still strong at that height — the station and crew simply fall together forever.

questions.q: Why do stars twinkle when you look up at the night sky?
c: Their light is bent by Earth's moving air
questions.f: Above the atmosphere, astronauts see stars shining steadily without any twinkle.

questions.q: True or False: A black hole's gravity is so strong that even light cannot escape it.
questions.f: That is exactly why black holes look completely black — no light comes back out.

questions.q: Which way does a comet's glowing tail always point?
questions.f: The Sun's energy blows the comet's dust and gas outward, so the tail leads on the way home.

questions.q: Venus is unusual because it spins which way compared with most other planets?
questions.f: On Venus the Sun would appear to rise in the west and set in the east.

questions.q: True or False: Earth's day is very slowly getting longer over millions of years.
questions.f: The Moon's pull gently slows Earth's spin, adding a tiny bit of time each century.

questions.q: Our Milky Way is which shape of galaxy?
questions.f: Our Sun sits on one of the Milky Way's curving spiral arms, far from the centre.

questions.q: What do we call the minimum speed needed to break free of Earth's gravity?
questions.f: Earth's escape velocity is about 40,000 kilometres per hour.

questions.q: Ganymede, the solar system's biggest moon, is even larger than which planet?
questions.f: If Ganymede orbited the Sun on its own, we might well call it a planet.

questions.q: True or False: The North Star, Polaris, is the brightest star in the whole night sky.
questions.f: The brightest night star is actually Sirius, the Dog Star; Polaris just holds still.

questions.q: Besides Pluto, which dwarf planet is found within the asteroid belt?
questions.f: Ceres is the largest object in the asteroid belt and the only dwarf planet there.

questions.q: What stream of particles flowing from the Sun helps create the colourful auroras?
questions.f: When the solar wind hits Earth's magnetic field, it lights up skies near the poles.

questions.q: True or False: Sunlight takes about eight minutes to travel from the Sun to Earth.
questions.f: If the Sun suddenly vanished, we would keep seeing it for about eight more minutes.

questions.q: About how fast does light travel through empty space?
questions.f: Nothing in the universe can travel faster than the speed of light.

questions.q: What is the giant explosion called when a very large star dies?
questions.f: A single supernova can briefly shine brighter than a whole galaxy of stars.

questions.q: Why can the small Moon completely hide the giant Sun during a total eclipse?
c: The Moon is much closer, so both look the same size
questions.f: By luck, the Sun is about 400 times wider than the Moon but also 400 times farther away.

questions.q: What is the name of India's first spacecraft sent to study the Sun?
questions.f: Launched in 2023, Aditya-L1 watches the Sun from a special point about 1.5 million km from Earth.

questions.q: How many players from one team are on a soccer field at once?
questions.f: A full soccer team has eleven players, and one of them is the goalkeeper!

questions.q: In basketball, what do you do to the ball while running with it?
questions.f: Bouncing the ball as you move is called dribbling — you can't just run holding it!

questions.q: In tennis, what do you swing to hit the ball?
questions.f: A tennis racket has tightly strung threads that spring the ball back fast!

questions.q: How many players from one team are on a basketball court at once?
questions.f: Basketball is played five-on-five, so ten players share the court in total!

questions.q: At the Olympics, which medal does the first-place winner receive?
questions.f: Gold medals are mostly silver with just a thin layer of real gold on top!

questions.q: Which swimming stroke shares its name with an insect?
questions.f: In butterfly, both arms sweep over the water together like flapping wings!

questions.q: In bowling, what are you trying to knock over?
questions.f: Bowling uses ten pins set up in a triangle at the end of the lane!

questions.q: Which game uses pieces called a king and a queen on a checkered board?
questions.f: Chess has six kinds of pieces, and the queen is the most powerful of all!

questions.q: How many wooden stumps stand behind a cricket batter?
questions.f: Three stumps topped with two little bails together make up the wicket!

questions.q: In soccer, who is the only player allowed to catch the ball with their hands?
questions.f: The goalkeeper can only use hands inside their own penalty box — not anywhere on the pitch!

questions.q: In a relay race, what do teammates pass from runner to runner?
questions.f: If a runner drops the baton, the whole team can lose the race!

questions.q: In cricket, what do you score by running between the wickets?
questions.f: Batters dash back and forth, and each completed length adds one run!

questions.q: What do you wear on your feet to glide across an ice rink?
questions.f: A thin metal blade under each skate lets you slice smoothly over the ice!

questions.q: In a running race, what do runners cross to finish?
questions.f: At big races a camera photographs the finish line to spot the winner in a close race!

questions.q: In badminton, what do players hit back and forth over the net?
questions.f: A shuttlecock has feathers or plastic wings, so it slows down quickly in the air!

questions.q: In table tennis, what do you use to hit the little ball?
questions.f: Table tennis paddles have a rubbery surface that helps players spin the ball!

questions.q: Which famous sport is played on the grass courts of Wimbledon?
questions.f: Wimbledon in England is the oldest tennis tournament in the world!

questions.q: In a hurdles race, what do runners leap over?
questions.f: Hurdlers barely lift their feet — good hurdling looks almost like flat-out running!

questions.q: Which winter sport lets you slide down snowy hills on two long boards?
questions.f: People have used skis to travel over snow for thousands of years!

questions.q: Which playground game is played with small glass balls?
questions.f: Players flick their marble to knock others out of a circle drawn on the ground!

questions.q: What do swimmers wear to see clearly under the water?
questions.f: Human eyes go blurry underwater, but goggles trap air so you can see sharply!

questions.q: What protects your head when you ride a bicycle?
questions.f: A bike helmet has a hard shell and soft foam inside to cushion a bump!

questions.q: What does a referee blow to stop a game?
questions.f: The whistle became popular for sport more than a hundred years ago!

questions.q: Which game do you play by hopping across numbered squares?
questions.f: In India, hopscotch is often called Stapu or Kith-Kith!

questions.q: In gymnastics, what is the long, narrow bar that gymnasts balance on called?
questions.f: A balance beam is only about as wide as your hand, yet gymnasts flip on it!

questions.q: In the game of darts, what do you throw at the board?
questions.f: A dartboard is split into twenty numbered slices around a small bullseye!

questions.q: In bowling, knocking down all the pins with one throw is called a strike.
questions.f: Rolling a strike with your very first ball of the frame is the best start you can get!

questions.q: A soccer ball is shaped like an egg.
questions.f: Soccer balls are round, but rugby and American football balls really are egg-shaped!

questions.q: In a swimming race, the first swimmer to touch the wall wins.
questions.f: Touch pads on the wall sense each swimmer and stop their clock the instant they touch!

questions.q: Table tennis is also known as ping-pong.
questions.f: The name 'ping-pong' comes from the sound the ball makes bouncing on the table!

questions.q: Sumo wrestling comes from which country?
questions.f: Sumo wrestlers eat a huge stew called chankonabe to grow big and strong!

questions.q: In which country did the Olympic Games first begin, long ago?
questions.f: The ancient Games were held at Olympia in Greece over 2,700 years ago!

questions.q: In which Indian sport does a raider chant the game's own name?
questions.f: A kabaddi raider must chant 'kabaddi, kabaddi' in a single breath the whole raid!

questions.q: Which sport is played on ice using a flat rubber disc called a puck?
questions.f: Pucks are frozen before games so they slide instead of bouncing on the ice!

questions.q: How many squares are on a chessboard?
questions.f: A chessboard is eight squares by eight squares, which makes sixty-four in total!

questions.q: About how long is a marathon race?
questions.f: The marathon is named after a Greek messenger who ran a very long way to deliver news!

questions.q: In soccer, what does it mean when the referee shows a red card?
questions.f: Two yellow-card warnings add up to a red card, and off the player goes!

questions.q: How many rings are on the Olympic flag?
questions.f: The five interlocking rings stand for the continents of the world joining together!

questions.q: What score is a perfect game in ten-pin bowling?
questions.f: To score 300 you must roll twelve strikes in a row — every single throw perfect!

questions.q: In Japanese, what does 'judo' translate to?
questions.f: In judo you use your opponent's own push and pull to flip them, not brute force!

questions.q: What kind of game is the Indian sport kho-kho?
questions.f: In kho-kho, chasers sit in a line and tag runners in a fast game of pursuit!

questions.q: How many balls does a bowler bowl in one cricket over?
questions.f: After six legal balls the umpire calls 'over' and a new bowler starts from the other end!

questions.q: In tennis, what is the special word for a score of zero?
questions.f: So a game that starts 'love-all' really means the score is nothing to nothing!

questions.q: At the Olympics, which medal is given for finishing in second place?
questions.f: Gold, silver and bronze were chosen because they were once among the most prized metals!

questions.q: The board game Snakes and Ladders was first invented in which country?
questions.f: It began in India as a game called Moksha Patam that taught lessons about good and bad deeds!

questions.q: How long is an Olympic swimming pool?
questions.f: An Olympic pool is 50 metres long — swimmers cross it many times in a single race!

questions.q: Which sport lets players kick a ball over a net using their feet and head?
questions.f: Sepak takraw is a bit like volleyball, but you can never touch the ball with your hands!

questions.q: What shape is a rugby ball?
questions.f: A rugby ball's pointed oval shape makes it bounce in surprising, tricky directions!

questions.q: Chess began in India long ago as a game with what name?
questions.f: 'Chaturanga' means 'four parts of an army' — foot soldiers, horses, elephants and chariots!

questions.q: Where is the Olympic flame lit before every Games?
questions.f: The flame is lit at ancient Olympia, then carried by runners all the way to the host city!

questions.q: In golf, where are you trying to get the ball?
questions.f: Each hole is marked by a flag, and the fewer hits you take, the better your score!

questions.q: In soccer, what is the marked box where the goalkeeper may use their hands called?
questions.f: Outside this box the keeper must use their feet just like everyone else!

questions.q: Which is the oldest tennis tournament, played on grass in England?
questions.f: Wimbledon players must wear almost all-white clothing — a rule that is over a century old!

questions.q: Which chess piece jumps in an 'L' shape?
questions.f: The knight is the only piece that can leap right over other pieces in its way!

questions.q: What weapon do fencers use in their sport?
questions.f: Fencers wear wired jackets so a machine can beep the moment their sword tip touches!

questions.q: In which country was the sport of rugby first played?
questions.f: The story says a schoolboy in the town of Rugby picked up a soccer ball and ran with it!

questions.q: The Olympic flag shows five coloured rings.
questions.f: The rings are blue, yellow, black, green and red on a white background!

questions.q: A cricket over is made up of ten balls.
questions.f: An over is six balls, not ten — after six the bowling switches to the other end!

questions.q: Badminton is played with a shuttlecock instead of a ball.
questions.f: The feathery shuttlecock, also called a birdie, can start a smash faster than a race car!

questions.q: In sumo, a wrestler tries to push the other out of the ring.
questions.f: You also win if you make your opponent touch the ground with anything but their feet!

questions.q: How many pieces does each chess player start with?
questions.f: Each side has sixteen pieces, so all thirty-two crowd the board at the start!

questions.q: How high above the floor is a basketball hoop in the pro game?
questions.f: The hoop is 3.05 metres up — that's why players train so hard to jump and dunk!

questions.q: How long is the pitch between the two wickets in cricket?
questions.f: The 22-yard pitch has stayed the same length for hundreds of years!

questions.q: How long is a full soccer match, not counting extra time?
questions.f: The match is two halves of 45 minutes each, with a short rest in between!

questions.q: In tennis, how many points must you usually win to take a single game?
questions.f: You need at least four points, and you must be ahead by two to win the game!

questions.q: In tennis, what point score comes right after 30?
questions.f: Tennis scores go 15, 30, 40 — no one is fully sure why those odd numbers were chosen!

questions.q: How many stitches hold a baseball together?
questions.f: Every baseball has exactly 108 double stitches, all sewn on by hand!

questions.q: How many separate events make up a decathlon?
questions.f: 'Deca' means ten, and athletes battle through all ten events over two long days!

questions.q: In volleyball, how many times may a team touch the ball before hitting it back?
questions.f: Teams usually bump, set and spike — three touches to fire the ball over the net!

questions.q: In which year were the first modern Olympic Games held?
questions.f: The modern Games returned in 1896 in Athens, Greece, the home of the ancient Games!

questions.q: In cricket, what is it called when one batter scores 100 runs?
questions.f: Fans clap and the batter often raises their bat to celebrate reaching a century!

questions.q: Which coloured ball is worth the most points in snooker?
questions.f: The black ball is worth seven points — the highest of all the coloured balls!

questions.q: How many points is the very centre bullseye worth in darts?
questions.f: The tiny red bullseye scores 50 — the trickiest and most valuable target on the board!

questions.q: The board game Go is played on a grid of how many lines?
questions.f: Those crossing lines make 361 points, giving Go an astonishing number of possible games!

questions.q: How far from the goal is the penalty spot in soccer?
questions.f: From 11 metres, a well-struck penalty is very hard for the keeper to stop in time!

questions.q: How many holes are played in a standard round of golf?
questions.f: A full golf course is eighteen holes, and players may walk several kilometres to finish!

questions.q: A triathlon is made up of which three sports in a row?
questions.f: Triathletes race straight from the water to a bike and then run — with no rest between!

questions.q: In gymnastics, which event involves swinging on two hanging hoops?
questions.f: Gymnasts must hold the rings perfectly still, which takes incredible arm strength!

questions.q: In many martial arts, which belt colour shows the highest skill?
questions.f: Beginners usually start with a white belt and work their way up to black over many years!

questions.q: In chess, what is the winning move that traps the king called?
questions.f: When the king is checkmated it cannot escape, and the game ends right there!

questions.q: In American football, how many points is a touchdown worth?
questions.f: After scoring six points for a touchdown, a team can kick for one extra point!

questions.q: The sport of curling is played on what surface?
questions.f: Players sweep the ice ahead of a sliding stone to help steer it toward the target!

questions.q: Which sport is part of the Winter Olympics?
questions.f: The Winter Olympics hold snow and ice sports, while summer sports have their own Games!

questions.q: In basketball, how many points is a shot from beyond the far arc worth?
questions.f: A basket from beyond the three-point line is worth one more than a normal two-point shot!

questions.q: A marathon is about 42 kilometres long.
questions.f: The exact distance is 42.195 kilometres — settled at the 1908 London Olympics!

questions.q: A boxing ring is actually shaped like a square.
questions.f: Even though it's called a 'ring', a boxing ring has four sides and four corners!

questions.q: The Olympic Games are held every four years.
questions.f: The gap of four years between Games is even called an 'Olympiad'!

questions.q: In tennis, the score is called 'deuce' when both players reach 40.
questions.f: From deuce a player must win two points in a row to finally take the game!

questions.q: Which of these is NOT an official Olympic swimming stroke?
questions.f: The four racing strokes are freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke and butterfly!

questions.q: Which of these balls is the lightest?
questions.f: A table-tennis ball weighs less than 3 grams — lighter than two paper clips!

questions.q: Which major tennis tournament is played on a clay court?
questions.f: Clay courts slow the ball down and make it bounce high, so rallies last much longer!

questions.q: Which of these races is the shortest?
questions.f: The 100-metre sprint is over in about ten seconds — a blink compared to a marathon!

questions.q: Which of these sports is NOT played with a racquet?
questions.f: Cricket uses a flat wooden bat, while the others all swing stringed racquets!

questions.q: Which board game starts with the most pieces on the board?
questions.f: Chess begins with 32 pieces — sixteen dark and sixteen light — filling four rows!

questions.q: At the Olympics, which medal is given for third place?
questions.f: Bronze is a mix of copper and tin, one of the first metals people ever made!

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a Winter Olympic sport?
questions.f: Field hockey is a Summer Olympic sport, played on grass or turf, not on ice!

questions.q: Which of these team sports has the fewest players on the field at once?
questions.f: Basketball fields five per side, while soccer, cricket and hockey each play eleven!

questions.q: In athletics, which event involves throwing a heavy metal ball as far as you can?
questions.f: The shot is a metal ball that can weigh over 7 kilograms — heavier than a bowling ball!

questions.q: Which is the correct order of tennis points starting from zero?
questions.f: Win four points in this order and, unless it's deuce, you take the game!

questions.q: Which is the most powerful piece in a game of chess?
questions.f: The queen can glide any number of squares in a straight line or diagonally!

questions.q: Which of these sports is NOT played over a net?
questions.f: Boxers face each other inside a roped ring, with no net anywhere in sight!

questions.q: Which of these games comes from India?
questions.f: In gilli-danda, players use a long stick to flick and whack a small pointed piece of wood!

questions.q: Which Olympic event combines exactly five different sports?
questions.f: Pentathletes fence, swim, ride a horse, shoot and run — all in a single day!

questions.q: Which chess piece may only move diagonally?
questions.f: Each side has two bishops — one stays on light squares and one on dark squares forever!

questions.q: In which sport do players pot coloured balls into pockets with a cue?
questions.f: A snooker table has six pockets, and players use a long stick called a cue!

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a real chess piece?
questions.f: The pieces are king, queen, rook, bishop, knight and pawn — no dragons allowed!

questions.q: A decathlon is made up of ten track-and-field events.
questions.f: They include running, jumping and throwing events all rolled into one huge contest!

questions.q: In golf, the player with the highest score wins.
questions.f: Golf is the opposite of most games — the lowest number of shots wins!

questions.q: The Paralympic Games are held for athletes with disabilities.
questions.f: The Paralympics take place right after the Olympics in the very same host city!

questions.q: Snakes and Ladders was first invented in India.
questions.f: Ladders lifted you up for good deeds and snakes slid you down for bad ones!

questions.q: Why do golf balls have hundreds of little dimples?
c: They help the ball fly farther
They help it float on water
questions.f: The dimples smooth the airflow around the ball, so it can fly nearly twice as far!

questions.q: The Olympic motto 'Citius, Altius, Fortius' means what in English?
questions.f: In 2021 the word 'Together' was added, making it 'Faster, Higher, Stronger — Together'!

questions.q: What do the five interlocking Olympic rings stand for?
questions.f: They picture the world's continents linked together in friendship through sport!

questions.q: In curling, why do sweepers brush the ice in front of the sliding stone?
c: It melts a thin film so the stone slides farther
It cleans the ice for the crowd
questions.f: The brushing warms the ice just enough to cut friction and steer the stone!

questions.q: In cricket, what is it called when a bowler takes three wickets in three balls?
questions.f: A hat-trick is so rare that fans remember it for years afterwards!

questions.q: In chess, 'checkmate' comes from a Persian phrase describing what?
questions.f: It comes from 'shah mat', where 'shah' means king — the same root as the word 'check'!

questions.q: Why do sprinters push off from starting blocks at the start of a race?
c: To launch forward for a faster start
questions.f: Blocks let runners drive their legs against a solid surface instead of slipping backward!

questions.q: Why does a spinning ball curve through the air, like a swerving free kick?
c: The spin makes air push it to one side
The ball is not perfectly round
questions.f: Spin makes air rush faster over one side, and the ball bends toward the slower side!

questions.q: What prize did winners of the ancient Olympic Games receive?
questions.f: There were no medals back then — just a leafy olive crown and lifelong fame!

questions.q: Which martial art's name means 'empty hand' in Japanese?
questions.f: 'Empty hand' means karate is fought with the body alone, using no weapons!

questions.q: In long-distance running, what does 'hitting the wall' mean?
c: The body runs low on stored energy
questions.f: Muscles store sugar for fuel, and when it runs out, runners suddenly feel exhausted!

questions.q: How fast can a powerful badminton smash travel?
questions.f: The record smash was clocked at 565 km/h, making badminton the fastest racquet sport!

questions.q: Why do competitive swimmers wear tight caps and smooth suits?
c: To reduce drag and swim faster
questions.f: Smoother swimmers slip through the water with less drag slowing them down!

questions.q: How is the Olympic flame traditionally lit before the Games?
c: By focusing the sun's rays with a mirror
questions.f: A curved mirror gathers sunlight to a hot point at ancient Olympia, sparking the flame!

questions.q: In chess, what is the special move where the king and rook move together called?
questions.f: Castling is the only move that lets you shift two of your own pieces at once!

questions.q: Which is the world's largest multi-sport event, held every four years?
questions.f: Thousands of athletes from more than 200 nations gather for the Olympic Games!

questions.q: The colours of the Olympic rings were chosen so at least one appears on every nation's flag.
questions.f: Blue, yellow, black, green, red and the white background cover the flags of the world!

questions.q: In chess, a pawn that reaches the far side can be turned into a queen.
questions.f: This is called promotion, and it means a single pawn can end up your strongest piece!

questions.q: A Test cricket match can last as long as five days.
questions.f: Even after five whole days of play, a Test match can still end in a draw!

questions.q: Skateboarding is now an Olympic sport.
questions.f: Skateboarding joined the Summer Olympics for the first time at the Tokyo Games!

questions.q: What is Cinderella's famous slipper made of?
questions.f: Charles Perrault's 1697 story gave Cinderella a glass slipper and a pumpkin coach!

questions.q: What grows longer every time Pinocchio tells a lie?
questions.f: In the original book, woodpeckers have to peck his giant nose back down to size!

questions.q: What does Jack trade his cow for in Jack and the Beanstalk?
questions.f: Overnight the beans grew a beanstalk that stretched up through the clouds!

questions.q: What colour is Little Red Riding Hood's cloak?
questions.f: Her red hooded cloak is so famous that it became her whole name!

questions.q: In Snow White, the queen gives her a poisoned what?
