questions.f: One bite of the poisoned apple sent Snow White into a deep, deep sleep.

questions.q: Goldilocks tastes the three bears' breakfast. What is it?
questions.f: Baby Bear's bowl was 'just right' - not too hot and not too cold!

questions.q: In The Three Little Pigs, what does the wolf do to the straw house?
questions.f: Only the brick house stood strong against the wolf's mightiest huff and puff!

questions.q: What is Humpty Dumpty sitting on before his great fall?
questions.f: All the king's horses and all the king's men couldn't put Humpty together again!

questions.q: What food does Winnie the Pooh love most?
questions.f: Pooh spells it 'hunny' on his jars - he never gets it right!

questions.q: In Hey Diddle Diddle, the cow jumps over the what?
questions.f: The dish ran away with the spoon - it is a very silly rhyme indeed!

questions.q: What does the Itsy Bitsy Spider climb up?
questions.f: Down came the rain and washed the spider out - but it always climbs back up!

questions.q: Twinkle Twinkle Little Star compares the star to a what?
questions.f: The tune is the same as the ABC song - try singing them together!

questions.q: Which little animal follows Mary to school one day?
questions.f: The rhyme may be based on a real girl whose pet lamb followed her to school!

questions.q: Who is Little Red Riding Hood bringing goodies to?
questions.f: The wolf sneaks ahead and dresses up in Grandma's clothes!

questions.q: Jack and Jill go up the hill to fetch a pail of what?
questions.f: Jack fell down and broke his crown - 'crown' is an old word for the top of the head!

questions.q: Which fairy-tale girl is famous for her very long hair?
questions.f: In the Grimms' tale, a prince climbs up Rapunzel's braid to reach her tower window!

questions.q: In the song, Old MacDonald had a what?
questions.f: E-I-E-I-O! On his farm he had a cow, a duck, a pig and many more.

questions.q: Whose garden does Peter Rabbit sneak into for vegetables?
questions.f: Beatrix Potter first wrote Peter Rabbit in a letter to cheer up a sick little boy!

questions.q: In The Frog Prince, what does the frog turn into?
questions.f: In the Grimms' original there is no kiss - the frog changes when the princess throws it!

questions.q: The three bears are Papa Bear, Mama Bear, and who?
questions.f: Baby Bear's tiny chair got broken when Goldilocks sat in it!

questions.q: Row, row, row your boat gently down the what?
questions.f: 'Merrily, merrily, merrily, merrily, life is but a dream' - a favourite round to sing!

questions.q: In the rhyme, what frightens Little Miss Muffet away?
questions.f: Miss Muffet was eating curds and whey - a lumpy, old-fashioned cheese snack!

questions.q: In Baa Baa Black Sheep, the sheep has three bags full of what?
questions.f: One bag for the master, one for the dame, and one for the little boy down the lane!

questions.q: The Gingerbread Man runs away so nobody can do what to him?
questions.f: 'Run, run, as fast as you can! You can't catch me!' shouts the speedy cookie.

questions.q: In Old Mother Hubbard, what does she look for to give her dog?
questions.f: But when she got to the cupboard it was bare, so the poor dog had none!

questions.q: The Ugly Duckling grows up to be a beautiful swan.
questions.f: Hans Christian Andersen hinted the story was about his own lonely childhood!

questions.q: In Hey Diddle Diddle, the little dog laughs to see such fun.
questions.f: And the dish ran away with the spoon - nobody knows what the rhyme really means!

questions.q: Cinderella must leave the ball before the clock strikes midnight.
questions.f: She ran so fast on the last stroke of twelve that she left a slipper behind!

questions.q: In The Three Little Pigs, the houses are blown down by a bear.
questions.f: It is the Big Bad Wolf who huffs and puffs and blows the houses down!

questions.q: Goldilocks visits a house that belongs to three bears.
questions.f: She tries their porridge, their chairs and their beds while they are out for a walk!

questions.q: Sleeping Beauty pricks her finger on what?
questions.f: One tiny prick sent her - and the whole castle - to sleep for a hundred years!

questions.q: What do Hansel and Gretel find deep in the forest?
questions.f: It had gingerbread walls and sugar windows - but it was a trap the clever kids escaped!

questions.q: Who wrote The Ugly Duckling and The Little Mermaid?
questions.f: Andersen wrote more than 150 fairy tales, including Thumbelina and The Snow Queen!

questions.q: In Aesop's most famous race, who beats the speedy hare?
questions.f: The hare was so sure he'd win that he stopped for a nap and snoozed past the finish!

questions.q: Little Bo Peep has lost her what?
questions.f: Leave them alone and they'll come home, wagging their tails behind them!

questions.q: In The Wizard of Oz, what is the famous road made of?
questions.f: Dorothy follows the yellow brick road all the way to the Emerald City!

questions.q: In Charles Perrault's tale, what clever animal wears boots?
questions.f: Puss in Boots tricks a king and makes his poor master rich!

questions.q: Rumpelstiltskin helps the miller's daughter spin straw into what?
questions.f: The only way to beat him was to guess his very strange name!

questions.q: Who wrote Charlie and the Chocolate Factory?
questions.f: Roald Dahl also wrote Matilda, The BFG and James and the Giant Peach!

questions.q: In The Jungle Book, what kind of animal is Baloo?
questions.f: Rudyard Kipling's hero Mowgli is raised by a family of wolves in the Indian jungle!

questions.q: A poem with three lines of 5, 7, then 5 syllables is called a what?
questions.f: Haiku began in Japan and often capture one tiny moment in nature.

questions.q: The lesson at the end of an Aesop fable is called the what?
questions.f: Morals like 'look before you leap' are still said every single day!

questions.q: In The Fox and the Grapes, what does the fox call the grapes?
questions.f: 'Sour grapes' now means pretending you never wanted something you couldn't get!

questions.q: In Snow White, the evil queen asks her magic what who is fairest?
questions.f: 'Mirror, mirror, on the wall, who is the fairest of them all?'

questions.q: The Panchatantra collection of animal tales comes from which country?
questions.f: These tales are about 2,000 years old and were told to teach young princes to be wise!

questions.q: In Peter Pan, what kind of creature is Tinker Bell?
questions.f: On stage, Tinker Bell is often just a darting spot of light and a jingling bell!

questions.q: In The Emperor's New Clothes, what is the emperor really wearing?
questions.f: Tricky weavers said the cloth was invisible to fools, so nobody dared admit they saw none!

questions.q: Which German brothers collected Cinderella, Rapunzel and Snow White?
questions.f: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm gathered old tales told around German firesides.

questions.q: In The Ant and the Grasshopper, who stores up food for winter?
questions.f: The busy ant worked all summer while the grasshopper just sang and played!

questions.q: Which animal does Alice follow down the hole in Wonderland?
questions.f: The rabbit checks a pocket watch and cries, 'Oh dear! I shall be too late!'

questions.q: Thumbelina is a tiny girl no bigger than a what?
questions.f: She was born inside a flower and slept in a walnut-shell cradle!

questions.q: Old King Cole is a merry old soul who calls for his what?
questions.f: He called for his pipe, his bowl, and his fiddlers three!

questions.q: In Peter Pan, who is the pirate villain with a hook for a hand?
questions.f: Hook is afraid of a crocodile that once swallowed a loudly ticking clock!

questions.q: In The Frog Prince, the princess drops her golden ball into a what?
questions.f: The friendly frog fetches it back, but only if she keeps her promise!

questions.q: Roald Dahl's gentle giant hero is known by which initials?
questions.f: BFG stands for Big Friendly Giant, who blows happy dreams into children's rooms!

questions.q: In Little Red Riding Hood, who dresses up as Grandma?
questions.f: 'Oh, Grandma, what big teeth you have!' says Little Red before she spots the trick.

questions.q: Aesop told his fables long ago in ancient Greece.
questions.f: Nobody is quite sure Aesop was one real person, but hundreds of fables carry his name!

questions.q: A fable is a short story that usually teaches a lesson.
questions.f: Fables often star talking animals who show us how to behave - or how not to!

questions.q: Hansel and Gretel was written by Roald Dahl.
questions.f: It was collected by the Brothers Grimm in Germany, long before Dahl was born!

questions.q: In The Tortoise and the Hare, the hare wins the race easily.
questions.f: The hare stops for a nap, and the slow, steady tortoise plods past to win!

questions.q: How many dwarfs live in the cottage Snow White finds?
questions.f: The Brothers Grimm collected Snow White from German storytellers over 200 years ago.

questions.q: In Aesop's fable, how does the tiny mouse rescue the mighty lion?
questions.f: The moral: even the smallest friend can be a mighty helper!

questions.q: How many lines does a haiku poem have?
questions.f: A haiku packs a whole scene into just three short lines - often about nature.

questions.q: In The Crow and the Pitcher, how does the thirsty crow reach the water?
questions.f: Scientists tested this - real birds really do drop stones to raise the water!

questions.q: In Charlotte's Web, Charlotte the spider spins words to save which pig?
questions.f: Author E. B. White watched a real spider in his barn before writing the story.

questions.q: Who wrote The Jungle Book, set in the Indian jungle?
questions.f: Kipling grew up in Mumbai and filled his stories with Indian animals and forests!

questions.q: In The Emperor's New Clothes, who finally says the emperor is wearing nothing?
questions.f: Only a small child was honest enough to shout out the plain truth!

questions.q: In the Panchatantra's Monkey and the Crocodile, where does the monkey live?
questions.f: The clever monkey escapes by claiming he left his heart back in his tree!

questions.q: In Aesop's The North Wind and the Sun, who gets the traveller's coat off?
questions.f: The gentle warmth beat the blustery wind - kindness can win where force cannot!

questions.q: Which country was fairy-tale author Hans Christian Andersen from?
questions.f: His birthday, April 2, is celebrated worldwide as International Children's Book Day!

questions.q: In The Little Mermaid, what does the mermaid most want to become?
questions.f: Andersen's original ending is far sadder than the cheerful cartoon versions!

questions.q: In the fable, why does the hare lose the race to the tortoise?
questions.f: So sure of winning, the hare snoozed while the tortoise plodded past the finish!

questions.q: Who lives under the bridge in Three Billy Goats Gruff?
questions.f: 'Trip, trap, trip, trap!' go the goats' hooves as they cross over the hungry troll!

questions.q: Roald Dahl wrote about a clever girl with secret powers named what?
questions.f: Matilda loves books so much she reads her way through the whole library!

questions.q: At the top of Jack's beanstalk lives a what?
questions.f: 'Fee-fi-fo-fum!' booms the giant, who owns a hen that lays golden eggs!

questions.q: A sly fox finally gobbles up which runaway treat?
questions.f: The fox tricked the cookie into riding on its nose across a river!

questions.q: How many lines does a limerick have?
questions.f: Limericks are short, funny poems made famous by Edward Lear's Book of Nonsense.

questions.q: In Rumpelstiltskin, the queen must guess the little man's what?
questions.f: She overhears him singing 'Rumpelstiltskin is my name!' by his fire.

questions.q: The character who works against the hero in a story is called the what?
questions.f: A villain gives the hero a problem to solve - and makes the story exciting!

questions.q: Who carves Pinocchio out of a piece of wood?
questions.f: The kind woodcarver Geppetto wishes his puppet could become a real boy!

questions.q: Cinderella's fairy godmother turns a pumpkin into a what?
questions.f: At midnight - poof! - the coach turned right back into a pumpkin again.

questions.q: In the fable, the greedy dog drops his bone snapping at his what?
questions.f: He wanted the 'other' dog's bone too, and lost his own in the water!

questions.q: In Beauty and the Beast, Beauty's father angers the Beast by picking a what?
questions.f: One single rose from the Beast's garden set the whole tale in motion!

questions.q: In the tale of Aladdin, rubbing the magic lamp calls out a what?
questions.f: Aladdin's story comes from the ancient collection One Thousand and One Nights.

questions.q: Roald Dahl wrote James and the Giant Peach.
questions.f: James sails across the ocean inside a giant peach with a crew of huge friendly bugs!

questions.q: A haiku poem must rhyme at the end of every line.
questions.f: Haiku almost never rhyme - what matters is the 5-7-5 count of syllables!

questions.q: The Brothers Grimm came from Germany.
questions.f: They collected over 200 folk tales that people had told aloud for centuries.

questions.q: In Jack and the Beanstalk, Jack climbs down the beanstalk to reach the giant.
questions.f: He climbs UP the giant beanstalk into a castle above the clouds!

questions.q: Which of these fairy tales was NOT written by Hans Christian Andersen?
questions.f: Snow White was collected by the Brothers Grimm in Germany, not by Andersen in Denmark.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of Aesop's fables?
questions.f: The Ugly Duckling is by Hans Christian Andersen, written long after Aesop's time!

questions.q: What do Hansel and Gretel drop FIRST to mark their trail home?
questions.f: The shiny pebbles worked, but the breadcrumbs they tried next were eaten by birds!

questions.q: In The Wizard of Oz, which of Dorothy's friends wishes for a brain?
questions.f: The Tin Woodman wants a heart, and the Cowardly Lion wants courage!

questions.q: Which of these stories comes from India's Panchatantra?
questions.f: In it, the monkey escapes a crocodile by saying he left his heart in a tree!

questions.q: Which of these books did Roald Dahl write?
questions.f: In it, a clever fox outwits three mean farmers to feed all the underground animals!

questions.q: Which famous fable warns you not to tell lies?
questions.f: When a real wolf came, no one believed the boy who had fooled them before!

questions.q: Which of these is a nursery rhyme, NOT a fairy tale?
questions.f: Nursery rhymes are short songs or poems, while fairy tales are longer magical stories.

questions.q: Which of these characters is usually the villain of a story?
questions.f: A villain is the 'bad guy' who tries to stop the hero and cause trouble!

questions.q: Who is famous for telling clever fables in ancient Greece?
questions.f: Aesop's fables are over 2,000 years old, yet children still read them today!

questions.q: Which tale was collected by the Brothers Grimm, NOT by Andersen?
questions.f: The Grimms gathered Hansel and Gretel in Germany, while Andersen wrote the other three!

questions.q: In The Ant and the Grasshopper, what does the lazy grasshopper do all summer?
questions.f: When winter came he had nothing, while the hard-working ant had plenty!

questions.q: Which fairy-tale character is the tiniest of these?
questions.f: Thumbelina is no taller than a thumb, while the others are all enormous!

questions.q: Which of these is a type of poem, NOT a story character?
questions.f: A limerick is a short, funny five-line poem with a bouncy rhythm.

questions.q: Who wrote the funny poems in A Book of Nonsense?
questions.f: Edward Lear made the silly five-line limerick famous back in the 1840s!

questions.q: Which fairy tale features a princess and a magic spinning wheel?
questions.f: A prick from the spinning wheel's spindle sends the princess to sleep for 100 years!

questions.q: In Goldilocks, whose porridge, chair and bed are always 'just right'?
questions.f: The biggest were too much and too hard, but Baby Bear's were perfect for Goldilocks!

questions.q: Which of these is NOT part of the Cinderella story?
questions.f: The snowman belongs in a different tale - Cinderella's magic is all slippers and coaches!

questions.q: In a fable, animals often talk and act just like people.
questions.f: Talking foxes, ants and tortoises help the fable teach us a lesson about ourselves!

questions.q: Every single one of Aesop's fables was also written by Roald Dahl.
questions.f: Aesop lived thousands of years before Dahl - they never even shared a language!

questions.q: The 'moral' of a story is the lesson it teaches you.
questions.f: Fairy tales and fables often hide a moral, like 'be kind' or 'work hard'.

questions.q: Cinderella and Sleeping Beauty are both nursery rhymes.
questions.f: They are fairy tales - longer magical stories, not short sing-song rhymes!

questions.q: Basho's most famous haiku describes a frog jumping into a what?
questions.f: Basho's frog haiku has been translated into English more than a hundred different ways!

questions.q: In Carlo Collodi's original book, what giant sea creature swallows Pinocchio?
questions.f: The famous whale came from a later film - Collodi wrote a monstrous Terrible Dogfish!

questions.q: The saying 'don't count your chickens before they hatch' comes from a fable about a what?
questions.f: She daydreamed of riches her milk would buy, tossed her head, and spilled the whole pail!

questions.q: The Panchatantra tales were first written in which ancient language?
questions.f: These animal tales travelled along trade routes and inspired fable books across the world!

questions.q: Who wrote both Alice in Wonderland and the nonsense poem Jabberwocky?
questions.f: Lewis Carroll was a pen name for a real maths teacher named Charles Dodgson!

questions.q: What is the moral of Aesop's The Goose That Laid the Golden Eggs?
questions.f: The farmer wanted all the gold at once, and ended up with no golden eggs at all!

questions.q: The Jataka tales from India tell stories about the earlier lives of whom?
questions.f: In these ancient tales the Buddha often appears as a wise animal teaching a lesson.

questions.q: In the original Wizard of Oz book, what colour are Dorothy's magic shoes?
questions.f: The dazzling ruby slippers were invented for the 1939 film to show off new colour cameras!

questions.q: In the Panchatantra's Blue Jackal, the jackal turns blue by falling into a tub of what?
questions.f: The other animals thought the blue jackal was a magic king - until he howled like a jackal!

questions.q: In a story, the main character or hero is also known by which special name?
questions.f: The protagonist is the person the story follows, whose choices drive the whole tale!

questions.q: In Aesop's The Fox and the Stork, the fable teaches you to treat others how?
c: The way you want to be treated
questions.f: The fox tricked the stork with a flat dish, so the stork served food in a tall, thin jar!

questions.q: The haiku form of poetry comes from which country?
questions.f: Haiku poets try to capture a single, still moment from nature in just seventeen syllables.

questions.q: In The North Wind and the Sun, what wins the contest instead of force?
questions.f: The harder the wind blew, the tighter the man clung to his coat - the sun's warmth won!

questions.q: Roald Dahl wrote about a poor boy who finds a golden ticket in which book?
c: Danny the Champion of the World
questions.f: Five lucky golden tickets win a tour of Willy Wonka's amazing sweet factory!

questions.q: 'Once upon a time' is the traditional way to do what to a fairy tale?
questions.f: Many tales then close with the happy words 'and they all lived happily ever after'!

questions.q: In many stories, the character who fights against the hero is called the what?
questions.f: The antagonist creates the trouble and conflict that the hero has to overcome!

questions.q: What is the moral of Aesop's The Tortoise and the Hare?
c: Slow and steady wins the race
The early bird gets the worm
questions.f: Being careful and never giving up can beat being fast but lazy!

questions.q: Aesop may not have been one single real person at all.
questions.f: Historians aren't sure he truly existed - many fables were simply gathered under his name!

questions.q: A haiku poem is usually longer than an entire novel.
questions.f: A haiku is one of the shortest poems there is - just three tiny lines!

questions.q: In the Jataka tales, the Buddha sometimes appears as an animal.
questions.f: He shows up as a wise monkey, deer or elephant to teach kindness and courage!

questions.q: What falls from clouds as tiny drops of water?
questions.f: A single rain cloud can hold millions of tons of water floating as tiny droplets.

questions.q: What do we call soft white flakes that fall on cold winter days?
questions.f: Snow is really frozen water — each flake is a tiny crystal of ice.

questions.q: What is the arc of colours in the sky after rain called?
questions.f: A rainbow always has its colours in the same order, with red on the outside.

questions.q: What loud rumbling sound do you hear during a storm?
questions.f: Thunder is the sound made when lightning suddenly heats the air around it.

questions.q: What gives Earth its light and warmth during the day?
questions.f: The Sun's heat is the engine that powers all of Earth's weather.

questions.q: What colour is a clear daytime sky?
questions.f: On Mars the daytime sky looks pinkish-brown instead of blue!

questions.q: Which season is usually the hottest of the year?
questions.f: Summer happens when your half of Earth leans toward the Sun.

questions.q: What are the spikes of ice that hang from cold roofs called?
questions.f: Icicles grow drip by drip — each drop freezes a new layer onto the tip.

questions.q: What is the bright flash of light that zigzags from storm clouds?
questions.f: About 100 lightning bolts strike the Earth every single second!

questions.q: What do we call a cloud that rests right on the ground?
questions.f: Fog is just a cloud that has formed at ground level instead of high in the sky.

questions.q: What are the bouncing balls of ice that fall in some thunderstorms?
questions.f: Hail only forms in thunderstorms, tumbling up and down inside the cloud as it grows.

questions.q: What are the sparkly white ice crystals on grass on cold mornings?
questions.f: Frost forms when water vapour in the air freezes right onto cold surfaces.

questions.q: What can you feel on your face and hear whooshing through trees?
questions.f: Wind is simply air moving from one place to another.

questions.q: Which tool tells you how hot or cold it is?
questions.f: A thermometer has liquid inside that rises when it gets warmer.

questions.q: Which spinning arrow on a roof shows which way the wind blows?
questions.f: A weather vane always points into the wind, toward where the wind is coming from.

questions.q: What do you open to keep dry when it rains?
questions.f: Umbrellas have been used to keep off rain and sun for over a thousand years.

questions.q: Clouds in the sky are made of billions of tiny what?
questions.f: Each droplet is so tiny that gently rising air keeps it floating.

questions.q: In which season do leaves turn colour and fall from many trees?
questions.f: Autumn is also called 'fall' because that is when the leaves come tumbling down.

questions.q: In which season do many flowers bloom and baby animals are born?
questions.f: In spring the days grow longer and warmer, waking up plants and animals.

questions.q: What melts snow and ice away?
questions.f: When ice warms up enough, it melts back into liquid water.

questions.q: What are the white fluffy things floating high in the sky?
questions.f: Clouds come in many shapes because winds high up push and stretch them.

questions.q: What are the little water drops found on grass early in the morning?
questions.f: Dew forms overnight when cool air turns its water vapour back into tiny drops.

questions.q: What do we call very light, gentle rain?
questions.f: Drizzle drops are smaller than a grain of sand.

questions.q: When a puddle dries up in the Sun, the water turns into invisible what?
questions.f: The water doesn't vanish — it floats up into the air as a gas you can't see.

questions.q: Snow is frozen water.
questions.f: Snowflakes form when water vapour high in a cloud freezes into ice crystals.

questions.q: Clouds are made of tiny drops of water.
questions.f: Each drop is smaller than a speck of dust, and there are billions in one cloud.

questions.q: You can see the wind with your eyes.
questions.f: You can't see wind itself, only what it moves — leaves, flags and waves.

questions.q: A rainbow can appear when sunshine hits falling rain.
questions.f: Sunlight passing through raindrops splits into a rainbow of colours.

questions.q: Summer is usually colder than winter.
questions.f: Summer is the warm season and winter is the cold one.

questions.q: What are the puffy, cotton-like clouds that look like cauliflowers?
questions.f: Cumulus clouds usually mean fair weather, but big ones can grow into storms.

questions.q: What are the thin, wispy clouds high in the sky made of ice crystals?
questions.f: Cirrus clouds float so high that they are made of ice, not water drops.

questions.q: What are the flat, grey clouds that spread like a blanket over the sky?
questions.f: Low, grey stratus clouds often bring drizzle or a dull, cloudy day.

questions.q: What is it called when water turns into vapour and rises into the air?
questions.f: The Sun's heat evaporates water from oceans, lakes and even puddles.

questions.q: What is it called when water vapour cools and turns back into droplets?
questions.f: Condensation is how clouds are born, and how dew forms on cold grass.

questions.q: What is the science word for rain, snow, sleet and hail falling from clouds?
questions.f: Precipitation is any water that falls from clouds, frozen or liquid.

questions.q: What is a spinning column of air that reaches down to touch the ground?
questions.f: Tornadoes can spin so fast they lift cars and rip roofs off houses.

questions.q: What do we call a giant spinning storm that forms over warm oceans?
questions.f: A hurricane can be hundreds of kilometres wide — bigger than some countries.

questions.q: What is the rainy season of heavy downpours called in India?
questions.f: India's monsoon brings most of the country's rain between June and September.

questions.q: Which instrument measures how much rain has fallen?
questions.f: A rain gauge is just a tube that collects rain so you can measure its depth.

questions.q: Which instrument measures the pressure of the air?
questions.f: When a barometer's reading drops quickly, stormy weather is often on the way.

questions.q: Which spinning instrument measures how fast the wind is blowing?
questions.f: An anemometer's little cups spin faster when the wind blows harder.

questions.q: How many main colours does a rainbow have?
questions.f: The seven colours are red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.

questions.q: Which colour is always on the outer, top edge of a rainbow?
questions.f: Red is on the outside and violet is on the inside of every rainbow.

questions.q: What do we call the individual frozen crystals that make up snow?
questions.f: Most snowflakes have six sides because of the way water freezes.

questions.q: What is a scientist who studies and forecasts the weather called?
questions.f: Meteorologists use satellites, radar and balloons to predict the weather.

questions.q: After rain flows down rivers, where does most of the water end up?
questions.f: Water travels from oceans to sky to land and back to the ocean — the water cycle.

questions.q: What do we call a strong wind that blows clouds of sand in a desert?
questions.f: A big sandstorm can turn the daytime sky orange and block out the Sun.

questions.q: How many sides does a typical snowflake have?
questions.f: Water molecules always line up in a six-sided pattern when they freeze.

questions.q: What do we call a long time with almost no rain at all?
questions.f: A long drought can dry up rivers and make it hard for crops to grow.

questions.q: What do we call it when lots of water covers land that is usually dry?
questions.f: Heavy rain or overflowing rivers can cause floods that spread far and wide.

questions.q: What do we call rain that freezes into tiny ice pellets as it falls?
questions.f: Sleet forms when raindrops fall through a layer of freezing-cold air.

questions.q: Which tall, towering clouds bring thunder, lightning and heavy rain?
questions.f: Cumulonimbus clouds can grow taller than Mount Everest.

questions.q: In which unit is temperature often measured in most of the world?
questions.f: Water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius and boils at 100 degrees Celsius.

questions.q: What do we call a gentle, pleasant, light wind?
questions.f: A sea breeze blows in from the ocean as the land warms up during the day.

questions.q: A bolt of lightning is hotter than the surface of the Sun.
questions.f: Lightning can reach about 30,000°C — around five times hotter than the Sun's surface.

questions.q: No two snowflakes are exactly alike.
questions.f: Each flake takes its own path through the cloud, so it freezes into a unique shape.

questions.q: A hurricane has a calm centre called the eye.
questions.f: Inside the eye the winds are quiet and the sky can even be clear and sunny.

questions.q: Warm air rises and cool air sinks.
questions.f: This rising and sinking of air is what stirs up wind and weather.

questions.q: Rainbows can only form at night.
questions.f: Rainbows need sunlight, so they usually appear in the daytime after rain.

questions.q: About how hot can a bolt of lightning get?
questions.f: That is hotter than the surface of the Sun, which is around 5,500°C.

questions.q: In a rainbow, which colour comes right after yellow?
questions.f: The order never changes: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet.

questions.q: Counting seconds between lightning and thunder tells you the storm's what?
questions.f: Sound travels about 1 kilometre every 3 seconds, so counting shows how far the storm is.

questions.q: The very largest hailstones can grow as big as what?
questions.f: Giant hailstones tumble up and down in a storm cloud, adding icy layers each time.

questions.q: In which ocean are hurricanes usually called typhoons?
questions.f: The same kind of storm has different names in different parts of the world.

questions.q: What powers the whole water cycle on Earth?
questions.f: The Sun's heat evaporates water, lifting it into the sky to form clouds.

questions.q: About how much of Earth's surface is covered by water?
questions.f: Because so much of Earth is ocean, our planet looks blue from space.

questions.q: Who first gave clouds their Latin names like cumulus and cirrus?
questions.f: Luke Howard was a British weather-watcher who named the clouds back in 1802.

questions.q: How do raindrops turn sunlight into a rainbow?
questions.f: Each raindrop acts like a tiny prism, bending light and splitting it into colours.

questions.q: What is the weather like inside the eye of a hurricane?
questions.f: The eye is a quiet, clear hole in the middle, ringed by the storm's fiercest winds.

questions.q: The wettest inhabited place on Earth, Mawsynram, is in which country?
questions.f: Mawsynram gets over 11 metres of rain a year — enough to bury a two-storey house.

questions.q: Why does snow look white even though it is made of clear ice?
c: It reflects all colours of light
questions.f: Snow's many tiny surfaces bounce back all colours of light, which we see as white.

questions.q: Which scale is used to rate how strong a tornado is?
questions.f: The strongest tornadoes are rated EF5, with winds over 320 km/h.

questions.q: Why does the daytime sky look blue?
questions.f: Tiny air molecules scatter blue light in every direction, filling the sky with blue.

questions.q: What do we call it when rain falls while the Sun is shining?
questions.f: Sunshowers are the perfect recipe for spotting a bright rainbow.

questions.q: What is roughly the coldest temperature ever recorded on Earth?
questions.f: That record was measured at Vostok Station in Antarctica in 1983.

questions.q: What do we call the boundary where warm air and cold air meet?
questions.f: Storms and rain often form right along a weather front.

questions.q: If a barometer's reading falls quickly, what is often coming?
questions.f: Falling air pressure usually means clouds, wind and rain are on the way.

questions.q: What is the main reason Earth has different seasons?
questions.f: Earth is tilted, so each half leans toward the Sun for part of the year.

questions.q: Which is the driest desert on Earth, where some spots get almost no rain?
questions.f: Parts of Chile's Atacama Desert have gone years without a single drop of rain.

questions.q: What is the fast, high river of air that planes ride to save fuel called?
questions.f: Jet streams high in the sky can blow at over 300 km/h.

questions.q: What do we call a small spinning whirlwind of dust on a sunny day?
questions.f: Dust devils form on hot, calm days when the ground heats the air just above it.

questions.q: What is roughly the hottest air temperature ever recorded on Earth?
questions.f: That scorching record was set in Death Valley, California, in 1913.

questions.q: What is 'virga', a curtain of rain seen hanging under some clouds?
c: Rain that dries up before landing
questions.f: Virga is rain that evaporates in dry air before it ever reaches the ground.

questions.q: Thunder is the sound of air heated so fast by lightning that it explodes.
questions.f: Lightning heats the air so quickly it expands with a bang we hear as thunder.

questions.q: Raindrops are shaped like round blobs, not pointy teardrops.
questions.f: Small raindrops are nearly round; only in cartoons are they tear-shaped.

questions.q: A hot-air balloon rises because hot air is lighter than cool air.
questions.f: Heating the air inside makes it less dense, so the balloon floats upward.

questions.q: Antarctica gets heavy rain almost every single day.
questions.f: Antarctica is actually a frozen desert — it gets very little precipitation.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a real type of cloud?
questions.f: Cumulus, cirrus and stratus are the three main cloud families scientists use.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a weather instrument?
questions.f: A telescope is for stargazing; the others all measure the weather.

questions.q: Which of these does NOT fall from the sky as precipitation?
questions.f: Snow, hail and sleet are all frozen precipitation; sunshine is just light and heat.

questions.q: In a rainbow, which colour comes right after blue?
questions.f: The order is blue, then indigo, then violet on the inner edge.

questions.q: Which is generally warmer all year round?
questions.f: The Equator gets the most direct sunlight, so it stays warm all year.

questions.q: Which of these does a rain gauge measure, using millimetres?
questions.f: Scientists report rainfall in millimetres of depth collected in the gauge.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a piece of frozen precipitation?
questions.f: A raindrop is liquid water; the other three are all made of ice.

questions.q: After water evaporates and rises, what happens next in the water cycle?
questions.f: High up, the vapour cools and condenses into the droplets that build clouds.

questions.q: When it is summer in India, what season is it in Australia?
questions.f: The two halves of Earth tilt opposite ways, so their seasons are swapped.

questions.q: Which is the stronger wind?
questions.f: On the Beaufort scale, a gale is strong enough to snap small branches off trees.

questions.q: What most often causes a flood?
questions.f: When rain falls faster than the ground can soak it up, rivers overflow and flood.

questions.q: Which of these temperatures is the coldest?
questions.f: The lower the number, the colder it is — and below zero, water freezes solid.

questions.q: Which kind of climate has the least rainfall?
questions.f: A desert is defined by how little rain it gets, not by how hot it is.

questions.q: In which layer of the air does nearly all of our weather happen?
questions.f: The troposphere is the lowest layer of air, where clouds and storms form.

questions.q: India's monsoon winds change direction with what?
questions.f: Summer winds blow in wet air from the sea; winter winds blow dry air back out.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a stage of the water cycle?
questions.f: The water cycle goes round and round through evaporation, condensation and precipitation.

questions.q: Which colour sits on the inner edge of a rainbow, nearest the ground?
questions.f: Red is on the outside and violet curves along the inside.

questions.q: Comparing the two storms, which is much larger?
questions.f: A hurricane can span hundreds of kilometres, while a tornado is usually under a kilometre wide.

questions.q: A tornado spins, but a hurricane stays perfectly still.
questions.f: Both storms are giant spinning columns of wind — hurricanes just spin more slowly and widely.

questions.q: The higher you climb up a mountain, the colder the air usually gets.
questions.f: Air cools by about 6°C for every kilometre you go up, so peaks can be snowy in summer.

questions.q: Some places near the Equator have no winter or summer, only wet and dry seasons.
questions.f: Tropical regions stay warm all year, so they swap seasons for a rainy time and a dry time.

questions.q: Hail can fall even during warm summer weather.
questions.f: Hail forms high inside cold storm clouds, so it can pelt down on a hot summer day.

questions.q: Why do thunderstorms often build up on hot summer afternoons?
c: Warm air rises fast carrying moisture up
questions.f: Hot, moist air shoots upward, cools, and piles into towering thunderclouds.

questions.q: What is the 'greenhouse effect' that keeps Earth warm?
questions.f: Gases like carbon dioxide act like a blanket, holding in some of the Sun's warmth.

questions.q: What does 'humidity' measure?
questions.f: On humid days the air is packed with water vapour, making it feel sticky and warm.

questions.q: The fastest wind gust ever measured was during what kind of storm?
questions.f: A gust of 408 km/h was recorded during a tropical cyclone near Australia in 1996.

questions.q: Why does the air feel colder when the wind blows on you?
c: Wind carries heat away from your skin
questions.f: This cooling effect is called wind chill — moving air whisks your body heat away.

questions.q: What is the strongest category of hurricane on the main hurricane scale?
questions.f: A Category 5 hurricane has winds over 250 km/h and can flatten buildings.

questions.q: Which place, Lake Maracaibo in Venezuela, is famous for having the most of what?
questions.f: Lake Maracaibo has lightning almost 300 nights a year — the lightning capital of the world.

questions.q: Why can thunder rumble on and on instead of a single sharp crack?
c: Sound comes from different parts of the bolt
questions.f: A lightning bolt is long, so sound from its far and near parts reaches you at different moments.

questions.q: A rainbow is really a full circle. Why do we usually see only half?
c: The ground hides the lower half
questions.f: From a high-flying plane you can sometimes spot the whole rainbow ring.

questions.q: What is a rare, pale rainbow made by moonlight at night called?
questions.f: Moonbows are so faint that they often look ghostly white to our eyes.

questions.q: Why are the seasons in the northern and southern halves of Earth opposite?
c: Each half tilts toward the Sun at different times
They are different distances from the Moon
questions.f: As Earth orbits, first one hemisphere leans sunward, then the other, flipping the seasons.

questions.q: Where in a hurricane are the strongest winds and heaviest rain found?
c: The eye wall around the centre
questions.f: The eye wall is the ring of towering thunderclouds hugging the calm eye.

questions.q: El Niño, which changes weather worldwide, is a warming of which ocean?
questions.f: When the Pacific warms during El Niño, it can shift rain and drought across the planet.

questions.q: Why do you always see lightning before you hear the thunder?
c: Light travels much faster than sound
questions.f: Light reaches you almost instantly, but sound takes about 3 seconds per kilometre.

questions.q: What mainly causes a monsoon's wind to reverse direction each year?
c: Land heating faster than the sea
questions.f: Land warms and cools faster than the ocean, and this difference flips the monsoon winds.

questions.q: Snow looks white but a solid block of ice looks clear. Why?
c: Snow has many surfaces that scatter light
Snow has white paint in it
questions.f: Snow is full of tiny crystals and air gaps that bounce light around, so it looks white.

questions.q: Noctilucent clouds are the highest clouds of all. When do they glow?
c: After sunset, high in the sky
questions.f: These clouds form about 80 km up and shine when sunlight lights them long after sunset.

questions.q: Why does warm air near the ground often rise upward?
c: Warm air is lighter than cool air
questions.f: Warmer air spreads out and becomes less dense, so it floats up above cooler air.

questions.q: Antarctica is technically the largest desert on Earth.
questions.f: A desert is any place with very little precipitation, and icy Antarctica gets almost none.

questions.q: Lightning never strikes the same place twice.
questions.f: Lightning can strike the same spot many times — tall towers are hit over and over.

questions.q: How many continents are there on Earth?
questions.f: Asia is the biggest continent, and more than half of all people on Earth live there!

questions.q: What covers most of the Earth's surface?
questions.f: Oceans cover about 71 percent of our planet, so Earth should almost be called Planet Water!

questions.q: Which is the tallest mountain on Earth?
questions.f: Mount Everest is still growing, getting about 4 millimeters taller every single year!

questions.q: Which country is the biggest in the whole world?
questions.f: Russia is so wide it has 11 time zones, so it can be morning on one side and night on the other!

questions.q: Which ocean is the biggest?
questions.f: The Pacific holds more than half of all the ocean water on Earth!

questions.q: Which continent is the coldest?
questions.f: Antarctica once got so cold that thermometers read minus 89 degrees Celsius. Brrr!

questions.q: What do we call land with water all around it?
questions.f: The country of Indonesia is made of more than 17,000 islands!

questions.q: What do we call a long stream of water flowing across the land?
questions.f: The Amazon River pours out so much fresh water that the sea stays less salty for miles!

questions.q: Where does the Sun rise every morning?
questions.f: The Sun only seems to move. Really it is the Earth spinning like a giant top!

questions.q: What do we call a drawing that shows where places are?
questions.f: The oldest known maps were scratched onto clay tablets thousands of years ago!

questions.q: Which place is at the very top of the Earth?
questions.f: In winter at the North Pole, the Sun does not rise for months. It is night all day long!

questions.q: What do we call water with land all around it?
questions.f: The Great Lakes in North America are so big that astronauts can see them from space!

questions.q: The Eiffel Tower is in which country?
questions.f: The Eiffel Tower is made of iron and grows a little taller on hot days when the metal expands!

questions.q: The Taj Mahal is in which country?
questions.f: The Taj Mahal is made of white marble that seems to change color from dawn to dusk!

questions.q: The Great Wall is in which country?
questions.f: All its sections together stretch over 20,000 kilometers, about halfway around the world!

questions.q: What do we call huge areas of land like Asia and Africa?
questions.f: There are seven continents, and they slowly drift a tiny bit every year!

questions.q: What do we call a giant chunk of ice floating in the sea?
questions.f: About 90 percent of an iceberg hides underneath the water where you cannot see it!

questions.q: What do we call a fiery mountain that can erupt?
questions.f: Big volcanoes can blast ash higher into the sky than airplanes fly!

questions.q: What do we call a very hot, dry, sandy place?
questions.f: Some desert sand dunes grow taller than the Eiffel Tower!

questions.q: What are the giant pointy stone buildings in Egypt called?
questions.f: The Great Pyramid was the tallest building on Earth for almost 4,000 years!

questions.q: What do we call a tall pile of sand in a desert?
questions.f: Wind can slowly push whole sand dunes across the desert like they are creeping along!

questions.q: What color is usually used for water on a map?
questions.f: Mapmakers often use green for forests and brown for mountains too!

questions.q: Which one is bigger?
questions.f: The Pacific Ocean alone is bigger than all the land on Earth put together!

questions.q: What do we call a slow-moving river of ice on a mountain?
questions.f: Glaciers store most of the fresh water on our whole planet!

questions.q: Which giant star gives Earth its light and heat?
questions.f: The Sun is so huge that more than a million Earths could fit inside it!

questions.q: The Sahara is the biggest hot desert in the world.
questions.f: The Sahara is almost as big as the entire United States!

questions.q: There are five oceans on Earth.
questions.f: The newest one to get a name is the Southern Ocean, swirling around Antarctica.

questions.q: Deserts are always hot.
questions.f: A desert just needs to be super dry. The biggest desert on Earth is freezing Antarctica!

questions.q: Antarctica is covered in thick ice.
questions.f: The ice in Antarctica is over 4 kilometers deep in some spots!

questions.q: Rivers can flow uphill on their own.
questions.f: Water always flows downhill, which is why rivers race toward the low sea.

questions.q: Which country is shaped like a tall boot?
questions.f: On a map, Italy's boot even looks like it is kicking the island of Sicily like a ball!

questions.q: On which continent would you find the Sahara Desert?
questions.f: Sahara dust blows across the Atlantic Ocean and helps feed the Amazon rainforest!

questions.q: Which country is also a whole continent by itself?
questions.f: Along Australia's coast lies the Great Barrier Reef, the biggest living structure on Earth!

questions.q: What is the imaginary line around Earth's middle called?
questions.f: Standing on the equator, you are spinning with the Earth at over 1,600 kilometers per hour!

questions.q: Which river is often called the longest in the world?
questions.f: The Nile is about 6,650 kilometers long and flows north through the desert!

questions.q: In which country are the Great Pyramids of Giza?
questions.f: Workers moved stone blocks heavier than elephants to build the pyramids by hand!

questions.q: In which city is the Eiffel Tower?
questions.f: Every night the Eiffel Tower sparkles with thousands of twinkling lights!

questions.q: In which country is the Statue of Liberty?
questions.f: The Statue of Liberty was a giant gift to America from the people of France!

questions.q: Which is the smallest country in the whole world?
questions.f: Vatican City is so tiny you could walk all the way around it in about an hour!

questions.q: Which country has the most people living in it?
questions.f: India is home to over 1.4 billion people, the most of any country on Earth!

questions.q: What is the capital city of Japan?
questions.f: Tokyo is one of the biggest cities in the world, with tens of millions of people!

questions.q: What is the capital city of the United Kingdom?
questions.f: London's famous clock tower holds a giant bell nicknamed Big Ben!

questions.q: On which continent is the Amazon rainforest?
questions.f: The Amazon rainforest makes so much oxygen it is nicknamed the lungs of the planet!

questions.q: Which mountain range is home to Mount Everest?
questions.f: The Himalayas have more than 100 peaks taller than 7,000 meters!

questions.q: What is the Great Barrier Reef mostly made of?
questions.f: Coral looks like colorful rock but is actually made by tiny living animals!

questions.q: What is the capital city of the United States?
questions.f: Washington, D.C. is named after the very first American president, George Washington!

questions.q: Which sea is so salty that people float on top of it?
questions.f: The Dead Sea is so salty that almost no fish or plants can live in it!

questions.q: What is the capital city of India?
questions.f: New Delhi is home to India's government and the huge red sandstone Red Fort!

questions.q: Penguins in the wild mostly live near which pole?
questions.f: Emperor penguins huddle together in Antarctica to stay warm in freezing winds!

questions.q: What is the capital city of Egypt?
questions.f: From Cairo you can see the ancient pyramids sitting right at the edge of the city!

questions.q: What is the capital city of China?
questions.f: Beijing is home to the Forbidden City, a palace with almost a thousand buildings!

questions.q: In which city is the famous Leaning Tower?
questions.f: The Leaning Tower of Pisa started tilting while it was being built because the ground was soft!

questions.q: What is Earth's largest tropical rainforest called?
questions.f: The Amazon is home to millions of kinds of insects, plants, and animals!

questions.q: Which ocean lies between America and Europe?
questions.f: Ships and planes cross the wide Atlantic Ocean every single day!

questions.q: Which is the world's largest island?
questions.f: Greenland is mostly covered by a giant sheet of ice, even though its name says green!

questions.q: Australia is both a country and a continent.
questions.f: Australia is the only place on Earth that is both a country and a whole continent!

questions.q: The equator is one of the hottest parts of Earth.
questions.f: Near the equator the Sun shines straight down all year, keeping it warm.

questions.q: The Nile River flows toward the north.
questions.f: Most rivers you know flow south, but the mighty Nile heads north to the sea!

questions.q: Penguins live in the wild at the North Pole.
questions.f: Wild penguins live near the South Pole. Polar bears live up north instead!

questions.q: Mount Everest is part of the Himalaya mountains.
questions.f: Everest sits on the border between Nepal and China, high in the Himalayas.

questions.q: How many stars are on the flag of the United States?
questions.f: Each star stands for one of the 50 states, and the 13 stripes stand for the first colonies!

questions.q: About what fraction of Earth's surface is covered by water?
questions.f: That is why Earth looks like a big blue marble when seen from space!

questions.q: About how tall is Mount Everest?
questions.f: That is so high that climbers must carry bottled air to breathe near the top!

questions.q: How many time zones does Russia stretch across?
questions.f: When people are eating breakfast in western Russia, others are asleep in the far east!

questions.q: Which country has the longest coastline in the world?
questions.f: Canada's coastline is so wiggly it would wrap around the equator several times!

questions.q: About how many countries are there in the world?
questions.f: The newest country, South Sudan, was born in 2011!

questions.q: The Amazon River is famous for carrying the most of what?
questions.f: The Amazon pushes out more water than the next seven biggest rivers combined!

questions.q: Which is the largest hot desert on Earth?
questions.f: The Sahara can reach a scorching 50 degrees Celsius, yet it freezes on some nights!

questions.q: Roughly how long is the Great Wall of China altogether?
questions.f: It was built and rebuilt over hundreds of years by millions of workers!

questions.q: What is the deepest place in all the oceans called?
questions.f: The Mariana Trench is so deep that Mount Everest could sink inside it and vanish!

questions.q: What is the capital city of Australia?
questions.f: Many people guess Sydney, but Canberra was specially built to be the capital!

questions.q: What is the capital city of Brazil?
questions.f: Brasília was built from scratch in the shape of an airplane when seen from above!

questions.q: Which is the world's tallest waterfall?
questions.f: Angel Falls in Venezuela is so tall the water turns to mist before it hits the ground!

questions.q: In which Indian city is the Taj Mahal?
questions.f: It took over 20 years and thousands of workers to build the Taj Mahal in Agra!

questions.q: Which is the highest mountain in Africa?
questions.f: Kilimanjaro is near the hot equator, yet snow sits on its very top!

questions.q: What is the giant canyon carved by a river in the USA called?
questions.f: The river took millions of years to carve the Grand Canyon over a mile deep!

questions.q: What is the world's largest coral reef system called?
questions.f: It is so huge that it can be seen from space, and it is alive!

questions.q: In which country can you often see the dancing Northern Lights?
questions.f: The Northern Lights glow when tiny bits from the Sun crash into Earth's air!

questions.q: Which is the largest lake in the world?
questions.f: The Caspian Sea is called a sea, but it is really the biggest lake on Earth!

questions.q: The Nile River empties into which sea?
questions.f: Where the Nile meets the sea, it spreads into a fan of land called a delta!

questions.q: The ancient stone city of Machu Picchu sits in which country?
questions.f: Machu Picchu was built high in the Andes mountains by the Inca people!

questions.q: What is the capital city of Canada?
questions.f: Many people guess Toronto, but Ottawa is Canada's real capital city!

questions.q: The Amazon rainforest is mostly inside which country?
questions.f: The Amazon is so big it spreads across nine countries, but most of it is in Brazil!

questions.q: Which is the smallest of Earth's five oceans?
questions.f: The Arctic Ocean is often covered by a floating cap of sea ice!

questions.q: The Pacific is the largest ocean on Earth.
questions.f: The Pacific is so wide that all the continents could fit inside it with room to spare!

questions.q: Canberra, not Sydney, is the capital of Australia.
questions.f: Canberra was chosen as a fair middle spot between rivals Sydney and Melbourne!

questions.q: The Amazon River is in Africa.
questions.f: The Amazon flows through South America. Africa's giant river is the Nile!

questions.q: Mount Kilimanjaro is the tallest mountain in the world.
questions.f: Kilimanjaro is Africa's tallest, but Mount Everest is the tallest on the whole planet!

questions.q: Which of these is NOT an ocean?
questions.f: The Sahara is a giant desert, not an ocean, and it is mostly sand and rock!

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a continent?
questions.f: Greenland is the world's largest island, but it belongs to the continent of North America!

questions.q: Which of these landmarks is NOT real?
questions.f: There is no Chocolate Tower, but the other three are all famous real landmarks!

questions.q: Which is the second-largest country in the world by area?
questions.f: Canada is second only to Russia, yet very few people live in its frozen north!

questions.q: Which of these is a river, NOT a mountain range?
questions.f: The Ganges is a great river in India, treated as sacred by millions of people!

questions.q: Which mountain range runs down the western side of South America?
questions.f: The Andes are the longest mountain range on land, stretching about 7,000 kilometers!

questions.q: What is the capital city of Turkey?
questions.f: Many people guess Istanbul, but the capital of Turkey is actually Ankara!

questions.q: Which continent has the most countries?
questions.f: Africa has 54 countries, more than any other continent on Earth!

questions.q: Which of these famous landmarks is in India?
questions.f: The Taj Mahal was built as a beautiful marble tomb for a beloved queen!

questions.q: Which is the largest continent on Earth?
questions.f: Asia is so big that about 60 out of every 100 people on Earth live there!

questions.q: Which South American country is named after the equator that crosses it?
questions.f: Ecuador is the Spanish word for equator, the invisible line around Earth's middle!

questions.q: The Ring of Fire around the Pacific is famous for having many what?
questions.f: Most of Earth's volcanoes and earthquakes happen along the Ring of Fire!

questions.q: Which imaginary line runs from pole to pole through Greenwich, England?
questions.f: The Prime Meridian is where the world sets its main clock time!

questions.q: The ancient rose-colored city of Petra is carved into cliffs in which country?
questions.f: Petra's giant buildings were carved right into pink stone cliffs long ago!

questions.q: Which country's flag shows a red circle for the rising Sun on white?
questions.f: Japan is nicknamed the Land of the Rising Sun, and its flag shows that Sun!

questions.q: What is the main background color of Brazil's flag?
questions.f: Brazil's green flag has a yellow diamond and a blue globe dotted with white stars!

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a capital city?
questions.f: Sydney is Australia's biggest city, but Canberra is the country's capital!

questions.q: Which of these deserts is found in Asia?
questions.f: The Gobi Desert is so far inland that it can be freezing cold in winter!

questions.q: Which is the tallest building in the world today?
questions.f: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai is so tall you can watch the sunset twice by riding up it!

questions.q: Africa has more countries than any other continent.
questions.f: Africa's 54 countries speak well over a thousand different languages!

questions.q: The Andes are the longest mountain range on land.
questions.f: The Andes run down the whole western edge of South America!

questions.q: Greenland is one of Earth's seven continents.
questions.f: Greenland is the world's largest island, but it is part of North America, not a continent.

questions.q: Why does the area near the equator get the most heat from the Sun?
c: The Sun's rays hit it most directly
It is closest to the Sun
questions.f: Straight-down sunlight is stronger, which is why rainforests thrive near the equator!

questions.q: What mainly causes the ocean's tides to rise and fall each day?
c: The Moon's gravity pulling the water
questions.f: The Moon's gentle pull tugs the seas, giving us high tides and low tides!

questions.q: Why are the North and South Poles so cold?
c: Sunlight hits them at a low, slanted angle
They are far from the Sun
questions.f: Slanted sunlight spreads out and weakens, so the poles never really warm up!

questions.q: What are Earth's giant tectonic plates?
c: Huge slabs of Earth's outer crust
questions.f: These enormous plates float on hot, gooey rock and slowly drift over millions of years!

questions.q: What causes most earthquakes on Earth?
questions.f: When stuck plates finally slip past each other, the ground shakes and rumbles!

questions.q: Why do mountains like the Himalayas keep slowly growing?
c: Two plates crash and push the land up
questions.f: India is still crashing into Asia, pushing Everest a few millimeters higher each year!

questions.q: What is the Ring of Fire?
c: A ring of volcanoes around the Pacific
A red sunset over the sea
questions.f: About three out of four of Earth's volcanoes sit along this fiery Pacific ring!

questions.q: Counting cold ones, which is the largest desert on the whole Earth?
questions.f: A desert is any place that is very dry, and icy Antarctica gets almost no rain or snow!

questions.q: Which is the longest mountain range on Earth, hidden under the sea?
questions.f: This underwater mountain chain winds around the globe for over 60,000 kilometers!

questions.q: What is the deepest known spot in the ocean called?
questions.f: Challenger Deep, in the Mariana Trench, is nearly 11 kilometers straight down!

questions.q: Which lake holds the most fresh water and is the deepest on Earth?
questions.f: Lake Baikal in Russia holds about a fifth of all the liquid fresh water on Earth!

questions.q: Why is it so easy for people to float in the Dead Sea?
c: Its very high salt makes the water dense
questions.f: So much salt is packed in that swimmers bob on the surface like corks!

questions.q: Why is a tropical rainforest so wet and green all year?
c: Heavy rain falls almost every day
The soil is full of salt
questions.f: Warm, damp air near the equator makes rain clouds burst almost daily!

questions.q: What do we call the imaginary line where each new day begins?
questions.f: Step across the Date Line and you can jump from today into tomorrow!

questions.q: Counting its faraway islands, which country covers the most time zones?
questions.f: France has land all over the world, so it stretches across 12 different time zones!

questions.q: Why does a place like the Sahara slowly grow and shrink over thousands of years?
c: Slow changes in the climate and rainfall
questions.f: Long ago the Sahara was green with lakes, rivers, and grazing animals!

questions.q: The Great Barrier Reef is so enormous it can be seen from where?
questions.f: Stretching over 2,000 kilometers, it is the largest thing on Earth built by living creatures!

questions.q: The Sahara is the largest desert on the whole Earth.
questions.f: The Sahara is the largest hot desert, but icy Antarctica is the largest desert of all!

questions.q: The Moon's gravity is the main reason we have ocean tides.
questions.f: As Earth spins, the Moon's pull creates a bulge of water we feel as the tides!

questions.q: Volcanoes and earthquakes are common around the Pacific Ring of Fire.
questions.f: Plates grinding together there make it Earth's most rumbly, fiery zone!

questions.q: Which animal is this?
questions.f: A lion's mighty roar can be heard up to 8 kilometres away!

questions.q: What do we call a baby dog?
questions.f: Puppies are born blind, deaf, and without any teeth.

questions.q: What do we call a baby cat?
questions.f: A newborn kitten can sleep for about 20 hours a day.

questions.q: What covers the body of a fish?
questions.f: Fish scales grow rings you can count to tell the fish's age, like tree rings.

questions.q: Which animal is famous for its black and white stripes?
questions.f: Every zebra has a stripe pattern as unique as your fingerprints.

questions.q: Whose shadow is this?
questions.f: An elephant is the only animal that cannot jump.

questions.q: What do we call a baby cow?
questions.f: A newborn calf can stand and walk within an hour of being born.

questions.q: Which animal hops and carries its baby in a pouch?
questions.f: A newborn kangaroo joey is only about the size of a grape.

questions.q: A snake has legs.
questions.f: Snakes have no legs and slither along using their belly scales.

questions.q: Which animal is the tallest in the world?
questions.f: A giraffe can be nearly 6 metres tall, taller than three grown-ups stacked up.

questions.q: What sound does a dog make?
questions.f: Dogs can make over a dozen different sounds to 'talk' to us.

questions.q: Which animal is this?
questions.f: A turtle can pull its head and legs inside its shell to stay safe.

questions.q: What do we call a baby sheep?
questions.f: A baby lamb can recognise its mother's bleat from across the field.

questions.q: A cow says 'moo'.
questions.f: Cows even have accents, so their moos can sound different in different places.

questions.q: Which animal is often called 'man's best friend'?
questions.f: Dogs have been human companions for over 15,000 years.

questions.q: What covers the body of most mammals?
questions.f: Fur keeps mammals warm like a cosy built-in coat.

questions.q: Which small animal has long ears and hops about?
questions.f: A rabbit's big ears help it hear danger and stay cool in the heat.

questions.q: Which animal is this?
questions.f: A frog can breathe through its skin as well as its lungs.

questions.q: Which pet says 'meow' and likes to purr?
questions.f: A cat's purr can help calm itself down, and you too!

questions.q: How many legs does a horse have?
questions.f: Horses can even sleep standing up on their four legs.

questions.q: Which big cat is the fastest animal on land?
questions.f: A cheetah can sprint as fast as a car on the motorway, around 100 km/h.

questions.q: Which bird is the biggest but cannot fly?
questions.f: An ostrich can't fly, but it can run faster than a galloping horse.

questions.q: Which bird is this?
questions.f: Penguins are birds that 'fly' underwater using their flipper wings.

questions.q: Which animal has humps and lives in the desert?
questions.f: A camel's hump stores fat, not water, for long desert journeys.

questions.q: Which bird is this?
questions.f: An owl can turn its head almost all the way around to look behind it.

questions.q: What do we call a baby lion?
questions.f: Lion cubs are born with faint spots that fade as they grow up.

questions.q: Which black and white bear eats mostly bamboo?
questions.f: A giant panda can munch bamboo for up to 12 hours a day.

questions.q: Which white bear lives on the icy Arctic?
questions.f: Under its white fur, a polar bear's skin is actually black.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am a super-smart sea mammal, I love to leap, and I chat in clicks and whistles. What am I?
questions.f: Dolphins even give each other names using special whistles.

questions.q: A group of lions is called a pride.
questions.f: A family group of lions really is called a pride.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I can change my skin colour and my two eyes can look in different directions at once. What am I?
questions.f: Chameleons change colour to show their mood, not just to hide.

questions.q: Which small reptile can climb straight up walls?
questions.f: Many geckos can drop their tail to escape, then grow a brand new one.

questions.q: Bats are the only mammals that can truly fly.
questions.f: Bats are the only mammals with wings for real flying.

questions.q: Which sleepy animal eats eucalyptus leaves in Australia?
questions.f: A koala sleeps up to 20 hours a day to save energy from its leafy diet.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I carry my home on my back, I move very slowly, and I can live for over one hundred years. What am I?
questions.f: Some tortoises live longer than 150 years.

questions.q: What is a group of flamingos called?
questions.f: A group of flamingos really is called a 'flamboyance'.

questions.q: What unusual shape is a wombat's poop?
questions.f: The wombat is the only animal that makes cube-shaped poop.

questions.q: How many bones are in a giraffe's long neck?
questions.f: A giraffe has just seven neck bones, the same number as you!

questions.q: Which mammal lays eggs instead of having live babies?
questions.f: The platypus is a mammal, yet it lays eggs like a bird.

questions.q: Which reptile is this?
questions.f: A crocodile can grow new teeth again and again all its life.

questions.q: A group of owls is called a parliament.
questions.f: A group of owls is charmingly called a 'parliament'.

questions.q: Which bird is the fastest animal when it dives?
questions.f: In a dive, a peregrine falcon is the fastest animal on Earth, over 300 km/h.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I sleep hanging upside down, and I am the only mammal that can really fly. What am I?
questions.f: Some bats use echoes, called echolocation, to 'see' in the dark.

questions.q: What is a baby swan called?
questions.f: A baby swan is called a cygnet and starts out fluffy and grey.

questions.q: What is a baby goat called?
questions.f: A baby goat can hop and climb almost as soon as it is born.

questions.q: Which animal is this?
questions.f: A sloth moves so slowly that green algae can grow in its fur.

questions.q: Flamingos turn pink because of what they eat?
questions.f: The tiny shrimp and algae flamingos eat contain a pink dye called carotenoid.

questions.q: A group of fish swimming together is called a school.
questions.f: A big group of fish swimming as one is called a school.

questions.q: Which animal is the fastest swimmer in the ocean?
questions.f: A sailfish can zoom through water at around 110 km/h.

questions.q: Which of these is the largest animal that has ever lived?
questions.f: A blue whale's heart alone can be as big as a small car.

questions.q: Which of these is the name for a baby deer?
questions.f: A fawn's spotty coat helps it hide in dappled sunlight.

questions.q: What do we call a group of wolves?
questions.f: A wolf pack works as a team to hunt and care for its pups.

questions.q: What does a camel really store inside its hump?
questions.f: A camel breaks down the fat in its hump for energy and water.

questions.q: An ostrich's eye is bigger than its brain.
questions.f: An ostrich's eye is bigger than its brain!

questions.q: Which of these is a reptile, not an amphibian?
questions.f: Reptiles have dry scaly skin, while amphibians have smooth wet skin.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am a bright pink bird, I stand on one leg, and I eat with my head upside down. What am I?
questions.f: Flamingos often rest by standing on just one leg to stay warm.

questions.q: Whose shadow is this?
questions.f: A rhino's horn is made of keratin, the same stuff as your hair and nails.

questions.q: Which of these animals can sleep while standing up?
questions.f: Horses can lock their leg joints to doze without falling over.

questions.q: What is a group of rhinos called?
questions.f: A group of rhinos really is called a 'crash'.

questions.q: What is the amazing change from caterpillar to butterfly called?
questions.f: During metamorphosis, a caterpillar turns to mush inside before becoming a butterfly.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the loudest land animals?
questions.f: A howler monkey's call can be heard up to 5 km away through the forest.

questions.q: Why can't a kangaroo hop backwards?
c: Its thick tail and big feet get in the way
Its knees bend the wrong way
It has no tail for balance
questions.f: Because they cannot go backwards, kangaroos appear on Australia's coat of arms as a symbol of moving forward.

questions.q: A sloth can hold its breath longer than a dolphin.
questions.f: A sloth can hold its breath longer than a dolphin by slowing its heartbeat right down.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I have blue blood, no bones at all, and I can squeeze through a hole the size of a coin. What am I?
questions.f: An octopus can squeeze through any gap bigger than its hard beak.

questions.q: Which tiny animal can survive the freezing vacuum of outer space?
questions.f: Tardigrades, or 'water bears', have even survived being sent into space and back.

questions.q: Which amphibian can regrow its legs, tail, and even parts of its heart?
questions.f: An axolotl keeps its feathery gills and baby looks for its whole life.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I live in the icy Arctic sea and I have one long spiral tusk, so people call me the unicorn of the sea. What am I?
questions.f: A narwhal's 'horn' is really a giant tooth that pokes through its lip.

questions.q: How does the peregrine falcon reach the fastest speed of any animal?
c: By diving steeply from high in the sky
By flapping its wings very fast
questions.f: This super-fast dive is called a 'stoop'.

questions.q: What do you get when you mix red and yellow paint?
questions.f: Orange is named after the fruit — the fruit's name came first!

questions.q: What do you get when you mix blue and yellow paint?
questions.f: Leaves look green for the same reason paint does — they bounce green light to your eyes.

questions.q: Mixing red paint with white paint makes which color?
questions.f: Adding white to any color makes a lighter 'tint' of it.

questions.q: What do you draw with that is made of colored wax?
questions.f: The biggest crayon ever made was over 4 metres long and weighed as much as a car!

questions.q: Which of these do painters put paint on?
questions.f: Canvas is a strong cloth — the same word gives us 'canvas shoes'!

questions.q: What do you call a picture you draw of yourself?
questions.f: Artists have painted self-portraits for centuries — it's like a hand-made selfie.

questions.q: Which color do you get by mixing ALL the paint colors together?
questions.f: Paints mix toward dark and muddy — but mixing LIGHT makes white. Opposites!

questions.q: What shape do you press your hand in to make a hand print?
questions.f: Some cave hand prints are more than 30,000 years old!

questions.q: Which tool has soft hairs and spreads paint?
questions.f: The first paintbrushes were made thousands of years ago from animal hair.

questions.q: Mixing blue and red paint makes purple.
questions.f: Purple was once so hard to make that only kings and queens wore it!

questions.q: The sky in a sunset can look orange and pink.
questions.f: Sunset light travels through extra air, which scatters away the blue and leaves the warm colors.

questions.q: A drawing of mountains and trees is called a portrait.
questions.f: A picture of nature is a LANDSCAPE — a portrait shows a person.

questions.q: Scissors and glued paper can be used to make art.
questions.f: Art made from cut and glued pieces is called a collage — French for 'gluing'!

questions.q: What is this artist's tool called?
questions.f: A palette is where painters mix their colors — one thumb hole, endless colors!

questions.q: What is this tool called?
questions.f: Brushes come in hundreds of sizes — some have just a few hairs for tiny details.

questions.q: Which colorful sky wonder is this?
questions.f: You can never reach a rainbow's end — it moves as you move!

questions.q: What do you call art hung in this?
questions.f: Fancy museum frames are sometimes worth thousands — the frame protects the painting.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am a stick of colored wax, and I love to draw. What am I?
questions.f: Crayons smell the same everywhere — that waxy smell is one of the most recognized in the world!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: Mix red paint with white paint. What color do I become?
questions.f: Pink is just red wearing a white coat!

questions.q: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.f: Leonardo was also an inventor who sketched flying machines 400 years before airplanes!

questions.q: The primary paint colors are red, yellow and…?
questions.f: With just these three you can mix almost every other color!

questions.q: Origami is the Japanese art of folding what?
questions.f: A single uncut square can become a crane, a frog or a dragon — just with folds!

questions.q: Rangoli patterns are made on the floor using colored…?
questions.f: Rangoli welcomes guests and good luck — especially at Diwali!

questions.q: What is the name for a giant painting done on a wall?
questions.f: Some murals cover whole buildings and take months to paint!

questions.q: Which color are school buses painted to be easy to see?
questions.f: Your eyes notice yellow faster than almost any other color — even at the edge of your vision.

questions.q: What do you call a picture made from tiny colored tiles?
questions.f: Ancient Roman floors still show mosaics made from thousands of tiny stones!

questions.q: An artist stands their painting on a three-legged…?
questions.f: 'Easel' comes from a Dutch word for donkey — it carries the painting like a little donkey!

questions.q: Which artist is famous for painting bright sunflowers?
questions.f: Van Gogh painted his sunflowers to decorate a friend's bedroom.

questions.q: Mehndi is beautiful skin art drawn with what plant paste?
questions.f: Henna designs fade away on their own after a couple of weeks.

questions.q: Pottery is shaped from which squishy material?
questions.f: Wet clay becomes rock-hard pottery after baking in a super-hot oven called a kiln.

questions.q: What is a statue usually carved from?
questions.f: Sculptors say the statue is 'already inside' the stone — they just remove the extra!

questions.q: The Mona Lisa hangs in a museum in Paris, France.
questions.f: About 30,000 people visit her at the Louvre every single day!

questions.q: Mixing yellow and blue paint makes red.
questions.f: Yellow and blue make GREEN — red is a primary color you can't mix from others.

questions.q: This spinning toy holds smaller ones inside. What is it called?
questions.f: Russian nesting dolls can hide 5, 10, even 50 dolls inside each other!

questions.q: What is this clay water pot called?
questions.f: Ancient Greek vases tell whole stories in pictures painted around them.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I have three legs, I never walk, and I hold paintings all day. What am I?
questions.f: Easels let painters work standing up and step back to check their picture.

questions.q: What happens when white light passes through a prism?
questions.f: Raindrops do the same job — that's exactly how rainbows happen!

questions.q: Which famous artist cut tiny dots to paint whole scenes, a style called pointillism?
questions.f: Stand far from a pointillist painting and thousands of dots melt into one picture!

questions.q: Van Gogh's famous swirling night-sky painting is called…?
questions.f: He painted it looking out of his window just before sunrise.

questions.q: Which ceiling did Michelangelo spend about four years painting?
questions.f: He painted standing on tall scaffolding with paint dripping on his face!

questions.q: Warm colors are red, orange and yellow. Which is a cool color?
questions.f: Artists use cool colors to make things feel calm, icy or far away.

questions.q: The Taj Mahal is built from which gleaming stone?
questions.f: Its marble seems to change color — pinkish at dawn, golden by moonlight!

questions.q: What is the special paint for painting on wet walls called?
questions.f: 'Fresco' means 'fresh' in Italian — artists paint before the wall plaster dries!

questions.q: A picture of fruit or objects on a table is called a…?
questions.f: Artists love still lifes because apples never wriggle while being painted!

questions.q: Which color did ancient Romans squeeze from sea snails?
questions.f: It took thousands of snails for one robe — that's why only emperors wore purple!

questions.q: What are the three 'secondary' paint colors?
questions.f: Each one is a mix of two primaries — they sit between them on the color wheel.

questions.q: Ancient Greek statues were originally painted in bright colors.
questions.f: The paint wore off over centuries — scientists find tiny traces and repaint copies!

questions.q: Black clothes feel hotter in the sun than white clothes.
questions.f: Black soaks up almost all the light and turns it to heat; white bounces it away.

questions.q: An artist who makes THIS kind of art is called a…?
questions.f: The first photo ever taken needed about eight HOURS of sitting still!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am a glass triangle. Shine white light through me and I make a rainbow. What am I?
questions.f: Isaac Newton used a prism to prove white light hides every color inside it.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a primary paint color?
