questions.f: Green is secondary — you mix it from blue and yellow.

questions.q: Put the artist's steps in order — which comes FIRST?
questions.f: Most painters sketch lightly first — mistakes are easy to fix at that stage.

questions.q: Which color is complementary to (opposite) red on the color wheel?
questions.f: Opposite colors make each other 'pop' — that's why holly berries look extra red on green leaves.

questions.q: Camouflage art hides things by copying…?
questions.f: Warships in WWI wore crazy zigzag 'dazzle' paint to confuse onlookers instead of hiding!

questions.q: The color magenta is named after…?
questions.f: The dye was discovered in 1859, the same year as the Battle of Magenta.

questions.q: Which of these words is NOT a shade of blue?
questions.f: Crimson is a deep RED — turquoise is named after a blue-green gemstone.

questions.q: Why do leaves in autumn show yellows and reds?
questions.f: The yellow was hiding under the green chlorophyll all summer long!

questions.q: Which art form uses a needle and colored thread on cloth?
questions.f: Some royal embroidered robes took a team of stitchers years to finish.

questions.q: The word 'indigo' — the I in ROY G BIV — originally comes from which country's name?
questions.f: Indigo dye from India was so precious it was called 'blue gold'!

questions.q: Gold leaf used in art is real gold hammered thinner than paper.
questions.f: It's beaten so thin that a stack of 10,000 sheets is only about 1 millimetre!

questions.q: Whose giant stone head sculpture is this, found on Easter Island?
questions.f: Nearly 1,000 moai were carved — the tallest is as heavy as ten elephants!

questions.q: Why does a peacock feather shimmer with color even though it has almost no pigment?
questions.f: That's called STRUCTURAL color — soap bubbles shimmer the same way!

questions.q: What is the technique of creating depth so far-off things look smaller called?
questions.f: Renaissance artists worked out perspective with math — art and geometry together!

questions.q: Which pigment, once made from crushed lapis lazuli stone, cost more than gold?
questions.f: Painters saved it for the most important part of a painting — often a queen's robe.

questions.q: The 'chiaroscuro' technique in painting plays with what?
questions.f: It's Italian for 'light-dark' — it makes flat paintings look dramatically 3D.

questions.q: Cave paintings at Lascaux, France are about how old?
questions.f: The painters used crushed rocks, charcoal — and sprayed paint with their mouths!

questions.q: What is a fake artwork sold as a famous original called?
questions.f: Museums use X-rays and chemistry labs to catch clever fakes.

questions.q: Which Spanish architect's colorful, curvy Sagrada Família church is STILL being built after 140+ years?
questions.f: Gaudí said straight lines belong to humans, curves belong to nature.

questions.q: 'Trompe l'oeil' paintings are designed to do what?
questions.f: It's French for 'deceives the eye' — some painted doorways look real enough to walk into!

questions.q: The Statue of Liberty was originally shiny copper-brown, not green.
questions.f: A century of air and rain slowly turned her copper skin into the green 'patina' we know.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am a blue made from crushed gemstones, once pricier than gold. Which color am I?
questions.f: True ultramarine came only from Afghan mines — one bag of stone made a thumb of paint.

questions.q: Which body part mashes your food into mush after you swallow?
questions.f: Your stomach makes strong acid that helps break your food into a soupy mush.

questions.q: Which body part is this?
questions.f: Your eyes can tell apart millions of different colours.

questions.q: How many senses do humans have?
questions.f: The five senses are sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch.

questions.q: Which body part is this?
questions.f: Your ears do two jobs at once: they help you hear and help you balance.

questions.q: Which body part is this?
questions.f: Your nose warms up cold air before it reaches your lungs.

questions.q: Which body part is this?
questions.f: The hard white coating on a tooth, called enamel, is the toughest stuff in your whole body.

questions.q: What are the swirly patterns on the tips of your fingers called?
questions.f: No two people in the whole world have exactly the same fingerprints.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: We are white and hard, we live in your mouth, and we help you chew your food. What are we?
questions.f: Kids grow a first set of 20 baby teeth before their bigger adult teeth push through.

questions.q: Which body part is this?
questions.f: Your brain feels a bit like squishy jelly if you could hold it.

questions.q: Which curved bones make a cage that protects your heart and lungs?
questions.f: You have 12 pairs of ribs curving around your chest like a bony cage.

questions.q: What salty liquid drips down your face when you are hot?
questions.f: Sweat cools you down by carrying heat away as it dries on your skin.

questions.q: What do your two eyes help you do?
questions.f: You blink about 15 times every minute to keep your eyes clean and wet.

questions.q: How many bones does a grown-up have?
questions.f: Over half of all your bones are found in your hands and feet.

questions.q: What is the yellowish gunk inside your ears called?
questions.f: Earwax is helpful because it traps dirt and keeps bugs out of your ears.

questions.q: Which body part is this?
questions.f: Your tongue is really a bundle of muscles working together.

questions.q: What is the watery liquid in your mouth called?
questions.f: You make enough spit each day to fill about six glasses of water.

questions.q: What is the tube called that carries air down toward your chest?
questions.f: Your windpipe has bendy rings of cartilage that keep it open like a vacuum hose.

questions.q: Which part of your body slowly repairs itself if it cracks?
questions.f: Bones are alive and can slowly heal and mend themselves after they break.

questions.q: What are your hair and fingernails both made of?
questions.f: Keratin is the same stuff that makes up a rhino's horn.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am red, I flow all around your body, and I carry oxygen to keep you alive. What am I?
questions.f: An adult has about five litres of blood, enough to fill a big drink bottle twice.

questions.q: Which body part protects your brain?
questions.f: Your skull is made of bony plates that lock together like a helmet.

questions.q: Which body parts keep slowly changing shape your whole life?
questions.f: Your nose and ears keep changing shape as you get older because of the soft cartilage inside them.

questions.q: Which body part is this?
questions.f: Your heart is tilted a little to the left side of your chest.

questions.q: What do your kidneys turn into wee?
questions.f: Your two kidneys clean your entire blood supply many times every single day.

questions.q: True or False: You can easily tickle yourself.
questions.f: You cannot really tickle yourself because your brain knows the touch is coming and cancels the surprise.

questions.q: What tube carries food from your mouth down to your stomach?
questions.f: Muscles in your throat squeeze the food down, so you could even swallow upside down.

questions.q: What is the longest bone in the human body?
questions.f: The thigh bone, or femur, is so strong it can hold more weight than concrete.

questions.q: About how many times does your heart beat in one day?
questions.f: Over a lifetime your heart beats more than two billion times.

questions.q: What is the smallest bone in your body?
questions.f: The tiniest bone, the stirrup bone in your ear, is about the size of a grain of rice.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am made of over two hundred bones joined together, and I hold your whole body up. What am I?
questions.f: Without a skeleton you would flop to the floor like a jellyfish.

questions.q: Which part of the eye lets light come inside?
questions.f: Your pupil grows bigger in the dark to let in more light so you can see.

questions.q: Which part of your ear beats like a drum when sound hits it?
questions.f: Your eardrum is a thin skin that shivers when sound waves bump into it.

questions.q: Which body part is this?
questions.f: Each foot has 26 bones, so your two feet hold about a quarter of all your bones.

questions.q: Which gas does your blood carry from your lungs to the rest of your body?
questions.f: Tiny red blood cells act like delivery trucks, dropping off oxygen everywhere it is needed.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: We work in pairs to pull your bones, we let you move, and you have six hundred of us. What are we?
questions.f: Your muscles make up almost half of your whole body weight.

questions.q: What is the hardest substance in the human body?
questions.f: Tooth enamel is even harder than steel, which is why teeth can crunch hard food.

questions.q: True or False: Hiccups happen because your heart skips a beat.
questions.f: Hiccups actually come from the diaphragm, a muscle under your lungs, twitching suddenly.

questions.q: Where is your blood made inside your body?
questions.f: Soft jelly called marrow deep inside your bones makes millions of new blood cells every second.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the five senses?
questions.f: Balance is handled inside your ears, but it is usually not counted as one of the five main senses.

questions.q: Which of these organs is the largest inside your body?
questions.f: The liver does over 500 jobs, including cleaning nasty stuff out of your blood.

questions.q: Which travels the shorter distance inside you?
c: Blood around your body in a day
Air through your windpipe in a day
questions.f: Even though it is called small, your small intestine is much longer than your large intestine when stretched out.

questions.q: Which of these carries blood AWAY from your heart?
questions.f: Arteries carry blood away from the heart while veins bring it back again.

questions.q: Which body part contains 27 bones, more than you might expect?
questions.f: Your hand has 27 bones, letting you do tiny careful jobs like tying a knot.

questions.q: Which of these body parts is soft and bendy, NOT made of hard bone?
questions.f: The bendy tip of your nose is made of cartilage, the same rubbery stuff in your ears.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am soft and bendy, I shape your ears and nose tip, and sharks are made entirely of me. What am I?
questions.f: Sharks have no bones at all; their entire skeleton is made of bendy cartilage.

questions.q: Put these in order: which body part sends fast messages to your brain?
questions.f: Signals zoom along your nerves faster than a racing car on a motorway.

questions.q: True or False: Your left lung is bigger than your right lung.
questions.f: The left lung is actually the smaller one, leaving a cosy pocket of space for your heart.

questions.q: Why does your skin turn darker when you spend time in the sun?
c: It makes more melanin to protect you
questions.f: Melanin is a natural pigment that acts like built-in sunscreen against harmful rays.

questions.q: True or False: The place people call the funny bone is really a nerve, not a bone.
questions.f: Banging your elbow zaps the ulnar nerve, which gives that weird tingly funny-bone feeling.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: Millions of us fill your lungs, we look like tiny balloons, and we pass oxygen into your blood. What are we?
questions.f: These tiny air sacs called alveoli give your lungs a huge surface to soak up oxygen.

questions.q: Which part of the brain helps you keep your balance and move smoothly?
questions.f: The cerebellum sits at the back of your brain and fine-tunes every step you take.

questions.q: True or False: Your body makes brand new skin cells so fast that you get a whole new outer layer over time.
questions.f: You shed millions of skin cells every day and grow fresh ones to replace them.

questions.q: Why does a doctor listen to your chest to hear your heart?
c: To hear the valves snapping shut
questions.f: The lub-dub sound is made by little doors called valves slamming shut to stop blood flowing backwards.

questions.q: What causes the sharp pain called brain freeze when you eat ice cream too fast?
c: Cold on the roof of your mouth
questions.f: Cold on the roof of your mouth confuses nearby nerves, and your brain wrongly thinks your forehead hurts.

questions.q: Why can you still feel your way in a pitch-black room?
c: Your eyes glow in the dark
questions.f: Your skin is packed with millions of touch sensors that feel shape, pressure and temperature.

questions.q: What sweet food do bees make?
questions.f: Bees turn flower nectar into honey inside their busy hive.

questions.q: Which bird cannot fly but is a super swimmer?
questions.f: A penguin uses its wings like flippers to zoom underwater.

questions.q: Where do baby birds hatch from?
questions.f: Every bird starts life curled up inside an egg.

questions.q: Which little bug can glow in the dark?
questions.f: Fireflies flash light in their bellies to send signals to each other.

questions.q: What is a spider's sticky trap called?
questions.f: A spider spins a web from silk to catch its next meal.

questions.q: Which red bug is famous for its black spots?
questions.f: A ladybug's bright spots warn hungry birds that it tastes yucky.

questions.q: Which insect chirps on a warm summer night?
questions.f: A cricket makes its chirp by rubbing its two wings together.

questions.q: What covers a bird's body to keep it warm?
questions.f: Birds are the only animals on Earth that grow feathers.

questions.q: What does a caterpillar turn into?
questions.f: A caterpillar wraps itself up and slowly changes into a butterfly.

questions.q: What sweet juice do bees collect from flowers?
questions.f: Bees sip sugary nectar and carry it home to make honey.

questions.q: Which bird likes to hoot at night?
questions.f: Owls stay awake at night and hoot to talk to each other.

questions.q: What do birds flap to fly through the air?
questions.f: Birds flap their strong wings to push against the air and lift up.

questions.q: Which insect is this?
questions.f: A single bee may visit thousands of flowers in just one day.

questions.q: Which bird is this?
questions.f: A duck's feathers are so oily that water rolls right off them.

questions.q: Whose shadow is this?
questions.f: A spider has eight legs and eight eyes, but still cannot fly.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: A honeybee dances to tell its hive friends where the best flowers are.
questions.say: I buzz from flower to flower and make sweet golden honey inside my hive. What am I?

questions.q: A spider is a kind of insect.
questions.f: A spider is really an arachnid, with eight legs instead of six.

questions.q: Penguins can fly high through the sky.
questions.f: Penguins cannot fly, but they swim as fast as a torpedo.

questions.q: Which is the largest bird in the whole world?
questions.f: An ostrich can grow taller than a grown-up person.

questions.q: What do we call a group of owls?
questions.f: A group of owls is called a parliament, like a wise meeting.

questions.q: How many wings does a bee have?
questions.f: A bee has four wings that hook together into two big flapping wings.

questions.q: Which bird can copy human words?
questions.f: Some clever parrots can learn to say over one hundred words.

questions.q: What is a baby bee called before it grows wings?
questions.f: A bee begins as a tiny white larva tucked inside a wax cell.

questions.q: Which insect builds tall towers out of dirt?
questions.f: Termite mounds can rise taller than a giraffe out of the ground.

questions.q: Which small flightless bird comes from New Zealand?
questions.f: A kiwi bird lays an egg that is huge compared to its little body.

questions.q: What is an insect's hard outer body armor called?
questions.f: Insects wear their skeleton on the outside like a suit of armor.

questions.q: Which beetle rolls balls of animal poop?
questions.f: A dung beetle rolls poop into a ball and uses it for food.

questions.q: Which colorful bird can spread a giant fan of tail feathers?
questions.f: A male peacock fans out a tail covered in shimmering eye spots.

questions.q: What is the leader that rules a beehive called?
questions.f: One queen bee rules the whole hive and lays all of its eggs.

questions.q: Which bird is this?
questions.f: An eagle can spot a rabbit from as far as a mile away.

questions.q: What is this small animal?
questions.f: A snail is not an insect, and it carries its house on its back.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: A dragonfly can fly forward, backward, and even hover in one spot.
questions.say: I have four shiny wings and I hover over ponds to snatch bugs from the air. What am I?

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: A woodpecker's head is built with cushions so it never gets a headache.
questions.say: I bang my strong beak on tree trunks to drill holes and find tasty bugs. What am I?

questions.q: A butterfly tastes its food using its feet.
questions.f: A butterfly steps on a leaf to taste whether it is good to eat.

questions.q: All insects have six legs.
questions.f: Six legs is one of the rules that makes a bug a true insect.

questions.q: Which is the only bird that can truly fly backwards?
questions.f: A hummingbird can hover and even fly backwards like a tiny helicopter.

questions.q: How do honeybees tell friends where flowers are?
questions.f: A bee wiggles in a special dance to point the way to flowers.

questions.q: About how far can an owl turn its head?
questions.f: An owl can twist its head almost all the way around to look behind.

questions.q: Why are flamingos pink?
questions.f: Flamingos turn pink from the tiny shrimp and algae they gobble up.

questions.q: Which tiny insect can carry things up to 50 times its own weight?
questions.f: That is like a kid lifting a car high above their head.

questions.q: What do we call a group of crows?
questions.f: A group of crows has the spooky name of a murder.

questions.q: What is the big change from caterpillar to butterfly called?
questions.f: During metamorphosis, a caterpillar's whole body is rebuilt into a butterfly.

questions.q: Which animal is the fastest when diving from the sky?
questions.f: A diving peregrine falcon is the fastest animal on the whole planet.

questions.q: Which bird is this?
questions.f: A flamingo often sleeps while standing on just one skinny leg.

questions.q: What is this creepy-crawly?
questions.f: A hungry caterpillar can eat many times its own weight in leaves.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: A praying mantis can turn its head to look right over its shoulder.
questions.say: I hold my two front legs together as if praying, then grab bugs to eat. What am I?

questions.q: A honeybee dies after it stings you once.
questions.f: A honeybee's stinger has hooks that stay stuck in your skin.

questions.q: Only female mosquitoes bite people for blood.
questions.f: Female mosquitoes need a blood meal to help their eggs grow.

questions.q: Which of these creatures is NOT a bird?
questions.f: A bat has wings and flies, but it is a furry mammal, not a bird.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT an insect?
questions.f: A scorpion has eight legs, so it is an arachnid like a spider.

questions.q: Which stinging insect can sting again and again without dying?
questions.f: A wasp's smooth stinger slides out easily, so it can sting many times.

questions.q: What are the colorful powdery bits on a butterfly's wings?
questions.f: Butterfly wings are covered in thousands of overlapping tiny scales.

questions.q: Which tiny bug do ladybugs love to eat?
questions.f: One ladybug can gobble up thousands of plant-munching aphids in its life.

questions.q: Which bird has a giant, colorful beak for its size?
questions.f: A toucan's huge beak is light and hollow, so it is not heavy at all.

questions.q: What is the hard case a caterpillar makes before turning into a butterfly?
questions.f: Butterflies form a chrysalis, while many moths spin a silky cocoon.

questions.q: Which insect is this?
questions.f: A grasshopper can leap about 20 times the length of its own body.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: Emperor penguin dads huddle together for months to keep their eggs warm.
questions.say: I am the tallest penguin, and dads balance our egg on their feet in freezing cold. What am I?

questions.q: A cockroach can stay alive for a while even without its head.
questions.f: A cockroach breathes through its body, so losing its head does not stop it fast.

questions.q: Hummingbirds are the smallest birds in the world.
questions.f: The tiny bee hummingbird is smaller than some of the moths it flies near.

questions.q: Why can a hummingbird hover perfectly still in midair?
c: It flaps its wings in a fast figure-eight
questions.f: Its figure-eight wingbeats push air down on both strokes to hold it still.

questions.q: An ostrich's eye is actually bigger than which of its own body parts?
questions.f: Each ostrich eye is about the size of a billiard ball, bigger than its brain.

questions.q: What is the smallest bird in the whole world?
questions.f: A bee hummingbird weighs less than a small coin and fits on a fingertip.

questions.q: How does a firefly make its glowing light?
c: A chemical reaction in its body
questions.f: A firefly mixes chemicals inside its body to glow without any heat.

questions.q: Why do monarch butterflies fly thousands of miles south each autumn?
questions.f: Monarchs travel all the way to warm Mexico to survive the cold winter.

questions.q: Which insect is this?
questions.f: A mosquito's buzzing whine comes from its wings beating hundreds of times a second.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: An insect's antennae can smell food and danger from far away.
questions.say: Insects use these two bendy feelers on their heads to smell and touch the world. What are they?

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: A dragonfly's compound eyes have around 30,000 tiny lenses each.
questions.say: My giant eyes are each built from thousands of tiny lenses stuck together. What are they called?

questions.q: Some birds fly thousands of miles every year to reach warmer weather.
questions.f: The Arctic tern flies from the top of the world to the bottom and back.

questions.q: A queen bee can lay thousands of eggs in a single day.
questions.f: A busy queen bee can lay around 2,000 eggs in just one day.

questions.q: Diwali is known as the festival of what?
questions.f: Homes across India glow with tiny lamps, fireworks, and sweets shared with the whole family!

questions.q: During Holi, what do friends joyfully throw at each other?
questions.f: The colored powder is called gulal — and squirting water balloons join the fun too!

questions.q: What do you blow out on a birthday cake?
questions.f: Legend says if you blow them all out in one breath, your wish comes true!

questions.q: What do you call your mother's mother?
questions.f: She has nicknames all over the world — Nani in Hindi, Abuela in Spanish, Obaachan in Japanese!

questions.q: In Japan, what do you take off before stepping inside a home?
questions.f: Many Japanese homes have cozy indoor slippers waiting right by the door for guests!

questions.q: At Mexican birthday parties, kids swing a stick at what hanging treat-holder?
questions.f: Players are blindfolded and spun around before they get to swing!

questions.q: What are two babies called when born to the same mom on the same day?
questions.f: Twins can be identical or fraternal — fraternal twins can look totally different from each other!

questions.q: What snack do many kids leave out for Santa on Christmas Eve?
questions.f: In some countries, kids leave out carrots for the reindeer too!

questions.q: What do trick-or-treaters collect on Halloween night?
questions.f: The phrase 'trick or treat' is a playful deal — hand over a treat, or get a silly trick!

questions.q: What do people shout when the clock strikes midnight on December 31?
questions.f: In New York City, a giant glittering ball drops at midnight in Times Square!

questions.q: Which festival has hunts for hidden painted eggs?
questions.f: In many places, the eggs are said to be hidden by the Easter Bunny!

questions.q: What do you call your aunt or uncle's child?
questions.f: Here's a twisty one — your cousin's child is your first cousin once removed!

questions.q: Your uncle is your parent's brother.
questions.f: And that makes you his niece or nephew!

questions.q: In India, 'didi' is a loving name for a big sister.
questions.f: Big brothers get a special name too — bhaiya!

questions.q: Birthday cakes are usually decorated with pickles.
questions.f: Frosting, sprinkles, and candles — much, much tastier!

questions.q: What is this little Diwali lamp called?
questions.f: Diyas are tiny clay lamps filled with oil, lit with a little cotton wick!

questions.q: This decorated tree belongs to which holiday?
questions.f: Families in Germany began decorating Christmas trees hundreds of years ago!

questions.q: What is this carved Halloween pumpkin called?
questions.f: Long ago in Ireland, the first jack-o'-lanterns were carved from turnips!

questions.say: Gobble gobble! I am the big bird that families roast for Thanksgiving dinner. What am I?
questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: A turkey's gobble is so loud it can be heard up to a mile away!

questions.say: You light my candles, sing me a song, make a wish, and blow! What am I?
questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: People have been putting candles on celebration cakes since ancient times!

questions.q: At Chinese New Year, kids get lucky money in envelopes of which color?
questions.f: The envelope is called a hongbao — and red stands for good luck and happiness!

questions.q: Which country celebrates the colorful Day of the Dead each November?
questions.f: Families gather with music, flowers, and food to share happy stories about loved ones!

questions.q: What greeting do people share on Eid?
questions.f: 'Eid Mubarak' means 'blessed festival' — and it comes with hugs and sweet treats!

questions.q: In the USA, Thanksgiving is celebrated in which month?
questions.f: The very first Thanksgiving feast in 1621 lasted three whole days!

questions.q: Ganesh Chaturthi celebrates a god with the head of which animal?
questions.f: Sweet dumplings called modak are said to be Ganesha's favorite treat!

questions.q: In Hindi, what is your father's brother called?
questions.f: Your mother's brother gets a different name — he's your mama!

questions.q: Which whirling dance lights up Navratri nights in Gujarat?
questions.f: Dancers twirl in circles and sometimes tap colorful sticks called dandiya!

questions.q: Bhangra, a bouncy harvest dance, comes from which Indian state?
questions.f: Farmers danced bhangra to celebrate the Baisakhi harvest — with big shoulder bounces!

questions.q: Which round treats do families share at China's Mid-Autumn Festival?
questions.f: Mooncakes are round like the full moon, and some hide a golden egg-yolk 'moon' inside!

questions.q: During Thailand's Songkran New Year, what do people splash everywhere?
questions.f: Songkran falls in April, one of Thailand's hottest months — it becomes a giant friendly water fight!

questions.q: Mexico's Day of the Dead is a quiet, gloomy festival.
questions.f: It's joyful — full of music, dancing, paper banners, and favorite family foods!

questions.q: In Japan, people greet each other by bowing.
questions.f: A deeper, longer bow shows extra respect!

questions.q: At the La Tomatina festival, people playfully throw these. What are they?
questions.f: Trucks dump more than 100 tonnes of squishy tomatoes for the world's biggest food fight!

questions.q: On Makar Sankranti, Indian skies fill with these. What are they?
questions.f: In Gujarat, friendly kite battles try to cut each other's strings out of the sky!

questions.say: Spin me at Hanukkah! I am a little top with four Hebrew letters on my sides. What am I?
questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: The four letters stand for 'a great miracle happened there'!

questions.say: On a special day in India, a sister ties me around her brother's wrist. What am I?
questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: The festival is called Raksha Bandhan — 'the bond of protection'!

questions.q: How many days does the Diwali festival last?
questions.f: The last day, Bhai Dooj, celebrates the love between brothers and sisters!

questions.q: Which bright orange flower decorates Day of the Dead celebrations in Mexico?
questions.f: Families believe the marigolds' bright petals and strong scent help guide ancestors home to the party!

questions.q: In which country do people hurl tomatoes at La Tomatina?
questions.f: It happens every August in the little town of Buñol!

questions.q: US Thanksgiving always lands on which day of the week?
questions.f: Millions watch the big parade that morning, with balloons as tall as buildings!

questions.q: Onam, with its snake boat races, is a harvest festival of which state?
questions.f: Families welcome Onam with pookalam — beautiful carpets made entirely of flowers!

questions.q: In China, birthday noodles are extra long. What do they stand for?
questions.f: Slurp, don't bite them short — cutting the noodle is said to cut the luck!

questions.q: Which sweet stuffed dumpling is a Holi favorite in North India?
questions.f: Gujiya is moon-shaped and stuffed with milky khoya, coconut, and dried fruits!

questions.q: In Japan, temple bells ring how many times to welcome the New Year?
questions.f: The tradition is called Joya no Kane — the ringing starts before midnight and rolls into the new year!

questions.q: The Hanukkah menorah is lit for eight nights.
questions.f: One more candle is lit each night until all eight glow together!

questions.q: Canada celebrates Thanksgiving in October, before the USA does.
questions.f: Canadians feast on the second Monday of October!

questions.q: At midnight on New Year's Eve, Spaniards eat 12 of these. What are they?
questions.f: One grape for each chime of the clock — finish all 12 for a lucky year!

questions.q: Whose shadow is this, dancing at Chinese New Year parades?
questions.f: Parade dragons are held up on poles and can need more than ten dancers to carry them!

questions.say: I am a colorful pattern made from powder, drawn on the floor to welcome guests at Diwali. What am I?
questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: Rangoli can be made from colored powder, rice, or even flower petals!

questions.q: Which animal is NOT in the Chinese zodiac?
questions.f: Legend says the rat never woke the cat for the great race — so the cat missed out forever!

questions.q: Which festival marks the end of Ramadan, the month of fasting?
questions.f: Eid begins when the thin new crescent moon is spotted in the sky!

questions.q: Which of these is NOT famously thrown at a festival somewhere in the world?
questions.f: Tomatoes fly at La Tomatina, water at Songkran, and colored powder at Holi!

questions.q: In parts of Canada, what gets rubbed on a birthday kid's nose for luck?
questions.f: The buttery nose is said to be too slippery for bad luck to catch!

questions.q: At a Dutch birthday party, who gets told 'congratulations'?
questions.f: In the Netherlands you might hear 'congratulations!' just for being the cousin of the birthday kid!

questions.q: Which of these festivals arrives in SPRING?
questions.f: Holi welcomes spring with colors — and a big bonfire the night before!

questions.q: A 'leapling' has a birthday only once every four years. When was a leapling born?
questions.f: Leap years add February 29 to keep our calendar matched with Earth's trip around the Sun!

questions.q: The name 'Diwali' means 'festival of kites'.
questions.f: It comes from 'Deepavali' — 'a row of lights' in Sanskrit!

questions.q: In Vietnam, everyone traditionally becomes a year older together at the Tet New Year.
questions.f: So Tet is like one giant shared birthday party for the whole country!

questions.q: What is this traditional Japanese festival outfit called?
questions.f: 'Kimono' simply means 'a thing to wear' in Japanese!

questions.say: Whoosh! At some Asian festivals, families light me and let me float glowing into the night sky. What am I?
questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: At Thailand's Yi Peng festival, thousands rise together like floating stars!

questions.q: Why does Diwali fall on a different date each year?
c: It follows the Moon-based Hindu calendar
A new date is voted on each year
It moves to always land on a weekend
It depends on when the rains end
questions.f: Diwali lands on the new-moon night of the month of Kartik — the darkest night, perfect for lamps!

questions.q: Why do people remove their shoes inside Japanese homes?
c: To keep floors clean for sitting and sleeping
Because the doors are too low
questions.f: Families relax and even sleep on tatami floor mats — shoes wait in an entryway called the genkan!

questions.q: Why is red the big color of Chinese New Year decorations?
c: A legend says red scares off a monster called Nian
Red was the first paint ever invented
Red is the color of the zodiac rat
questions.f: Loud firecrackers were said to frighten Nian away too — that's why the holiday is so noisy!

questions.q: Which island nation is among the very FIRST on Earth to welcome each New Year?
questions.f: Kiribati's Line Islands use the earliest time zone on Earth — a whole day ahead of some places!

questions.q: How do identical twins begin?
c: One egg cell splits into two
One egg grows twice as big
questions.f: That's why identical twins share almost exactly the same DNA!

questions.q: Who is your 'paternal' grandmother?
questions.f: Hindi has separate words for each — dadi on your father's side, nani on your mother's!

questions.q: During Day of the Dead, what is the 'ofrenda' families lovingly build at home?
c: A table with photos and favorite foods of loved ones
A tower of tomatoes to throw
questions.f: It's a happy way to remember family — even their favorite snacks get a spot!

questions.q: In South Korea, birthdays often start with a bowl of seaweed soup.
questions.f: The soup, miyeok-guk, honors moms — it's the meal new mothers traditionally eat!

questions.q: What is this nine-branched Hanukkah candle holder called?
questions.f: The ninth candle, the shamash or 'helper', is used to light all the others!

questions.say: In Hindi, there is a special name just for your mother's sister. What is she called?
questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's question!
questions.f: Hindi has a name for almost every relative — bua is your father's sister!

questions.q: Which food is this?
questions.f: A classic Margherita's toppings — red tomato, white cheese, green basil — match the colors of Italy's flag!

questions.q: Name this green vegetable!
questions.f: A broccoli head is really hundreds of tiny flower buds packed together!

questions.q: What spiky fruit do you see?
questions.f: Pineapples were once so fancy that people rented them just to show off at parties!

questions.q: Whose shadow is this crunchy vegetable?
questions.f: Carrots get sweeter after a frost — the plant makes extra sugar to protect itself from the cold!

questions.q: Which food is this?
questions.f: An ear of corn almost always has an even number of rows of kernels!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am long and yellow, monkeys love me, and you peel me before you eat me. What am I?
questions.f: A bunch of bananas is called a 'hand' — and each single banana is a 'finger'!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: Chop me up and I will make you cry, even though I never feel sad. What am I?
questions.f: Cooked onions taste sweeter because heat breaks down their sharp, tear-making chemicals.

questions.q: Raisins are dried grapes.
questions.f: Drop a raisin into fizzy soda and it will bounce up and down like a tiny elevator!

questions.q: 'An ___ a day keeps the doctor away.' Which fruit fills the blank?
questions.f: Apples float in water because they are about one-quarter air!

questions.q: Butter is made by shaking and churning what?
questions.f: Shake a jar of cream long enough and you will make real butter at home!

questions.q: Which big orange food gets carved with silly faces in October?
questions.f: Pumpkins are secretly fruits — to scientists, anything with seeds inside is a fruit!

questions.q: Which small round fruits grow in big bunches on vines?
questions.f: Thousands of different grape varieties are grown around the world!

questions.q: What is bread mostly made from?
questions.f: Sliced bread was invented in 1928 — that's why we say 'the best thing since sliced bread'!

questions.q: Which frozen treat is scooped into a cone?
questions.f: Ice cream cones became a huge hit at the 1904 World's Fair in St. Louis!

questions.q: Which fruit is green on the outside and red on the inside?
questions.f: Japan grows square watermelons so they fit neatly inside refrigerators!

questions.q: Name this fruit!
questions.f: An avocado is actually a berry — one with a single giant seed!

questions.q: Which baked treat is this?
questions.f: One croissant can hide dozens of flaky, buttery layers folded inside!

questions.q: What fuzzy fruit do you see?
questions.f: Kiwifruit is named after New Zealand's fuzzy brown kiwi bird!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I start as a tiny hard kernel, then I get hot and burst into a fluffy white snack. What am I?
questions.f: Popping kernels can leap up to three feet in the air!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am made from cacao beans, I come in milk, dark, and white, and I melt in your mouth.
questions.f: Chocolate melts just below body temperature — that's why it melts in your mouth!

questions.q: Watermelons are mostly water.
questions.f: A watermelon is about 92 percent water — basically a giant juice balloon!

questions.q: Chocolate milk comes from brown cows.
questions.f: Chocolate milk is just regular milk mixed with cocoa — any color of cow works!

questions.q: French fries were invented in France.
questions.f: Many food historians say fries were first made in Belgium, not France!

questions.q: Which pancake topping is made from tree sap?
questions.f: It takes about 40 gallons of maple sap to make just one gallon of syrup!

questions.q: Bees make honey from what?
questions.f: Bees visit about two million flowers to make a single pound of honey!

questions.q: Pickles are made from which vegetable?
questions.f: Cucumbers are about 95 percent water — one of the wateriest foods you can crunch!

questions.q: Prunes are dried versions of which fruit?
questions.f: In the year 2000, America officially let prunes be renamed 'dried plums' to sound tastier!

questions.q: This shadow belongs to which food?
questions.f: Mushrooms are fungi — scientists say they are more closely related to animals than to plants!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am red and round, and though I hang out with vegetables, I am secretly a fruit. What am I?
questions.f: In 1893, America's highest court ruled tomatoes count as vegetables — for tax reasons!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am the bark of a tree, ground into a sweet brown powder for cookies and toast. What am I?
questions.f: Cinnamon bark curls itself into sticks all on its own as it dries!

questions.q: Carrots were originally purple, not orange.
questions.f: Dutch farmers bred the first popular orange carrots in the 1600s — before that, most were purple or white!

questions.q: A banana plant is a giant herb, not a tree.
questions.f: The banana plant is the world's largest herb — its 'trunk' is tightly rolled leaves, not wood!

questions.q: A red food dye called carmine is made from what surprising thing?
questions.f: Carmine comes from tiny cochineal bugs — it has colored foods and fabrics for centuries!

questions.q: Which is the world's most expensive spice?
questions.f: It takes about 150 hand-picked crocus flowers to make a single gram of saffron!

questions.q: Where does a cashew nut grow?
c: On the bottom of a cashew apple
questions.f: Each cashew apple grows exactly one cashew nut, dangling from its bottom!

questions.q: Which fruit smells so strong it is banned on trains in Singapore?
questions.f: Durian fans say it tastes like sweet custard — despite smelling like stinky socks!

questions.q: What living ingredient makes bread dough puff up?
questions.f: Yeast are tiny fungi that burp carbon dioxide bubbles into the dough!

questions.q: How many of the world's people eat rice as a main food?
questions.f: Rice is a daily staple for over half the planet — billions of bowls every day!

questions.q: What are the holes in Swiss cheese called?
questions.f: A Swiss cheese with no holes at all is called a 'blind' cheese!

questions.q: Nutmeg and which other spice grow inside the very same fruit?
questions.f: Nutmeg is the seed, and mace is the red, lacy net wrapped around it!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: My flavor comes from the seed pod of an orchid flower, and ice cream loves me. What am I?
questions.f: Vanilla is the world's second most expensive spice, right after saffron!

questions.q: Fortune cookies were invented in China.
questions.f: Fortune cookies were invented in America and are based on a Japanese cracker!

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a true berry to scientists?
questions.f: Bananas and avocados are true berries, but strawberries are berry impostors!

questions.q: Which of these snacks grows underground?
questions.f: Peanuts are not nuts at all — they are legumes, cousins of peas and beans!

questions.q: Hawaiian pizza was invented in which country?
questions.f: A Greek-born cook created Hawaiian pizza in Ontario, Canada, in 1962!

questions.q: Which of these is NOT the same plant species as cabbage?
questions.f: Broccoli, kale, cauliflower, and Brussels sprouts are all one species, bred into different shapes!

questions.q: Croissants trace back to a pastry from which country?
questions.f: The croissant's ancestor, the kipferl, came from Austria before France made it famous!

questions.q: In the 1830s, ketchup was sold as what?
questions.f: Doctors once sold tomato ketchup pills as a cure for tummy troubles!

questions.q: Which of these did the Aztecs use as money?
questions.f: In Aztec markets, a turkey could cost about 100 cacao beans!

questions.q: Which of these fruits sinks in water?
questions.f: Limes are denser than water, but lemons, apples, and oranges all float!

questions.q: Pasteurization, the process that makes milk safe, is named after a real scientist.
questions.f: Louis Pasteur discovered that gentle heating kills the germs hiding in milk and juice.

questions.q: Why does a popcorn kernel pop?
c: Water inside turns to steam and bursts it
Air leaks in until it explodes
The shell melts and flips over
questions.f: The kernel flips inside out at about 180 degrees Celsius — way hotter than boiling water!

questions.q: Why does chopping onions make you cry?
c: They release a gas that stings your eyes
Their juice splashes acid into the air
Their smell dries out your eyes
questions.f: Chill an onion in the fridge first — the cold slows the gas, so fewer tears!

questions.q: Why do chili peppers feel burning hot?
c: They burn tiny holes in your tongue
They react with saliva to make heat
questions.f: Birds cannot feel capsaicin at all, so they happily eat chilies and spread the seeds!

questions.q: Why does mint make your mouth feel cold?
c: Menthol switches on your cold sensors
It lowers your mouth's real temperature
It slows blood flow in your tongue
questions.f: Your mouth's temperature doesn't change at all — menthol just tricks your brain!

questions.q: Besides sweet, salty, sour, and bitter, what is the fifth taste?
questions.f: Umami means 'delicious taste' in Japanese and is strong in cheese, tomatoes, and soy sauce!

questions.q: Why do apple slices turn brown?
c: They react with oxygen in the air
questions.f: A splash of lemon juice slows the browning — its vitamin C blocks the oxygen reaction!

questions.q: Why can sealed honey stay good for thousands of years?
c: It is too dry and acidic for germs to grow
It is cooked at very high heat
questions.f: Archaeologists found 3,000-year-old honey in Egyptian tombs — still perfectly edible!

questions.q: Ripe bananas release which gas that ripens fruit nearby?
questions.f: Pop an unripe avocado in a paper bag with a banana and it ripens much faster!

questions.q: What turns toast golden brown?
c: Sugars and proteins reacting in the heat
questions.f: It's called the Maillard reaction — the same one that browns cookies and toasted marshmallows!

questions.q: Which animal did knights ride in jousting contests?
questions.f: Jousting horses wore their own armor and fancy colored coats too.

questions.q: What could a castle pull up to close the path across its moat?
questions.f: Heavy chains and weights lifted the drawbridge like a giant seesaw.

questions.q: On old pirate maps, what did the X mark?
questions.f: Real pirates almost never buried treasure — that idea mostly comes from storybooks!

questions.q: What did ancient Egyptians use to build the pyramids?
questions.f: The Great Pyramid holds about 2.3 million stone blocks.

questions.q: What do we call the study of things that happened long ago?
questions.f: The word history comes from an old Greek word meaning finding out.

questions.q: What special chair did kings and queens sit on?
questions.f: King Tut's golden throne was buried with him and found again about 3,000 years later.

questions.q: Baby dinosaurs hatched out of what?
questions.f: Some dinosaur eggs were bigger than footballs.

questions.q: What did knights hold in front of them for protection?
questions.f: Knights painted family symbols called coats of arms on their shields so friends could spot them.

questions.q: A knight's metal suit is called armor.
questions.f: Full armor weighed about 50 pounds, but knights could still run and climb in it.

questions.q: What kind of building is this?
questions.f: Windsor Castle is about 1,000 years old, and people still live in it today.

questions.q: Whose giant shadow is this?
questions.f: T. rex had the strongest bite of any land animal that ever lived.

questions.q: Kings and queens long ago wore this on their heads. What is it?
questions.f: The oldest crown ever found is more than 6,000 years old.

questions.q: Which Ice Age giant makes this shaggy shadow?
questions.f: Baby mammoths have been found frozen whole in the ice, fur and all.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am a giant, pointy stone building in Egypt, built for a pharaoh long ago. What am I?
questions.f: The Great Pyramid was built about 4,500 years ago.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am wrapped in cloth bandages from head to toe, and I rest in ancient Egypt. What am I?
questions.f: Ancient Egyptians also made mummies of cats, crocodiles, and even beetles.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I wear a shiny metal suit, ride a horse, and serve the king. Who am I?
questions.f: Knight training started at age seven, as a helper called a page.

questions.q: What were the kings of ancient Egypt called?
questions.f: Pharaoh means great house — the name of the palace became the name of the king.

questions.q: The Great Sphinx has a human head and the body of which animal?
questions.f: The Sphinx was carved from one single, giant piece of limestone.

questions.q: What is ancient Egypt's picture writing called?
questions.f: There are more than 700 different hieroglyph signs.

questions.q: Which country invented paper almost 2,000 years ago?
questions.f: Early Chinese paper was made from tree bark, old rags, and even fishing nets.

questions.q: Ancient Egyptians built their homes along which river?
questions.f: The Nile's yearly flood left rich black mud, so Egyptians called their home the black land.

questions.q: The very first Olympic Games were held in which country?
questions.f: Ancient Olympic champions won crowns of olive leaves, not gold medals.

questions.q: What were the Vikings' long wooden ships called?
questions.f: Longships floated in water so shallow that Vikings could sail right up onto a beach.

questions.q: Which ancient people built the Colosseum?
questions.f: The Colosseum could hold about 50,000 cheering fans.

questions.q: What is the big strong tower at the heart of a castle called?
questions.f: Many keeps had their own well inside, so defenders never ran out of drinking water.

questions.q: Some dinosaurs had feathers.
questions.f: Even some cousins of T. rex were covered in fluffy feathers.

questions.q: Humans and dinosaurs lived at the same time.
questions.f: Dinosaurs vanished about 66 million years before the first humans existed.

questions.q: Giant stone statues like this one stand on which island?
questions.f: Many of these statues have whole bodies hidden under the ground!

questions.q: Archaeologists love digging these up. What is it?
questions.f: Broken pots are an archaeologist's favorite clue, because pottery lasts thousands of years.

questions.q: What is this ancient throwing tool called?
questions.f: Boomerangs are at least 10,000 years old — King Tut even had some in his tomb.

questions.q: Ancient Egyptians adored this animal. Whose shadow is it?
questions.f: The ancient Egyptian word for cat was miu — just like meow!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am the longest wall ever built, and I stretch across China for thousands of miles. What am I?
questions.f: Counting every branch, the Great Wall runs for more than 13,000 miles.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I dig carefully in the ground to find treasures people left long ago. What is my job called?
questions.f: Archaeologists have even dug up 4,000-year-old homework written on clay tablets.

questions.q: About how long did it take to make a mummy in ancient Egypt?
questions.f: The body spent about 40 of those days drying out in a special salt called natron.

questions.q: What is fossilized dinosaur poop called?
questions.f: One T. rex coprolite found in Canada is longer than a baguette!

questions.q: Which body part did Egyptian mummy-makers pull out through the nose?
questions.f: They used a long hook, then threw the brain away because they thought it was unimportant!

questions.q: What is a scientist who studies dinosaur fossils called?
questions.f: Famous fossil hunter Mary Anning made her first huge discovery when she was only about twelve.

questions.q: What sticky food was mixed into mortar to hold the Great Wall together?
questions.f: Scientists found the sticky rice mortar is still stronger than some modern cement.

questions.q: China's famous Terracotta Army is made of thousands of what?
questions.f: Farmers digging a well found the buried army by accident in 1974 — and no two faces match.

questions.q: What frozen treat did rich ancient Romans enjoy?
questions.f: Runners raced snow down from the mountains before it could melt.

questions.q: T. rex teeth were about the size of which fruit?
questions.f: T. rex grew new teeth its whole life, so it always had spares.

questions.q: Ancient China invented this tool. What is it?
questions.f: The first Chinese compasses were shaped like soup spoons that spun on a shiny plate.

questions.q: You can see the Great Wall of China from the Moon.
questions.f: The Wall is far too thin to spot from the Moon — like trying to see a single hair from miles away.

questions.q: Vikings wore helmets with horns on them.
questions.f: Horned helmets were invented for opera costumes in the 1800s — real Vikings never wore them.

questions.q: Honey found in ancient Egyptian tombs was still good to eat.
questions.f: Honey almost never spoils, because it holds so little water that germs cannot grow in it.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I became ruler of Egypt when I was only nine, and my golden mask is famous. Who am I?
questions.f: King Tut's tomb was packed with more than 5,000 treasures, including board games.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am a dinosaur bone that slowly turned to stone over millions of years. What am I?
questions.f: It takes at least 10,000 years for a fossil to form.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a real dinosaur?
questions.f: Scientists name dozens of brand-new dinosaur species every single year.

questions.q: What were the very first wheels used for?
questions.f: Potter's wheels came first — wheels for carts showed up hundreds of years later.

questions.q: Which of these was invented in ancient China?
questions.f: The first firecrackers were pieces of bamboo that popped loudly when thrown into a fire.

questions.q: Which of these was built FIRST?
questions.f: Stonehenge is even older than Egypt's Great Pyramid.

questions.q: Which discovery finally let scholars read Egyptian hieroglyphs?
questions.f: The stone carries the same message in three different scripts, so scholars could compare them.

questions.q: Which sailors reached North America about 500 years before Columbus?
questions.f: Leif Erikson's Viking crew landed in Canada about 1,000 years ago.

questions.q: Which organ did Egyptians leave INSIDE a mummy's body?
questions.f: Egyptians believed the heart would be weighed against a feather in the afterlife.

questions.q: Marshmallows began as a sweet treat in which ancient land?
questions.f: Egyptians mixed sap from the mallow plant with honey — a treat saved for gods and royalty.

questions.q: Where did a castle toilet usually empty?
questions.f: Castle toilets were called garderobes — people hung clothes in them because the smell kept moths away!

questions.q: Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire.
questions.f: Teaching began at Oxford before the year 1100 — the Aztec Empire only began in 1428.

questions.q: Woolly mammoths were still alive when the Great Pyramid was built.
questions.f: The very last mammoths lived on a remote Arctic island called Wrangel Island.

questions.q: King Tut's special dagger was made from iron that came from where?
questions.f: Iron from space holds extra nickel — that clue helped scientists crack the mystery.

questions.q: The word 'salary' comes from the Latin word for which item?
questions.f: Salt was precious long ago because it kept food from rotting.

questions.q: The first vending machine, invented about 2,000 years ago, dispensed what?
questions.f: Greek inventor Hero built it — drop in a coin, and water poured out for temple visitors.

questions.q: How long did the Great Pyramid stay the tallest building on Earth?
questions.f: A cathedral in England finally passed it in the 1300s.

questions.q: What was Stone Age chewing gum made from?
questions.f: Ancient gum lumps still show the tooth marks of Stone Age kids.

questions.q: How do the giant stones of Machu Picchu stay in place?
c: They fit together perfectly with no cement
questions.f: The stones fit so tightly that even a knife blade cannot slide between them.

questions.q: Why does the Leaning Tower of Pisa lean?
c: It was built on soft ground that sank
Builders read the plans upside down
questions.f: It started leaning before it was even finished — and builders kept going for about 200 years.

questions.q: Cleopatra lived closer in time to which of these?
c: The building of the Great Pyramid
The taming of the first horses
The painting of the Lascaux cave
questions.f: The pyramids were already about 2,500 years old when Cleopatra ruled Egypt.

questions.q: T. rex lived closer in time to you than to Stegosaurus.
questions.f: More than 80 million years separate Stegosaurus from T. rex, but only 66 million separate T. rex from you.

questions.q: Suitcases with wheels were invented after astronauts landed on the Moon.
questions.f: The wheeled suitcase was patented in 1970 — one year after the Moon landing.

questions.q: How many wheels does a tricycle have?
questions.f: "Tri" means three — count the wheels next time you see one!

questions.q: Which flying machine is this?
questions.f: A helicopter's spinning blades are called rotors.

questions.q: Which machine blasts off into space?
questions.f: Rockets must reach about 28,000 km/h to stay in orbit around Earth!

questions.q: True or false: A submarine can travel underwater.
questions.f: Some submarines can stay underwater for months at a time!

questions.q: What do you squeeze on a bicycle's handlebars to stop?
questions.f: Bicycle brakes squeeze the wheel to slow it down using friction.

questions.q: Which vehicle is this?
questions.f: Some freight trains stretch longer than 100 cars — over a mile long!

questions.q: What do you wear in a car to stay safe?
questions.f: Volvo gave away its seatbelt invention for free so every car could use it.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I have a loud siren and a long ladder, and I rush to help when there is a fire. What am I?
questions.f: The tallest fire truck ladders can stretch higher than a ten-story building.

questions.q: True or false: A helicopter can hover, staying in one spot in the air.
questions.f: That's how helicopters rescue people from mountains and stormy seas.

questions.q: Which machine do you see?
questions.f: Tractors have huge back wheels so they don't sink into soft, muddy fields.

questions.q: Which kitchen machine keeps food cold?
questions.f: Before refrigerators, people kept food cold with big blocks of ice delivered to their homes.

questions.q: What does a boat travel on?
questions.f: Giant cruise ships float even though they weigh more than 100,000 tons!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: Beep beep! I am long, I am often yellow, and I carry children to school every morning. What am I?
questions.f: In the United States, school buses are yellow because that color is easy to spot at dawn and dusk.

questions.q: Which tool twists screws into wood?
questions.f: A screw is secretly a simple machine — it's a ramp wrapped around a pole!

questions.q: What is this ride called?
questions.f: The first Ferris wheel, built in 1893, could carry more than 2,000 people at once!

questions.q: True or false: Trains drive on ordinary roads like cars do.
questions.f: Trains roll on smooth steel rails — steel wheels on steel rails make very little friction.

questions.q: What lights up the road at the front of a car at night?
questions.f: The first car headlights burned a gas called acetylene, like little lanterns.

questions.q: Which machine cleans your dirty clothes?
questions.f: Before washing machines, laundry was scrubbed by hand and could take a whole day.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am round, I spin, and I help bikes, cars, and skateboards roll along. What am I?
questions.f: People invented the wheel more than 5,000 years ago — first spinning it to make pottery!

questions.q: Which flying machine did the Wright brothers build?
questions.f: Their very first flight in 1903 lasted just 12 seconds.

questions.q: What does a car's speedometer measure?
questions.f: A cheetah can hit 100 km/h — faster than cars are allowed to drive in most cities!

questions.q: What kind of simple machine is a seesaw?
questions.f: A seesaw tips back and forth on a balance point called a fulcrum.

questions.q: True or false: Maglev trains float above their tracks using magnets.
questions.f: With no wheels touching the track, a maglev ride is smooth and whisper-quiet.

questions.q: Which simple machine uses a wheel and a rope to lift heavy loads?
questions.f: Flagpoles use pulleys so you can raise a flag to the top without climbing.

questions.q: What is this ship part called?
questions.f: An anchor digs into the seabed to stop a ship from drifting away.

questions.q: What makes a sailboat move?
questions.f: Sailboats can even travel toward the wind by zigzagging — sailors call it tacking!

questions.q: Which digging machine has a long arm with a scoop called a bucket?
questions.f: An excavator can spin its whole cab in a circle without moving its tracks.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am a tall machine with a long arm. I lift heavy loads to the tops of tall buildings. What am I?
questions.f: Tower cranes grow taller by adding new pieces to their own middles!

questions.q: True or false: A unicycle has two wheels.
questions.f: "Uni" means one — riders balance on a single wheel, and some even ride mountain trails!

questions.q: Zippers first became popular on which clothing item?
questions.f: A boot company named them "zippers" in 1923 after the zzzip sound they made.

questions.q: What does a car's GPS help the driver do?
questions.f: GPS signals come from satellites flying about 20,000 kilometers above your head.

questions.q: What do you call a person who flies an airplane?
questions.f: Big passenger planes carry two pilots, so one can rest on long flights.

questions.q: Which invention lets you talk with someone far away?
questions.f: Alexander Graham Bell made the first telephone call in 1876 — to his helper in the next room.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: Vroom! I have two wheels and an engine, and my riders wear helmets. What am I?
questions.f: The fastest motorcycles can zoom along at over 300 km/h.

questions.q: Which train runs through tunnels under big cities?
questions.f: London opened the world's first underground railway in 1863 — pulled by steam engines!

questions.q: What is this mountain ride called?
questions.f: Cable cars hang from strong steel ropes and can glide high over valleys.

questions.q: In what year did the Wright brothers make the first airplane flight?
questions.f: That first flight covered only 120 feet — shorter than a jumbo jet's wingspan!

questions.q: What did old steam trains burn to boil water into steam?
questions.f: A crew member called the fireman shoveled coal into the firebox all day long.

questions.q: How fast did Japan's maglev train go in its record test run?
questions.f: That 2015 run hit 603 km/h — much faster than a Formula 1 race car.

questions.q: True or false: A Boeing 747 jumbo jet has four engines.
questions.f: The 747 was so huge that people nicknamed it the Queen of the Skies.

questions.q: What does a car's odometer count?
questions.f: One Volvo's odometer passed 3 million miles — the world record for a car!

questions.q: What machine is this, circling high above Earth?
questions.f: Thousands of satellites orbit Earth, beaming down TV, GPS, and weather pictures.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I dive deep under the sea on purpose, then blow air into my tanks to float back up. What am I?
questions.f: Submarines let water into tanks to sink, then push it out with air to rise.

questions.q: What kind of simple machine is a ramp?
questions.f: Ancient Egyptians likely used giant ramps to haul stones up the pyramids.

questions.q: Which planet do the robot rovers Curiosity and Perseverance explore?
questions.f: Perseverance brought along a mini helicopter named Ingenuity that flew on Mars!

questions.q: What does an airplane's "black box" record?
questions.f: Black boxes are actually painted bright orange so searchers can find them!

questions.q: True or false: One of the first escalators was a ride at an amusement park.
questions.f: In 1896, visitors at Coney Island rode Jesse Reno's moving stairway just for fun.

questions.q: What is this machine that tells cars when to stop and go?
questions.f: The first electric traffic light started working in 1914 in Cleveland, Ohio.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I glide on a cushion of air, so I can travel over land and water. What am I?
questions.f: Giant hovercraft once carried cars and passengers across the English Channel.

questions.q: How many pedals does a car with automatic gears have?
questions.f: Cars with manual gears add a third pedal called the clutch.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a simple machine?
questions.f: The six simple machines are the lever, pulley, wheel and axle, inclined plane, wedge, and screw.

questions.q: Which of these flew first in history?
questions.f: The first balloon passengers in 1783 were a sheep, a duck, and a rooster!

questions.q: Which of these aircraft has no engine?
questions.f: Gliders ride rising columns of warm air called thermals, just like eagles do.

questions.q: Which of these travels the fastest?
questions.f: A passenger jet cruises at about 900 km/h — most of the way to the speed of sound.

questions.q: True or false: A moving bicycle balances more easily than one standing still.
questions.f: The spinning wheels plus tiny steering corrections keep a rolling bike upright.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a real flying machine?
questions.f: Blimps really do fly — they float using helium, the same gas in party balloons.

questions.q: Which of these tools works as a wedge?
questions.f: A wedge's thin edge pushes things apart — even your front teeth cut like little wedges.

questions.q: Which of these trains is the fastest?
questions.f: Maglev is short for "magnetic levitation" — and levitation means floating!

questions.q: True or false: Factory robots were first used less than ten years ago.
questions.f: The first factory robot, Unimate, started work at a car plant way back in 1961.

questions.q: Which of these can a helicopter NOT do?
c: Fly faster than a jet plane
questions.f: Helicopters top out near 400 km/h, while passenger jets cruise around 900.

questions.q: Whose shadow is this?
questions.f: The word "robot" comes from a Czech word meaning "hard work."

questions.q: Why do helicopters have a small rotor on the tail?
c: To stop the body from spinning around
questions.f: Without the tail rotor, the body would spin the opposite way from the main blades.

questions.q: Why do rocket engines carry their own oxygen?
c: Fuel cannot burn without oxygen, and space has none
Oxygen keeps the fuel tanks cold
Oxygen stops the engines from rusting
questions.f: Fire needs oxygen, so rockets bring their own supply to burn fuel in airless space.

questions.q: Which force pushes up on a boat and keeps it floating?
questions.f: A ship floats by pushing aside water that weighs as much as the whole ship — Archimedes figured this out over 2,000 years ago.

questions.q: How do airplane wings lift the plane up?
c: They push air down, so the air pushes them up
They are filled with floaty helium
questions.f: That push-back rule is Newton's third law: every action has an equal and opposite reaction.

questions.q: What is the fastest machine humans have ever built?
questions.f: The Parker Solar Probe swoops past the Sun at more than 600,000 km/h!

questions.q: True or false: Some robots can do backflips.
questions.f: A robot called Atlas can run, leap between boxes, and land backflips like a gymnast.

questions.q: Which spinning device helps rockets and ships stay steady?
questions.f: Your smartphone has tiny gyroscopes inside that sense every time you tilt it.

questions.q: Which invention made skyscrapers practical by carrying people to high floors?
questions.f: Elisha Otis proved his elevator was safe in the 1850s by cutting its rope in front of a crowd — it didn't fall.

questions.q: What gives a hybrid car its power?
c: A gasoline engine plus an electric motor
questions.f: Hybrids recharge their batteries every time they brake — it's called regenerative braking.

questions.q: What powers the International Space Station?
questions.f: The station's solar wings stretch about as long as a football field.

questions.q: How many strings does a violin have?
questions.f: A violin has no frets — players find every single note just by feel!

questions.q: Which instrument is this?
questions.f: A full-size piano has 88 keys — 52 white and 36 black.

questions.q: Singers hold this on stage. What is it?
questions.f: A microphone turns your voice into electricity, then speakers turn it back into BIG sound!

questions.q: Which instrument is this?
questions.f: Most guitars have 6 strings, but a tiny ukulele has only 4.

questions.q: Which instrument is this?
questions.f: Trumpet players buzz their lips into the mouthpiece to make the sound.

questions.q: What do you usually use to play a drum?
questions.f: Drummers can also play with wire brushes or just their bare hands.

questions.q: In ballet, what is the fluffy skirt called?
questions.f: A professional tutu can have ten or more layers of stiff netting!

questions.q: Which part of your body makes the sound in tap dancing?
questions.f: Tap shoes have metal plates on the bottom that click and clack on the floor.

questions.q: Which instrument do you shake to make music?
questions.f: Maracas are often filled with seeds or tiny beads that rattle inside.

questions.q: How do you play a flute?
questions.f: A flute makes sound the same way blowing across a bottle top does.

questions.q: What is a group of people singing together called?
questions.f: When choir singers breathe and sing together, their heartbeats can start beating in time too!

questions.q: Which animal makes its buzzing sound by beating its wings super fast?
questions.f: A bee's wings beat about 200 times every second — that's what makes the buzz!

questions.q: What do you call a soft song sung to help babies fall asleep?
questions.f: 'Rock-a-bye Baby' has been sung to sleepy babies for more than 250 years.

questions.q: Which body part do you use to whistle a tune?
questions.f: The loudest whistlers on Earth can whistle louder than a lawnmower!

questions.q: You play a piano by blowing into it.
questions.f: Pressing a piano key makes a tiny hammer jump up and hit strings inside.

questions.q: Bigger drums make lower, deeper sounds.
questions.f: The giant timpani drums in an orchestra can even be tuned with a foot pedal.

questions.q: A xylophone is played by hitting it with mallets.
questions.f: 'Xylophone' means 'wood sound' in Greek.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am a metal shape with three sides. Tap me with a small rod and I go ting! What am I?
questions.f: The triangle looks easy, but playing your one 'ting' at exactly the right moment is tricky!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: Shake me and I jingle! Tap my skin and I thump! Dancers love to rattle me. What am I?
questions.f: A tambourine's little jingling discs have a special name — zills!

questions.q: What do you call the words of a song?
questions.f: The word 'lyrics' comes from the lyre, a small harp played in ancient Greece.

questions.q: Which country is the home of flamenco dancing?
questions.f: Flamenco dancers stamp their heels so fast it sounds like a drumroll.

questions.q: Which Australian instrument is a long wooden tube you blow into?
questions.f: Some didgeridoo players breathe in through their nose while still blowing out — so the drone never stops!

questions.q: The tabla from India is a pair of what?
questions.f: Tabla players learn spoken rhythm syllables called 'bols' before they even start drumming.

questions.q: What is the person who leads an orchestra called?
questions.f: Conductors wave a thin stick called a baton to keep everyone playing together.

questions.q: Hula dancing comes from which islands?
questions.f: In hula, the dancer's hands help tell the story of the song.

questions.q: Which instrument do Scottish pipers squeeze under their arm?
questions.f: Pipers fill the bag with air, then squeeze it out through the pipes to keep the sound going.

questions.q: Which dance style began on the streets of New York City?
questions.f: Breakdancing even became an Olympic sport at the Paris 2024 Games!

questions.q: What do you call a person who writes music?
questions.f: Mozart began composing his own music when he was just five years old.

questions.q: Which big brass instrument plays the lowest notes in the band?
questions.f: A big tuba can weigh about as much as a car tire!

questions.q: Which instrument is this?
questions.f: A violin bow is strung with real horsehair — from a horse's tail!

questions.q: Which squeeze-box instrument is this?
questions.f: Accordion players squeeze air through the middle while pressing buttons and keys on both ends.

questions.q: Which dance style uses these special shoes?
questions.f: Ballerinas balance on the very tips of their toes in hard-toed pointe shoes.

questions.q: A ukulele is smaller than a guitar.
questions.f: 'Ukulele' means 'jumping flea' in Hawaiian!

questions.q: The harp is played by hitting it with sticks.
questions.f: Harpists pluck up to 47 strings with their fingers — that's a lot of strings to know!

questions.q: The flute is the loudest instrument in the orchestra.
questions.f: The loudest sounds in an orchestra usually come from the brass and the drums.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am a long shiny horn. Slide my arm in and out to change my notes. What am I?
questions.f: The trombone is the only common brass instrument with a slide instead of buttons.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: Shout my name into a canyon and I will shout it right back at you. What am I?
questions.f: An echo is your own sound bouncing off something hard and racing back to your ears.

questions.q: Which instruments make up a string quartet?
c: Two violins, a viola and a cello
A violin, viola, cello and double bass
questions.f: The viola looks like a violin's slightly bigger sibling and sounds a little deeper.

questions.q: The sitar is a long-necked string instrument from which country?
questions.f: A sitar has extra 'sympathetic' strings that ring all on their own when the others are played.

questions.q: Which instrument does the whole orchestra tune to before a concert?
questions.f: The oboe plays one long note called 'A', and every other player matches it.

questions.q: What is the biggest string instrument in the orchestra?
questions.f: Some double basses stand over six feet tall — taller than most grown-ups!

questions.q: 'Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star' shares its tune with which other song?
questions.f: 'Baa Baa Black Sheep' uses the very same melody too — three songs, one tune!

questions.q: The tango dance comes from which country?
questions.f: Tango bands feature the bandoneón, a squeezebox that looks like a small accordion.

questions.q: Which instrument is this?
questions.f: The saxophone is named after its inventor — a man called Adolphe Sax!

questions.q: Which instrument is this?
questions.f: A banjo's body is like a drum — its strings stretch over a tight skin, giving it that twang.

questions.q: Sound travels faster in water than in air.
questions.f: Sound zips through water about four times faster than through air!

questions.q: A cricket chirps by rubbing its wings together.
questions.f: Crickets chirp faster in warm weather — you can guess the temperature by counting chirps!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I fit in your pocket. Blow in and out across my little holes and I play a tune. What am I?
questions.f: The harmonica is the best-selling musical instrument in the world!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I rumble across the sky right after a bright flash of lightning. What sound am I?
questions.f: You see lightning before you hear thunder because light travels much faster than sound.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT in the brass family?
questions.f: The clarinet is a woodwind — a thin cane reed buzzes to make its sound, not your lips.

questions.q: Which of these instruments is NOT played with a bow?
questions.f: The harp is plucked — and a concert harp has seven foot pedals to change its notes!

questions.q: Which instrument plays the HIGHEST notes in the orchestra?
questions.f: 'Piccolo' means 'small' in Italian — it's a mini flute about half a flute's size.

questions.q: Which Brazilian art form mixes dance with martial-arts moves?
questions.f: Capoeira is done to live music, including a bow-shaped instrument called a berimbau.

questions.q: In a waltz, how many beats are in each measure?
questions.f: That ONE-two-three rhythm is why waltzing couples seem to glide around in circles.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a percussion instrument?
questions.f: Percussion instruments make sound when struck — the flute only needs your breath.

questions.q: The haka, a powerful stomping chant-dance, comes from which country?
questions.f: New Zealand's rugby team performs a Māori haka before every international match.

questions.q: Which instrument is played WITHOUT touching it at all?
questions.f: Theremin players wave their hands near two antennas to change the pitch and the volume.

questions.q: Which dance style keeps the arms held straight down at the sides?
questions.f: Irish dancers' legs fly while their upper bodies stay perfectly still — like in Riverdance!

questions.q: The saxophone belongs to the brass family.
questions.f: It's made of metal, but its buzzing cane reed makes it a woodwind!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: In a choir, I am the lowest grown-up singing voice, and my name rhymes with 'race'. What am I?
questions.f: Voice types from low to high are bass, tenor, alto and soprano.

questions.q: Why can't sound travel through outer space?
c: There is no air to carry the vibrations
The stars soak up the sound
questions.f: Space is a vacuum — with nothing to vibrate, even a huge explosion would be totally silent.

questions.q: What makes a note sound HIGHER in pitch?
questions.f: A tiny piccolo shakes the air far faster than a giant tuba — that's why it sounds so high.

questions.q: Which unit measures how LOUD a sound is?
questions.f: A jet taking off is about 140 decibels — loud enough to hurt your ears in seconds.

questions.q: Why do longer, thicker strings make lower notes?
questions.f: That's why the towering double bass sounds deep and the tiny violin sounds high.

questions.q: Beethoven kept composing great music even after losing what?
questions.f: Beethoven could still feel the music as vibrations through the piano and the floor.

questions.q: What is a gamelan, played in Indonesia?
c: An orchestra of gongs and metal chimes
questions.f: Each gamelan set is tuned only to itself, so its instruments stay together for life.

questions.q: What is the largest musical instrument in the world?
questions.f: The Boardwalk Hall organ in the USA has more than 33,000 pipes!

questions.q: Why does the same note sound different on a flute and a violin?
c: Each instrument adds its own mix of overtones
questions.f: That sound fingerprint is called 'timbre' — say it 'TAM-ber'.

questions.q: About how fast does sound travel through air?
questions.f: Supersonic jets outrun their own sound — the boom arrives after they've already passed!

questions.q: Sound travels faster than light.
questions.f: Light is nearly 900,000 times faster — that's why you see fireworks before you hear them.

questions.q: How many horns does a unicorn have?
questions.f: The unicorn is the official national animal of Scotland!

questions.q: Which legendary creature is this?
questions.f: The flag of Wales has a big red dragon right in the middle of it.
