questions.q: In stories, what do dragons love to sleep on?
questions.f: In the old tale of Beowulf, a dragon got furious when just one golden cup went missing from its pile!

questions.q: Which tiny winged creature is this?
questions.f: In Irish legends, fairies live in grassy mounds called fairy forts — many farmers still leave them untouched.

questions.q: What does the tooth fairy swap for coins under your pillow?
questions.f: In Spain, a little mouse named Ratoncito Pérez collects the teeth instead of a fairy!

questions.q: Thor, the Norse god of thunder, carries a magic what?
questions.f: Thor's hammer, Mjolnir, always flies back to his hand after he throws it!

questions.q: A cyclops is a giant with three eyes.
questions.f: A cyclops has just one big eye, right in the middle of its forehead.

questions.q: Where does a leprechaun hide his pot of gold?
c: At the end of a rainbow
questions.f: Irish legends say leprechauns work as shoemakers — tap, tap, tap!

questions.q: Who is this magical wish-granter?
questions.f: Genie stories come from old Arabic tales, where they are called jinn.

questions.q: In fairy tales, who hides under bridges and growls at travelers?
questions.f: In Norwegian folklore, trolls turn to stone if sunlight touches them!

questions.q: Bigfoot is a legendary creature famous for leaving giant what?
questions.f: Bigfoot's other name, Sasquatch, comes from a Native American word.

questions.q: Whose magical shadow is this?
questions.f: A unicorn's horn was called an alicorn, and legends said it could clean poisoned water.

questions.q: What did legendary knights wear to protect their bodies?
questions.f: A full suit of armor weighed about as much as a seven-year-old kid!

questions.q: In legends, elves have pointed ears.
questions.f: In Iceland, elves are called the huldufólk — the 'hidden people.'

questions.q: What does a wizard wave to cast a spell?
questions.f: The word 'wizard' comes from an old word meaning 'wise.'

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: In 'Jack and the Beanstalk,' the giant lives in a castle high above the clouds.
questions.say: Fee fi fo fum! I am huge, and I live above the clouds at the top of a beanstalk. What am I?

questions.q: In old legends, what happens to a werewolf at the full moon?
c: It changes from a person into a wolf
It falls asleep for a week
questions.f: The word 'werewolf' means 'man-wolf' in Old English.

questions.q: Which Greek god rules the sky and throws lightning bolts?
questions.f: Zeus's lightning bolts were forged by one-eyed giants called Cyclopes.

questions.q: Ganesha, the gentle Hindu god of new beginnings, has the head of which animal?
questions.f: Ganesha's favorite treat is a sweet dumpling called a modak.

questions.q: In Norse myths, the god Loki is best known as a what?
questions.f: Loki was a shape-shifter who could turn into a fly, a salmon, or even a horse.

questions.q: What did young King Arthur pull from a stone to prove he was king?
questions.f: Arthur's legendary sword was named Excalibur.

questions.q: Which Greek god of the sea carries this?
questions.f: The Romans called Poseidon 'Neptune' — the blue planet is named after him!

questions.q: The Sphinx of Greek myth had a lion's body and the head of a what?
questions.f: The Sphinx loved stumping travelers with tricky riddles.

questions.q: Medusa had living snakes instead of hair.
questions.f: In the myths, looking straight at Medusa would turn you to stone.

questions.q: A famous monster is said to live in which Scottish lake?
questions.f: The monster's nickname is Nessie, and scientists have searched for her with sonar and underwater robots.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: Kraken legends were likely inspired by real giant squid, which can grow longer than a school bus!
questions.say: I am a huge sea monster with long, long arms that wrap around whole ships. What am I?

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: Old legends said griffins guarded mountains full of gold.
questions.say: My front half is a mighty eagle and my back half is a lion. What am I?

questions.q: In Norse myth, a magical bridge to Asgard looked like this. What was it?
questions.f: The Norse called this glowing bridge Bifrost.

questions.q: In Chinese stories, dragons bring good luck.
questions.f: Chinese emperors wore dragon robes as a symbol of their power.

questions.q: What magical object does the queen in Snow White speak to?
questions.f: Snow White's story was written down by the Brothers Grimm over 200 years ago.

questions.q: Legendary hero Robin Hood lived in which English forest?
questions.f: Sherwood Forest is real, and its famous Major Oak tree is over 800 years old!

questions.q: How many heads does Cerberus, the giant guard dog of Greek myth, have?
questions.f: In one story, the hero Orpheus made Cerberus doze off just by playing beautiful music.

questions.q: What did the Norse god Odin trade for a drink from the well of wisdom?
questions.f: Odin also had two ravens, Huginn and Muninn — 'Thought' and 'Memory' — who flew the world gathering news.

questions.q: Everything King Midas touched turned into what?
questions.f: Even Midas's breakfast turned to gold, so he begged for the magic to be undone!

questions.q: Where did the Minotaur, half man and half bull, live?
questions.f: The hero Theseus escaped the maze by following a trail of thread back to the exit.

questions.q: Which day of the week is named after the thunder god Thor?
questions.f: Wednesday is named for the Norse god Odin — it means 'Woden's day.'

questions.q: In Greek myth, Icarus flew with wings made of feathers and what?
questions.f: He flew too close to the sun, the wax melted, and he splashed into the sea now called the Icarian Sea.

questions.q: What was the special food of the Greek gods called?
questions.f: The gods washed it down with a magical drink called nectar.

questions.q: How did Greek soldiers finally sneak inside the city of Troy?
c: Hiding inside a giant wooden horse
questions.f: Today, a sneaky computer virus is still called a 'Trojan horse.'

questions.q: In Japanese folklore, kitsune are magical what?
questions.f: The oldest and wisest kitsune were said to grow nine tails!

questions.q: Long ago, traders sold narwhal tusks and called them unicorn horns.
questions.f: Some 'unicorn horns' sold for more than their weight in gold!

questions.q: The hero Hercules had to complete twenty impossible tasks.
questions.f: It was twelve labors — for one, he cleaned giant stables in a single day by rerouting a whole river!

questions.q: In Roman legend, this animal cared for the twins Romulus and Remus. What is it?
questions.f: The twins grew up to found Rome, which is named after Romulus.

questions.q: This bird was the special symbol of which Greek goddess of wisdom?
questions.f: The city of Athens in Greece is named after her.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: Anansi's stories traveled across the ocean and are still told in the Caribbean today.
questions.say: I am a clever spider from West African stories, famous for my tricks. Who am I?

questions.q: Which of these mythical creatures is NOT part lion?
questions.f: The Minotaur is part bull — but the Chimera mixed a lion, a goat, AND a snake in one body!

questions.q: What did the Romans call the Greek god Zeus?
questions.f: Most planets are named after Roman gods — Jupiter, king of the gods, got the biggest one.

questions.q: Which hero sailed off on a quest for the Golden Fleece?
questions.f: Jason's ship was called the Argo, so his crew were the Argonauts.

questions.q: Which animals pulled Thor's flying chariot across the sky?
questions.f: Thor could cook his two goats for dinner, and by morning his hammer brought them back, good as new!

questions.q: What happened to Arachne after her weaving contest with the goddess Athena?
c: She was turned into a spider
questions.f: That is why spiders and their relatives are called 'arachnids' today!

questions.q: The snowy Yeti of the Himalayas is also known as the what?
questions.f: Yeti stories come from the high Himalayas, home of Mount Everest.

questions.q: Which small animal does the elephant-headed god Ganesha ride?
questions.f: The story teaches that even the smallest helper can carry the greatest load.

questions.q: In Greek myth, Atlas held the Earth on his shoulders.
questions.f: Atlas actually held up the SKY — but statues often show a globe, which is why map books are called atlases.

questions.q: The Great Sphinx statue in Egypt is longer than a basketball court.
questions.f: The Great Sphinx is about 73 meters long and was carved from a single mass of limestone.

questions.q: Legends surround these giant stone statues. Where do they stand?
questions.f: Scientists showed the statues could be 'walked' upright across the island using ropes!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: Heimdall's hearing was so sharp he could even hear wool growing on sheep!
questions.say: I guard a rainbow bridge, and my ears are so sharp I can hear grass grow. Which Norse god am I?

questions.q: In the original Greek story, Pandora opened a what?
questions.f: A translation mix-up centuries later turned Pandora's jar into the famous 'box.'

questions.q: Why do we call someone's weak spot their 'Achilles heel'?
c: Achilles could only be harmed on his heel
Achilles lost his sandal in a race
questions.f: His mother dipped baby Achilles in a magic river while holding his heel — the one spot the water never touched.

questions.q: Nike, whose name a sports brand borrowed, was the Greek goddess of what?
questions.f: A famous winged statue of Nike stands in the Louvre museum in Paris.

questions.q: In Norse myth, what is Yggdrasil?
c: A giant tree connecting the nine worlds
A wolf as big as a mountain
A hall with a golden roof
questions.f: A squirrel named Ratatoskr runs up and down Yggdrasil carrying messages — mostly insults!

questions.q: Which real animal's skull may have started the one-eyed cyclops legend?
questions.f: The big hole in the skull's middle — really for the trunk — looked just like one giant eye socket.

questions.q: Which civilization worshipped Quetzalcoatl, the feathered serpent?
questions.f: His name comes from the quetzal, a bird with brilliant shimmering green feathers.

questions.q: How do Chinese dragons differ from European dragons in most legends?
questions.f: Chinese dragons were kind water spirits who brought rain for the crops.

questions.q: Stories of a great flood appear in myths from many parts of the world.
questions.f: Ancient Greece, India, and the Maya all told their own great-flood tales.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: Egyptians believed Ra sailed a night boat through the dark, then rose again every dawn.
questions.say: Each day I sail my shining boat across the sky, carrying the sun. Which Egyptian god am I?

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: Some Pacific Northwest legends say the Thunderbird was so huge it could carry a whale in its claws!
questions.say: When I flap my giant wings, thunder booms, and lightning flashes from my eyes. What am I?

questions.q: How many sides does a square have?
questions.f: A square's four sides are all exactly the same length — that's what makes it a square!

questions.q: What number comes right after 9?
questions.f: Ten is the first number that needs two digits to be written!

questions.q: How many things make a pair?
questions.f: The word 'pair' comes from a Latin word meaning 'equal things' — like two matching socks!

questions.q: Which shape has no corners at all?
questions.f: Every point on a circle is exactly the same distance from its middle.

questions.q: Which number means 'nothing at all'?
questions.f: The word 'zero' came from the Arabic word 'sifr' — which also gave us the word 'cipher'!

questions.q: How many wheels does a tricycle have?
questions.f: 'Tri' means three — that's why triangle, tricycle, and triceratops all start the same way!

questions.q: What is one less than 100?
questions.f: 99 is the very biggest number you can write with just two digits!

questions.q: Which of these numbers is odd?
questions.f: Odd numbers end in 1, 3, 5, 7, or 9 — they always leave one lonely leftover when shared by two.

questions.q: What is 10 minus 1?
questions.f: Nine is the biggest number you can write with a single digit!

questions.q: Bizzy counts by fives: 5, 10, 15 … what comes next?
questions.f: Counting by fives is easy to spot — the numbers always end in 5 or 0!

questions.q: Which of these numbers is the biggest?
questions.f: Swap the digits of 15 and you get 51 — in numbers, order matters a lot!

questions.q: Six is more than nine.
questions.f: Nine is bigger — but write a 6 upside down and it magically turns into a 9!

questions.q: Two hands have ten fingers altogether.
questions.f: People probably started counting in tens because we carry ten fingers everywhere we go!

questions.q: The number 5 is an even number.
questions.f: Five is odd — share 5 cookies between two friends and one cookie is always left over!

questions.q: How many fingers is this hand showing?
questions.f: A 'high five' is named after these five fingers!

questions.q: What is this shape called?
questions.f: 'Triangle' means 'three angles' — count its three pointy corners!

questions.q: What number is this?
questions.f: Teachers use this 100 symbol to mean a perfect score!

questions.q: What time does this clock show?
questions.f: The short hand points to the hour and the long hand points to the minutes.

questions.q: Listen! Which number does Bizzy say?
questions.say: Listen closely! The number is fifteen. Fifteen! Which number did you hear?
questions.f: Fifteen and fifty sound almost the same — but 'teen' secretly means 'add ten'!

questions.q: What do we call 100 years?
questions.f: 'Century' comes from centum, Latin for one hundred — same as centipede, the 'hundred-footed' bug!

questions.q: What is a shape with five sides called?
questions.f: The Pentagon building in the USA has exactly five sides — that's how it got its name!

questions.q: What comes next: 10, 20, 30, …?
questions.f: When you count by tens, only the first digit changes — 1, 2, 3, 4!

questions.q: What is half of 50?
questions.f: 25 is a quarter of 100 — four 25s snap together to make 100, like four quarters make a dollar!

questions.q: What is 9 + 9?
questions.f: Doubling is speedy math — 9 + 9 is just one less than 10 + 10!

questions.q: A rectangle always has four right angles.
questions.f: 'Rect' comes from a Latin word meaning 'right' — a rectangle is full of right angles!

questions.q: There are 100 centimeters in one meter.
questions.f: 'Centi' means one hundredth — a centimeter is one hundredth of a meter!

questions.q: What is the shape of this sign called?
questions.f: Stop signs have 8 sides so drivers can recognize the shape even when snow covers the words!

questions.q: What number is on this pool ball?
questions.f: In pool, the black 8-ball must be sunk last — knock it in early and you lose!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's flower count!
questions.say: Bizzy visited six flowers this morning and five more this afternoon. How many flowers in all?
questions.f: Eleven comes from an old English word meaning 'one left over' after counting to ten!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's week puzzle!
questions.say: A week has seven days. How many days are in two weeks?
questions.f: Two weeks is also called a fortnight — short for 'fourteen nights'!

questions.q: A triangle's three angles always add up to how many degrees?
questions.f: Skinny, wide, or lopsided — every triangle's angles total exactly 180 degrees!

questions.q: What number does the Roman numeral L stand for?
questions.f: Roman letters I, V, X, L, C, D, M stand for 1, 5, 10, 50, 100, 500, and 1,000.

questions.q: How many years are in a millennium?
questions.f: 'Mille' means thousand in Latin — that's why a millipede's name claims a thousand feet!

questions.q: What do we call 20 of something?
questions.f: Abraham Lincoln's famous 'four score and seven years' was a fancy way to say 87 years!

questions.q: How many dots are on a whole six-sided die?
questions.f: Opposite faces of a die always add up to 7 — check it: 6 and 1, 5 and 2, 4 and 3!

questions.q: How many degrees are in a right angle?
questions.f: A right angle is exactly the corner of a book — a perfect 90-degree turn.

questions.q: What is 12 × 12?
questions.f: 144 has a special name — a 'gross' — because it's a dozen dozens!

questions.q: What do we call one thousand thousands?
questions.f: Counting to a million out loud, one number every second, would take more than 11 days nonstop!

questions.q: What is 7 × 8?
questions.f: This one trips up grown-ups — remember 5, 6, 7, 8: 56 = 7 × 8!

questions.q: A hexagon has more sides than an octagon.
questions.f: Hexa means six and octa means eight — think of an octopus and its eight arms!

questions.q: There are 1,000 grams in a kilogram.
questions.f: 'Kilo' always means one thousand — kilometer, kilogram, even kilobyte!

questions.q: What math operation does this symbol mean?
questions.f: The division symbol has a fancy name — it's called an obelus!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's animal math!
questions.say: An octopus has eight arms and a spider has eight legs. How many arms and legs is that altogether?
questions.f: Doubles are speedy math — 8 + 8 = 16, two whole spiders' worth of legs!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am an odd number. But take away one of my letters and I become even. What number am I?
questions.f: Take the S off SEVEN and you're left with EVEN!

questions.q: What comes next in the pattern 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, …?
questions.f: That's the Fibonacci sequence — add the last two numbers — and sunflower seeds spiral in it!

questions.q: Which Roman numeral stands for the biggest number?
questions.f: M means 1,000 — the year 2026 written in Roman numerals is MMXXVI!

questions.q: What is a shape with 12 sides called?
questions.f: Some countries mint 12-sided coins — the British one-pound coin is a dodecagon!

questions.q: Which of these is a prime number?
questions.f: Cicadas hide underground for 17 years — scientists think the prime number helps them dodge predators!

questions.q: How many degrees make a full circle?
questions.f: The Babylonians picked 360 because it divides evenly by 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and lots more!

questions.q: Which of these numbers is a palindrome — the same forwards and backwards?
questions.f: 121 is also 11 × 11 — multiply 11 by itself and the digits come out mirrored!

questions.q: Tom is taller than Sam. Sam is taller than Joe. Who is tallest?
c: They are all the same height
questions.f: That's called transitive reasoning — the same logic trick detectives use to crack cases!

questions.q: Zero is a positive number.
questions.f: Zero sits exactly in the middle of the number line — neither positive nor negative!

questions.q: Every square is also a rectangle.
questions.f: A square is just a rectangle whose sides all match — but a rectangle isn't always a square!

questions.q: What is this counting tool called?
questions.f: In a famous 1946 contest, an abacus champion beat an electric calculator at math!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's number puzzle!
questions.say: Here is Bizzy's puzzle. Double my number, then take away two, and you get forty-two. What number am I?
questions.f: Solve it backwards: 42 plus 2 is 44, and half of 44 is 22!

questions.q: What is a googol?
questions.f: The search engine Google is named after a misspelling of googol!

questions.q: Numbers that divide evenly only by 1 and themselves are called what?
questions.f: 2 is the only even prime — making it the oddest even number in math!

questions.q: What do we call a number below zero?
questions.f: Negative numbers live to the left of zero — that's how thermometers show freezing winter cold!

questions.q: Computers count in binary using only which digits?
questions.f: Every game, video, and photo on a screen is secretly just a giant pile of 0s and 1s!

questions.q: What is one hundred hundreds?
questions.f: Japanese has a single word just for ten thousand — 'man'!

questions.q: Pi is a circle's ______ divided by its diameter.
questions.f: Pi starts 3.14159… and its digits run on forever without ever repeating!

questions.q: What fraction is one half of one third?
questions.f: Splitting fractions has a trick — the bottom numbers multiply: 2 × 3 = 6!

questions.q: There is a largest number of all.
questions.f: Name any giant number and adding 1 beats it — even a googol plus one is bigger!

questions.q: What does this math symbol mean?
questions.f: The infinity symbol has a fancy name — a lemniscate, from a word for 'ribbon'!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's digit riddle!
questions.say: I am a three-digit number. My hundreds digit is one, my tens is zero, my ones is one. What am I?
questions.f: 101 is a palindrome — flip it around and it reads exactly the same!

questions.q: Which sea animal is this?
questions.f: An octopus has eight arms, and each one can taste whatever it touches!

questions.q: How many arms does an octopus have?
questions.f: Eight arms let an octopus grab food from every direction at once.

questions.q: True or False: A whale is a type of fish.
questions.f: Whales are mammals, so they breathe air and cannot breathe underwater like fish.

questions.q: Which sea animal is this?
questions.f: Dolphins must swim up to breathe air through a blowhole on top of their head.

questions.q: The ocean is filled with what kind of water?
questions.f: The ocean is so salty that you float in it more easily than in a pool.

questions.q: True or False: Crabs walk sideways.
questions.f: A crab's leg joints bend sideways, so scuttling left and right is easiest for it.

questions.q: Which sea animal is this?
questions.f: Crabs wear their skeleton on the outside, like a suit of armor.

questions.q: What color is most ocean water?
questions.f: Water soaks up red light and reflects blue light, so the sea looks blue to us.

questions.q: What is this ocean object?
questions.f: A seashell is the hard home that a sea creature like a snail grew and left behind.

questions.q: How many arms does a starfish usually have?
questions.f: Most starfish have five arms, but some kinds grow forty or more!

questions.q: Which of these animals lives in the ocean?
questions.f: Whales spend their whole lives in the sea but must swim up to breathe air.

questions.q: What do surfers ride on top of in the sea?
questions.f: Waves are made mostly by wind pushing across the surface of the ocean.

questions.q: Which sea animal is this?
questions.f: A shark can grow thousands of teeth in its life because lost ones keep growing back.

questions.q: What do we call the sandy place where the ocean meets the land?
questions.f: Beach sand is made of tiny bits of rock and crushed-up seashells.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: A starfish can regrow a lost arm, and a few kinds can regrow a whole body from one arm!
questions.say: I have five arms and live on the sea floor. Lose an arm and I grow a new one. What am I?

questions.q: Which sea animal is this?
questions.f: A pufferfish gulps water to blow up like a spiky balloon so nothing can bite it.

questions.q: Which fish is famous for hiding among a sea anemone's stinging tentacles?
questions.f: A clownfish has a slimy coating that keeps the anemone's stingers from hurting it.

questions.q: True or False: A seahorse dad carries the babies, not the mom.
questions.f: Male seahorses keep the eggs safe in a special pouch until the babies hatch.

questions.q: What is the hard, rocky structure built by tiny sea animals called?
questions.f: A coral reef is built by thousands of tiny animals over hundreds of years.

questions.q: Which sea animal is this?
questions.f: Seals can nap in the water, sometimes floating upright like a bottle!

questions.q: What do we call the regular rise and fall of the ocean's water level?
questions.f: Tides happen mostly because the Moon's gravity gently pulls the ocean toward it.

questions.q: True or False: Jellyfish have a brain.
questions.f: Jellyfish have no brain, no heart, and no bones, just a soft jelly-like body!

questions.q: Which shellfish has two big claws and turns red when it is cooked?
questions.f: A lobster can also swim backwards very fast by flipping its powerful tail.

questions.q: True or False: Some sharks must keep swimming to keep breathing.
questions.f: Some sharks push water over their gills by swimming, so they rarely fully stop.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: A seahorse swims upright and holds on to seaweed with its curly tail.
questions.say: I look like a horse's head, I swim standing up, and my dad carries the eggs. What am I?

questions.q: What is the biggest ocean on Earth?
questions.f: The Pacific Ocean is so wide that all of Earth's land could fit inside it.

questions.q: Which animal pinches with claws but is not a crab and lives in a borrowed seashell?
questions.f: A hermit crab moves into an empty shell and finds a bigger one as it grows.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: A stingray glides through the water by flapping its wide, wing-like body.
questions.say: I am a fish, but I am flat like a diamond and I have a long, whip-like tail. What am I?

questions.q: True or False: Dolphins are mammals, not fish.
questions.f: Dolphins breathe air, feed their babies milk, and are warm-blooded, just like us.

questions.q: What is seaweed really made of?
questions.f: Seaweed isn't a true plant; it's algae, and some kinds grow longer than a bus.

questions.q: What do we call the tiny animals that build coral reefs?
questions.f: Each coral polyp is a tiny animal that builds a hard cup of limestone around itself.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: The whale shark is the biggest fish in the world, yet it eats tiny ocean creatures.
questions.say: I am the biggest fish in the sea, with spots like stars, but I eat only tiny plankton. What am I?

questions.q: A shrimp's heart is found in which part of its body?
questions.f: A shrimp's heart sits inside its head, just behind its brain!

questions.q: About how much of the Earth's surface is covered by ocean?
questions.f: Oceans cover about 71% of Earth, which is why it is nicknamed the Blue Planet.

questions.q: True or False: Some parts of the deep ocean have never been explored by humans.
questions.f: We have better maps of the Moon's surface than of the deep ocean floor.

questions.q: Which sea animal is this?
questions.f: The giant squid has eyes as big as dinner plates to see in the dark deep sea.

questions.q: What is the name of the deepest place in the ocean?
questions.f: The Mariana Trench is so deep that Mount Everest could sink into it and vanish.

questions.q: Which deep-sea fish dangles a glowing light to lure its prey closer?
questions.f: The anglerfish waves a glowing lure in front of its mouth to trick prey closer.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: A sea urchin's spikes protect it, and it walks on hundreds of tiny tube feet.
questions.say: I am covered in sharp spikes like a pincushion, and I move slowly on the sea floor. What am I?

questions.q: What do we call a scientist who studies ocean life?
questions.f: Marine biologists dive and use submarines to discover brand-new sea creatures.

questions.q: Which furry sea mammal holds hands while sleeping so it won't drift away?
questions.f: Sea otters float on their backs and hold paws so they stay together on the waves.

questions.q: What are the long, stinging body parts of a jellyfish called?
questions.f: A jellyfish uses its stinging tentacles to catch small fish and other tiny animals.

questions.q: What is the hard outer covering of a crab or lobster called?
questions.f: A crab must shed its exoskeleton to grow a bigger one, like changing clothes.

questions.q: Which kind of whale strains tiny food from the water using bristles instead of teeth?
questions.f: Baleen whales gulp huge mouthfuls of water and strain out tiny krill to eat.

questions.q: Which of these is the largest animal that has ever lived on Earth?
questions.f: A blue whale can grow longer than three school buses and its heart is car-sized.

questions.q: Which of these ocean animals is NOT a fish?
questions.f: A jellyfish has no backbone, so it isn't a fish at all, it's an invertebrate.

questions.q: Which of these is the fastest swimmer in the ocean?
questions.f: A sailfish can zoom through the water about as fast as a car on the highway.

questions.q: True or False: Coral is a type of rock.
questions.f: Coral looks like rock but is really built by living animals called polyps.

questions.q: Which ocean layer is so deep that no sunlight ever reaches it?
questions.f: In the midnight zone it is pitch black, so many animals make their own light.

questions.q: Which sea animal is this?
questions.f: A shrimp can flip its tail to shoot backwards through the water in a flash.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: A manta ray can be as wide as a car and does underwater somersaults while it feeds.
questions.say: I am flat and wide, I glide like a bird underwater with huge fins, and I have no bones. What am I?

questions.q: What causes most ocean waves to form?
questions.f: Most waves are made by wind blowing across the surface of the water.

questions.q: Which of these ocean animals can live the longest?
questions.f: A Greenland shark can live for hundreds of years; some may be over 400 years old!

questions.q: Which of these would you NOT find living in the salty ocean?
questions.f: Most frogs need fresh water because salt water would dry out their soft skin.

questions.q: What mainly causes the ocean's high and low tides?
questions.f: The Moon's gravity pulls the ocean toward it, creating a bulge we feel as high tide.

questions.q: Why does the deep ocean stay completely dark?
c: It is always night down there
questions.f: Below about 1,000 meters no sunlight can reach, so it is always pitch black.

questions.q: True or False: An octopus has blue blood.
questions.f: Octopus blood is blue because it uses a copper-based chemical called hemocyanin to carry oxygen.

questions.q: What is it called when a coral reef turns white and can die?
questions.f: When the water gets too warm, coral pushes out the tiny algae that give it color and food.

questions.q: Why can a fish breathe underwater but a person cannot?
c: Fish have gills that pull oxygen from water
Fish can hold their breath forever
Fish do not need any oxygen
Ocean water has no oxygen at all
questions.f: Gills are packed with blood vessels that grab dissolved oxygen straight from the water.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: Bioluminescence is light made by a living thing through a chemical reaction in its body.
questions.say: Deep-sea animals make their own blue-green glow to find food and confuse enemies. What is this glow called?

questions.q: What is the name for a fast-moving 'river' of water that flows through the ocean?
questions.f: The warm Gulf Stream current carries more water than all the world's rivers combined.

questions.q: Which gas do tiny ocean plankton make that we need to breathe?
questions.f: Tiny ocean plankton make more than half of all the oxygen we breathe on Earth!

questions.q: Why is the ocean salty?
c: Rivers wash salt from rocks into it
questions.f: Over millions of years, rivers dissolved salt from rocks and carried it into the sea.

questions.q: What is the largest coral reef system on Earth, so big it can be seen from space?
questions.f: The Great Barrier Reef off Australia is made of thousands of reefs and hundreds of islands.

questions.q: Which part of a plant grows underground?
questions.f: Roots drink water from the soil and hold the plant steady.

questions.q: What color are most healthy leaves?
questions.f: Leaves are green because of a coloring called chlorophyll.

questions.q: What do plants need from the sky to grow?
questions.f: Plants use sunlight like energy to make their own food.

questions.q: Which fruit is this?
questions.f: Some apple trees can keep growing fruit for over 100 years.

questions.q: Which flower is this?
questions.f: A sunflower slowly turns to follow the sun across the sky.

questions.q: Whose shadow is this?
questions.f: A cactus stores water inside its thick stem for dry desert days.

questions.q: A seed can grow into a whole new plant.
questions.f: Inside every seed is a tiny baby plant waiting to sprout.

questions.q: Cactuses grow in hot, dry deserts.
questions.f: A cactus can survive months of sun without a single drop of rain.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: A rose grows thorns to stop hungry animals from eating it.
questions.say: A rose smells sweet, but watch out for the sharp points on my stem. What am I called?

questions.q: What do we call a baby plant just poking out of a seed?
questions.f: A little sprout is also known as a seedling.

questions.q: Which of these grows on trees?
questions.f: Oranges grow on branches, but potatoes grow deep underground.

questions.q: What sweet liquid do bees collect from flowers?
questions.f: Bees turn flower nectar into the honey we love to eat.

questions.q: Which plant floats on top of a pond?
questions.f: Water lilies float on top while their roots reach down into the mud.

questions.q: Which part of a plant usually turns into fruit and seeds?
questions.f: After a flower is visited by bees, it can grow into a fruit.

questions.q: What do a plant's leaves make for it?
questions.f: Leaves are like tiny kitchens cooking food out of sunlight.

questions.q: Which of these is a vegetable that grows underground?
questions.f: The orange carrot we eat is really the plant's root.

questions.q: What is the part that holds a plant up called?
questions.f: The stem carries water up from the roots all the way to the leaves.

questions.q: What falls from many trees in autumn?
questions.f: Many trees drop their leaves to rest through the cold winter.

questions.q: Which drink is made from plant leaves?
questions.f: Tea is made by soaking dried plant leaves in hot water.

questions.q: What do we call a big plant with a strong wooden trunk?
questions.f: The trunk is really the tree's giant, woody stem.

questions.q: Which tree drops little nuts called acorns?
questions.f: One oak tree can drop thousands of acorns in a single year.

questions.q: What gas do plants give off that people need to breathe?
questions.f: One big tree can make enough oxygen for two people each day.

questions.q: Which gas do plants take in to help make their food?
questions.f: Plants breathe in carbon dioxide, the gas we breathe out.

questions.q: Which plant do pandas eat almost all day?
questions.f: A panda can munch on bamboo for up to 12 hours a day.

questions.q: Which plant traps insects inside a deep, slippery cup?
questions.f: Bugs slide down into the pitcher plant's cup and cannot climb out.

questions.q: Which kind of tree is this?
questions.f: Palm trees can bend in strong storm winds without snapping.

questions.q: What is this?
questions.f: Surprise! Mushrooms are not plants at all, they are fungi.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: The Venus flytrap snaps shut in less than one second.
questions.say: I snap my leaves shut to trap flies, and I even count to two before I close. What plant am I?

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: Coast redwoods can grow taller than a 30-story building.
questions.say: I am the tallest kind of tree on Earth, and I grow near the ocean in California. What am I?

questions.q: Bamboo is one of the fastest-growing plants in the world.
questions.f: Some bamboo can shoot up almost a whole meter in one day.

questions.q: Every plant in the world grows flowers.
questions.f: Pine trees and ferns make new plants without ever growing flowers.

questions.q: What do we call the bright, colorful part of a flower?
questions.f: Bright petals act like signs telling bees where the nectar is.

questions.q: Which fruit wears its tiny seeds on the outside?
questions.f: One strawberry can have about 200 tiny seeds on its skin.

questions.q: What sticky stuff do pine trees ooze from their bark?
questions.f: Sticky sap can trap insects and harden into golden amber.

questions.q: Which part of a dandelion floats away on the wind?
questions.f: Each dandelion seed has a tiny parachute to fly to new ground.

questions.q: What do we call plants that catch and eat bugs?
questions.f: Carnivorous plants eat insects to get food when the soil is poor.

questions.q: What is the tough outer covering of a tree trunk called?
questions.f: Bark is like a tree's armor against bugs, cold, and fire.

questions.q: Which fruit is this?
questions.f: Bananas actually grow curving upward toward the sun.

questions.q: Which grain plant is this?
questions.f: Rice feeds more than half of all the people on Earth.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: A coast redwood seed weighs less than a paperclip.
questions.say: A tree taller than a skyscraper grows from me, yet I am tinier than a tomato seed. What am I?

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: Without photosynthesis, there would be almost no oxygen to breathe.
questions.say: Green leaves use me and sunlight to turn water and air into sugar. What is this process called?

questions.q: The Venus flytrap waits for two touches before it snaps shut.
questions.f: Counting to two stops it from wasting a snap on a raindrop.

questions.q: A cactus's sharp spines are really a kind of leaf.
questions.f: Cactus leaves shrank into needles so the plant loses less water.

questions.q: How tall can the tallest coast redwoods grow?
questions.f: The record redwood, named Hyperion, stands about 116 meters tall.

questions.q: How long can a lotus seed stay alive before sprouting?
questions.f: Scientists grew a lotus plant from a seed more than 1,000 years old.

questions.q: What are the tiny holes in leaves that let gases pass through?
questions.f: Leaves open and close these little holes like thousands of tiny mouths.

questions.q: Which plant can grow without soil, drinking water from the air?
questions.f: Air plants soak up water and food straight through their leaves.

questions.q: Which plant has the largest single flower in the world?
questions.f: The rafflesia can be a meter wide and smells like rotting meat.

questions.q: How often does some bamboo flower?
questions.f: Some bamboo blooms only once about every 100 years, then dies.

questions.q: What do we call a plant that lives for only one year?
questions.f: An annual plant sprouts, flowers, and dies all in a single year.

questions.q: Which plant grows the biggest seed in the world?
questions.f: A coco de mer seed can weigh as much as a small child.

questions.q: Which of these is a broadleaf tree, not a needle-leaf conifer?
questions.f: Maple leaves blaze red and orange before they drop in autumn.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: The sensitive plant folds its leaves in seconds when touched.
questions.say: I fold up my leaves the moment you touch me, as if I am shy. What plant am I?

questions.q: Bananas grow on giant trees with hard, wooden trunks.
questions.f: The banana plant is actually the world's largest herb, with no wood.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a way seeds travel to new places?
questions.f: Seeds hitch rides on wind, water, and animal fur to spread far and wide.

questions.q: Which of these trees can live the longest?
questions.f: Some bristlecone pines are more than 4,800 years old.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a real bug-eating plant?
questions.f: The sundew catches bugs with sticky drops, but the snapdragon is harmless.

questions.q: Ferns do not use seeds. What do they use to make new plants?
questions.f: Ferns puff out millions of dust-like spores from under their leaves.

questions.q: Which of these does a plant NOT need to grow?
questions.f: Plants make their own food, so they never need to eat a thing.

questions.q: What is the leafy top layer of a forest called?
questions.f: The canopy can be so thick that little sunlight reaches the ground.

questions.q: About how much of a fresh plant's weight is water?
questions.f: Many plants are more than 80% water, like a living water balloon.

questions.q: Which type of tree is this?
questions.f: Conifers make their seeds inside woody cones instead of flowers.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: Despite its nickname, the agave blooms after 10 to 30 years, then dies.
questions.say: I am a desert plant nicknamed the century plant. I bloom just once, then die. What am I?

questions.q: Some plants warn each other of danger using chemicals in the air.
questions.f: When bugs attack, some plants release a scent that alerts their neighbors.

questions.q: A Venus flytrap can tell a live insect from a raindrop.
questions.f: It counts touches on its trigger hairs so it only snaps for real prey.

questions.q: Why do leaves turn orange and yellow in autumn?
questions.f: As the green fades, hidden orange and yellow colors finally show through.

questions.q: What sugar do plants make during photosynthesis?
questions.f: Plants store extra glucose as starch to use for energy later.

questions.q: Which record belongs to the giant sequoia?
questions.f: A sequoia named General Sherman is the biggest single tree on Earth.

questions.q: What is the name for pollen moving so flowers can make seeds?
questions.f: Bees, wind, and even bats help carry pollen from flower to flower.

questions.q: How does a giant saguaro cactus survive months with no rain?
c: It stores water in its stem
questions.f: A soaked saguaro can hold hundreds of liters of water and swell up fatter.

questions.q: Why can't plants grow deep down on the dark ocean floor?
questions.f: Without sunlight for photosynthesis, plants cannot make any food.

questions.q: What is this science tool called?
questions.f: Giant junkyard magnets are strong enough to lift a whole car!

questions.q: What appears in the sky when sun shines through rain?
questions.f: You can never reach the end of a rainbow — it moves whenever you move!

questions.q: What do you wear to protect your eyes in a science lab?
questions.f: Real scientists wear goggles because even tiny splashes can sting your eyes.

questions.q: Which of these floats in the bathtub?
questions.f: The duck is full of air, which makes it lighter than the water it sits on.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: Raindrops aren't teardrop-shaped — they fall looking like tiny hamburger buns!
questions.say: I fall from dark clouds in little drops and fill up puddles on the ground. What am I?

questions.q: What is this flash you see in a storm?
questions.f: A lightning bolt is only about as wide as your thumb — but miles long!

questions.q: Where at home do magnets hold up notes and drawings?
questions.f: Fridge doors have steel inside, and magnets love to grab steel.

questions.q: When you stir sugar into water, the sugar is still there even though it disappears.
questions.f: The sugar dissolves into invisible tiny pieces — taste the water and it's sweet!

questions.q: What is this hot, glowing thing called?
questions.f: Fire needs three things to burn: heat, fuel, and oxygen from the air.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: Every snowflake has six sides, and no two are exactly alike!
questions.say: I am white and cold, and I fall softly from winter clouds. What am I?

questions.q: At what temperature does water freeze?
questions.f: Ponds only start to freeze when the temperature drops all the way to zero degrees Celsius.

questions.q: At what temperature does water boil?
questions.f: At 100°C, water bubbles madly as it turns into gas — way too hot to touch!

questions.q: Which gas makes party balloons float?
questions.f: Breathe in helium and your voice goes squeaky — sound travels faster through it!

questions.q: What happens when two north poles of magnets meet?
questions.f: Opposites attract: a north pole and a south pole snap together instead!

questions.q: Which science container is this?
questions.f: Scientists use test tubes to mix tiny amounts of liquids and watch what happens.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: A fluffy white cloud can weigh as much as 100 elephants!
questions.say: I float high in the sky, and I am made of millions of tiny water drops. What am I?

questions.q: Which measuring tool is this?
questions.f: The liquid inside a thermometer expands as it warms, climbing higher up the tube.

questions.q: A rainbow can appear in the spray of a garden hose.
questions.f: Any water drops in sunshine can split light into colors — even a waterfall's mist!

questions.q: What is a puddle doing when it slowly disappears on a warm day?
questions.f: The water turns into invisible vapor and floats up to help make new clouds.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: Lightning is a giant spark of static electricity jumping from cloud to ground!
questions.say: Rub a balloon on your hair and I will make it stand straight up. What am I?

questions.q: How hot is a lightning bolt compared with the Sun's surface?
questions.f: Lightning can reach about 30,000°C — the Sun's surface is only about 5,500°C!

questions.q: Which two ingredients make a water molecule?
questions.f: That's why scientists call water H2O — two hydrogens stuck to one oxygen.

questions.q: Which gas makes up most of the air you breathe?
questions.f: Air is about 78% nitrogen — oxygen is only about a fifth of every breath!

questions.q: Which lab tool is this?
questions.f: A microscope can make tiny things look hundreds of times bigger — even your own cells!

questions.q: What forms when iron meets water and oxygen?
questions.f: Mars looks red because its dust is full of rusty iron!

questions.q: What is a healthy human body temperature?
questions.f: Your body stays near 37°C all the time — shivering and sweating are its thermostat tricks!

questions.q: Water gets bigger when it freezes.
questions.f: Freezing water expands so powerfully it can crack rocks and burst metal pipes!

questions.q: Which gem is the hardest natural material on Earth?
questions.f: Diamonds are so hard that only another diamond can scratch them!

questions.q: What does a prism do to white light?
questions.f: White light is secretly all the rainbow colors mixed together — a prism just un-mixes them!

questions.q: Which of these will a magnet NOT attract?
questions.f: Magnets only pull on a few metals — iron, nickel, and cobalt. Aluminum ignores them!

questions.q: Which of these temperatures is the coldest?
questions.f: Your home freezer runs at about -18°C to keep ice cream rock solid.

questions.q: Which change turns water vapor into liquid drops?
questions.f: That's why a cold drink 'sweats' — invisible vapor in the air turns into drops on the glass.

questions.q: About how many lightning bolts flash around the world every second?
questions.f: That adds up to millions of lightning flashes across the world every single day!

questions.q: Which tool compares how heavy two things are?
questions.f: Balance scales were weighing gold in ancient Egypt more than 4,000 years ago!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: Stars — including our Sun — are giant balls of glowing plasma!
questions.say: I am the fourth state of matter, and I make lightning and stars glow. What am I?

questions.q: What is the coldest temperature possible, called absolute zero?
questions.f: At absolute zero, atoms almost completely stop moving — nothing can ever get colder!

questions.q: Metal and wood are the same temperature. Why does metal feel colder?
c: Metal pulls heat from your hand faster
questions.f: Metal conducts heat away hundreds of times faster than wood — same temperature, different feel!

questions.q: What causes the sound of thunder?
c: Lightning heats air so fast it bursts outward
questions.f: Lightning superheats the air in a split second, and the air explodes outward as a shockwave!

questions.q: Sound can travel through empty space.
questions.f: Space has no air to carry sound waves — astronauts must use radios to chat!

questions.q: Why does the sky look blue?
c: Blue light scatters most in the air
The Sun gives off blue fire
questions.f: At sunset, light travels through more air, so reds and oranges take over the sky!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: The Celsius scale is named after Anders Celsius, the astronomer who invented it in 1742.
questions.say: You measure me in degrees. Water boils when I reach one hundred Celsius. What am I?

questions.q: Why does sweating cool you down?
c: Sweat is made of ice water
Salt in sweat freezes the skin
questions.f: Dogs barely sweat at all — they pant to let heat escape from their tongues instead!

questions.q: What do astronauts wear to stay safe outside their spaceship?
questions.f: A spacesuit is like a tiny wearable spaceship — it even carries its own air to breathe!

questions.q: What lights up the night sky and changes shape through the month?
questions.f: The Moon is slowly drifting away from Earth — about 4 centimeters every year!

questions.q: Where do astronauts live while they work in space?
questions.f: The International Space Station is as big as a football field and circles Earth every 90 minutes!

questions.q: Which tool makes faraway stars look closer?
questions.f: Galileo used a telescope to spot Jupiter's four biggest moons more than 400 years ago.

questions.q: What is the giant glowing ball that warms our planet?
questions.f: About one million Earths could fit inside the Sun!

questions.q: What do we call everything that exists — all the stars, planets, and space?
questions.f: The universe is so enormous that nobody has ever found its edge!

questions.q: True or False: Astronauts float inside their spaceship.
questions.f: They are really falling around Earth the whole time — that is what makes everything float!

questions.q: Look at the picture! Which planet is this?
questions.f: Saturn has more than 100 moons — more than any other planet!

questions.q: Whose shadow is this?
questions.f: Only twelve people have ever walked on the Moon!

questions.q: Look at the Moon! Which shape is it showing?
questions.f: A full moon comes about once a month — that is where the word 'month' comes from!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I twinkle high in the night sky. I am a giant ball of hot, glowing gas, very far away. What am I?
questions.f: The starlight you see tonight traveled for years just to reach your eyes!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: Five, four, three, two, one, blast off! I roar into the sky with fire and smoke below me. What am I?
questions.f: To reach orbit, a rocket must fly faster than a speeding bullet!

questions.q: What do we call a group of stars that forms a picture?
questions.f: The famous Big Dipper is part of a constellation called the Great Bear.

questions.q: What is the name of our galaxy?
questions.f: The Milky Way holds more than 100 billion stars!

questions.q: What force pulls you back down when you jump?
questions.f: Without gravity you would float right off the ground like an astronaut!

questions.q: How many planets are in our solar system?
questions.f: Neptune, the eighth planet, was found using math before anyone ever saw it!

questions.q: What vehicle did astronauts drive around on the Moon?
questions.f: The Apollo Moon buggies are still parked up on the Moon today!

questions.q: What do we call the path the Moon travels around Earth?
questions.f: The Moon takes about 27 days to travel around Earth once.

questions.q: What color does the sky look when you are up in space?
questions.f: There is no air in space to scatter sunlight, so space always looks black — even in daytime!

questions.q: True or False: You could hear a friend shout on the Moon.
questions.f: Sound needs air to travel, and the Moon has almost no air at all!

questions.q: True or False: Footprints left on the Moon can last for millions of years.
questions.f: There is no wind or rain on the Moon, so nothing ever wipes the footprints away!

questions.q: True or False: The Sun travels around the Earth.
questions.f: It is the other way around — Earth zooms around the Sun at about 30 kilometers every second!

questions.q: What is this mystery flying object called?
questions.f: UFO means Unidentified Flying Object — most turn out to be planes, balloons, or satellites!

questions.q: What is this machine that circles high above Earth?
questions.f: Satellites beam TV shows, maps, and weather reports down to Earth every day!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: Make a wish! I flash across the night sky in a bright streak, gone in a blink. What am I?
questions.f: A shooting star is not a star at all — it is a tiny space rock burning up in the air!

questions.q: How long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.f: If the Sun suddenly switched off, we would not notice for 8 whole minutes!

questions.q: What do we call a space rock that lands on Earth's surface?
questions.f: Scientists hunt for meteorites in Antarctica because dark rocks are easy to spot on white ice!

questions.q: Which giant space telescope, launched in 2021, photographs baby galaxies?
questions.f: The James Webb telescope's huge mirror is coated in real gold!

questions.q: What was the name of the first satellite ever launched into space?
questions.f: Sputnik was about the size of a beach ball and beeped as it circled Earth in 1957.

questions.q: About how many days does Earth take to orbit the Sun once?
questions.f: The leftover quarter of a day is why we add a leap day every four years!

questions.q: Who was the first human to travel into space?
questions.f: Yuri Gagarin circled Earth once in 1961 — the whole trip took just 108 minutes!

questions.q: What is the Great Red Spot on Jupiter?
questions.f: This storm is bigger than the whole Earth and has been raging for over 150 years!

questions.q: What are Saturn's rings mostly made of?
questions.f: Some ring chunks are as small as pebbles and others as big as houses!

questions.q: True or False: Mars has two moons.
questions.f: They are named Phobos and Deimos, and both are shaped like lumpy potatoes!

questions.q: True or False: There is no gravity at all on the Moon.
questions.f: The Moon's gravity is real but weak — that is why astronauts bounce when they walk!

questions.q: Look at the Moon! What is this phase called?
questions.f: During a half moon, you are seeing exactly half of the Moon's sunny side.

questions.q: Whose shadow is peeking out of this flying saucer?
questions.f: Scientists use giant radio telescopes to listen for real alien signals — none found yet!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am a robot with six wheels. I roll across the red planet Mars, taking pictures and zapping rocks. What am I?
questions.f: NASA's rover Curiosity once hummed 'Happy Birthday' to itself on Mars!

questions.q: What is the name of the biggest volcano in the solar system, found on Mars?
questions.f: Olympus Mons stands about two and a half times taller than Mount Everest!

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the eight planets?
questions.f: Pluto is a dwarf planet — it is even smaller than Earth's Moon!

questions.q: How long is one day — one full spin — on giant Jupiter?
questions.f: Jupiter is the fastest-spinning planet — a whole day whips by in about 10 hours!

questions.q: Where would you weigh the least?
questions.f: Moon gravity is one-sixth of Earth's — a 60-pound kid would weigh only 10 pounds there!

questions.q: Which list shows the correct order of planets starting from the Sun?
questions.f: 'My Very Excellent Mother Just Served Us Noodles' helps you remember all eight planets!

questions.q: Which is there MORE of?
c: Grains of sand on Earth's beaches
questions.f: Scientists estimate there are more stars than every grain of sand on every beach on Earth!

questions.q: True or False: Saturn would float if you could drop it into a giant ocean of water.
questions.f: Saturn is mostly gas — it is the only planet less dense than water!

questions.q: The Moon looks completely dark here. What phase is this?
questions.f: During a new moon, the Moon's sunny side is facing away from us, so we see almost nothing.

questions.q: Whose shadow is this? This animal flew to space before any person did!
questions.f: Ham the chimpanzee flew to space in 1961 and came home safe to live in a zoo!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am the seventh planet from the Sun. I spin lying on my side, like a rolling ball. What am I?
questions.f: A giant collision long ago probably knocked Uranus over onto its side!

questions.q: Why is Venus hotter than Mercury, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun?
c: Its thick carbon dioxide air traps the Sun's heat
questions.f: Venus's clouds even hold drops of acid — but the rain evaporates before it ever lands!

questions.q: Why is Pluto called a dwarf planet instead of a planet?
c: It has not cleared other objects out of its orbit
It is too cold to count
It is too far away to see
questions.f: Pluto actually has five moons — the biggest one is called Charon!

questions.q: Why do we always see the same side of the Moon?
c: The Moon spins exactly once each time it orbits Earth
The Moon does not spin at all
questions.f: Nobody saw the Moon's far side until a spacecraft photographed it in 1959!

questions.q: What is a black hole?
c: A place where gravity is so strong not even light escapes
questions.f: Near a black hole, time itself runs slower — a falling clock would seem to tick more slowly!

questions.q: Why do sunsets on Mars look blue?
c: Fine dust in its air scatters blue light toward you
Mars has blue oceans that reflect light
The Sun shines blue from there
Its air is thicker than Earth's
questions.f: On Mars the daytime sky is butterscotch-pink and sunsets glow blue — the opposite of Earth!

questions.q: Why does a comet's tail always point away from the Sun?
c: The Sun's wind of tiny particles pushes it away
The tail steers the comet like a rudder
Comets always fly away from the Sun
questions.f: When a comet leaves the Sun, it actually travels tail-first!

questions.q: Why is the Moon covered in craters while Earth shows so few?
c: The Moon has no weather to wear its craters away
The Moon is much older than Earth
Moon volcanoes blasted all the holes
questions.f: Earth gets hit too, but wind, rain, and plants slowly hide most of our craters!

questions.q: True or False: A day on Venus lasts longer than its whole year.
questions.f: Venus spins so slowly that it finishes a trip around the Sun before it finishes one turn!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: Sailors used me to find their way. I sit above the North Pole and never seem to move. What am I?
questions.f: The North Star, called Polaris, sits almost exactly above Earth's North Pole!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I happen when the Moon slides in front of the Sun and day turns dark for a few minutes. What am I?
questions.f: The Sun is 400 times wider than the Moon but 400 times farther away — so they look the same size!

questions.q: Which sport do you play by kicking a ball into a goal?
questions.f: Soccer is called football in most countries because you play it with your feet!

questions.q: In basketball, what do you throw the ball through to score?
questions.f: The first hoops were peach baskets — someone had to climb up and get the ball after every score!

questions.q: In cricket, what does the batter use to hit the ball?
questions.f: Cricket bats are made from a special springy wood called willow!

questions.q: In rock-paper-scissors, which one beats scissors?
questions.f: Rock-paper-scissors is centuries old — in Japan it's called jan-ken!

questions.q: In musical chairs, what must you find when the music stops?
c: A door to run out of
questions.f: There is always one chair fewer than players, so someone is out every round!

questions.q: In tag, what do you become when someone tags you?
questions.f: Tag is played all over the world — in France it's called 'chat', which means cat!

questions.q: What do swimmers wear to see clearly underwater?
questions.f: Human eyes can't focus well underwater — goggles trap air so you can see sharply!

questions.q: In tug of war, what do the two teams pull?
questions.f: The giant rope in Japan's Naha tug-of-war festival weighs about 40 tonnes!

questions.q: Which piece of gear protects your head when you ride a bike?
questions.f: Your skull protects your brain, and a helmet protects your skull — double armor!

questions.q: In carrom, what do you flick with your finger to hit the pieces?
questions.f: Carrom was invented in India and is now played in living rooms all across South Asia!

questions.q: What does the seeker do first in hide-and-seek?
questions.f: In France, hide-and-seek is called cache-cache!

questions.q: In soccer, the goalkeeper may pick up the ball with their hands.
questions.f: Goalkeepers can only use their hands inside their own penalty area — outside it, that's a foul!

questions.q: In volleyball, players kick the ball over the net with their feet.
questions.f: Volleyball uses hands and arms — but sepak takraw is a real sport where players kick over a net!

questions.q: A cricket ball is soft and squishy like a sponge.
questions.f: A cricket ball has a cork center wrapped in tight leather — it's hard as a rock!

questions.q: Which sport uses this stitched ball?
questions.f: Every baseball has exactly 108 double stitches holding it together!

questions.q: Which sport uses this fuzzy yellow ball?
questions.f: Tennis balls were white or black until 1972, when yellow was chosen so TV viewers could see them!

questions.q: Which game is shown here?
questions.f: A perfect bowling game of 12 strikes in a row scores exactly 300 points!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am round and orange. Players bounce me down the court and throw me through a hoop. What am I?
questions.f: Basketballs are orange so players and fans can spot them easily!

questions.q: What color card does a soccer referee show to send a player off?
questions.f: A yellow card is a warning — collect two yellows and you're shown the red!

questions.q: Sumo wrestling was invented in which country?
questions.f: Sumo wrestlers grow strong by eating a giant stew called chankonabe!

questions.q: In cricket, what are the three wooden sticks behind the batter called?
questions.f: Two tiny pieces of wood called bails balance on top of the stumps!

questions.q: In which Indian game do raiders chant the game's own name?
questions.f: A kabaddi raider traditionally chants 'kabaddi, kabaddi' in one single breath!

questions.q: In which country did the Olympic Games begin long ago?
questions.f: Ancient Olympic winners received crowns of olive leaves instead of medals!

questions.q: Which sport is played on ice with a flat disc called a puck?
questions.f: Pucks are frozen before games so they slide smoothly instead of bouncing!

questions.q: Which game is played on a board of 64 black and white squares?
questions.f: Chess began in India about 1,500 years ago as a game called chaturanga!

questions.q: In the Indian game kho-kho, what do the chasers try to do?
questions.f: Kho-kho chasers kneel in a row, each one facing the opposite way from their neighbor!

questions.q: Which player is called the 'God of Cricket' in India?
questions.f: Sachin Tendulkar scored 100 international centuries — a record nobody has matched!

questions.q: Who makes sure players follow the rules during a soccer match?
questions.f: In cricket and baseball, this official is called an umpire instead!

questions.q: Snakes and Ladders was invented in which country?
questions.f: It began as Moksha Patam — ladders stood for good deeds and snakes for bad ones!

questions.q: The Olympic Games are held every single year.
questions.f: The Olympics come only once every four years — and so does the FIFA World Cup!

questions.q: In golf, the player with the LOWEST score wins.
questions.f: Golf is one of the few sports where fewer points is better — a hole-in-one is just one swing!

questions.q: What is this winner's prize called?
questions.f: The FIFA World Cup trophy is made of 18-karat gold and weighs about 6 kilograms!

questions.q: Which sport uses this small paddle and ball?
questions.f: A table tennis ball weighs less than 3 grams — lighter than a sheet of paper!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I use a curved stick to push a small ball across the grass into a goal. What sport am I?
questions.f: India's men's hockey team has won eight Olympic gold medals — more than any other country!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: Boing! Boing! I bounce high on a big stretchy bed and do flips in the air. What sport am I?
questions.f: Trampoline became a real Olympic sport in the year 2000!

questions.q: How long is a full soccer match?
questions.f: It's played as two 45-minute halves with a 15-minute break called half-time!

questions.q: How many balls are bowled in one cricket over?
questions.f: Australia once used extra-long eight-ball overs — they only stopped in 1979!

questions.q: How many players from one basketball team are on court at a time?
questions.f: The very first basketball game in 1891 was played nine-a-side!

questions.q: What is a cricket batter's score of 100 runs called?
questions.f: Scoring zero is called a duck — because the number 0 looks like a duck's egg!

questions.q: How many players does a kabaddi team have on the court?
questions.f: Legends say kabaddi was played in India over 4,000 years ago!

questions.q: What is it called when a soccer player scores three goals in one game?
questions.f: The name comes from cricket, where a bowler taking three wickets in a row was gifted a hat!

questions.q: How high is a basketball hoop above the ground?
questions.f: The hoop has stayed exactly 10 feet high ever since basketball was invented in 1891!

questions.q: Which gymnast scored the first perfect 10 in Olympic history?
questions.f: The 1976 scoreboard couldn't display 10.00, so her perfect score showed up as 1.00!

questions.q: The Olympic flame is lit in Greece before every Games.
questions.f: It's lit at ancient Olympia using a curved mirror that focuses the Sun's rays!

questions.q: A badminton shuttlecock is made with real feathers.
questions.f: Top-quality shuttlecocks use exactly 16 goose feathers!

questions.q: What place did the athlete with this medal win?
questions.f: Olympic 'gold' medals are actually mostly silver, coated with only about 6 grams of real gold!

questions.q: Which sport is this athlete doing?
questions.f: Simone Biles invented gymnastics moves so difficult that several are officially named after her!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: Ready, set, run! I sprint down a track and leap as far as I can into a sandpit. What event is this?
questions.f: The world record long jump is 8.95 meters — about as long as two cars parked end to end!

questions.q: Which of these sports does NOT use a ball?
questions.f: Karate means 'empty hand' in Japanese — you don't need any equipment at all!

questions.q: Which country has won the most soccer World Cups?
questions.f: Brazil is the only country to have played in every single World Cup!

questions.q: Which board game grew out of Pachisi, an ancient Indian game?
questions.f: Emperor Akbar is said to have played Pachisi on giant courtyard boards, using people as the pieces!

questions.q: Which of these flies the fastest?
questions.f: India's Satwiksairaj Rankireddy smashed a shuttle at 565 km/h — faster than a Formula 1 car!

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a real Olympic swimming stroke?
questions.f: Doggy paddle is how dogs swim — Olympic races use freestyle, butterfly, backstroke and breaststroke!

questions.q: Which chess piece is the most powerful on the board?
questions.f: The queen can slide any number of squares in any straight direction — no other piece can!

questions.q: Which color cricket ball is used for day-night Test matches?
questions.f: Red balls are for daytime Tests and white for one-day games — pink shows up best under floodlights!

questions.q: Tug of war was once a real Olympic event.
questions.f: Teams battled for Olympic tug-of-war medals at five Games between 1900 and 1920!

questions.q: A marathon race is longer than 40 kilometers.
questions.f: It's 42.195 km — extra distance was added in 1908 so the race could finish in front of the royal family!

questions.q: This shadow shows a bat and ball from which sport?
questions.f: A cricket bat is flat on one side — a baseball bat is round all the way around!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: Twang! I fly from a bow, spinning toward a round target, hoping to hit the golden middle. What sport is this?
questions.f: The center ring of an archery target is called the gold — hitting it scores 10 points!

questions.q: Why do golf balls have dimples all over them?
c: They help the ball fly farther
questions.f: A golf ball has 300 to 500 dimples — a smooth ball would fly only about half as far!

questions.q: Who ran the fastest 100 meters ever recorded?
questions.f: Bolt ran 100 m in 9.58 seconds, reaching nearly 45 km/h — faster than city traffic!

questions.q: Which swimmer has won the most Olympic gold medals ever?
questions.f: Phelps owns 23 Olympic golds — more than most entire countries have ever won!

questions.q: Which sport has actually been played on the Moon?
questions.f: Astronaut Alan Shepard smuggled a golf club aboard Apollo 14 and hit two balls on the Moon in 1971!

questions.q: Why do soccer referees add extra minutes at the end of each half?
c: To make up for time lost to stoppages
questions.f: Soccer's clock never stops running, so referees add 'stoppage time' for injuries and delays!

questions.q: Hockey is officially India's national game.
questions.f: India has never officially declared any national game — hockey's Olympic fame just made everyone believe it!

questions.q: Which sport is this masked athlete competing in?
questions.f: Fencing is one of only five sports that has appeared at every modern Olympics since 1896!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: Born in Hawaii, I ride giant ocean waves while standing on a special board. What sport am I?
questions.f: Surfing finally became an Olympic sport at the Tokyo 2020 Games!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: In cricket, I am hit along the ground and bounce before crossing the boundary rope. How many runs do I score?
questions.f: If the ball flies over the boundary without bouncing at all, that's a six!

questions.q: Where does Peter Rabbit sneak in to nibble vegetables?
questions.f: Beatrix Potter first wrote Peter Rabbit as a letter to cheer up a sick little boy!

questions.q: Who went up the hill to fetch a pail of water?
questions.f: Jack fell down and broke his crown — 'crown' is an old word for the top of your head!

questions.q: In Hey Diddle Diddle, the dish runs away with what?
questions.f: This silly rhyme is more than 250 years old, and nobody knows what it really means!

questions.q: Twinkle Twinkle Little Star compares the star to what?
questions.f: The tune is the same as the ABC song — try singing them at the same time!

questions.q: Which animal follows Mary to school one day?
questions.f: The rhyme may be based on a real girl, Mary Sawyer, whose pet lamb really followed her to school!

questions.q: In Hey Diddle Diddle, the cow jumps over the sun.
questions.f: It's the moon! And the little dog laughed to see such fun.

questions.q: This slow-and-steady animal wins Aesop's famous race. What is it?
questions.f: The hare was so sure he'd win that he stopped for a nap — and snoozed past the finish line!

questions.q: Cinderella's fairy godmother turns this into a coach. What is it?
questions.f: At midnight — poof! — the coach turned right back into a pumpkin.

questions.q: Three of these built houses of straw, sticks, and bricks. What animal is it?
questions.f: Only the brick house stood strong against the wolf's mightiest huff and puff!

questions.q: Whose shadow scared Little Miss Muffet away?
questions.f: Miss Muffet was eating curds and whey — a lumpy, old-fashioned cheese snack!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle! Who says this?
questions.f: He outruns an old woman, an old man, and even a cow — what a speedy cookie!
questions.say: Run, run, as fast as you can! You can't catch me! Who am I?

questions.q: Who wrote The Ugly Duckling?
questions.f: Andersen wrote more than 150 fairy tales, including The Little Mermaid and Thumbelina!

questions.q: The boy who cried 'Wolf!' as a joke gets a surprise when a real wolf comes. What happens?
questions.f: Aesop's moral: if you tell lies, people may not believe you even when you tell the truth.

questions.q: Which rhyme character lost her sheep and doesn't know where to find them?
questions.f: Leave them alone and they'll come home, wagging their tails behind them!

questions.q: Old Mother Hubbard goes to her cupboard to fetch her dog what?
questions.f: But when she got there, the cupboard was bare — so the poor dog had none!

questions.q: Which fairy-tale cat wears boots and makes his master rich?
questions.f: Puss in Boots is in Charles Perrault's 1697 fairy-tale book — the very same book as Cinderella!

questions.q: Aesop's fables end with a lesson called a moral.
questions.f: Some of Aesop's morals, like 'look before you leap,' are still said every single day!

questions.q: Old King Cole calls for his fiddlers ten.
questions.f: Old King Cole was a merry old soul, and he called for his fiddlers three!

questions.q: A princess's kiss turns this creature into a prince. What is it?
questions.f: In the Grimms' original tale there's no kiss — the princess throws the frog at a wall and POOF, a prince!

questions.q: In Hickory Dickory Dock, this animal runs up the clock. What is it?
questions.f: The clock struck one, and down he ran — hickory dickory dock!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle! Who is speaking?
questions.f: Rapunzel is named after a leafy salad plant her mother craved in the Grimms' tale!
questions.say: I let down my long, long hair from a tall tower window. Who am I?

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle! Who is it?
questions.f: Author J. M. Barrie gave all the rights to Peter Pan to a children's hospital in London!
questions.say: I can fly, I never grow up, and I live in Neverland. Who am I?

questions.q: In Aesop's fable, how does the tiny mouse rescue the mighty lion?
c: It chews through the ropes of a net
questions.f: The moral: even the smallest friend can be a mighty helper!

questions.q: A haiku's three lines follow which syllable pattern?
questions.f: Haiku began in Japan centuries ago and often capture one tiny moment in nature.

questions.q: The Panchatantra, a famous collection of animal tales, comes from which country?
questions.f: These tales are about 2,000 years old and were told to teach young princes to be wise!

questions.q: What words does Charlotte the spider first weave into her web?
questions.f: Author E. B. White watched a real spider spinning in his barn before he wrote Charlotte's Web.

questions.q: In Alice in Wonderland, which animal does Alice follow down the hole?
questions.f: The rabbit checks a pocket watch and cries, 'Oh dear! I shall be too late!'

questions.q: In Aesop's The Crow and the Pitcher, how does the thirsty crow reach the water?
c: It drops pebbles in to raise the water
It pecks a hole in the side
questions.f: Scientists tested this — real birds really did drop stones to raise the water, just like the fable!

questions.q: Hans Christian Andersen came from Denmark.
questions.f: His birthday, April 2, is celebrated around the world as International Children's Book Day!

questions.q: Little Jack Horner pulls a cherry out of his pie.
questions.f: He stuck in his thumb and pulled out a plum, and said, 'What a good boy am I!'

questions.q: In Aesop's fable, this animal walks away calling the grapes 'sour.' What is it?
questions.f: 'Sour grapes' now means pretending you never wanted something you couldn't get!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle! Who is it?
questions.f: Pinocchio was written in Italian by Carlo Collodi, and kids read it chapter by chapter in a newspaper!
questions.say: A kind woodcarver named Geppetto carved me, and I dream of becoming a real boy. Who am I?

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle! Who is speaking?
questions.f: In The Jungle Book, Baloo the bear teaches Mowgli the Law of the Jungle!
questions.say: I was raised by wolves in the jungle, and a wise old bear taught me the law. Who am I?

questions.q: Which of these stories comes from the Panchatantra?
questions.f: The clever monkey escapes by claiming he left his heart hanging back in his fruit tree!

questions.q: Why does the country mouse hurry home from the city in Aesop's fable?
c: He would rather be safe than eat fancy feasts
He cannot find his cousin's house
The city smells too much like cheese
questions.f: Every fancy nibble in town was interrupted by danger — better a plain supper eaten in peace!

questions.q: Which line comes right after 'Twinkle, twinkle, little star'?
c: How I wonder what you are
Up above the world so high
Like a diamond in the sky
When the blazing sun is gone
questions.f: The words come from a poem called 'The Star,' written by Jane Taylor in 1806.

questions.q: The rhyme Humpty Dumpty never actually says he is an egg.
questions.f: It began as a riddle — listeners had to guess that the thing that broke was an egg!

questions.q: A limerick is a serious poem that is ten lines long.
questions.f: Limericks are five-line funny poems, made famous by Edward Lear's Book of Nonsense!

questions.q: Whose shadow goes tick-tock as it follows Captain Hook?
questions.f: The crocodile in Peter Pan swallowed a ticking clock, so Hook always hears it coming!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle! Who is speaking?
questions.f: The town refused to pay him — that's why 'paying the piper' means facing the cost of your promises!
questions.say: With my magic pipe, I led all the rats out of the town of Hamelin. Who am I?

questions.q: Matsuo Basho, the great haiku master, wrote his most famous poem about a frog jumping into what?
questions.f: Basho's frog haiku is so loved it has been translated into English more than a hundred different ways!

questions.q: The saying 'don't count your chickens before they hatch' comes from a fable about whom?
c: A milkmaid carrying a pail of milk
questions.f: She daydreamed of riches the milk would buy, tossed her head, and spilled the whole pail!

questions.q: The Panchatantra was originally written in which ancient language?
questions.f: Its animal tales traveled along trade routes and inspired fable books across Persia and Europe!

questions.q: Who wrote both Alice's Adventures in Wonderland and the nonsense poem Jabberwocky?
questions.f: Lewis Carroll was a pen name — he was really a mathematics teacher named Charles Dodgson!

questions.q: What is the moral of Aesop's The Goose That Laid the Golden Eggs?
c: Greed can make you lose what you already have
Slow and steady wins the race
questions.f: The farmer demanded all the gold at once — and ended up with no golden eggs at all.

questions.q: In The Velveteen Rabbit, what makes a toy become Real?
