c: Being truly loved by a child
questions.f: The wise Skin Horse says it takes a long time — and rarely happens to toys with sharp edges!

questions.q: In the original Wizard of Oz book, Dorothy's magic shoes are silver, not ruby.
questions.f: The ruby slippers were invented for the 1939 movie to show off dazzling new color film!

questions.q: In a famous old Indian tale, six blind men each touch a different part of this animal. What is it?
questions.f: One felt the trunk and said 'snake,' one felt a leg and said 'tree' — one view is never the whole truth!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle! Who is it?
questions.f: No one knows for sure if Aesop was a real person, but hundreds of fables carry his name!
questions.say: I told fables in ancient Greece, and my slow tortoise beat a speedy hare. Who am I?

questions.q: What do we call very light, gentle rain?
questions.f: Drizzle drops are less than half a millimeter wide — smaller than a grain of sand.

questions.q: What is this arc of colors in the sky called?
questions.f: A rainbow is really a full circle — from a plane you can see the whole ring!

questions.q: What do you hear during a storm right after lightning flashes?
questions.f: Thunder can be heard rumbling from about 10 miles away.

questions.q: What color is a clear daytime sky?
questions.f: On Mars, the daytime sky looks butterscotch-brown — and the sunsets there are blue!

questions.q: What is this called when it falls from winter clouds?
questions.f: The biggest snowflake ever reported was 15 inches wide — bigger than a dinner plate!

questions.q: Which season is usually the hottest?
questions.f: Summer happens when your half of Earth is tilted toward the Sun.

questions.q: What are the frozen spikes of ice that hang from roofs called?
questions.f: Icicles grow drip by drip — each drop freezes a tiny new layer onto the tip.

questions.q: Clouds are made of cotton.
questions.f: Clouds are really billions of tiny water droplets, each smaller than a speck of dust.

questions.q: What is this bright flash that zigzags from storm clouds?
questions.f: About 100 lightning bolts strike the Earth every single second!

questions.q: What is this glowing object in the night sky?
questions.f: The Moon makes no light of its own — it reflects sunlight like a giant mirror.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: Wind is born when the Sun heats some places more than others, making air rush around.
questions.say: You cannot see me, but you feel me on your face and hear me whoosh through trees. What am I?

questions.q: What do we call a cloud resting on the ground?
questions.f: Some desert beetles drink fog by letting it collect in droplets on their own backs!

questions.q: What are the bouncing balls of ice that fall during some thunderstorms?
questions.f: Hail only forms in thunderstorms — never in calm winter snowstorms.

questions.q: What do puddles turn into on a freezing night?
questions.f: Black ice on roads is so thin and clear you can see the road right through it.

questions.q: Which tool tells you how hot or cold it is?
questions.f: The word thermometer literally means 'heat measurer.'

questions.q: What are the tiny water drops on grass in the early morning called?
questions.f: Dew forms overnight when water vapor in the air condenses onto cool grass.

questions.q: Which puffy cloud looks like a floating ball of cotton?
questions.f: Cumulus clouds form on sunny days when warm air bubbles rise like invisible hot-air balloons.

questions.q: What is this spinning funnel of wind called?
questions.f: A tornado's funnel can be skinnier than a house or wider than a whole town.

questions.q: What is a scientist who studies the weather called?
questions.f: Meteorology comes from an old Greek word for 'things high in the sky' — not space rocks!

questions.q: Snowflakes always have eight sides.
questions.f: Snow crystals grow six sides, because water molecules lock together in hexagons.

questions.q: What is the calm center of a hurricane called?
questions.f: Inside the eye the wind goes calm and you can even see blue sky — while a wall of storm spins around it.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: The word monsoon comes from an Arabic word meaning 'season.'
questions.say: I am a season of heavy rain that comes every year to India. Farmers wait for me. What am I?

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: Storm names come from alphabetical lists — the first storm each year starts with A!
questions.say: I am a giant storm born over warm ocean water, and scientists give me a person's name. What am I?

questions.q: What do we call a storm with heavy snow and howling winds?
questions.f: In a blizzard, blowing snow can cause a 'whiteout' where you can't see even a few steps ahead.

questions.q: Which cloud name means 'rain' in Latin?
questions.f: When 'nimbus' is in a cloud's name — like cumulonimbus — expect rain!

questions.q: What do we call a long time with no rain at all?
questions.f: During long droughts, lakes can shrink so much that sunken old towns reappear!

questions.q: What is it called when rainwater covers streets and homes?
questions.f: Just six inches of fast-moving flood water can knock a grown-up off their feet.

questions.q: What kind of storm is this cloud brewing?
questions.f: At any moment, about 2,000 thunderstorms are rumbling somewhere on Earth.

questions.q: Light travels faster than sound.
questions.f: That's why you see a lightning flash before you hear its thunder rumble.

questions.q: What do we call a tornado that spins up over water?
questions.f: Waterspouts can suck up fish and frogs and rain them down on land!

questions.q: What is the white line an airplane draws across the sky?
questions.f: Contrails are human-made clouds — ice crystals formed from the plane's hot exhaust.

questions.q: What makes summer air feel hot and sticky?
questions.f: On humid days your sweat can't dry off, so your body feels even hotter.

questions.q: How many times hotter than the Sun's surface is a lightning bolt?
questions.f: The flash reaches your eyes at the speed of light — 300,000 kilometers per second.

questions.q: What is the hottest air temperature ever recorded on Earth?
questions.f: It was measured in 1913 at Furnace Creek in Death Valley, California.

questions.q: Where was Earth's coldest temperature ever recorded?
questions.f: Vostok Station hit minus 89°C in 1983 — tossed boiling water would instantly turn to ice fog.

questions.q: The United States has more tornadoes than any other country.
questions.f: About 1,200 tornadoes touch down in the USA each year, many in 'Tornado Alley.'

questions.q: How big was the largest hailstone ever found in the United States?
c: As big as a car tire
questions.f: It fell in Vivian, South Dakota in 2010 — 8 inches wide and weighing almost 1 kilogram.

questions.q: What is this icy visitor from deep space with a long glowing tail?
questions.f: A comet's tail always points away from the Sun, pushed by the solar wind.

questions.q: What is this band of stars stretching across the night sky?
questions.f: The Milky Way is our home galaxy — it holds over 100 billion stars.

questions.q: A hurricane and a typhoon are the same kind of storm.
questions.f: The name depends on the ocean — hurricane near the Americas, typhoon near Asia, cyclone near India.

questions.q: Which place gets more rain each year than anywhere else on Earth?
questions.f: Mawsynram gets nearly 12 meters of rain a year — deep enough to cover a three-story house.

questions.q: You count 5 seconds between a lightning flash and thunder. How far is the storm?
questions.f: Sound takes about 5 seconds to travel one mile, so counting tells you a storm's distance!

questions.q: What shape is a big raindrop while it falls?
questions.f: Air pushing up flattens falling drops — the teardrop shape is a myth!

questions.q: Which scale rates how strong a tornado is?
questions.f: An EF5 tornado has winds over 200 miles per hour — strong enough to peel pavement off roads.

questions.q: How much can one fluffy white cumulus cloud weigh?
c: About as much as a feather
About as much as a bicycle
About as much as a bathtub of water
questions.f: A cumulus cloud weighs around 500,000 kilograms — the water is just spread into billions of tiny drops.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a real cloud type?
questions.f: In Latin, cirrus means 'curl of hair,' stratus means 'layer,' and cumulus means 'heap.'

questions.q: Which of these places is the driest?
questions.f: Parts of the Atacama went about 400 years without rain — NASA tests Mars robots there!

questions.q: In the water cycle, what happens right after water evaporates?
questions.f: Earth recycles the same water — the glass you drank today may once have been sipped by a dinosaur!

questions.q: Which of these weather events has NEVER really happened?
questions.f: Fish rain, thundersnow, and red dust rain are all real — spaghetti storms are not (yet)!

questions.q: Which planet has the Great Red Spot, a storm bigger than Earth?
questions.f: The Great Red Spot has been raging nonstop for well over 150 years.

questions.q: Which cloud type grows the tallest?
questions.f: Cumulonimbus thunderheads can tower 12 kilometers high — taller than Mount Everest!

questions.q: It has never snowed in the Sahara Desert.
questions.f: Snow has dusted the Sahara's sand dunes several times — most recently in the 2020s!

questions.q: Antarctica is a desert.
questions.f: Deserts are defined by dryness, not heat — inner Antarctica gets less precipitation than parts of the Sahara.

questions.q: Whose shadow is this, watching storms from space?
questions.f: Weather satellites orbit about 22,000 miles up, photographing storms day and night.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: Jet stream winds can top 250 miles per hour — planes riding them arrive early!
questions.say: I am a river of fast wind high above the clouds. Airplanes ride me to travel faster. What am I?

questions.q: Which instrument measures air pressure?
questions.f: Falling air pressure on a barometer often means a storm is on the way.

questions.q: Why does thunder boom after a lightning flash?
c: Lightning heats air so fast it explodes outward
questions.f: Lightning heats air to about 30,000°C in a split second — the shockwave is the boom you hear.

questions.q: What makes a rainbow appear in the sky?
c: Rain washing color from the sky
Lightning splitting the air into colors
questions.f: On bright full-moon nights, moonlight can make a ghostly 'moonbow'!

questions.q: Why is the sky blue?
c: Air scatters blue light more than other colors
The sky reflects the blue ocean
questions.f: At sunset, light crosses more air — the blue scatters away and reds and oranges shine through.

questions.q: How do hailstones grow inside a storm cloud?
c: Updrafts toss frozen drops up and down, adding icy layers
Rain freezes after touching the ground
questions.f: Slice a hailstone open and you'll find onion-like rings — one layer per trip through the cloud.

questions.q: What is the main fuel that powers a hurricane?
questions.f: Hurricanes need seawater of about 26°C or warmer — that's why they fade over cold water or land.

questions.q: What is the earthy smell of rain falling on dry ground called?
questions.f: The scent comes partly from geosmin, a chemical made by soil bacteria — your nose detects tiny traces of it.

questions.q: What is rain that evaporates before ever reaching the ground called?
questions.f: On Venus, sulfuric acid rain evaporates before landing — the whole planet has virga!

questions.q: Almost all weather happens in the troposphere, the lowest layer of air.
questions.f: Nearly all clouds, rain, and storms live in the troposphere — jet planes cruise near its top.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.f: Auroras glow when particles from the Sun crash into gases in our atmosphere and light them up.
questions.say: I glow green and pink, and I dance across the night sky near the North Pole. What am I?

questions.q: How many letters are in the English alphabet?
questions.f: The Greek alphabet gets by with only 24 letters.

questions.q: What do you call more than one mouse?
questions.f: English plurals get weird — but more than one house is never 'hice'!

questions.q: Which of these words copies a real sound?
questions.f: Say it out loud — 'hiccup' sounds just like the thing it names!

questions.q: Which letter is also a word all by itself?
questions.f: 'I' and 'A' are the only one-letter words in English.

questions.q: What kind of letter starts your name when written correctly?
questions.f: Capitals are called 'uppercase' because printers stored them in the upper tray.

questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'cat'?
questions.f: Rhyming words share the same ending sound — cat, hat, bat, splat!

questions.q: Which vowel starts the word 'apple'?
questions.f: Every English word needs at least one vowel sound to work.

questions.q: Which word do we write for the sound of a sneeze?
questions.f: In Japan, a sneeze is written 'hakushon'!

questions.q: What do we call words with opposite meanings, like hot and cold?
questions.f: The grown-up name for them is antonyms!

questions.q: How many main vowels does the English alphabet have?
questions.f: A, E, I, O, U — and sometimes Y sneaks in as a helper!

questions.q: What do we call all the letters from A to Z together?
questions.f: 'Alphabet' comes from alpha and beta, the first two Greek letters.

questions.q: The word 'level' reads the same backward as forward.
questions.f: Words like level are called palindromes — even 'wow' is one!

questions.q: The alphabet song uses the same tune as 'Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star.'
questions.f: 'Baa Baa Black Sheep' borrows the very same tune too!

questions.q: The word 'dog' rhymes with 'cat.'
questions.f: Rhymes need matching endings — dog rhymes with frog and log.

questions.q: Look! What sound word does this animal make?
questions.f: In French, cows say 'meuh'!

questions.q: What sound word does this bird say?
questions.f: People once claimed a duck's quack has no echo — scientists proved it does!

questions.q: This little boat's name reads the same backward. What is it?
questions.f: Kayak comes from the Inuit word 'qajaq' — a palindrome in two languages!

questions.q: This insect gives its name to a famous spelling contest. What's the contest?
questions.f: 'Bee' is an old word for friends gathering to work together, like a quilting bee.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy spell!
questions.say: Listen carefully while I spell a word: B, U, G. What word did I spell?
questions.f: Spelling out loud is exactly what spelling bee champions do!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's rhyme question!
questions.say: Which of these words rhymes with moon: star, spoon, sun, or cloud?
questions.f: Moon, spoon, and balloon all share the same '-oon' ending sound.

questions.q: Which meal name mixes 'breakfast' and 'lunch' together?
questions.f: Squished-together words like brunch are called portmanteau words.

questions.q: What is a group of fish called?
questions.f: Fish swim in schools to stay safer from hungry hunters.

questions.q: Finish the famous sentence: 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy ___.'
questions.f: That sentence is a pangram — it uses every one of the 26 letters!

questions.q: Which punctuation mark ends a question?
questions.f: Spanish questions also start with an upside-down question mark: ¿

questions.q: What do we call two words joined into one, like 'rain' + 'bow'?
questions.f: Butterfly, popcorn, and starfish are all compound words.

questions.q: Which term names words with the same meaning, like 'quick' and 'fast'?
questions.f: 'Synonym' comes from Greek words meaning 'same name.'

questions.q: A dictionary lists its words in what order?
questions.f: Samuel Johnson's famous English dictionary took about nine years to write.

questions.q: What is a group of geese on the ground called?
questions.f: When geese fly in a V shape, the group can be called a skein!

questions.q: Which tiny word is understood in almost every country on Earth?
questions.f: One story says OK began in 1839 as a joke spelling of 'all correct' — 'oll korrect'!

questions.q: Which marks show the exact words someone says in a story?
questions.f: Curly quotation marks look like tiny 66s and 99s.

questions.q: In English words, the letter Q is almost always followed by U.
questions.f: Q brings its buddy U to nearly every word, like queen and quiet.

questions.q: The word 'bark' can mean a dog's sound and also a tree's outer layer.
questions.f: A bat can be an animal or a baseball stick — English loves double-duty words.

questions.q: The word 'jump' copies a real-life sound.
questions.f: Crash, beep, and pop imitate real sounds — jump doesn't.

questions.q: A group of these big cats has a very proud name. What is it?
questions.f: A pride is usually a big family of related lionesses and their cubs.

questions.q: This clock shows a time whose name reads the same backward. What time?
questions.f: The digits 12:21 read the same both ways too!

questions.q: Listen for Bizzy's odd one out!
questions.say: Listen for the odd one out: meow, woof, table, oink. Which is not an animal sound?
questions.f: Table isn't a sound at all — it's just furniture!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy spell a tricky word!
questions.say: Listen while I spell a tricky word: G, E, E, S, E. What word did I spell?
questions.f: One goose, two geese — but one moose is still two moose!

questions.q: What is the tiny dot above the letter i called?
questions.f: The letter j wears a tittle too!

questions.q: How many letters are in the Hawaiian alphabet?
questions.f: Hawaiian's small alphabet builds long words like the fish name humuhumunukunukuapua'a!

questions.q: Which letter appears most often in written English?
questions.f: About one in every eight letters you read is an E.

questions.q: What is a group of puppies born together called?
questions.f: A group of kittens can be called a kindle!

questions.q: Which two words squashed together to make 'smog'?
questions.f: 'Motel' squashes motor and hotel together the very same way.

questions.q: In what year was the first National Spelling Bee held in the United States?
questions.f: The champion, eleven-year-old Frank Neuhauser, won 500 dollars in gold coins.

questions.q: What do we call a sentence that uses every letter of the alphabet?
questions.f: Typists have tested keyboards with 'the quick brown fox' since the 1880s.

questions.q: What are words that sound alike but are spelled differently, like 'flour' and 'flower'?
questions.f: 'Eight' and 'ate' are homophones too — say them out loud, they're twins!

questions.q: The word 'bookkeeper' has three sets of double letters in a row.
questions.f: OO, KK, EE — no other common English word stacks doubles like that!

questions.q: Storybook cats say 'meow' in every language.
questions.f: Japanese cats say 'nyan' and French cats say 'miaou'!

questions.q: A group of these birds shares its name with a group of lawmakers. What is it?
questions.f: Owls earned the lawmaker name because they look so wise.

questions.q: This zoomy machine's name is a palindrome. What is it?
questions.f: Whole sentences can be palindromes too: 'Was it a cat I saw?'

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: Buzz! Hiccup! Splash! I am a word that copies the sound it names. What kind of word am I?
questions.f: 'Onomatopoeia' comes from Greek words meaning 'making a name.'

questions.q: Which of these words is NOT a palindrome?
questions.f: Banana backward is 'ananab' — but madam, rotor, and civic all flip perfectly.

questions.q: Which of these words was NOT made by blending two words?
questions.f: Moped blends motor and pedal, sitcom blends situation and comedy — picnic is just picnic.

questions.q: Which word's letters appear in perfect alphabetical order?
questions.f: 'Almost' is often called the longest common English word in A-to-Z order.

questions.q: Which is the real name for a group of jellyfish?
questions.f: Scientists also call a huge swarm of jellyfish a bloom.

questions.q: Which word can you type using only the top letter row of a keyboard?
questions.f: All ten letters of 'typewriter' sit on the Q-W-E-R-T-Y row.

questions.q: Which word contains none of the vowels A, E, I, O, or U?
questions.f: The letter Y sneaks in and does the vowel's job in 'rhythm.'

questions.q: Which word, written in capital letters, reads the same upside down?
questions.f: Turn SWIMS a full 180 degrees and it still says SWIMS — try it!

questions.q: What was the winning word of the very first National Spelling Bee in 1925?
questions.f: A gladiolus is a flower whose name comes from the Latin for 'little sword.'

questions.q: Every odd number, when spelled out, contains the letter E.
questions.f: OnE, thrEe, fivE, sevEn, ninE — try to escape the E, you can't!

questions.q: What is the wonderfully fancy name for a group of these birds?
questions.f: It fits perfectly — flamboyant means showy and bright!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: Remove my last four letters and I still sound the same. I mean a waiting line. What word am I?
questions.f: 'Queue' sounds like just the letter Q — its last four letters are silent.

questions.q: How many letters are in the longest word in major English dictionaries?
questions.f: It's pneumonoultramicroscopicsilicovolcanoconiosis — a lung illness from breathing fine volcanic dust.

questions.q: Which author invented the term 'portmanteau word' for blends like 'slithy'?
questions.f: Carroll also invented 'chortle' — a blend of chuckle and snort.

questions.q: Which language's alphabet is the world's longest, with 74 letters?
questions.f: Rotokas, spoken in Papua New Guinea, has one of the shortest — about 12 letters.

questions.q: The word 'nerd' first appeared in a book by which author?
questions.f: It popped up in 'If I Ran the Zoo' in 1950 as the name of a funny creature.

questions.q: What was the '&' symbol, the ampersand, once treated as?
questions.f: Kids recited 'X, Y, Z, and per se and' — which slurred into 'ampersand'!

questions.q: The joke word 'hippopotomonstrosesquippedaliophobia' names a fear of what?
questions.f: The prank is that the name for fearing long words is itself 36 letters long!

questions.q: The word 'goodbye' started as a squashed version of which old phrase?
questions.f: Centuries of fast talking shortened it, with 'good' swapped in from greetings like 'good day.'

questions.q: What is the mark that combines a question mark and an exclamation point called?
questions.f: An advertising man invented it in 1962 for astonished questions like 'You did WHAT?!'

questions.q: In 2019, the Scripps National Spelling Bee crowned eight champions at once.
questions.f: The bee ran out of words hard enough to stump them — fans called them the 'octochamps'!

questions.q: Listen closely to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: Hear my riddle: I am a nine-letter word with only one vowel, and I mean powers. What word am I?
questions.f: 'Strengths' is often called the longest English word with just one vowel.

questions.q: Which ocean is the biggest?
questions.f: The Pacific holds more than half of all the ocean water on Earth!

questions.q: What is this fiery mountain called?
questions.f: Big volcanoes can blast ash higher into the sky than airplanes fly!

questions.q: What kind of dry, sandy place is this?
questions.f: Some desert sand dunes grow taller than the Eiffel Tower!

questions.q: In which city does this famous statue stand?
questions.f: The Statue of Liberty was a giant gift to America from the people of France.

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am salty and huge. Waves roll across me and whales dive deep inside me. What am I?
questions.f: We have explored only a tiny part of the deep ocean — most of it is still a mystery!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am a giant chunk of ice floating in the sea. Only my tip peeks above the water. What am I?
questions.f: About 90 percent of an iceberg hides underneath the water!

questions.q: The Amazon rainforest is mostly in which country?
questions.f: The Amazon makes so much moisture it creates its own rain clouds — rivers in the sky!

questions.q: Which ocean would you cross to sail from America to Europe?
questions.f: The Atlantic Ocean gets a few centimeters wider every year as the continents slowly drift apart!

questions.q: Which US state is a chain of volcanic islands in the Pacific?
questions.f: Hawaii's islands were built by volcanoes rising up from the bottom of the sea!

questions.q: Penguins live at the North Pole.
questions.f: Wild penguins live in the south and polar bears live in the north — so they never meet!

questions.q: This side of the globe shows which continents?
questions.f: North and South America are joined by a skinny strip of land called Panama.

questions.q: This famous snow-capped peak is the tallest mountain in which country?
questions.f: Mount Fuji is really a volcano — it last erupted about 300 years ago!

questions.q: What is this tool that helps explorers find north?
questions.f: A compass needle points north because the whole Earth is a giant magnet!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am the biggest rainforest on Earth, and a mighty river with the same name flows through me. What am I?
questions.f: About one in ten of all the animal species on Earth lives in the Amazon!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I spin around once every day, I am covered in blue oceans, and everyone you know lives on me. What am I?
questions.f: Earth is the only planet we know with liquid oceans on its surface!

questions.q: What is the largest island in the world?
questions.f: Greenland is covered by an ice sheet up to 3 kilometers thick!

questions.q: Which river carved the Grand Canyon?
questions.f: The river took millions of years to carve the canyon, which drops more than 1.6 kilometers deep!

questions.q: The Great Barrier Reef was built by billions of tiny animals called what?
questions.f: The reef is so huge that astronauts can spot it from space!

questions.q: What is the tallest waterfall on land?
questions.f: Angel Falls in Venezuela drops so far that its water can turn to mist before hitting the ground!

questions.q: What is the smallest country in the world?
questions.f: Vatican City is so tiny you could walk all the way around it in under an hour!

questions.q: In which super-salty lake do swimmers float like corks?
questions.f: The Dead Sea's shore is the lowest dry land on Earth — over 400 meters below sea level!

questions.q: Which mountain range is home to the world's highest peaks?
questions.f: The name Himalaya means 'home of snow' in the ancient Sanskrit language.

questions.q: What is the longest mountain range on land?
questions.f: The Andes stretch about 7,000 kilometers down the side of South America!

questions.q: Which Italian city has canals full of boats instead of streets?
questions.f: Venice is built on more than 100 tiny islands connected by bridges!

questions.q: The Nile carries more water than any other river on Earth.
questions.f: That champion is the Amazon — it pours out more water than the next seven biggest rivers combined!

questions.q: In parts of Norway, you can see the Sun shining at midnight in summer.
questions.f: It's called the Midnight Sun — above the Arctic Circle, a summer 'day' can last for weeks!

questions.q: On which faraway island do these giant stone heads stand?
questions.f: Many of the giant heads have full stone bodies hidden under the ground!

questions.q: What do we call a giant wave caused by an undersea earthquake?
questions.f: In deep water, a tsunami can race along as fast as a jet plane!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am a huge river of ice that slides down mountains so slowly you cannot see me move. What am I?
questions.f: Glaciers store nearly 70 percent of all the fresh water on Earth!

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a real continent?
questions.f: The Arctic is mostly frozen ocean — but Antarctica in the south is real land under the ice!

questions.q: Which is the largest freshwater lake by surface area?
questions.f: Lake Superior holds enough water to cover North and South America 30 centimeters deep!

questions.q: What is the horseshoe of volcanoes circling the Pacific Ocean called?
questions.f: About three-quarters of all Earth's volcanoes sit along the Ring of Fire!

questions.q: Where was the hottest air temperature on Earth ever recorded?
questions.f: In 1913, Death Valley hit a world record 56.7 degrees Celsius!

questions.q: Which ancient stone city sits high in the mountains of Peru?
questions.f: The Inca built Machu Picchu over 500 years ago without wheels or iron tools!

questions.q: In which country is the Taj Mahal?
questions.f: The Taj Mahal's white marble seems to change color — pinkish at dawn and golden by moonlight!

questions.q: Africa is the only continent crossed by both the equator and the prime meridian.
questions.f: The two lines meet in the ocean near Africa at a spot jokingly called Null Island — where there is no island!

questions.q: Mount Everest is a volcano.
questions.f: Everest was pushed up by two continents slowly crashing together — and they're still pushing!

questions.q: What is this huge spinning storm that forms over warm oceans called?
questions.f: The same storm is called a typhoon or a cyclone in other parts of the world!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am a colorful city in Brazil, and my name means River of January. Which city am I?
questions.f: Portuguese explorers named it in January 1502, mistaking its bay for a giant river mouth!

questions.q: What is the deepest place in all the world's oceans?
questions.f: The Mariana Trench plunges nearly 11 kilometers down — deeper than any mountain is tall!

questions.q: Which mountain is tallest when measured from its base under the sea?
questions.f: From the seafloor, Hawaii's Mauna Kea rises over 10,000 meters — beating Everest!

questions.q: What causes most earthquakes?
c: Giant plates of Earth's crust suddenly slipping
questions.f: Earth's plates creep along about as fast as your fingernails grow!

questions.q: What do scientists call the single supercontinent that existed long ago?
questions.f: Pangaea means 'all the Earth' in Greek — every continent was squished into one!

questions.q: What is the deepest lake in the world?
questions.f: Russia's Lake Baikal holds about 20 percent of all the unfrozen fresh water on Earth!

questions.q: Despite its name, which 'sea' is really the world's largest lake?
questions.f: The Caspian Sea is a lake bigger than the whole country of Germany!

questions.q: What makes the northern lights glow in the sky?
c: Particles from the Sun hitting gases in Earth's air
questions.f: The south has its own light show too — the aurora australis!

questions.q: Which desert is the driest place on Earth outside the poles?
questions.f: Some weather stations in Chile's Atacama Desert have never recorded a single drop of rain!

questions.q: Earth's biggest waterfall is hidden under the ocean.
questions.f: The Denmark Strait cataract drops about 3,500 meters underwater as cold, heavy water sinks below warmer water!

questions.q: Listen to Bizzy's riddle!
questions.say: I am an invisible line in the Pacific. Cross me and you jump a whole day forward or back. What am I?
questions.f: Step across the date line and you can hop into 'tomorrow' — then step right back to 'today'!

questions.q: Which big animal has a long trunk to grab food and spray water?
questions.f: An elephant's trunk has no bones but around 40,000 muscles, strong enough to lift a log yet gentle enough to pick up a single leaf.

questions.q: Which sea animal has eight wiggly arms?
questions.f: An octopus can squeeze its whole body through a gap as small as a coin because it has no bones.

questions.q: Which animal swings from branches and loves to eat bananas?
questions.f: Many monkeys use their tails like an extra hand to hold on tight while they swing.

questions.q: Which bushy-tailed animal gathers nuts and hides them for winter?
questions.f: Squirrels sometimes forget where they buried their nuts, and the leftover ones grow into new trees.

questions.q: Which farm animal loves to roll in the mud and says 'oink'?
questions.f: Pigs roll in mud to cool off and protect their skin from the sun, since they cannot sweat much.

questions.q: Which bird stays awake at night to hunt with big round eyes?
questions.f: An owl's feathers are so soft that it can swoop down almost completely silently.

questions.q: Which tiny insects march in a long line to carry crumbs of food?
questions.f: Ants leave a scent trail so their friends can follow the same path to the food.

questions.q: What does a spider spin to catch flies and other insects?
questions.f: Spider silk is sticky in some spots and dry in others, so the spider can walk on its own web without getting stuck.

questions.q: Which fluffy farm animal gives us soft wool for sweaters?
questions.f: One sheep can grow enough wool in a year to make several warm sweaters.

questions.q: Which pet loves to chase mice and purrs when it is happy?
questions.f: A cat's purr is made by tiny muscles in its throat and may even help its bones heal.

questions.q: Which big cat has a thick fluffy mane around its head?
questions.f: Only male lions grow a mane, and a darker mane usually means a stronger, healthier lion.

questions.q: Which farm bird lays the eggs we often eat for breakfast?
questions.f: A hen can lay around 300 eggs in a single year.

questions.q: What colour are most frogs that live near a pond?
questions.f: A frog's green skin helps it hide among leaves and lily pads so hungry birds cannot spot it.

questions.q: How do fish breathe while they are underwater?
questions.f: Gills pull oxygen straight out of the water so a fish never needs to come up for air.

questions.q: Which animal likes to hang upside down when it sleeps?
questions.f: A bat's feet lock in place automatically, so it can hang all day without using any energy.

questions.q: Which busy insect visits flowers to collect sweet nectar?

questions.q: What do cows eat in the field all day long?
questions.f: A cow can spend up to eight hours a day just chewing grass.

questions.q: Which shelled sea animal walks sideways along the sandy beach?

questions.q: Which sea animal is shaped like a five-pointed star?
questions.f: A starfish has tiny tube feet under each arm that help it creep slowly across the seafloor.

questions.q: Which farm animal eats hay and can gallop very fast?
questions.f: Horses can even sleep standing up because their legs lock in place to hold them steady.

questions.q: Which big grey animal has a thick horn growing on its nose?
questions.f: A rhino's horn is not bone at all but is made of the same stuff as your hair and fingernails.

questions.q: Which little red beetle is covered in black spots?
questions.f: Ladybugs are a gardener's friend because they gobble up bugs that harm plants.

questions.q: Which sea giant breathes air through a hole on top of its head?
questions.f: A whale's blowhole works like a nostril on top of its head, letting it grab a breath at the surface.

questions.q: Which spotted animal has a very long neck to reach tall tree leaves?
questions.f: A giraffe's tongue is about 45 cm long and dark blue-purple to keep it from getting sunburnt.

questions.q: Which horned farm animal loves to climb and nibbles on almost everything?
questions.f: Goats have rectangular pupils, which helps them watch for danger over a very wide area.

questions.q: Which small orange fish is often kept as a pet in a bowl?
questions.f: Goldfish have a much better memory than people think and can be taught simple tricks.

questions.q: What do we call a baby goose?
questions.f: Goslings can walk, swim, and find food within a day of hatching.

questions.q: What do we call a baby duck?

questions.q: What do we call a baby pig?

questions.q: What do we call a baby bear?

questions.q: What do we call a baby frog that has a tail and lives in water?

questions.q: What do we call a baby owl?

questions.q: What do we call a baby seal?

questions.q: What sound does a cat make?

questions.q: What sound does a duck make?

questions.q: What sound does a pig make?

questions.q: What sound does a sheep make?

questions.q: What sound does an owl make?
questions.f: Owls hoot to tell other owls where they are and to claim their patch of forest.

questions.q: What sound does a bee make as it flies?
questions.f: The buzz comes from a bee's wings beating around 200 times every second.

questions.q: What sound does a lion make?
questions.f: A lion's roar can be heard from as far as eight kilometres away.

questions.q: What sound does a horse make?
questions.f: Horses also snort, whinny, and nicker to talk to each other and to people.

questions.q: What do we call the home where bees live and make honey?
questions.f: A single beehive can be home to more than 50,000 busy bees.

questions.q: What do we call a doctor who takes care of animals?
questions.f: The word vet is short for veterinarian, and vets look after everything from hamsters to horses.

questions.q: What do we call a group of puppies all born at the same time?
questions.f: A mother dog can have a litter of anywhere from one to more than ten puppies at once.

questions.q: What word do we use for tame animals we keep at home for company?
questions.f: Cats and dogs are the most popular pets in homes all around the world.

questions.q: Fish use gills to breathe underwater.
questions.f: Gills take in oxygen from the water so fish never need to breathe air like we do.

questions.q: Cats have whiskers on their faces.
questions.f: A cat's whiskers sense the tiniest movement in the air and help it judge if a gap is wide enough to fit through.

questions.q: Cows can fly high up in the sky.
questions.f: Cows have no wings and stay firmly on the ground, though calves do love to jump and skip.

questions.q: A duck's body is covered in feathers.
questions.f: Ducks have a special waterproof coating on their feathers that keeps them dry while swimming.

questions.q: An elephant is one of the smallest animals on Earth.
questions.f: The African elephant is the largest land animal alive, weighing as much as several cars.

questions.q: Which clever sea animal leaps out of the water and clicks to talk?
questions.f: Dolphins call each other with clicks and whistles, and each dolphin has its own special whistle like a name.

questions.q: Which wild animal howls loudly at night?
questions.f: Wolves howl to tell their family where they are, and a howl can carry for many kilometres.

questions.q: Which farm bird crows loudly early in the morning?
questions.f: A rooster starts crowing before sunrise because his body has a built-in clock.

questions.q: Which forest animal grows branch-like antlers on its head?
questions.f: A deer drops its antlers every year and grows a brand new set, a little bigger each time.

questions.q: Which red-furred animal has a long bushy tail and pointy ears?
questions.f: A fox wraps its bushy tail around itself like a warm blanket when it sleeps in the cold.

questions.q: Which black-and-white bird slides on its belly across the ice?
questions.f: Sliding on its belly, called tobogganing, is much faster for a penguin than waddling.

questions.q: Which long, thin creature has no legs and wriggles through the soil?
questions.f: Earthworms are a garden's best helpers because their tunnels let air and water reach plant roots.

questions.q: Which green insect jumps a long way using strong back legs?
questions.f: A grasshopper can leap about 20 times the length of its own body in one jump.

questions.q: Which tiny insect buzzes near your ear and leaves itchy bites?
questions.f: Mosquitoes find people by sensing the warmth of their skin and the breath they puff out.

questions.q: Which tall pink bird often stands on just one leg?
questions.f: Standing on one leg helps a flamingo keep the other leg warm and takes less effort than you would think.

questions.q: Which rainforest bird has a huge, brightly coloured beak?
questions.f: A toucan's giant beak is mostly hollow, so it is much lighter than it looks.

questions.q: Which tiny bird can hover in one spot, beating its wings very fast?
questions.f: A hummingbird's wings can beat more than 50 times a second, making a soft humming sound.

questions.q: Which large white water bird has a long, curved neck?
questions.f: Swans often stay with the same partner for many years and raise their babies together.

questions.q: Which heavy animal cools off all day in African rivers?
questions.f: A hippo can hold its breath for about five minutes and even walk along the river bottom.

questions.q: Which small animal stands up tall on its back legs to keep watch?
questions.f: One meerkat always stands guard while the rest of the group digs and looks for food.

questions.q: Which small animal is covered in prickly spines and rolls into a ball?
questions.f: A hedgehog has around 5,000 spines, and rolling up hides its soft tummy from danger.

questions.q: Which animal looks like it is wearing a black mask over its eyes?
questions.f: Raccoons have such clever paws that they can open jars, bins, and even door latches.

questions.q: Which playful river animal floats on its back while it eats?
questions.f: Otters sometimes hold hands while they sleep floating, so they do not drift apart.

questions.q: Which small pet stuffs food into its puffy cheeks?
questions.f: A hamster's stretchy cheek pouches can hold almost as much food as half its own body.

questions.q: Which tiny grey animal has a long thin tail and squeaks?
questions.f: A mouse can squeeze through a hole no wider than a pencil.

questions.q: Which big furry animal loves to eat honey and berries?
questions.f: A bear's thick fur and fat keep it warm while it naps through the whole winter.

questions.q: Which large ape thumps its chest with its hands?
questions.f: A gorilla drums its chest with cupped hands to say hello or to show how strong it is.

questions.q: Which big cat has a golden coat covered in dark spots?
questions.f: Every leopard's spot pattern is different, just like your fingerprints.

questions.q: Which wobbly sea creature looks like a see-through umbrella?
questions.f: A jellyfish is almost entirely water, which is why it looks so clear and glassy.

questions.q: Which sea animal has a pointy fin that pokes above the water?
questions.f: A shark's skin feels rough like sandpaper because it is covered in tiny tooth-like scales.

questions.q: Which sea animal claps its flippers and barks?
questions.f: A seal can close its nostrils tight shut to keep water out while it dives.

questions.q: Which sea animal has a hard red shell and two big front claws?
questions.f: A lobster keeps growing all its life and must wriggle out of its old shell to get bigger.

questions.q: Which shelled animal swims through the sea using flippers?
questions.f: A sea turtle can swim thousands of kilometres, and its flippers work like paddles.

questions.q: Which fish has a long body shaped like a snake?
questions.f: Some eels hide in rocky holes all day and slide out at night to find food.

questions.q: Which insect flutters around a lamp at night?
questions.f: Moths usually steer by moonlight, so a bright lamp can muddle up their sense of direction.

questions.q: Which insect chirps loudly on warm summer nights?
questions.f: A cricket chirps by rubbing its wings together, a bit like running a finger along a comb.

questions.q: Which sea creature slowly opens and closes its two hard shells?
questions.f: A clam pulls its two shells shut with a strong muscle when it wants to stay safe.

questions.q: What does a snail leave behind as it slides along?
questions.f: The slime lets a snail glide smoothly, even straight up a wall or across a sharp edge.

questions.q: What do we call baby fish?
questions.f: Thousands of fry may hatch at once, but only a few grow up into big fish.

questions.q: What do we call a baby eagle?
questions.f: An eaglet grows so fast that in three months it is nearly as big as its parents.

questions.q: What do we call a big group of bees flying together?
questions.f: Bees swarm when the hive gets crowded and half of them leave to build a brand new home.

questions.q: What do we call the underground home a rabbit digs?
questions.f: Rabbit burrows join up into a maze of tunnels called a warren, with many secret exits.

questions.q: What do we call the cosy home where a bear rests?
questions.f: A bear may line its den with leaves and grass to make a soft winter bed.

questions.q: What do we call the little house where chickens live?
questions.f: Chickens are shut safely in the coop at night to keep foxes away.

questions.q: Where does a horse sleep on a farm?
questions.f: Horses only need a few hours of sleep a night and often doze standing up in the stable.

questions.q: What do we call a horse's hard feet?
questions.f: A hoof is made of the same tough stuff as your fingernails and keeps growing all the time.

questions.q: What do we call the sharp nails on a cat's paws?
questions.f: A cat can pull its claws back inside its paws, which keeps them sharp and its steps silent.

questions.q: What do we call the hard mouth part of a bird?
questions.f: Birds have no teeth, so a beak is shaped for the food each bird eats, from seeds to fish.

questions.q: What do we call the branch-like horns on a deer's head?
questions.f: Antlers are made of bone and can grow more than a centimetre a day in summer.

questions.q: What do we call the flat parts a fish uses to swim?
questions.f: A fish steers with its side fins and pushes forward with the big fin on its tail.

questions.q: What do we call the two long teeth poking out of an elephant's mouth?
questions.f: Tusks are really giant front teeth, and elephants use them to dig and to strip bark.

questions.q: How does a snake move across the ground?
questions.f: A snake pushes against tiny bumps in the ground with its belly scales to slide forward.

questions.q: How does a duck walk on land?
questions.f: A duck waddles because its legs are set far back on its body, which is perfect for swimming.

questions.q: A dolphin must come up to the surface to breathe air.
questions.f: A dolphin is a mammal, so it breathes air through a blowhole and cannot breathe underwater.

questions.q: Fish have feathers.
questions.f: Fish are covered in scales, while feathers belong to birds.

questions.q: Which farm animal has long ears and can pull a heavy cart?
questions.f: Donkeys are very sure-footed and can carry loads along narrow mountain paths.

questions.q: Which woolly animal has a long neck and lives in South America?
questions.f: Llamas hum softly to each other, and a mother llama hums to her baby.

questions.q: Which insect sips nectar through a long tube like a drinking straw?
questions.f: A butterfly keeps its long feeding tube curled up like a party blower when it is not drinking.

questions.q: Which orange fish with white stripes lives among coral?
questions.f: A clownfish hides safely among the stinging arms of a sea anemone, which never stings it.

questions.q: Which tall bird stands very still in shallow water waiting for fish?
questions.f: A heron can stay frozen in place for many minutes, then stab at a fish in the blink of an eye.

questions.q: Which shiny black bird is very clever and calls 'caw'?
questions.f: Crows can use sticks as simple tools and remember which people have been kind to them.

questions.q: Which small garden bird has a bright reddish-orange front?
questions.f: Robins often follow gardeners around, hoping a dug-up worm will pop out of the soil.

questions.q: Which striped insect builds a papery nest and can sting?
questions.f: A wasp chews up wood and mixes it with spit to build its papery nest.

questions.q: Which big bird has a stretchy pouch under its beak for scooping up fish?
questions.f: A pelican's throat pouch can hold several litres of water and fish in one big scoop.

questions.q: Which pet wags its tail when it is happy to see you?
questions.f: Dogs can understand many words and read the look on a person's face.

questions.q: Which round sea animal is covered in sharp spikes?
questions.f: A sea urchin walks slowly on tiny tube feet hidden between its spines.

questions.q: Which large bird has very sharp eyes and hooked claws for catching food?
questions.f: An eagle can spot a small animal moving from as high as a kilometre in the air.

questions.q: Which insect has a hard shiny case covering its wings?
questions.f: There are more kinds of beetle than any other animal on Earth, with hundreds of thousands of species.

questions.q: Which small striped animal fills its cheeks with seeds and lives in the woods?
questions.f: A chipmunk can carry so many seeds in its cheeks that its head looks twice as wide.

questions.q: Which colourful sea creature looks like a rocky plant but is really an animal?
questions.f: A coral reef is built by millions of tiny animals, each smaller than your fingernail.

questions.q: Which bird builds a cup-shaped mud nest under the roofs of houses?
questions.f: Swallows fly thousands of kilometres each year and often return to the very same nest.

questions.q: Which insect can walk upside down on the ceiling?
questions.f: A fly has sticky pads and tiny claws on its feet, so it can grip smooth glass and ceilings.

questions.q: Which small brown bird is famous for singing beautifully at night?
questions.f: A nightingale can sing more than 200 different tunes.

questions.q: Which noisy grey-and-white bird follows boats and lives by the sea?
questions.f: Seagulls can drink salty seawater because special glands get rid of the extra salt.

questions.q: What sound does a turkey make?
questions.f: Only male turkeys gobble, and the sound can be heard a kilometre away.

questions.q: What sound does a snake make?
questions.f: A snake hisses by pushing air out fast, which is its way of saying 'stay away'.

questions.q: What do we call the loud trumpeting sound an elephant makes?
questions.f: An elephant trumpets through its trunk when it is excited, and it can be heard far across the plains.

questions.q: What sound does a hen make?
questions.f: A mother hen clucks softly to her chicks even before they have hatched from their eggs.

questions.q: What do we call the loud 'hee-haw' sound a donkey makes?
questions.f: A donkey's bray can be heard up to three kilometres away across open land.

questions.q: What sound does a goat make?
questions.f: Goats bleat in different voices, and a mother goat knows her own kid's call.

questions.q: What do we call the short, sweet sound a small bird makes?
questions.f: Baby birds chirp loudly to tell their parents they are hungry.

questions.q: What do we call a baby whale?
questions.f: A blue whale calf can drink hundreds of litres of its mother's milk every single day.

questions.q: What do we call a baby turtle that has just come out of its egg?
questions.f: Baby turtle hatchlings hurry straight to the sea as soon as they dig out of the sand.

questions.q: What do we call a butterfly before it grows its wings?
questions.f: A caterpillar can eat many times its own weight in leaves before it is ready to change.

questions.q: What do we call a group of sheep together?
questions.f: Sheep stay close together in a flock because being in a group keeps them safer.

questions.q: What do we call a group of cows in a field?
questions.f: Cows in a herd have best friends and get upset if they are kept apart from them.

questions.q: What do we call a big group of ants living together?
questions.f: An ant colony works as one team, with every ant having its own special job.

questions.q: What do we call the small outdoor house a dog sleeps in?
questions.f: The word kennel comes from an old word for dog, the same root as in the word canine.

questions.q: What do we call the muddy pen where pigs are kept?
questions.f: Pigs actually like to keep their sleeping corner clean and use a separate spot as a toilet.

questions.q: What do we call the glass tank where pet fish are kept?
questions.f: The word aquarium comes from aqua, meaning water.

questions.q: What do we call the soft hair that covers a rabbit's body?
questions.f: A rabbit's fur traps a layer of warm air next to its skin, like wearing a cosy coat.

questions.q: What do we call the wide, flat limbs a seal swims with?
questions.f: Flippers work like paddles in the water, but they make walking on land slow and wobbly.

questions.q: What do we call the long, bendy limbs of an octopus?
questions.f: Each octopus arm is covered in suckers that can grip, feel, and even taste.

questions.q: What do we call the flat nose at the end of a pig's face?
questions.f: A pig's snout is packed with so many smell sensors that pigs are used to sniff out food underground.

questions.q: What do we call the hard, pointed pair of growths on a cow's head?
questions.f: Unlike a deer's antlers, a cow's horns stay on for life and never drop off.

questions.q: What do we call it when a baby bird breaks out of its egg?
questions.f: A chick may take a whole day of tapping and resting before it finally hatches.

questions.q: What word describes an animal that lives free in nature and is not tame?
questions.f: Wild animals find their own food and shelter without any help from people.

questions.q: What do we call a person who keeps cows, sheep, and hens on land?
questions.f: Farmers wake up very early because animals need feeding at the same time every day.

questions.q: What do we call the place where people go to see many kinds of wild animals?
questions.f: The word zoo is short for zoological garden and comes from a Greek word meaning animal.

questions.q: What do we call the hard outer covering of an egg?
questions.f: An eggshell has thousands of tiny holes so that air can reach the growing chick inside.

questions.q: What do we call a mother sheep?
questions.f: A ewe usually has one or two lambs each spring and knows their bleats straight away.

questions.q: A bat is a kind of bird.
questions.f: A bat is a mammal with fur that feeds its babies milk, even though it flies.

questions.q: Ducks have webbed feet that help them push through water.
questions.f: The skin between a duck's toes spreads out like a paddle with every kick.

questions.q: Which is the largest fish swimming in the ocean today?
questions.f: A whale shark can grow longer than a school bus yet feeds mostly on tiny plankton.

questions.q: Which animal has the biggest ears, using them to stay cool in the heat?
questions.f: An elephant flaps its huge ears to cool the blood flowing through them, like a natural fan.

questions.q: Which snake raises a wide hood and sways when it feels threatened?
questions.f: A cobra spreads its hood by lifting the long ribs behind its head to look bigger and scarier.

questions.q: Which small creature spins the silk once used to make fine cloth?
questions.f: A single silkworm cocoon can be unwound into a thread nearly a kilometre long.

questions.q: Which animal sheds its whole skin in one piece as it grows bigger?
questions.f: A snake even sheds the clear scale covering each eye when it wriggles out of its old skin.

questions.q: Which small animal digs underground tunnels and can barely see?
questions.f: A mole can dig a tunnel as long as a football field in a single night.

questions.q: Which bird drums on tree trunks to dig out insects hiding inside?
questions.f: A woodpecker's skull has spongy bone that cushions its brain from all that hammering.

questions.q: Which sea animal squirts a cloud of dark ink to escape danger?
questions.f: The ink cloud confuses a predator and can also dull its sense of smell while the squid darts away.

questions.q: Which is the largest lizard alive today?
questions.f: A Komodo dragon can grow to three metres long and swallow prey almost as big as itself.

questions.q: Which scaly mammal rolls into a tight ball to protect itself?
questions.f: The pangolin is the only mammal covered in hard scales, all made of keratin like your nails.

questions.q: Which animal defends itself by spraying a very smelly liquid?
questions.f: A skunk can spray its stinky mist accurately at a target up to three metres away.

questions.q: Which large Arctic sea mammal has long tusks and bristly whiskers?
questions.f: A walrus uses its tusks like ice picks to haul its heavy body out of the water.

questions.q: Which fast ocean fish has a long, pointed bill like a sword?
questions.f: A swordfish uses its long bill to slash through schools of fish, stunning its next meal.

questions.q: Which animal glides between trees using flaps of skin on its sides?
questions.f: A flying squirrel does not truly fly but can glide the length of several classrooms between trees.

questions.q: What do we call an animal that eats both plants and meat?
questions.f: Bears and pigs are omnivores, happily eating berries, plants, and small animals alike.

questions.q: What do we call a group of monkeys living together?
questions.f: A troop of monkeys grooms one another to stay clean and to keep their friendships strong.

questions.q: What do we call a group of geese on the ground?
questions.f: Once geese take to the air, the same group is instead called a skein.

questions.q: What is the surprising name for a group of crows?
questions.f: Crows are among the cleverest birds and can even recognise individual human faces.

questions.q: What do we call a baby elephant?
questions.f: A newborn elephant calf can already weigh about 100 kilograms, as much as a grown man.

questions.q: What do we call a baby rabbit?
questions.f: Baby rabbits, called kits, are born with no fur and their eyes tightly shut.

questions.q: What do we call the hard case a caterpillar forms before becoming a butterfly?
questions.f: Inside the chrysalis the caterpillar's body breaks down almost completely and rebuilds into a butterfly.

questions.q: An animal described as 'nocturnal' is mostly active at what time?
questions.f: Nocturnal animals like owls and bats have special eyes and ears for hunting in the dark.

questions.q: An 'aquatic' animal is one that lives mainly in what?
questions.f: Aquatic animals such as fish and dolphins have streamlined bodies that slip easily through water.

questions.q: The word 'canine' is used to describe animals related to which pet?
questions.f: Canine comes from the Latin word canis, meaning dog, and wolves and foxes are canines too.

questions.q: What do we call a group of elephants moving together?
questions.f: An elephant herd is usually led by the oldest and wisest female, called the matriarch.

questions.q: Insects, jellyfish, snails, and worms all belong to which large group of animals?
questions.f: About 97 out of every 100 animal species on Earth are invertebrates, meaning they have no backbone.

questions.q: An animal described as 'diurnal' is mostly active at what time?
questions.f: Diurnal animals like squirrels and most birds are busy in the daylight and rest at night.

questions.q: What do we call an animal that is hunted and eaten by another animal?
questions.f: Many prey animals have eyes on the sides of their heads to watch for danger all around them.

questions.q: A slug is basically a snail without a shell.
questions.f: Slugs and snails are close cousins, but slugs lost the big shell over millions of years.

questions.q: Ostriches bury their heads in the sand to hide from danger.
questions.f: This is just a myth; an ostrich actually lowers its head to turn eggs in its nest or to eat.

questions.q: A butterfly can taste with its feet.
questions.f: A butterfly has taste sensors on its feet, so it knows if it has landed on a tasty plant.

questions.q: Which animal group has feathers, wings, and lays hard-shelled eggs?
questions.f: Every bird alive today has feathers, and no other animal group on Earth grows them.

questions.q: Which animal group is cold-blooded, scaly, and lays its eggs on land?
questions.f: Reptile eggs have a leathery shell that keeps the moisture in, so they do not dry out on land.

questions.q: What do all mammal mothers make to feed their babies?
questions.f: Making milk is the one thing every mammal does, from a tiny mouse to a blue whale.

questions.q: An animal that is 'warm-blooded' can do what?
questions.f: Warm-blooded animals burn energy from food to hold their temperature steady, which is why they must eat often.

questions.q: How does a dolphin find fish in murky water?
c: It makes clicks and listens for echoes
It waits for them to glow
questions.f: A dolphin sends out clicks and reads the returning echoes so well that it can tell a rock from a fish.

questions.q: Kangaroos and koalas are found naturally on which continent?
questions.f: Australia broke away from other landmasses long ago, so its pouched mammals evolved in their own world.

questions.q: On which freezing continent do emperor penguins raise their chicks?
questions.f: No penguin species lives naturally at the North Pole, so polar bears and penguins never meet in the wild.

questions.q: Polar bears live naturally in which part of the world?
questions.f: Polar bears roam the sea ice of the far north, hunting where the ice meets open water.

questions.q: Which is the largest kind of bear?
questions.f: A big male polar bear can stand three metres tall on its back legs, taller than two doorways stacked.

questions.q: In a food chain, what is usually the very first link?
questions.f: Plants capture energy from sunlight, and every animal in the chain above them depends on that energy.

questions.q: Why do many desert animals come out only at night?
c: Because they cannot see in daylight
Because plants close in the day
questions.f: A desert can be scorching at noon and chilly by midnight, so night is the safest time to be active.

questions.q: Why do fast-swimming fish have smooth, pointed bodies?
questions.f: A streamlined shape cuts down drag, which is why submarines and fish end up looking rather similar.

questions.q: Besides confusing predators, a zebra's stripes may also help by doing what?
questions.f: Experiments show biting flies land far less often on striped surfaces than on plain ones.

questions.q: How can a snake swallow prey wider than its own head?
c: Its jaw bones stretch far apart
questions.f: A snake's lower jaw is in two halves joined by stretchy tissue, so its mouth can open enormously wide.

questions.q: How many main stages does a butterfly pass through in its life?
questions.f: Egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, and adult make four completely different-looking stages of the same animal.

questions.q: How does a jellyfish catch the tiny animals it eats?
questions.f: Each tentacle is loaded with thousands of microscopic stingers that fire faster than you can blink.

questions.q: Which is the largest wild cat living in Africa?
questions.f: Lions are the only big cats that live in family groups, sharing hunting and cub-raising.

questions.q: How many toes does a horse walk on with each foot?
questions.f: A horse's hoof is really one enormous toenail, and its ancestors had several toes millions of years ago.

questions.q: Which big cat is the top predator of the Amazon rainforest?
questions.f: A jaguar is a strong swimmer and happily hunts in rivers, unlike most other big cats.

questions.q: Which large deer of the frozen tundra grows antlers on both males and females?
questions.f: Reindeer are the only deer where females grow antlers too, useful for digging through snow to reach food.

questions.q: Which fast-flying insect is a champion hunter of mosquitoes?
questions.f: A dragonfly catches nearly every insect it goes after, and it can fly backwards and hover too.

questions.q: Which insects build tall earth mounds and live in colonies ruled by a queen?
questions.f: Some termite mounds reach eight metres high and have built-in air shafts that keep the nest cool.

questions.q: Which is the largest reptile alive today?
questions.f: A big saltwater crocodile can be six metres long and has been known to swim far out to sea.

questions.q: Which sea animal can make a pearl inside its shell?
questions.f: A pearl forms when an oyster wraps a piece of grit in smooth layers to stop it rubbing.

questions.q: What can a crab do if it loses one of its claws?
questions.f: A crab regrows the missing claw a bit at a time each time it moults its shell.

questions.q: What does a beaver do with its wide, flat tail when it senses danger?
questions.f: The loud slap can be heard far along the river and sends the whole beaver family diving for safety.

questions.q: Why do a cat's eyes seem to glow when a light shines on them?
c: A mirror-like layer behind the eye
questions.f: That mirror layer bounces light back through the eye, letting a cat see in near darkness.

questions.q: Why does a dog pant with its tongue out?
questions.f: Dogs barely sweat through their skin, so panting evaporates water from the tongue to shed heat.

questions.q: Why do most birds have hollow bones?
c: To make them lighter for flying
questions.f: Hollow bones with tiny struts inside stay strong while weighing very little.

questions.q: Why does a snake stretch out on a warm rock in the morning?
c: To warm its body with the sun
questions.f: A snake cannot make its own body heat, so soaking up sunshine is how it gets going for the day.

questions.q: Which insect builds a nest of wax cells shaped like six-sided boxes?
questions.f: Hexagons fit together with no wasted space, so bees store the most honey using the least wax.

questions.q: Which animal is famous for flopping over and playing dead when frightened?
questions.f: An opossum does not choose to do it; the shock makes it stiffen up automatically for minutes at a time.

questions.q: Which insect lives for only a day or so once it becomes an adult?
questions.f: An adult mayfly cannot even eat, since it has no working mouthparts and lives just long enough to breed.

questions.q: Which tiny animal can jump over 100 times its own height?
questions.f: A flea stores energy in a springy pad of protein, then releases it all at once like a catapult.

questions.q: Which sense does an owl rely on most to find prey in total darkness?
questions.f: An owl's dish-shaped face funnels sound to its ears so precisely it can catch a mouse hidden under snow.

questions.q: What do we call a group of kangaroos?
questions.f: A mob of kangaroos may have dozens of members, all keeping watch for danger together.

questions.q: What is the old-fashioned name for a group of cats?
questions.f: A group of kittens, on the other hand, is called a kindle.

questions.q: What do we call a group of mice?
questions.f: The name fits, since a mischief of mice can chew through almost anything in a kitchen.

questions.q: What do we call an enormous group of locusts flying together?
questions.f: A single locust plague can contain billions of insects and strip a whole field bare in hours.

questions.q: What do we call a young male horse?
questions.f: A young female horse is called a filly, and both are foals when newborn.

questions.q: What do we call a young bird that has just learned to fly?
questions.f: A fledgling still begs its parents for food for days after leaving the nest.

questions.q: What do we call a baby spider?
questions.f: Hundreds of spiderlings may hatch at once, and some float away on strands of silk like tiny balloonists.

questions.q: What do we call the wormlike young stage of an insect such as a beetle or fly?
questions.f: A larva does almost nothing but eat, growing fast before it changes into an adult.

questions.q: What do we call the resting stage when an insect larva is changing into an adult?
questions.f: Inside the pupa the insect's body is rebuilt almost from scratch.

questions.q: What do we call a male duck?
questions.f: A drake often has brighter feathers than the female, who stays dull to hide on the nest.

questions.q: What do we call a male goose?
questions.f: A gander guards the nest fiercely and will hiss at anything that comes too close.

questions.q: What do we call an adult female horse?
questions.f: A mare carries her foal for about eleven months before it is born.

questions.q: What do we call a male sheep?
questions.f: A ram's curled horns keep growing all its life and can weigh several kilograms.

questions.q: What do we call an adult female pig?
questions.f: A sow builds a nest of straw before her piglets are born, even in a barn.

questions.q: What do we call a female fox?
questions.f: A vixen makes an eerie screaming call in winter that many people mistake for a person shouting.

questions.q: What do we call a female deer?
questions.f: A doe hides her fawn in tall grass and returns only a few times a day to feed it.

questions.q: What do we call the maze of underground tunnels where rabbits live?
questions.f: A big warren can have dozens of entrances so rabbits always have an escape route.

questions.q: What do we call a squirrel's nest of twigs high in a tree?
questions.f: A drey is lined with moss and leaves and is usually built close to the trunk for shelter from wind.

questions.q: What do we call a badger's underground home?
questions.f: Badger setts are used by family after family and some are over a hundred years old.

questions.q: What do we call an eagle's nest built high on a cliff or tall tree?
questions.f: Eagles add sticks to the same eyrie year after year until it can weigh as much as a small car.

questions.q: What do we call a place where bees are kept in hives?
questions.f: Apiary comes from the Latin apis, meaning bee.

questions.q: What do we call a large cage or building where birds are kept?
questions.f: Aviary comes from the Latin avis, meaning bird.

questions.q: The word 'feline' describes animals related to which pet?
questions.f: Feline comes from the Latin feles, meaning cat, and covers lions and tigers as well as house cats.

questions.q: The word 'equine' describes animals related to which creature?
questions.f: Equine comes from the Latin equus, meaning horse, and includes zebras and donkeys.

questions.q: The word 'avian' describes which group of animals?
questions.f: Avian comes from the Latin avis, meaning bird, the same root behind aviator and aviary.

questions.q: What do we call an animal that feeds on animals that are already dead?
questions.f: Scavengers such as vultures and hyenas are nature's clean-up crew, stopping disease from spreading.

questions.q: A dolphin is a kind of fish.
questions.f: A dolphin is a mammal: it breathes air, has warm blood, and feeds its calf milk.

questions.q: A penguin's wings work like flippers for swimming.
questions.f: Penguin wings are stiff and narrow, making them superb paddles but useless for flight.

questions.q: Which bird is the fastest runner on two legs?
questions.f: An ostrich can sprint at about 70 km/h and cover five metres in a single stride.

questions.q: Which sea mammal wraps itself in seaweed so it does not drift away while sleeping?
questions.f: Sea otters also sleep in floating groups called rafts, sometimes hundreds strong.

questions.q: How does a squid shoot quickly through the water?
c: It squirts out a jet of water
questions.f: A squid fills its body with water and blasts it out through a tube, steering by aiming the tube.

questions.q: Which owl lives in burrows in the ground instead of in trees?
questions.f: Burrowing owls often move into tunnels dug by prairie dogs and stand at the entrance like little guards.

questions.q: Which insect can see ultraviolet light, which is invisible to human eyes?
questions.f: Many flowers have ultraviolet patterns that act like landing lights, guiding bees straight to the nectar.

questions.q: Which small desert fox has enormous ears that help it lose body heat?
questions.f: The fennec fox is the smallest wild dog in the world, light enough to sit in your hands.

questions.q: Which is the smallest kind of penguin?
questions.f: The little blue penguin stands only about 33 cm tall and comes ashore after dark.

questions.q: Which animal pokes a stripped twig into a termite mound to fish out a snack?
questions.f: Young chimps learn this trick by watching their mothers for years, which makes it a kind of culture.

questions.q: Which great ape has shaggy orange fur and lives only in Asia?
questions.f: Orangutans build a fresh leafy nest to sleep in nearly every night, high up in the trees.

questions.q: Which gentle sea mammal grazes on seagrass in warm shallow water?
questions.f: A manatee can munch through a tenth of its own body weight in plants every day.

questions.q: Which flat fish has both of its eyes on the same side of its head?
questions.f: A young flounder starts with one eye on each side, and one eye slowly travels over as it grows.

questions.q: How does a starfish eat a shellfish that is too big to swallow?
c: It pushes its stomach out onto the food
It cracks the shell with its arms
It waits for it to open
questions.f: A sea star can turn its stomach inside out through its mouth to digest a meal outside its own body.

questions.q: Which brightly coloured bird dives head-first into a river to catch small fish?
questions.f: A kingfisher can judge exactly where a fish is even though water bends the light.

questions.q: Which forest animal has striped legs and is a close relative of the giraffe?
questions.f: The okapi was unknown to scientists outside Africa until 1901 and has a long dark tongue like a giraffe's.

questions.q: Which tall white bird often builds its big stick nest on rooftops and chimneys?
questions.f: Storks return to the same nest year after year, adding sticks until it weighs hundreds of kilograms.

questions.q: Which animal sleeps with only half its brain at a time so it can keep breathing?
questions.f: One eye stays open while the matching half of the brain rests, then the halves swap over.

questions.q: Roughly how many muscles does a cat have in each ear?
questions.f: All those muscles let a cat swivel each ear separately to pinpoint the faintest rustle.

questions.q: Which farm animal can remember and recognise around 50 different faces?
questions.f: Sheep remember faces of both other sheep and people for two years or more.

questions.q: How many eyelids does a camel have on each eye?
questions.f: The third eyelid is thin enough to see through, so a camel can wipe away sand without going blind in a storm.

questions.q: Which is the largest kind of jellyfish?
questions.f: The tentacles of a lion's mane jellyfish can trail more than 30 metres behind its bell.

questions.q: Which small bird can walk right along the bottom of a fast-flowing stream?
questions.f: A dipper grips stones with its strong feet and flicks over pebbles to find insects underwater.

questions.q: Which fish blows a floating raft of bubbles to hold its eggs?
questions.f: The male builds and guards the bubble nest, catching any egg that sinks and puffing it back up.

questions.q: Which insects look after aphids in order to collect their sweet honeydew?
questions.f: Ants protect aphids from predators and even carry them to fresh plants, rather like tiny farmers with cattle.

questions.q: Which sea animal protects itself by living inside an empty shell it finds?
questions.f: As it grows, a hermit crab must find a bigger shell, and several may queue up to swap shells in order.

questions.q: About how much water can an adult elephant drink in one day?
questions.f: An elephant can suck around eight litres of water into its trunk at once before pouring it into its mouth.

questions.q: Which popular pet rodent is also known by the name 'cavy'?
questions.f: Guinea pigs are not pigs and are not from Guinea; they come from the Andes mountains of South America.

questions.q: Which animal licks its own eyes clean because it has no eyelids to blink with?
questions.f: A clear scale covers each gecko eye, and the gecko keeps it clean with a swipe of its tongue.

questions.q: Which insect goes through a nymph stage that looks like a small version of the adult?
questions.f: A grasshopper nymph simply grows bigger with each moult instead of turning into a pupa.

questions.q: Which bird can copy the calls of many other birds and even mechanical sounds?
questions.f: A lyrebird can imitate other birds so well that scientists have to look twice to know who is singing.

questions.q: Which monkey is famous for its extremely large, drooping nose?
questions.f: The bigger a male proboscis monkey's nose, the louder his honking call carries through the mangrove forest.

questions.q: What do we call the thick layer of fat that keeps whales and seals warm?
questions.f: Blubber can be over 30 cm thick on a bowhead whale, working like a wetsuit made of fat.

questions.q: What do we call the comb-like plates some whales use to strain food from seawater?
questions.f: Baleen is made of keratin, the same material as your fingernails, and it filters tonnes of krill.

questions.q: What do we call the hard shell covering the back of a crab or turtle?
questions.f: A turtle's lower shell has its own name too: the plastron.

questions.q: Spiders, scorpions, and ticks all belong to which group of animals?
questions.f: Arachnids have eight legs and no antennae, which is the easiest way to tell them from insects.

questions.q: What do we call colours and patterns that help an animal blend into its surroundings?
questions.f: Camouflage comes from a French word meaning to disguise, and it works for hunters and hunted alike.

questions.q: What do we call the long yearly journey animals make to find food or warmth?
questions.f: Migration comes from a Latin word meaning to move from one place to another.

questions.q: What does it mean if an animal is 'extinct'?
questions.f: Extinct comes from a Latin word meaning put out, like a flame that has been snuffed.

questions.q: What does it mean if an animal is 'endangered'?
c: So few are left that it may die out
questions.f: Giant pandas were once endangered, but careful protection has slowly increased their numbers.

questions.q: What does 'domesticated' mean when we talk about animals?
c: Tamed and raised by people over many generations
questions.f: Dogs were the first domesticated animals, living alongside people for well over 15,000 years.

questions.q: What do we call an animal that hunts and eats other animals?
questions.f: Predator comes from a Latin word meaning to seize, and predators keep prey numbers in balance.

questions.q: What do we call the harmful liquid a snake injects when it bites?
questions.f: Venom is really super-strong spit, and scientists now turn some venoms into life-saving medicines.

questions.q: What do we call the way bats and dolphins find things using sound echoes?
questions.f: Echolocation builds a sound picture so detailed that a bat can catch a moth in complete darkness.

questions.q: What do we call it when a bird sheds its worn feathers and grows new ones?
questions.f: Most birds moult a few feathers at a time so that they can keep flying throughout.

questions.q: What do we call all the eggs a bird lays in one nesting attempt?
questions.f: Once the eggs hatch, the group of chicks is instead called a brood.

questions.q: What do we call the mass of eggs a fish or frog lays in water?
questions.f: A single frog can lay thousands of eggs in one jelly-like blob of spawn.

questions.q: What do we call the sweet liquid inside flowers that insects come to drink?
