questions.f: Layered in different arrangements, the same protein makes something as soft as hair or as hard as a hoof.

questions.q: A stretchy protein that lets skin snap back after a pinch, and whose slow loss over decades brings wrinkles: what is it called?
questions.f: A single elastin fibre can stretch to twice its length and still recoil.

questions.q: A word from the Greek for 'clear water', a fluid with no pump of its own, and a liquid moved along purely by your own movements: what is it?
questions.f: Sitting still for hours is why ankles can puff up; walking is the lymph system's engine.

questions.q: A structure named from the Latin for 'threshold', the entrance chamber of the inner ear, sitting between cochlea and canals: what is it?
questions.f: Its name is why the balance system as a whole is called the vestibular system.

questions.q: A word meaning 'to squeeze together', a ring of muscle that guards an opening, and the gatekeeper at the stomach's exit: what is this class of muscle?
questions.f: Your body has dozens of them, from your eyelids to the base of your bladder.

questions.q: A term from Greek words meaning 'to wrap around', a wave that travels in only one direction, and the reason swallowing works upside down: what is it?
questions.f: An astronaut in zero gravity can swallow perfectly well thanks to this muscular wave.

questions.q: A word combining Greek roots for 'same' and 'standing still', naming the body's habit of holding conditions steady: what is it?
questions.f: Sweating, shivering and thirst are all this principle quietly at work.

questions.q: A gland named from the Latin for 'tears', tucked above the outer edge of each eye, and the reason crying makes you sniff: which is it?
questions.f: Tears drain into your nose through a tiny duct, which is why a good cry blocks it up.

questions.q: A groove almost everyone has between nose and upper lip, once believed by the Greeks to be the body's most romantic spot: what is it called?
questions.f: Its name comes from a Greek word meaning 'love potion'.

questions.q: A fold of tissue under your tongue, a name meaning 'little bridle', and the tether that can be clipped in a baby who cannot latch: what is it?
questions.f: You have several frenula in the body, including small ones inside your lips.

questions.q: A term from Latin for the armpit, a hollow crowded with lymph nodes, and the place a doctor checks for swelling: what is it?
questions.f: That is why swollen glands under the arm are described as axillary nodes.

questions.q: A hollow behind the knee named from a Latin word for the ham of the leg, crossed by nerves and vessels: what is this region called?
questions.f: The artery running through it is a favourite spot for surgeons checking leg circulation.

questions.q: A term from Latin for the big toe, the pillar you push off with at the end of every step: what is it called?
questions.f: Losing this single toe affects walking more than losing all four of the others.

questions.q: An anatomical word for the thumb, the digit whose muscles let humans grip a pen precisely: what is it?
questions.f: Only primates have a thumb that can swing across to touch every fingertip.

questions.q: A word from Latin for 'cheek', used for the inside lining of your mouth and for medicine you tuck there: which term is it?
questions.f: Some medicines are absorbed through the buccal lining straight into the blood.

questions.q: A word from Latin for 'sole', describing the surface you press with every step and the fascia that can inflame beneath it: which is it?
questions.f: Plantar fasciitis is a common ache in runners, felt sharply first thing in the morning.

questions.q: A bone named from a Latin word meaning 'to chew', the only skull bone that moves freely: which is it?
questions.f: It is also the strongest bone in the face, built to take enormous chewing force.

questions.q: The upper jaw, fixed firmly to the rest of the skull, and the bone that holds your top teeth is called…?
questions.f: Because the maxilla cannot move, all the work of chewing falls to the lower jaw.

questions.q: A bone named after a Greek word for a 'wedge', sitting at the centre of the skull and cradling the pituitary: which is it?
questions.f: It touches almost every other skull bone, locking the whole structure together.

questions.q: A bone named for its resemblance to a sieve, riddled with holes for smell fibres, high inside the nose: which is it?
questions.f: Nerve threads from your nose thread through its holes on the way to the brain.

questions.q: A term from Latin for 'little hammer', the bony bump you can feel on each side of your ankle: what is it called?
questions.f: You have an inner one from the tibia and an outer one from the fibula.

questions.q: A bone named after an ancient gaming die, forming the top of the ankle joint and taking your full weight: which is it?
questions.f: Roman soldiers really did use animal ankle bones as dice, which is how it got the name.

questions.q: A word from the Latin for 'knuckle', used for the rounded knobs at the end of a bone where it meets a joint: what is it?
questions.f: You can feel the condyles of your femur as the two bumps just above your knee.

questions.q: A word meaning 'runner', naming the big bony bumps at the top of your thigh bone where muscles pull: what is it?
questions.f: You can feel the greater trochanter as the hard point on the side of your hip.

questions.q: A word from the Greek for 'shuttle', used for the boat-shaped wrist bone most often broken in a fall: which term is it?
questions.f: Its blood arrives from one end only, so a break there is notoriously slow to heal.

questions.q: Bone is stronger than concrete when measured by how much squeezing force it can take.
questions.f: A cubic inch of bone can bear loads of thousands of kilograms, yet it stays light.

questions.q: About 480 million alveoli give the lungs a surface area roughly the size of a tennis court.
questions.f: Folding that huge surface into your chest is one of the body's neatest packing tricks.

questions.q: A single red blood cell carries roughly 270 million molecules of hemoglobin.
questions.f: Each hemoglobin molecule grips up to four oxygen molecules, so one cell hauls a billion of them.

questions.q: An adult body contains about four grams of iron, most of it inside red blood cells.
questions.f: That is roughly the weight of a small nail, spread through your entire bloodstream.

questions.q: The human body has roughly 360 joints, far more than its 206 bones.
questions.f: Many are fixed joints in the skull and pelvis that barely move at all.

questions.q: Which element is the most abundant in the human body by number of atoms?
questions.f: Oxygen wins by weight, but water gives you two hydrogen atoms for every oxygen one.

questions.q: Roughly what fraction of the energy in your food does your brain consume at rest?
questions.f: That works out to around 20 watts, roughly the power of a dim light bulb.

questions.q: A person who takes care of a garden is called a...?
questions.f: A gardener plants, waters, and weeds to help a garden grow.

questions.q: On which part of a tree do apples grow?
questions.f: Apples ripen on the branches before we pick them.

questions.q: A very young, thin tree is called a...?
questions.f: A sapling is a young tree with a slim, bendy trunk.

questions.q: Which flower turns into a fluffy puffball you can blow?
questions.f: Each dandelion puff is a bunch of seeds ready to float away.

questions.q: A group of fruit trees grown together is called an...?
questions.f: Farmers grow apples and oranges in neat rows in an orchard.

questions.q: Which yellow, curved fruit grows in big bunches?
questions.f: Bananas grow in bunches called hands on tall leafy plants.

questions.q: A person who sells flowers is called a...?
questions.f: A florist arranges flowers into pretty bunches called bouquets.

questions.q: Which vegetable is often cut up to make french fries?
questions.f: Potatoes grow underground and can be baked, mashed, or fried.

questions.q: What do we call a flower before it opens up?
questions.f: A bud is a tight little package that opens into a flower.

questions.q: What do many trees drop from their branches in autumn?
questions.f: Many trees shed their leaves in fall and grow new ones in spring.

questions.q: A place where flowers and plants are grown on purpose is a...?
questions.f: People plant gardens to grow food and pretty flowers.

questions.q: Which red fruit do we often slice onto pizza?
questions.f: Tomatoes grow on vines and turn from green to red as they ripen.

questions.q: What do we call a bunch of cut flowers tied together?
questions.f: A bouquet is a gift of flowers arranged into a pretty bunch.

questions.q: What does a visiting bee help a flower do?
questions.f: As bees gather nectar they carry pollen, helping flowers make seeds.

questions.q: A plant that climbs up walls and fences is called a...?
questions.f: Vines have long stems that climb and cling as they grow.

questions.q: Which drink is made by squeezing oranges?
questions.f: Oranges are full of sweet juice and vitamin C.

questions.q: Someone whose job is to study how plants grow is a...?
questions.f: A botanist learns how plants grow, feed, and make seeds.

questions.q: What grows on a rose stem that can prick your finger?
questions.f: Roses have sharp thorns that help protect the plant.

questions.q: What is the plural of the word "leaf"?
questions.f: One leaf, many leaves - the spelling changes in the middle.

questions.q: Which sweet treat is made from cocoa tree beans?
questions.f: Chocolate is made from roasted cocoa beans that grow in pods on trees.

questions.q: A "treehouse" is a play house built up in a...?
questions.f: A treehouse is built among a tree’s strong branches.

questions.q: Which small green vegetables grow lined up inside a pod?
questions.f: Several round peas grow in a row inside each long green pod.

questions.q: What do we call plants that farmers grow for food?
questions.f: Wheat, corn, and rice are important food crops around the world.

questions.q: What color is a ripe lemon?
questions.f: Lemons start green and turn bright yellow when ripe and sour.

questions.q: Which food is made from wheat that has been ground into flour?
questions.f: Wheat grains are ground into flour and baked into bread.

questions.q: What is the special plural of the word "cactus"?
questions.f: "Cacti" is the plural of cactus, borrowed from Latin.

questions.q: Where do potato plants grow their potatoes?
questions.f: Potatoes are swollen underground stems called tubers.

questions.q: A "rosebush" is a thorny plant that grows...?
questions.f: A rosebush grows many rose flowers on prickly stems.

questions.q: Which plant gives us the kernels that pop into popcorn?
questions.f: Popcorn kernels puff up into fluffy popcorn when heated.

questions.q: What do we call the sweet smell a flower makes?
questions.f: A flower’s scent helps attract bees and butterflies.

questions.q: Which juicy fruit has one big hard pit in the middle?
questions.f: Peaches, plums, and cherries all have a hard pit called a stone.

questions.q: What do we call tree wood that is cut for building?
questions.f: Timber is wood cut from trees to build houses and furniture.

questions.q: What do we call the skin we peel off a banana or orange?
questions.f: The peel protects the soft, tasty fruit inside.

questions.q: A "flowerpot" is a container made for growing a...?
questions.f: A flowerpot holds soil so a plant can grow in it.

questions.q: Which part of a lettuce plant do we usually eat?
questions.f: Crunchy lettuce leaves are often used in salads.

questions.q: What is the plural of the word "berry"?
questions.f: One berry, many berries - the "y" becomes "ies".

questions.q: A "greenhouse" is a glass building used to grow...?
questions.f: A greenhouse traps sunlight and warmth to help plants grow.

questions.q: Which fruit does the saying "keeps the doctor away" talk about?
questions.f: "An apple a day keeps the doctor away" is an old healthy-eating saying.

questions.q: What do we call a person who grows crops on a farm?
questions.f: Farmers plant, care for, and harvest crops like wheat and corn.

questions.q: Which vegetable often makes people cry when it is cut?
questions.f: Cutting an onion releases a gas that stings the eyes.

questions.q: The word "seedling" tells you a plant is very...?
questions.f: A seedling is a tiny young plant that has just started to grow.

questions.q: What do we call the soft, colorful parts of a flower?
questions.f: Petals are often bright to attract bees and butterflies.

questions.q: Which tall grass plant is grown in flooded fields for food?
questions.f: Rice grows in wet fields called paddies and feeds billions of people.

questions.q: A "weed" is a plant that grows where people...?
questions.f: Weeds are wild plants that pop up where gardeners don’t want them.

questions.q: Which big orange fruit is carved into a lantern at Halloween?
questions.f: Pumpkins are giant fruits that grow on long trailing vines.

questions.q: What is the plural of the word "tomato"?
questions.f: Tomato adds "es" to become tomatoes.

questions.q: What do we call the time when farmers gather ripe crops?
questions.f: The harvest is the season when ripe crops are picked.

questions.q: A "meadow" is an open field full of grass and...?
questions.f: A meadow is covered in grasses and colorful wildflowers.

questions.q: Which leafy green vegetable is said to make you strong?
questions.f: Spinach is a leafy green packed with iron and vitamins.

questions.q: The words "petal" and "pedal" sound alike, but a petal is part of a...?
questions.f: A petal is a flower part; a pedal is what your foot pushes.

questions.q: Which plant gives us the fluffy fibers used to make soft cloth?
questions.f: Cotton grows in fluffy white bolls that are spun into thread.

questions.q: Which long, green vegetable with bumpy skin is often sliced into salads?
questions.f: Cucumbers grow on trailing vines and are mostly water, so they stay crisp.

questions.q: What do we call all the plants of a place, like a country?
questions.f: "Flora" means the plants of a place; "fauna" means the animals.

questions.q: What do we call the long central part that holds a flower up?
questions.f: The stem carries water up and holds the flower toward the sun.

questions.q: A pumpkin grows on a vine that creeps along the ground.
questions.f: Pumpkins grow on sprawling vines that spread across the soil.

questions.q: Carrots can be orange, purple, or even white.
questions.f: Carrots come in many colors; the familiar orange kind was bred later.

questions.q: All plants need at least some water to stay alive.
questions.f: Every plant needs water, though desert plants need only a little.

questions.q: A daisy is a kind of flower.
questions.f: Daisies have white petals around a bright yellow center.

questions.q: Some trees can grow taller than a house.
questions.f: Many trees grow far taller than a house, some over 300 feet.

questions.q: Grass is a type of plant.
questions.f: Grass is a green plant that covers lawns, fields, and meadows.

questions.q: When a flower "blooms," it means its petals have opened.
questions.f: When a flower blooms, its petals open up wide.

questions.q: A vine is a plant that climbs or creeps as it grows.
questions.f: Vines have long, flexible stems that climb walls and fences.

questions.q: The word "orchard" means a place where fruit trees grow.
questions.f: An orchard is land planted with rows of fruit or nut trees.

questions.q: Which insect, besides bees, flutters between flowers by day?
questions.f: Butterflies sip nectar and help carry pollen between flowers.

questions.q: What do we call a plant that has just started to grow from a seed?
questions.f: A sprout is the first tiny shoot that pushes up from a seed.

questions.q: What do we call the fine soil that plants send their roots into?
questions.f: Plants grow their roots down into soil, or dirt, to find water.

questions.q: What do we call someone who plants and tends trees in a forest?
questions.f: A forester looks after forests, planting and caring for the trees.

questions.q: What are the tubes that carry water up from a plant’s roots called?
questions.f: Xylem tubes carry water and minerals upward from roots to leaves.

questions.q: The root "photo" in "photosynthesis" means...?
questions.f: From Greek "photos," meaning light - the energy plants use to make food.

questions.q: Which gas do plants release into the air as they make food?
questions.f: Plants take in carbon dioxide and give off oxygen we breathe.

questions.q: A plant that lives for only one growing season is called an...?
questions.f: An "annual" lives one year, from Latin "annus," meaning year.

questions.q: Which desert plant stores water in its thick, fleshy stem?
questions.f: A cactus swells with stored water to survive long dry spells.

questions.q: The word "herb" usually means a plant used for...?
questions.f: Herbs like basil and mint add flavor and were once common medicines.

questions.q: What are the tiny grains a flower makes to fertilize other flowers?
questions.f: Pollen is the fine powder that helps flowers make seeds.

questions.q: The prefix "ever" in "evergreen" tells you the tree stays green...?
questions.f: Evergreens keep green leaves through every season, all year long.

questions.q: Which part of a flower makes the pollen?
questions.f: The stamen is the flower’s pollen-making part.

questions.q: Which tree keeps its needles and cones through the whole winter?
questions.f: Pines are conifers that stay green and hold their needles all year.

questions.q: The word "petal" comes from a root meaning a thin, spread-out...?
questions.f: From Greek "petalon," meaning a leaf or thin plate.

questions.q: What do we call the swollen underground stem of a potato?
questions.f: A tuber is a fat underground stem that stores food for the plant.

questions.q: What do we call the useful powdery mix of rotted plants for soil?
questions.f: Compost is rotted plant matter that adds nutrients back to soil.

questions.q: Which part of a plant grows upward toward the light?
questions.f: Shoots grow up toward light while roots grow down toward water.

questions.q: What do we call a person whose job is arranging and growing gardens?
questions.f: A gardener designs, plants, and tends gardens of all kinds.

questions.q: The root "hydro" in "hydroponic" plants means...?
questions.f: Hydroponic plants grow in water, from Greek "hydor," meaning water.

questions.q: Which broad-leaved tree gives us acorns AND strong furniture wood?
questions.f: Oaks drop acorns and provide tough, long-lasting timber.

questions.q: What do we call the tiny openings on a leaf that let gases pass?
questions.f: These pores, called stomata, let carbon dioxide in and oxygen out.

questions.q: A plant that comes back and lives many years is called a...?
questions.f: A perennial keeps living year after year; from Latin "per annum."

questions.q: Which food crop is a grass that gives us the grain for tortillas?
questions.f: Corn, also called maize, is a tall grass grown for its grain.

questions.q: The word "root" in a plant and a word’s "root" both mean the...?
questions.f: A root anchors a plant; a word root is the base other words grow from.

questions.q: What do we call the study of plants as a branch of science?
questions.f: Botany is the science of plants; a scientist who studies it is a botanist.

questions.q: Which tree oozes a sticky, golden fluid we call resin?
questions.f: Pine resin is a sticky sap that can harden and protect the tree.

questions.q: What do we call a plant grown mainly for its beautiful flowers?
questions.f: Ornamental plants, like tulips and roses, are grown for their looks.

questions.q: Which fluffy white crop is picked from bolls and spun into thread?
questions.f: Cotton fibers grow around the plant’s seeds in puffy bolls.

questions.q: The suffix "-ist" in "botanist" tells you it is a...?
questions.f: The suffix "-ist" names a person, like artist or botanist.

questions.q: What do we call trees that lose all their leaves each autumn?
questions.f: Deciduous trees shed their leaves; the word means "tending to fall."

questions.q: Which vegetable is really the flower buds of a green plant?
questions.f: Broccoli heads are clusters of tiny unopened flower buds.

questions.q: What do we call the outer protective layer on a tree trunk?
questions.f: Bark shields the living wood beneath from weather and insects.

questions.q: The word "florist" comes from a root that means...?
questions.f: From Latin "flos, floris," meaning flower.

questions.q: Which plant part grows first and anchors a sprouting seed?
questions.f: The root pushes down first to anchor the seedling and drink water.

questions.q: What do we call a large group of trees grown for their wood?
questions.f: A plantation is a big area planted with one crop, like trees.

questions.q: The root "flor" in "flora" and "floral" means...?
questions.f: "Flor" comes from Latin for flower; "flora" means a region’s plants.

questions.q: Which sweet syrup is boiled down from the sap of a certain tree?
questions.f: Maple sap is collected in spring and boiled into thick sweet syrup.

questions.q: What do we call plants like moss that make spores instead of seeds?
questions.f: Mosses are simple plants that spread by tiny spores, not seeds.

questions.q: The word "sapling" is built from "sap," the liquid that...?
questions.f: Sap carries food and water inside a tree; a sapling is a young tree.

questions.q: Which brightly colored plant part is designed to attract insects?
questions.f: Colorful flowers lure bees and butterflies that carry pollen.

questions.q: What do we call a scientist who studies and grows trees?
questions.f: An arborist cares for trees; the word comes from Latin "arbor," tree.

questions.q: Which climbing fruit plant gives us raisins when its fruit is dried?
questions.f: Dried grapes become raisins, sultanas, and currants.

questions.q: The prefix "photo-" appears in "photosynthesis" and "photograph" to mean...?
questions.f: Both words share the Greek root "photos," meaning light.

questions.q: What do we call the fine threads at root tips that soak up water?
questions.f: Tiny root hairs greatly increase the surface that absorbs water from soil.

questions.q: Which crop plant’s seeds are pressed to make cooking oil, like sunflower?
questions.f: Sunflower seeds are crushed to make a light cooking oil.

questions.q: What do we call a young shoot growing from a seed or a stem?
questions.f: A sprout is the tender new growth that appears from a seed or bud.

questions.q: Which part of a strawberry plant runs sideways to grow new plants?
questions.f: Strawberries send out runners that root and become new plants.

questions.q: The word "orchard" and the word "yard" both name a piece of...?
questions.f: An orchard is ground planted with fruit trees; a yard is open ground.

questions.q: Which tree’s wood is traditionally used to make cricket bats?
questions.f: Cricket bats are carved from light, springy willow wood.

questions.q: What do gardeners call unwanted wild plants that crowd out crops?
questions.f: Weeds compete with crops for water, light, and space.

questions.q: The root "aqua" links "aquatic plants" to which thing they live in?
questions.f: Aquatic plants grow in water; "aqua" is Latin for water.

questions.q: Which fast-growing woody grass is used to build houses and floors?
questions.f: Bamboo is a giant grass strong enough for building and flooring.

questions.q: What do we call a plant, like ivy, whose stem is too weak to stand alone?
questions.f: Climbers lean on walls, trees, or trellises to reach the light.

questions.q: The word "seed" in "seedling" and "seedy" points to a plant’s...?
questions.f: Both words relate to seeds, the tiny starts of new plants.

questions.q: Which nutrient-rich mineral in soil helps make leaves green and leafy?
questions.f: Nitrogen helps plants build the green pigment and grow lush leaves.

questions.q: What do we call a plant kept and grown inside a house?
questions.f: Houseplants brighten rooms and can help clean the air.

questions.q: Which part of the wheat plant is ground to make flour?
questions.f: The grains, or seeds, of wheat are milled into flour.

questions.q: The word "bloom" and "blossom" both describe a plant when it...?
questions.f: To bloom or blossom is to open flowers.

questions.q: Which juicy citrus fruit is sour, yellow, and full of vitamin C?
questions.f: Lemons grow on small evergreen trees and taste tart and sour.

questions.q: What do we call the leafy roof formed by the tops of forest trees?
questions.f: The canopy is the layer of leaves and branches high above the ground.

questions.q: The word "germinate" describes what a seed does when it...?
questions.f: To germinate is to sprout and begin growing into a plant.

questions.q: Which of these is a fruit that scientists say is really a berry?
questions.f: Botanically a banana is a berry, while a strawberry is not.

questions.q: What do we call a hedge or row of shrubs planted as a leafy wall?
questions.f: A hedge is a living wall made of closely planted shrubs.

questions.q: Deciduous trees drop their leaves in autumn, while conifers keep theirs.
questions.f: Deciduous means "tending to fall," so those trees shed their leaves each year.

questions.q: Chlorophyll is the pigment that makes plant leaves look green.
questions.f: Chlorophyll absorbs sunlight for photosynthesis and reflects green light.

questions.q: A cactus is a type of plant that stores water in its stem.
questions.f: Cactus stems swell with stored water to survive the dry desert.

questions.q: Roots usually grow downward while a plant’s stem grows upward.
questions.f: Roots reach down toward water while stems climb up toward the light.

questions.q: Pollen must reach a flower for it to make seeds.
questions.f: Pollination brings pollen to a flower so seeds can form.

questions.q: Bamboo is actually a very tall, fast-growing type of grass.
questions.f: Bamboo belongs to the grass family and can shoot up remarkably fast.

questions.q: A "perennial" plant dies completely after one summer.
questions.f: Perennials live for many years, regrowing each season.

questions.q: A seed needs water, warmth, and air before it will start to sprout.
questions.f: With moisture, warmth, and oxygen, the tiny embryo inside a seed swells and grows.

questions.q: What do we call the fine dust roots pull water and food from?
questions.f: Healthy soil holds the water, air, and minerals that roots need.

questions.q: The word "chlorophyll" combines Greek roots meaning green and...?
questions.f: From "chloros" (green) and "phyllon" (leaf) - the green stuff in leaves.

questions.q: What do we call the network of underground threads fungi share with trees?
questions.f: Mycorrhizal fungi trade nutrients with tree roots in a helpful partnership.

questions.q: The root "dendro" in "dendrology" refers to the study of...?
questions.f: Dendrology is the study of trees; "dendron" is Greek for tree.

questions.q: Which process moves water from a plant’s leaves into the air?
questions.f: Transpiration is the evaporation of water from tiny leaf pores.

questions.q: The prefix "photo-" plus "-synthesis" (putting together) means making food with...?
questions.f: "Synthesis" means combining; photosynthesis builds sugar using light.

questions.q: Which tube system carries sugary food down from a plant’s leaves?
questions.f: Phloem carries sugars made in leaves to the rest of the plant.

questions.q: The word "deciduous" comes from a Latin root meaning to...?
questions.f: From Latin "decidere," to fall - deciduous trees drop their leaves.

questions.q: What do we call the way a sunflower turns to follow the sun?
questions.f: Heliotropism is growth or movement toward the sun; "helios" means sun.

questions.q: Which flower part receives pollen and leads down to the seeds?
questions.f: The pistil is the female part; pollen lands on its sticky tip.

questions.q: The root "carn" in "carnivorous plant" tells you it eats...?
questions.f: Carnivorous plants trap insects; "carn" is Latin for flesh or meat.

questions.q: Which layer just under the bark makes a tree grow wider each year?
questions.f: The cambium is a thin growing layer that adds new wood and bark.

questions.q: The word "annual" means one year and "biennial" means how many years?
questions.f: A biennial plant completes its life over two years; "bi-" means two.

questions.q: What do we call the study and growing of garden plants?
questions.f: Horticulture comes from Latin "hortus," garden, plus "cultura," growing.

questions.q: Which tiny leaf pores open and close to control gas and water loss?
questions.f: Stomata are pores that let carbon dioxide in and oxygen and vapor out.

questions.q: The root "hydro" in "hydroponics" tells you the plants grow in...?
questions.f: Hydroponic plants grow in nutrient-rich water instead of soil.

questions.q: Which giant cactus of the American Southwest can grow tall arms?
questions.f: The saguaro grows arm-like branches and can live over 150 years.

questions.q: What do we call the two-word Latin naming system for every plant species?
questions.f: Linnaeus’s system gives each species a genus and species name, like Rosa canina.

questions.q: The suffix "-culture" in "agriculture" and "horticulture" means...?
questions.f: From Latin "cultura," the tending or cultivating of living things.

questions.q: Which fruit type is a fleshy fruit with a single hard stone, like a cherry?
questions.f: A drupe has soft flesh around one hard pit; peaches and plums are drupes.

questions.q: What do we call all of a region’s plant life taken together?
questions.f: "Flora" is the plant life of a place; "fauna" is the animal life.

questions.q: The word "petiole" names the small stalk that joins a leaf to the...?
questions.f: The petiole is the slender stalk connecting a leaf blade to the stem.

questions.q: Which sweet liquid do flowers make to reward pollinating insects?
questions.f: Nectar is a sugary liquid that lures bees, butterflies, and birds.

questions.q: The root "geo" in "geranium" comes from a Greek word for a crane, a...?
questions.f: Geranium seed pods look like a crane’s bill; "geranos" means crane.

questions.q: What do we call the age rings you count inside a cut tree trunk?
questions.f: Each year usually adds one ring, so counting them gives the tree’s age.

questions.q: Which family do wheat, rice, corn, and bamboo all belong to?
questions.f: These staple food plants are all members of the grass family.

questions.q: The word "germinate" comes from Latin "germen," meaning a...?
questions.f: To germinate is to sprout; "germen" means a bud or shoot.

questions.q: Which non-green plant is really a fungus, not a true plant at all?
questions.f: Mushrooms lack chlorophyll and belong to the fungi, a separate kingdom.

questions.q: What do we call the outermost green leaves that protect a flower bud?
questions.f: Sepals wrap and shield the bud before the flower opens.

questions.q: The root "arbor" in "arboretum" means...?
questions.f: An arboretum is a garden of trees; "arbor" is Latin for tree.

questions.q: Which tree, native to China, is called a "living fossil" and barely changed for ages?
questions.f: Ginkgo biloba looks much like its ancestors from over 200 million years ago.

questions.q: What do we call it when a flower is fertilized by its own pollen?
questions.f: Self-pollinating flowers can make seeds without pollen from another plant.

questions.q: The word "botany" comes from a Greek root "botane," meaning...?
questions.f: Botany, the science of plants, grew from "botane," meaning herb or pasture.

questions.q: Which plant defends itself with tiny hairs that inject a stinging sap?
questions.f: Stinging nettle’s hairs break off and sting the skin like little needles.

questions.q: What do we call plants such as peas and beans that grow seeds in pods?
questions.f: Legumes grow their seeds inside pods and enrich soil with nitrogen.

questions.q: The prefix "trans-" in "transpiration" carries the meaning of...?
questions.f: Water passes across the leaf surface into the air during transpiration.

questions.q: Which flower is named from a Greek word for gold plus flower?
questions.f: From "chrysos" (gold) and "anthemon" (flower).

questions.q: What do we call leaves that grow directly opposite each other on a stem?
questions.f: In opposite arrangement, two leaves sprout at the same spot on opposite sides.

questions.q: Which plant hormone helps shoots bend and grow toward the light?
questions.f: Auxin gathers on the shaded side and makes stems bend toward light.

questions.q: The word "verdant," used for lush green fields, comes from a root meaning...?
questions.f: From Latin "viridis," meaning green.

questions.q: Which cone-bearing trees make up the group called conifers?
questions.f: Conifers like pines and firs carry their seeds in woody cones.

questions.q: What do we call the fine white or yellow threads a fungus grows underground?
questions.f: Mycelium is the web of fungal threads that spreads through soil.

questions.q: The root "phyll" in "chlorophyll" and "phyllotaxis" means...?
questions.f: From Greek "phyllon," meaning leaf.

questions.q: Which plant closes its leaflets quickly when you touch it?
questions.f: The sensitive plant, Mimosa pudica, folds its leaves at a touch.

questions.q: What do we call the young leaf inside a seed that feeds the first sprout?
questions.f: A cotyledon is a seed leaf that stores or gathers early food.

questions.q: Which spice comes from the dried inner bark of a tropical tree?
questions.f: Cinnamon sticks are curls of bark peeled from cinnamon trees.

questions.q: The word "perennial" splits into "per" (through) and "ennial," from a root for...?
questions.f: From Latin "annus," year; perennials live through many years.

questions.q: Which structure lets pea and bean vines curl and cling as they climb?
questions.f: Tendrils are thin coiling stems that grab supports as the vine climbs.

questions.q: What is the leafy top layer of a rainforest, home to many creatures, called?
questions.f: The canopy is the dense roof of leaves high in the forest.

questions.q: The word "florist" and the month-name goddess "Flora" both grew from a root for...?
questions.f: From Latin "flos, floris," flower; Flora was the Roman flower goddess.

questions.q: Which tall tree of California is among the most massive living things?
questions.f: Giant sequoias grow enormous trunks and can weigh thousands of tons.

questions.q: What do we call a thick underground stem that grows sideways, like ginger?
questions.f: A rhizome creeps horizontally underground, sprouting new shoots.

questions.q: The root "hort" in "horticulture" comes from a Latin word for...?
questions.f: From Latin "hortus," garden.

questions.q: Which desert-loving group of water-storing plants includes aloe and jade?
questions.f: Succulents store water in thick fleshy leaves or stems.

questions.q: What do we call a scientist who studies and cares for trees professionally?
questions.f: An arborist prunes, plants, and protects trees; from Latin "arbor."

questions.q: Which sweet, sticky substance is fossilized tree resin, sometimes with bugs inside?
questions.f: Amber is ancient tree resin that hardened over millions of years.

questions.q: The word "sapling" and "sap" both point to the tree’s inner...?
questions.f: Sap is the fluid that carries food and water inside a tree.

questions.q: Which bitter plant compound in tea and oak bark makes the mouth feel dry?
questions.f: Tannins taste astringent and help protect plants from being eaten.

questions.q: What do we call the study of how to farm crops and raise plants for food?
questions.f: Agriculture, from Latin "ager" (field), is the science of farming.

questions.q: Which tiny floating plant is among the smallest flowering plants on Earth?
questions.f: Duckweed forms green mats on ponds, each plant smaller than a fingernail.

questions.q: The prefix "bi-" in "biennial" and "bicycle" means...?
questions.f: A biennial takes two years; a bicycle has two wheels.

questions.q: What do we call the swelling of a plant’s ovary into a seed-carrying fruit?
questions.f: After pollination, the flower’s ovary swells and ripens into fruit.

questions.q: Which climbing plant is famous for turning red and covering old walls?
questions.f: Ivy clings to walls with tiny rootlets and can blaze red in autumn.

questions.q: The word "nectar," a flower’s sweet drink, once meant the drink of the...?
questions.f: In Greek myth, nectar was the sweet drink of the gods.

questions.q: Which part of the flower holds up the anther where pollen forms?
questions.f: The filament is the thin stalk of the stamen that lifts up the anther.

questions.q: What do we call the practice of shaping and growing tiny trees in pots?
questions.f: Bonsai is the art of growing dwarf trees in shallow containers.

questions.q: Xylem carries water up while phloem carries food down in a plant.
questions.f: Xylem moves water and minerals upward; phloem moves sugars around the plant.

questions.q: A mushroom is a fungus and not a true plant.
questions.f: Fungi have no chlorophyll and make up their own kingdom, separate from plants.

questions.q: Mistletoe is a partly parasitic plant that taps into tree branches for water.
questions.f: Mistletoe makes some food itself but steals water and minerals from its host tree.

questions.q: Legumes such as beans can help add nitrogen to the soil.
questions.f: Legume roots host bacteria that pull nitrogen from the air into the soil.

questions.q: Transpiration is the loss of water vapor from a plant’s leaves.
questions.f: Water evaporates from leaf pores called stomata during transpiration.

questions.q: A ginkgo tree is a modern invention with no ancient relatives.
questions.f: The ginkgo is a "living fossil," nearly unchanged for over 200 million years.

questions.q: The word "phloem" comes from a Greek root "phloios," meaning...?
questions.f: Phloem, the food-carrying tissue, is named from "phloios," bark.

questions.q: Which flowering plants are called "angiosperms" because seeds form inside a...?
questions.f: From Greek "angeion" (vessel) and "sperma" (seed): seeds in an enclosed ovary.

questions.q: Which group of seed plants, the conifers, bear "naked" seeds on cones?
questions.f: "Gymnosperm" means "naked seed," from Greek "gymnos" (naked) plus "sperma."

questions.q: The word "xylem" derives from the Greek "xylon," meaning...?
questions.f: Xylem, the water-carrying tissue, takes its name from "xylon," wood.

questions.q: Which specialized photosynthesis lets desert plants open pores only at night?
questions.f: CAM plants like cacti open at night, storing CO2 as acid to save water by day.

questions.q: What do we call a plant that completes its whole life in one season and self-seeds heavily?
questions.f: Annuals race through germinating, flowering, and seeding in one year.

questions.q: The word "stomata" comes from a Greek root meaning...?
questions.f: Stomata, the leaf pores, are named from Greek "stoma," mouth.

questions.q: Which tough polymer stiffens the walls of wood cells, letting trees stand tall?
questions.f: Lignin is the rigid glue in wood; without it, land plants could never tower over us.

questions.q: The root "sperma" in "gymnosperm" and "angiosperm" means...?
questions.f: From Greek "sperma," seed; the two groups differ in how seeds are held.

questions.q: Which single quaking-aspen colony in Utah is considered one huge organism?
questions.f: Pando is a grove of genetically identical aspens sharing one root system.

questions.q: What do we call the waxy, waterproof layer coating many leaves?
questions.f: The cuticle is a waxy skin that reduces water loss from leaves.

questions.q: The word "succulent" comes from a Latin root "sucus," meaning...?
questions.f: Succulents are "juicy" plants storing water; "sucus" means juice.

questions.q: Which growth response makes roots grow downward with gravity?
questions.f: Gravitropism (or geotropism) steers roots down and shoots up.

questions.q: What do we call the study of tree rings to date events and past climates?
questions.f: Dendrochronology reads ring patterns to date wood and reconstruct climate.

questions.q: The prefix "epi-" in "epiphyte" means...?
questions.f: An epiphyte grows "upon" another plant; "phyton" means plant.

questions.q: Which flower, the world’s largest single bloom, smells of rotting flesh?
questions.f: Rafflesia’s bloom can span a meter and reeks to attract carrion flies.

questions.q: What do we call plant tissue made of dead, thick-walled cells that give support, like in wood?
questions.f: Sclerenchyma cells have tough walls that strengthen stems and shells.

questions.q: The word "arboreal," describing tree-dwelling life, shares the root "arbor" with...?
questions.f: Both "arboreal" and "arboretum" trace to Latin "arbor," tree.

questions.q: Which region of active dividing cells lets a plant grow at its tips?
questions.f: Meristem tissue at shoot and root tips produces new cells for growth.

questions.q: The word "photosynthesis" pairs "photo" (light) with "synthesis," meaning to...?
questions.f: Synthesis means combining; photosynthesis assembles sugar using light.

questions.q: What do we call the central growth form of firs and spruces with one straight trunk?
questions.f: Excurrent trees keep a single dominant leader, giving them a conical shape.

questions.q: What do we call a plant that draws food from a host, harming it?
questions.f: Parasitic plants like dodder tap into a host to steal water and nutrients.

questions.q: The root "myco" in "mycorrhiza" refers to...?
questions.f: Mycorrhiza joins "myco" (fungus) and "rhiza" (root) into a partnership.

questions.q: Which tree gives us natural rubber, tapped as a milky latex?
questions.f: The Para rubber tree oozes latex that is processed into rubber.

questions.q: What do we call the tiny opening in an ovule through which a pollen tube enters?
questions.f: The micropyle is a minute pore that lets the pollen tube reach the egg.

questions.q: The word "verdure" for lush greenery comes from the same Latin root as...?
questions.f: Both "verdure" and "verdant" come from Latin "viridis," green.

questions.q: Which fine, powdery structures do ferns and mosses use to reproduce?
questions.f: Spores are single reproductive cells that grow into new fern or moss plants.

questions.q: What is the innermost, often darker dead wood at the center of a trunk called?
questions.f: Heartwood is old, strong central wood that no longer carries sap.

questions.q: The root "rhiz" in "rhizome" and "mycorrhiza" means...?
questions.f: From Greek "rhiza," root.

questions.q: Which spice, the world’s most expensive by weight, is the dried stigmas of a crocus?
questions.f: Each saffron thread is a hand-picked crocus stigma, so it is very costly.

questions.q: What do we call the joining of two plants so they grow as one, common in orchards?
questions.f: Grafting fuses a shoot of one plant onto the roots of another.

questions.q: The word "chloroplast" contains "chloro" (green) and "plast," meaning...?
questions.f: Chloroplasts are the green "formed bodies" where photosynthesis happens.

questions.q: Which trees drop needle-like leaves each autumn despite being conifers?
questions.f: Larches are deciduous conifers whose needles turn gold and fall in autumn.

questions.q: What do we call thick roots that grow above ground to prop up trees like mangroves?
questions.f: Prop, or stilt, roots brace trees growing in soft, wet, or shifting ground.

questions.q: The word "herbaceous" describes plants with soft stems, from "herba," Latin for...?
questions.f: Herbaceous plants have green, non-woody stems; "herba" means grass or herb.

questions.q: Which plant hormone triggers fruit ripening and can spread as a gas?
questions.f: Ethylene is a gas, so one ripe apple really can ripen a whole bowl of fruit around it.

questions.q: What do we call a plant adapted to very dry conditions, like a cactus?
questions.f: Xerophytes, from Greek "xeros" (dry), thrive with little water.

questions.q: The root "anthos" in "chrysanthemum" and "anther" means...?
questions.f: From Greek "anthos," flower; an anther is the flower’s pollen sac.

questions.q: Which plant, native to the Carolinas, snaps shut to trap insects with trigger hairs?
questions.f: The Venus flytrap’s hinged leaves snap when tiny trigger hairs are touched twice.

questions.q: What do we call plants that can live in salty conditions, like mangroves?
questions.f: Halophytes tolerate salt; "halo" is Greek for salt.

questions.q: The word "cotyledon" names the seed leaf; a plant with two is called a...?
questions.f: Dicots ("two cotyledons") include beans and oaks; monocots have one.

questions.q: Which ancient bristlecone pine is one of the oldest known individual trees?
questions.f: Methuselah, a Great Basin bristlecone pine, is over 4,800 years old.

questions.q: What do we call the chemical warfare where one plant releases toxins to stop rivals?
questions.f: Allelopathy lets plants like black walnut release chemicals that suppress neighbors.

questions.q: The prefix "gymno-" in "gymnosperm" and "gymnastics" means...?
questions.f: Greek "gymnos" (naked); gymnosperms bear uncovered seeds on cones.

questions.q: Which tree yields cork, harvested from its thick, spongy bark?
questions.f: Cork oak bark can be stripped every few years and regrows, giving us cork.

questions.q: What do we call the sticky tip of a pistil that catches pollen?
questions.f: The stigma is the receptive tip where pollen lands and germinates.

questions.q: The word "corolla," the ring of petals, comes from Latin for a little...?
questions.f: From Latin "corolla," a small crown or garland, describing the petals.

questions.q: Which large tropical plant, though tree-like, is actually a giant herb with no wood?
questions.f: A banana "tree" has a soft pseudostem of leaf bases, not true wood.

questions.q: What do we call the leaf-like structures, often colorful, below a flower, as in poinsettias?
questions.f: The red "petals" of a poinsettia are actually bracts, modified leaves.

questions.q: The root "chloros" in "chlorophyll" and "chlorine" means...?
questions.f: From Greek "chloros," pale green; chlorophyll makes leaves green.

questions.q: Which movement makes climbing tendrils coil when they touch a support?
questions.f: Thigmotropism is growth in response to touch; "thigma" means touch.

questions.q: What do we call a swollen, food-storing underground bud like an onion?
questions.f: A bulb is layered fleshy leaves around a bud, storing food underground.

questions.q: The word "arboretum" and "herbarium" share the suffix "-arium," meaning a...?
questions.f: The suffix "-arium" names a place, like aquarium or planetarium.

questions.q: Which pigment family colors autumn leaves and carrots orange?
questions.f: The orange was there all along; it only shows once green chlorophyll breaks down in fall.

questions.q: What do we call the swollen underground stem base of a crocus or gladiolus?
questions.f: A corm is a short, solid, swollen stem base that stores food.

questions.q: The word "deciduous" and "decadent" share a Latin root meaning to...?
questions.f: Both trace to Latin "cadere/decidere," to fall down.

questions.q: Which fungus-plus-alga partnership grows as crusty patches on rocks and bark?
questions.f: A lichen is a fungus and an alga living together as one organism.

questions.q: What do we call the practice of removing dead or overgrown branches from a plant?
questions.f: Pruning shapes plants and encourages healthy new growth.

questions.q: The Greek root "hydor" links "hydrophyte" and "hydrant" to...?
questions.f: A hydrophyte is a water plant; both words come from Greek for water.

questions.q: Which massive banyan-type tree spreads by dropping aerial roots that become new trunks?
questions.f: A single banyan can spread over acres as its aerial roots root down.

questions.q: What do we call the pale, living outer wood that actively carries water in a tree?
questions.f: Sapwood is the younger outer wood that conducts water and sap.

questions.q: The word "petiole," a leaf stalk, comes from a Latin root meaning a little...?
questions.f: From Latin "petiolus," a little foot or stalk.

questions.q: Which staple crop, first domesticated in the Andes, comes in thousands of varieties?
questions.f: The potato was domesticated in South America and now has thousands of types.

questions.q: The prefix "peri-" in "perianth" (the petals and sepals together) means...?
questions.f: The perianth surrounds the reproductive parts; "peri" means around.

questions.q: Which climbing pitcher plant lures prey into a fluid-filled cup with a slippery rim?
questions.f: Nepenthes pitchers trap insects in a pool of digestive fluid.

questions.q: What do we call a plant that grows and flowers, then dies, all within two years?
questions.f: A biennial grows leaves the first year and flowers the second, then dies.

questions.q: The word "flora" for regional plant life comes from the name of a Roman...?
questions.f: Flora was the Roman goddess of flowers and spring.

questions.q: Which drink comes from roasting the seeds inside the fruit of a certain shrub?
questions.f: Coffee beans are the roasted seeds from the red cherries of coffee shrubs.

questions.q: What do we call the fusion of a shoot from one plant onto another’s stem?
questions.f: A graft joins tissues so they grow together as one plant.

questions.q: The root "phyton" appears in "epiphyte" and "phytoplankton" to mean...?
questions.f: From Greek "phyton," plant; phytoplankton are plant-like drifters.

questions.q: Which desert shrub of Namibia grows just two ever-lengthening leaves for over 1,000 years?
questions.f: Welwitschia produces only two strap-like leaves that grow for centuries.

questions.q: What do we call the study of fungi, close partners and relatives of plant science?
questions.f: Mycology studies fungi; "myco" is Greek for fungus.

questions.q: The word "annual" for a yearly plant and "annals" of history share a root meaning...?
questions.f: Both come from Latin "annus," year.

questions.q: Which trees, the world’s heaviest by trunk volume, include one named General Sherman?
questions.f: General Sherman, a giant sequoia, is the largest tree by trunk volume.

questions.q: What do we call the loss of green color when a leaf lacks nutrients or light?
questions.f: In chlorosis leaves turn yellow because chlorophyll fails to form.

questions.q: The root "helios" in "heliotropism" and "helium" means...?
questions.f: From Greek "helios," sun; heliotropic plants track the sun.

questions.q: Which plant tissue of thin-walled living cells fills soft parts and stores food?
questions.f: Parenchyma cells make up much of a plant’s soft, food-storing tissue.

questions.q: What do we call the natural drop of leaves, flowers, or fruit from a plant?
questions.f: Abscission is the controlled shedding of leaves and other parts.

questions.q: The word "orchid" comes from a Greek word describing the shape of its...?
questions.f: From Greek "orkhis"; the twin root tubers gave the orchid its name.

questions.q: What do we call a plant with a single seed leaf, like grasses and lilies?
questions.f: Monocots have one cotyledon and usually parallel-veined leaves.

questions.q: The suffix "-phyte" in "epiphyte" and "xerophyte" means...?
questions.f: From Greek "phyton," plant.

questions.q: Which structure protects a fern’s clusters of spore cases on the leaf underside?
questions.f: The little umbrella-like indusium shields the sori until the spores are ready to fly.

questions.q: What do we call the sweet reward and the special cells that ooze it in flowers?
questions.f: Nectaries are glands that secrete nectar to attract pollinators.

questions.q: The word "bract" describes a modified leaf; the showy red parts of a poinsettia are...?
questions.f: A poinsettia’s color comes from leaf-like bracts, not true petals.

questions.q: Gymnosperms bear their seeds on cones rather than inside fruits.
questions.f: "Gymnosperm" means "naked seed"; conifers carry seeds openly on cone scales.

questions.q: A banana plant is a giant herb, not a true woody tree.
questions.f: Its trunk is a soft pseudostem of packed leaf bases, so it is technically an herb.

questions.q: The gas ethylene helps fruit ripen and can spread from fruit to fruit.
questions.f: Ethylene is a plant hormone; one ripe fruit can ripen others nearby.

questions.q: The word "xylem" comes from the Greek word for wood.
questions.f: Xylem carries water and gives support, matching its root "xylon," wood.

questions.q: Mosses lack true roots and grip surfaces with thread-like rhizoids.
questions.f: Rhizoids anchor a moss but, unlike roots, do not carry water through vessels.

questions.q: Lichens are made of a fungus and an alga living together.
questions.f: The fungus gives structure while the alga photosynthesizes; together they form lichen.

questions.q: Saffron, the costly spice, is harvested from the stigmas of a crocus flower.
questions.f: Each crocus gives only a few tiny stigmas, so saffron is very expensive.

questions.q: A dicot seed contains a single seed leaf, or cotyledon.
questions.f: Dicots have two cotyledons; it is monocots that have just one.

questions.q: Which fruit is small, round, and grows on bushes in red or black kinds?
questions.f: Currants grow in little bunches and are often cooked into jam.

questions.q: What is the plural of the word "bush"?
questions.f: Words ending in "sh" add "es" to make the plural.

questions.q: Which tree is famous for its pale white bark that peels like paper?
questions.f: Birch bark peels in papery strips and was once used to make canoes.

questions.q: What do we call the sweet, sticky stuff bees store in honeycomb?
questions.f: Bees turn flower nectar into honey and seal it in wax combs.

questions.q: Which vegetable is round, purple-red, and stains your fingers?
questions.f: Beets grow underground and their deep red juice is used as a dye.

questions.q: The word "sunflower" is made from two smaller words. What are they?
questions.f: A sunflower is named for its big, bright, sun-like yellow head.

questions.q: Which part of a carrot plant do we usually eat?
questions.f: A carrot is a fat orange root that stores food for the plant.

questions.q: What do we call a very large group of trees growing wild together?
questions.f: Forests cover about a third of the land on Earth.

questions.q: Which green herb is often torn onto pizza and pasta?
questions.f: Basil leaves smell sweet and peppery and grow best in warm weather.

questions.q: What is the plural of the word "bunch"?
questions.f: Words ending in "ch" add "es" to make the plural.

questions.q: Which fruit is fuzzy and brown outside but bright green inside?
questions.f: Kiwifruit grows on a climbing vine and is full of tiny black seeds.

questions.q: What do we call a tiny plant grown in a pot on a windowsill?
questions.f: Houseplants live indoors and need water and light just like garden plants.

questions.q: Which tall yellow crop is grown in fields and ground into flour?
questions.f: Wheat is one of the most widely grown food crops in the world.

questions.q: The word "treetop" means the very...?
questions.f: Birds often build nests in the treetops, high above the ground.

questions.q: Which small red fruit is often eaten with cream in summer?
questions.f: Strawberries grow low to the ground on small leafy plants.

questions.q: Which vegetable looks like a tiny green tree on your plate?
questions.f: Each broccoli floret is a bundle of tiny flower buds.

questions.q: A "seed packet" is a paper envelope that holds...?
questions.f: Gardeners buy seed packets and sow the seeds in spring.

questions.q: Which fruit grows on a tall palm and has a hard, hairy shell?
questions.f: A coconut holds sweet water inside its tough shell.

questions.q: What do we call the long green stalk of a celery plant that we eat?
questions.f: Celery stems are crunchy because they are full of water-carrying tubes.

questions.q: The word "leafy" describes a plant with lots of...?
questions.f: Leafy greens like spinach and lettuce are full of vitamins.

questions.q: Which juicy fruit is sliced into rings and often has a hard core?
questions.f: A pineapple is really many small fruits joined into one big one.

questions.q: What do we call the little hairs on a peach skin?
questions.f: Peach fuzz helps protect the soft fruit underneath.

questions.q: Which plant has fronds and grows in shady, damp places?
questions.f: Fern leaves are called fronds and often unroll like a curl.

questions.q: What is the plural of the word "branch"?
questions.f: Branch ends in "ch," so it takes "es" in the plural.

questions.q: Which fruit dries up to become a raisin?
questions.f: Raisins are grapes that have been dried in the sun or in ovens.

questions.q: What do we call the job of cutting grass short and neat?
questions.f: Mowing keeps a lawn low and tidy, and grass keeps growing back.

questions.q: Which tree has needles and is often decorated in December?
questions.f: Fir trees keep their green needles right through the winter.

questions.q: The word "rainforest" tells you the forest gets lots of...?
questions.f: Rainforests are warm and wet, and they are packed with plants.

questions.q: Which vegetable grows in a tight ball of layered green leaves?
questions.f: A cabbage head is made of leaves wrapped tightly around each other.

questions.q: What do we call the water drops found on grass early in the morning?
questions.f: Dew forms when cool air makes water settle on leaves overnight.

questions.q: Which small purple flower has a sweet smell used in soaps?
questions.f: Lavender is dried and used to make things smell fresh and calm.

questions.q: What do we call a young shoot of grass or grain just coming up?
questions.f: A single piece of grass is called a blade of grass.

questions.q: Which fruit is famous for being long, thin, and full of vitamin C?
questions.f: Limes are small green citrus fruits with a sharp, sour taste.

questions.q: The word "flowerbed" is a patch of garden planted with...?
questions.f: A flowerbed is a shaped area of soil filled with flowering plants.

questions.q: Which nut comes in a hard shell and is often cracked at holidays?
questions.f: Walnuts grow on trees inside a green husk and a hard, wrinkled shell.

questions.q: What do we call the tall, thin plant part that holds a sunflower head up?
questions.f: A sunflower stalk can grow taller than an adult person.

questions.q: Which of these grows tall with a woody trunk?
questions.f: A maple is a tree; tulips, daisies, and clover are small soft plants.

questions.q: What do we call a small forest area you can walk through?
questions.f: A wood is a smaller patch of trees than a big forest.

questions.q: Which yellow-green fruit is used to make guacamole?
questions.f: An avocado has one large seed, sometimes called a stone, in the middle.

questions.q: The word "evergreen" tells you the plant stays green all...?
questions.f: Evergreens like pines and holly keep leaves through every season.

questions.q: What do we call the sharp points on a cactus?
questions.f: Cactus spines protect the plant and give a little shade.

questions.q: Which drink is squeezed from crushed apples?
questions.f: Apples are pressed to squeeze out their sweet juice.

questions.q: What do we call the act of putting seeds into the ground?
questions.f: To sow means to scatter or plant seeds in soil.

questions.q: Which plant part would you find at the very bottom of a plant?
questions.f: Roots spread out underground to grip the soil and drink water.

questions.q: The word "grassland" names a wide place covered mostly in...?
questions.f: Grasslands are open plains where grasses grow instead of forests.

questions.q: Which vegetable is long, orange, and often eaten by rabbits in stories?
questions.f: Carrots are crunchy roots that grow straight down into the soil.

questions.q: What do we call a plant that gives us food we can eat?
questions.f: Food crops like rice, beans, and wheat feed people everywhere.

questions.q: Which sweet, sticky syrup is poured from a bottle onto pancakes?
questions.f: Maple syrup is boiled down from the watery sap of maple trees.

questions.q: What is the plural of the word "potato"?
questions.f: Potato takes "es" in the plural, just like tomato.

questions.q: Which small green plant with three leaves is a sign of good luck?
questions.f: Most clovers have three leaflets, so a four-leaf clover is rare.

questions.q: What do we call the bright yellow center of a daisy?
questions.f: A daisy centre is packed with dozens of tiny flowers.

questions.q: Which part of the mint plant do we use to flavour food?
questions.f: Mint leaves hold the oils that give mint its cool, fresh taste.

questions.q: The word "woodland" describes land covered with...?
questions.f: A woodland is an area filled with trees and the life beneath them.

questions.q: Which fruit has a thick yellow skin you peel before eating it?
questions.f: A banana peel protects the soft fruit inside until you open it.

questions.q: What do we call the pretty smell of a whole garden of flowers?
questions.f: Fragrance is a sweet or pleasant smell, especially from flowers.

questions.q: Which plant grows on a stalk with a big brown centre full of seeds?
questions.f: A single sunflower head can hold over a thousand seeds.

questions.q: What do we call the little green top left on a strawberry?
questions.f: The leafy green cap on a strawberry is called the calyx.

questions.q: Which grain is served in bowls and grows in wet fields?
questions.f: Rice feeds more people around the world than almost any other crop.

questions.q: The word "petal" names a part of which thing?
questions.f: Petals are the soft coloured parts that ring a flower.

questions.q: What do we call a garden tool with a long handle used to dig soil?
questions.f: A spade has a flat blade for digging and turning over soil.

questions.q: Which plant part becomes an apple after the flower is pollinated?
questions.f: A flower turns into fruit, which carries the plant’s seeds.

questions.q: What do we call trees planted in a row along a street?
questions.f: Street trees give shade and help clean a city’s air.

questions.q: Which vegetable is green, round, and eaten in a pod or on its own?
questions.f: Peas grow in pods and are picked while still sweet and green.

questions.q: The word "seedless" describes a fruit with no...?
questions.f: Seedless grapes and watermelons are grown specially without seeds.

questions.q: What do we call the brown, dry leaves that cover the ground in autumn?
questions.f: Leaf litter rots down and feeds the soil for next year.

questions.q: Which tall plant has a woody trunk and can live for hundreds of years?
questions.f: Trees are the biggest and longest-living plants on Earth.

questions.q: What do we call a bunch of bananas growing together?
questions.f: A cluster of bananas is called a hand, and each banana is a finger.

questions.q: Which orange-fleshed vegetable is roasted and served sweet?
questions.f: Sweet potatoes are starchy roots that turn soft and sweet when baked.

questions.q: The word "planted" is the past tense of which verb?
questions.f: Yesterday I planted a seed; today I plant another.

questions.q: What do we call the soft green plant that grows in damp, shady spots?
questions.f: Moss forms soft green cushions on rocks, logs, and damp soil.

questions.q: Which fruit has a stone in the middle and dries into a prune?
questions.f: A dried plum is called a prune.

questions.q: What do we call the wide, flat top part of a mushroom?
questions.f: A mushroom has a cap on top and a stalk, or stem, below.

questions.q: A tree trunk is covered in a protective layer called bark.
questions.f: Bark shields the living wood inside from weather, insects, and injury.

questions.q: Sunflowers can grow taller than a grown-up person.
questions.f: Some sunflowers reach over three metres, far taller than an adult.

questions.q: Rubbing a mint leaf between your fingers releases its smell.
questions.f: Crushing the leaf breaks tiny oil pockets, letting the scent escape.

questions.q: A lemon tastes sweet like sugar.
questions.f: Lemons are famous for tasting sour, not sweet.

questions.q: Leaves grow on the branches of a tree.
questions.f: Leaves sprout from twigs and branches to catch the sunlight.

questions.q: A pea grows inside a pod.
questions.f: Several peas sit in a row inside each long green pod.

questions.q: Roses have soft, harmless stems with no prickles at all.
questions.f: Rose stems carry sharp thorns that help protect the plant.

questions.q: Some flowers open in the morning and close again at night.
questions.f: Many flowers, like daisies and morning glories, open and close each day.

questions.q: A pinecone comes from a pine tree.
questions.f: Pine trees carry their seeds tucked inside woody cones.

questions.q: Watering a plant too little can make it droop and wilt.
questions.f: Without enough water, a plant’s stems and leaves go soft and floppy.

questions.q: An acorn will one day grow into an oak tree.
questions.f: Each acorn is an oak seed, though only a few ever become trees.

questions.q: The root "terra" in "terrarium" and "terrace" means...?
questions.f: A terrarium is a glass container of earth and plants; "terra" is Latin for earth.

questions.q: Which part of a flower will grow into the seeds after pollination?
questions.f: Tiny ovules inside the flower ripen into seeds once pollen reaches them.

questions.q: What do we call a plant’s ability to turn toward a window for light?
questions.f: Stems bend toward the brightest side so leaves can catch more sunlight.

questions.q: Which large group of plants includes both pines and firs?
questions.f: Conifers carry their seeds inside woody cones instead of fruit.

questions.q: The prefix "sub-" in "subsoil" tells you it lies...?
questions.f: Subsoil is the layer under the topsoil, poorer in food for plants.

questions.q: What is the main food that plants store in a potato?
questions.f: Potatoes pack away starch so the plant has food for next season.

questions.q: Which insect helps plants by carrying pollen but is not a bee?
questions.f: Butterflies sip nectar with a long tube and carry pollen as they feed.

questions.q: The word "biodegradable" describes rubbish that can be broken down by...?
questions.f: Bacteria, fungi, and worms break biodegradable waste into simple matter.

questions.q: What do we call the outer skin of a seed that protects the baby plant?
questions.f: The tough seed coat keeps the embryo safe until it is time to sprout.

questions.q: Which crop is grown in cool climates and rolled into oatmeal?
questions.f: Oats grow well in cool, damp places and make a warm breakfast.

questions.q: The word "shrub" describes a plant that is...?
questions.f: Shrubs have woody stems but stay short and branch near the ground.

questions.q: How do dandelion and maple seeds mainly travel to new ground?
questions.f: Light seeds with wings or parachutes catch the breeze and drift away.

questions.q: What do we call the top, richest layer of soil where most roots grow?
questions.f: Topsoil is dark and crumbly because it is full of rotted plant matter.

questions.q: Which sweet vegetable is grown in fields and crushed to make sugar?
questions.f: Sugar beet roots are boiled down to make much of the world’s sugar.

questions.q: The suffix "-y" in "thorny" and "leafy" means the plant is...?
questions.f: Adding "-y" turns a noun into a describing word: thorn becomes thorny.

questions.q: What do we call a plant grown for its seeds, like wheat or rice?
questions.f: Grain crops are grasses grown for their dry, edible seeds.

questions.q: Which part of the coffee plant is roasted to make the drink?
questions.f: Coffee beans are really the seeds from inside small red fruits.

questions.q: The word "sapwood" tells you this part of a trunk carries...?
questions.f: Sapwood is the outer wood that moves water and sap up the tree.

questions.q: What do we call the fine dust that makes some people sneeze in spring?
questions.f: Wind-blown tree and grass pollen causes hay fever in many people.

questions.q: Which plant part do we eat when we eat an onion?
questions.f: An onion is a bulb made of thick, layered leaves packed underground.

questions.q: The root "vita" in "vitamin" points to something needed for...?
questions.f: Vitamins in fruit and vegetables keep the body working; "vita" means life.

questions.q: What do we call the woody plant tissue used to make paper?
questions.f: Wood is mashed into pulp, then pressed and dried into sheets of paper.

questions.q: Which crop grows in pods and gives us peanut butter?
questions.f: Peanuts form in pods that ripen underground, not on branches.

questions.q: The word "seedbed" names a patch of soil prepared for...?
questions.f: Gardeners rake a fine seedbed so tiny seeds can sprout easily.

questions.q: What happens to most leaves before they fall in autumn?
questions.f: As green chlorophyll fades, yellow and orange colours show through.

questions.q: Which of these is a citrus fruit?
questions.f: Citrus fruits like lemons, limes, and grapefruit are juicy and tangy.

questions.q: The prefix "re-" in "replant" means to plant...?
questions.f: To replant is to plant something again, often in a better spot.

questions.q: What do we call a plant that lives in water, like a water lily?
questions.f: Aquatic plants have floating leaves and stems built for life in water.

questions.q: Which tree gives us the wood used for most cricket stumps and furniture?
questions.f: Ash wood is tough and springy, good for handles and sports gear.

questions.q: The word "germ" in "germinate" points to the plant’s tiny...?
questions.f: The germ of a seed is the living part that grows into a new plant.

questions.q: What do we call the practice of growing different crops in a field each year?
questions.f: Rotating crops keeps soil healthy and reduces pests and disease.

questions.q: Which spice is the dried root of a knobbly tropical plant?
questions.f: Ginger is a spicy underground stem used fresh, dried, or ground.

questions.q: The suffix "-less" in "leafless" tells you the plant has...?
questions.f: The suffix "-less" means "without," so leafless means having no leaves.

questions.q: What do we call plants that grow back from the same roots every spring?
questions.f: Perennials survive winter underground and shoot up again each year.

questions.q: Which layer of a forest is closest to the ground, below the shrubs?
questions.f: The forest floor is dim and damp, full of fallen leaves and fungi.

questions.q: The word "flour" is made by grinding which part of a grain plant?
questions.f: Grain seeds are milled between stones or rollers to make flour.

questions.q: What do we call the sticky sweet liquid a bee turns into honey?
questions.f: Bees gather nectar from flowers and thicken it into honey in the hive.

questions.q: Which desert plant is grown for the soothing gel inside its thick leaves?
questions.f: Aloe leaves hold a clear gel long used to soothe burns and dry skin.

questions.q: The root "photo" also appears in "photograph," which is a picture made with...?
questions.f: A photograph is drawn by light, just as photosynthesis is powered by light.

questions.q: What do we call the food-making factories inside a plant leaf?
questions.f: Chloroplasts are tiny green packets where sunlight becomes sugar.

questions.q: Which fruit tree blossoms in spring with pink and white flowers in Japan?
questions.f: Crowds gather each spring to watch cherry blossom open and fall.

questions.q: The word "gardening" describes the hobby of...?
questions.f: Gardening means planting, watering, weeding, and caring for plants.

questions.q: What do we call the swelling on a bean root where helpful bacteria live?
questions.f: Root nodules hold bacteria that pull nitrogen from the air for the plant.

questions.q: Which of these plants stores water to survive long dry spells?
questions.f: Aloe stores water in fat, fleshy leaves so it can outlast a drought.

questions.q: The word "husk" names the dry outer covering of a...?
questions.f: Corn cobs are wrapped in husks that must be stripped away.

questions.q: What do we call a fruit that has one hard stone inside, like a cherry?
questions.f: Stone fruits, or drupes, hold a single seed in a hard pit.

questions.q: Which plant is used to make linen cloth?
questions.f: Flax stems hold long fibres that are spun into cool, strong linen.

questions.q: The prefix "over-" in "overwater" warns you about giving a plant...?
questions.f: Overwatering drowns roots, which need air pockets in the soil too.

questions.q: What do we call the low plants and bushes growing under forest trees?
questions.f: Undergrowth is the tangle of shrubs and seedlings beneath the trees.

questions.q: Which vegetable is a long white root with a peppery, spicy taste?
questions.f: Radishes grow fast and taste sharp and peppery when raw.

questions.q: The word "compost" describes rotted plant waste used to...?
questions.f: Compost returns nutrients to soil and helps it hold water.

questions.q: What do we call the way a sunflower head follows the sun across the sky?
questions.f: Young sunflower heads swing from east to west each day, following the sun.

questions.q: Which crop covers huge fields and is fed to farm animals as hay?
questions.f: Grass is cut and dried into hay to feed animals through the winter.

questions.q: The root "auto" in "automatic" and the word "self" both mean the same. What does self-seeding mean?
c: a plant sows its own seeds
questions.f: Self-seeding plants scatter their own seeds and come up again on their own.

questions.q: What do we call a plant with soft, green, non-woody stems?
questions.f: Herbs have soft stems that usually die back at the end of the season.

questions.q: Which part of a rose would a gardener cut to make a bouquet?
questions.f: Gardeners cut long stems so roses last well in a vase of water.

questions.q: The word "windbreak" names a row of trees planted to block...?
questions.f: A windbreak shelters crops, soil, and animals from strong winds.

questions.q: What do we call the small dry fruit of a grass, like a wheat kernel?
questions.f: A grain is a one-seeded dry fruit produced by grasses.

questions.q: Which plant part carries food from the leaves to the rest of the plant?
questions.f: Phloem tubes deliver sugary sap made in the leaves everywhere it is needed.

questions.q: The word "orchardist" names a person who grows...?
questions.f: An orchardist plants, prunes, and harvests trees in an orchard.

questions.q: What do we call the process of a fruit becoming soft, sweet, and ready to eat?
questions.f: As fruit ripens, starches turn to sugar and the flesh softens.

questions.q: Which plant gives us the beans used to make chocolate?
questions.f: Cacao pods grow straight from the trunk and hold the beans for chocolate.

questions.q: The prefix "in-" in "indoor plant" tells you it grows...?
questions.f: Indoor plants are chosen because they cope with lower light levels.

questions.q: What do we call the trunk, branches, and twigs of a tree together?
questions.f: A tree’s woody frame supports its leaves and carries water upward.

questions.q: Which vegetable is a thick white stem in the onion family, mild in soups?
questions.f: Leeks are related to onions but taste milder and sweeter.

questions.q: The word "harvester" names a machine or person that...?
questions.f: A combine harvester cuts, threshes, and cleans grain in one pass.

questions.q: What do we call the small green leaves that first appear from a bean seed?
questions.f: The first pair of leaves come from the seed itself and feed the seedling.

questions.q: Which giant plant family do wheat, oats, barley, and rye all belong to?
questions.f: These cereal crops are all grasses grown for their grain.

questions.q: The word "sapling" and the word "seedling" differ in that a sapling is...?
questions.f: A seedling is a tiny sprout; a sapling is a slim young tree.

questions.q: What do we call plants that people grow just to look at, not to eat?
questions.f: Ornamentals such as tulips and pansies are grown for beauty alone.

questions.q: Which tree grows in hot, wet places and drops nuts inside a fibrous husk?
questions.f: A coconut’s fibrous husk helps it float across the sea to new shores.

questions.q: The word "pesticide" names something used to control...?
questions.f: The ending "-cide" means killing, so a pesticide targets crop pests.

questions.q: What do we call the pale rings of new wood a tree adds each spring?
questions.f: A tree usually adds one ring a year, so rings reveal its age.

questions.q: Which vegetable is really a large flower bud that we boil and eat?
questions.f: An artichoke is an unopened flower bud with tough, tasty scales.

questions.q: The word "vineyard" names a field planted with...?
questions.f: Grapes are grown in rows in a vineyard, often on wire supports.

questions.q: What do we call the fine white threads a mushroom spreads through soil?
questions.f: Fungal threads spread widely underground, feeding on rotting matter.

questions.q: Which part of a plant is designed to attract animals to spread its seeds?
questions.f: Sweet, colourful fruit tempts animals that carry seeds far away.

questions.q: The word "deforestation" describes the cutting down of...?
questions.f: The prefix "de-" means removal, so deforestation is losing forest cover.

questions.q: What do we call a plant that traps and digests insects for extra food?
questions.f: Carnivorous plants live in poor soil and get nutrients from insects.

questions.q: Which nut grows on trees and is often used in marzipan and milk?
questions.f: Almonds are the seeds inside the stony fruit of the almond tree.

questions.q: The word "mulch" names material spread on soil to...?
questions.f: Mulch of bark or straw keeps soil damp and blocks weeds.

questions.q: What do we call the tiny plants and algae that drift in the ocean?
questions.f: Drifting plant plankton makes much of the oxygen in the air.

questions.q: A bulb, like an onion, stores food underground for the plant.
questions.f: Bulbs are packed with food so the plant can shoot up quickly in spring.

questions.q: Conifers usually carry their seeds inside woody cones.
questions.f: Cone scales open in dry weather to release the winged seeds.

questions.q: All fungi, including mushrooms, make their own food from sunlight.
questions.f: Fungi have no chlorophyll and must feed on other living or dead matter.

questions.q: Crop rotation helps keep farm soil healthy.
questions.f: Changing crops each year balances nutrients and breaks pest cycles.

questions.q: Peanuts ripen in pods below the ground.
questions.f: After flowering, peanut stalks bend down and push pods into the soil.

questions.q: The word "biodegradable" means something can rot away naturally.
questions.f: Living decomposers break biodegradable material back into simple matter.

questions.q: A shrub is simply a tree that has not grown up yet.
questions.f: Shrubs are their own kind of plant, staying low with many woody stems.

questions.q: Grass keeps growing back after it is cut.
