questions.f: Dwarfing rootstocks let growers pick fruit from the ground instead of ladders.

questions.q: A dormant twig cut from a prized apple, a sloping cut matched to a chosen rootstock, and the piece that decides the variety is called what?
questions.f: The rootstock supplies vigour and size; the scion supplies the fruit.

questions.q: Which citrus is a hybrid whose parents are believed to include the pomelo and the mandarin?
questions.f: Almost all familiar citrus fruits are tangles of hybrids from a few wild ancestors.

questions.q: Which wheat relative, einkorn, differs from bread wheat by having how many chromosome sets?
questions.f: Bread wheat is hexaploid, the result of two ancient hybridisations.

questions.q: Which crop is a wheat-rye hybrid created deliberately by breeders?
questions.f: Triticale combines rye’s hardiness with wheat’s baking quality.

questions.q: Bread wheat carrying six chromosome sets, a colchicine-soaked seedling, and blooms larger than either parent could manage describe which condition?
questions.f: Whole-genome doubling is a common engine of new plant species.

questions.q: Seedless watermelons are usually sterile because they have how many chromosome sets?
questions.f: A triploid cannot divide its chromosomes evenly, so it makes no viable seed.

questions.q: Which method regenerates whole plants from small pieces of tissue in sterile jars?
questions.f: Tissue culture can turn one prized plant into thousands of identical copies.

questions.q: A microbe that splices its own genes into a plant, knobbly crown gall tumours on a stem, and the original tool of genetic engineering point to what?
questions.f: Engineers simply swapped the bacterium’s tumour genes for genes they wanted.

questions.q: A crystal protein from a soil bacterium, caterpillars that stop feeding within hours, and a spray long approved for organic growers point to which pest control?
questions.f: The same protein organic farmers spray is the one engineered into Bt maize.

questions.q: Which gene-editing tool has largely replaced older methods for precise crop improvement?
questions.f: Edits can now be made without leaving foreign DNA in the finished plant.

questions.q: Which older breeding technique deliberately used radiation or chemicals to create useful mutants?
questions.f: Thousands of released varieties, including some popular grains, began as induced mutants.

questions.q: Which vitamin-A precursor was engineered into rice grains to combat deficiency?
questions.f: The pigment is also what turns the engineered grains a distinctive golden colour.

questions.q: Millions of hectares sharing a single genotype, wild relatives ploughed under, and one new disease able to cross a continent describe what?
questions.f: Uniform fields are efficient right up to the moment they all fail together.

questions.q: Two feeble inbred maize lines, offspring towering over both parents, and farmers who must buy fresh seed every season describe which effect?
questions.f: Hybrid vigour doubled American maize yields in a single generation of breeding.

questions.q: Which practice of leaving land unplanted for a season restores fertility?
questions.f: A fallow year lets nutrients rebuild and breaks the cycle of weeds and pests.

questions.q: A willow cut to the same high stump for two centuries, regrowth kept safely above a cow’s reach, and a word meaning to crop the head describe what?
questions.f: Pollards are often far older than nearby uncut trees of the same species.

questions.q: Which farming system deliberately grows trees among crops or pasture?
questions.f: Trees provide shade, fodder, and deep roots that lift nutrients and hold soil.

questions.q: Prairie sod broken by new tractors, drought settling in from 1931, and black blizzards darkening the sky over Chicago describe which disaster?
questions.f: Ploughing destroyed the deep grass roots that had held the plains for millennia.

questions.q: Which deep-rooted native vegetation had held the southern Plains soil together before ploughing?
questions.f: Their dense sod could survive drought that killed shallow-rooted wheat.

questions.q: Overgrazed Sahel pasture, topsoil lifted away by wind, and dryland tipping past the point of recovery describe what?
questions.f: It is less about advancing sand dunes than about land losing the power to recover.

questions.q: Which build-up of salts, common under heavy irrigation, poisons soil for most crops?
questions.f: Irrigation water evaporates and leaves its dissolved salts behind in the topsoil.

questions.q: Which African initiative aims to plant a vast mosaic of vegetation across the Sahel?
questions.f: The goal has shifted from a literal wall of trees to restoring whole landscapes.

questions.q: Apple varieties must be grafted because seedlings do not breed true to the parent.
questions.f: Every Bramley or Gala tree is a clone joined onto a chosen rootstock.

questions.q: The old grouping "dicots" is now known not to be a single natural lineage.
questions.f: Several early branches were lumped together, so botanists now speak of eudicots.

questions.q: Balsa counts as a hardwood in botanical terms despite being very light.
questions.f: Hardwood and softwood describe the type of tree, not the density of the timber.

questions.q: Most of the water a plant takes up is built into its tissues rather than transpired.
questions.f: Well over ninety percent evaporates away through the leaves.

questions.q: Triploid plants such as seedless watermelons cannot produce viable seed.
questions.f: Three chromosome sets cannot be shared out evenly during cell division.

questions.q: What color is a ripe strawberry?
questions.f: Strawberries turn from green to bright red as they ripen in the sunshine.

questions.q: Which sweet treat do we put candles on at a birthday?
questions.f: The custom of birthday cakes with candles began in Germany hundreds of years ago.

questions.q: Which drink is made by squeezing lemons with water and sugar?
questions.f: Cloudy lemonade uses whole squeezed lemons, while clear lemonade is often just the juice.

questions.q: Which green vegetable looks like a tiny tree?
questions.f: Each little top on broccoli is really a bundle of tiny unopened flower buds.

questions.q: Which warm drink is made from leaves soaked in hot water?
questions.f: After plain water, tea is the most popular drink in the entire world.

questions.q: Which round baked treat has a hole in the middle?
questions.f: The hole helps a doughnut cook evenly so the middle is not still raw.

questions.q: Which flat breakfast food do we stack and pour syrup on?
questions.f: People have flipped pancakes for thousands of years using flour, milk, and eggs.

questions.q: Which little green vegetables pop out of a long pod?
questions.f: A single pea pod usually hides about six to eight tiny green peas inside.

questions.q: Where do bees store the honey they make?
questions.f: Bees build honeycomb from wax to store honey in neat six-sided cells.

questions.q: Which cold treat is frozen juice on a stick?
questions.f: The ice pop was invented by accident by an 11-year-old boy who left juice out on a cold night.

questions.q: Which yellow fruit is very sour and used to make lemonade?
questions.f: Lemons taste sour because they are full of a natural acid called citric acid.

questions.q: Which yellow vegetable grows in rows on a cob?
questions.f: One ear of corn usually has about 800 kernels lined up in neat rows.

questions.q: Which red fruit with a pit is often baked into pies?
questions.f: Cherries grow on trees and come in sweet kinds for eating and sour kinds for pies.

questions.q: Which orange vegetable is called a 'sweet' potato?
questions.f: Sweet potatoes are orange inside and taste sugary when they are baked.

questions.q: Which cheesy Italian food is served in triangle slices?
questions.f: The most popular pizza topping in many countries is simple cheese.

questions.q: Which pasta is shaped like little curved tubes?
questions.f: Macaroni and cheese is one of the most loved kid meals around the world.

questions.q: Which red sauce is poured over a plate of spaghetti?
questions.f: Tomato sauce for pasta was made popular in the country of Italy.

questions.q: Which crunchy food do we pour milk over in a breakfast bowl?
questions.f: Breakfast cereal was invented as a healthy morning food over 100 years ago.

questions.q: Which sweet white topping is sprinkled over doughnuts?
questions.f: Sugar comes from plants like sugar cane and sugar beet.

questions.q: Which thin, crispy potato slice comes in a snack bag?
questions.f: Potato chips were first made when a cook sliced potatoes super thin for a fussy customer.

questions.q: Which nut grows inside a hard shell you must crack open?
questions.f: A walnut's wrinkly shape reminded old doctors of a tiny brain.

questions.q: Which food is a sausage served inside a long soft bun?
questions.f: People eat billions of hot dogs every summer at ballgames and picnics.

questions.q: Which food is a round beef patty served in a bun?
questions.f: Despite its name, a hamburger has no ham in it at all.

questions.q: Which chewy sweet can you blow into a bubble?
questions.f: Bubble gum is usually colored pink because that was the only dye the inventor had.

questions.q: Which big bird is roasted for Thanksgiving dinner?
questions.f: A roast turkey is the center of the Thanksgiving meal in the United States.

questions.q: Which round, juicy fruit has the same name as a color?
questions.f: The fruit came first, and the color 'orange' was later named after it.

questions.q: Which round, leafy vegetable has layers you can peel apart?
questions.f: Cabbage can be green, red, or purple and is packed inside tight leafy layers.

questions.q: Which baked treat is round, sweet, and full of chocolate chips?
questions.f: The chocolate chip cookie was invented by a cook named Ruth Wakefield.

questions.q: Which small blue fruit grows in bunches on a bush?
questions.f: Blueberries are one of the few foods that are naturally a true blue color.

questions.q: Which long, green vegetable is called a 'string' or 'green' one?
questions.f: Green beans are picked young while the pod is still soft enough to eat.

questions.q: Which small red fruit grows on bushes and is used in jam and pies?
questions.f: A single raspberry is made of many tiny juicy beads all joined together.

questions.q: Which drink is fizzy, sweet, and full of bubbles?
questions.f: The bubbles in soda are made from a gas called carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Which sweet, hard candy comes stuck on a stick?
questions.f: The lollipop got its modern name and machine-made shape about 100 years ago.

questions.q: A baby cow is called a what?
questions.f: A newborn calf can stand and walk within about an hour of being born.

questions.q: A baby chicken is called a what?
questions.f: A chick uses a tiny bump on its beak called an egg tooth to peck out of its shell.

questions.q: A shop where bread and cakes are baked and sold is a…?
questions.f: The word 'bakery' comes from 'bake', to cook food with dry heat in an oven.

questions.q: The sweet food eaten at the end of a meal is called…?
questions.f: 'Dessert' comes from a French word meaning to clear the table before the sweet course.

questions.q: A person who cooks food in a restaurant kitchen is a…?
questions.f: The word 'chef' is French and means 'chief' or head of the kitchen.

questions.q: The list of foods you can order at a restaurant is the…?
questions.f: 'Menu' comes from a Latin word meaning small or detailed, like a small list.

questions.q: The last meal of the day is usually called…?
questions.f: Long ago 'dinner' meant the biggest meal, which people ate in the middle of the day.

questions.q: 'Breakfast' means the meal that breaks your…?
questions.f: 'Breakfast' literally means breaking the fast, since you have not eaten all night.

questions.q: Which tool do we use to eat soup?
questions.f: The rounded bowl of a spoon is perfect for scooping up liquids like soup.

questions.q: Which tool with pointy prongs do we use to pick up food?
questions.f: The word 'fork' comes from a Latin word for a farmer's pitchfork.

questions.q: The tiny bits of bread left after eating are called…?
questions.f: 'Crumb' is a very old English word for a small broken piece of bread.

questions.q: A person who grows food on the land is a…?
questions.f: The word 'farm' once meant a fixed rent paid for using land.

questions.q: The round dish we serve and eat our food from is a…?
questions.f: 'Plate' comes from a word meaning flat, since a plate is a flat dish.

questions.q: A small amount of food eaten between meals is a…?
questions.f: The word 'snack' once meant a quick bite, like a small snap of the teeth.

questions.q: A baby sheep is called a…?
questions.f: 'Lamb' is one of the oldest words in English and has barely changed for 1,000 years.

questions.q: A group of cows together is called a…?
questions.f: Cows in a herd look after each other and even have close friends.

questions.q: A large group of fish swimming together is called a…?
questions.f: Fish swim in a school to stay safe, since a big group confuses hungry predators.

questions.q: When food tastes really, really good, we say it is…?
questions.f: 'Delicious' comes from a Latin word meaning to delight or give pleasure.

questions.q: Which taste is the opposite of sweet, like a lemon?
questions.f: Your tongue can sense sour, sweet, salty, bitter, and a savory taste called umami.

questions.q: A drink made by squeezing fruit is called…?
questions.f: 'Juice' comes from a Latin word for broth or liquid.

questions.q: The room in a home where we cook food is the…?
questions.f: 'Kitchen' comes from a Latin word meaning to cook.

questions.q: A big, fancy meal shared by many people is a…?
questions.f: 'Feast' comes from a Latin word for a joyful holiday or festival.

questions.q: The written set of steps for making a dish is a…?
questions.f: 'Recipe' comes from a Latin word meaning 'take', once used at the start of instructions.

questions.q: We keep food cold and fresh inside the…?
questions.f: 'Fridge' is short for refrigerator, from a Latin word meaning to make cold.

questions.q: We bake bread and cakes inside a hot…?
questions.f: 'Oven' is a very old word, related to words for a hot enclosed space.

questions.q: A person who brings your food to the table is a…?
questions.f: A waiter 'waits' on you, an old meaning of 'wait' that means to attend or serve.

questions.q: Fruit like apples and cherries grow on…?
questions.f: The seeds inside a fruit can grow into a brand new tree.

questions.q: The word 'yolk' names which yellow part of an egg?
questions.f: 'Yolk' comes from an old English word meaning 'the yellow part'.

questions.q: A tomato grows on a plant.
questions.f: Tomatoes grow on leafy plants that need warm sun and lots of water.

questions.q: Lemons taste sweet, just like candy.
questions.f: Lemons taste sour, not sweet, because they are packed with citric acid.

questions.q: Which pink sea food has a curl and a little shell before it is peeled?
questions.f: Shrimp turn from grey to pink the moment they are cooked.

questions.q: Which warm drink is made from cocoa powder mixed into hot milk?
questions.f: People in Central America drank chocolate as a hot drink long before it became candy.

questions.q: Which fluffy fair treat is made from sugar spun into fine threads?
questions.f: A machine melts the sugar and spins it out through tiny holes into a cloud.

questions.q: Which dark green leafy vegetable made the cartoon sailor Popeye strong?
questions.f: Spinach really is packed with iron and vitamins that help your body.

questions.q: Which breakfast food is baked with a grid of little squares to hold syrup?
questions.f: The deep pockets of a waffle are perfect little cups for syrup and butter.

questions.q: Which bright yellow, tangy sauce is squeezed onto hot dogs?
questions.f: Mustard is made by grinding up the tiny seeds of the mustard plant.

questions.q: Which food is cheese melted between two slices of buttered, toasted bread?
questions.f: A grilled cheese sandwich is toasted in a hot pan until the cheese goes gooey.

questions.q: Which warm meal is made of noodles floating in a tasty broth?
questions.f: Noodle soups are loved all over the world, from chicken soup to ramen.

questions.q: Which small red root vegetable is crunchy and a little peppery?
questions.f: Radishes grow quickly, so they are a favorite first plant for young gardeners.

questions.q: Which crunchy triangle snack is made from corn and eaten with dips?
questions.f: Tortilla chips are made by cutting corn tortillas into wedges and frying them crisp.

questions.q: Which small orange fruit is fuzzy and looks like a tiny peach?
questions.f: Apricots ripen early in summer, before most other stone fruits.

questions.q: Which small cake is baked in a paper cup and often has a berry inside?
questions.f: Muffins can be sweet with berries or savory with cheese and corn.

questions.q: Which round green melon has sweet orange flesh and lots of seeds inside?
questions.f: You can tell a ripe cantaloupe by its sweet smell at the stem end.

questions.q: Which drink is made by stirring cocoa into cold milk for a sweet treat?
questions.f: Chocolate milk was invented in Jamaica over 300 years ago.

questions.q: A baby pig is called a…?
questions.f: A mother pig can have a litter of ten or more piglets at once.

questions.q: A baby duck is called a…?
questions.f: Ducklings can swim within a day of hatching from their eggs.

questions.q: A shop that sells fresh fruit and vegetables is called a…?
questions.f: A greengrocer's name comes from selling 'green' foods, meaning fresh plants.

questions.q: The meal we eat in the middle of the day is called…?
questions.f: The word 'lunch' is short for 'luncheon', an old word for a light midday meal.

questions.q: We keep ice cream and frozen peas cold and hard inside the…?
questions.f: A home freezer is kept well below the freezing point of water to keep food solid.

questions.q: Which flat kitchen tool is used to flip pancakes and burgers?
questions.f: The wide, thin blade of a spatula slides easily under food to turn it.

questions.q: Which big, deep-bowled spoon is used to serve soup from a pot?
questions.f: A ladle's long handle keeps your hand away from the hot soup.

questions.q: The cloth or paper we use to wipe our hands and mouth at meals is a…?
questions.f: 'Napkin' comes from an old word 'nappe', meaning a tablecloth.

questions.q: Which tall cup with a handle do we drink hot cocoa or tea from?
questions.f: A mug's thick walls help keep your hot drink warm for longer.

questions.q: Food that has gone bad and is no longer safe to eat is called…?
questions.f: Food rots when tiny microbes break it down, so we keep food cold to slow them.

questions.q: We chop and slice vegetables safely on top of a…?
questions.f: A chopping board protects the table and keeps the knife's edge sharp.

questions.q: Which sweet orange tropical fruit has one big flat pit inside?
questions.f: Mangoes are so loved in India that the tree is a national symbol there.

questions.q: Which green fruit is narrow at the top and round at the bottom?
questions.f: Pears keep ripening after picking, so they soften in the fruit bowl.

questions.q: Which small purple fruit has smooth skin and a pit in the middle?
questions.f: When a plum is dried it becomes a prune.

questions.q: Which fruit has soft fuzzy skin and a big wrinkled pit inside?
questions.f: Peaches first grew in China thousands of years ago.

questions.q: Which long green vegetable is cool, crunchy, and sliced into salads?
questions.f: A cucumber is more than 95 percent water, which is why it tastes so refreshing.

questions.q: Which food grows in damp woods and has a stalk with a round cap on top?
questions.f: Some mushrooms are tasty, but wild ones must never be eaten without an expert's help.

questions.q: Which strong-smelling bulb comes apart into little pieces called cloves?
questions.f: One head of garlic can hold ten or more cloves under its papery skin.

questions.q: Which pale green vegetable grows in long crunchy stalks?
questions.f: Celery makes such a loud crunch because its stalks are packed with water.

questions.q: What do we call bread that has been browned in a toaster?
questions.f: Bread turns brown and smells wonderful when the heat browns its surface.

questions.q: What do we call food packed between two slices of bread?
questions.f: People eat millions of sandwiches every single day for lunch.

questions.q: Which soft, squishy white sweet is toasted on a stick over a campfire?
questions.f: A toasted marshmallow goes crisp and golden outside while turning gooey inside.

questions.q: Which baked dessert has a pastry crust filled with fruit?
questions.f: Apple pie is one of the oldest and best-loved pies in the world.

questions.q: Which small cake is baked in a paper case and topped with swirls of frosting?
questions.f: Cupcakes got their name because the batter was once measured out in cups.

questions.q: Which thick, cold drink is made by blending ice cream with milk?
questions.f: Milkshakes became a huge treat once electric blenders reached soda shops.

questions.q: Which fluffy white topping is made by whipping cream until it holds its shape?
questions.f: Whipping traps tiny air bubbles in the cream, making it light and puffy.

questions.q: Which salty breakfast strips come from a pig?
questions.f: Bacon is salted and often smoked, which keeps it tasty for longer.

questions.q: Which round ball of ground meat is often served with spaghetti?
questions.f: Meatballs are made all over the world, from Sweden to Italy to Turkey.

questions.q: Which white seasoning do we shake on food to make it taste less plain?
questions.f: Salt is the only rock that people eat on purpose every single day.

questions.q: Which dark seasoning sits beside the salt in a pair of shakers?
questions.f: Black pepper is made from dried berries picked from a climbing vine.

questions.q: Which white powder is made by grinding wheat and used to bake bread?
questions.f: Flour is made by crushing grains of wheat between heavy rollers or stones.

questions.q: Which thin tube do we use to sip a drink from a cup?
questions.f: A straw works because sucking lowers the air pressure so the drink rises.

questions.q: Which deep, round dish do we eat cereal and soup from?
questions.f: A bowl's high curved sides keep runny food from spilling over.

questions.q: Which flat kitchen dish with a handle do we fry eggs in?
questions.f: A frying pan spreads the stove's heat evenly across the food.

questions.q: Which kitchen machine do we use to boil water for tea?
questions.f: An electric kettle can bring a cup of water to the boil in under a minute.

questions.q: Which machine has two slots and browns your bread for breakfast?
questions.f: Glowing hot wires inside the toaster do the browning.

questions.q: Which machine has spinning blades that whizz fruit into a smoothie?
questions.f: A blender's blades spin so fast they chop and mix at the same time.

questions.q: What does a cook tie on to keep their clothes clean?
questions.f: An apron catches the splashes and flour that fly around a busy kitchen.

questions.q: What do we call a meal we carry outdoors and eat on a blanket?
questions.f: Picnic baskets are packed with foods that taste good cold.

questions.q: Which big shop has aisles of food and trolleys to push around?
questions.f: A large supermarket can stock tens of thousands of different foods.

questions.q: A book full of recipes for making meals is called a…?
questions.f: Some of the oldest cookbooks ever found were written on clay tablets.

questions.q: A person who keeps bees and collects their honey is a…?
questions.f: Beekeepers wear veils and use gentle smoke to keep the bees calm.

questions.q: A male chicken, the one that crows in the morning, is called a…?
questions.f: A rooster's tall red comb and long tail feathers make him easy to spot.

questions.q: A baby goose is called a…?
questions.f: Goslings follow their parents in a neat line almost as soon as they hatch.

questions.q: When your tummy is empty and you want food, you feel…?
questions.f: Your stomach can even rumble when it is empty and waiting for food.

questions.q: When you really need a drink of water, you feel…?
questions.f: Feeling thirsty is your body's clever way of asking for more water.

questions.q: Which part of your body do you taste food with?
questions.f: Your tongue is covered in thousands of tiny taste buds.

questions.q: Which part of your body do you use to chew your food?
questions.f: Chewing breaks food into small pieces so your body can use it.

questions.q: Honey and sugar both taste…?
questions.f: Sweetness is the first taste most babies ever enjoy.

questions.q: Potato chips and pretzels both taste…?
questions.f: A little salt makes many foods taste richer and fuller.

questions.q: Which word describes the sharp taste of a strong, dark coffee?
questions.f: Bitterness warns animals away from many plants that would not be good for them.

questions.q: Food that makes your mouth feel hot, like chili, is called…?
questions.f: Spicy heat is not really a taste at all, but a feeling on your tongue.

questions.q: A fruit that is ready to eat is said to be…?
questions.f: Fruit often changes color and smell to show that it is ripe.

questions.q: Food that has not been cooked yet is called…?
questions.f: Some foods, like carrots, are lovely raw, while others must be cooked first.

questions.q: What do we do to bread dough when we cook it in the oven?
questions.f: Baking uses dry heat all around the food instead of hot water or oil.

questions.q: The skin you take off a banana before eating it is called the…?
questions.f: Banana peel is thick and slippery, which is why it is famous for slips.

questions.q: The little brown things in the middle of an apple are the…?
questions.f: Each apple seed could grow into a whole new apple tree.

questions.q: The box you carry your midday meal to school in is a…?
questions.f: Keeping a cold pack in a lunchbox helps stop food from spoiling.

questions.q: Food that is left over after a meal is called…?
questions.f: Storing leftovers in the fridge means a tasty meal can be enjoyed twice.

questions.q: A small piece of food taken with your teeth is called a…?
questions.f: Taking small bites and chewing well makes food easier to swallow.

questions.q: A small mouthful of a drink is called a…?
questions.f: Sipping a hot drink slowly keeps you from burning your tongue.

questions.q: Carrots grow under the ground.
questions.f: A carrot is the plant's root, with leafy green tops above the soil.

questions.q: Apples grow on small bushes close to the ground.
questions.f: Apples grow on trees, often in big planted fields called orchards.

questions.q: Ice cream melts when it gets warm.
questions.f: Ice cream is mostly frozen water and cream, so warmth turns it runny.

questions.q: A fork is the best tool for eating runny soup.
questions.f: A spoon's little bowl holds liquid, while soup would drip right off a fork.

questions.q: Cheese is a kind of fruit that grows on trees.
questions.f: Cheese is a dairy food made from milk, not a fruit at all.

questions.q: A hen lays eggs.
questions.f: A busy hen can lay around 300 eggs in one year.

questions.q: Potatoes grow high up on tall trees.
questions.f: Potatoes grow under the soil, while leafy green stems grow above it.

questions.q: A pineapple has a rough, spiky skin.
questions.f: That tough, prickly skin protects the sweet yellow fruit inside.

questions.q: Onions grow under the ground as round bulbs.
questions.f: An onion bulb stores food for the plant inside its many layers.

questions.q: Lettuce is a leaf.
questions.f: When you eat lettuce, you are eating the leaves of the lettuce plant.

questions.q: You should wash your hands before you help make food.
questions.f: Washing with soap removes germs that could otherwise get into the food.

questions.q: Frozen peas should be kept in a warm cupboard.
questions.f: Frozen food belongs in the freezer, where it stays safely frozen solid.

questions.q: A potato is which part of the plant?
questions.f: A potato is a tuber, a swollen underground stem the plant uses to store energy.

questions.q: Which vitamin, made by our skin in the sun, is the 'sunshine vitamin'?
questions.f: Vitamin D helps our bodies absorb calcium to build strong bones.

questions.q: Which mineral is added to table salt to keep our bodies healthy?
questions.f: Adding iodine to salt is one of the cheapest health measures ever invented.

questions.q: Which meat comes from a pig?
questions.f: Beef comes from cattle, mutton from sheep, and venison from deer.

questions.q: Which sea creature is sliced into rings and fried as 'calamari'?
questions.f: 'Calamari' is simply the Italian word for squid.

questions.q: Which fruit hides juicy red seeds inside a tough leathery skin?
questions.f: A single pomegranate can hold over 600 juicy seeds called arils.

questions.q: Which sweet is made by heating sugar until it melts into golden brown?
questions.f: Caramel forms when sugar gets hot enough to break down and turn brown and nutty.

questions.q: Which vegetable is called 'eggplant' in America and 'aubergine' in Britain?
questions.f: Early eggplants were small and white, which is why they were named after eggs.

questions.q: Which spice is a dried flower bud used in baking and holiday ham?
questions.f: Cloves are so strong that just a few can flavor a whole pot of food.

questions.q: Which drink is made from crushed and pressed apples?
questions.f: Fresh apple cider is cloudy because it still contains tiny bits of the whole apple.

questions.q: Which sweet fruit grows in heavy bunches on a desert palm tree?
questions.f: Date palms have been grown for food for over 6,000 years in the Middle East.

questions.q: Which grain is ground into flour to make most pasta?
questions.f: The best pasta is made from a hard type of wheat called durum.

questions.q: Which fruit gives traditional marmalade its main flavor?
questions.f: Marmalade is usually made with bitter Seville oranges, peel and all.

questions.q: Which cheese is famous for its blue-green veins running through it?
questions.f: The blue veins are a safe, edible mold added on purpose for flavor.

questions.q: Which part of a peach is hard and should not be eaten?
questions.f: The pit, or stone, holds the seed the tree would use to grow a new peach.

questions.q: Which crop failed in Ireland in the 1840s, causing a terrible famine?
questions.f: A disease called blight rotted Ireland's potatoes, the main food for most people.

questions.q: Which country is the home of the rice-and-seafood dish called paella?
questions.f: Paella began near the city of Valencia in eastern Spain.

questions.q: Which fruit is fuzzy brown outside with green flesh and tiny black seeds?
questions.f: The kiwifruit was renamed after New Zealand's kiwi bird to help it sell abroad.

questions.q: Which food is made from ground chickpeas shaped into fried balls?
questions.f: Falafel is a popular street food across the Middle East.

questions.q: Which leafy green is the classic base of a Caesar salad?
questions.f: The Caesar salad was named after a restaurant owner, not the Roman ruler.

questions.q: Which cooking method uses water heated until it bubbles rapidly?
questions.f: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level, but lower up a tall mountain.

questions.q: Which sweet pepper comes in red, yellow, and green and has no heat?
questions.f: Bell peppers turn from green to red, yellow, or orange as they ripen.

questions.q: Which Japanese soup is made from a fermented soybean paste?
questions.f: Miso paste is made by fermenting soybeans with salt for months or even years.

questions.q: Which meat is traditionally served with mint sauce in Britain?
questions.f: The tang of mint sauce was long thought to balance the richness of lamb.

questions.q: Which fruit is picked green and ripens to yellow after it is harvested?
questions.f: Bananas give off a gas that ripens both themselves and nearby fruit.

questions.q: Which orange root vegetable is grated into a famous sweet cake?
questions.f: Carrot cake became popular when sugar was scarce and carrots added natural sweetness.

questions.q: Which mineral in red meat and spinach helps blood carry oxygen?
questions.f: Iron sits at the center of hemoglobin, the part of blood that grabs oxygen.

questions.q: Which long green vegetable has a woody end you snap off before cooking?
questions.f: Asparagus can grow astonishingly fast, sometimes several inches in a single day.

questions.q: A person whose job is baking bread is called a…?
questions.f: 'Baker' comes from the old word 'bake', to cook with dry heat.

questions.q: A baby goat is called a…?
questions.f: That is why calling a child a 'kid' started as a playful joke long ago.

questions.q: An animal that eats both plants and meat is called an…?
questions.f: 'Omnivore' comes from Latin 'omni' (all) plus 'vorare' (to devour).

questions.q: An animal that eats only plants is called a…?
questions.f: 'Herbivore' comes from Latin 'herba' (plant) plus 'vorare' (to devour).

questions.q: An animal that eats only meat is called a…?
questions.f: 'Carnivore' comes from Latin 'carn' (flesh) plus 'vorare' (to devour).

questions.q: A person who chooses not to eat any meat is called a…?
questions.f: The word 'vegetarian' was made popular by a society founded in England in 1847.

questions.q: The word 'dairy' means foods made from…?
questions.f: 'Dairy' comes from an old word for a woman who milked cows and made butter.

questions.q: The word 'poultry' means meat from which kind of animal?
questions.f: 'Poultry' comes from a French word for a young hen or fowl.

questions.q: A place planted with rows of grapevines is called a…?
questions.f: 'Vineyard' joins 'vine' with 'yard', meaning an enclosed piece of ground.

questions.q: A place planted with rows of fruit trees is called an…?
questions.f: 'Orchard' comes from old words meaning a garden enclosure for growing plants.

questions.q: If a food is 'edible', it is…?
questions.f: 'Edible' comes from the Latin word 'edere', which simply means to eat.

questions.q: To 'knead' bread dough means to…?
questions.f: Kneading lines up stretchy strands of gluten so bread can rise and hold its shape.

questions.q: A 'whisk' is a kitchen tool used mainly to…?
c: Beat air into eggs or cream
questions.f: The loops of a whisk trap air, turning cream and egg whites light and fluffy.

questions.q: The word 'brunch' is a blend of which two meals?
questions.f: 'Brunch' was coined in England in 1895 for a lazy weekend meal.

questions.q: To 'grate' cheese means to…?
questions.f: 'Grate' comes from an old word meaning to scrape or scratch.

questions.q: The hard, browned outer layer of a loaf of bread is called the…?
questions.f: 'Crust' comes from a Latin word meaning a hard shell or rind.

questions.q: Herbs such as basil and parsley usually come from a plant's…?
questions.f: Spices, by contrast, often come from seeds, bark, or roots rather than leaves.

questions.q: To 'simmer' a food means to cook it in liquid that is…?
c: Gently bubbling just below a boil
questions.f: A gentle simmer keeps delicate foods from breaking apart the way a hard boil would.

questions.q: A shaped, baked amount of bread is called a…?
questions.f: 'Loaf' is a very old English word, older than the word 'bread' itself.

questions.q: The word 'marmalade' names a jam made mainly from…?
questions.f: 'Marmalade' comes from 'marmelo', the Portuguese word for quince.

questions.q: To 'ferment' a food means to change it using tiny living…?
questions.f: Fermenting microbes give us yogurt, cheese, pickles, and fluffy bread.

questions.q: An orchard is a place where fruit trees are grown.
questions.f: Apple, cherry, and orange orchards can hold hundreds of neatly planted trees.

questions.q: A carnivore is an animal that eats only plants.
questions.f: A carnivore eats meat; an animal that eats only plants is a herbivore.

questions.q: Which is the largest fruit that grows on a tree, sometimes weighing over 50 pounds?
questions.f: A single jackfruit can grow as big as a small child and feed a whole family.

questions.q: Which dark, curly-leaved green is a member of the cabbage family and full of vitamins?
questions.f: Kale grows well in cold weather and even tastes sweeter after a frost.

questions.q: The pasta dish spaghetti bolognese takes its name from a city in which country?
questions.f: Bologna, in northern Italy, is famous for its rich meat sauces.

questions.q: Which Mexican dish is a tortilla folded over melted cheese and grilled?
questions.f: 'Quesadilla' comes from 'queso', the Spanish word for cheese.

questions.q: Which sweet pastry is made of thin layers stacked with nuts and honey syrup?
questions.f: Baklava is popular across Turkey, Greece, and the Middle East.

questions.q: Which soft, sweet fruit full of tiny seeds grows on a tree and is often dried?
questions.f: A fig is unusual because its flowers actually bloom hidden inside the fruit.

questions.q: Which cold, refreshing drink is made from tea leaves, ice, and often lemon?
questions.f: Iced tea became hugely popular after being served at a hot 1904 world's fair.

questions.q: Which nut is blended with cocoa to make the famous chocolate spread Nutella?
questions.f: Nutella was invented in Italy when cocoa was scarce, so hazelnuts stretched it further.

questions.q: Besides cows, which animal is often milked to make cheese and yogurt?
questions.f: Goat's milk is easier for some people to digest than cow's milk.

questions.q: Which frozen dessert is made from fruit and sugar but contains no milk?
questions.f: Because it has no dairy, sorbet is a favorite for people who avoid milk.

questions.q: Which tan, bell-shaped squash is roasted for soups and has sweet orange flesh?
questions.f: Butternut squash keeps for months in a cool, dry place thanks to its tough skin.

questions.q: Which fish is very commonly sold in cans and used in sandwiches and salads?
questions.f: Tuna are powerful swimmers that can cross entire oceans.

questions.q: The dish 'fish and chips' is a national favorite in which country?
questions.f: Fish and chips shops became common in Britain in the 1860s.

questions.q: Which knobbly root adds warm spice to gingerbread and ginger tea?
questions.f: Ginger is not really a root but an underground stem called a rhizome.

questions.q: Which round bread with a hole is boiled in water before it is baked?
questions.f: Boiling first is what gives a bagel its chewy inside and shiny crust.

questions.q: Which mild vegetable looks like a giant green onion with a white base?
questions.f: The leek is a national symbol of Wales, worn on Saint David's Day.

questions.q: Which spiky, sweet tropical fruit grows on a low plant, not on a tall tree?
questions.f: A pineapple plant grows just one fruit at a time from its center.

questions.q: The hamburger is said to be named after a port city in which country?
questions.f: 'Hamburg steak' was minced beef linked to the German city of Hamburg.

questions.q: Which round root vegetable is deep red-purple and stains your fingers?
questions.f: The red color of beetroot comes from a pigment called betalain.

questions.q: A baby fish is called a…?
questions.f: A large group of newly hatched baby fish is even called a 'fry' too.

questions.q: A person who catches fish for food is a…?
questions.f: Fishing is one of the oldest ways humans have gathered food.

questions.q: A farm building or business that produces milk, butter, and cheese is a…?
questions.f: 'Dairy' comes from an old word for the maid who milked the cows.

questions.q: The suffix '-vore' in words like 'herbivore' means one who…?
questions.f: From Latin 'vorare', to devour, giving carnivore, herbivore, and omnivore.

questions.q: Which kitchen tool is used to strip the skin off potatoes and carrots?
questions.f: A good peeler removes just the thin skin, saving the food underneath.

questions.q: Bread that has gone 'stale' has become…?
questions.f: Bread goes stale as its starch slowly firms up, even without drying out completely.

questions.q: Food described as 'crisp' is pleasantly…?
questions.f: A fresh apple or cracker snaps cleanly, which is what makes it crisp.

questions.q: A drink that is 'fizzy' is full of…?
questions.f: The fizz is carbon dioxide gas escaping as tiny bubbles.

questions.q: Which food is famous for its 'sour' taste?
questions.f: Sour foods contain acids, which is why they can make your mouth pucker.

questions.q: A 'dozen' eggs means how many eggs?
questions.f: Eggs are often sold by the dozen because twelve divides evenly many ways.

questions.q: Half a dozen eggs is how many?
questions.f: 'Half a dozen of one, six of the other' is a saying meaning two things are the same.

questions.q: A recipe that calls for 'a pinch' of salt means a…?
questions.f: A pinch is about what you can hold between your thumb and finger.

questions.q: To 'stir' a pot of soup means to…?
questions.f: Stirring spreads the heat so the soup does not burn on the bottom.

questions.q: A 'slice' of bread is a…?
questions.f: 'Slice' comes from an old word meaning to split or cut.

questions.q: An adult female chicken, kept for laying eggs, is called a…?
questions.f: A hen can lay around 300 eggs in a single year.

questions.q: Which country is most famous for its thick, deep-pocketed waffles?
questions.f: Belgium has several waffle styles, including the light Brussels and chewy Liege.

questions.q: The small steamed dishes called dim sum come from which country?
questions.f: Dim sum is served in little baskets with tea, often for a long weekend brunch.

questions.q: The gyro, meat carved from a tall spit into flatbread, comes from which country?
questions.f: 'Gyro' comes from a Greek word meaning to turn, like the rotating spit.

questions.q: Which country produces the most oranges in the world?
questions.f: Much of Brazil's orange crop is squeezed into juice and shipped worldwide.

questions.q: Which country produces the most maple syrup in the world?
questions.f: The province of Quebec alone makes the large majority of the world's maple syrup.

questions.q: Which country grows the most tomatoes in the world?
questions.f: China grows roughly a third of all the tomatoes on Earth.

questions.q: Which meatballs served with gravy and jam are a famous dish of Sweden?
questions.f: Swedish meatballs are traditionally served with lingonberry jam.

questions.q: In which two countries are chopsticks the most traditional eating tools?
questions.f: Chopsticks have been used in China for well over 3,000 years.

questions.q: When you eat celery, which part of the plant are you eating?
questions.f: Celery stalks carry water up from the roots to the leaves.

questions.q: When you eat peas, which part of the plant are you eating?
questions.f: Each pea is a seed that could have grown into a whole new pea plant.

questions.q: What do green plants need from the sun in order to make their own food?
questions.f: Plants use light, water, and air to build sugar in a process called photosynthesis.

questions.q: Bees help fruit grow by moving pollen between flowers, a job called…?
questions.f: Without pollinators, we would lose many apples, almonds, and berries.

questions.q: In which season are most apples picked in orchards?
questions.f: Apples need a long warm summer before they sweeten and ripen in autumn.

questions.q: Which huge machine cuts, threshes, and cleans wheat all in one pass?
questions.f: It is called a 'combine' because it combines several harvesting jobs at once.

questions.q: Cow's milk is mostly made of which substance?
questions.f: Milk is roughly 87 percent water, with fat, sugar, and protein making up the rest.

questions.q: At what temperature does water freeze into ice?
questions.f: Adding salt lowers water's freezing point, which is how old ice-cream makers worked.

questions.q: A 'fillet' of fish is a piece that has had its what removed?
questions.f: Filleting takes skill, since the knife must follow the fish's bone structure.

questions.q: Farms labelled 'organic' avoid using which of these?
questions.f: Organic farmers rely on compost, crop rotation, and helpful insects instead.

questions.q: Which shellfish with a dark hinged shell is often steamed open and eaten?
questions.f: Mussels cling to rocks with strong natural threads called byssus.

questions.q: Which colour does a lobster turn when it is cooked?
questions.f: Heat destroys the other pigments in the shell, leaving only the red one behind.

questions.q: Which shellfish is famous for sometimes growing a pearl inside its shell?
questions.f: A pearl forms when the oyster coats a piece of grit with smooth layers.

questions.q: A 'crouton' scattered on soup or salad is a small cube of…?
questions.f: Croutons were invented as a clever way to use up bread that had gone stale.

questions.q: A 'batter' for pancakes is a runny mixture of flour, eggs, and…?
questions.f: Batter is pourable, while a stiffer dough can be kneaded and shaped by hand.

questions.q: Which mixture is stiff enough to knead and shape by hand?
questions.f: Bread dough becomes stretchy as it is worked, thanks to the protein gluten.

questions.q: A 'brine' used for pickling and curing food is water mixed with plenty of…?
questions.f: Salty brine draws water out of food, making it hard for spoiling microbes to grow.

questions.q: The 'zest' a recipe asks for is the grated outer…?
questions.f: Citrus peel holds tiny pockets of fragrant oil that carry most of the aroma.

questions.q: Crunchy 'bean sprouts' in a stir-fry are beans that have just begun to…?
questions.f: Sprouting wakes the seed up and makes its nutrients easier to absorb.

questions.q: Which pale root vegetable looks like a cream-coloured carrot and tastes sweet when roasted?
questions.f: Before sugar was common in Europe, parsnips were used to sweeten cakes.

questions.q: Which green pod vegetable turns soups and gumbo thick and silky?
questions.f: Okra releases a natural thickener when it is sliced and simmered.

questions.q: Which starchy relative of the banana is usually cooked before it is eaten?
questions.f: Fried plantain slices are a favourite side dish across Africa and the Caribbean.

questions.q: Which round-bottomed pan is used for fast Chinese stir-frying?
questions.f: A wok's sloped sides let a cook toss food up into the hottest part of the pan.

questions.q: Which fine mesh tool is used to sift flour and strain lumps out?
questions.f: Sifting flour through a sieve also mixes in air, making cakes lighter.

questions.q: Which kitchen tool is rolled over pastry to flatten it out?
questions.f: Chilled dough rolls out best, since warm butter makes the pastry sticky.

questions.q: Which kitchen machine heats food quickly using invisible waves?
questions.f: The waves make water inside the food jiggle, and that jiggling creates heat.

questions.q: An egg cooked gently in simmering water without its shell is called…?
questions.f: A splash of vinegar in the water helps a poached egg hold its shape.

questions.q: Which cooking method uses the hot vapour rising from boiling water?
questions.f: Steaming is gentle, so vegetables keep more of their colour and vitamins.

questions.q: A large group of bees flying together is called a…?
questions.f: Bees swarm when a hive grows crowded and part of it leaves to find a new home.

questions.q: A group of sheep kept together is called a…?
questions.f: Sheep stick close together in a flock because it keeps them safer.

questions.q: A single corn cob is properly called an…?
questions.f: 'Ear' here comes from an old word for a spike of grain, not the ear you hear with.

questions.q: A single small segment of garlic is called a…?
questions.f: Confusingly, the spice cloves are a totally different thing: dried flower buds.

questions.q: A whole round cabbage or lettuce is called a…?
questions.f: Farmers count leafy crops like cabbage and lettuce by the head.

questions.q: A whole large round of cheese is called a…?
questions.f: A single wheel of Parmesan can weigh more than a large dog.

questions.q: A small leafy stem of a herb like parsley is called a…?
questions.f: Cooks tie sprigs of herbs together to flavour a pot, then lift them out.

questions.q: Food described as 'bland' has…?
questions.f: A pinch of salt, a squeeze of lemon, or fresh herbs can rescue a bland dish.

questions.q: Meat described as 'tender' is…?
questions.f: Slow, gentle cooking softens tough meat by breaking down its connective tissue.

questions.q: Food that stretches and needs a lot of chewing is described as…?
questions.f: Toffee and bagels are both famous for being pleasantly chewy.

questions.q: Food described as 'nutritious' is…?
c: Full of goodness for your body
questions.f: 'Nutritious' comes from a Latin word meaning to nourish or feed.

questions.q: A small dish served before the main meal is called an…?
questions.f: An appetizer is meant to wake up your appetite for what is coming.

questions.q: The word 'beverage' means any kind of…?
questions.f: 'Beverage' comes from a Latin word meaning to drink.

questions.q: A 'utensil' in the kitchen is a…?
questions.f: 'Utensil' comes from a Latin word meaning something fit for use.

questions.q: An 'ingredient' is…?
c: One item that goes into a dish
questions.f: 'Ingredient' comes from a Latin word meaning to enter or go in.

questions.q: A 'portion' of food is…?
c: The amount served to one person
questions.f: 'Portion' comes from a Latin word meaning a share or part.

questions.q: To 'preserve' food means to…?
questions.f: Drying, salting, freezing, and canning are all ways to preserve food.

questions.q: To 'roast' food means to cook it with…?
c: Dry heat in an oven or fire
questions.f: Roasting browns the outside of food, building deep, savoury flavour.

questions.q: To 'mince' food means to…?
questions.f: Minced garlic releases far more flavour than a whole clove, since more is exposed.

questions.q: To 'sift' flour means to…?
c: Pass it through a fine mesh
questions.f: Sifting breaks up lumps and lets air in, so cakes rise more evenly.

questions.q: A 'garnish' on a plate of food is…?
questions.f: 'Garnish' comes from an old French word meaning to adorn or equip.

questions.q: A 'seasoning' is added to food mainly to…?
questions.f: Salt, pepper, and herbs are the most widely used seasonings in the world.

questions.q: The 'agri' in 'agriculture' means…?
questions.f: From Latin 'ager', field; agriculture is literally the care of fields.

questions.q: An 'apiary' is a place where people keep…?
questions.f: From Latin 'apis', bee; an apiary is a collection of beehives.

questions.q: A 'greenhouse' helps plants grow by trapping…?
questions.f: Glass lets sunlight in but slows the escape of warmth, so crops grow all year.

questions.q: To 'thaw' frozen food means to…?
c: Let it warm up and soften
questions.f: The safest place to thaw food slowly is in the fridge, not on the counter.

questions.q: Lobsters are bright red even before they are cooked.
questions.f: Live lobsters are usually dark blue-green or brown; heat turns them red.

questions.q: Bees help pollinate many of the fruits that people eat.
questions.f: Around a third of the food we eat depends on pollinating insects.

questions.q: Mushrooms are a kind of plant.
questions.f: Mushrooms are fungi, which form their own separate kingdom of living things.

questions.q: All cheese must be made from cow's milk.
questions.f: Cheese is also made from the milk of goats, sheep, and even buffalo.

questions.q: An appetizer is served at the very end of a meal.
questions.f: An appetizer opens the meal, while dessert closes it.

questions.q: Frozen vegetables can be just as nutritious as fresh ones.
questions.f: They are frozen soon after picking, which locks in their vitamins.

questions.q: Chocolate is safe for dogs to eat in large amounts.
questions.f: Chocolate contains theobromine, which dogs cannot break down the way people can.

questions.q: Eating vegetables of many different colours gives you a wider range of vitamins.
questions.f: The pigments that colour vegetables often come with their own helpful nutrients.

questions.q: A cucumber is more than 90 percent water.
questions.f: At about 95 percent water, cucumber is one of the most watery foods we eat.

questions.q: A lack of which vitamin causes the sailors' disease called scurvy?
questions.f: Without vitamin C the body cannot make collagen, so gums bleed and wounds reopen.

questions.q: Which citrus fruit did British sailors eat so often they were nicknamed 'limeys'?
questions.f: The British navy issued limes to prevent scurvy on long ocean voyages.

questions.q: On which continent did the tomato first grow wild?
questions.f: Tomatoes came from the Americas and only reached Italy in the 1500s.

questions.q: In which mountains did the potato first grow before spreading worldwide?
questions.f: Farmers in the Andes grew thousands of potato varieties long before Europeans arrived.

questions.q: Which acid gives yogurt and soured milk their tangy taste?
questions.f: Bacteria make lactic acid as they turn milk into yogurt, thickening it too.

questions.q: Which natural sugar is found in milk?
questions.f: People who cannot digest lactose lack enough of the enzyme lactase.

questions.q: Which natural sugar makes fruit taste sweet?
questions.f: Fructose is the sweetest of the common natural sugars.

questions.q: What is the chemical name for ordinary table sugar?
questions.f: Sucrose is really two smaller sugars, glucose and fructose, joined together.

questions.q: Which fruit contains an enzyme that stops gelatin jelly from setting?
questions.f: Pineapple's enzyme bromelain breaks down the protein that lets jelly set, unless the fruit is cooked first.

questions.q: Which acid gives vinegar its sharp, sour smell and taste?
questions.f: Vinegar forms when bacteria turn the alcohol in cider or wine into acetic acid.

questions.q: Which enzyme in your saliva begins breaking down starchy food?
questions.f: That is why a plain cracker slowly starts to taste sweet as you chew it.

questions.q: Black pepper is made from the dried berries of what kind of plant?
questions.f: Peppercorns were once so valuable they were used to pay rent and taxes.

questions.q: Tofu is made by curdling the milk pressed from which bean?
questions.f: Tofu was invented in China more than 2,000 years ago.

questions.q: Sauerkraut is a tangy food made by fermenting which vegetable?
questions.f: 'Sauerkraut' is German for 'sour cabbage', preserved by salt and good bacteria.

questions.q: The savory taste 'umami' was first identified from a broth made with what?
questions.f: In 1908 chemist Kikunae Ikeda found the umami taste came from glutamate in kombu.

questions.q: Green tea differs from black tea mainly because green tea leaves are…?
questions.f: Stopping oxidation early keeps green tea's fresh, grassy color and flavor.

questions.q: In which country did people first grow and drink tea thousands of years ago?
questions.f: Legend says a Chinese emperor discovered tea when leaves blew into his boiling water.

questions.q: Which country drinks the most tea per person?
questions.f: In Turkey, tea is served all day in small tulip-shaped glasses.

questions.q: The ancient Maya and Aztecs drank chocolate mostly in what form?
questions.f: They flavored their chocolate drink with chili and had no sugar to sweeten it.

questions.q: Which strong-smelling bulb is famous in folklore for keeping vampires away?
questions.f: Garlic gets its powerful smell from sulfur compounds released when it is crushed.

questions.q: Which mineral, plentiful in bananas, helps muscles and nerves work?
questions.f: Potassium helps send the electrical signals that make your muscles move.

questions.q: Which pale vegetable's name means 'cabbage flower' and looks like a white brain?
questions.f: Cauliflower is grown so its flower buds stay white by shading them from sunlight.

questions.q: Which country eats the most cheese per person each year?
questions.f: France makes hundreds of different cheeses, from soft Brie to blue Roquefort.

questions.q: Which grain is stirred slowly with broth to make the Italian dish risotto?
questions.f: Short, starchy Arborio rice gives risotto its famous creamy texture.

questions.q: When we eat an artichoke, we are really eating the plant's unopened…?
questions.f: If left to grow, an artichoke opens into a large purple thistle flower.

questions.q: Which dried sea vegetable is wrapped around sushi rolls?
questions.f: Nori sheets are made by shredding seaweed and drying it flat like paper.

questions.q: The warming spice blend 'garam masala' comes from which country?
questions.f: 'Garam masala' means 'hot spice mix', though its heat is warmth, not chili fire.

questions.q: Which creamy dessert is thickened by gently cooking eggs with milk?
questions.f: If custard gets too hot the eggs scramble, so cooks stir it slowly and gently.

questions.q: Which crisp dessert is made by baking whipped egg whites and sugar?
questions.f: Whipping traps air in the egg whites, so meringue bakes light and crunchy.

questions.q: A skilled cook who specializes in cakes and desserts is a…?
questions.f: 'Patisserie' is the French word for both the pastry shop and the art of pastry making.

questions.q: A shopkeeper who cuts and sells meat is called a…?
questions.f: 'Butcher' comes from an old French word linked to 'bouc', a male goat.

questions.q: A person trained to make and serve coffee drinks is a…?
questions.f: 'Barista' is Italian and simply means 'bartender'.

questions.q: The root 'lact' in words like 'lactose' means…?
questions.f: From Latin 'lac', milk, which also gives us 'lactic' and 'lactate'.

questions.q: The root 'carn' in 'carnivore' means…?
questions.f: From Latin 'caro, carnis', flesh, which also gives us the word 'chili con carne'.

questions.q: The prefix 'omni-' in 'omnivore' means…?
questions.f: From Latin 'omnis', all; an omnivore eats all kinds of food.

questions.q: The word 'culinary' describes anything to do with…?
questions.f: From Latin 'culina', kitchen; a culinary school teaches the art of cooking.

questions.q: The root 'gastro-' in 'gastronomy' means…?
questions.f: From Greek 'gaster', stomach; gastronomy is the art and study of good eating.

questions.q: Peaches, plums, and cherries all belong to a fruit group called…?
questions.f: A drupe has soft flesh around a single hard pit that holds the seed.

questions.q: Beans, peas, and lentils belong to a plant group called…?
questions.f: Legumes grow their seeds inside pods and help enrich the soil with nitrogen.

questions.q: A diet that includes no animal products at all, not even eggs, is called…?
questions.f: The word 'vegan' was coined in 1944 by taking the start and end of 'vegetarian'.

questions.q: The word 'ferment' comes from a Latin word meaning to…?
questions.f: From Latin 'fervere', to boil; fermenting foods really do bubble as gas forms.

questions.q: To 'sauté' food, a French term, literally means to…?
questions.f: From French 'sauter', to jump; food is tossed so it 'jumps' in a hot pan.

questions.q: A 'condiment' is a food whose main job is to…?
questions.f: From Latin 'condire', to season or preserve; ketchup and mustard are condiments.

questions.q: The word 'salad' comes from a Latin word meaning…?
questions.f: From Latin 'sal', salt; early Romans ate greens dressed with salty brine.

questions.q: The word 'salary' shares a root with 'salad'; that shared root means…?
questions.f: Roman soldiers were said to receive money for salt, giving us 'salary'.

questions.q: To 'marinate' food means to…?
c: Soak it in a seasoned liquid
questions.f: 'Marinate' comes from a word for sea brine, since early marinades were salty.

questions.q: The root 'therm' in 'thermometer' and 'thermos' means…?
questions.f: From Greek 'therme', heat; a thermos keeps hot food hot by trapping heat.

questions.q: In nature, 'nectar' is the sweet liquid that bees collect from…?
questions.f: In Greek myth, nectar was also the drink of the gods on Mount Olympus.

questions.q: A full set of knives, forks, and spoons is together called…?
questions.f: 'Cutlery' comes from 'cutler', a craftsman who made knives and blades.

questions.q: The word 'omelette' comes from an old French word meaning a thin…?
questions.f: A flat, folded omelette was thought to resemble the thin blade of a knife.

questions.q: A 'gastronome' is best described as a person who is an expert in…?
questions.f: From Greek roots meaning 'stomach law', a gastronome studies the rules of good eating.

questions.q: Green tea leaves are less oxidized than black tea leaves.
questions.f: Both come from the same plant, but black tea is fully oxidized while green tea is not.

questions.q: The chemical name for ordinary table sugar is glucose.
questions.f: Table sugar is sucrose, which is made of one glucose and one fructose joined together.

questions.q: The smoky seasoning 'chipotle' is made by drying and smoking which chili?
questions.f: A ripe red jalapeño loses much of its water when smoked, concentrating the flavor.

questions.q: The thin pancake called a 'crepe' is a specialty of which country?
questions.f: French crepes can be filled with anything from lemon and sugar to ham and cheese.

questions.q: The juice of which fruit can be used as invisible ink that browns when heated?
questions.f: Lemon juice weakens the paper so those spots brown first when warmed.

questions.q: Which fizzy drink was first sold in pharmacies as a medicine and colored with caramel?
questions.f: Early colas were marketed as tonics to cure headaches and tiredness.

questions.q: Which fresh Italian cheese melts into stretchy strings, making it perfect for pizza?
questions.f: The best mozzarella is traditionally made from the milk of water buffalo.

questions.q: Which country produces the most wheat in the world?
questions.f: China harvests more wheat than any other nation, mostly to feed its own people.

questions.q: Which thick, dark syrup is left over from boiling down sugar cane juice?
questions.f: Molasses gives brown sugar and gingerbread their deep, rich color and flavor.

questions.q: Which fragrant herb is the main ingredient in Italian pesto sauce?
questions.f: 'Pesto' comes from a word meaning to pound, since it is crushed with a pestle.

questions.q: Before pumpkins, people in Ireland carved lanterns from which vegetable?
questions.f: Irish immigrants switched to pumpkins in America because they were bigger and easier to carve.

questions.q: In the 1700s, which fruit was so rare and costly that people rented one to show off?
questions.f: A single pineapple could cost as much as a small carriage, so hosts displayed it uneaten.

questions.q: Olive oil belongs to which class of nutrients?
questions.f: Olive oil is rich in healthy fats and is a key part of the Mediterranean diet.

questions.q: Which fast cooking method tosses food in a little very hot oil in a wok?
questions.f: The high heat of stir-frying cooks food in minutes while keeping it crisp.

questions.q: The Italian cured meat 'prosciutto' is made from which animal?
questions.f: Prosciutto is salted and air-dried for many months, sometimes over a year.

questions.q: Which pink-fleshed fish is famous for swimming upstream to lay its eggs?
questions.f: Salmon can leap up waterfalls to reach the stream where they were born.

questions.q: The spicy, deep-red sausage 'chorizo' comes mainly from which country?
questions.f: Spanish chorizo gets its color and smoky taste from a spice called paprika.

questions.q: In Europe, much of our sugar comes not from cane but from which pale root crop?
questions.f: Sugar beet farming grew in Europe when wars cut off supplies of tropical cane.

questions.q: Which fiery green Japanese paste is traditionally served with sushi?
questions.f: Its sharp burn hits the nose rather than the tongue, unlike a chili's heat.

questions.q: Which small fruit is pressed for oil and changes from green to black as it ripens?
questions.f: Both green and black olives grow on the same tree; the difference is ripeness.

questions.q: Onion, garlic, and leek all belong to the allium family, along with which herb?
questions.f: Alliums share the sulfur compounds that give them their strong smell and taste.

questions.q: The coffee-and-cream layered dessert 'tiramisu' comes from which country?
questions.f: 'Tiramisu' means 'pick me up', likely for its coffee and sugar boost.

questions.q: Which white, crumbly cheese from Greece is traditionally made from sheep's milk?
questions.f: Real feta is stored in salty brine, which keeps it fresh and firm.

questions.q: Which tiny Andean seed is cooked like a grain and is a complete protein?
questions.f: The Inca called quinoa the 'mother grain' and grew it high in the mountains.

questions.q: Fuji, Gala, and Braeburn are all popular varieties of which fruit?
questions.f: There are more than 7,500 named varieties of apple grown around the world.

questions.q: Which eight-armed sea creature is grilled or fried in many Mediterranean dishes?
questions.f: Cooks often tenderize octopus by simmering it slowly so it does not turn rubbery.

questions.q: Which citrus fruit is a cross between a tangerine and a grapefruit?
questions.f: The tangelo's loose skin makes it as easy to peel as its tangerine parent.

questions.q: Which soft, flat Indian bread is unleavened and cooked on a hot griddle?
questions.f: Chapati puffs up with steam when pressed briefly over an open flame.

questions.q: The cooling yogurt drink 'lassi' comes from which country?
questions.f: A sweet mango lassi is a favorite way to cool down after spicy food.

questions.q: Which grain is ground into the Italian dish 'polenta' and popped into popcorn?
questions.f: Polenta was a peasant food long before it appeared on fancy restaurant menus.

questions.q: Which preserved food is meat that has been salted and dried into chewy strips?
questions.f: 'Jerky' comes from the Quechua word 'ch'arki', meaning dried, salted meat.

questions.q: Which tart red berry is harvested by flooding its field so the fruit floats up?
questions.f: Cranberries have tiny air pockets inside that make them bob to the surface.

questions.q: The word 'radish' comes from the Latin word 'radix', meaning…?
questions.f: The same root gives us 'radical', which literally means going to the root of things.

questions.q: The word 'vegetable' comes from a Latin word 'vegetare' meaning to…?
questions.f: The same root gives 'vigor', the lively energy of a healthy, growing plant.

questions.q: The root 'herb' in 'herbivore' and 'herbal' means…?
questions.f: From Latin 'herba', grass or green plant.

questions.q: A person who studies food and healthy eating is a…?
questions.f: 'Nutrition' comes from a Latin word meaning to nourish or feed.

questions.q: The word 'cuisine' means a style or art of…?
questions.f: From the Latin 'coquere', to cook, the same root behind 'kitchen'.

questions.q: The word 'appetite' comes from a Latin word meaning to…?
questions.f: An appetite is literally a reaching or striving toward food.

questions.q: The word 'digest' comes from Latin words meaning to…?
questions.f: Digestion carries food apart into pieces small enough for the body to use.

questions.q: In a meal, a 'course' is…?
questions.f: A formal dinner may run from a soup course all the way to a dessert course.

questions.q: A 'banquet' is a…?
questions.f: 'Banquet' comes from an Italian word for a little bench where guests once sat.

questions.q: At a 'buffet', guests usually…?
questions.f: 'Buffet' first meant the sideboard table where the food was laid out.

questions.q: The words 'grill' and 'griddle' come from a word for a…?
questions.f: From Latin 'craticula', a small gridiron of iron bars over the fire.

questions.q: The words 'sauce' and 'salsa' both come from the Latin word for…?
questions.f: From 'sal', salt; the earliest sauces were simply salted liquids.

questions.q: A 'confection' is a food that is mainly…?
questions.f: 'Confection' comes from a Latin word meaning to put together or prepare.

questions.q: A food 'connoisseur' is a person with…?
questions.f: 'Connoisseur' comes from a French word meaning 'one who knows'.

questions.q: The words 'ripe' and 'reap' are related, both about crops being…?
questions.f: When a crop is ripe, it is ready to be reaped, or gathered in.

questions.q: The word 'harvest' originally named which season of the year?
questions.f: Only later did 'harvest' come to mean the act of gathering crops.

questions.q: The prefix 'mono-' in 'monosodium glutamate' means…?
questions.f: From Greek 'monos', single; MSG carries a single sodium atom.

questions.q: The prefix 'bi-', as hidden in 'biscuit', means…?
questions.f: A biscuit was 'bis coctus', twice cooked, to make it last on long journeys.

questions.q: A 'staple' food is one that is…?
questions.f: Rice, wheat, and corn are the staple foods for most of the world.

questions.q: The words 'grain' and 'granule' share a root meaning a small…?
questions.f: From Latin 'granum', seed, the same root as 'granary' and 'granola'.

questions.q: A 'carafe' is a container used mainly to serve…?
questions.f: 'Carafe' traveled into English through French and Italian from an Arabic word.

questions.q: The word 'spatula' comes from a Latin word for a broad…?
questions.f: The same root gives us 'spade', another broad, flat tool.

questions.q: A 'colander' is a bowl full of holes used to…?
questions.f: 'Colander' comes from a Latin word meaning to strain or filter.

questions.q: Something that is not safe to eat is described as…?
questions.f: The prefix 'in-' flips 'edible', safe to eat, into its opposite.

questions.q: The words 'crumb' and 'crumble' both describe breaking into…?
questions.f: A fruit crumble is topped with a mixture rubbed into small, buttery crumbs.

questions.q: Which strong acid in your stomach helps break down the food you swallow?
questions.f: A thick layer of mucus protects the stomach lining from its own acid.

questions.q: In which part of the body does digestion actually begin?
questions.f: Chewing and saliva start breaking food down before you even swallow.

questions.q: Which vitamin is most easily destroyed by boiling vegetables for a long time?
questions.f: Vitamin C dissolves into the cooking water, so steaming keeps more of it.

questions.q: Which juice is squeezed onto cut apples to stop them turning brown?
questions.f: Lemon's vitamin C and acid slow the enzyme that causes the browning.

questions.q: Cooking oil floats on top of water because the oil is…?
questions.f: Because oil never mixes in, cooks must whisk hard to make salad dressing hold together.

questions.q: Keeping food in the fridge helps it last longer mainly because cold…?
questions.f: Chilling does not kill microbes, it just makes them multiply far more slowly.

questions.q: The fuzzy patches that grow on old bread are a kind of…?
questions.f: Bread mould spreads invisible threads through the loaf, so a mouldy slice is best binned.

questions.q: The coffee plant was first used for drinks in which part of the world?
questions.f: Legend tells of a goatherd who noticed his goats grew lively after eating the berries.

questions.q: Which island nation was long the world's main source of true cinnamon?
questions.f: True 'Ceylon' cinnamon has thin, papery layers, unlike the harder cassia sold as cinnamon.

questions.q: The Indian state of Kerala has been famous for centuries for growing which spice?
questions.f: Traders sailed to Kerala's Malabar coast for pepper long before Europeans arrived.

questions.q: The island of Zanzibar became world-famous for growing which spice?
questions.f: Zanzibar and nearby Pemba were once nicknamed the Clove Islands.

questions.q: The vanilla orchid grew wild first in which country?
questions.f: The Totonac people of Mexico were the first to cultivate and cure vanilla pods.

questions.q: Farmers plant different crops in a field each year, a practice called…?
questions.f: Rotating crops keeps the soil healthy and stops pests from settling in.

questions.q: The herb basil belongs to the same plant family as which other herb?
questions.f: Mint-family herbs have square stems and paired leaves, a handy way to spot them.

questions.q: A queen bee is fed almost entirely on which special substance?
questions.f: Royal jelly is what turns an ordinary larva into a queen instead of a worker.

questions.q: A honeybee tells the hive where flowers are by performing a…?
questions.f: The angle of the dance shows the flowers' direction relative to the sun.

questions.q: 'Skimmed' milk is milk that has had most of its what removed?
questions.f: The cream was once literally skimmed off the top after it rose.

questions.q: Milk is 'homogenized' so that the cream will not…?
questions.f: The milk is forced through tiny holes, breaking the fat into droplets too small to float up.

questions.q: Tangy 'buttermilk' was traditionally the liquid left over after making…?
questions.f: Bakers prize its acidity, which reacts with baking soda to lift pancakes and scones.

questions.q: Thick 'clotted cream', served with scones and jam, is a speciality of which country?
questions.f: Devon and Cornwall famously argue over whether jam or cream goes on the scone first.

questions.q: Which fizzy, tangy drink is made by fermenting milk with bacteria and yeast?
questions.f: Kefir is made using clusters of microbes that look like tiny cauliflower florets.

questions.q: Raising fish and shellfish for food on purpose is called…?
questions.f: Aquaculture now supplies roughly half of all the fish that people eat.

questions.q: Why does a pressure cooker cook food faster than an ordinary pan?
questions.f: Trapped steam raises the pressure, pushing water's boiling point above 100 degrees Celsius.

questions.q: Whipped cream holds its shape because its fat traps tiny bubbles of…?
questions.f: Whip it too long and the fat clumps together, turning your cream into butter.

questions.q: Even a drop of egg yolk stops egg whites whipping well because yolk contains…?
questions.f: Fat breaks the delicate protein film that holds each air bubble together.

questions.q: Which metal is prized for pans because it conducts heat especially well?
questions.f: Professional kitchens line copper pans with steel so the food never touches the copper.

questions.q: Leaving bread dough to rest and puff up before baking is called…?
questions.f: During proving, the yeast makes gas that stretches the dough's gluten network.

questions.q: The pasta name 'penne' comes from an Italian word meaning…?
questions.f: The tubes are cut at a slant, like the nib of an old-fashioned quill pen.

questions.q: The pasta name 'rigatoni' refers to the pasta being…?
questions.f: Those ridges are there to grip more sauce with every bite.

questions.q: The pasta name 'fusilli' means little…?
questions.f: The corkscrew shape recalls the spindle used for spinning wool into thread.

questions.q: The pasta name 'fettuccine' means little…?
questions.f: From Italian 'fetta', a slice or ribbon of dough.

questions.q: The pasta name 'tagliatelle' comes from an Italian verb meaning to…?
questions.f: The sheet of dough is rolled up and sliced into long, flat ribbons.

questions.q: The tiny rice-shaped pasta called 'orzo' takes its name from the Italian word for…?
questions.f: Orzo is made of wheat, but its shape reminded Italians of barley grains.

questions.q: The pasta name 'cannelloni' means large…?
questions.f: The big tubes are stuffed with filling, then baked under sauce.

questions.q: The pasta name 'conchiglie' comes from the Italian word for…?
questions.f: Their curved, hollow shape scoops up chunky sauce beautifully.

questions.q: A French 'boulangerie' is a shop that mainly sells…?
questions.f: French law protects the title, so a true boulangerie must bake its bread on site.

questions.q: A 'sommelier' in a fine restaurant is an expert on…?
questions.f: The word once described a servant in charge of transporting a household's supplies.

questions.q: In a professional kitchen, a 'sous chef' is the…?
questions.f: 'Sous' is French for 'under', so a sous chef works directly under the head chef.

questions.q: The restaurant title 'maitre d'hotel' literally means…?
questions.f: Usually shortened to 'maitre d', this is the person who runs the dining room.

questions.q: The dessert called a 'mousse' takes its name from a French word meaning…?
questions.f: Whipped air is what gives chocolate mousse its light, foamy texture.

questions.q: To 'blanch' a vegetable, a term from a French word meaning 'to whiten', is to…?
c: Boil it briefly then chill it
questions.f: A quick dip in boiling water sets the colour and loosens skins from tomatoes and almonds.

questions.q: A 'puree' is food that has been…?
questions.f: 'Puree' comes from a French word meaning purified or refined.

questions.q: A 'compote' is a dish of fruit that has been…?
questions.f: 'Compote' comes from a French word meaning a mixture, related to 'composed'.

questions.q: To 'baste' a roasting chicken means to…?
questions.f: Basting keeps the surface moist and helps it brown evenly.

questions.q: To 'sear' meat means to…?
c: Brown it fast in a very hot pan
questions.f: Searing builds a savoury brown crust through the Maillard reaction.

questions.q: When milk 'curdles', its proteins…?
questions.f: Cheesemakers curdle milk deliberately, using acid or the enzyme rennet.

questions.q: The word 'pickle' comes from a Dutch word meaning…?
questions.f: From Dutch 'pekel', the salty liquid that preserves the vegetables.

questions.q: Growing fruit, vegetables, and flowers in gardens is called…?
questions.f: From Latin 'hortus', garden, joined to 'cultura', cultivation.

questions.q: The keeping of bees for honey is called…?
questions.f: From Latin 'apis', bee; an apiculturist is simply a beekeeper.

questions.q: The growing of grapevines is called…?
questions.f: From Latin 'vitis', vine; viticulture is the farming side of making wine.

questions.q: An animal that eats mainly fruit is called a…?
questions.f: From Latin 'frux', fruit; many bats and monkeys are frugivores.

questions.q: An animal that eats mainly insects is called an…?
questions.f: Anteaters, swallows, and many bats are insectivores.

questions.q: An animal that eats mainly fish is called a…?
questions.f: From Latin 'piscis', fish, the same root behind 'Pisces'.

questions.q: An animal that eats mainly seeds and grain is called a…?
questions.f: From Latin 'granum', grain; finches and many mice are granivores.

questions.q: The word 'famine' comes from a Latin word meaning…?
questions.f: From Latin 'fames', hunger, which also gives us the word 'famished'.

questions.q: To 'masticate' food means to…?
questions.f: From Latin 'masticare', to chew, related to the resin called mastic.

questions.q: A 'morsel' of food is a…?
questions.f: From a Latin word meaning to bite, the same root as 'remorse', which 'bites' the conscience.

questions.q: A fruit described as 'succulent' is…?
questions.f: From Latin 'sucus', juice; desert 'succulent' plants are named for storing water.

questions.q: A person who is 'satiated' after dinner feels…?
questions.f: From Latin 'satis', enough, the same root as 'satisfy' and 'insatiable'.

questions.q: To 'nourish' someone means to…?
questions.f: From Latin 'nutrire', to feed, which also gives 'nutrient' and 'nurse'.
