questions.q: An Italian opera composer as famous for his appetite as his overtures, a beef fillet crowned with pate and truffle, and 'The Barber of Seville' point to which dish?
questions.f: Rossini retired early from opera and spent years devising rich dishes with chefs.

questions.q: An Australian state governor around 1900, a sponge cube rolled in chocolate and coconut, and a national day each July point to which cake?
questions.f: It is named for Lord Lamington, once governor of Queensland.

questions.q: A physician who prescribed minced beef for digestion, a patty served without a bun, and a name that sounds like an English cathedral city point to which dish?
questions.f: Dr James Salisbury urged Americans to eat minced beef three times a day.

questions.q: A rice grain milled so hard it lost the vitamin that prevents beriberi, a Dutch doctor's chickens in Java, and polished white grains point to which discovery?
questions.f: Christiaan Eijkman's sick chickens led to the discovery of vitamin B1.

questions.q: An Austrian city on the Danube, a lattice-topped tart of nuts and jam, and a claim to be the oldest cake known by name point to which dessert?
questions.f: Recipes for the Linzer torte survive from as far back as the 1650s.

questions.q: What do baseball players wear on one hand to help them catch the ball?
questions.f: Baseball gloves are made of leather and have a deep pocket to trap the ball safely.

questions.q: In jump rope, what do you swing under your feet again and again?
questions.f: Some champion jumpers can skip a rope more than 100 times in just 30 seconds!

questions.q: What color is a basketball most of the time?
questions.f: Basketballs are orange so players and fans can see them easily as they fly around the court.

questions.q: In ice hockey, what do players use to push the puck along the ice?
questions.f: A hockey stick has a flat blade at the bottom that lets players pass, steer, and shoot the puck.

questions.q: In volleyball, players hit the ball back and forth over a tall what?
questions.f: A volleyball net stands taller than most grown-ups, so players jump high to send the ball over.

questions.q: What animal does a jockey ride in a race?
questions.f: Racehorses can gallop at over 60 kilometers per hour, faster than a car driving through town.

questions.q: In a sack race, you hop to the finish with your legs inside a what?
questions.f: Sack races have been a favorite party game for hundreds of years, often using old potato sacks.

questions.q: In archery, what do you shoot from a bow at the target?
questions.f: Arrows have feathers or plastic fins at the back to help them fly straight to the target.

questions.q: What do you use to move a canoe through the water?
questions.f: Canoe paddlers switch sides with their paddle to keep the boat gliding in a straight line.

questions.q: Which sport happens in a swimming pool?
questions.f: Swimming uses almost every muscle in your body, which is why it is such great exercise.

questions.q: In a three-legged race, how many friends run together as one team?
questions.f: Partners tie one leg together, so they must step at the same time or they topple over laughing.

questions.q: What do you stand on and roll around at a skate park?
questions.f: The first skateboards were made by kids who nailed roller-skate wheels onto wooden boards.

questions.q: In golf, what do you swing to hit the little white ball?
questions.f: Golfers carry a whole bag of clubs, choosing long ones for far shots and short ones for close shots.

questions.q: A yo-yo rolls up and down on a what?
questions.f: Yo-yo players can do amazing string tricks with names like Walk the Dog and Rock the Baby.

questions.q: Where do you spin a hula hoop to play with it?
questions.f: Some hula hoop stars can spin dozens of hoops at once, from their ankles up to their arms!

questions.q: In baseball, where does the batter run first after hitting the ball?
questions.f: A batter runs the bases in order, and touching all four bases scores a run for the team.

questions.q: What do soccer players wear under their socks to protect their legs?
questions.f: Shin guards are hard on the outside and soft inside, protecting legs from bumps and kicks.

questions.q: Which bouncy piece of equipment do gymnasts jump on to fly high in the air?
questions.f: Trampoline jumping is a real Olympic sport where athletes bounce as high as a house roof!

questions.q: Which game do you win by getting three X's or O's in a row?
questions.f: Tic-tac-toe is so old that people scratched its grids into stone in ancient Rome.

questions.q: In the card game Snap, what do you shout when two matching cards appear?
questions.f: In Snap, the fastest shouter wins the pile of cards, so sharp eyes really pay off.

questions.q: How many dots are on the side of a die that shows the biggest number?
questions.f: On most dice, the dots on opposite sides always add up to seven: six pairs with one!

questions.q: What do you roll in many board games to see how far to move?
questions.f: Dice are one of the oldest game tools ever; ancient players made them from bone and wood.

questions.q: In dodgeball, what should you do when a ball flies toward you?
questions.f: The word 'dodge' means to move quickly aside, which is exactly how you stay in the game.

questions.q: What do cheerleaders shake in their hands while they cheer?
questions.f: Fluffy pom-poms make cheer moves easy to see from the very top row of a big stadium.

questions.q: In four square, what do players bounce between the squares?
questions.f: Four square only needs chalk, a bouncy ball, and four friends, so you can play almost anywhere.

questions.q: What do you fly on a string at the park on a windy day?
questions.f: Kite flying is a big sport in some countries, with festivals where the sky fills with color.

questions.q: In a wheelbarrow race, your partner holds your what while you walk on your hands?
questions.f: The player walking on their hands is the 'wheelbarrow', and the holder steers from behind!

questions.q: What flat, round toy do you throw so it glides through the air to a friend?
questions.f: A frisbee flies far because its spinning shape works like a little wing.

questions.q: In musical statues, what must you do the moment the music stops?
questions.f: In musical statues, even a tiny wiggle can put you out, so players stand as still as stone.

questions.q: In leapfrog, what do you jump over?
questions.f: Leapfrog is named after real frogs, who can leap many times their own body length.

questions.q: Where is beach volleyball played?
questions.f: Soft sand makes running and jumping harder, so beach volleyball players get super strong legs.

questions.q: What do you wear on your hands to keep them safe in boxing practice?
questions.f: Boxing gloves are thick and padded to protect the hands of both training partners.

questions.q: In bingo, what do you shout when you finish your card?
questions.f: Shouting 'Bingo!' tells everyone you filled your line first, and the caller checks your card.

questions.q: Gymnasts land safely from their flips onto a thick, soft what?
questions.f: Landing mats are filled with squishy foam that soaks up the bump of a big jump.

questions.q: A soccer game is played on a big grassy field.
questions.f: Soccer fields are covered in real or artificial grass and are bigger than most playgrounds.

questions.q: In basketball, players kick the ball into the hoop with their feet.
questions.f: Basketball players use only their hands, bouncing and throwing the ball up into the hoop.

questions.q: A person who swims is called a...?
questions.f: Adding '-er' to an action word often names the person who does it: swim becomes swimmer!

questions.q: A person who rides a bicycle in races is called a...?
questions.f: The word 'cyclist' comes from 'cycle', which means a circle, just like a bike's round wheels.

questions.q: The person who teaches a sports team and plans its practice is the...?
questions.f: A coach watches every practice and helps each player learn new skills and get stronger.

questions.q: People who love a team and cheer for it are called its...?
questions.f: The word 'fan' is short for 'fanatic', someone who is super excited about something.

questions.q: A group of players who play together on the same side is called a...?
questions.f: Long ago, 'team' meant animals pulling together, and now it means people working together!

questions.q: When both sides finish a game with the same score, we call it a...?
questions.f: A tied game means nobody wins or loses; some sports play extra time to break a tie.

questions.q: The word 'football' is made from 'foot' and which other word?
questions.f: Words built from two smaller words, like football, are called compound words.

questions.q: Which two words are joined together to make 'skateboard'?
questions.f: English loves joining words: skateboard, snowboard, and surfboard are all word teams!

questions.q: The short word 'gym' comes from which longer word?
questions.f: We often shorten long words: gymnasium becomes gym, just like mathematics becomes math.

questions.q: A player who is on YOUR team is your...?
questions.f: 'Teammate' joins 'team' and 'mate', an old friendly word meaning companion or friend.

questions.q: The player you play AGAINST in a game is your...?
questions.f: Good players shake hands with their opponent after a game to show good manners.

questions.q: What do we call the winner of a big competition?
questions.f: 'Champ' is the short, friendly form of 'champion', a word for the very best player.

questions.q: The 'tri' at the start of 'tricycle' tells you it has how many wheels?
questions.f: 'Tri' means three in many words: tricycle, triangle, and even triceratops!

questions.q: The 'bi' at the start of 'bicycle' means...?
questions.f: 'Bi' means two, so a bicycle has two wheels and binoculars have two little telescopes.

questions.q: A unicycle has how many wheels? ('Uni' gives the clue!)
questions.f: 'Uni' means one, so circus riders on a unicycle balance on just a single wheel.

questions.q: The word 'replay' means to play a game...?
questions.f: The prefix 're-' means again, so we replay games, reread books, and retell stories.

questions.q: If a team is 'unbeaten', what has never happened to it?
questions.f: The prefix 'un-' means not, so an unbeaten team is one that has not been beaten!

questions.q: The runner at the very front of a race is in the...?
questions.f: 'Lead' rhymes with 'seed' here, and the front runner is called the leader of the race.

questions.q: The place with a hoop at each end where you play basketball is called a...?
questions.f: Basketball courts have shiny wooden floors that help the ball bounce nice and high.

questions.q: The icy place where you go skating is called a skating...?
questions.f: 'Rink' and 'ring' look almost the same, but only one letter turns a circle into an ice floor!

questions.q: The big oval path that runners race around is called a...?
questions.f: Change one letter in 'track' and you get 'truck' or 'trick', so spell it carefully!

questions.q: A baby horse, which might grow up to be a racehorse, is called a...?
questions.f: A foal can stand up and wobble around within about an hour of being born.

questions.q: What is the round prize on a ribbon that winners wear around their neck?
questions.f: Medals for first, second, and third place are usually gold, silver, and bronze.

questions.q: What is the big shiny cup given to a winning team called?
questions.f: Some famous trophies are so precious that they travel with their very own guards.

questions.q: Someone who takes part in a game is called a...?
questions.f: Every player on a team has a job to do, from scoring goals to guarding the net.

questions.q: The word 'goalkeeper' is made of 'goal' plus which word?
questions.f: A keeper is someone who guards or looks after something, like a zookeeper or a goalkeeper.

questions.q: When you run as fast as you can for a short distance, you...?
questions.f: Sprinters explode into a super-fast run, but only for a short dash, not a whole long race.

questions.q: To 'dive' into a pool means to go into the water...?
questions.f: Divers stretch their arms in front of their head to slip into the water with a tiny splash.

questions.q: Which word means to jump on just one foot?
questions.f: In hopscotch you must hop on one foot, which is where the game gets its name.

questions.q: In sports, another word for a game between two teams is a...?
questions.f: We say a tennis match or a soccer match, because the two sides are 'matched' against each other.

questions.q: The word 'snowboard' is made from the two smaller words 'snow' and 'board'.
questions.f: Snowboard is a compound word, joining 'snow' and 'board' into one new word.

questions.q: A 'winner' is the person who loses the game.
questions.f: A winner is the one who wins; the player who loses is called the loser, but can win next time!

questions.q: You need snow to go sledding down a hill.
questions.f: Sleds slide on slippery snow; on green grass, they mostly just sit still!

questions.q: A tennis ball is bigger than a basketball.
questions.f: A basketball is much bigger; a tennis ball can fit in your hand, but a basketball cannot.

questions.q: Floaties and kickboards help new swimmers stay on top of the water.
questions.f: Floaties are filled with air, and air floats on water, holding new swimmers up safely.

questions.q: What does a swimming teacher ask you to kick to splash across the pool?
questions.f: Strong, steady leg kicks push swimmers forward, like a motor at the back of a boat.

questions.q: How many bases must a baseball player touch to score a run?
questions.f: A runner touches first, second, and third base, then home plate, making four in all.

questions.q: The martial art taekwondo, famous for high kicks, began in which country?
questions.f: Taekwondo is Korea's national martial art and has been an Olympic sport since 2000.

questions.q: How many players from one ice hockey team are on the ice at once?
questions.f: Each hockey team skates five players plus a goalie, making six on the ice at a time.

questions.q: Which snowy sport features riders doing tricks in a U-shaped 'halfpipe'?
questions.f: Halfpipe snowboarders launch off the icy walls and spin high above the edge.

questions.q: In the sport of rowing, what do teammates do together in a long narrow boat?
questions.f: Rowing crews must pull their oars at exactly the same moment to make the boat fly.

questions.q: Shogi, a board game much like chess, comes from which country?
questions.f: In shogi, captured pieces can switch sides and return to the board for their captor!

questions.q: In the board game Scrabble, what do players build with their letter tiles?
questions.f: Scrabble players score points for each letter, so rare letters like Z are worth the most.

questions.q: In bowling, knocking down all ten pins using two rolls is called a...?
questions.f: A spare is marked with a slash on the scoresheet and adds bonus points from your next roll.

questions.q: How many players from one volleyball team are on the court at once?
questions.f: Volleyball players rotate positions every time their team wins back the serve.

questions.q: How many points do you usually need to win a game of table tennis?
questions.f: Table tennis games once went to 21, but the rules changed to 11 points in 2001.

questions.q: In cricket, a batter who gets out without scoring any runs is out for a...?
questions.f: 'Duck' is short for 'duck's egg', because the number zero looks just like an egg!

questions.q: Which sport is played on a field whose inner part is called a 'diamond'?
questions.f: The four bases of a baseball field form a square that looks like a sparkling diamond shape.

questions.q: How many innings are in a standard professional baseball game?
questions.f: If the score is tied after nine innings, teams keep playing extra innings until someone wins.

questions.q: In the game Jenga, what makes a player lose?
questions.f: 'Jenga' comes from a Swahili word meaning 'to build', which is exactly what players do.

questions.q: In basketball, what is a 'free throw'?
c: An unguarded shot from a special line
questions.f: Free throws are given after fouls; each successful free throw is worth one point.

questions.q: Which two suits in a deck of playing cards are red?
questions.f: Every deck has two red suits and two black suits, with thirteen cards in each suit.

questions.q: How many cards are in a standard deck of playing cards, not counting jokers?
questions.f: With 13 cards in each of 4 suits, a full deck holds 52 cards, one for each week of the year!

questions.q: Ice hockey pucks are kept frozen before big games.
questions.f: Freezing the rubber puck stops it from bouncing, so it slides smoothly along the ice.

questions.q: In a relay swimming race, all four swimmers swim at the same time.
questions.f: Relay swimmers take turns: each one swims their part after a teammate touches the wall.

questions.q: In volleyball, a team scores when the ball lands on the other team's side of the floor.
questions.f: Teams battle to keep the ball off their own floor, diving and digging to keep it in the air.

questions.q: A 'spectator' is a person who watches a game.
questions.f: 'Spectator' comes from a Latin word meaning 'to watch', which is just what fans do.

questions.q: A person who does flips, cartwheels, and balance-beam routines is called a...?
questions.f: 'Gymnast' and 'gymnasium' share the same ancient Greek root about exercising.

questions.q: A runner who races very fast over short distances is called a...?
questions.f: Sprinters run races like the 100 meters, which top athletes finish in about ten seconds.

questions.q: What is the special name for a hall where karate and judo are practiced?
questions.f: 'Dojo' is a Japanese word meaning 'place of the way', where students train with respect.

questions.q: Which word means the player chosen to lead a team on the field?
questions.f: Team captains often wear a special armband and speak to the referee for their team.

questions.q: The word 'goalie' is a short, friendly form of which longer word?
questions.f: English speakers love shortening words: goalkeeper becomes goalie, referee becomes ref.

questions.q: Which little word hides inside 'baseball', 'basketball', and 'football'?
questions.f: All three sports are named as compound words ending in the object they are played with!

questions.q: A practice soccer match played just for fun, not for a trophy, is called a...?
questions.f: Even national teams play 'friendlies' to test new players before big tournaments.

questions.q: What does 'sportsmanship' mean?
c: Playing fairly and being kind, win or lose
questions.f: Good sportsmanship means congratulating winners and encouraging players who lose.

questions.q: A brand-new player in their first season is often called a...?
questions.f: Many leagues give a 'Rookie of the Year' award to the best first-season player.

questions.q: What is the big group of people cheering from the stands called?
questions.f: A roaring home crowd is sometimes called the 'twelfth player' because cheers boost the team.

questions.q: The word 'skiing' is unusual because it has two of which letter side by side?
questions.f: 'Skiing' is one of very few common English words spelled with a double i.

questions.q: The 'over' in 'overtime' tells you the extra minutes are played...?
questions.f: The prefix 'over-' often means beyond or extra, as in overtime, overgrown, and overflow.

questions.q: What is a team 'mascot'?
c: A fun character that brings the team luck
questions.f: 'Mascot' comes from a French word for a lucky charm, and mascots dance to fire up the crowd.

questions.q: In sports awards, what do the letters MVP stand for?
questions.f: The MVP award goes to the player judged most important to their team's success.

questions.q: How many Grand Slam tennis tournaments are held around the world each year?
questions.f: The four Grand Slams are the Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon, and US Open.

questions.q: Which tennis Grand Slam is played on hard courts in New York City?
questions.f: The US Open's main stadium, Arthur Ashe Stadium, is the largest tennis arena on Earth.

questions.q: What color jersey does the overall leader of the Tour de France wear?
questions.f: The yellow jersey began in 1919, reportedly matching the yellow paper of a sponsor newspaper.

questions.q: What is the highest score a single dart can earn with one throw?
questions.f: Hitting the thin triple-20 band scores 60, even more than the 50-point bullseye!

questions.q: Which gymnastics event uses a leather-topped 'horse' with two handles on top?
questions.f: On the pommel horse, gymnasts swing their legs in circles without ever stopping.

questions.q: In which sport can a team score a 'try' by grounding the ball over a line?
questions.f: It is called a 'try' because long ago it only earned a chance to try a kick at goal.

questions.q: Which sport is played on the largest field: polo, soccer, or basketball?
questions.f: A polo field can cover the space of several soccer fields, since horses need room to gallop.

questions.q: Which swimming stroke starts in the water instead of with a dive from a block?
questions.f: Backstrokers grip the wall and push off on their backs, so a headfirst dive would not work.

questions.q: Which board game is played with 15 checkers per player and a pair of dice?
questions.f: Backgammon is about 5,000 years old, making it one of the oldest board games still played.

questions.q: How many frames make up one full game of ten-pin bowling?
questions.f: A perfect 300 game needs twelve strikes in a row, thanks to bonus rolls in the tenth frame.

questions.q: In baseball, what is a 'grand slam'?
c: A home run hit with all three bases loaded
A catch made over the fence
A game that ends in a tie
questions.f: A grand slam scores four runs at once, the most possible from a single swing.

questions.q: In soccer, when is a corner kick awarded?
c: When the defending team sends the ball over its own goal line
At the start of each half
questions.f: Corner kicks curl in from the field's corner arc and often lead to headed goals.

questions.q: In which Winter Olympic sliding sport do athletes race head-first down an icy track?
questions.f: Skeleton riders zoom face-down at over 120 km/h with their chins just above the ice.

questions.q: What does a golfer warn people about by shouting 'Fore!'?
questions.f: Shouting 'Fore!' gives people time to duck before a wayward golf ball lands nearby.

questions.q: In golf, finishing a hole one stroke over par is called a...?
questions.f: Par is the expected score for a hole, so a bogey means you took one shot too many.

questions.q: In Scrabble, which two letters are worth ten points each, the most in the game?
questions.f: Q and Z score ten points because so few English words use them, making them hard to play.

questions.q: In volleyball, what is a 'spike'?
c: A hard downward smash into the other court
A gentle tap over the net
questions.f: A well-timed spike can send the ball downward at over 100 km/h.

questions.q: What does the checkered flag mean in motor racing?
questions.f: The black-and-white checkered flag waves as the winner flashes across the finish line.

questions.q: Which sport is lovingly nicknamed 'the beautiful game'?
questions.f: The nickname is linked to Brazilian legend Pele, who titled his book 'My Life and the Beautiful Game'.

questions.q: In cricket, which fielder stands right behind the stumps wearing big gloves?
questions.f: Only the wicketkeeper may wear gloves in the field, ready to catch balls the batter misses.

questions.q: In Monopoly, what do you collect every time your token passes GO?
questions.f: Passing GO pays a salary, giving players fresh cash to buy streets and build houses.

questions.q: How many pockets does a snooker table have?
questions.f: A snooker table has a pocket in each corner plus one in the middle of each long side.

questions.q: The Stanley Cup is the championship trophy of which sport?
questions.f: Every winning player gets a day with the Stanley Cup, and it has even held ice cream!

questions.q: How many players from one handball team are on the court at once?
questions.f: Handball teams field six court players plus a goalkeeper, and games are fast and high-scoring.

questions.q: Which racket sport is played inside a four-walled court with a small rubber ball?
questions.f: The squash ball warms up during play, getting bouncier the longer a rally goes on.

questions.q: What is the sand-filled pit beside a golf green called?
questions.f: Golfers need special lofted 'sand wedge' clubs to splash the ball out of a bunker.

questions.q: Modern ice hockey's first official rules were written down in which country?
questions.f: Students in Montreal, Canada published early hockey rules in the 1870s, shaping today's game.

questions.q: In badminton, the shuttlecock may bounce once on the floor before you hit it.
questions.f: Unlike tennis, badminton allows no bounces; the shuttle must be struck while in the air.

questions.q: In cricket, a six is scored when the ball crosses the boundary without bouncing.
questions.f: If the ball bounces before crossing the boundary rope, the batter scores four instead of six.

questions.q: In chess, each player's two bishops start on different colored squares.
questions.f: Each bishop stays on its starting color forever, since bishops only move diagonally.

questions.q: Olympic gold medals are made completely of pure gold.
questions.f: Modern 'gold' medals are mostly silver with a thin gold coating; solid gold ended in 1912.

questions.q: The ancient root 'athlon' in 'athlete' and 'triathlon' means...?
questions.f: In ancient Greek, an 'athlon' was a prize, so an athlete is literally a prize-competitor.

questions.q: The 'hepta' in 'heptathlon' tells you the event includes how many contests?
questions.f: 'Hepta' means seven in Greek; heptathletes run, jump, and throw across seven events.

questions.q: The word 'gymnasium' originally named an ancient Greek place for...?
questions.f: Greek gymnasiums were training grounds where athletes also listened to teachers and thinkers.

questions.q: The 'velo' in 'velodrome', the arena for track cycling, refers to a...?
questions.f: 'Velo' is the everyday French word for bicycle, so a velodrome is a cycling track.

questions.q: A 'medal' is a prize; which same-sounding word means to interfere in others' business?
questions.f: 'Medal' and 'meddle' are homophones: they sound alike but have different spellings and meanings.

questions.q: 'Pedal' is what a cyclist pushes; its homophone 'peddle' means to...?
c: Sell goods from place to place
questions.f: Street sellers 'peddle' their wares; mixing up pedal and peddle is a classic spelling trap.

questions.q: What is the official who watches a tennis match from a tall chair called?
questions.f: The chair umpire announces the score after every single point of the match.

questions.q: The root 'aqua' in 'aquatics', the group of Olympic water sports, means...?
questions.f: From Latin, 'aqua' gives us aquatics, aquarium, and aqueduct, all about water.

questions.q: The word 'stadium' began as an ancient Greek unit measuring what?
questions.f: A 'stadion' was about 185 meters, the length of the famous footrace at Olympia.

questions.q: A 'veteran' player is one who...?
questions.f: 'Veteran' comes from a Latin word meaning old, the opposite of a rookie.

questions.q: Why is the fastest swimming race called 'freestyle'?
c: Swimmers are free to choose any stroke
questions.f: Almost everyone chooses front crawl in freestyle races because it is the fastest stroke.

questions.q: An 'annual' tournament is one that happens...?
questions.f: 'Annual' comes from the Latin word for year, which also hides in 'anniversary'.

questions.q: What is the swimming race called in which all four strokes are swum one after another?
questions.f: A 'medley' means a mixture, so the medley race mixes butterfly, backstroke, breaststroke, and freestyle.

questions.q: In fencing, what does the starting call 'en garde' tell fencers to do?
questions.f: 'En garde' means 'on guard'; fencers crouch ready before the director calls 'fence!'

questions.q: Why is a team 'uniform' called that? The 'uni' part means...?
questions.f: A uniform makes the whole team dress as one, in matching colors and crest.

questions.q: In tennis, a serve so good the opponent cannot even touch the ball is an...?
questions.f: Big servers can fire down more than 20 aces in a single professional match.

questions.q: The motor-racing title 'Grand Prix' literally means...?
questions.f: 'Grand Prix' is French; the first Grand Prix motor race was held at Le Mans in 1906.

questions.q: The 'hippo' in 'hippodrome', the ancient racing arena, means the races featured...?
questions.f: 'Hippos' is Greek for horse, so a hippopotamus is literally a 'river horse'!

questions.q: The 'bi' in 'biathlon' signals that it combines which two winter skills?
questions.f: Biathletes must slow their pounding hearts to aim steadily after skiing at full speed.

questions.q: The word 'tournament' originally described medieval contests between...?
questions.f: Medieval knights jousted in tournaments; today the word means any organized competition.

questions.q: What is the big tight bunch of riders in a cycling road race called?
questions.f: Riding inside the peloton saves energy, because the riders in front block the wind.

questions.q: In cricket, what is the rope marking the outer edge of the playing field called?
questions.f: Clearing the boundary on the full earns six runs, cricket's most exciting shot.

questions.q: A 'semifinal' is the round played...?
questions.f: 'Semi' means half, and the two semifinal winners meet in the final.

questions.q: The prefix 'inter-' in 'international match' means...?
questions.f: An international is played between nations, just as an interview happens between people.

questions.q: At sports practice, what is a 'drill'?
c: A repeated exercise to sharpen a skill
questions.f: Coaches use passing and shooting drills so that skills become automatic in real games.

questions.q: In a match listing like 'Tigers versus Sharks', the word 'versus' means...?
questions.f: 'Versus', often shortened to 'vs', is Latin, and means the two teams face each other.

questions.q: The 'aero' in 'aerobics' means the exercise gets you using lots of...?
questions.f: 'Aero' means air; aerobic exercise makes you breathe hard, feeding oxygen to your muscles.

questions.q: The root 'cardio' in 'cardio workout' refers to which part of the body?
questions.f: 'Kardia' is Greek for heart; cardio exercise makes your heart stronger with every beat.

questions.q: The ending '-athon' in words like 'readathon' and 'danceathon' signals an event that is...?
questions.f: English borrowed '-athon' from 'marathon' to build fun words for long charity events.

questions.q: In sports slang, what does the nickname GOAT stand for?
questions.f: Calling an athlete 'the GOAT' is a huge compliment, despite the funny farm animal spelling!

questions.q: The word 'referee' contains the smaller word 'refer', because disagreements are referred to that official.
questions.f: A referee is literally the person disputes are 'referred' to for a final decision.

questions.q: Basketball was invented in 1891 by a gym teacher who first had players shoot at what?
questions.f: James Naismith nailed peach baskets to a balcony; a janitor had to fetch the ball after every score.

questions.q: When volleyball was invented in 1895, its creator originally named it what?
questions.f: William Morgan called his gentle new game 'mintonette'; spectators soon renamed it for its volleys.

questions.q: The Ashes, one of cricket's fiercest rivalries, is contested between which two nations?
questions.f: The tiny Ashes urn is said to hold the burnt remains of a cricket bail from 1882.

questions.q: In rowing, what is the job of the coxswain, the one crew member without an oar?
c: Steering the boat and calling the rhythm
questions.f: The cox faces forward, steers with a small rudder, and shouts commands to the rowers.

questions.q: What is the famous maximum break score in snooker?
questions.f: A 147 needs 15 reds each followed by a black, then all six colors, without a single miss.

questions.q: The back-first high jump technique used by nearly all champions today is called the...?
questions.f: Dick Fosbury stunned the 1968 Olympics with his backwards leap and won the gold medal.

questions.q: How many players are on a rugby union team during a match?
questions.f: Rugby union fields 15 a side; its cousin rugby league plays with just 13.

questions.q: The 'snatch' and the 'clean and jerk' are the two lifts of which Olympic sport?
questions.f: In the clean and jerk, the bar pauses at the shoulders; in the snatch it flies up in one motion.

questions.q: In chess piece values, the queen is usually counted as worth how many pawns?
questions.f: Counting points, a queen at nine outweighs a rook at five and a bishop or knight at three.

questions.q: What is 'stalemate' in chess?
c: A draw when a player has no legal move but is not in check
A win by capturing every pawn
questions.f: Stalemate saves many losing players; grandmasters set clever traps to sneak this draw.

questions.q: The Ryder Cup is a famous team competition between Europe and the USA in which sport?
questions.f: The Ryder Cup began in 1927 and swaps between American and European courses every two years.

questions.q: The longest tennis match ever, at Wimbledon in 2010, lasted about how long?
questions.f: John Isner finally beat Nicolas Mahut 70-68 in the last set; a plaque at Wimbledon marks the feat.

questions.q: What makes a table tennis serve different from a tennis serve?
c: The ball must bounce on the server's own side first
questions.f: A legal table tennis serve bounces once on each side of the table, starting with the server's.

questions.q: In volleyball, the 'libero' wears a different colored jersey and specializes in what?
questions.f: The libero, from an Italian word for 'free', may swap in and out without normal substitutions.

questions.q: Which rule makes water polo especially exhausting?
c: Players may not touch the bottom of the pool
questions.f: Water polo players tread water for the whole game using a whirling 'eggbeater' kick.

questions.q: What is the object of the ancient board game Go?
c: Surround more territory than your opponent
questions.f: Go has simple rules but more possible positions than there are atoms in the known universe.

questions.q: Despite its name, the game Chinese checkers was actually invented where?
questions.f: Chinese checkers appeared in Germany in the 1890s; the exotic name was pure marketing.

questions.q: What is the highest score possible with three darts in one visit?
questions.f: Three triple-20s make 180, and darts crowds famously roar 'one hundred and eighty!'

questions.q: About how quickly can a Formula 1 pit crew change all four tires?
questions.f: Around 20 crew members swarm the car at once; the record pit stop is well under two seconds.

questions.q: What do the colored dots printed on squash balls indicate?
questions.f: A double-yellow dot marks the least bouncy ball, used by professionals for longer rallies.

questions.q: In biathlon, what happens to skiers who miss a shooting target?
c: They ski an extra penalty loop
questions.f: Each miss usually costs a 150-meter penalty loop, so calm shooting beats pure skiing speed.

questions.q: How long does a top-division sumo tournament, or basho, last?
questions.f: Top sumo wrestlers fight once daily for 15 days; the best record lifts the Emperor's Cup.

questions.q: In cricket, the Duckworth-Lewis method recalculates a team's target after what?
c: A tie in the first innings
questions.f: Two statisticians invented the formula so rain-shortened matches could still end fairly.

questions.q: What makes a baseball knuckleball so hard to hit?
c: It barely spins, so it flutters unpredictably
It spins faster than any other pitch
It is heavier than a normal ball
questions.f: With almost no spin, air currents push the knuckleball randomly; even catchers struggle to hold it.

questions.q: Why are tennis balls covered in fuzzy felt?
c: The fuzz slows the ball and helps rackets grip it for spin
To make them float in water
questions.f: The felt's drag keeps rallies playable, and its grip lets players brush the ball for heavy topspin.

questions.q: In cricket, what is a 'googly'?
c: A ball that spins the opposite way from what the batter expects
A six hit behind the batter
questions.f: The googly was popularized around 1900 by Bernard Bosanquet, and batters still fall for it.

questions.q: In rugby, what is the 'scrum'?
c: A pushing contest where both packs bind together over the ball
questions.f: Eight forwards from each side lock shoulders in the scrum, shoving like two colliding walls.

questions.q: In baseball, what is the 'bullpen'?
c: The area where relief pitchers warm up
questions.f: Relief pitchers loosen their arms in the bullpen, ready to enter the game at any moment.

questions.q: A chess 'gambit' offers a pawn to gain an advantage; the word originally described what?
questions.f: 'Gambit' traces to Italian 'gambetto', a wrestling leg-trip, via 'gamba' meaning leg.

questions.q: In fencing, what does a fencer admit by saying 'touche'?
c: That the bout is a draw
questions.f: 'Touche' means 'touched'; outside fencing we say it when someone makes a clever point against us.

questions.q: In cricket, what is a 'maiden over'?
c: An over in which the batters score no runs
The last over of the day
questions.f: Bowling six balls without conceding a run takes great accuracy, and scorers mark it with an M.

questions.q: In bowling, what is the special name for three strikes in a row?
questions.f: Early tournaments awarded a real turkey as a prize for three straight strikes, and the name stuck.

questions.q: In swimming, what does the abbreviation 'IM' stand for?
questions.f: In the IM, one swimmer races all four strokes in order: butterfly, back, breast, then freestyle.

questions.q: In soccer, slipping the ball between an opponent's legs is cheekily called a...?
questions.f: A nutmegged defender is left frozen as the ball rolls right between their feet.

questions.q: A team captain is often nicknamed the 'skipper'; the word originally meant the master of a...?
questions.f: 'Skipper' sailed into English from Dutch 'schipper', the person who commands a ship.

questions.q: Before it meant a trainer of athletes, the word 'coach' named what?
questions.f: Coaches were carriages from Kocs, Hungary; tutors were joked to 'carry' students to success.

questions.q: The name of the board game 'Ludo' literally means what?
questions.f: 'Ludo' is Latin for 'I play', and the same root gives us the word 'ludicrous'.

questions.q: The 'shuttle' in 'shuttlecock' compares its flight to which tool's back-and-forth motion?
questions.f: A weaving shuttle zips to and fro across a loom, just as a shuttlecock crosses the net.

questions.q: The word 'score' originally meant a notch cut into what?
questions.f: From Old Norse 'skor', keepers of accounts notched sticks to count; now we 'keep score' in games.

questions.q: A billiards 'cue' takes its name from a word meaning what?
questions.f: French 'queue' means tail; players once struck the ball with the thin tail end of a mace.

questions.q: The ancient Greek throwing implement 'diskos' gave English which everyday word?
questions.f: The discus throw is so ancient it starred in the original Olympic pentathlon of 708 BC.

questions.q: The marathon's odd distance of 26.2 miles was fixed in 1908 partly so the race could finish in front of the British royal box.
questions.f: The 1908 London course was stretched to end by the royal viewing box, and the distance later became official.

questions.q: A regulation soccer goal is exactly twice as wide as it is tall.
questions.f: A goal is 7.32 m wide and 2.44 m tall, making it three times as wide as it is high.

questions.q: In badminton, serves must be struck from below the waist in an underarm action.
questions.f: Unlike tennis, badminton bans overhead serves, so rallies begin with a low, rising shuttle.

questions.q: The Winter and Summer Olympics were once held in the same year.
questions.f: Both Games shared the same year until 1992; the Winter Games then shifted to 1994 to alternate.

questions.q: The name 'ping-pong' imitates the sound of the ball hitting paddle and table.
questions.f: 'Ping-pong' is onomatopoeia, a word built from a sound, and was once a trademarked name.

questions.q: The word 'soccer' began as playful slang clipped from which longer term?
questions.f: Victorian students shortened 'association football' to 'assoc', then 'soccer', just as rugby became 'rugger'.

questions.q: The sport of rugby is named after what kind of place?
questions.f: Legend says a pupil at Rugby School picked up the ball and ran with it during a football game in 1823.

questions.q: The sport of badminton takes its name from what?
questions.f: The game was popularized at Badminton House, though British officers first knew it in India as 'poona'.

questions.q: The word 'marathon' comes from the name of what?
questions.f: Legend tells of a messenger racing about 40 km from the town of Marathon to Athens with news of victory.

questions.q: The name 'lacrosse' refers to which piece of the game's equipment?
questions.f: French settlers thought the netted stick resembled 'la crosse', a bishop's hooked staff.

questions.q: The 'volley' in 'volleyball' means the ball is struck when?
c: While it is still in the air
questions.f: A 'volley' is a shot before the bounce; in volleyball the ball must never touch the floor at all.

questions.q: The ending '-drome' in 'velodrome' and 'hippodrome' means a place for what?
questions.f: Greek 'dromos' means a running course, which is why an airfield is called an aerodrome.

questions.q: An 'amateur' athlete is literally one who plays for the what of the game?
questions.f: 'Amateur' grew from Latin 'amare', to love, describing those who compete purely for joy.

questions.q: 'Umpire' was once 'a noumpere'; the word originally described a person who was what?
c: Without an equal, a neutral third party
questions.f: English speakers mis-split 'a noumpere' as 'an oumpere', and the n hopped words forever.

questions.q: The word 'kayak' originally described a boat built for what purpose?
questions.f: The word comes from Inuit 'qajaq'; hunters sealed themselves in so the craft could roll and right itself.

questions.q: The word 'ski' originally meant a what?
questions.f: Old Norse 'skith' meant a split stick of wood, and Norwegians turned planks into transport.

questions.q: The martial art name 'taekwondo' translates roughly as the way of the what?
questions.f: 'Tae' means to kick, 'kwon' means fist, and 'do' means the way, in Korean.

questions.q: Olympic 'equestrian' events feature which animal, as the root 'equus' tells us?
questions.f: Equestrian sport is the only Olympic event where animals compete alongside humans.

questions.q: 'Dressage', the elegant horse-training discipline, literally means what?
questions.f: From French 'dresser', to train, dressage horses learn moves as precise as ballet steps.

questions.q: In boxing and baseball, a 'southpaw' is a player who is what?
questions.f: One story says old ballparks faced east, so a lefty pitcher's throwing arm pointed south.

questions.q: The word 'scuba' in scuba diving is actually what?
c: An acronym for the diver's breathing gear
questions.f: SCUBA stands for Self-Contained Underwater Breathing Apparatus.

questions.q: In cycling, the letters BMX stand for what?
questions.f: The X stands for 'cross'; BMX riders race dirt tracks and pull tricks on 20-inch-wheel bikes.

questions.q: The frisbee got its name from a company that originally made what?
questions.f: Students tossed empty tins from the Frisbie Pie Company, shouting 'Frisbie!' as they threw.

questions.q: The gymnast's 'leotard' is named after a 19th-century performer famous for what act?
questions.f: French trapeze star Jules Leotard invented the snug garment so nothing would snag mid-flight.

questions.q: The skateboarding jump called the 'ollie' is named after what?
questions.f: Alan 'Ollie' Gelfand invented the no-hands aerial in the late 1970s, and every skater learns it first.

questions.q: The figure-skating jump called the 'axel' is named after what?
questions.f: Axel Paulsen first landed the forward-launching jump in 1882; it is still the trickiest takeoff.

questions.q: A local sports rivalry is called a 'derby' after an English earl who founded what?
questions.f: The Earl of Derby's 1780 horse race became so famous that 'derby' now means any big local clash.

questions.q: The 'steeplechase' got its name because early races were run between what landmarks?
questions.f: Irish riders in 1752 raced from one church steeple to the next, jumping every hedge between.

questions.q: The chess piece name 'pawn' comes from a word meaning what?
questions.f: Medieval Latin 'pedo' meant foot soldier, from 'pes', foot, the same root as 'pedal' and 'pedestrian'.

questions.q: Tennis's strange word 'love' for zero may come from 'l'oeuf', a word meaning what?
questions.f: A zero looks like an egg; cricket's 'duck' for zero hatched from exactly the same joke.

questions.q: The word 'rival' originally described people who shared and argued over the same what?
questions.f: Latin 'rivalis' meant neighbors using one stream, always squabbling over the water.

questions.q: In cricket, what does the dismissal abbreviated LBW stand for?
questions.f: A batter is out LBW if their leg blocks a ball that would otherwise have hit the stumps.

questions.q: In fencing, what is a 'parry'?
c: A defensive move that blocks the opponent's blade
questions.f: A parry deflects the attack, and the lightning reply that follows is called the riposte.

questions.q: In gymnastics, what does 'sticking the landing' mean?
c: Landing firmly without moving your feet
questions.f: A stuck landing, feet frozen like glue, saves precious tenths from the judges' deductions.

questions.q: The word 'sport' is a shortening of 'disport', which meant to amuse oneself.
questions.f: 'Disport' came from Old French, literally 'carry away' from work, into fun and games.

questions.q: 'Soccer' and 'rugger' both began as playful British school slang.
questions.f: Adding '-er' to shortened words was a Victorian student fad, giving soccer, rugger, and even 'brekker' for breakfast.

questions.q: The Davis Cup is a men's national-team championship in which sport?
questions.f: Begun in 1900 as a USA-Britain challenge, the Davis Cup now draws well over 100 nations.

questions.q: Which is the longest race in which runners must stay in their own lane the whole way?
questions.f: The 400 m is one full lap run entirely in lanes; 800 m runners may break inward after the first bend.

questions.q: In Australian Rules football, kicking the ball between the two tall middle posts scores how many points?
questions.f: A 'goal' through the middle posts earns six points; hitting a post or the outer gap earns one 'behind'.

questions.q: In netball, what may a player holding the ball NOT do?
questions.f: Netballers must stop once they catch the ball, pivoting on one foot before passing within three seconds.

questions.q: How many points does a try score in rugby union?
questions.f: A try is worth five points, and the conversion kick that follows can add two more.

questions.q: About how wide is the gymnastics balance beam that athletes flip along?
questions.f: Elite gymnasts somersault on a padded beam only about as wide as this card is tall.

questions.q: What is the standard length of an Olympic rowing course?
questions.f: All Olympic crews race a straight 2,000-meter course, taking around six lung-burning minutes.

questions.q: In tennis, when do players switch ends of the court?
questions.f: Changing ends after odd games shares out any advantage from sun, wind, or shadows.

questions.q: The races called 'giant slalom' and 'super-G' belong to which sport?
questions.f: Super-G blends downhill speed with slalom turns; racers top 100 km/h between the gates.

questions.q: What does pressing the button on a chess clock do?
c: Stops your timer and starts your opponent's
questions.f: In 'blitz' chess each player gets just five minutes or less for every move of the game.

questions.q: In American football, what is an 'interception'?
c: Catching a pass meant for the other team
questions.f: An interception flips the game in a second: the defense instantly becomes the attack.

questions.q: Why do gymnasts dust their hands with white chalk before the bars?
c: To dry sweat and improve grip
questions.f: The 'chalk' is magnesium carbonate, which soaks up sweat so hands do not slip mid-swing.

questions.q: In judo, what is the name of the perfect throw that wins a match instantly?
questions.f: An ippon, the flawless full-point throw, ends the bout at once, like a knockout in chess terms.

questions.q: In baseball, how many balls must a pitcher throw outside the strike zone to give the batter a free walk?
questions.f: Four balls send the batter strolling to first base; three strikes and they are out.

questions.q: An ice hockey game is divided into how many periods?
questions.f: Hockey's three 20-minute periods give the ice crew two breaks to resurface the rink.

questions.q: In a game of catch, what do you toss back and forth with a friend?
questions.f: Playing catch helps you practice throwing and catching, two skills used in lots of sports.

questions.q: What do you sit on when you ride a horse?
questions.f: A saddle has stirrups for your feet so riders can sit safely while the horse trots.

questions.q: What do table tennis players stand around to play their game?
questions.f: A table tennis table has a little net across the middle, like a tiny tennis court.

questions.q: What do you sit on to slide down a snowy hill?
questions.f: Some sleds have runners like skates, and others are smooth all over like a big spoon.

questions.q: Which part of the body do soccer players use to 'head' the ball?
questions.f: Tall players often jump and head the ball into the goal from corner kicks.

questions.q: In tee-ball, where does the ball sit waiting to be hit?
questions.f: Tee-ball lets young players hit from a standing tee before they try hitting thrown balls.

questions.q: What color are tennis balls usually?
questions.f: Fuzzy yellow balls were chosen because they are easiest to see on television and courts.

questions.q: How many people play one game of chess against each other?
questions.f: Chess is a two-player game, but big halls can hold hundreds of games at once.

questions.q: In the game of jacks, what do you bounce while you scoop up the pieces?
questions.f: You must grab the jacks and catch the ball before it bounces twice, so be speedy!

questions.q: In duck-duck-goose, what do you do when someone calls you the goose?
questions.f: The goose races around the circle trying to tag the picker before they steal the empty seat.

questions.q: Where do you jump when you do a big splashy cannonball?
questions.f: Hugging your knees in the air makes a cannonball splash bigger than a straight dive.

questions.q: In Simon Says, when should you follow the order?
c: Only when it starts with 'Simon says'
Only when you feel like it
questions.f: Sneaky leaders skip the magic words to trick players into moving and being out!

questions.q: How many teams play against each other in one soccer match?
questions.f: Two teams share one ball, and each tries to score in the other team's goal.

questions.q: What are the shoes with four wheels on the bottom called?
questions.f: 'Roller skates' tells you just what they do: skates that roll along on little wheels.

questions.q: In a card game, the cards you hold are called your...?
questions.f: Funny but true: in cards, your 'hand' means the cards, not the fingers holding them!

questions.q: What is the person who shouts 'Ready, set, go!' at a race called?
questions.f: The starter begins the race, sometimes with a flag, a whistle, or a starting pistol sound.

questions.q: The rope-marked path each swimmer must stay inside is called a...?
questions.f: Pool lanes have floating rope markers so racing swimmers never bump into each other.

questions.q: Which word means to throw the ball toward the batter?
questions.f: 'Pitch' has other meanings too; in music, it means how high or low a sound is!

questions.q: A goal, a basket, and a home run are all ways for a team to...?
questions.f: Different sports use different names, but scoring points is how teams win games.

questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'ball' and means to trip and tumble down?
questions.f: Rhyming words like ball, fall, tall, and wall all end with the same '-all' sound.

questions.q: Which word means the same as 'quick', something every racer wants to be?
questions.f: Words that mean the same thing, like fast and quick, are called synonyms.

questions.q: What does a scoreboard show everyone at a game?
questions.f: 'Scoreboard' is a compound word: a board that shows the score, simple as that!

questions.q: Soccer shoes with little bumps underneath to grip the grass are called...?
questions.f: The bumps, called studs, dig into the grass so players can turn without slipping.

questions.q: In volleyball, you hit the ball with your hands and arms.
questions.f: Players bump the ball with their forearms and push or smash it with their hands.

questions.q: A golf ball is bigger than a soccer ball.
questions.f: A golf ball fits in your pocket, but a soccer ball needs both arms for a good hug!

questions.q: In chess, the pawn moves straight ahead but captures how?
questions.f: Pawns are the only chess pieces that capture differently from the way they normally move.

questions.q: In kickball, after booting the ball, where do you run?
questions.f: Kickball follows baseball's rules, but you kick a big rubber ball instead of batting.

questions.q: Which sport's players wear helmets and shoulder pads and throw a brown oval ball?
questions.f: American football players wear about 5 kilograms of padding to play safely.

questions.q: Which fast-growing sport uses paddles and a plastic ball with holes in it?
questions.f: Pickleball mixes tennis, badminton, and table tennis, and the holey ball keeps it slow enough for all ages.

questions.q: A soccer match is split into how many halves?
questions.f: Between the two halves, players rest at halftime and teams swap ends of the field.

questions.q: In baseball, what is the player who throws the ball to the batter called?
questions.f: Top pitchers can hurl a baseball at over 150 kilometers per hour.

questions.q: In gym class, what do groups lift and lower to make a giant colorful mushroom?
questions.f: Parachute games teach teamwork, because the mushroom only forms if everyone lifts together.

questions.q: How many finger holes does a bowling ball usually have?
questions.f: Bowlers grip with two fingers and a thumb, and holes are drilled to fit each player's hand.

questions.q: In freeze tag, how does a frozen player get back into the game?
questions.f: Freeze tag rewards brave teammates who dash in to unfreeze their frozen friends.

questions.q: In soccer, what happens when the ball rolls all the way over the side line?
c: The other team gets a throw-in
questions.f: The throw-in is the only time outfield soccer players may use their hands on the ball.

questions.q: In PE, walking on your hands and feet with your belly facing up is called the...?
questions.f: Lots of PE moves borrow animal names: crab walks, bear crawls, and frog jumps!

questions.q: In the game Reversi, also called Othello, what happens to discs you trap?
questions.f: One clever move in Reversi can flip a whole line of discs from black to white.

questions.q: Which sport has special positions called 'setter' and 'blocker'?
questions.f: The setter is like the team's playmaker, lifting the ball perfectly for a teammate to smash.

questions.q: In Uno, what must you shout when you have only one card left?
questions.f: 'Uno' means 'one' in Spanish, and forgetting to shout it can cost you two extra cards!

questions.q: Which puzzle challenges you to find words hidden in a grid of letters?
questions.f: Word searches hide words forwards, backwards, and diagonally, so scan every direction.

questions.q: In baseball, a home run lets the batter run all the way around the bases.
questions.f: Most home runs fly right over the outfield fence, giving the batter a free trip home.

questions.q: A standard skateboard rolls on four wheels.
questions.f: Two pairs of wheels sit under metal parts called trucks, which let the board turn as you lean.

questions.q: Bowling pins are set up in a triangle shape.
questions.f: The ten pins form a neat triangle: one pin in front, then rows of two, three, and four.

questions.q: In most card games, the jack is worth more than the king.
questions.f: Card royalty usually ranks jack, then queen, then king, with the ace often highest of all.

questions.q: A person who plays golf is called a...?
questions.f: Adding '-er' builds many sports words: golfer, bowler, boxer, and swimmer.

questions.q: A person who competes in boxing is called a...?
questions.f: 'Boxer' is also a dog breed, named because the dogs seem to spar with their front paws!

questions.q: Someone who skates is a skater, so someone who surfs is a...?
questions.f: English often turns actions into people with '-er': surf, surfer; ride, rider.

questions.q: What is 'halftime' at a sports game?
c: The rest break in the middle
questions.f: Halftime lets players drink water and rest while coaches share new plans.

questions.q: The rows of seats where fans watch a game are called the...?
questions.f: They are called stands because long ago most fans really did stand to watch!

questions.q: A 'league' is a group of what?
questions.f: League teams play a schedule of matches, and a points table decides the champion.

questions.q: Defense protects your goal; what does the offense try to do?
questions.f: 'Offense' and 'defense' are opposites: one attacks to score, the other guards the goal.

questions.q: What is a 'personal best'?
c: The first score of a season
questions.f: Athletes chase their personal best, or PB, competing against themselves to improve.

questions.q: Which word sounds exactly like 'won', as in winning a game?
questions.f: 'Won' and 'one' are homophones: they sound the same but are spelled differently.

questions.q: Which number word sounds exactly like 'ate' and might be on a jersey?
questions.f: Homophones like eight and ate trip up spellers, so listen and look carefully!

questions.q: Which spelling names the thing you ride at a skate park: board or bored?
questions.f: You ride a board, but you feel bored; same sound, totally different meanings.

questions.q: A 'cheerleader' is someone who...?
questions.f: Cheerleading is a sport of its own, full of jumps, lifts, and human pyramids.

questions.q: What is a 'rematch'?
c: A match played in the rain
The last game of the year
questions.f: The prefix 're-' means again, so a rematch gives the loser a fresh chance.

questions.q: Why do athletes do a 'warm-up' before playing?
c: Gentle moves get their body ready
questions.f: Warming up literally raises your muscles' temperature, helping prevent injuries.

questions.q: The 'kickoff' is the moment a soccer or football game...?
questions.f: 'Kickoff' is now used for any beginning; even meetings can 'kick off'!

questions.q: In sports, a 'penalty' is...?
c: A punishment for breaking a rule
questions.f: Penalties can mean free kicks, sin-bins, or lost points, depending on the sport.

questions.q: How many fielders, counting the pitcher and catcher, defend in baseball?
questions.f: Nine defenders cover the diamond and outfield, one for each batting spot in the lineup.

questions.q: Which two kinds of chess pieces could possibly make a game's very first move?
questions.f: Only knights can leap over the front row, so every game opens with a pawn or knight move.

questions.q: In tennis, what happens if a serve clips the net cord but still lands in the box?
c: It is a 'let' and is replayed
questions.f: A net-cord serve that lands in is called a let, and the server simply serves again.

questions.q: What does a waving yellow flag warn drivers about in motor racing?
questions.f: Under yellow flags drivers must not overtake, keeping everyone safe near a crash site.

questions.q: In Battleship, how do you call your shots at the hidden fleet?
c: Grid letters and numbers, like B-5
questions.f: Battleship uses coordinates just like maps do: a letter for the row, a number for the column.

questions.q: In checkers, what happens when your piece reaches the far side of the board?
questions.f: A crowned checker gets a second disc stacked on top and can then move backwards too.

questions.q: The London ground called Lord's is nicknamed the home of which sport?
questions.f: Lord's is named after its founder Thomas Lord, and its famous slope makes the ball wobble.

questions.q: During baseball's 'seventh-inning stretch', what do fans traditionally do?
questions.f: Crowds sing 'Take Me Out to the Ball Game' during the stretch, a tradition over a century old.

questions.q: Which of these balls is the biggest?
questions.f: A basketball is about 24 cm across, edging out soccer balls and volleyballs.

questions.q: In a relay race, where must the baton be handed over?
questions.f: If the baton changes hands outside the exchange zone, the whole team is disqualified.

questions.q: Which gymnastics event uses a springboard and a padded table to soar over?
questions.f: Vaulters sprint, punch the springboard, and can flip twice before landing.

questions.q: In baseball, how many outs does a 'double play' earn at once?
questions.f: A slick double play can end an inning in seconds, often flowing shortstop to second to first.

questions.q: In table tennis, players swap the serve after how many points?
questions.f: Serves alternate in pairs, except at 10-10, when they switch every single point.

questions.q: What does 'sudden death' overtime mean?
c: The first team to score wins instantly
The game ends in a tie
questions.f: Sudden-death endings create huge drama, because one goal or point finishes everything.

questions.q: In basketball, grabbing the ball after a missed shot is called a...?
questions.f: 'Rebound' literally means to bounce back, which is just what the ball does off the rim.

questions.q: When is a penalty shootout used in soccer?
c: To decide a tied knockout match
questions.f: Shootouts only happen when a winner must be found, after regular and extra time end level.

questions.q: What does the assistant referee's raised flag most famously signal in soccer?
questions.f: The offside rule stops attackers from camping by the goal, keeping play fair and flowing.

questions.q: In cricket, what are the painted white lines near the stumps called?
questions.f: A batter safely 'in their crease' cannot be stumped or run out.

questions.q: In American football, how many downs does a team get to gain ten yards?
questions.f: Gain ten yards within four downs and you earn a 'first down', a fresh set of four tries.

questions.q: Which three movements, in order, make up the triple jump?
questions.f: The triple jump was once called the hop, step, and jump, describing exactly what athletes do.

questions.q: In snooker and pool, which ball do you strike with the cue?
questions.f: Players never hit the colored balls directly; every shot begins with the white cue ball.

questions.q: Where does a baseball batter stand while waiting for the pitch?
questions.f: Chalk lines mark the batter's box on each side of home plate, one for lefties and one for righties.

questions.q: Where does a badly aimed ten-pin bowling ball end up?
questions.f: The gutters run along both edges of the lane, and gutter balls score exactly zero.

questions.q: Starting a motor race from the very first grid spot is called...?
questions.f: 'Pole position' comes from horse racing, where the inside post, or pole, was the best start.

questions.q: What are the extra side strips of a tennis court, used only in doubles, called?
questions.f: Also called tramlines, the alleys make the court wider when four players share it.

questions.q: In which direction do baseball players run around the bases?
questions.f: Runners always turn left, heading from home to first base and onwards counterclockwise.

questions.q: In table tennis, you must win a game by at least two clear points.
questions.f: At 10-10, play continues past 11 until one player leads by two, sometimes to huge scores.

questions.q: In chess, the two kings can never stand on touching squares.
questions.f: A king may not step into check, so the two kings always keep at least one square between them.

questions.q: An Olympic trampoline routine is judged partly on how high the gymnast bounces.
questions.f: Sensors measure 'time of flight'; longer airtime means bigger bounces and better scores.

questions.q: A javelin thrower spins in a full circle before releasing the javelin.
questions.f: Javelin throwers sprint straight down a runway; it is discus and hammer throwers who spin.

questions.q: An 'archer' is a person who does what?
questions.f: The word comes from a Latin root 'arcus', meaning bow, which also gives us 'arch'.

questions.q: The 'mono' in 'monoski' tells you the skier rides on how many skis?
questions.f: 'Mono' means one, appearing in monorail, monologue, and monocle too.

questions.q: 'Postseason' games are played when?
c: In the middle of the season
questions.f: The prefix 'post-' means after, so the postseason brings playoffs and finals.

questions.q: The 'pre' in 'pregame warm-up' means the warm-up happens...?
questions.f: 'Pre-' means before, as in preview, prepare, and prehistoric.

questions.q: How many teams are still in a tournament at the quarterfinal stage?
questions.f: Quarterfinals cut eight teams to four, semifinals cut four to two, and the final crowns one.

questions.q: Athletes drink to stay 'hydrated'; the root 'hydr' means...?
questions.f: From Greek 'hydor', water, we also get hydrant, hydroelectric, and hydrogen.

questions.q: The word 'opponent' is built from Latin parts meaning to place...?
questions.f: 'Ob' (against) plus 'ponere' (to place) gives opponent: one placed against you.

questions.q: A 'novice' at a sport is...?
questions.f: 'Novice' shares its root with 'new' and 'novel'; a novice is new to the game.

questions.q: 'Agility' is the ability to...?
questions.f: Agility ladders and cone drills train athletes to cut, dodge, and dart.

questions.q: 'Endurance' is the power to...?
c: Keep going for a long time
questions.f: Marathoners are endurance athletes; the word shares a root with 'durable', lasting.

questions.q: If a team 'forfeits' a match, what happens?
c: They give up the match and lose it
questions.f: Teams can forfeit by not showing up or breaking rules, handing victory to the opponent.

questions.q: A 'disqualified' athlete has been...?
c: Removed from the event for breaking a rule
questions.f: The prefix 'dis-' flips the meaning: qualified to compete, disqualified to sit out.

questions.q: Which spelling names the place where golf is played: course or coarse?
questions.f: A 'course' is a path or ground; 'coarse' means rough, a classic homophone trap.

questions.q: Which spelling names a swimming or track competition: meet or meat?
questions.f: Athletes 'meet' to compete at a meet; 'meat' is food and 'mete' means to hand out.

questions.q: Which spelling names the bottom of a running shoe: sole or soul?
questions.f: The sole is underfoot; homophones sole and soul sound identical but never swap jobs.

questions.q: The word 'exercise' comes from a Latin root meaning to...?
questions.f: Latin 'exercere' meant to keep at work or drill, exactly what practice does.

questions.q: In sports, a 'tactic' is...?
c: A clever plan to gain an advantage
questions.f: Coaches draw tactics on whiteboards, from corner-kick plays to full-court presses.

questions.q: The 'grand' in 'grandstand' tells you the seating is...?
questions.f: 'Grand' means great or large; a grandstand is the biggest, best bank of seats.

questions.q: A 'nimble' player is...?
c: Quick and light on their feet
questions.f: 'Nimble' comes from an Old English word meaning quick to grasp, in body or mind.

questions.q: The word 'course', as in racecourse, comes from a Latin root meaning to...?
questions.f: Latin 'currere', to run, also gives us current, courier, and corridor.

questions.q: A substitute who spends most of the game sitting is jokingly called a...?
questions.f: Benchwarmers 'keep the bench warm', but many leap up to become surprise heroes.

questions.q: The last runner in a relay team is called the...?
questions.f: Like a ship's anchor at the end of its chain, the anchor leg runner finishes the job.

questions.q: A 'shutout' is a game in which one team...?
c: Allows the opponent no score at all
questions.f: Goalies love shutouts; in soccer the same feat is called keeping a clean sheet.

questions.q: A 'triathlete' competes in three different sports in a single race.
questions.f: 'Tri' means three: triathletes swim, cycle, and run without stopping between.

questions.q: 'Stadium' ends in '-ium' just like 'aquarium' and 'gymnasium'.
questions.f: Latin gave English many '-ium' place words; their plurals can even be stadia and aquaria.

questions.q: In the medley relay, which stroke is always swum first, and why?
c: Backstroke, since it starts in the water
questions.f: Backstrokers start gripping the wall, so putting them first avoids colliding with an incoming teammate.

questions.q: How many tiles are in a standard double-six set of dominoes?
questions.f: Every pairing from 0-0 up to 6-6 appears once, which works out to exactly 28 tiles.

questions.q: A standard game of darts counts down from which starting score?
questions.f: Players race from 501 to exactly zero and must finish on a double or the bullseye.

questions.q: Which bowling leave is nicknamed 'goalposts' and feared as nearly impossible?
questions.f: The 7-10 split strands one pin in each back corner; even pros convert it less than 1% of the time.

questions.q: In match play golf, how is the winner decided?
c: By holes won, not total strokes
questions.f: Match play is hole-by-hole combat, so a disaster on one hole costs only that hole.

questions.q: What does basketball's 24-second shot clock force the attacking team to do?
c: Attempt a shot before it expires
questions.f: The shot clock was invented in 1954 after stalling teams produced a famous 19-18 NBA game.

questions.q: About how high is the top of a men's volleyball net?
questions.f: At 2.43 m the net stands taller than nearly every player, so spikers rely on huge vertical leaps.

questions.q: In cricket, a bowler is called for a 'no-ball' for doing what?
questions.f: A no-ball costs a run and, in limited-overs cricket, gifts the batter a 'free hit'.

questions.q: What is soccer's 'offside trap'?
c: Defenders stepping up together to strand attackers offside
Kicking the ball out on purpose
questions.f: One mistimed step ruins the trap, so elite defenses drill the move endlessly.

questions.q: Which player calls the plays and throws most passes in American football?
questions.f: The quarterback barks coded signals at the line and may change the play with an 'audible'.

questions.q: Flyweight, featherweight, and welterweight are competition classes in which sport?
questions.f: Weight classes keep bouts fair; 'featherweight' really does suggest fighters light as feathers.

questions.q: In rowing slang, what has happened to a rower who 'catches a crab'?
c: Their oar jams in the water, jolting the boat
questions.f: A badly caught crab can stop a racing shell dead and has even catapulted rowers overboard.

questions.q: A basketball 'triple-double' means reaching double figures in how many statistics?
questions.f: Ten or more points, rebounds, and assists is the classic triple-double combination.

questions.q: In baseball, a batter 'hits for the cycle' by collecting what in one game?
c: A single, double, triple, and home run
questions.f: The triple is usually the hardest piece, which makes a cycle about as rare as a no-hitter.

questions.q: In cricket, what is a 'nightwatchman'?
c: A lower-order batter sent in to survive until stumps
A fielder posted near the boundary
questions.f: Teams sacrifice a bowler's wicket late in the day to shield their star batters overnight.

questions.q: In table tennis, the 'penhold' style describes a way of doing what?
c: Gripping the paddle like a pen
questions.f: Penhold grips are popular in China and once dominated world championships.

questions.q: In ice hockey slang, where is the goalie's 'five-hole'?
questions.f: Shooters number the net's openings one to five, and the gap between the pads is number five.

questions.q: In baseball, a 'balk' penalizes the pitcher for what?
questions.f: A balk advances every runner one base, punishing pitchers who fake their delivery.

questions.q: In Formula 1, what does the DRS system let a chasing driver do?
c: Open a rear-wing flap to gain straight-line speed
questions.f: DRS, the drag reduction system, may only be used within one second of the car ahead.

questions.q: In keirin track cycling, what do riders follow during the early laps?
questions.f: Born in Japan, keirin unleashes a mass sprint once the pacer pulls off with laps to go.

questions.q: The 'Queensberry Rules', which introduced gloves and timed rounds, govern which sport?
questions.f: Published in 1867 under a marquess's name, the rules made boxing far safer and more orderly.

questions.q: Which course is celebrated as the oldest and most famous 'home of golf'?
questions.f: Golf has been played at St Andrews for around 600 years, and its Old Course set the 18-hole standard.

questions.q: In basketball, 'goaltending' is the violation of doing what?
c: Blocking a shot on its downward flight to the hoop
Standing in the key too long
questions.f: Once the ball is falling toward the basket, defenders must let it fly; interference gifts the points.

questions.q: In squash, what is the 'tin'?
c: The out-of-bounds strip at the base of the front wall
questions.f: The tin works like a net in the wall: any ball striking it is out, ending the rally.

questions.q: A standard badminton game is played to how many points?
questions.f: Badminton switched to 21-point rally scoring in 2006, so every rally now wins a point.

questions.q: Chess ratings are measured on the 'Elo' scale, which is named after what?
c: The first computer to use it
questions.f: Arpad Elo, a Hungarian-American physicist, devised the system; grandmasters sit above 2500.

questions.q: In Scrabble, what bonus do you earn for using all seven of your tiles in one turn?
questions.f: Players call the feat a 'bingo', and top competitors memorize word lists to chase them.

questions.q: The first crossword, published in a New York paper in 1913, carried what name?
questions.f: Arthur Wynne's diamond-shaped 'word-cross' was renamed when a typesetter flipped the words.

questions.q: Erno Rubik, who created the Rubik's Cube in 1974, was a professor of what?
questions.f: Rubik built the cube to teach 3D thinking, then spent a month solving his own invention.

questions.q: The very first jigsaw puzzles, cut in the 1760s, were pictures of what?
questions.f: Mapmaker John Spilsbury mounted maps on wood and cut along borders to teach geography.

questions.q: Ribbon, hoop, ball, and clubs are apparatus in which Olympic sport?
questions.f: Rhythmic gymnasts keep the apparatus constantly moving, tossing ribbons high while dancing.

questions.q: Why do water polo players wear those distinctive caps with guards?
c: To protect their ears and show team and number
questions.f: The caps' ear guards shield eardrums from ball strikes; goalkeepers wear red caps.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the 'D'-shaped arc on the edge of soccer's penalty box?
c: Keeping players 9.15 m from the penalty spot during a kick
questions.f: The arc completes a 9.15 m circle around the spot, since the box itself cuts the circle short.

questions.q: Why are certain cricket fielding positions called 'silly', as in silly point?
c: They stand daringly close to the batter
questions.f: 'Silly' once meant defenseless; these fielders crouch just meters from a swinging bat.

questions.q: How many outs end a team's turn at bat in one baseball inning?
questions.f: Each inning gives both teams a turn, and three outs flip the sides.

questions.q: Australian cricket once used eight-ball overs instead of six.
questions.f: Australia bowled eight-ball overs for decades until 1979, when six became the world standard.

questions.q: In tennis, the receiver must let the serve bounce before hitting it.
questions.f: Volleying a serve out of the air loses the point; every return begins after one bounce.

questions.q: The very first basketball games were played with soccer balls.
questions.f: Naismith's players used a soccer ball for years; the laced brown basketball came later.

questions.q: An official marathon must always finish inside a stadium.
questions.f: Big-city marathons finish on ordinary streets; only the measured 42.195 km distance is required.

questions.q: A smashed shuttlecock slows down far more sharply than a hit tennis ball.
questions.f: The feather skirt creates huge drag, so a 300 km/h smash can float over the net at a fraction of that.

questions.q: In cricket, a 'yorker' is a delivery that lands where?
questions.f: A perfect yorker sneaks under the bat's swing, making it the deadliest ball at the death of an innings.

questions.q: In baseball statistics, what does RBI stand for?
questions.f: An RBI credits the batter whose hit, walk, or out brings a teammate home to score.

questions.q: In tennis slang, winning a set 6-0 is called serving your opponent a...?
questions.f: The zero looks like a bagel; losing 6-0, 6-0 is ruefully known as a double bagel.

questions.q: The narrow strip on which a fencing bout takes place is called the...?
questions.f: The piste is about 14 m long and only 2 m wide, so fencers duel along a line, never in circles.

questions.q: A 'furlong', the unit used in horse racing, was originally the length of what?
c: A plowed furrow in a field
questions.f: 'Furrow-long' was one ox-team furrow, 220 yards; eight furlongs make a mile.

questions.q: In archery, 'fletching' refers to which part of an arrow?
c: The feathers or vanes at the back
questions.f: Fletching spins the arrow like a football pass, and the workers who fixed feathers were fletchers.

questions.q: In sailing, 'starboard' refers to which side of the boat?
questions.f: Old ships hung their steering board on the right, the 'steer-board' side, before rudders moved aft.

questions.q: In traditional marbles, what is the larger shooting marble called?
questions.f: Players flick the taw from their knuckles, which is why the starting line is the 'knuckle line'.

questions.q: In curling, the bullseye-like rings the stones must reach are called the...?
questions.f: Only stones touching the house can score, and the very center button is the 'tee'.

questions.q: In archery competition, an 'end' is what?
c: A set of arrows shot before scoring
