questions.f: Astronomer Carl Sagan meant the atoms in our bodies were made long ago inside stars.

questions.q: 'Curious' means...?
questions.f: Einstein said he had no special talents but was 'passionately curious.'

questions.q: Sprinter Usain Bolt said: 'Don't think about the start of the race, think about the ___.' The what?
questions.f: Bolt, the fastest human ever timed, kept his mind on the finish line.

questions.q: Thomas Edison said: 'I have not failed. I've just found ten thousand ways that won't work.'
questions.f: Edison tested thousands of materials before his light bulb finally glowed.

questions.q: An 'inventor' is a person who...?
questions.f: Inventor Thomas Edison held more than 1,000 patents for his creations.

questions.q: Who said: 'So many people say I can't, but the ones who succeed say I can'?
questions.f: Swimmer Michael Phelps won 23 Olympic gold medals, more than anyone in history.

questions.q: What does the African proverb 'It takes a village to raise a child' mean?
c: A whole community helps a child grow up
questions.f: It means teachers, neighbors, and family all share in helping kids thrive.

questions.q: Einstein said: 'It's not that I'm so smart, it's just that I stay with problems ___.' Stay how?
questions.f: Einstein believed sticking with a hard problem matters more than being a genius.

questions.q: Who said: 'Kids are born scientists. They are curious about everything'?
questions.f: Astrophysicist Tyson says children explore and question just like real researchers.

questions.q: Aristotle said: 'Well begun is half ___.' What completes it?
questions.f: The Greek philosopher meant a good start carries you halfway to the finish.

questions.q: 'The best time to plant a tree was twenty years ago. The second best time is ___.' What completes this Chinese proverb?
questions.f: It means even if you are late to start something, the best moment to begin is today.

questions.q: Peter Pan's directions: 'Second star to the right and straight on till ___.' Till when?
questions.f: That is how you fly to Neverland in J. M. Barrie's beloved story.

questions.q: What does the Buddhist proverb 'Enough is a feast' mean?
c: Having just enough can feel like plenty
questions.f: Being thankful for what you have can make it feel like a banquet.

questions.q: A 'goal' is...?
questions.f: Swami Vivekananda said, 'Arise, awake, and stop not till the goal is reached.'

questions.q: 'Vision without action is a daydream.' This Japanese proverb warns that a plan without work is just a...?
questions.f: The full proverb adds, 'Action without vision is a nightmare,' so you need both.

questions.q: The proverb 'A chain is only as strong as its weakest link' is about teamwork.
questions.f: A team, like a chain, needs every single member to hold strong.

questions.q: What does the Urdu proverb 'One hand cannot clap' mean?
c: Some things simply can't be done alone
One hand is stronger than two
questions.f: Just as clapping needs two hands, big jobs need people working together.

questions.q: What does the German proverb 'Small streams make big rivers' mean?
c: Many small efforts add up to something great
Rivers are always small at the end
questions.f: Every mighty river on Earth really is fed by thousands of tiny streams.

questions.q: 'If you want to go fast, go alone. If you want to go far, go ___.' What completes this African proverb?
questions.f: Teamwork may be slower, but it carries you much further than going solo.

questions.q: What does the Peruvian proverb 'Little by little, one walks far' mean?
c: Small steps taken again and again cover a long distance
questions.f: Steady small steps have carried hikers across whole mountain ranges.

questions.q: A 'journey' is...?
c: a long trip from one place to another
questions.f: Lao Tzu famously said the longest journey begins with a single step.

questions.q: To 'succeed' means to...?
c: reach the goal you were trying for
questions.f: Many champions say they succeeded only because they kept trying after failing.

questions.q: The 'moral' of a story is...?
questions.f: Lewis Carroll wrote, 'Everything's got a moral, if only you can find it.'

questions.q: Who wrote: 'Sometimes the smallest things take up the most room in your heart'?
questions.f: It reflects Winnie-the-Pooh's love for his little friend Piglet.

questions.q: Who wrote the famous line: 'Curiouser and curiouser'?
questions.f: Alice says it in Wonderland when things get stranger and stranger.

questions.q: Coach John Wooden advised: 'Be quick, but don't ___.' Don't what?
questions.f: He meant move with purpose but stay calm, a favorite saying in basketball.

questions.q: Abdul Kalam said: 'If you want to shine like a sun, first ___ like a sun.' First what?
questions.f: He meant that bright success comes only after hard, fiery effort.

questions.q: Audrey Hepburn said: 'To plant a garden is to believe in ___.' In what?
questions.f: Planting seeds shows hope, because you trust they will grow in the days ahead.

questions.q: 'Gratitude' means...?
questions.f: A. A. Milne wrote that Piglet's Very Small Heart could hold a large amount of Gratitude.

questions.q: Aesop, the famous teller of fables, lived in ancient Greece.
questions.f: Aesop's stories are around 2,500 years old and still teach lessons today.

questions.q: Malala Yousafzai won the Nobel Peace Prize while she was still a teenager.
questions.f: She was 17 in 2014, the youngest Nobel Prize winner in history.

questions.q: To 'explore' means to...?
c: travel through a place to discover new things
questions.f: Astronaut Sally Ride urged kids to explore the universe and never stop asking questions.

questions.q: 'Effort' means...?
c: the hard work you put into something
questions.f: Gandhi said, 'Full effort is full victory,' meaning trying your hardest is itself a win.

questions.q: 'When eating fruit, remember the one who planted the ___.' What completes this Vietnamese proverb?
questions.f: It reminds us to thank the people whose work we now enjoy.

questions.q: 'A good laugh and a long sleep are the best ___.' What completes this Irish proverb?
questions.f: Doctors agree that laughter and rest really do help our bodies heal.

questions.q: What does the African proverb 'However long the night, the dawn will break' mean?
c: Hard times always end and better times come
questions.f: No night in history has ever stopped the sun from rising.

questions.q: 'Give a person a fish and you feed them for a day; teach them to ___ and you feed them for a lifetime.'
questions.f: This proverb means teaching a skill helps far more than a quick gift.

questions.q: Who said: 'With the new day comes new strength and new thoughts'?
questions.f: Eleanor Roosevelt was a First Lady who worked for kindness and fairness worldwide.

questions.q: Who said: 'Champions are made from something they have deep inside them: a desire, a dream, a vision'?
questions.f: Boxer Muhammad Ali called himself 'The Greatest' and backed it up with three world titles.

questions.q: 'A single rose can be my garden; a single friend, my world.' What does this mean?
c: One true friend can mean everything
questions.f: Author Leo Buscaglia meant that one loyal friend is worth more than a crowd.

questions.q: 'Imagination' is...?
c: the mind's power to picture new things
questions.f: In Wonderland, Alice claims she has believed six impossible things before breakfast.

questions.q: Alice said: 'Sometimes I've believed as many as six impossible things before ___.' Before what?
questions.f: Lewis Carroll's Alice books celebrate letting your imagination run wild.

questions.q: Dr. Seuss wrote: 'You're off to great places! Today is your day! Your mountain is waiting, so get on your ___!'
questions.f: The line is from Oh, the Places You'll Go!, a favorite gift for graduates.

questions.q: Maya Angelou said: 'If you don't like something, change it. If you can't change it, change your ___.'
questions.f: She meant we can always choose a better outlook, even when we can't fix a problem.

questions.q: 'Courage' means...?
questions.f: The word comes from the Latin 'cor,' meaning heart.

questions.q: 'Teachers open the door, but you must enter by ___.' What completes this Chinese proverb?
questions.f: Teachers can guide you, but the learning is always up to you.

questions.q: Confucius said: 'Wheresoever you go, go with all your heart.' What does this mean?
c: Put your whole self into whatever you do
Travel only to places you love
questions.f: Confucius's sayings were collected by his students into a book called the Analects.

questions.q: Who said: 'When the whole world is silent, even one voice becomes powerful'?
questions.f: Malala kept speaking up for girls' education even when it was dangerous.

questions.q: 'A good name is more desirable than great ___.' What completes this line from the Book of Proverbs?
questions.f: It means a trustworthy reputation is worth more than money.

questions.q: Who joked: 'Even if you're on the right track, you'll get run over if you just sit there'?
questions.f: Cowboy humorist Will Rogers meant that even good plans need action.

questions.q: What does the Hausa proverb 'Give thanks for a little and you will find a lot' mean?
c: Being thankful for small things brings you more
questions.f: The Hausa people of West Africa passed this wisdom down for generations.

questions.q: Who said: 'The greatest glory in living lies not in never falling, but in rising every time we fall'?
questions.f: Mandela spent 27 years in prison, then rose to become South Africa's president.

questions.q: 'Success is not final, failure is not fatal: it is the ___ to continue that counts.' Complete this famous saying.
questions.f: It is popularly credited to Churchill, but scholars have never found it anywhere in his speeches or writings.

questions.q: Michael Jordan says obstacles don't have to stop you. An 'obstacle' is...?
questions.f: Jordan advised that if you run into a wall, you find a way to climb it.

questions.q: Dr. Seuss wrote: 'Unless someone like you cares a whole awful lot, nothing is going to get better.' What does it mean?
c: Things improve only when caring people take action
questions.f: The line is spoken by the Lorax, who speaks for the trees.

questions.q: Who said: 'You never fail until you stop trying'?
questions.f: Einstein saw every wrong attempt as just another step toward the answer.

questions.q: Walt Disney said: 'First, think. Second, believe. Third, dream. And finally, ___.' Finally what?
questions.f: Disney's four Ds end with daring: being brave enough to act on your dream.

questions.q: What does the Russian proverb 'If you chase two rabbits, you will not catch either one' mean?
c: Focus on one goal at a time
Rabbits are too fast to catch
questions.f: Splitting your attention between two goals often means finishing neither.

questions.q: Who said: 'He who is not courageous enough to take risks will accomplish nothing in life'?
questions.f: Ali took bold risks in the ring and became a three-time heavyweight champion.

questions.q: Maya Angelou said: 'You may encounter many defeats, but you must not be defeated.'
questions.f: Angelou meant that losing sometimes is normal, but letting it crush your spirit is a choice.

questions.q: Malala said: 'One child, one teacher, one book, one ___ can change the world.' One what?
questions.f: She spoke these words at the United Nations on her sixteenth birthday.

questions.q: An 'opportunity' is...?
c: a good chance to do something
questions.f: From Latin ob portum, 'toward the harbor' — like a favorable wind carrying ships home.

questions.q: Who said: 'Every individual matters. Every individual has a role to play'?
questions.f: Jane Goodall lived among wild chimpanzees and showed the world how clever they are.

questions.q: What does the Chinese proverb 'Be not afraid of going slowly, be afraid only of standing still' mean?
c: Slow progress is fine; the danger is not moving at all
Standing is more tiring than walking
questions.f: Even tiny progress each day adds up to enormous progress over a year.

questions.q: Franklin warned: 'By failing to prepare, you are preparing to ___.' To what?
questions.f: Franklin loved sayings with a twist — skipping the prep work is itself a plan to fail.

questions.q: Who said: 'The biggest adventure you can take is to live the life of your dreams'?
questions.f: Oprah rose from a poor childhood to become one of the world's most famous broadcasters.

questions.q: The suffix '-ist' in words like 'scientist' and 'artist' means...?
c: a person who does or studies something
questions.f: So a physicist studies physics, and a novelist writes novels.

questions.q: The Chinese proverb 'A book holds a house of gold' means the knowledge inside books is precious.
questions.f: For centuries in China, studying books was seen as a path to fortune and wisdom.

questions.q: Steve Jobs's famous advice: 'Stay hungry, stay ___.' Stay what?
questions.f: He shared this motto in a famous graduation speech at Stanford in 2005.

questions.q: What does the African proverb 'Tomorrow belongs to the people who prepare for it today' mean?
c: Getting ready now shapes your future
questions.f: Athletes, spellers, and scientists all win tomorrow's contests with today's practice.

questions.q: Who wrote: 'Two roads diverged in a wood, and I took the one less traveled by'?
questions.f: Frost's poem The Road Not Taken is one of the most quoted poems in American history.

questions.q: A 'defeat' is...?
c: a loss in a contest or battle
questions.f: Olympic champion Wilma Rudolph said the real secret of success is learning how to lose.

questions.q: Aristotle said: 'Patience is bitter, but its fruit is ___.' Is what?
questions.f: Waiting is hard, said the Greek philosopher, but what you gain at the end is delicious.

questions.q: Who joked: 'Outside of a dog, a book is a man's best friend. Inside of a dog it's too dark to read'?
questions.f: Comedian Groucho Marx was famous for wordplay — the joke flips the meaning of 'outside of.'

questions.q: 'Give me six hours to chop down a tree and I will spend the first four sharpening the axe.' What does this saying mean?
c: Good preparation makes the work much easier
questions.f: Often credited to Lincoln, though no record of him saying it exists — the wisdom about preparation stands anyway.

questions.q: Twain said: 'If you tell the truth, you don't have to remember anything.' What does he mean?
c: Honest people never need to keep track of lies
questions.f: One lie often needs more lies to protect it, but the truth stays the same forever.

questions.q: Emerson said: 'For every minute you are angry you lose sixty seconds of ___.' Of what?
questions.f: Ralph Waldo Emerson meant anger only steals joy from your own day.

questions.q: Who wrote: 'Somewhere inside all of us is the power to change the world'?
questions.f: It is from Matilda, whose small hero proves that even little people have great power.

questions.q: Comedian Steven Wright joked: 'I intend to live forever. So far, so good.'
questions.f: Wright is famous for deadpan one-liners delivered without ever cracking a smile.

questions.q: An 'ambition' is...?
c: a strong desire to achieve something
questions.f: From Latin ambitio, 'going around' — Roman candidates walked around town asking for votes.

questions.q: What does the African proverb 'The one who asks questions doesn't lose their way' mean?
c: Asking for help keeps you from getting lost
questions.f: In many cultures, asking good questions is treated as a sign of wisdom, not weakness.

questions.q: Ali said: 'I hated every minute of training, but I said, don't quit. Suffer now and live the rest of your life as a ___.'
questions.f: Ali trained before sunrise, believing hard practice bought a lifetime of glory.

questions.q: Who said: 'However difficult life may seem, there is always something you can do and succeed at'?
questions.f: Hawking made world-changing discoveries about black holes while living with a serious illness.

questions.q: A 'discovery' is...?
c: finding something real that was unknown before
questions.f: Penicillin was a discovery, while the light bulb was an invention — scientists love the difference.

questions.q: What does the Chinese proverb 'Learning is a treasure that will follow its owner everywhere' mean?
c: What you learn stays with you wherever you go
questions.f: Unlike gold, knowledge cannot be lost, stolen, or left behind.

questions.q: Who said: 'Do your little bit of good where you are; it's those little bits of good put together that overwhelm the world'?
questions.f: Archbishop Desmond Tutu won the Nobel Peace Prize for his peaceful fight for fairness.

questions.q: 'A good friend is like a four-leaf ___: hard to find and lucky to have.' What completes this Irish proverb?
questions.f: Only about one in every 5,000 clovers has four leaves, which is why they mean luck.

questions.q: 'Confidence' means...?
c: belief in yourself and your abilities
questions.f: Tennis champion Arthur Ashe said the key to confidence is preparation.

questions.q: Gandhi said: 'A man is but the product of his thoughts. What he thinks, he becomes.' What does this mean?
c: Your thoughts shape the person you turn into
questions.f: Gandhi believed training your mind was the first step to changing the world.

questions.q: 'Practice like you've never won. Perform like you've never lost' is a traditional sports saying.
questions.f: It means train with humility and compete with confidence.

questions.q: Who said: 'There is no shortcut to success. One has to work hard to achieve it'?
questions.f: Milkha Singh, called the Flying Sikh, became one of India's greatest runners.

questions.q: 'Hold a true friend with both your ___.' What completes this Nigerian proverb?
questions.f: It means a real friend is precious, so cherish them and never let go.

questions.q: Hockey star Wayne Gretzky said: 'You miss one hundred percent of the shots you don't ___.' Don't what?
questions.f: Gretzky scored more goals than anyone in hockey history — because he kept shooting.

questions.q: Who said: 'Do small things with great love'?
questions.f: Mother Teresa spent her life caring for the poorest people in Kolkata, India.

questions.q: Dr. Seuss wrote: 'The more that you read, the more things you will know. The more that you learn, the more places you'll ___.'
questions.f: The rhyme is from his book I Can Read With My Eyes Shut!

questions.q: A golfer joked: 'The more I practice, the luckier I get.' What does this mean?
c: Practice creates your own good luck
questions.f: Scientists agree: hours of practice explain most of what looks like sporting 'luck.'

questions.q: In quotes like 'Follow your dreams,' a 'dream' means...?
c: a big hope you want to make real
questions.f: Abdul Kalam said a real dream is one that doesn't let you sleep — it keeps you excited.

questions.q: Who wrote the encouraging line: 'Kid, you'll move mountains'?
questions.f: It appears in Oh, the Places You'll Go!, the last book Dr. Seuss published in his lifetime.

questions.q: 'Shoot for the moon. Even if you miss, you'll land among the ___.' What completes this saying?
questions.f: It means aiming very high brings you something great even if you fall short.

questions.q: Mother Teresa said: 'Kind words can be short and easy to speak, but their echoes are truly endless.'
questions.f: She meant one small kind sentence can keep spreading good long after it is spoken.

questions.q: What does the old saying 'Cranes fly together' mean?
questions.f: Real cranes do migrate in flocks, flying in a V to help each other along.

questions.q: To 'observe' means to...?
questions.f: Yogi Berra joked, 'You can observe a lot by just watching.'

questions.q: 'Yesterday is history, tomorrow is a mystery, but today is a ___.' What completes this saying?
questions.f: That is why today is called 'the present' — it is a gift you get to open.

questions.q: Who said: 'Just play. Have fun. Enjoy the game'?
questions.f: Even the most competitive player ever said the fun of the game comes first.

questions.q: What does the Japanese proverb 'A single arrow is easily broken, but not ten in a bundle' mean?
questions.f: A famous Japanese lord is said to have taught his sons unity with real arrows.

questions.q: 'Portable' — like a book you can carry anywhere — means...?
questions.f: Author Stephen King calls books 'a uniquely portable magic.'

questions.q: Ray Bradbury's advice: 'Love what you do and do what you ___.' What completes it?
questions.f: Bradbury wrote hundreds of stories simply because writing made him happy.

questions.q: Bill Nye said: 'Everyone you will ever meet knows something you don't.' What does this mean?
c: Every person can teach you something
questions.f: Bill Nye the Science Guy taught a generation of kids to love asking questions.

questions.q: Who said: 'If you don't like to read, you haven't found the right book'?
questions.f: The Harry Potter author believes there is a perfect book waiting for every reader.

questions.q: An 'author' is a person who...?
questions.f: The word comes from Latin auctor, meaning 'one who originates or creates.'

questions.q: Neil Gaiman said: 'A book is a ___ that you hold in your hand.' A what?
questions.f: He meant every book carries a whole imagined world inside its covers.

questions.q: A library is a place where you can borrow books to read.
questions.f: Ray Bradbury said that without libraries 'we have no past and no future.'

questions.q: What does the saying 'Wear the old coat and buy the new book' mean?
c: Spend on learning before spending on things
questions.f: It means knowledge is a better buy than fancy possessions.

questions.q: Twain said: 'Kindness is the language which the deaf can hear and the blind can ___.' Can what?
questions.f: Kind actions are understood by everyone, no matter what.

questions.q: In 'Turn your face to the sun and the shadows fall behind you,' the 'shadows' stand for...?
questions.f: Face the sun and your real shadow falls behind you too — the saying works both ways.

questions.q: Who sang and said: 'One good thing about music, when it hits you, you feel no pain'?
questions.f: Bob Marley brought reggae music from Jamaica to the whole world.

questions.q: 'Don't judge each day by the harvest you reap but by the seeds that you ___.' What completes this line?
questions.f: Robert Louis Stevenson meant a good day is one where you start good things.

questions.q: Who said: 'Winners never quit and quitters never win'?
questions.f: The Super Bowl trophy is named after Vince Lombardi, coach of the Green Bay Packers.

questions.q: Serena Williams said: 'A champion is defined by how they ___ when they get knocked down.' They what?
questions.f: Serena won 23 Grand Slam singles titles, many after tough comebacks.

questions.q: 'Persistence' means...?
c: continuing firmly even when it is difficult
questions.f: Benjamin Franklin said, 'Energy and persistence conquer all things.'

questions.q: Who said: 'You must never be fearful about what you are doing when it is right'?
questions.f: Rosa Parks's quiet courage on a bus in 1955 helped spark the civil rights movement.

questions.q: Harriet Tubman said: 'If you are tired, keep going; if you are scared, keep going; if you are hungry, keep ___.'
questions.f: Tubman bravely guided many people to freedom and never lost a single one.

questions.q: Frederick Douglass said: 'If there is no struggle, there is no progress.' What does this mean?
c: Getting better always takes hard effort
questions.f: Douglass taught himself to read and became one of America's greatest speakers.

questions.q: Who said: 'Failure is simply the opportunity to begin again, this time more intelligently'?
questions.f: Ford's first two car companies failed before the Ford Motor Company changed the world.

questions.q: The 'extra-' in 'extraordinary' means...?
questions.f: Coach Jimmy Johnson said the difference between ordinary and extraordinary is 'that little extra.'

questions.q: Rowling wrote: 'We do not need magic to change the world, we carry all the power we need inside ___ already.'
questions.f: She said it in a famous Harvard speech about the power of imagination.

questions.q: Grace Hopper said: 'A ship in port is safe, but that's not what ships are built for.' What does she mean?
c: Growth requires leaving your comfort zone
Ships should stay in the harbor
questions.f: Hopper was a computing pioneer and U.S. Navy admiral who loved bold thinking.

questions.q: Which great artist, even in old age, said: 'I am still learning'?
questions.f: Michelangelo was still designing buildings in his late eighties.

questions.q: Isaac Newton said: 'If I have seen further it is by standing on the shoulders of giants.'
questions.f: Newton meant his discoveries were built on the work of earlier scientists.

questions.q: A 'genius' is...?
questions.f: Newton had a humbler view — he said, 'Genius is patience.'

questions.q: Mother Teresa said: 'I can do things you cannot, you can do things I cannot; together we can do ___ things.'
questions.f: She won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979 for her lifetime of service.

questions.q: A famous saying warns that if you judge a fish by its ability to climb a tree, it will believe it is stupid. The point?
c: Everyone is smart in their own way
questions.f: The line is widely credited to Einstein but appears in none of his writings — its lesson is sound all the same.

questions.q: Who said: 'The beautiful thing about learning is that nobody can take it away from you'?
questions.f: Blues legend B. B. King named his beloved guitar Lucille.

questions.q: Kipling's six honest serving-men are 'What and Why and When and How and Where and ___.' And who?
questions.f: Kipling meant the six question words that help anyone learn anything.

questions.q: A 'motto' is...?
c: a short saying that guides a person or group
questions.f: The Olympic motto 'Citius, Altius, Fortius' means faster, higher, stronger.

questions.q: Who said: 'When one door of happiness closes, another opens'?
questions.f: Keller added that we often stare so long at the closed door we miss the open one.

questions.q: Zig Ziglar said: 'There is no elevator to success. You have to take the stairs.' Meaning?
c: Success comes step by step, with no shortcuts
questions.f: Motivational speaker Ziglar loved picture-sayings that stick in your mind.

questions.q: Napoleon Hill said: 'A goal is a dream with a ___.' With a what?
questions.f: Writing down a dream and picking a date turns it into a real plan.

questions.q: Harriet Tubman escaped slavery and then bravely guided many others to freedom.
questions.f: She made about 13 rescue missions on the Underground Railroad.

questions.q: 'Humble' means...?
questions.f: From Latin humilis, 'low to the ground,' from humus, meaning earth.

questions.q: Who wrote: 'Nothing happens unless first we dream'?
questions.f: Sandburg won three Pulitzer Prizes — for his poems and a biography of Lincoln.

questions.q: Marilyn Monroe said: 'The sky is not the limit. Your ___ is.' Your what?
questions.f: She meant imagination sets the only real ceiling on what you can do.

questions.q: What does the Chinese proverb 'Behind an able person there are always other able people' mean?
c: Great people are supported by great teams
questions.f: Even solo champions have coaches, teachers, and helpers behind them.

questions.q: The 'pre-' in 'prepare' means...?
questions.f: From Latin prae — to prepare is literally to get things ready beforehand.

questions.q: Who said: 'I'm not the next Usain Bolt or Michael Phelps. I'm the first Simone Biles'?
questions.f: Biles has more world championship gymnastics medals than anyone in history.

questions.q: Billie Jean King said: 'Be bold. If you're going to make an error, make a ___.' A what?
questions.f: A 'doozy' is American slang for something extraordinary — so make even mistakes boldly.

questions.q: Jane Austen wrote: 'I declare there is no enjoyment like reading!'
questions.f: The line is spoken in Pride and Prejudice, published in 1813.

questions.q: The 'value' of something is...?
questions.f: Edison said, 'The value of an idea lies in the using of it.'

questions.q: Which American president said: 'I cannot live without books'?
questions.f: Jefferson's personal library of 6,487 books restarted the Library of Congress.

questions.q: Roald Dahl urged: throw your TV set away 'and in its place you can install a lovely ___ on the wall.'
questions.f: The rhyming plea comes from Charlie and the Chocolate Factory.

questions.q: Stephen Covey advised: 'Seek first to understand, then to be understood.' What does this mean?
c: Listen to others before asking them to listen to you
questions.f: It is one of his famous 7 Habits of Highly Effective People.

questions.q: Who said: 'Kids don't remember what you try to teach them. They remember what you are'?
questions.f: The creator of the Muppets taught mostly through playfulness and kindness.

questions.q: 'Wonder' means...?
c: a feeling of amazement and curiosity
questions.f: The ancient Greeks listed Seven Wonders of the World that amazed every traveler.

questions.q: Robert Frost wrote: 'The best way out is always ___.' Always what?
questions.f: Frost meant the surest way past a problem is straight through the work it takes.

questions.q: Anne of Green Gables author L. M. Montgomery wrote: 'Tomorrow is always fresh, with no mistakes in it yet.' Meaning?
c: Each new day is a clean start
questions.f: Anne Shirley says a version of this line to her teacher in the beloved novel.

questions.q: Who said: 'Find out who you are and do it on purpose'?
questions.f: Dolly Parton has also given more than 200 million free books to children.

questions.q: 'Companion' literally means...?
questions.f: From Latin com (with) + panis (bread) — India's Ruskin Bond calls books our best companions.

questions.q: Who said: 'Go confidently in the direction of your dreams. Live the life you have imagined'?
questions.f: Thoreau tested his advice by living simply in a cabin at Walden Pond for two years.

questions.q: Emerson said: 'Do not go where the path may lead, go instead where there is no path and leave a ___.'
questions.f: Emerson urged people to be original instead of only following others.

questions.q: Coach Wooden said: 'Do not let what you cannot do interfere with what you can do.' Meaning?
c: Focus on your strengths instead of your limits
questions.f: Wooden's teams won 88 college games in a row using this focused mindset.

questions.q: 'Enthusiasm' means...?
c: great excitement and energy for something
questions.f: From Greek entheos, 'a god within' — the ancients thought excitement was heaven-sent.

questions.q: Who said: 'If you hear a voice within you say you cannot paint, then by all means paint, and that voice will be silenced'?
questions.f: Van Gogh sold almost nothing in his lifetime, yet kept painting — now his works are priceless.

questions.q: Picasso said: 'Every child is an ___. The problem is how to remain one once we grow up.'
questions.f: Picasso spent years learning to paint with the free spirit of a child again.

questions.q: Leonardo da Vinci said: 'Learning never exhausts the mind.'
questions.f: Leonardo filled thousands of notebook pages with art, inventions, and questions.

questions.q: Soccer legend Pele said: 'Everything is practice.' What did he mean?
c: You improve at anything by practicing it
questions.f: Pele won three World Cups, more than any other player ever.

questions.q: A 'masterpiece' is...?
questions.f: Originally it was the 'master piece' an apprentice made to prove they had become a master craftsman.

questions.q: Who said: 'Everything negative, pressure, challenges, is all an opportunity for me to rise'?
questions.f: Kobe Bryant's famous 'Mamba Mentality' meant treating every difficulty as fuel.

questions.q: Zig Ziglar said: 'You don't have to be great to start, but you have to start to be ___.'
questions.f: Every expert was once a beginner who simply began.

questions.q: Jim Rohn said if you really want something you'll find a way; if you don't, you'll find a(n)...?
questions.f: Rohn taught that desire, not difficulty, decides whether we act.

questions.q: An 'excuse' is...?
c: a reason given to avoid blame or work
questions.f: From Latin excusare, 'to free from blame.'

questions.q: George Washington Carver said ninety-nine percent of failures come from people who have the habit of making excuses.
questions.f: Carver rose from slavery to become a famous scientist who found 300+ uses for the peanut.

questions.q: Who said: 'The best way to do it, is to do it'?
questions.f: Earhart lived her words, becoming the first woman to fly solo across the Atlantic.

questions.q: Marie Curie advised: 'Have perseverance, and above all confidence in ___.'
questions.f: Curie persevered through years of hard lab work to discover two new elements.

questions.q: What does the Hopi proverb 'One finger cannot lift a pebble' mean?
c: Pebbles are heavier than they look
questions.f: The Hopi people of the American Southwest prize working together as a community.

questions.q: A 'talent' is...?
c: a natural ability to do something well
questions.f: From Greek talanton, an ancient unit of money — its meaning changed through a famous parable.

questions.q: Who said: 'To invent, you need a good imagination and a pile of junk'?
questions.f: Edison's Menlo Park lab was famously stuffed with spare parts for tinkering.

questions.q: Walt Disney said: 'We keep moving forward, opening new doors, because we're curious and ___ keeps leading us down new paths.'
questions.f: The line appears at the end of the film Meet the Robinsons.

questions.q: 'Everything is theoretically impossible, until it is done.' What does this mean?
c: Many things seem impossible until someone does them
questions.f: Flight, moon landings, and instant messages were all once called impossible.

questions.q: Marie Curie won Nobel Prizes in two different sciences.
questions.f: She remains the only person ever to win Nobels in both physics and chemistry.

questions.q: The 'universe' means...?
c: everything that exists — space, stars, and all
questions.f: From Latin unus + versus, 'turned into one' — everything combined into a single whole.

questions.q: Who said: 'It is easier to build strong children than to repair broken adults'?
questions.f: Douglass escaped slavery and became a legendary voice for freedom and education.

questions.q: Booker T. Washington's advice: 'Turn every setback into a ___.'
questions.f: He built the Tuskegee Institute from a shack into a famous university.

questions.q: Fred Rogers said you rarely have time for everything you want, 'so you need to make ___.' Make what?
questions.f: Mister Rogers meant that choosing what matters most is a skill for life.

questions.q: 'Progress' means...?
questions.f: From Latin pro + gradi, 'to step forward.'

questions.q: Which NASA mathematician said: 'Like what you do, and then you will do your best'?
questions.f: Katherine Johnson's hand calculations helped guide astronauts to the Moon.

questions.q: The poem asks: 'you ask, what if I fall? Oh but my darling, what if you ___?'
questions.f: Poet Erin Hanson's line reminds us to imagine success, not just failure.

questions.q: Dr. Seuss wrote: 'Oh, the thinks you can think up if only you try!'
questions.f: His book Oh, the Thinks You Can Think! celebrates wild imagination.

questions.q: Helen Keller said the best and most beautiful things in the world cannot be seen or touched, but must be...?
questions.f: Keller, who could not see or hear, knew that love and friendship need no eyes or ears.

questions.q: 'Bold' means...?
questions.f: Robert Frost wrote, 'Freedom lies in being bold.'

questions.q: Who wrote: 'Ideas are like rabbits. You get a couple, and pretty soon you have a dozen'?
questions.f: Steinbeck won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1962.

questions.q: 'Choose a job you love, and you will never have to ___ a day in your life.' Complete this well-known saying.
questions.f: Usually credited to Confucius, yet it appears in no Chinese classic — the earliest printed versions are modern.

questions.q: Confucius said: 'Everything has beauty, but not everyone sees it.' What does this mean?
c: Beauty is everywhere if you look closely
questions.f: Confucius taught his students to notice the ordinary world with fresh attention.

questions.q: Malala Yousafzai said: 'Let us pick up our books and our pens. They are our most powerful weapons.'
questions.f: She spoke these words at the United Nations in 2013.

questions.q: What makes a proverb different from a quotation?
c: A proverb is a traditional saying with no single known author
A proverb is always about animals
questions.f: Sayings like 'Look before you leap' belong to everyone — no one knows who said them first.

questions.q: Who said: 'The scariest moment is always just before you start'?
questions.f: Even the master of scary stories admits that beginning is the frightening part.

questions.q: Martin Luther King Jr. said: 'We must accept finite disappointment, but never lose infinite ___.'
questions.f: He meant setbacks have limits, but hope can be endless.

questions.q: Yoko Ono said: 'A dream you dream alone is only a dream. A dream you dream together is reality.' Meaning?
c: Shared dreams become real through teamwork
questions.f: John Lennon loved the line so much it inspired his song Imagine.

questions.q: Who said: 'It is during our darkest moments that we must focus to see the light'?
questions.f: Aristotle tutored a young student who became Alexander the Great.

questions.q: Socrates said: 'The secret of change is to focus all of your energy not on fighting the old, but on building the ___.'
questions.f: Socrates taught in the marketplace of Athens by asking endless questions.

questions.q: Seneca said: 'Difficulties strengthen the mind, as labor does the body.' What does this mean?
c: Hard problems make your mind stronger, like exercise
Thinking is a kind of sport
questions.f: Seneca was a Roman philosopher who wrote letters full of practical advice.

questions.q: Lao Tzu said: 'Watch your thoughts, they become your words; watch your words, they become your ___.'
questions.f: The chain continues: actions become habits, and habits become character.

questions.q: Who said: 'Twenty years from now you will be more disappointed by the things you didn't do than by the ones you did do'?
questions.f: Twain's advice continues: 'So throw off the bowlines. Sail away from the safe harbor.'

questions.q: 'Loyal' means...?
questions.f: Ernest Hemingway said, 'There is no friend as loyal as a book.'

questions.q: 'Reading is a discount ticket to everywhere.' What does this mean?
c: Books let you travel the world cheaply through imagination
questions.f: A library card really is free in most towns — the cheapest ticket on Earth.

questions.q: 'A house without books is like a room without ___.' What completes Horace Mann's saying?
questions.f: Mann fought to give every American child a free public education.

questions.q: Which Roman statesman said: 'A room without books is like a body without a soul'?
questions.f: Cicero was ancient Rome's most famous speaker, and his letters still survive.

questions.q: Scientist Temple Grandin, who is autistic, said: 'I am different, not less.'
questions.f: Grandin's inventions improved animal care around the world.

questions.q: A 'chore' is...?
questions.f: Author Kate DiCamillo says reading should be offered to children as a gift, not a chore.

questions.q: Eleanor Roosevelt said: 'You must do the things you think you cannot ___.'
questions.f: She overcame deep shyness to become a fearless voice at the United Nations.

questions.q: Tolkien wrote: 'All we have to decide is what to do with the time that is given us.' Meaning?
c: We choose how to spend our own time
questions.f: The wizard Gandalf says this to Frodo in The Lord of the Rings.

questions.q: Whose joke is this: 'My grandmother started walking five miles a day when she was sixty. She's ninety-seven now and we don't know where she is'?
questions.f: Ellen's gentle, silly humor made her one of TV's favorite hosts.

questions.q: The 're-' in 'retry' and 'rewrite' means...?
questions.f: From Latin — so to 'rise' after failing is often really to re-rise, again and again.

questions.q: Who said: 'I don't focus on what I'm up against. I focus on my goals and I try to ignore the rest'?
questions.f: Venus won Wimbledon five times and fought for equal prize money for women.

questions.q: Coach George Halas said: 'Nobody who ever gave his best ___ it.'
questions.f: Halas founded the Chicago Bears and coached them for 40 seasons.

questions.q: 'The only discipline that lasts is self-discipline.' What does this mean?
c: Lasting control must come from inside yourself
questions.f: Champions train even when no coach is watching.

questions.q: 'Ordinary' means...?
questions.f: From Latin ordo, 'order' — ordinary things simply follow the usual order.

questions.q: Who said the best measure of a game he played was 'how much better I made my teammates play'?
questions.f: Russell won 11 championships, the most of any NBA player ever.

questions.q: Colin Powell said: 'A dream doesn't become reality through magic; it takes determination and hard ___.'
questions.f: Powell rose from a New York City childhood to become a top American statesman.

questions.q: Sheryl Sandberg said: 'We cannot change what we are not aware of.' What does this mean?
c: Noticing a problem is the first step to fixing it
questions.f: First see it clearly, then you can start to fix it.

questions.q: The Chinese proverb 'A gem cannot be polished without friction, nor a person perfected without trials' means hard times help us grow.
questions.f: Real gemstones only sparkle after long grinding against rough surfaces.

questions.q: A 'coach' trains athletes — but the word originally named...?
questions.f: From Kocs, a Hungarian town famous for carriages — a coach 'carries' you to your goal.

questions.q: Who said: 'Anyone who stops learning is old, whether at twenty or eighty'?
questions.f: Ford added that whoever keeps learning stays young.

questions.q: Debby Boone said: 'Dreams are the seeds of ___. Nothing ever grows without a seed.'
questions.f: Every giant redwood on Earth began as a seed lighter than a paperclip.

questions.q: 'Your dreams don't have an expiration date. Take a deep breath and try again.' Meaning?
c: It is never too late to chase a dream
questions.f: Author Laura Ingalls Wilder published her first Little House book at age 65.

questions.q: 'Faith' means...?
questions.f: From Latin fides, meaning trust — the same root as 'fidelity.'

questions.q: Who said: 'When you do the common things in life in an uncommon way, you will command the attention of the world'?
questions.f: Carver turned humble crops like peanuts and sweet potatoes into hundreds of products.

questions.q: The proverb 'Fall down seven times, stand up eight' comes from ancient Rome.
questions.f: It is a Japanese proverb — 'nana korobi ya oki' — beloved by athletes worldwide.

questions.q: Which punctuation marks show that you are giving a speaker's exact words?
questions.f: English uses double quotes, but many countries use angled marks like « these ».

questions.q: 'Jobs fill your pocket, but adventures fill your soul.' What does this mean?
c: Experiences enrich you more than money
questions.f: Studies really do show experiences bring more lasting joy than possessions.

questions.q: 'A day dreamed is never ___.' What completes this saying?
questions.f: Daydreaming actually helps the brain sort ideas and spark creativity.

questions.q: Who said: 'Great minds discuss ideas'?
questions.f: The full saying adds: average minds discuss events; small minds discuss people.

questions.q: The word 'adventure' comes from Latin roots meaning...?
questions.f: From advenire, 'to arrive' — Amelia Earhart said adventure is worthwhile in itself.

questions.q: Hockey legend Wayne Gretzky is nicknamed 'The Great One.'
questions.f: Gretzky holds or shares 61 NHL records — more than any other player.

questions.q: Kobi Yamada wrote: 'Follow your dreams, they know the ___.'
questions.f: Your interests often point toward the work you were meant to do.

questions.q: An 'apprentice' is...?
c: a person learning a craft from a master
questions.f: From Latin apprehendere, 'to grasp' — apprentices grasp their trade by doing it.

questions.q: Churchill said the pessimist sees difficulty in every opportunity. A 'pessimist' is someone who...?
questions.f: From Latin pessimus, 'worst' — while the optimist, from optimus, expects the best.

questions.q: Who said: 'Opportunity is missed by most people because it is dressed in overalls and looks like work'?
questions.f: Edison napped on a lab bench so he could work on his inventions day and night.

questions.q: Tagore said: 'You can't cross the sea merely by standing and staring at the water.' What does this mean?
c: The sea is too wide to cross
questions.f: Rabindranath Tagore was the first non-European to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.

questions.q: Twain defined courage as 'resistance to fear, mastery of fear, not ___ of fear.' Not what?
questions.f: Brave people still feel fear — they simply refuse to let it steer.

questions.q: Who wrote: 'Hope is the thing with feathers that perches in the soul'?
questions.f: Dickinson wrote nearly 1,800 poems but published fewer than a dozen in her lifetime.

questions.q: Maya Angelou called courage 'the most important of all the virtues.' A 'virtue' is...?
questions.f: She explained that without courage, no other virtue can be practiced steadily.

questions.q: Who warned: 'It takes twenty years to build a reputation and five minutes to ruin it'?
questions.f: Investor Warren Buffett is nicknamed the Oracle of Omaha.

questions.q: What does the Turkish proverb 'No matter how far you have gone down the wrong road, turn back' mean?
c: It is never too late to correct a mistake
questions.f: Admitting a wrong path early saves far more time than stubbornly continuing.

questions.q: Vivekananda advised: 'Take up one idea. Make that one idea your ___.' Your what?
questions.f: He electrified the 1893 World Parliament of Religions in Chicago with his opening words.

questions.q: Mark Twain responded to a false rumor with the line: 'The reports of my death are greatly exaggerated.'
questions.f: A newspaper had confused him with an ill cousin — Twain found it hilarious.

questions.q: 'The flower that blooms in adversity is the most rare and beautiful of all.' 'Adversity' means...?
questions.f: The line is spoken by the Emperor in Disney's film Mulan.

questions.q: Who said: 'A team is not a group of people who work together. A team is a group of people who trust each other'?
questions.f: Sinek is famous for telling leaders to 'start with why.'

questions.q: Kalam warned not to rest after your first victory, because if you fail next, 'more lips are waiting to say' what?
c: that your first victory was just luck
questions.f: Abdul Kalam led India's rocket program before becoming its beloved president.

questions.q: Jobs said: 'The people who are crazy enough to think they can change the world are the ones who ___.'
questions.f: The line anchored Apple's famous 'Think Different' campaign in 1997.

questions.q: Who said: 'Laughter is the shortest distance between two people'?
questions.f: Borge, the 'Clown Prince of Denmark,' mixed piano concerts with comedy.

questions.q: Yogi Berra joked, 'It's like deja vu all over again.' The phrase 'deja vu' literally means...?
questions.f: From French — which makes 'deja vu all over again' a double repeat, and twice as funny.

questions.q: 'An army of sheep led by a lion would defeat an army of lions led by a sheep.' This Arabic proverb means...?
c: Good leadership matters more than raw strength
questions.f: Alexander the Great is often linked with the same idea about leaders.

questions.q: Marie Curie said: 'Now is the time to understand more, so that we may ___ less.' What?
questions.f: Curie carried radium samples in her pockets before anyone understood the danger.

questions.q: Who said: 'Don't raise your voice, improve your argument'?
questions.f: Archbishop Tutu was famous for disarming opponents with humor instead of anger.

questions.q: Victor Hugo said 'every syllable that is spelled out is a spark.' A 'syllable' is...?
c: a single beat of sound in a word
questions.f: 'Spelling' has two syllables — and Hugo, author of Les Miserables, called each one a spark.

questions.q: Who said: 'The only way to have a friend is to be one'?
questions.f: Emerson's essays made him one of America's most quoted thinkers.

questions.q: Olympic sprinter Wilma Rudolph said the secret to really doing something in life is 'learning how to lose.' Why?
c: Handling defeat well is what lets you keep growing
Losing is more fun than winning
questions.f: Rudolph overcame childhood polio to win three Olympic golds in 1960.

questions.q: Aristotle said: 'The antidote for fifty enemies is one ___.'
questions.f: An antidote literally means 'something given against' a poison.

questions.q: Emerson said every artist was first an amateur. 'Amateur' literally means...?
c: one who does something for love
questions.f: From Latin amator, 'lover' — amateurs create purely because they love it.

questions.q: Which astronaut joked: 'There's no problem so bad that you can't make it worse'?
questions.f: Hadfield, famous for singing on the space station, meant: stay calm and don't add errors.

questions.q: What does the Native American proverb 'Listen, or your tongue will keep you deaf' mean?
c: Talking too much stops you from learning
questions.f: Many Native nations honored councils where each speaker was heard in full silence.

questions.q: Gandhi said: 'Truth never damages a cause that is ___.' What word completes it?
questions.f: 'Just' here means fair and right — honest scrutiny only strengthens a fair cause.

questions.q: C. S. Lewis said integrity is doing right when no one is watching. 'Integrity' comes from a Latin root meaning...?
questions.f: Same root as 'integer,' a whole number — a person of integrity is undivided.

questions.q: Who wrote: 'A reader lives a thousand lives before he dies. The man who never reads lives only one'?
questions.f: The Game of Thrones author gives the line to a bookish character named Jojen.

questions.q: Astronomer Carl Sagan said that books 'break the shackles of time.'
questions.f: Sagan marveled that a reader can hear an author's voice across thousands of years.

questions.q: Thoreau said: 'Success usually comes to those who are too busy to be looking for it.' Meaning?
c: Focus on the work and success follows
questions.f: Thoreau wrote two million words in his journals while living this advice.

questions.q: Frost wrote: 'The woods are lovely, dark and deep, But I have promises to keep, And miles to go before I ___.'
questions.f: He repeats the line twice — some readers hear a hint of life's final rest in it.

questions.q: Which artist said: 'Creativity takes courage'?
questions.f: When illness stopped him from painting, Matisse bravely invented art from paper cutouts.

questions.q: Tendulkar said people throw stones at you and you turn them into milestones. A 'milestone' is...?
c: a marker of an important stage on a journey
questions.f: Roman roads had a stone every mile — some are still standing after 2,000 years.

questions.q: Brene Brown said: 'Joy comes to us in moments, ordinary moments.' What does this mean?
c: Happiness often hides in everyday life
questions.f: Her research found people who notice small joys handle hard times better.

questions.q: Who said: 'We realize the importance of our voices only when we are silenced'?
questions.f: Malala wrote it about her childhood in Swat, where girls' schools were being closed.

questions.q: Mandela said a good head and a good heart are 'a formidable combination.' 'Formidable' means...?
questions.f: From Latin formidare, 'to dread' — a formidable team makes opponents nervous.

questions.q: Who said: 'Do not pray for an easy life, pray for the strength to endure a difficult one'?
questions.f: Bruce Lee was a philosophy student who filled notebooks with sayings like this.

questions.q: Jesse Owens said the battles that count aren't for gold medals but are 'the struggles within yourself.' Meaning?
c: Inner growth matters more than prizes
questions.f: Owens won four golds at the 1936 Berlin Olympics, defying the host regime's hateful ideas.

questions.q: Churchill said: 'Continuous effort, not strength or intelligence, is the key to unlocking our ___.'
questions.f: Churchill failed exams as a boy, then became one of history's most honored leaders.

questions.q: Many sayings are listed as 'Author unknown.' A writer whose name is not known is called...?
questions.f: From Greek an + onyma, 'without a name' — note the near-miss words in the choices!

questions.q: Who said: 'Some people want it to happen, some wish it would happen, others make it happen'?
questions.f: Jordan famously arrived hours before practice to work on shots he had already mastered.

questions.q: What does the German proverb 'A clear conscience is a soft pillow' mean?
questions.f: Your conscience is your inner sense of right and wrong — clear it, and rest comes easy.

questions.q: Ali said: 'It isn't the mountains ahead to climb that wear you out; it's the ___ in your shoe.'
questions.f: Small nagging worries drain more energy than the big challenge itself.

questions.q: The proverb 'Unity is strength, division is weakness' comes from the Swahili language of East Africa.
questions.f: Swahili is spoken by over 200 million people across East Africa.

questions.q: Franklin said 'Diligence is the mother of good luck.' 'Diligence' means...?
questions.f: From Latin diligere, 'to value highly' — diligent workers treat every task as valuable.

questions.q: Which Irish poet wrote: 'There are no strangers here; only friends you haven't yet met'?
questions.f: Yeats won the Nobel Prize in 1923, the first Irish writer to do so.

questions.q: Ratan Tata said: 'I take decisions and then make them right.' What does he mean?
c: Commit to a choice and work to make it succeed
questions.f: Under Tata, his company created the Nano, once the world's cheapest car.

questions.q: Kalam said: 'All birds find shelter during a rain. But eagle avoids rain by flying above the ___.'
questions.f: Eagles really can soar above rain clouds, riding warm air currents to great heights.

questions.q: Oscar Wilde is described as an Irish playwright and 'wit.' A 'wit' is...?
c: a person famous for clever, funny remarks
a person who argues a lot
questions.f: Wilde once quipped that he could resist everything except temptation.

questions.q: Who said: 'A real friend is one who walks in when the rest of the world walks out'?
questions.f: Winchell was a famous American newspaper and radio commentator of the 1930s and 40s.

questions.q: What does the Nepali proverb 'An empty vessel makes the most noise' mean?
c: Those who know the least often talk the loudest
questions.f: Try it: an empty jar really does ring louder when tapped than a full one.

questions.q: Twain said: 'Continuous improvement is better than delayed ___.'
questions.f: Getting 1 percent better daily beats waiting forever for a flawless start.

questions.q: Confucius said: 'Study the past if you would define the future.'
questions.f: Confucius saw history as a mirror for choosing tomorrow's path.

questions.q: Who wrote: 'Let the rain kiss you. Let the rain sing you a lullaby'?
questions.f: Hughes was a star of the Harlem Renaissance, the great flowering of Black art in the 1920s.

questions.q: Confucius and Socrates are called philosophers. 'Philosopher' literally means...?
questions.f: From Greek philos (loving) + sophia (wisdom).

questions.q: Muir said: 'In every walk with nature one receives far more than he seeks.' What does this mean?
c: Nature gives you unexpected gifts beyond what you came for
Nature hides what you search for
questions.f: Muir's walks led to the creation of Yosemite National Park.

questions.q: Biologist E. O. Wilson said: 'Look closely at nature. Every species is a ___.'
questions.f: Wilson, called 'the ant man,' identified over 400 species of ants.

questions.q: Who said: 'I know nothing with any certainty, but the sight of the stars makes me dream'?
questions.f: He painted The Starry Night from his window the year after writing about starry dreams.

questions.q: Tyson said the universe is 'under no obligation' to make sense to you. An 'obligation' is...?
c: a duty you are bound to fulfill
questions.f: From Latin ligare, 'to bind' — the same root hiding in 'ligament.'

questions.q: MLK said: 'The ultimate measure of a person is where they stand in times of challenge.' Meaning?
questions.f: He preached this while facing jail, threats, and hardship without abandoning peace.

questions.q: Grace Hopper said the most damaging phrase in the language is: 'We've always done it this ___.'
questions.f: Hopper kept a clock running backward in her office to prove routines can be questioned.

questions.q: Which cricket captain said: 'You always get a second chance in life. What matters is what you do with the first one'?
questions.f: Dhoni captained India to the 2011 World Cup title, sealing it with a six.

questions.q: The saying 'Necessity is the mother of invention' is an English proverb.
questions.f: Versions of the idea go back to ancient times — needs push people to invent.

questions.q: An African proverb says one 'falsehood' spoils a thousand truths. A 'falsehood' is...?
questions.f: One discovered lie can make people doubt everything else you said.

questions.q: Who said: 'In the middle of difficulty lies opportunity'?
questions.f: Einstein's own career bloomed from a difficulty — he couldn't get a university job at first.

questions.q: Yogi Berra joked: 'The future ain't what it used to be.' What truth hides in the joke?
c: Things rarely turn out the way we once expected
questions.f: Berra's confusing sayings, called Yogi-isms, often carry surprising wisdom.

questions.q: Cervantes wrote: 'Sing away sorrow, cast away ___.'
questions.f: Cervantes wrote Don Quixote, often called the first modern novel.

questions.q: Who wrote: 'A book, too, can be a star, a living fire to lighten the darkness'?
questions.f: L'Engle's A Wrinkle in Time was rejected 26 times before winning the Newbery Medal.

questions.q: The word 'library' comes from a Latin root meaning...?
questions.f: From liber — in French, a librairie is actually a bookshop, not a library.

questions.q: Booker T. Washington measured success 'not so much by the position that one has reached' but by...?
c: the obstacles overcome along the way
questions.f: Washington was born enslaved and rose to advise presidents.

questions.q: Who said: 'Show me a family of readers, and I will show you the people who move the world'?
questions.f: Napoleon traveled with a portable library of hundreds of tiny books.

questions.q: Who said: 'What makes us human, I think, is an ability to ask questions'?
questions.f: Goodall's chimpanzee studies blurred old lines between humans and other animals.

questions.q: Seneca said: 'Luck is what happens when preparation meets ___.'
questions.f: Roman philosopher Seneca tutored an emperor and wrote about luck being earned.

questions.q: Bruce Lee said: 'Knowing is not enough, we must apply. Willing is not enough, we must do.' Meaning?
c: Knowledge and desire only count when turned into action
Learning is a waste of time
questions.f: Lee's martial art Jeet Kune Do was built on testing ideas in practice.

questions.q: Mark Twain is described as an author and 'humorist.' A 'humorist' is...?
c: a writer or speaker known for clever humor
questions.f: Twain earned worldwide fame doing comic lecture tours decades before stand-up comedy.

questions.q: Who said: 'A life is not important except in the impact it has on other lives'?
questions.f: Robinson broke baseball's color barrier in 1947; his number 42 is retired by every team.

questions.q: What does the Persian proverb 'The man who speaks the truth is always at ease' mean?
questions.f: With nothing to hide and no lies to track, an honest mind can rest.

questions.q: Shakespeare wrote: 'It is not in the stars to hold our destiny but in ___.'
questions.f: In Shakespeare's day many people truly believed the stars ruled their lives.

questions.q: The Chinese proverb 'He who returns from a journey is not the same as he who left' means travel changes us.
questions.f: New places and people reshape how we see our own home.

questions.q: In Shakespeare's 'to thine own self be true,' the old word 'thine' means...?
questions.f: 'Thou, thee, thy, thine' were once everyday English for 'you' and 'your.'

questions.q: Who said nature offers 'not only great curiosity, but great fulfillment'?
questions.f: Attenborough has narrated nature films across nine different decades of his life.

questions.q: Rowling said it is impossible to live without failing, 'unless you live so cautiously that you might as well not have ___ at all.'
questions.f: She spoke from experience — a dozen publishers rejected Harry Potter.

questions.q: The word 'autobiography' is built from Greek parts meaning...?
questions.f: From autos, bios, graphein — Anne Frank's diary is one of the most-read life stories ever.

questions.q: Who said: 'Be alone, that is the secret of invention; be alone, that is when ideas are born'?
questions.f: Tesla imagined entire machines in his head before building them.

questions.q: What does the Arabic proverb 'Every sun has to set' mean?
c: All things, good or bad, come to an end
questions.f: The comfort hidden inside: hard times must also end, like every setting sun.

questions.q: Angelou said: 'Do the best you can until you know better. Then when you know better, do ___.'
questions.f: Angelou recited a poem at a presidential inauguration in 1993.

questions.q: Who said: 'The path from dreams to success does exist. May you have the vision to find it and the courage to get on to it'?
questions.f: Chawla was the first woman of Indian origin in space; asteroids and hills on Mars honor her.

questions.q: Leonardo da Vinci wrote his notebooks in mirror writing that reads correctly when held to a mirror.
questions.f: Left-handed Leonardo wrote right to left — thousands of pages survive.

questions.q: Albert Pike said what we do for others 'is immortal.' 'Immortal' means...?
questions.f: From Latin in + mortalis, 'not subject to death.'

questions.q: Wilde said the smallest act of kindness is worth more than the grandest intention. Meaning?
c: A tiny good deed beats a big plan never done
questions.f: Psychologists confirm small kind acts measurably boost both giver and receiver.

questions.q: Socrates said: 'Education is the kindling of a flame, not the filling of a ___.'
questions.f: A vessel is a container — Socrates meant minds should be lit, not stuffed.

questions.q: Who said: 'If your dreams don't scare you, they are too small'?
questions.f: Sirleaf of Liberia was Africa's first elected female head of state and a Nobel Peace laureate.

questions.q: What does the Arabic proverb 'Ask the experienced rather than the learned' mean?
c: People who have done a thing teach better than books alone
questions.f: A sailor who has weathered storms knows things no textbook can tell.

questions.q: Van Gogh said: 'Great things are not done by impulse, but by a series of small things brought ___.'
questions.f: His masterpieces were built from thousands of tiny, deliberate brushstrokes.

questions.q: Tagore and Malala are Nobel laureates. 'Laureate' literally means...?
questions.f: Ancient Greeks crowned victors with laurel wreaths — the honor lives on in the word.

questions.q: Which Norwegian playwright wrote: 'A forest bird never wants a cage'?
questions.f: Ibsen is called the father of modern drama; the line celebrates wild freedom.

questions.q: Goethe said: 'Doubt grows with knowledge.' What does this mean?
c: The more you learn, the more questions you discover
questions.f: Scientists agree — every answered question uncovers several new ones.

questions.q: Plato said: 'The beginning is the most important part of the ___.'
questions.f: Plato founded the Academy, the school that gave 'academics' its name.

questions.q: Plato, famous for his sayings about learning, was a student of Socrates.
questions.f: The chain continues: Socrates taught Plato, Plato taught Aristotle.

questions.q: Pele is called a soccer 'legend.' The word 'legend' originally meant...?
c: things that ought to be read
questions.f: From Latin legenda — saints' life stories were required reading in medieval times.

questions.q: Who advised: 'Judge a man by his questions rather than by his answers'?
questions.f: Voltaire wrote so much that his collected works fill over 200 volumes.

questions.q: The Persian proverb says 'the rose and the thorn, and sorrow and gladness, are linked together.' Meaning?
c: Life mixes joys and hardships inseparably
questions.f: Persian poetry has paired roses and thorns as symbols for over a thousand years.

questions.q: Confucius said we learn wisdom by three methods: 'by reflection, imitation, and ___.'
questions.f: He called reflection the noblest method and experience the bitterest.

questions.q: Who said: 'If you want to fly, you have to give up the things that weigh you down'?
questions.f: Morrison was the first Black woman to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.

questions.q: Jane Goodall is a 'primatologist.' What does a primatologist study?
c: primates, such as apes and monkeys
questions.f: From Latin primus, 'first' — primates were ranked the 'first order' of mammals.

questions.q: Michelle Obama said: 'Don't ever ___ the importance you can have.' Which word completes it?
questions.f: To underestimate is to judge something as smaller than it really is.

questions.q: Which Roman emperor wrote that waking each morning is 'a precious privilege' — to be alive, to breathe, to think, to love?
questions.f: His private journal, Meditations, was never meant for publication — yet it became immortal.

questions.q: Who said: 'Imagination will often carry us to worlds that never were. But without it we go nowhere'?
questions.f: Sagan's TV series Cosmos carried 500 million viewers to those imagined worlds.

questions.q: Yogi Berra's famous directions: 'When you come to a fork in the road, ___ it.'
questions.f: The road to Berra's house looped, so both forks really did lead there.

questions.q: Aristotle: 'It is the mark of an educated mind to be able to entertain a thought without accepting it.' Here 'entertain' means...?
c: to consider or hold in mind
questions.f: From Latin inter + tenere, 'to hold among' — you host the idea without adopting it.

questions.q: 'Millions saw the apple fall, but Newton was the one who asked why.' What is Baruch's point?
c: Curiosity about ordinary things leads to discovery
questions.f: Newton's apple question led to his law of universal gravitation.

questions.q: Which Renaissance scholar said: 'When I get a little money I buy books; and if any is left, I buy food and clothes'?
questions.f: Erasmus of Rotterdam was Europe's most famous scholar — and its hungriest book buyer.

questions.q: Aristotle said: 'The whole is more than the sum of its parts.'
questions.f: A team, a song, or a sentence is more than its separate pieces — the idea founded systems science.

questions.q: Dickinson wrote: 'There is no frigate like a book to take us lands away.' A 'frigate' is...?
questions.f: Frigates were the speedsters of the sailing navy — her book outruns them all.

questions.q: Who wrote: 'You give but little when you give of your possessions. It is when you give of yourself that you truly give'?
questions.f: Gibran's book The Prophet has never gone out of print since 1923.

questions.q: Marlene Dietrich said: 'It is the friends you can call up at 4 a.m. that matter.' Meaning?
c: True friends help you at any hour
Call friends early in the morning
questions.f: The film star kept a famously short list of such friends — and treasured them.

questions.q: Emerson wrote: 'The creation of a thousand forests is in one ___.'
questions.f: One oak can drop 10,000 acorns in a single autumn.

questions.q: Who said some books are to be tasted, others swallowed, 'and some few to be chewed and digested'?
questions.f: Bacon, a founder of the scientific method, read exactly the way he experimented — deliberately.

questions.q: 'Manuscript' literally means...?
questions.f: From Latin manus + scribere — before printing, every single book was copied by hand.

questions.q: What does the Arabic proverb 'Trust in God, but tie up your camel' mean?
c: Hope for the best but still take sensible precautions
questions.f: The saying comes from a story of a traveler who lost his camel by trusting luck alone.

questions.q: Eleanor Roosevelt said: 'It is better to light a candle than curse the ___.'
questions.f: The motto was adopted by charities worldwide — do one small useful thing instead of complaining.

questions.q: Who said: 'Quality means doing it right when no one is looking'?
questions.f: Ford's assembly line demanded parts that fit perfectly, seen or unseen.

questions.q: Rabbi Heschel said: 'Wonder rather than doubt is the root of all knowledge.' Meaning?
c: Amazement, not suspicion, drives us to learn
questions.f: Einstein agreed — he called the mysterious 'the most beautiful thing we can experience.'

questions.q: An 'aphorism' is a short, wise saying.
questions.f: From Greek aphorizein, 'to mark off' — Hippocrates wrote a famous book of them.

questions.q: Who joked: 'I'm writing a book. I've got the page numbers done'?
questions.f: Wright delivers every joke in the same flat, sleepy voice — which makes them funnier.

questions.q: Steven Wright is called a 'deadpan' comedian. 'Deadpan' means...?
c: delivered with a completely expressionless face
questions.f: 'Pan' was old slang for the face — a 'dead pan' shows no life at all.

questions.q: 'The mediocre teacher tells. The good teacher explains. The great teacher ___.'
questions.f: William Arthur Ward's ladder ends with teachers who light a lifelong love of learning.

questions.q: 'Certain things catch your eye, but pursue only those that capture the heart.' This Native American proverb means...?
c: Chase what you truly love, not what merely looks shiny
questions.f: It is often shared as advice for choosing a life's path, not just possessions.

questions.q: Who said: 'Education is not preparation for life; education is life itself'?
questions.f: Dewey's Chicago 'laboratory school' let children learn by doing real projects.

questions.q: Educator Mary McLeod Bethune said: 'The whole world opened up to me when I learned to ___.'
questions.f: Bethune founded a college with $1.50 and faith — it still thrives in Florida today.

questions.q: An 'era' is...?
c: a long, distinct period of history
questions.f: Historians name eras after ideas, rulers, or even quotes — like the 'Space Age.'

questions.q: Who said: 'It marks a big step in your development when you realize that other people can help you do a better job than you could alone'?
questions.f: Carnegie gave away 90 percent of his fortune, building over 2,500 public libraries.

questions.q: The Sioux proverb 'With all things and in all things, we are relatives' teaches that...?
c: everything is connected, so we care for each other
questions.f: The Lakota phrase 'Mitakuye Oyasin' — all my relations — carries this worldview.

questions.q: Whitman wrote: 'O Captain! my Captain! our fearful trip is ___.'
questions.f: The poem mourns Abraham Lincoln, the fallen 'captain' of the American ship of state.

questions.q: The word 'poet' comes from a Greek word meaning 'maker.'
questions.f: From poietes — a poet literally 'makes' something new out of words.

questions.q: Which aviator said: 'A single act of kindness throws out roots in all directions'?
questions.f: Surprising but true — the record-setting pilot wrote often about kindness.

questions.q: The Filipino proverb 'While the blanket is short, learn how to bend' means...?
c: Adapt to what you have and make the best of it
questions.f: It is a beloved lesson in 'making do' passed down in Filipino families.

questions.q: Dr. Seuss wrote: 'Fill your house with stacks of books, in all the crannies and all the ___.'
questions.f: 'Nooks and crannies' — cozy corners and narrow cracks — have rhymed together for centuries.

questions.q: A 'triumph' is...?
questions.f: Victorious Roman generals paraded through Rome in a ceremony called a triumphus.

questions.q: Who said: 'Inspiration exists, but it has to find you working'?
questions.f: Picasso produced an estimated 50,000 artworks — inspiration found him constantly.

questions.q: Balzac said: 'Reading brings us unknown friends.' What does this mean?
c: Books introduce us to characters and minds we'd never meet
questions.f: Balzac wrote about 90 novels packed with over 2,000 characters.

questions.q: Astronomer Edwin Hubble said man 'explores the universe around him and calls the adventure ___.'
questions.f: The Hubble Space Telescope, named for him, has made over 1.5 million observations.

questions.q: Who said: 'Don't wish it were easier, wish you were better'?
questions.f: Rohn mentored many famous speakers — including Tony Robbins himself.

questions.q: Which rocket engineer joked: 'Research is what I'm doing when I don't know what I'm doing'?
questions.f: Von Braun led the team that built the Saturn V, the rocket that carried astronauts to the Moon.

questions.q: Einstein said: 'Any fool can know. The point is to ___.'
questions.f: He could recite few phone numbers but understood the fabric of space and time.

questions.q: 'The larger the island of knowledge, the longer the shoreline of wonder.' What does this mean?
c: The more you know, the more marvels you discover to explore
questions.f: Every scientific answer exposes a longer coastline of brand-new questions.

questions.q: John Dewey praised the 'audacity of imagination' behind great advances. 'Audacity' means...?
questions.f: From Latin audax, 'daring' — every big leap starts with an audacious idea.

questions.q: Who said: 'You can't wait for inspiration. You have to go after it with a club'?
questions.f: London forced himself to write 1,000 words every single day — club in hand.

questions.q: The phrase 'glass ceiling' describes an invisible barrier that unfairly blocks people from rising higher.
questions.f: CEO Indra Nooyi said the glass ceiling breaks when women help other women through it.

questions.q: Dolly Parton said: 'We cannot direct the wind, but we can adjust the ___.'
questions.f: Sailors really do reach any destination by trimming sails to whatever wind blows.

questions.q: The Irish proverb says the tongue 'weighs practically nothing, but few people can hold it.' Meaning?
c: Controlling what you say is surprisingly hard
questions.f: The tongue weighs about 60 grams — yet holding it defeats almost everyone.

questions.q: Tolkien wrote: 'The world is indeed full of peril.' 'Peril' means...?
questions.f: From Latin periculum — the same root gives us 'perilous' and even 'experiment.'

questions.q: Who wrote: 'Stories are light. Light is precious in a world so dark'?
questions.f: The line comes from her Newbery-winning The Tale of Despereaux.

questions.q: 'Learning is like rowing upstream: not to advance is to drop ___.' What completes this Chinese proverb?
questions.f: Stop rowing against a current and the river quietly carries you backward.

questions.q: 'Examine what is said, not who speaks.' What does this Arabic proverb teach?
c: Judge ideas by their merit, not the speaker's fame
questions.f: Scientists call the opposite mistake an 'appeal to authority.'

questions.q: Who said: 'The best thing about music is that it brings people together'?
questions.f: Cellist Yo-Yo Ma has performed on every continent — including for penguins in Antarctica.

questions.q: Beethoven urged musicians to force their way into art's secrets. 'Composer' literally means...?
questions.f: From Latin com + ponere, 'to place together' — notes assembled into music.

questions.q: Rudyard Kipling, author of The Jungle Book, was born in India.
questions.f: He was born in Bombay in 1865 and later became the youngest Literature Nobel winner.

questions.q: Which Russian novelist said: 'Everyone thinks of changing the world, but no one thinks of changing himself'?
questions.f: Tolstoy practiced what he preached, giving up wealth to live simply.

questions.q: Michelangelo warned the danger is not aiming too high and missing, but aiming too low 'and achieving our ___.'
questions.f: He aimed absurdly high — painting 500 square meters of ceiling almost single-handedly.

questions.q: Vivekananda said: 'The greatest sin is to think yourself weak.' What does this mean?
c: Believing you are helpless is the most damaging mistake
questions.f: He taught that confidence in yourself unlocks every other strength.

questions.q: Galileo was an astronomer. The Greek roots of 'astronomy' mean...?
questions.f: From astron + nomos — while 'astrology' swaps in logos and lost its science.

questions.q: Who said: 'Art is the only way to run away without leaving home'?
questions.f: Choreographer Tharp has created over 160 dances — each one an escape.

questions.q: Indira Gandhi said: 'The power to question is the basis of all human progress.' Meaning?
c: Daring to ask questions drives humanity forward
questions.f: She was India's first — and so far only — female prime minister.

questions.q: Socrates said: 'The only true wisdom is in knowing you know ___.'
questions.f: The Oracle at Delphi called him the wisest man — he said it was only because he admitted his ignorance.

questions.q: Socrates never wrote any books — we know his ideas through his students.
questions.f: Nearly everything we know of him comes from Plato's written dialogues.

questions.q: Sylvia Earle is a marine biologist. 'Marine' means...?
questions.f: From Latin mare, 'sea' — Earle has spent over 7,000 hours underwater.

questions.q: Who said: 'Don't think about making art, just get it done. Let everyone else decide if it's good or bad'?
questions.f: Warhol turned soup cans into museum art while critics argued — proving his point.

questions.q: Thomas J. Watson said: 'The way to succeed is to double your failure rate.' What does this mean?
c: Trying more, even failing more, speeds you toward success
questions.f: Watson built IBM on bold experiments — many flopped, a few changed the world.

questions.q: Blake wrote: 'To see a World in a Grain of Sand / And a Heaven in a Wild ___.'
questions.f: Blake hand-printed and painted his own poem books — few sold in his lifetime.

questions.q: 'Infinite' literally means...?
questions.f: From Latin in + finis, 'no boundary' — mathematicians only tamed infinity in the 1800s.

questions.q: Arnold Schwarzenegger said: 'Strength does not come from winning. Your struggles develop your strengths.' Meaning?
c: Effort against difficulty is what builds strength
questions.f: In weightlifting it is literally true — muscles grow from resistance, not ease.

questions.q: 'When spider webs unite, they can halt even a ___.' What completes this Ethiopian proverb?
questions.f: Spider silk really is, weight for weight, stronger than steel.

questions.q: Helen Keller, often quoted on optimism, earned a college degree.
questions.f: She graduated from Radcliffe in 1904 — the first deafblind person to earn a bachelor's degree.
