questions.q: Which of these was the first Indian-run bank founded during the Swadeshi years and still famous?
questions.f: Swadeshi enthusiasm in 1906 led Indian businessmen to launch banks, insurers and mills of their own.

questions.q: Which Indian revolutionary movement in Bengal took its name from a physical-culture society?
questions.f: Gymnasiums and reading rooms doubled as meeting places when open politics was restricted.

questions.q: Which 1919 protest tool did Gandhi use nationwide for the first time against the Rowlatt Act?
questions.f: Shops shut and work stopped across cities on 6 April 1919, an early show of coordinated action.

questions.q: A private dairy called Polson, a farmers' refusal to supply milk in 1946, and advice from Sardar Patel led to the founding of what?
questions.f: The Kaira district union began with two villages and grew into a movement covering millions of farmers.

questions.q: Who was the first chairman of the farmers' union that became Amul?
questions.f: A farmer-leader rather than a technician, he recruited Kurien and kept him for decades.

questions.q: Operation Flood was partly financed by selling which donated commodity inside India?
questions.f: Kurien insisted the aid be sold, not given away, so the money could build Indian dairies.

questions.q: Which company, founded in 1968, is regarded as India's first software services firm?
questions.f: Its early work included punch-card processing for Burroughs machines, long before software was fashionable.

questions.q: The Tata Indica of 1998 mattered because it was India's first what?
questions.f: Designed and engineered in India, it proved an Indian firm could build a car from a blank sheet.

questions.q: Ratan Tata said the idea for the Nano came from seeing what?
c: A family of four on a scooter
questions.f: He sketched a safer four-wheeled alternative, at first drawing something closer to a covered scooter.

questions.q: Air India's Maharajah mascot was devised by which company insider in the 1940s?
questions.f: He worked with artist Umesh Rao, and insisted the character be a cheeky host, not a real royal.

questions.q: India's first rocket launch in 1963 used a building at Thumba that had been what?
questions.f: The bishop handed over St Mary Magdalene church; the prayer room became the design office.

questions.q: Which Indian satellite was famously photographed being moved on a bullock cart in 1981?
questions.f: The cart was chosen because it had no metal or magnets to interfere with the antenna tests.

questions.q: India's Mars mission needed a long series of orbit-raising burns because of what?
questions.f: The PSLV could not fling it straight at Mars, so engineers used Earth's gravity like a slingshot.

questions.q: Vikram Sarabhai founded the Physical Research Laboratory in 1947 inside which building?
questions.f: Indian space science began in an Ahmedabad house called the Retreat, funded by his family.

questions.q: India's oldest working steam locomotive, a Guinness record holder, is named what?
questions.f: Built in 1855, she still hauls occasional heritage runs out of Delhi.

questions.q: Navapur railway station is unusual because it lies in how many states?
questions.f: The platform straddles the Maharashtra-Gujarat border, so announcements and even prices can differ along it.

questions.q: Which Indian railway station holds the record for the longest name?
questions.f: Its 28 letters barely fit on the station board on the Andhra-Tamil Nadu border.

questions.q: Which Indian train is famous for carrying passengers with no ticket at all?
questions.f: Run by the dam authority as a public service, it has carried villagers free for decades.

questions.q: The Matheran Hill Railway is notable for using which very narrow track gauge?
questions.f: Its tiny carriages climb from Neral to a hill station where motor vehicles are banned.

questions.q: The song sequence Chaiyya Chaiyya was filmed on top of a moving train on which line?
questions.f: Dancers were harnessed out of sight while the train climbed through the hills above Ooty.

questions.q: Which was the first Indian film ever submitted for the foreign-language Academy Award?
questions.f: It reached the final five and reportedly lost by a single vote to an Italian film.

questions.q: Which Indian epic film was in production for over a decade before releasing in 1960?
questions.f: One battle sequence used real regiments, and part of the film was shot in colour and part in black and white.

questions.q: The Duleep Trophy in Indian cricket is named after a prince related to which other trophy's namesake?
questions.f: Duleepsinhji was Ranjitsinhji's nephew, and like his uncle he played Test cricket for England.

questions.q: Which cricketer captained India in Tests and had earlier played Test cricket for England?
questions.f: He scored a century for England against Australia, then led India on its 1946 tour.

questions.q: Who captained India in its very first Test match, in 1932?
questions.f: He once hit eleven sixes against a touring MCC side, which made him a household name.

questions.q: India's first Test victory, in 1952, came at which venue?
questions.f: Vinoo Mankad took twelve wickets in the match, and Vijay Hazare was captain.

questions.q: India's first overseas Test series win, in 1968, was achieved in which country?
questions.f: Mansur Ali Khan Pataudi led the side, having become the youngest Test captain in history at 21.

questions.q: Bhausaheb Nimbalkar's 443 not out in 1948 is remembered because the innings ended how?
questions.f: He was nine short of Bradman's first-class record when the opposition conceded the game.

questions.q: A method of running out a non-striker who leaves early is named after which Indian cricketer?
questions.f: He did it in a 1947 Test in Australia, entirely within the laws, and the name stuck for eighty years.

questions.q: Which Indian Test centurion had two sons who also played Test cricket for India?
questions.f: Mohinder and Surinder Amarnath both played for India, and Mohinder starred in the 1983 World Cup.

questions.q: India's last Olympic gold medal in hockey came at which Games?
questions.f: It ended a run of eight golds that began in Amsterdam in 1928.

questions.q: Which Indian hockey player won three Olympic gold medals between 1948 and 1956?
questions.f: He scored five goals in the 1952 final, still a record for an Olympic hockey final.

questions.q: Who became the first Indian to win the All England badminton title?
questions.f: He won in 1980; Gopichand became the second Indian champion twenty-one years later.

questions.q: Leander Paes's 1996 Olympic bronze was special because it was India's first individual medal in how long?
questions.f: The last had been K. D. Jadhav's wrestling bronze in 1952.

questions.q: Who won India's first Paralympic gold medal, in 1972?
questions.f: A former army boxer, he won the 50-metre freestyle swim in a world-record time.

questions.q: The Mitticool refrigerator, which needs no electricity, is made mainly of what?
questions.f: A potter from Gujarat invented it, using evaporation through terracotta walls to keep food cool.

questions.q: The Jaipur Foot became world famous as a low-cost what?
questions.f: It is rugged enough to walk barefoot, squat and climb trees, and is often fitted the same day.

questions.q: Aravind Eye Hospital in Madurai became a global case study for its approach to what?
questions.f: Paying patients subsidise free ones, and surgeons work two tables at once to save minutes.

questions.q: Bindeshwar Pathak founded a movement famous for spreading affordable what?
questions.f: Sulabh's twin-pit design needs little water and turns waste into compost and gas.

questions.q: Which household shoe brand, hugely familiar in India, was actually founded in Europe?
questions.f: Founded in Zlin in what is now the Czech Republic, it built a whole company town near Kolkata.

questions.q: The 1982 Asian Games in Delhi introduced India's first sporting mascot, named what?
questions.f: Appu the elephant was so popular that a Delhi amusement park was named after him.

questions.q: Viswanathan Anand first became a world chess champion in which year?
questions.f: He won the FIDE knockout title in Tehran, then unified the crown in 2007.

questions.q: Koneru Humpy made history in 2002 by becoming the youngest woman ever to earn which title?
questions.f: She was 15, and her father had left his teaching job to coach her full time.

questions.q: Anil Kumble finished his Test career with how many wickets, the most by an Indian?
questions.f: He bowled leg-spin without huge turn, relying on accuracy, bounce and relentless pressure.

questions.q: The Amul girl's cartoons are drawn by an outside agency that has kept the account since 1966.
questions.f: The daCunha family firm has produced them for nearly sixty years, usually within a day of the news.

questions.q: Which Indian firm supplied much of the steel for India's early railway workshops and later made typewriters and locks?
questions.f: Godrej's first product was a lock, and its springless lock design was patented in the 1890s.

questions.q: Which ISRO mission was the first Indian spacecraft to be recovered after re-entry?
questions.f: The 2007 Space Capsule Recovery Experiment splashed down in the Bay of Bengal after twelve days in orbit.

questions.q: Which Indian company name is short for a business that once refined vegetable oils?
questions.f: Western India Palm Refined Oils became Wipro; the founder pivoted to computers in the 1970s.

questions.q: India's dabbawalas are often cited for accuracy rates studied by which institution?
questions.f: Their coded lid symbols work for a workforce where many carriers read little printed text.

questions.q: India's Chandrayaan-1 found evidence of water using an instrument built by which partner?
questions.f: The Moon Mineralogy Mapper flew as a guest instrument, and its data made headlines worldwide.

questions.q: Which Indian car, launched in 1983, was made by a joint venture with a Japanese firm?
questions.f: Suzuki's partnership put a small, light, fuel-efficient car into millions of Indian driveways.

questions.q: The name Maruti, used by India's best-known car maker, refers to what?
questions.f: Maruti means born of the wind, a fitting name for something meant to be light and quick.

questions.q: The name Vande Bharat, given to India's fast trains, means what?
questions.f: It echoes Vande Mataram, where vande means I bow or I praise.

questions.q: The name Aadhaar, India's identity system, means what?
questions.f: The word suggests a base that other services can be built on top of.

questions.q: The word dabbawala breaks down into parts meaning what?
questions.f: Dabba is a tin box and -wala means one connected with, so the name describes the job exactly.

questions.q: The name Mangal, used for India's Mars mission, has which second meaning in Indian languages?
questions.f: Mangal names both the planet and good fortune, which is why weddings are called mangal karya.

questions.q: The English word algorism first meant what?
questions.f: It comes from al-Khwarizmi, whose book explained the Indian decimal system; later it gave us algorithm.

questions.q: The English words zero and cipher are doublets, both tracing to a word translating which Sanskrit term?
questions.f: Shunya, empty, became Arabic sifr, which travelled into Latin twice and split into two English words.

questions.q: The artificial sweetener name saccharin shares an ancient root with which Indian sugar product?
questions.f: Sanskrit sharkara gave Greek sakkharon, Latin saccharum, and, by another road, Portuguese jagara.

questions.q: Muslin, the cloth most associated with Dhaka, actually takes its name from which city?
questions.f: The finest Dhaka muslin was so fine that a whole sari could reportedly pass through a ring.

questions.q: The correct plural of mongoose is mongooses because the word is not related to what?
questions.f: From Marathi mungus; English ears heard a goose that was never there.

questions.q: The phrase curry favour has nothing to do with food. Its curry originally meant what?
questions.f: From Old French correier, to curry a horse, plus Favel, a chestnut horse in a medieval poem.

questions.q: The word samosa traces back to a Persian word describing what?
questions.f: From sanbusag; the snack travelled along trade routes from Central Asia into India.

questions.q: The dish name biryani comes from a Persian word meaning what?
questions.f: From biryan; the rice is often part-fried or the meat browned before the layers are sealed and cooked.

questions.q: The word tandoor has a distant ancestor in which ancient language's word for oven?
questions.f: Akkadian tinuru travelled through Persian tanur to Hindi tandoor and then into English menus.

questions.q: The word howdah, an elephant seat, came into English from which language family?
questions.f: From Arabic haudaj, a camel litter; Indian usage moved it from camels to elephants.

questions.q: The sola topee, that classic pith helmet, takes its first word from what?
questions.f: Sola is the spongy plant used for the pith; many people mishear it as solar.

questions.q: The word purdah comes from a Persian word meaning what?
questions.f: From pardah; English still uses in purdah for anyone kept out of public view before an announcement.

questions.q: The word chowkidar, a watchman, is built on a root meaning what?
questions.f: From chauki, a guard post; the -dar ending means holder, as in zamindar, landholder.

questions.q: The script name Devanagari means what?
c: Of the city of the gods
questions.f: Deva, god, plus nagari, of the city; the horizontal line across the top is called the shirorekha.

questions.q: The language name Urdu comes from a Turkic word meaning what?
questions.f: From ordu, an army camp, the same root as English horde; the language grew as zaban-e-urdu, camp speech.

questions.q: The state name Bihar comes from a word meaning what?
questions.f: From vihara; the region was dotted with Buddhist monasteries, and the name simply stuck.

questions.q: The state name Meghalaya means what?
questions.f: Coined by a geographer in the 20th century; Mawsynram there is among the wettest places on Earth.

questions.q: Arunachal Pradesh's name describes it as the land of what?
questions.f: India's sunrise reaches its eastern edge well before it reaches Gujarat, on the same clock.

questions.q: The name Jharkhand means what?
questions.f: Jhar means bush or forest and khand a region; the state holds much of India's coal and iron.

questions.q: The word Deccan comes from a Sanskrit word meaning what?
questions.f: From dakshina, south; the same word gives dakshin in many Indian languages.

questions.q: The Coromandel Coast takes its name from a phrase meaning what?
questions.f: From Cholamandalam; European traders reshaped it into Coromandel on their charts.

questions.q: The Malabar Coast's name begins with a word meaning what?
questions.f: From Malayalam mala, hill, the same element as in Malayalam itself, the language of the hill country.

questions.q: The Nilgiri Hills' name means what?
questions.f: Nila, blue, plus giri, mountain; the kurinji flower blooming en masse can genuinely tint the slopes.

questions.q: The English word serendipity was coined from an old name for which island?
questions.f: Serendip came from Sanskrit Simhaladvipa through Arabic; Horace Walpole invented the word in 1754.

questions.q: The name Singapore comes from Sanskrit words meaning what?
questions.f: From simha, lion, plus pura, city; Sanskrit place names spread across Southeast Asia with Indian trade.

questions.q: Cambodia's name derives from which Sanskrit-linked name?
questions.f: Its old kingdom of Kambujadesa took its name from a legendary ancestor, Kambu.

questions.q: The old Thai capital Ayutthaya was named after which Indian city?
questions.f: Southeast Asian kings often took Indian epic names to link their courts to the Ramayana.

questions.q: The Sanskrit word dvipa, meaning island, literally breaks down as what?
questions.f: Dvi, two, plus ap, water: an island has water on both sides, as in Maladvipa, the Maldives.

questions.q: The word gurdwara means what?
questions.f: From guru plus dwara, door; the same dwara appears in Haridwar and shares a root with English door.

questions.q: The word Sikh comes from a root meaning what?
questions.f: From Sanskrit shishya through Pali sikkha, learning; the word describes a lifelong student.

questions.q: The word stupa comes from a root meaning what?
questions.f: The earliest stupas were literally mounds; the shape later became stylised across Asia into pagodas.

questions.q: The word mandala means what?
questions.f: The same root gives Cholamandalam, the Chola realm, from which Europeans made Coromandel.

questions.q: The word Buddha is a title meaning what?
questions.f: From budh, to wake or know; bodhi, the tree's name, means awakening from the same root.

questions.q: The word Jain comes from a term meaning what?
questions.f: From jina, one who has conquered, referring to victory over one's own desires.

questions.q: The word Ganga is thought to come from a root meaning what?
questions.f: From gam, to go, describing a swift-moving river; the doubled form suggests going and going.

questions.q: The river name Brahmaputra means what?
questions.f: Putra means son; in Assam the same river is simply called Luit or Burhaluit, the old one.

questions.q: The Indian English word cutcha is the opposite of pukka. What does it mean?
questions.f: From kachcha, unripe; a cutcha road is unmetalled and a cutcha house is of mud, not baked brick.

questions.q: Which cloth word is often confused with cashmere but actually comes from an English village name?
questions.f: Kersey in Suffolk gave its name to a coarse woollen; the similar sound caused centuries of mix-ups.

questions.q: The word khadi comes from a term describing cloth that is what?
questions.f: From khaddar, coarse homespun; Gandhi made it a badge of self-reliance rather than a fashion.

questions.q: The word atoll, sometimes assumed Indian, actually came from a language of which islands?
questions.f: From Dhivehi atolu; Charles Darwin helped popularise the word in English through his coral reef studies.

questions.q: The English word rice probably traces back to which south Indian word?
questions.f: Tamil arisi may lie behind Greek oryza, which travelled through Latin and Old French into English.

questions.q: The gemstone name opal is thought by many etymologists to come from a Sanskrit word meaning what?
questions.f: Sanskrit upala, stone, may have become Greek opallios and then Latin opalus.

questions.q: The word musk traces back to a Sanskrit word originally meaning what?
questions.f: From muska, a little pouch, describing the gland from which the scent was taken.

questions.q: Which pair of English words are both borrowings from Indian languages rather than Persian?
questions.f: Chutney is Hindi and cheetah Sanskrit; bazaar, durbar, purdah, sepoy, khaki and cummerbund are all Persian.

questions.q: The word pundit had a special 19th-century meaning in India, describing what?
questions.f: Indian explorers disguised as pilgrims mapped forbidden territory, and the Survey called them pundits.

questions.q: The word Dravidian, for a family of south Indian languages, was popularised by which scholar?
questions.f: His 1856 comparative grammar showed Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam form their own family.

questions.q: The language name Pali means what?
questions.f: It came to mean the canon's text itself, distinguishing scripture from commentary.

questions.q: The word yaan in Chandrayaan comes from a root meaning what?
questions.f: From ya, to go, giving yaana, a vehicle; the same root appears in Mangalyaan and Gaganyaan.

questions.q: The name Gaganyaan, India's crewed spaceflight programme, begins with a word meaning what?
questions.f: Gagana means sky or heavens, so the name reads sky vehicle.

questions.q: The name of the Chandrayaan-3 lander, Vikram, is a word meaning valour or a stride.
questions.f: It honours Vikram Sarabhai, and the word also lies behind the title Vikramaditya.

questions.q: The word rickshaw, common in Indian English, is actually shortened from a word in which language?
questions.f: From jinrikisha, meaning human-powered vehicle; the cycle rickshaw was a later Indian adaptation.

questions.q: The word palanquin, a covered litter, traces back to a Sanskrit word meaning what?
questions.f: From palyanka, a couch; Portuguese palanquim carried it into English.

questions.q: A cricket-loving prince, a Bombay mill fortune and India's oldest surviving cricket club point to which city's Test ground opened in 1974?
questions.f: Built in months after a row with the older Brabourne Stadium, it later hosted the 2011 World Cup final.

questions.q: The word chit fund, a savings scheme common in India, uses chit in which older sense?
c: A written slip drawn by lot
questions.f: Members put in money and a slip is drawn to decide who collects, from Hindi chitthi, a note.

questions.q: What do you slide around on a desk to move the pointer on a computer screen?
questions.f: Many computer mice have a tiny light underneath that watches every move they make.

questions.q: You use the keyboard to type letters into a computer.
questions.f: Most keyboards have over 100 keys, including letters, numbers, and arrows.

questions.q: Which part of a computer shows you pictures and words?
questions.f: A computer screen is also called a monitor.

questions.q: Which machine puts words and pictures from a computer onto paper?
questions.f: Printers squirt tiny drops of ink onto the paper faster than your eye can see.

questions.q: The word 'laptop' means a computer that fits on your…?
questions.f: It is called a laptop because you can rest it on your lap — lap + top!

questions.q: A password is a special word that should be kept…?
questions.f: A password works like a key — it opens your account, so only you should know it.

questions.q: A computer mouse is a real live animal.
questions.f: A computer mouse is a tool for pointing — it got its name because early ones had a long tail-like cord!

questions.q: What lets you see and talk to Grandma on a screen even when she is far away?
questions.f: Video calls send your picture and voice across the world in about one second.

questions.q: The word 'app' is short for…?
questions.f: An app is a little program — games, drawing tools, and maps on a tablet are all apps.

questions.q: In his video games, what is Mario famous for doing?
questions.f: Mario jumps so much that in his very first game he was called 'Jumpman'!

questions.q: In the game Pac-Man, what does Pac-Man love to eat?
questions.f: Pac-Man munches dots in a maze while colorful ghosts chase him around.

questions.q: If a gadget is 'wireless', what does it work without?
questions.f: Wireless gadgets send invisible radio waves through the air instead of using cables.

questions.q: What should you do to your work on a computer so it is not lost?
questions.f: Saving puts a copy of your work into the computer's memory so you can open it again later.

questions.q: What is it called when you press a mouse button once?
questions.f: The word 'click' sounds just like the little noise the mouse button makes.

questions.q: A robot vacuum can find its own way back to its charger.
questions.f: Robot vacuums drive around a room cleaning the floor with nobody pushing them.

questions.q: What do we call a letter that is sent from one computer to another?
questions.f: An email can travel around the whole world in just a few seconds.

questions.q: If you are 'online', your computer is connected to the…?
questions.f: Being online means your computer can reach websites, videos, and friends far away.

questions.q: What gives a phone or tablet power when it is not plugged in?
questions.f: The battery stores electricity, which is why gadgets need charging when it runs low.

questions.q: The small pictures you tap on a screen to open games and tools are called…?
questions.f: 'Icon' means a little picture — each one is a door into a different app.

questions.q: Which button fixes the very last mistake you made on a computer?
questions.f: Undo is like a tiny time machine — it makes your last change disappear.

questions.q: What do you wear on your ears to hear a computer without bothering others?
questions.f: Headphones put two tiny speakers right next to your ears.

questions.q: The little arrow that moves on the screen when you move the mouse is called the…?
questions.f: The cursor shows exactly where your next click or letter will land.

questions.q: Robots are machines that people build.
questions.f: Every robot was designed and built by people — robots do not grow or hatch!

questions.q: When you 'download' a game, what are you doing?
questions.f: Downloading copies a game or file from the internet onto your own tablet or computer.

questions.q: Which part of a computer listens to your voice?
questions.f: A microphone turns your voice into signals a computer can understand.

questions.q: Which key on the keyboard is the longest?
questions.f: The space bar is extra long so either thumb can tap it to make spaces between words.

questions.q: On a computer, what do you keep your files inside, just like papers at school?
questions.f: Computer folders are named after the paper folders people keep in filing cabinets.

questions.q: What do you hold in your hands to play games on a console?
questions.f: Game controllers have buttons and little sticks that tell the game what to do.

questions.q: The name you pick for yourself in a game or website is called your…?
questions.f: A username is like a nickname that tells the computer who is playing.

questions.q: What does the camera on a phone do?
questions.f: Phone cameras save your pictures as files you can look at again and again.

questions.q: Which part of a computer makes the sound come out?
questions.f: Speakers wiggle the air very fast, and those wiggles reach your ears as sound.

questions.q: The 'web' on the internet is named after a web made by which animal?
questions.f: Like a spider's web, the World Wide Web is full of threads — links joining pages together.

questions.q: What do we call the moving pictures you watch on a screen?
questions.f: A video is really lots of still pictures shown super fast, one after another.

questions.q: A 'keyboard' gets its name because it is a board covered with…?
questions.f: Each key sends a different letter, number, or command to the computer.

questions.q: Which button removes something you do not want anymore?
questions.f: Deleted files often go to a trash can on the screen first, in case you change your mind.

questions.q: Someone who plays a lot of video games is called a gamer.
questions.f: Gamers can play together online even when they live in different countries.

questions.q: What can you use to find a website about your favorite animal?
questions.f: You type words into a search engine, and it hunts through millions of pages for you.

questions.q: A person who writes instructions for computers is called a…?
questions.f: Programmers are also called coders, because the instructions they write are called code.

questions.q: What do you plug into a phone to fill its battery back up?
questions.f: A charger pours electricity into the battery, a bit like filling a water bottle.

questions.q: On a screen, a list of choices you can pick from is called a…?
questions.f: It is called a menu just like at a restaurant — a list of things to choose from!

questions.q: Computers need electricity to work.
questions.f: Every computer runs on electricity, from a wall plug or from a battery inside.

questions.q: If a picture on the screen is too small, what can you do to see it better?
questions.f: Zooming in makes things on the screen look bigger, like using a magnifying glass.

questions.q: If you press 'mute' during a video, what happens?
questions.f: Mute silences the sound — press it again and the sound comes back.

questions.q: A drone is a machine that can fly.
questions.f: Drones are flying robots — some take pictures from the sky, and some deliver packages.

questions.q: Where do new emails wait for you to read them?
questions.f: The inbox is like a mailbox that lives inside your computer.

questions.q: Which button do you press to turn a computer on?
questions.f: The power button usually has a little circle-and-line symbol on it.

questions.q: In a video game, your best score ever is called your…?
questions.f: Old arcade machines showed the high score to dare the next player to beat it.

questions.q: Pressing pause erases your game forever.
questions.f: Pausing only freezes the game so you can come back right where you left off.

questions.q: You can carry a laptop computer around with you.
questions.f: Laptops fold shut like a book, so people carry them to school, work, and cafes.

questions.q: The big picture behind the icons on a screen is called the…?
questions.f: It is called wallpaper because it decorates your screen like paper decorates a wall.

questions.q: When you send a photo from your device onto the internet, you…?
questions.f: Upload means sending up to the internet; download means bringing something back to you.

questions.q: In big factories, what job do robot arms often do?
questions.f: Robot arms can weld and lift car parts all day without getting tired.

questions.q: Typing your username and password to enter a game is called…?
questions.f: Logging in tells the computer it is really you, so it opens your own stuff.

questions.q: What can a 3D printer make?
questions.f: 3D printers build objects layer by layer, like stacking super-thin pancakes.

questions.q: The tiny smiley faces and hearts you add to messages are called…?
questions.f: There are thousands of emoji, from laughing faces to pizza slices and rockets.

questions.q: What can a smart speaker do when you ask it a question?
questions.f: Smart speakers listen for a special wake word, then try to help with what you asked.

questions.q: On a computer, 'copy' means making a new version that is exactly the…?
questions.f: You can copy words or pictures and the original stays right where it was.

questions.q: After copying something, which command puts it in a new place?
questions.f: Copy and paste are named after the old way of fixing pages with scissors and glue.

questions.q: You can play video games on some phones.
questions.f: Phones are little computers, so millions of people use them to play games.

questions.q: Turning a computer off and then on again is called…?
questions.f: Restarting gives the computer a fresh start and often fixes small problems.

questions.q: How do you tell a tablet what to do?
questions.f: Tablet screens can feel exactly where your finger taps and swipes.

questions.q: In the game Minecraft, what do players use to build things?
questions.f: Almost everything in Minecraft, even the sun, is made of squares and blocks.

questions.q: Moving a webpage up or down to see more of it is called…?
questions.f: The word comes from paper scrolls, which people rolled up and down to read long ago.

questions.q: Which key do you hold to type a CAPITAL letter?
questions.f: Hold Shift and press A, and you get a big A instead of a little one.

questions.q: What does a spell-checker look for in your writing?
questions.f: Spell-checkers often draw a squiggly red line under a word that looks wrong.

questions.q: What does autocorrect try to do while you type?
questions.f: Autocorrect guesses the word you meant — but sometimes its guesses are very funny.

questions.q: The little character or picture that stands for you in a game is your…?
questions.f: You can often dress up your avatar with fun hats, hair, and outfits.

questions.q: What can a map app on a phone help you find?
questions.f: Map apps use signals from space satellites to work out exactly where you are.

questions.q: When you finish a level in a video game, what usually comes next?
questions.f: Games get a little harder at each level so players keep learning new tricks.

questions.q: The first page you see when you visit a website is called its…?
questions.f: A homepage is like the front door of a website — it helps you find everything else.

questions.q: What are the robot cars that drive around on Mars called?
questions.f: Mars rovers are robots — people on Earth send them instructions across space.

questions.q: A smartwatch is like a tiny computer you wear on your…?
questions.f: Some smartwatches can count your steps, show messages, and even make calls.

questions.q: Turning a computer off and on again can sometimes fix a problem.
questions.f: Restarting clears out little mix-ups — it is the most famous computer fix of all.

questions.q: The main screen you see first on a computer is called the…?
questions.f: It is called the desktop because it works like the top of a desk where you lay things out.

questions.q: Where do deleted files go first on many computers?
questions.f: Files wait in the trash bin for a while, so you can rescue them if you deleted them by mistake.

questions.q: A photo you take of yourself with a phone is called a…?
questions.f: Most phones have a camera on the front just for taking selfies.

questions.q: The big game machines you play standing up at a fun center are called…?
questions.f: Long ago, kids lined up with coins to play arcade machines like Pac-Man.

questions.q: Which buttons make a tablet's sound louder or quieter?
questions.f: Volume comes from a word for 'amount' — the amount of sound you hear.

questions.q: 'The net' is a short nickname for the…?
questions.f: People shorten 'internet' to 'the net' because it connects computers like a giant net.

questions.q: A computer does its jobs by following…?
questions.f: Computers only do what their instructions say — they cannot guess what you meant.

questions.q: Writing special instructions to tell a computer what to do is called…?
questions.f: Kids can start coding by snapping picture blocks together on the screen.

questions.q: Besides letters, what else can you type with a keyboard?
questions.f: The number keys sit in a row above the letters, and many keyboards have extra ones on the side.

questions.q: A book you read on a screen instead of paper is called an…?
questions.f: One small e-reader can hold thousands of e-books — a whole library in your backpack.

questions.q: What can friends do together online even when they live far apart?
questions.f: Online games connect players' computers so everyone sees the same game world.

questions.q: The soft mat that a computer mouse slides around on is called a…?
questions.f: A mousepad gives the mouse a smooth, comfy surface so the pointer moves without jumping.

questions.q: Some fun robots are built to look and act like which pet?
questions.f: Robot dogs can walk, wag, and do tricks — but they never need feeding!

questions.q: A computer can play music and songs.
questions.f: Computers can store thousands of songs and play them through speakers or headphones.

questions.q: The sound a phone makes when someone calls you is its…?
questions.f: It is called a ringtone because old phones really rang a metal bell inside.

questions.q: A webcam lets other people see you during a video call.
questions.f: A webcam is a little camera that sends live video across the internet.

questions.q: Touching the screen quickly one time with your finger is called a…?
questions.f: A tap on a touchscreen works just like a click with a mouse.

questions.q: What does the checkout machine scan at the store when it beeps?
questions.f: The black and white stripes of a barcode tell the computer what the item is and its price.

questions.q: The helper inside a phone that you can talk to is called a voice…?
questions.f: Voice assistants can set timers, answer questions, and tell jokes when you ask.

questions.q: You should tell everyone in your class your password.
questions.f: Passwords are secrets — share them only with a parent or guardian who helps keep you safe.

questions.q: Which of these is a computer small enough to hold in one hand?
questions.f: A smartphone is a real computer — it just fits in a pocket.

questions.q: In a video game, what do the words 'game over' mean?
questions.f: 'Game over' appeared in old arcade games — but you can almost always play again!

questions.q: An old game console at home usually connects to which machine so you can play?
questions.f: Consoles send their pictures to the TV screen, turning it into a game world.

questions.q: A password like '1234' is a bad idea because it is…?
questions.f: Strong passwords mix letters and numbers so they are much harder to guess.

questions.q: Robots get bored when they do the same job again and again.
questions.f: Robots have no feelings, so they can repeat a task thousands of times without getting bored.

questions.q: What covers the front of a phone so you can see the apps?
questions.f: Phone screens use extra-tough glass, but a case still helps when phones go flying.

questions.q: In some restaurants, what job do rolling robots do?
questions.f: Food-carrying robots roll between tables and beep politely so people move aside.

questions.q: A little lightning bolt on the battery picture means the phone is…?
questions.f: The lightning bolt means electricity is flowing in and filling up the battery.

questions.q: Computers help traffic lights know when to change color.
questions.f: City computers time the lights so cars and walkers each get their safe turn.

questions.q: 'Double-click' means pressing the mouse button how?
questions.f: A quick double-click is the classic way to open a file or folder.

questions.q: What does a fitness tracker on your wrist count as you walk?
questions.f: A tiny motion sensor inside feels each step your body takes.

questions.q: What is inside robot toys that makes their parts move?
questions.f: Little electric motors spin, and gears turn that spinning into walking or rolling.

questions.q: What does the little clock on a computer screen show you?
questions.f: Computer clocks keep time even when the computer is turned off, thanks to a tiny battery.

questions.q: The stick you tilt to steer in some video games is called a…?
questions.f: Joysticks came from airplane controls before they became game controls.

questions.q: In many computer games, what do the arrow keys make your character do?
questions.f: The four arrow keys point up, down, left, and right — perfect for steering.

questions.q: 'Screen time' means the time you spend…?
questions.f: Balancing screen time with outside play keeps both your brain and body happy.

questions.q: A calculator is a small computer that helps you with…?
questions.f: Calculators can add huge numbers in less than a blink.

questions.q: A 'notebook computer' is another name for a…?
questions.f: It is called a notebook because it folds open and shut like a paper notebook.

questions.q: In many games, what do you earn by collecting coins or stars?
questions.f: In old arcade games, players chased points because there was no way to win — only to score!

questions.q: What is the special pen for drawing on a tablet screen called?
questions.f: Long ago, 'stylus' meant a pointed tool Romans used to write on wax tablets.

questions.q: PlayStation and Nintendo Switch are kinds of game…?
questions.f: A console is a machine made especially for playing video games.

questions.q: The emoji of a face laughing with tears usually means something is very…?
questions.f: The laughing-with-tears face is one of the most used emoji in the whole world.

questions.q: The download arrow on a screen usually points down.
questions.f: Down for download, up for upload — the arrows show which way the file is traveling.

questions.q: What kind of robot helper is attached to the outside of the space station?
questions.f: The space station's long robot arm can grab visiting spaceships and move astronauts around.

questions.q: What does the Caps Lock key do to your letters?
questions.f: Caps Lock stays on until you press it again — WHICH IS WHY TYPING CAN LOOK LIKE THIS.

questions.q: How many ghosts chase Pac-Man around his maze?
questions.f: The four ghosts even have names — Blinky, Pinky, Inky, and Clyde.

questions.q: When a computer is in 'sleep mode', what is it doing?
questions.f: Sleep mode saves power but remembers everything, so the computer wakes up fast.

questions.q: Which animal is the mascot of the kids' coding tool Scratch?
questions.f: In Scratch, kids snap colorful blocks together to make the orange cat move and dance.

questions.q: What does a timer on a phone do?
questions.f: When the countdown reaches zero, the phone rings to tell you time is up.

questions.q: What is the name of Mario's brother?
questions.f: Luigi wears green, while his brother Mario wears red.

questions.q: Pressing the camera button during a call lets people…?
questions.f: Turning on the camera changes a voice call into a video call.

questions.q: What gives a solar-powered calculator its energy?
questions.f: A tiny solar panel turns light into the little bit of electricity a calculator needs.

questions.q: What does a lock screen do for a phone?
questions.f: The lock screen asks for a code, fingerprint, or face before letting anyone in.

questions.q: What does a robot lawn mower cut?
questions.f: Robot mowers trim the lawn in little bites every day, all by themselves.

questions.q: Where do you go on a tablet to get new apps and games?
questions.f: App stores hold millions of apps — many of them are free.

questions.q: What does clicking the X at the corner of a window do?
questions.f: The X is the universal 'goodbye' button for windows on a screen.

questions.q: A 'backup' is an extra…?
questions.f: If something happens to a computer, a backup copy keeps the work safe somewhere else.

questions.q: Many cars have a camera and screen to help drivers see while going…?
questions.f: The backup camera turns on automatically and shows what is behind the car.

questions.q: In an online game, where can you see which of your friends are playing?
questions.f: Friend lists show a little green light when a friend is online.

questions.q: The internet lets computers around the world share information.
questions.f: The internet links billions of computers, so a message can cross the ocean in a blink.

questions.q: A short nickname for a microphone is a…?
questions.f: Singers say 'check the mic' — mic is just microphone made short and snappy.

questions.q: Which key erases the letter you just typed?
questions.f: Backspace nibbles away letters one at a time, moving backward.

questions.q: What is the green creature that sneaks up and goes BOOM in Minecraft?
questions.f: The creeper was born from a coding mix-up — a pig model got its shape tangled up!

questions.q: A thumbs-up emoji usually means…?
questions.f: People send the thumbs-up to agree without typing a single word.

questions.q: Robots can go to places that are too dangerous for people, like inside a volcano.
questions.f: Scientists have sent robots into volcanoes, deep oceans, and even onto other planets.

questions.q: If your tablet is 'offline', what is it NOT connected to?
questions.f: Some games and books still work offline — no internet needed.

questions.q: What do you point at a QR code to make it work?
questions.f: The camera reads the QR code's black and white squares like a secret message.

questions.q: What does a password hint help you do?
questions.f: A good hint jogs only YOUR memory — it should not give the secret away to others.

questions.q: What does a robot use to 'see' the world around it?
questions.f: Sensors tell robots about bumps, walls, and edges so they do not crash or fall.

questions.q: When you 'reply' to a message, what are you doing?
questions.f: Reply means your answer travels straight back to the person who wrote to you.

questions.q: A smart doorbell with a camera lets you see…?
questions.f: Smart doorbells send live video to a phone, even when nobody is home.

questions.q: Sliding your finger across a touchscreen is called a…?
questions.f: Swiping left and right is how people flip through photos on a phone.

questions.q: Round, shiny discs that can hold games, movies, or music are called…?
questions.f: A laser inside the player reads tiny bumps on the disc to play the game or song.

questions.q: An email can include a photo.
questions.f: Files added to an email are called attachments — photos, drawings, even videos.

questions.q: A person whose job is inventing new video games is called a game…?
questions.f: Game designers dream up the worlds, characters, and rules that make games fun.

questions.q: Where on a tablet do you go to change how things look and work?
questions.f: The settings app usually has a little gear picture on it.

questions.q: Deep down, computers store everything using which two digits?
questions.f: This two-digit system is called binary — every photo, song, and game becomes 0s and 1s.

questions.q: An 'algorithm' is best described as…?
questions.f: A recipe is like an algorithm for cooking — computers follow their steps exactly.

questions.q: Which part of a computer is often called its 'brain'?
questions.f: The CPU does the thinking — billions of tiny calculations every single second.

questions.q: The letters WWW in a web address stand for…?
questions.f: The World Wide Web is the huge collection of linked pages you visit with a browser.

questions.q: Pictures on a screen are built from thousands of tiny colored dots called…?
questions.f: Lean very close to an old screen and you can actually see the single glowing pixels.

questions.q: Pong, one of the first hit video games, was based on which sport?
questions.f: Pong was just two paddles and a bouncing dot, but in 1972 people lined up to play it.

questions.q: In the game Tetris, what do players do with the falling shapes?
c: Fit them together into full rows
questions.f: When a row is completely filled, it vanishes — and the game slowly gets faster and faster.

questions.q: What is Mario's job, according to his games?
questions.f: That is why pipes are everywhere in Mario games — plumbers know their way around pipes!

questions.q: The 'bi' in 'binary' means…?
questions.f: Just like a bicycle has two wheels, binary uses exactly two digits: 0 and 1.

questions.q: Ada Lovelace, who lived about 200 years ago, is often called the world's first…?
questions.f: Ada wrote instructions for a computing machine before any real computer was ever built.

questions.q: The 'e' in 'email' stands for…?
questions.f: Email means electronic mail — letters that travel as signals instead of on paper.

questions.q: What does a computer's memory do?
questions.f: Memory holds your files, photos, and games as patterns of millions of tiny switches.

questions.q: In coding, a 'loop' makes the computer…?
questions.f: Instead of writing 'move' 100 times, a coder writes a loop that says 'do this 100 times'.

questions.q: Websites live on powerful computers with a fitting name — they 'serve' pages, so they are called…?
questions.f: When you open a website, a server somewhere in the world serves the page to your screen.

questions.q: A 'screenshot' is a…?
c: Picture of what is on your screen
questions.f: Screenshots let you save exactly what you see — high scores, funny messages, anything.

questions.q: The common keyboard layout is called QWERTY. Where does that name come from?
questions.f: Look at the top-left letter row of a keyboard and you can read the name: Q-W-E-R-T-Y.

questions.q: Which kind of app do you use to visit websites?
questions.f: Browsers 'browse' the web for you — the word means looking around at this and that.

questions.q: Google is a famous example of a…?
questions.f: Search engines sort through billions of webpages in less than a second.

questions.q: When your files are saved 'in the cloud', where are they really kept?
questions.f: Cloud files sit in giant buildings full of computers called data centers.

questions.q: How big were some of the very first computers in the 1940s?
c: As big as a whole room
questions.f: Early computers weighed as much as several cars and needed teams of people to run them.

questions.q: Computer parts you can actually touch, like the keyboard and screen, are called…?
questions.f: Hardware is the machine itself; software is the invisible programs running on it.

questions.q: Games, apps, and programs are all examples of…?
questions.f: Software is written by programmers and can be copied onto millions of computers.

questions.q: In which country were emoji first invented?
questions.f: Emoji began on Japanese phones in the late 1990s before spreading around the world.

questions.q: A computer 'virus' is a harmful program named after what?
questions.f: Like real germs, computer viruses spread by making copies of themselves.

questions.q: The cash machine at a bank, called an ATM, is really a kind of…?
questions.f: ATMs are computers that talk to the bank over a network before handing out money.

questions.q: The letters AI stand for…?
questions.f: AI is computer smartness made by people — 'artificial' means made by humans, not nature.

questions.q: Which company created Mario?
questions.f: Nintendo is a Japanese company, and Mario has starred in its games since the 1980s.

questions.q: A game that lots of people can play together at once is called…?
questions.f: 'Multi' means many — multiplayer games connect many players in one shared world.

questions.q: What do satellites in space help beam around the world?
questions.f: Some satellites fly about 36,000 kilometers up and still deliver signals in a flash.

questions.q: What is the smallest piece of computer information called?
questions.f: A single bit is just a 0 or a 1 — but billions of bits together make a movie.

questions.q: Who works together to make a big video game?
questions.f: Big games can take hundreds of people several years to build.

questions.q: A PIN code, like the one used at cash machines, is made only of…?
questions.f: PIN stands for personal identification number — a secret number that proves it is you.

questions.q: Pilots can practise flying in a computer simulator without leaving the ground.
questions.f: Simulators feel so real that pilots train for emergencies safely on the ground.

questions.q: A 'simulation' is a computer's way of…?
questions.f: Simulations let scientists test cities, weather, and rockets without touching the real thing.

questions.q: Every piece in Tetris is built from how many squares?
questions.f: All seven Tetris pieces are different ways of joining exactly four squares.

questions.q: The 'auto' in 'autopilot' and 'autocorrect' means the machine does it…?
questions.f: From Greek, 'auto' means self — an automatic machine works on its own.

questions.q: Every email address contains the @ symbol.
questions.f: The @ sign separates a person's name from the place their mailbox lives.

questions.q: Where do you type a website's address in a browser?
questions.f: The address bar sits at the top of the browser and shows where you are on the web.

questions.q: Sonic the Hedgehog is famous for being incredibly…?
questions.f: Sonic zooms through loops at video-game 'supersonic' speed — faster than sound!

questions.q: 'Spam' is the nickname for what kind of email?
c: Junk mail you did not ask for
questions.f: Spam clogs up inboxes, so email programs use filters to sweep it into a junk folder.

questions.q: The famous keyboard shortcut Ctrl+Z does what?
questions.f: Coders and artists press Ctrl+Z so often that some wish real life had an undo key.

questions.q: Video games from the 1970s and 1980s looked blocky compared with today's games.
questions.f: Old machines could only draw a few big pixels, so characters looked like little block mosaics.

questions.q: Megabytes and gigabytes are units that measure…?
questions.f: A gigabyte can hold hundreds of songs — and a thousand megabytes make one gigabyte.

questions.q: What is the box called that spreads Wi-Fi through your home?
questions.f: The router takes the internet from a cable and shares it through the air as radio waves.

questions.q: On a laptop, what is the flat area that works like a mouse called?
questions.f: Trackpads feel your fingertip sliding and turn it into pointer moves on the screen.

questions.q: The earliest websites were mostly plain words with no videos.
questions.f: The first webpages were simple text and links — online video came many years later.

questions.q: A smiley face made from keyboard symbols, like :-) , is called an…?
questions.f: Tilt your head to the left and :-) turns into two eyes, a nose, and a smile.

questions.q: Before USB sticks, people carried computer files on bendy square things called…?
questions.f: A floppy disk held less than one photo does today — kids often carried a whole box of them.

questions.q: A USB stick that stores your files is also called a flash…?
questions.f: Flash drives have no moving parts, so they keep files safe even when dropped.

questions.q: Which was invented first — radio or the internet?
questions.f: Radio is more than a century old; the internet grew up in the 1970s and 1980s.

questions.q: Headphones with a microphone attached are called a…?
questions.f: Gamers love headsets because they can hear the game and talk to teammates at once.

questions.q: How many main buttons do most computer mice have?
questions.f: Left-click chooses things; right-click opens a secret menu of extra choices.

questions.q: Computers can beat even very good human players at chess.
questions.f: Since the 1990s, chess computers have been strong enough to challenge world champions.

questions.q: The word 'webcam' is a mash-up of which two words?
questions.f: A webcam is simply a camera made for sending pictures over the web.

questions.q: A tablet computer is heavier than a desktop computer.
questions.f: Tablets are light enough to hold in one hand; desktops sit on a desk and stay put.

questions.q: The Game Boy was famous for being a console you could…?
questions.f: Nintendo's Game Boy came out in 1989 and ran for hours on ordinary batteries.

questions.q: A 'handheld' game device is one that…?
questions.f: Handheld consoles pack a screen, speakers, and buttons into one pocket-sized machine.

questions.q: In the classic game Space Invaders, players defend Earth from rows of…?
questions.f: Space Invaders was such a hit in 1978 that arcades ran out of room for the machines.

questions.q: An 'invader' is someone who…?
c: Enters a place where they are not wanted
questions.f: From Latin, 'invade' means to go in — game invaders march right into your territory!

questions.q: The Enter key on some keyboards has another name. What is it?
questions.f: On old typewriters, 'carriage return' slid the paper back to start a new line.

questions.q: Before computers, people typed letters on a machine called a…?
questions.f: Typewriters stamped ink onto paper — and gave us the QWERTY keyboard we still use.

questions.q: Some charging cables can carry information as well as electricity.
questions.f: A USB cable can charge a phone and copy photos to a computer at the same time.

questions.q: When you 'stream' a video, what happens?
c: It plays right away over the internet
It is mailed to your house
questions.f: Streaming means the data flows to you like a stream of water — no waiting for a full download.

questions.q: In some hospitals, robots carry supplies along the corridors.
questions.f: Delivery robots bring medicine and meals, riding elevators all by themselves.

questions.q: Holding the mouse button down while moving something across the screen is called…?
questions.f: Drag and drop — you drag the file to a new spot, then drop it by letting go.

questions.q: The word 'keyboard' is also used for which musical instrument?
questions.f: Both keyboards are boards of keys — one types letters, the other plays notes.

questions.q: In Pokemon games, what do players catch and train?
questions.f: Trainers store their creatures in small balls and battle them in friendly matches.

questions.q: A secret button combination that unlocks tricks in a game is called a…?
questions.f: Game makers hide cheat codes on purpose — famous ones give extra lives or silly hats.

questions.q: Very old telephones had a spinning dial. What do smartphones have instead?
questions.f: To call someone on a dial phone, you spun the dial once for every single digit!

questions.q: A 'smart' TV or 'smart' watch is called smart because it can…?
c: Connect to the internet and run apps
questions.f: 'Smart' gadgets are ordinary machines with a little computer tucked inside.

questions.q: In online games, what does 'lag' mean?
questions.f: Lag happens when game information takes too long to travel across the internet.

questions.q: Robots can milk cows on some farms.
questions.f: On robotic farms, cows walk up to the milking robot whenever they feel ready.

questions.q: Getting a newer, better version of an app is called an…?
questions.f: Upgrades can add new features, fix bugs, and make apps run faster.

questions.q: Computers have fans inside to keep their parts cool.
questions.f: Working chips get hot, so fans pull in cool air — that is the whoosh you hear.

questions.q: Minecraft was first created by just one programmer.
questions.f: One coder built the first version of Minecraft — it grew into one of the biggest games ever.

questions.q: In games, 'leveling up' means your character…?
questions.f: Leveling up often unlocks new powers, tools, or places to explore.

questions.q: Which came first: black-and-white screens or color screens?
questions.f: Early computers glowed in one color — often green letters on a black screen.

questions.q: How does a digital camera store the photos it takes?
c: As numbers a computer can read
questions.f: Every digital photo is really millions of numbers describing the color of each pixel.

questions.q: What do special underwater robots help explorers study?
questions.f: Robot submarines can dive deeper than any human diver and send video back up.

questions.q: The 'remote' in 'remote control' means…?
questions.f: A remote control lets you command a machine from far away — no wires needed.

questions.q: Which video game came first?
questions.f: Pong arrived in 1972 — decades before the others were even imagined.

questions.q: A file you add to an email, like a photo, is called an…?
questions.f: 'Attach' means to fasten — the file is fastened to your message for the ride.

questions.q: How does a phone's touchscreen know where your finger is?
c: It senses your finger's tiny electric charge
questions.f: That is why most touchscreens ignore gloves — wool does not carry your body's charge.

questions.q: A 'sensor' is a machine part that…?
c: Detects things like light or touch
questions.f: Sensors are a robot's senses — they feel bumps, see light, and measure heat.

questions.q: Wikipedia is a giant online…?
questions.f: Volunteers all over the world write and fix Wikipedia's millions of articles.

questions.q: A GIF is a little picture that…?
questions.f: GIFs loop the same few frames forever — perfect for a dancing banana.

questions.q: Python and Scratch are both names of…?
questions.f: Programmers choose different languages for different jobs, just like tools in a toolbox.

questions.q: Turning screen brightness down saves battery power.
questions.f: Lower brightness is also much easier on your eyes at night.

questions.q: Wireless earbuds connect to a phone using…?
questions.f: The radio connection they use is called Bluetooth, and it works across a whole room.

questions.q: In the 1980s, many home computers used which household machine as their screen?
questions.f: Kids plugged early computers into the living room TV — and had to share it with cartoons.

questions.q: Why is it smart to give your file a clear name?
c: So you can find it again later
questions.f: A file called 'my-volcano-project' is much easier to find than one called 'ffff123'.

questions.q: Some robots can dance.
questions.f: Engineers have programmed robots to do full dance routines — videos of them are famous online.

questions.q: Pixels on a screen are arranged in a pattern of rows and columns called a…?
questions.f: Screens are giant grids — a common one is 1920 pixels across and 1080 down.

questions.q: The little magnifying glass icon on apps and websites usually means…?
questions.f: The magnifying glass says 'look closer' — click it and type what you want to find.

questions.q: Which was invented first: the laptop or the smartphone?
questions.f: Portable computers appeared in the early 1980s; smartphones came along years later.

questions.q: The 're' in 'reload' and 'restart' means…?
questions.f: From Latin, 're' means again — reload a page and the computer fetches it again.

questions.q: In the game Donkey Kong, the hero has to dodge rolling…?
questions.f: Donkey Kong hurls barrels down the ramps while the hero climbs ladders to the top.

questions.q: If a gadget is 'high-tech', it uses…?
questions.f: 'Tech' is short for technology — high-tech means at technology's cutting edge.

questions.q: A VR headset puts small screens right in front of your…?
questions.f: Each eye gets its own picture, which tricks your brain into seeing a 3D world.

questions.q: If something is 'virtual', it exists…?
questions.f: A virtual pet or virtual world feels real on screen, but you cannot touch it.

questions.q: Which needs more computer storage?
questions.f: A movie can use more storage than a million text messages put together.

questions.q: Where do copies of the emails you have already sent get kept?
questions.f: Email apps keep your sent mail so you can check exactly what you wrote.

questions.q: Modern animated movies are mostly drawn using…?
questions.f: Computer animators build characters in 3D, then the computer draws every frame.

questions.q: 'Animation' is the art of making pictures seem to…?
questions.f: From Latin 'anima', meaning life or breath — animators bring drawings to life.

questions.q: The first email was sent more than 50 years ago.
questions.f: Email is older than home computers — the first one was sent in the early 1970s.

questions.q: 'Robotics' is the science of…?
questions.f: Robotics mixes coding, electronics, and mechanics — many schools have robotics clubs.

questions.q: What does a phone's fingerprint sensor scan to unlock the phone?
questions.f: No two people have the same fingerprint pattern, so it works like a built-in key.

questions.q: 'Touch typing' means typing…?
questions.f: Touch typists rest their fingers on the home row and can type faster than they write.

questions.q: A smart fridge can send a message to say you are running low on milk.
questions.f: Cameras inside smart fridges peek at the shelves so you never forget the shopping.

questions.q: The internet is owned by one single company.
questions.f: Nobody owns the internet — it is millions of networks around the world agreeing to connect.

questions.q: The word 'robot' first appeared in a play, and it came from a word meaning…?
questions.f: Czech writer Karel Capek used 'robota' — hard forced work — for his play's artificial workers in 1920.

questions.q: The word 'wiki', as in Wikipedia, comes from a word meaning…?
questions.f: From Hawaiian 'wiki wiki', meaning very quick — because anyone can edit a wiki page fast.

questions.q: Bluetooth, the wireless technology, is named after a…?
questions.f: King Harald Bluetooth united parts of Denmark and Norway — Bluetooth unites your gadgets.

questions.q: The 'inter' in 'internet' means…?
questions.f: The internet is a network between networks — 'inter' plus 'net' says exactly that.

questions.q: A computer 'firewall' is named after a real wall that stops…?
questions.f: Buildings use fireproof walls to block flames; computer firewalls block harmful traffic.

questions.q: In computing, a 'bug' means…?
questions.f: Fixing those mistakes is called debugging — coders hunt bugs like detectives.

questions.q: A 'browser' has its name because it lets you…?
c: Look around from page to page
questions.f: To browse means to wander and look — exactly what people do on the web.

questions.q: The word 'digital' is related to a Latin word for…?
questions.f: Romans counted on their fingers — 'digitus' means finger, and digits are what computers count with.

questions.q: A 'pixel' gets its name from a shortening of which two words?
questions.f: Each pixel is one tiny element of a picture — millions of them make a photo.

questions.q: The 'micro' in 'microchip' and 'microphone' means…?
questions.f: From Greek 'mikros', meaning small — a microchip is smaller than your fingernail.

questions.q: A 'monitor' has a name meaning something that…?
questions.f: From Latin 'monere', to warn — the screen lets you watch what the computer is doing.

questions.q: 'Cyber' words like cyberspace originally came from a word about…?
questions.f: From Greek 'kybernetes', a ship's steersman — cybernetics is the study of control systems.

questions.q: The 'graph' in 'graphics' means…?
questions.f: From Greek 'graphein', to write or draw — computer graphics are computer drawings.

questions.q: A 'gigabyte' uses 'giga', which means…?
questions.f: 'Giga' comes from a Greek word for giant — a gigabyte is about a billion bytes.

questions.q: The 'mega' in 'megabyte' and 'megaphone' means…?
questions.f: From Greek 'megas', great — a megaphone makes your voice great and loud.

questions.q: A 'network' is named for something that connects like a…?
questions.f: Just as a net is knotted threads crossing each other, a network is machines linked together.

questions.q: 'Software' was invented as a word to contrast with…?
questions.f: Hardware is the hard, solid machine; software is the soft, changeable instructions inside.

questions.q: A 'terminal' where you type commands is named because it sits at the…?
questions.f: From Latin 'terminus', an end or boundary — the same root as a bus terminal.

questions.q: Programs called 'apps' are short for applications — and 'apply' means to…?
questions.f: An application applies the computer's power to one job: drawing, chatting, or playing.

questions.q: The 'mini' in 'minicomputer' means…?
questions.f: When room-sized computers ruled, a fridge-sized machine counted as 'mini'!

questions.q: 'Data' is a word from Latin meaning things that are…?
questions.f: From 'datum', a thing given — data are the facts given to a computer to work with.

questions.q: To 'compute' originally meant to…?
questions.f: From Latin 'computare', to reckon up — so a computer is literally a counting machine.

questions.q: The 'port' in 'USB port' comes from a word for a…?
questions.f: From Latin 'porta', a gate — a port is where cables enter and leave the machine.

questions.q: A 'menu' on screen borrowed its name from…?
questions.f: A restaurant menu is a list of dishes; a computer menu is a list of commands.

questions.q: A 'window' on a computer screen is named after a real window because it…?
c: Shows you a view of something
questions.f: Each window frames one program's view, and you can have many open at once.

questions.q: A 'virus' takes its name from a Latin word meaning…?
questions.f: Biologists borrowed it for germs, and computer scientists borrowed it again for bad programs.

questions.q: To 'boot' a computer means to…?
questions.f: It is short for bootstrapping — the computer pulls itself up by its own bootstraps.

questions.q: 'Hyperlink' begins with 'hyper', which means…?
questions.f: A hyperlink jumps you beyond the page you are on, straight to another one.

questions.q: To 'program' something comes from Greek words meaning…?
questions.f: A program is instructions written in advance — like the program for a school concert.

questions.q: 'Automatic' and 'automobile' share 'auto', meaning…?
questions.f: An automobile moves itself; an automatic door opens by itself.

questions.q: The 'trans' in 'transmit' and 'transfer' means…?
questions.f: To transmit is to send across — radios transmit signals across the sky.

questions.q: A 'chip' inside a computer got that name because it is a small…?
c: Piece cut from a larger crystal
questions.f: Chips are sliced from big crystals of silicon, then packed with millions of tiny switches.

questions.q: 'Silicon', used to make computer chips, is a…?
questions.f: Silicon comes from ordinary sand — which is why Silicon Valley got its name.

questions.q: The 'byte' was named as a playful respelling to avoid confusion with which word?
questions.f: Bit and byte sound too alike when spelled the same way, so 'bite' became 'byte'.

questions.q: A 'keypad' is a small pad of keys — so what does 'pad' suggest?
questions.f: Number keypads group the digits so people can type them quickly with one hand.

questions.q: The word 'algorithm' comes from the name of a real person.
questions.f: It honours al-Khwarizmi, a mathematician who wrote step-by-step methods over 1,000 years ago.

questions.q: 'Multimedia' means using more than one…?
c: Kind of media, like sound and video
questions.f: 'Multi' means many; media means ways of sharing — text, pictures, sound, and video together.

questions.q: A 'modem' does two jobs, and its name is a blend of…?
questions.f: It changes computer signals for the phone line and changes them back at the other end.

questions.q: 'Cache' means a hidden store, so a computer cache holds…?
c: Data kept ready for quick reuse
questions.f: Your browser caches images so a page you revisit loads much faster.

questions.q: 'Icon' comes from a Greek word meaning…?
questions.f: From 'eikon', an image — screen icons are little images standing for bigger things.

questions.q: A 'console' for gaming borrowed its name from a…?
questions.f: Aeroplanes and organs have consoles too — panels where all the controls sit together.

questions.q: The 'com' in 'communicate' and '.com' means…?
questions.f: To communicate is to share — and .com stands for commercial, a business site.

questions.q: 'Text' comes from a Latin word meaning…?
questions.f: From 'texere', to weave — a text weaves words together, just like textiles weave threads.

questions.q: A 'sim' card is short for a word meaning…?
questions.f: SIM stands for subscriber identity module — the little card that tells the network who you are.

questions.q: The word 'code' originally referred to a…?
questions.f: From Latin 'codex' — a set of written rules, which is close to what computer code is.

questions.q: A 'password' is literally a word that lets you…?
questions.f: Guards long ago asked travellers for a word before letting them pass the gate.

questions.q: The word 'byte' is a deliberate misspelling of 'bite'.
questions.f: Engineers respelled it so nobody would mix up 'bit' and 'bite' in their notes.

questions.q: Charles Babbage designed two great machines. What were they called?
c: The Difference Engine and the Analytical Engine
The Steam Brain and the Iron Mind
The Number Loom and the Fact Mill
The Cog Clock and the Sum Wheel
questions.f: Babbage's Analytical Engine, designed in the 1830s, had all the ideas of a modern computer.

questions.q: Ada Lovelace wrote her famous notes about which of Babbage's machines?
questions.f: Her notes are longer than the article she was translating, and they contain the first program.

questions.q: The Turing test is designed to check whether a machine can…?
c: Hold a conversation that seems human
questions.f: Alan Turing suggested it in 1950 as a way to sidestep arguing about whether machines 'think'.

questions.q: ENIAC, one of the first electronic computers, filled a whole room and was used to calculate…?
questions.f: ENIAC had about 18,000 glass vacuum tubes and weighed roughly 30 tonnes.

questions.q: Grace Hopper's team famously found a real moth stuck inside a computer, helping popularise which term?
questions.f: They taped the moth into the logbook in 1947 with the note that they were 'debugging' the machine.

questions.q: What is the difference between the internet and the World Wide Web?
c: The web is one service that runs on the internet
They are exactly the same thing
The internet runs on the web
The web is older than the internet
questions.f: Email and games use the internet without using the web at all — the web is pages and links.

questions.q: Who invented the World Wide Web while working at a physics laboratory in Europe?
questions.f: He wrote the first web browser and server at CERN around 1990 — and gave the web away free.

questions.q: The famous 1997 chess match saw world champion Garry Kasparov lose to which computer?
questions.f: Deep Blue could examine around 200 million chess positions every second.

questions.q: In 2016, a program called AlphaGo beat a top human champion at which ancient board game?
questions.f: Go has more possible board positions than there are atoms in the observable universe.

questions.q: Tetris was invented in the 1980s by a programmer working in which country?
questions.f: Alexey Pajitnov coded it in Moscow in 1984, and the game spread west almost like a rumour.

questions.q: The name 'Tetris' combines the Greek for four with the name of which sport its inventor loved?
questions.f: 'Tetra' means four — every Tetris piece is made of four squares — plus tennis, Pajitnov's favourite game.

questions.q: In his very first game, Mario was not called Mario. What was his name?
questions.f: He was Jumpman in Donkey Kong (1981) before Nintendo renamed him Mario.

questions.q: Which company released Pong and became an early giant of video games?
questions.f: Atari's first Pong machine reportedly broke down because its coin box was stuffed too full.

questions.q: The word 'algorithm' honours al-Khwarizmi, who was a…?
questions.f: He worked in Baghdad around 820 CE, and his name also gave us the word 'algebra'.

questions.q: In programming, what does a 'loop' let you avoid?
c: Writing the same instruction over and over
questions.f: A loop with a counter can repeat a task a million times from just two or three lines of code.

questions.q: How many different values can a single bit hold?
questions.f: One bit is a single yes-or-no switch; eight bits together make a byte with 256 possibilities.

questions.q: How many bits are in one byte?
questions.f: Eight bits give 256 combinations — enough for every letter, digit, and symbol on a keyboard.

questions.q: In binary, what number does 1010 represent?
questions.f: Reading right to left the place values are 1, 2, 4, 8 — so 8 + 2 = 10.

questions.q: The word 'robot' entered English from a 1920 play by Karel Capek titled…?
questions.f: R.U.R. stands for Rossum's Universal Robots, and its artificial workers were named from 'robota', forced labour.

questions.q: Web 'cookies' are small files that websites use to…?
questions.f: Cookies remember your language or what is in your shopping basket between visits.

questions.q: Junk email is called 'spam' thanks to a comedy sketch about a cafe where every dish contained…?
questions.f: In the Monty Python sketch the word 'spam' is repeated until it drowns out everything else.

questions.q: What is a computer's 'operating system'?
c: The master software that runs everything else
questions.f: Windows, macOS, Android, and Linux are all operating systems managing files, screens, and apps.

questions.q: Which pair are BOTH operating systems?
questions.f: An operating system is the software the whole machine depends on to start and run.

questions.q: The word 'wiki' comes from a Hawaiian phrase, 'wiki wiki', that was used for the…?
questions.f: Programmer Ward Cunningham rode the 'Wiki Wiki' shuttle in Honolulu and borrowed the name for fast-editing pages.

questions.q: Which of these does a 'search engine' actually store to answer questions so fast?
questions.f: Search engines crawl the web and build a giant index, like the index at the back of a book.

questions.q: Roughly how many characters could an old text message hold?
questions.f: The 160-character limit was chosen because engineers found most postcards fitted in that space.

questions.q: What does a 'compiler' do?
c: Turns human-readable code into machine instructions
questions.f: Grace Hopper championed the idea that computers could translate English-like code themselves.

questions.q: Which everyday object inspired the name of the 'desktop' on your screen?
c: The top of a real desk
questions.f: Designers copied real offices — files, folders, and a wastebasket all sat on the desktop.

questions.q: The 'www' part of an address tells you the page belongs to which system?
questions.f: Many sites now work without typing www at all, but the habit stuck for decades.

questions.q: What is 'open source' software?
c: Software whose code anyone may read and improve
Software that only opens at night
questions.f: Linux, Firefox, and Wikipedia's software are all built and improved by volunteers worldwide.

questions.q: Which of these is a programming language named after a snake — but really after a comedy group?
questions.f: Its creator was a fan of Monty Python's Flying Circus, and the name stuck.

questions.q: What does the 'S' in 'https' tell you about a website?
questions.f: The S means the data is scrambled on the way, so eavesdroppers only see nonsense.

questions.q: What do we call a computer program that talks with you by typing, like a helper on a website?
questions.f: The very first chatbot, ELIZA, was written in the 1960s and imitated a therapist's questions.

questions.q: A 'megapixel' in a camera means how many pixels?
questions.f: A 12-megapixel photo contains about twelve million tiny coloured squares.

questions.q: Which of these best describes 'machine learning'?
c: Programs that improve by finding patterns in data
questions.f: Instead of being told every rule, the program studies thousands of examples and works rules out.

questions.q: What did the first computer mouse, built in the 1960s, have on the outside?
questions.f: Douglas Engelbart's prototype was a carved wooden block with a button and two metal wheels.

questions.q: The 'GPS' that guides maps on a phone works using…?
questions.f: Your phone compares timing from several satellites to work out where it is within a few metres.

questions.q: What is a 'QR code' short for?
questions.f: A Japanese engineer invented it in 1994 to track car parts faster than barcodes could.

questions.q: In coding, what does an 'if' statement let a program do?
questions.f: An if statement is a fork in the road: do this when the answer is yes, that when it is no.

questions.q: What is a 'variable' in a computer program?
c: A named box that stores a value
questions.f: Change what is in the box and the whole program uses the new value — that is why it varies.

questions.q: The 'analytical' in Babbage's Analytical Engine points to a word meaning to…?
c: Break something into parts to study it
questions.f: From Greek 'analusis', a loosening-up — his engine was meant to take problems apart step by step.

questions.q: Babbage's Difference Engine was named for the mathematical 'method of differences', which builds tables using only…?
questions.f: Clever mathematics let a machine of gears produce whole tables using nothing but adding.

questions.q: What was Ada Lovelace's father famous for?
questions.f: Ada was the daughter of the poet Lord Byron, though she was raised on mathematics instead of verse.

questions.q: Ada Lovelace suggested Babbage's engine might one day compose which kind of art?
